## 0.1 ⛔ THE PRECEDENCE LAW

```

```

⛔ **If a legacy document and this plan disagree, THIS PLAN WINS. Always. No
exceptions. Do not reconcile, do not average, do not ask.**

⭐ **Mine the legacy corpus for three things only:**
1. **Authored content** — profiles, help articles, language packs, page decks
2. **Technical detail** — the CC slices' depth on specific mechanisms
3. **Feature names** — so nothing is lost *(the union rule, §7A.3)*

⛔ **Never take a law, a ruling, a date, a price, a phase or a module count from
legacy.**

## 0.3 ⭐ HOW WE WORK — THE METHOD

**Ten behaviours. A turn that breaks one is a turn done wrong.**

| # | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **1** | ⭐ **Every module turn OPENS with domain research** *(§7E)*. Research first, spec second — it has changed the architecture five times |
| **2** | ⭐ **Every warning gets a SOLUTION in the same turn** *(law 21)*. A compliance matter becomes a mechanism, a CI number, or honest copy — **never a gate, never a pending question** |
| **3** | ⭐ **Run the grep, don't recall** *(law 71)*. A completeness claim is worth exactly the check behind it |
| **4** | ⭐ **Three files, modified in place** *(law 20)*. No copies, no versions, no new files |
| **5** | ⛔ **No gates. Features first, concerns parked** *(R92)*. Matt auto-approves; build it |
| **6** | ⭐ **Nothing is ever removed** *(§7A.3)*. A feature named in any source enters the plan. Union, never replacement |
| **7** | ⭐ **An owner ruling supersedes IMMEDIATELY** and gets written into the plan the same turn — including into this kill list |
| **8** | ⭐ **Every module carries the market leader's number and must beat it** *(§7D)* |
| **9** | ⭐ **Everything automatic** *(law 25)*. A *"review this monthly"* line in any spec is a defect |
| **10** | ⛔ **Say what's actually true.** Honest limits stated in the spec — *"a 200-truck shop should still buy ServiceTitan"*, *"replay reconstructs decisions not outcomes"*, *"we're B+ on ops, not A+"* |

### The turn shape

```
  ① research the domain          ② spec against it
  ③ name every risk              ④ solve every risk you named
  ⑤ write to the master plan     ⑥ update the tracker
  ⑦ present both files           ⑧ report what changed and why
```

## 0.B ⭐⭐⭐ THE PRODUCT-LAW REGISTER — EVERY LIVE PRODUCT LAW, ONCE *(H-2 · T672 · the source of the "laws that bind" line in every brief)*

> **How to use this:** each law has an ID *(P-nnn)*, one sentence, its **source §** and what it **supersedes**. R-/M-/Law-numbers are aliases. **If a section of this file disagrees with a line here, the line here wins — it was written by reading the section and its supersessions.** A law with no source is not a law; none below lacks one. *Process laws (how the plan is written and how the swarm builds) are §0.C (H-3), not here.*

| **P-001** | **Two packages — Basic and Everything Else — and pricing never changes:** everything we ship, as we ship it, at the price you joined at | T468 · §0.2 #3 · *kills founder pricing, R18's window, "retail returns at the flip"* | ⭐⭐ **[AMENDED T677 · §215] STANDS INTACT alongside P-201: the LIST PRICE of each package never changes. A DISCOUNT is not a price change — it is a recorded, expiring, attributed reduction against a stable list price.** ⛔ **`doctor` asserts the package price row is IMMUTABLE; a promotion writes to `promotion_redemptions`, never to the package.** *That is what keeps "our prices never change" true while offers exist.*

Nobody migrates blind.** ⛔ **AN IMPORT IS NOT A PERMIT: every imported `Person` is UNPERMITTED until the tenant establishes their own relationship.** ⛔ **A MERGE NEEDS TWO STRONG IDENTIFIERS; one weak match is REJECTED to the report, never merged.** ⭐⭐⭐ **THE RECONCILIATION REPORT IS THE PRODUCT** — *what came in, what was rejected and why, which fields had no home, and how many cards cannot transfer, all BEFORE commit.* ⛔⛔ **A competitor's free-text NOTES contain gate and alarm codes — the burglary kit arriving in bulk. | **P-204** | ⭐⭐ **THE PLATFORM MEASURES WORK, IT DOES NOT PAY PEOPLE.** ⛔⛔ **NO PAYROLL, NO HR.** *Wages, tax, withholding, filings, W-2, pay runs, garnishments, final pay, timesheets, attendance, benefits, performance management — all OUT.* ✅ **IN, because it is the JOB's data: job time** *(arrival, duration, completion — dispatch and costing)* **· job expenses and mileage** *(a JOB COST feeding the pricebook's COST column and X-210's margin guard)* **· COMMISSION EARNED as a number derived from collected revenue and actual cost · and the EXPORT of hours and commission to the tenant's own payroll provider.** ⛔ **THE EXPORT SHIPS HOURS AND COMMISSION-EARNED AND NOTHING ELSE — `doctor` asserts no field named `gross`, `net`, `tax` or `withholding` exists in the export module.** *If the provider needs gross pay, the provider computes it; that is what they are licensed for.* ⭐⭐⭐ **AND EVERY COMMISSION FIGURE THE PLATFORM SHOWS CARRIES ONE LINE: “calculated from collected revenue; your employer’s payroll is the final word.”** ⛔ *Asserted on every surface that renders a commission — the distance between “the platform says I earned $2,400” and “the platform owes me $2,400” is smaller in a dispute than in a spec.* ⭐ **Consequence: §198's no-model zone shrinks from three modules to ONE (X-170's commission arithmetic).** *The cleanest way to never produce a wrong wage is to never produce a wage.* | **T677 (owner)** · §220 · fences X-169, narrows X-168 to `JobTime` |

Four rows of DATA, one fixed order, no override.** ⛔⛔ **AN OPEN `RECOVER` ON A `Person` SUPPRESSES EVERY `GROW` TOWARD THEM until it closes** — *this unifies five rules already written separately at §216, §199, §192, §190 and R21.* **Within a class: OLDEST WAITING WINS — queue age, never module importance, because age cannot be gamed. The loser is DEFERRED with a visible reason, never dropped; a deferred GROW expires with its own window.** *The cadence ceiling is the CAP; the ladder is the CHOICE — both apply.* **MUTATION COLLISIONS: a HUMAN action beats any autopilot and for a window afterwards (R21 generalised) · narrower scope beats broader · observed beats assigned · irreconcilable goes to the blocked-work queue as a recommendation.** **SPEND COLLISIONS do not arbitrate — they STACK against a per-job MAXIMUM GIVE as a percentage of margin, and a breach RAISES rather than silently trimming a promised discount or a promised reward.** ⛔ **The arbiter is a SPINE service: a module that resolves a collision locally has re-created the problem.** | **T677** · §224 (turn 52) |

| **P-210** | ⭐⭐ **THE AGENT DOES NOT AUTHOR ITS TESTS.** ⛔⛔ *A swarm agent writes both the code and the test from the same brief — so if it misread the brief, the code is wrong AND the test agrees with it, and every gate downstream (the DoD, the evidence dump, the wave review) inherits the same blind spot.* ⭐⭐⭐ **The 539 ⑥ assertions and 114 TEST ANCHORs already in this plan were written BEFORE any agent existed, by a different process, against the FAILURE MODES rather than the implementation. Scope the review to CONSEQUENCE, not to confidence.* ⭐⭐⭐ **A TIE ON THE DANGEROUS CLASS IS THE DERIVATION SAYING IT DOES NOT KNOW.** *`X-200 CallCenter` scored SERVE 3 / GROW 3 — an OUTBOUND DIALER whose seat-side vocabulary matched “dispatch”, “hold” and “greeting”. It is `GROW` and `L1`, always.* | **T677** · §234 |

the drafts were current.* | **T677** · §251 | ⭐⭐ **ONE EVENT, ONE EMITTER — AND THE CONTRACT IS EDITED WHOLE, NEVER PATTERN-SUBSTITUTED.** ⛔ **Two modules emitting the same event means a consumer cannot know whose semantics or whose payload it is getting.** *At T677 thirteen events had two emitters; Neither was written until something broke.* ⭐ **And a check should PROPOSE the fix, not only refuse** — *`doctor` emits “add `@excludes X` to module Y” rather than failing silently, because a check that tells you the fix gets maintained and one that only says “no” gets disabled.* | **T677** · §248 | ⭐⭐ **`@module` ANCHORS MUST BE UNIQUE — AND A FIX IS NOT LANDED UNTIL THE READER SEES IT.** ⛔⛔ *At T677 eight modules carried duplicate anchors and `X-180`'s brief contained `X-186`'s entire description. The split was written (§233), blocked (§235.4) and gate-verified (§236) — **and never reached the generator**, because the stale anchor came first and a first-match reader takes it.* ⭐⭐⭐ **A duplicate does not error, does not warn and does not fail a gate — it silently hands one module another module's description, and every downstream check counts it as present and correct.** *The header check counted 116 blocks; it counted one twice under two names.* ⛔ **`doctor` asserts anchor uniqueness. It is one line.** ⭐ **And the general form: A MECHANISM BUILT TO MAKE SOMETHING FINDABLE CAN MAKE IT FINDABLE TWICE** — *`@module` was inserted after every heading that mentioned a module; a SHARED header mentions two, and a CODE FENCE demonstrating the annotation contains it.* | **T677** · §246 | ⭐⭐ **AN OWNER OVERRULE IS NOT COMPLETE UNTIL IT HAS A LEDGER ROW.** ⛔⛔ *The CONTESTED LEDGER's stated job is “these rulings overruled an earlier position that is STILL READABLE in the file.” At T677 it held twelve entries and was missing SIX — including `R26`'s revocation and the payroll fence, **both owner rulings made in the same session.*** ⭐⭐⭐ **A fresh window reads the ledger, sees it as complete, then finds the old text in the plan and has no reason to doubt it — which is precisely the failure the ledger exists to prevent, occurring in the ledger.** ⛔ **The ledger does not go stale gradually; it goes stale the moment a ruling lands and nobody adds a line.** *Same shape as §211's “a kill is not a kill until the tracker says so,” and learned the same way.* | **T677** · §243 | ⭐⭐ **A MODULE HEADER MAY NOT CONTRADICT A LAW — AND `doctor` GREPS FOR IT.** ⛔⛔ **No module header may contain a term from a FENCED capability.** *At T677 an `X-168` header still specced “overtime math · payroll export” for the entire session after `P-204` fenced payroll — through the eight gates, through §221's audit, through §237's brief emission.* ⭐⭐⭐ **Every one of those checks asked whether a header EXISTED. None asked whether it AGREED WITH THE LAWS** — *and a header is what becomes a brief.* ⛔ **A ruling recorded in three places and applied in two is a ruling that will be built wrong.** ⭐⭐ **AND THE SHAPE OF A SPINE MODULE'S ⑥: A PROPERTY, NOT A FEATURE.** *A feature spec asks “does it do X?” and passes when the happy path works; a property spec asks “is X EVER false?” and passes when no path makes it false.* ⛔ **An absent feature is obvious; an invariant violated ONCE, on one path, at 3am, is invisible — and that is exactly how infrastructure fails.** | **T677** · §240  ⭐⭐⭐ **[REFINED §241] THE GREP HAS THREE OUTCOMES, NOT TWO — and a two-outcome version gets switched off in a week.** **① AFFIRMATIVE** *(the header claims to DO the fenced thing)* → ⛔ **FAIL.** **② NEGATION** *(the header explicitly EXCLUDES it — “Warehouse depth stays PARKED — pick path, FIFO…”)* → ✅ **PASS, and it is GOOD that it says so** — *a module that names what it refuses is doing exactly what §219's fences asked for.* **③ VOCABULARY DRIFT** *(the term survives from before a RENAME — “`JobTime` record” after X-168 became `JobTime`)* → ⭐ **FIX THE WORD, NOT THE CAPABILITY.** ⛔ *A naive two-outcome grep flagged 6 modules at T677: **one real** (X-157 listing “payroll export” as a capability), **two vocabulary drift**, **three negations doing their job.** A check that cries wolf four times out of six gets disabled by the fourth.*|

| ⭐⭐⭐ **P-195** | ⭐⭐ **THE AUTONOMY LADDER.** Every AI action sits at one of four levels and **MOVES**: **L0 OBSERVE** *(a signal; acts on nothing)* → **L1 PROPOSE** *(drafts and asks, through `X-202 ApprovalDesk`)* → **L2 ACT & REPORT** *(does it, tells them immediately)* → **L3 AUTONOMOUS** *(does it; it appears in the weekly ROI push)*. ⭐⭐⭐ **PROMOTION IS EARNED, NEVER SET: §149.1's content trust ladder generalised to EVERY capability — N clean approvals promotes one level, an EDIT resets the counter, a REJECT drops a level. `X-149` measures. Per tenant. ⛔ IT IS NEVER A TENANT SETTING — a slider marked 'AI autonomy' is a preference set once, wrongly, and never revisited.** **Floors: L2 for anything a customer is already waiting on · L1 for anything that reaches a stranger, publishes or spends · L0 for anything that only observes.** ⛔⛔ **THREE THINGS NEVER PROMOTE AT ANY LEVEL: the CONSENT decision · a PRICE (P-092) · a CLAIM (the claim lint).** | **T677** · §189 · generalises §149.1 from content to the whole roster |

No deploy, ever.** ⛔⛔ **And impossible to bypass: `doctor` FAILS THE BUILD on any model string in code not read from the table.** *That is what actually solved the unauthorised-model incident — not purging the model, but making an unregistered model uncallable.* ⭐ **The price-drift problem solved properly: `verified_on` per row + a cron that re-reads published pricing and RAISES on drift + stale rows surfaced in the console. A watched row beats a constant nobody re-reads, and it needs no release to correct.** **Roster of record: GPT-4o-Mini · GPT-5-Mini · Luna Mini 5.6 · Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite · Grok 4.1 Fast · Claude Haiku · Claude Sonnet (escalation, CAPPED) · Gemma 2.5 Flash-Lite · Claude Opus · image + embedding models.** `ai_models` and `ai_providers` are **SPINE tables, WAVE 0.** | **T677 (owner)** · §176 · extends P-193 to the roster; supersedes the relay's purge order |

The 10 AI lines and the 20 channels are OUTBOUND ceilings only** — no outbound campaign can ever produce a busy signal for a real customer (P-095). *"Uncapped" means we impose no ceiling; an operator alert fires when inbound approaches the stack's real limit — early enough to add capacity, never a rejection.* | **T677 (owner)** · §171B · supersedes §160.1's scope and §171A's proposal |

## 0.C ⭐⭐⭐ THE PROCESS-LAW REGISTER — HOW THE PLAN IS WRITTEN AND HOW THE SWARM BUILDS *(H-3 · T673)*

> **Process laws govern the work, never the product.** *A process law is never a product gate, a compliance rule or a threshold — those are §0.B. Each entry: ID (Q-nnn) · one sentence · source · what it superseded. If any section disagrees with a line here, the line here wins.*

# GOAIEZ — THE MASTER PLAN

**Version:** 1.21 · T482 · 2026-08-23 · **M6 AMENDED**
**Status:** LIVING DOCUMENT. This file is updated every turn and never replaced.
**Companions:** `GOAIEZ-TRACKER.md` (task sheet) · `GOAIEZ-GODTIER-CAPABILITY-REGISTER.md` (905 capabilities) · `GOAIEZ-MASTER-BUILD-DOCUMENT-V2-B2B.md` (absorbed into this file at B4)

---

## 0. THE FILE ARCHITECTURE

**The constraint that shapes everything: Antigravity can hold a few files, not a
thousand.** The 349-file corpus is unusable by an agent — that is why five
separate Gemini runs produced inert scaffolding. They could never see the whole
system at once.

So: **four working files during the arc, two at the end.**

| File | Role | Grows? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`GOAIEZ-MASTER-PLAN.md`** | This file. Architecture + every module + every integration. **The single source of truth.** | Every turn |
| **`GOAIEZ-TRACKER.md`** | Task sheet. Turn state, what's done, what's next, what's blocked. | Every turn |
| **`GOAIEZ-GODTIER-CAPABILITY-REGISTER.md`** | The 905 capabilities. Drained into this file as modules get specced. | Shrinks |
| **`GOAIEZ-DECISIONS.md`** | Rulings + parked concerns. | On decisions |
| **`GOAIEZ-SWARM-DOCTRINE.md`** | The 60-agent operating model. Folds into §26 at B2. | On build rules |

**At B4 the register and decisions fold into this file. An agent then loads two
files and has the entire system.**

**Rules for this file:**
1. Append and amend. Never rewrite from scratch.
2. Every module has a fixed number. Numbers never shift.
3. Every section is addressable — a slice brief cites `§4.2 X-105`, not "the
   part about the sales agent."
4. If it isn't in this file, it isn't in the system.

---

## 1. WHAT WE ARE BUILDING

> **An AI operating system for local business — where a single conversational
> agent can operate, configure, and connect every part of the platform, and
> where the company sells itself using the exact product it sells.**

Three claims, each of which has to be built, not asserted:

**① One AI runs everything.** Not a chatbot per module. One assistant with a
machine-callable surface over all 198 modules. "Turn on review invites for my
top 50 customers and text anyone who doesn't answer in 3 days" executes — it
does not open a settings page.

**② Every module reaches every other module.** Not by integration projects. By
three shared substrates every module is built on top of (§3).

**③ The company is its own best customer.** GO AI EZ runs on GO AI EZ. Every
growth tool we build to sell the platform ships as a customer feature the same
day (§5).

---

## 2. THE EIGHT LAYERS

Modules are not the unit of construction. **Layers are.** A module built on a
finished substrate is a week; the same module built without one is a quarter.
This is the entire reason the previous runs produced empty shells — they built
modules with no substrate underneath, so every module had to invent its own
plumbing and none of them connected.

```
 L7  TENANT ZERO          GO AI EZ running on its own platform
     ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 L6  THE ASSISTANT        Anti-Gravity: one AI, every action
     ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 L5  THE 198 MODULES      Features. Thin, because L0–L4 exist.
     ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 L4  SURFACES             Widget · WP plugin · builder · templates · console
     ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 L3  DATA                 Scrape · enrich · pixel · prospects
     ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 L2  INTELLIGENCE         Agent · RAG · model router · grounding
     ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 L1  CHANNELS             Voice · SMS · email · chat · web
     ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 L0  THE SPINE            Entity graph · action registry · event bus
```

**Build downward-first. Nothing in L5 starts until L0 is done.**

---

## 3. THE SPINE — HOW EVERYTHING INTEGRATES

This is the core architectural answer and the most important section in this
document.

**The problem:** "every module integrates with every module" across 198 modules
is 39,204 pairs. Nobody builds that. Every attempt so far produced modules that
*claim* integration in a docblock and are wired to nothing.

**The solution: three shared substrates.** A module integrates with the
substrate, not with other modules. Integration count goes from N² to N.

### 3.1 THE ENTITY GRAPH — shared nouns

Every module reads and writes the *same objects*. Not its own copies.

| Entity | Meaning | Owner |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Business` | A tenant | Tenant |
| `Contact` | A person with a relationship | CRM |
| `Prospect` | A researched target, no relationship | Data layer |
| `Conversation` | A thread across any channel | Messaging |
| `Message` | One inbound or outbound unit | Messaging |
| `Job` | A booked piece of work | Booking |
| `Review` | A review on any destination | Reviews |
| `Campaign` | An orchestrated sequence | Campaigns |
| `Asset` | Page, template, image, video, doc | Content |
| `LedgerEntry` | Any credit or money movement | Billing |

**Ten nouns. Every module speaks them.** When the ads module builds an audience
it queries `Contact`. When the voice agent books, it writes `Job`. When the
review engine asks, it reads the same `Job`. Nobody syncs anything, because
there is nothing to sync.

**Law:** a module may not create a private table for a concept in this list.
Extension goes in a typed attribute bag on the canonical entity.

### 3.2 THE ACTION REGISTRY — the machine-callable surface

**This is what makes the Anti-Gravity assistant possible.** Without it, "an AI
that can configure anything" means writing a bespoke integration per module —
198 of them, each drifting.

Every module publishes a manifest:

```yaml
module: X-56 ReviewEngine
actions:
  - id: reviews.invite.send
    label: "Send a review invite"
    params:
      contact_id: {type: uuid, required: true}
      destination: {type: enum[google,facebook,yelp], default: google}
      delay_hours: {type: int, default: 0}
    returns: {invite_id: uuid, scheduled_for: datetime}
    permission: reviews.write
    reversible: true
    preview: "Ask {contact.name} for a Google review{delay}"
  - id: reviews.autopilot.configure
    label: "Turn review invites on or off"
    params:
      enabled: {type: bool}
      trigger: {type: enum[job_complete,payment,manual]}
    permission: reviews.admin
    reversible: true
```

**~198 modules × ~8 actions ≈ 1,600 actions.** That registry *is* the platform's
API, the assistant's tool list, the automation builder's node palette, the
Zapier app's action list, and the permission model — one artifact, five uses.

**Every action carries:**
- `preview` — what will happen, in plain words, before it runs
- `reversible` — can it be undone, and how
- `permission` — the role gate
- `params` — typed and validated

**Laws:**
1. A module without a manifest cannot ship. Build-failing check.
2. Anything the UI can do, an action can do. **If a button has no action behind
   it, that's a bug.** This is what makes the assistant complete rather than
   partial.
3. Actions are versioned. Breaking a signature requires a new version.

### 3.3 THE EVENT BUS — the reaction layer

Every module emits typed events. Any module subscribes. Nobody imports anybody.

```
 job.completed        →  reviews.invite.send · billing.invoice.draft · crm.stage.advance
 review.received      →  casestudy.draft · social.post.draft · roi.recalculate
 call.missed          →  sms.textback.send · crm.contact.upsert · owner.notify
 prospect.replied     →  lane.promote · agent.takeover · sequence.stop
 payment.failed       →  dunning.start · hold.evaluate · owner.notify
 form.submitted       →  crm.contact.upsert · agent.respond · pixel.identify
```

**Law:** a module never calls another module directly. It emits, or it invokes an
action from the registry. Direct imports across module boundaries fail the
build.

That single rule is what keeps 198 modules from becoming a hairball — and it is
what "everything integrates with everything" actually means in code.

### 3.4 THE INTEGRATION MATRIX

Because of §3.1–3.3, integration is provable rather than promised. Every module
declares:

```yaml
consumes_entities: [Contact, Job]
emits_events: [review.received, review.replied]
subscribes_events: [job.completed, payment.received]
exposes_actions: [reviews.invite.send, reviews.autopilot.configure]
calls_actions: [sms.send, email.send]
```

The matrix is generated from the manifests, not maintained by hand. **A module
that emits an event nobody subscribes to, or calls an action nobody exposes, is
caught by a build check.** That check is the thing that would have caught every
"wired to nothing" defect in the last five Gemini runs on day one.

### 4.2 THE ASSISTANT — X-124, THE ANTI-GRAVITY LAYER

The corpus calls it the "Antigravity-Style Command Center." It is the single
most differentiating thing in the plan, and it is **only buildable because of
§3.2.**

**What it is:** a persistent chat surface on every page. The primary interface,
not a help widget.

**What it does:**
- **Operates** — "text everyone who didn't show up last week"
- **Configures** — "turn on review invites after every completed job"
- **Builds** — "make me a landing page for emergency drain cleaning"
- **Explains** — "why didn't this campaign send?" → reads the actual refusal
  reason and says it in plain words
- **Onboards** — the client speaks their goals and the system configures itself
  (X-118)

**How it works:**
1. Intent → candidate actions from the registry (retrieval over ~1,600 actions)
2. Parameter fill from the entity graph and the conversation
3. **Preview** — every action renders its `preview` string; the user sees exactly
   what will happen before it happens
4. Execute with `CapabilityGate` (X-126) checking permission and grounding
5. **Undo** — every `reversible` action offers one-click reversal
6. Every execution written to the audit log with the actor and the prompt

**D5 RESOLVED (T453): the assistant asks.** Every action renders its `preview`
before running. Reversible actions offer one-tap undo; irreversible ones require
explicit confirmation. Per-tenant autopilot may be enabled for whitelisted
reversible actions once trust is established.

**The property that makes it trustworthy:** it can only do what the registry
exposes. It cannot invent an action, cannot reach past a permission, cannot act
on an entity it wasn't given. Its power is exactly the union of what the UI can
do — no more, and no less.

**Multi-step:** "find everyone who got a quote and never booked, text them a
10% offer, and put anyone who replies on my calendar" is a *plan* of registry
actions, shown as a plan, approved once, executed as a job.

## 5. TENANT ZERO — THE INTERNAL MARKETING ENGINE

**The law: GO AI EZ is tenant #0 on its own platform.** Not a copy. Not a
staging clone. The same code, the same database, the same modules.

### 5.1 What that means concretely

| We need to… | We use… | Which is also a customer feature |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Find local businesses to sell to | X-16 `MapsHarvester` | Their prospecting |
| Know which ones have bad reviews | `C-Reviews` ⛔ *(was `X-19 ReviewIntel` — §5 repaired 2026-08-27, roster renumbered)* | Their competitor intel |
| Enrich and score them | `X-134 WaterfallEnrichment` ⛔ *(was `X-06`)* | Their lead scoring |
| Reach them | X-105 `InternalSalesAgent` | Their outbound |
| Reach them by form | X-109 `ContactFormScraper` | Their form outreach |
| Show them what they're missing | `X-161` demo/audit ⛔ *(was `C-38`)* | Their lead magnet |
| Let them try it | `X-161 DemoAgent` ⛔ *(was `C-35`)* | Their demo |
| Convert them | X-116 templates + funnels | Their funnels |
| Onboard them | X-118 `AutoPilotOnboarding` | Their onboarding |
| Answer them 24/7 | `C-Agent` ⛔ *(was `C-06`)* | Their agent |
| Bill them | `C-Billing` ⛔ *(was `C-27/C-28`)* | Their billing |
| Keep them | `X-08` + `X-211` dunning ⛔ *(`X-89` struck — no longer in the roster)* | Their retention |
| Prove value | `X-138` ROI/attribution ⛔ *(was `X-09`)* | Their client reporting |
| Publish wins | `X-182` case studies ⛔ *(was `X-38`)* | Their case studies |

**Every row is one build serving two customers.**

### 5.2 The three laws of Tenant Zero

**Law 1 — Nothing is built for marketing alone.** If we need a growth tool, it
ships as a module. There is no marketing codebase.

**Law 2 — If it doesn't work for us, it doesn't ship.** We are the first
production user of every module. A feature that fails to move our own numbers is
a feature with a design problem, and we find out before customers do.

**Law 3 — Our own numbers are the proof.** No invented statistics, ever. Every
claim on the site is a metric from tenant #0's real dashboard, with the metric
definition published. *"Our own AI answered 4,412 calls last month"* is a query,
not a marketing decision.

### 5.3 Why this is worth more than the sum

Three compounding effects:

- **The demo is the product.** A prospect texting the demo number is talking to
  the real agent on a real tenant. It cannot over-promise, because it is the
  thing.
- **Dogfooding is free QA at production scale** across every module, running
  continuously, on the highest-stakes account on the platform.
- **The sales motion is a product feature.** Competitors sell a tool. We sell
  the machine that sold them — and hand it over.

## 5A. THE ONE-BUILD LAW  ⭐ *(owner ruling, T457)*

> **There is no soft launch. There is no Build 1, 2 or 3. One system, built
> whole, launched once.**

This replaces the four-phase model that governed every prior document. It is not
a schedule change — it changes what gets built and how risk is carried.

### 5A.1 What dissolves

| Was | Now |
| :--- | :--- |
| SL → B1 → B2 → B3 | **One release** |
| A `Phase` field on every module | **Deleted.** A module has a dependency wave, not a phase |
| Five site states (PRELAUNCH → SL → B1 → B2 → B3) | **Two:** pre-launch and live |
| B2/B3 scope documents that were never written | **No longer a gap.** There is one scope: everything |
| M-108 *"the phase data does not exist"* | **Dissolved.** No phases, nothing to separate |
| The staggered calendar (Aug 20 → Nov 5) | **Void.** Re-dated from the dependency graph at B1 |
| R18 founder window closing at the B1 flip | **Needs a new trigger — D6** |

### 5A.2 What survives, and why

**Feature flags survive — with a different job.** They were staged reveal; they
are now **blast-radius control.** When 206 modules go live together, a flag is
how you switch one off at 3 a.m. without rolling back the other 205. That makes
flags more important under one-build, not less.

**The versioned-site law survives.** The site still cannot claim what the product
has not shipped — that is the claim law, and it is independent of phasing.

**The doctrine's waves survive untouched.** Waves 0–4 were always *dependency*
ordering, never phase ordering. Spine → channels → assistant → surfaces →
integration. Nothing in the swarm doctrine changes.

### 5A.3 ⛔ THE ONE REAL COST, AND THE FIX

One-build removes the production feedback loop. Under phasing, the review engine
would have been carrying real traffic while the ads module was still being
written. Under one-build, **nothing is live until everything is** — so the first
real user meets 206 modules that have never met a real user.

That also breaks two things this plan depends on: **Tenant Zero as first
production user (§5)** and **shadow-mode rollout (doctrine §6.5)**. Both assumed
something was live to run against.

**The fix, which does not reintroduce phasing:**

> **INTERNAL-LIVE IS NOT A LAUNCH.** GO AI EZ starts running on GOAIEZ in-house
> the moment the spine, channels and agent land — real calls, real numbers, real
> money, one tenant: us. No customers, no announcement, no tiers, no staged
> reveal. **The public launch is still one event, everything at once.**

This is phasing *our own usage*, not the product. It costs nothing, it is
invisible from outside, and it means the 206 modules meet a real user — us —
months before they meet a customer. Every module gets a real-traffic rehearsal
and the shadow-mode mechanism keeps working exactly as specified.

**Without this, one-build means the first person to ever use the system in anger
is a paying customer.** That is the only part of this ruling I would push back
on, and internal-live resolves it completely.

## 7A. THE MERGE DOCTRINE — FIVE SOURCES, ONE PLAN  ⭐ *(T459)*

The design changed. Five bodies of work now describe the same platform, they
overlap, and in places they disagree. **This section is how they become one
document without losing a single feature.**

### 7A.1 The five sources

| # | Source | Size | What it is best at |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1** | **This plan** | 210 modules | **Structure** — the spine, the layers, how anything connects to anything |
| **2** | **The T592 CC slices** | ~130 slices | **Depth** — pixel, SEO, billing, mail, voice at build detail |
| **3** | **The capability register** | 905 lines | **Breadth** — named behaviours inside modules |
| **4** | **The content library** | ~300 docs | **Words** — profiles, copy, help, languages, scripts |
| **5** | **The codebase** | 1,687 files | **Reality** — what already runs |

### 7A.2 ⛔ THE PRECEDENCE LADDER

> **New supersedes legacy on STRUCTURE. Legacy supplies DETAIL wherever the new
> plan is silent. Neither ever deletes the other's features.**

| Question | Answer comes from |
| :--- | :--- |
| How do modules connect? | **This plan** (§3). Legacy seam maps fold in as detail. |
| What does a module *do*? | **The union of all five.** |
| How exactly does it work? | **The CC slices**, then the register, then this plan. |
| What does it say to the user? | **The content library**, verbatim. Never re-author. |
| Does it already exist? | **The codebase.** Extend, don't rebuild. |
| A number, a threshold, a name? | **Newest wins.** Legacy figures are superseded silently. |

### 7A.3 ⭐ THE UNION RULE — NOTHING IS EVER REMOVED

**A feature named in any source enters the plan.** Not "considered." Enters.

Three consequences the swarm has to honour:

1. **Two sources describing one feature merge into the richer version.** Never
   the shorter one, never a summary of both.
2. **Two sources contradicting each other become a setting**, defaulting to the
   newer behaviour — *unless* the contradiction is structural, in which case it
   goes to §7A.7.
3. **A feature nobody can find a home for gets a module number anyway.** An
   orphan with a number survives to the next pass. An orphan without one is
   deleted by accident.

⛔ **"I removed it because it seemed redundant" is not an available move.**
Redundancy is resolved by merging, not by dropping.

### 7A.4 ⭐ THE EXPANSION MANDATE — WHAT "MAKE IT BETTER" MEANS

*Expansion is not adding bullets. It is five specific upgrades applied to every
feature in all 210 modules.* A feature is not finished until all five are
answered.

| Axis | The question | What it produces |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **① AUTOMATE** | Does this still require a human? | Anything the docs describe as *a report*, *a list*, *an audit* or *a recommendation* becomes **a one-click action with the words already written.** Nothing ships as "here is a report, good luck." |
| **② WIRE** | Can the AI do it? | Every feature gets an **action-registry entry** (§3.2) — typed params, a permission, a plain-language preview, reversible or not. If the UI can do it, an action can. |
| **③ CONNECT** | What else does this touch? | Every feature declares **at least one seam** — a producer, a consumer, a direction, and **an invalidation rule** (§3.4). A feature with no seam is a feature nobody benefits from. |
| **④ MEASURE** | Did it work? | Every feature emits an outcome event. **Every recommendation is graded after the fact:** did the fix move the number? Before/after from field data, not from the tool that suggested it. |
| **⑤ EXPLAIN** | Would a five-year-old follow it? | Plain-language preview, plain-language result, plain-language failure. **Grade ≤6 on every tenant-facing string.** |

**Worked example — `SEO A1 robots.txt audit`:**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **As documented** | "Fetch, parse, flag blocked assets and blocked crawlers." |
| **① Automate** | Flag → **one-click fix**, with the corrected file previewed and the change reversible |
| **② Wire** | `seo.robots.audit` · `seo.robots.fix` — the assistant can run both by voice |
| **③ Connect** | Reads the pixel's real page list · writes to the crawl-health record · **invalidates** the index-coverage report the moment the file changes |
| **④ Measure** | Emits `seo.robots.fixed` → 28 days later, did indexed-page count move? Reported either way |
| **⑤ Explain** | *"Your site is telling Google not to look at 34 pages. Two of them are your pricing pages. Fix this?"* |

**That is the difference between a feature and a god-tier feature, and it is
mechanical — the same five questions, 210 times.**

### 7A.5 THE SEO RULE — GOOGLE IS THE SOURCE

> **Where Google has published guidance, Google wins. Where Google is silent, we
> measure. We never ship folk SEO.**

- Every SEO capability carries its **source** — a Google statement, a documented
  API behaviour, or our own measured result with its date.
- The legacy docs already do this correctly and should be followed: the EXIF
  geotag question was settled by citing Google's own people rather than by
  opinion, and the conclusion — *strip it* — is what ships.
- **Where a capability rests on our own measurement, it says so and shows the
  date.** A claim with no source does not go on a page.

⭐ **This is also the strongest version of the feature.** "We follow Google's
published guidance and show you the source" is a better product than any
contrarian trick, and it never goes stale the way a trick does.

### 7A.6 THE MODULE TEMPLATE — the shape that makes the union provable

Every one of the 210 modules is written to this exact shape. **A slot left empty
is a visible gap, which is the point.**

```
X-nnn  <Name>
──────────────────────────────────────────────
WHAT IT DOES        one sentence, plain
SOURCES             which of the five, cited by file
CAPABILITIES        the union — every named behaviour, from every source
ENTITIES            consumed / produced        (§3.1)
ACTIONS EXPOSED     id · params · permission · preview · reversible   (§3.2)
ACTIONS CALLED      what it invokes elsewhere
EVENTS EMITTED      typed                      (§3.3)
EVENTS SUBSCRIBED   typed
SEAMS               owner · direction · INVALIDATION RULE   (§3.4)
SURFACES            where a human sees it
CONTENT             which library docs supply its words
MEASURES            what outcome it emits, how it is graded
DEPENDS ON          modules that must exist first
BUILD NOTE          extend existing code, or new
```

**The template is the union rule made mechanical.** Fourteen slots per module ×
210 modules — and any source's contribution has a slot to land in, so nothing
falls out during the merge.

### 7A.7 THE CONFLICT PROCEDURE

Most conflicts resolve themselves at §7A.3. The rest:

| Conflict type | Resolution |
| :--- | :--- |
| Two names for one thing | Newest name, older kept as an alias |
| Two numbers/thresholds | Newest wins, silently |
| Two mechanisms, same outcome | **Both, behind a setting.** Default = newer |
| Two mechanisms, incompatible structure | ⛔ **Escalate to Matt.** Do not pick. |
| A legacy feature the new plan omitted | **The legacy feature is right.** Add it. |
| A new feature legacy contradicts | **The new feature is right.** Keep both if they can coexist. |

⛔ **Only structural incompatibility escalates.** Everything else has a rule, so
the merge does not stall on judgment calls.



---

## 7B. THE CONTENT ARCHITECTURE — ~300 DOCUMENTS, AND WHERE THEY GO  ⭐ *(T460)*

### 7B.1 ⛔ The rule that keeps the plan loadable

> **Content is DATA. It never lives in the master plan.**

The master plan carries, per content set: **its shape · which module renders it ·
which seeder loads it · where the file is.** Four facts. Not the words.

A hundred industry profiles is ~800 price rows and ~600 FAQ answers. Pasted into
this document it would make the plan unreadable and unloadable — the exact defect
that made the 349-file corpus useless to an agent. **The seeder reads the content
files. Antigravity reads the plan.**

### 7B.2 The content register

| Set | Volume | Shape | Rendered by | Seeded from |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Industry profiles** | 100 · ~800 prices · ~600 FAQ · 100 tone seeds | `industry_profiles` + `profile_prices` + `profile_faqs` | X-107 · X-37 · C-35 | `content/profiles/` |
| **Page templates** | 200 industries | Block JSON matching the builder's state engine | X-116 · X-103 | `content/templates/` |
| **Help articles** | 132 | `help_articles` — one row, three renders | X-11 · C-40 · the agent | `content/help/` |
| **Language packs** | 31 locales · 3 encoding classes | `lang/{locale}` catalogs | every surface | `content/lang/` |
| **Site page decks** | 7 pages, v2 versions | Section blocks bound to flags | X-103 · the site | `content/site/` |
| **App screen copy** | 10 screens documented, the rest to inventory | `lang/en` keys, never Blade literals | every Livewire screen | `content/app/` |
| **Doc packs** | 6 families × 5 docs | **A document is a VIEW of registry data**, re-rendered, never hand-edited | X-107 | `content/docs/` |
| **Lifecycle sets** | Email + SMS ladders | `message_templates` | X-68 · C-23 | `content/lifecycle/` |
| **Video scripts** | 6 × ≤90s | Scripts + captions | X-114 | `content/video/` |
| **Demo transcripts + QR set** | Per family | Demo seed data | C-35 | `content/demo/` |
| **Legal** | ⛔ **NONE** | Empty slots, admin upload | X-133 | *(nothing ships)* |

### 7B.3 The three content laws

1. **Never re-author.** If a document exists, it is the source. The plan cites
   the path; the seeder parses it.
2. **A document is a view.** Doc packs, help cards and price sheets re-render
   from registries. **Nothing is a hand-edited file that can drift from the data.**
3. **One row, many renders.** A help article is the in-app "?", the site help
   page, and something the agent knows — from one row. Same for a price, a
   profile, a template.

### 7B.4 Where content becomes a feature

Content sets are not passive. Each one wires into the spine like any other module:

- **The help registry generates itself from the action registry** — a help card
  is a rendered view of an action's `label`, `preview` and params (§3.2). 1,600
  actions, always current, structurally unable to drift.
- **Profiles ground the agent** from minute one and seed the demo.
- **Templates feed the builder** and the 200 industry pages.
- **The inbox writes content** — FAQ blocks and GBP Q&A come from real questions
  customers asked (the conversation loop).


---

## 7C. THE VERIFICATION TRACK — ASSUME NOTHING WORKS  ⭐ *(owner ruling, T460)*

> **Every module is planned as if it does not exist. Every module is built as if
> what exists is wrong until proven otherwise.**

### 7C.1 What this replaces

The plan previously treated `C-01…C-78` as built, extension only. **That
assumption is withdrawn.** 1,687 files and 225,640 lines are now *unverified* —
not condemned, not trusted.

The justification is on the record: the five-starters class passed every test
while four features did not run at all, because **a test supplies its own input.**
Green tests over a system that cannot run is the failure mode this track exists
to catch.

### 7C.2 The 15th template slot

Every module spec gains a **VERIFY** slot:

```
VERIFY   the file(s) that should already implement this
         what "correct" looks like, as an assertion
         the runtime proof — a real artifact, not a test double
         verdict: MATCHES · PARTIAL · ABSENT · WRONG
```

**Four verdicts, four different jobs.** `MATCHES` costs nothing. `PARTIAL` is an
extension. `ABSENT` is a build. **`WRONG` is the expensive one and the reason
this track exists** — code that runs, passes, and does the wrong thing.

### 7C.3 The systemic sweeps — what no single module owns

Per-module verification cannot find an absent *connection*. Six sweeps do, each
covering 100% of a dimension with a denominator so "done" is provable:

| Sweep | Denominator | Finds |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **V2 Entry points** | routes · jobs · commands · events | Anything with no runner — the five-starters class |
| **V3 Writers & readers** | 122 models · 131 tables | A table written by nobody, or read by nobody |
| **V4 Screens → services** | 48 Livewire components, **never audited** | Every screen a tenant touches |
| **V5 The money paths** | ledger · gateways · webhooks | Pairs with the billing spec |
| **V6 Cross-module promises** | every seam in §3.4 | **The sweep that would have found the five starters directly** |

Plus **V1**, which sets the method: **every sweep runs two passes.** Pass 1 asks
the naive question and produces candidates. Pass 2 enumerates every legitimate
reason a candidate could be false and subtracts each. Nothing is reported until
pass 2 has run — a pilot found 182 "unreachable" enum cases and pass 2 reduced it
to zero; all 182 were the instrument.

⭐ **A sweep that finds nothing and proves it is a good result.** *"659 cases, all
reachable"* is stronger than any finding.

### 7C.4 Why this is folded into the build, not run after it

A separate audit produces findings that wait. **Findings that wait get restated
instead of fixed** — fifty turns of history say so. Verification is a slot in
every module and a phase before the build order, so a defect is found by the
person about to build on top of it.



---

## 7D. THE BENCHMARK LAW  ⭐ *(T461 — from the market research)*

> **Every module carries the market leader's number, and ours has to beat it.**
> A module spec without a benchmark row is not finished.

The research established what the category leaders actually ship in 2026. These
are the numbers to clear — a 16th template slot, `BENCHMARK`.

| Domain | Leader | Their number | GOAIEZ target |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Enrichment coverage** | Clay (150+ providers, waterfall) | 30% single-provider → **80–90%** waterfall | **≥85% email coverage, <5% bounce** |
| **Contact database** | Apollo 270M / ZoomInfo 321M | ~90-day refresh; ~3%/month decay | Refresh cadence beats 90 days on active records |
| **Person-level visitor ID** | RB2B / Warmly | **5–20%** (US, LinkedIn-dependent) | Match it, and **beat it on what happens next** |
| **Company-level visitor ID** | Leadfeeder / Dealfront | **30–65%** (global) | ≥55%, global |
| **Voice latency** | Retell | **~600ms p50** | **≤600ms p50** |
| **Voice cost** | Retell $0.07 · Vapi $0.05+ · Bland $0.09 | $0.07–0.15/min all-in | **≤$0.10/min all-in** |
| **AI agent resolution** | Fin ~76% claimed / 38–72% observed | $0.99 per resolution | Publish our real rate, not the claim |
| **Review response time** | Birdeye / Podium AI | 8–10 min → **2–3 min** | **Under 60 seconds, automatic** |
| **Review volume lift** | Birdeye | **3× in 90 days** (vendor claim) | Measure ours on tenant zero and publish |
| **Local pack weight** | Whitespark 2026 survey | GBP ~32% · reviews ~20% · on-page ~15% | Instrument all three, weekly |
| **Geo-grid tracking** | Local Falcon (225 points) | Agency reports **monthly** | **Weekly**, automatic, with delta overlays |
| **AEO tracking** | Profound $399/mo for 3 engines | Weekly citation scans | **Included**, 5+ engines, verbatim answers kept with dates |
| **Core Web Vitals** | Lab tools (Lighthouse) | Synthetic, not field | **Field data from our own tag**, 28-day rolling, same basis Google uses |
| **MCP surface** | Salesforce · HubSpot · Klaviyo · Braze · Apollo · Clay | Read-mostly servers | **Full read/write over all ~1,600 actions** |
| **AI agent pricing** | Intercom Fin $0.99/outcome | Per-outcome | Per-outcome option on the rate registry |

⚠️ **Caveat carried from the research:** the local-pack weights are practitioner
survey estimates, not Google-published figures — Google states only relevance,
distance and prominence. Vendor match rates and coverage claims are
self-reported. **Validate every number on tenant zero before it appears on a
page** (the claim law, §7A.5).

---

## 7E. THE PER-MODULE RESEARCH RULE  ⭐ *(T461)*

> **Every module turn opens with targeted research on that domain's current
> state, before a line of spec is written.**

The market research proved the value: it surfaced twelve modules the plan did not
have, and a benchmark for nearly every module it already had. A domain researched
at the moment it is specced produces a better spec than one written from the
2026 general picture.

**Per M-turn:** current leaders · what they ship · their numbers · what they
*don't* do. Findings land in the module's `BENCHMARK` and `CAPABILITIES` slots.

---

## 7F. THE TWELVE MODULES THE RESEARCH ADDED  ⭐ *(X-134 … X-145)*

### The data layer the plan was missing

**X-134 `WaterfallEnrichment`** — the Clay pattern, properly. 5–15 providers
ranked per field; try provider 1, fall to 2 only on miss or quality-check
failure; **charge credits only on usable returns**; per-field confidence and
provenance; "run only if column is empty"; verification gate before the golden
record lands. *Lifts coverage from ~30% to 80–90%. The waterfall is a living
config — hit rates get reviewed monthly.*

**X-135 `ResearchAgent`** — the Claygent equivalent. LLM-driven web research on a
prospect answering arbitrary questions: *"Is this B2B or B2C?" "What problems is
this company solving, based on its job listings?" "Infer pricing strategy from
the pricing page."* Tiered models by cost/depth. Conditional runs so it only
fires where it pays.

**X-136 `SignalEngine`** — job changes, funding, hiring velocity, tech stack,
new locations, in-market topics, **review gaps**. ⚠️ *Research finding worth
heeding: generic signals (funding, basic job changes) are now commodity — they
reach thousands of senders simultaneously. Our edge is the signals only we have:
call transcripts, review sentiment, geo-grid movement, page-level intent.*

### ⭐ The closed loop — the flagship gap

**X-137 `CallTracking` (DNI)** — dynamic number insertion. Swap the displayed
number per visitor so a phone call carries its source, campaign, keyword and
landing page. **This was missing from the plan entirely and it is the join that
makes attribution possible.**

**X-138 `AttributionGraph`** — ⭐ **the flagship.** Page → call → job → invoice →
revenue, in one graph. Research verdict: CallRail does DNI plus call
attribution; GoHighLevel connects calls to appointments and pipeline; **nobody
unifies visitor identity + DNI + booking + invoice + review + ad platform into a
single revenue graph.** Target: every booked job traceable to its originating
page, keyword and call.

**X-139 `OfflineConversionSync`** — push the completed job back to Google and
Meta as an offline conversion. *This is what makes a tenant's ad spend actually
optimise, and almost no SMB tool does it.*

### The three unshipped ideas

**X-140 `ConversationToContent`** — every call transcript, review and chat is
first-party corpus nobody mines. Feed it to generate and refresh website copy,
FAQ blocks, GBP Q&A and schema. **Technically trivial — the transcripts already
exist** — and it closes the conversation loop the SEO system already described.

**X-141 `ReplaySimulator`** — replay a tenant's real history against a *changed*
configuration. *"What would last quarter have looked like if review invites had
been on?"* Real modules, real historical events, real number. Falls out of the
event bus (§3.3). Klaviyo has agent simulations; **nobody offers counterfactual
replay of actual history.**

### The agentic surface

**X-142 `McpServer`** — the action registry (§3.2) exposed as MCP. Salesforce,
HubSpot, Klaviyo, Braze, Apollo, ZoomInfo and Clay all ship one; theirs are
mostly read-only. **Ours is full read/write over ~1,600 actions**, because the
registry was built for it from day one.

**X-143 `WebMcpToolContracts`** — `navigator.modelContext`. Tenant sites publish
tool contracts so a visitor's own browser agent can book, quote or enquire
directly. W3C draft (Google + Microsoft), Chrome origin trial. Declarative form
attributes plus `registerTool()`, and `agent.requestUserInteraction()` for
confirmation on sensitive actions. **Nobody in the SMB category has this.**

**X-144 `AiVisibilityTracker`** — AEO as a product, not a checkbox. Ask the
assistants the queries that matter on a schedule, across ChatGPT, Perplexity,
Google AI Mode, Claude, Gemini and Copilot; record whether the business is named,
**keep the answer verbatim with its date**; citation frequency, share of voice,
position, sentiment. *Profound charges $399/mo for three engines. We include it.*

**X-145 `DecisioningStudio`** — per-contact next-best-action learned from
outcomes rather than authored as rules (the Braze/OfferFit shape). Sits on the
action registry, so anything the platform can do is a candidate action.

### Folded in rather than given numbers

**Audit cards** — every AI action logged with timestamp, properties changed and
**previous values** (the HubSpot pattern) → **X-126 `CapabilityGate`**.
**Approve-then-autonomize** — approve each action while trust is built, then let
it run → **X-124**. **Per-outcome pricing** → the rate registry at M12a.
**Branch-based safe iteration** (Framer) → **X-103**. **Crawl-and-rebuild
migration**, which no builder ships → **X-129**, already in the plan.

**The twelve nouns every one of the 223 modules speaks.** Get these right and a
module is a week; get them wrong and every module invents its own and none of
them connect. This is the reason wave 0 runs alone.

## 11.1 THE TWELVE

| # | Entity | One line | Owner module |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **E1** | `Business` | A tenant | C-Tenant |
| **E2** | `Location` | A place or service area a Business operates | X-53 geography |
| **E3** | `Person` | ⭐ Anyone — anonymous visitor through paying customer, **one record, one state machine** | X-132 PersonGraph |
| **E4** | `Visit` | One session on a tenant surface | X-110 pixel |
| **E5** | `Conversation` | A thread on any channel, voice included | C-Conversations |
| **E6** | `Message` | One inbound or outbound unit inside a Conversation | C-Messaging |
| **E7** | `Job` | Booked, performed, or completed work | X-108 scheduler |
| **E8** | `Review` | A review on any destination | C-Reviews |
| **E9** | `Campaign` | An orchestrated sequence | C-Campaigns |
| **E10** | `Asset` | Page, template, image, video, document | X-103 builder |
| **E11** | `LedgerEntry` | Any credit or money movement | C-Billing |

## 11.2 ⭐ E3 `Person` — THE ONE-RECORD DECISION

**This supersedes the earlier `prospects` / `customers` two-table design.**

*Why the change (§7A.2 — new supersedes legacy on structure):* two tables means
two records for the same human the moment a researched prospect calls in, and
then a sync problem forever. The identity waterfall, the pixel's person graph and
the CRM all need to converge on one row. **The lane router reads a state field
just as easily as it reads a table name — and the state field is the one that
doesn't drift.**

### The state machine

```
  ANONYMOUS ──► IDENTIFIED ──► PROSPECT ──► CONTACT ──► CUSTOMER
      │              │              │            │           │
      │              │              │            │           └─► past customer
      │              │              │            └─► reachable, has a relationship
      │              │              └─► researched, no relationship yet
      │              └─► we know who, by pixel or enrichment
      └─► a visit with no identity
```

**Transitions are one-directional except `CUSTOMER → past customer`.** A Person
never falls back a state; history is additive.

⭐ **The transition that matters: `PROSPECT → CONTACT` happens only by the
person's own act** — they called, texted, submitted a form, replied, or bought.
Never by import, never by enrichment, never by a pixel match. That single rule is
what keeps every downstream lane honest without a gate anywhere.

### Shape

```
Person
  id                    ULID
  business_id           → E1        (tenant scope)
  state                 enum        anonymous|identified|prospect|contact|customer|past
  state_changed_at      timestamp
  state_reason          string      what caused the last transition
  first_seen_at         timestamp
  last_seen_at          timestamp

  identity              PersonIdentity[]      ⭐ per-field, see 11.3
  attributes            typed bag             (§11.9)
  tags                  string[]
  do_not_pitch          bool                  tenant's own suppression, tenant-scoped

  -- derived, recomputed, never authored
  stage                 enum      browsing|comparing|ready      (from page classes)
  return_velocity       float
  abandon_point         string    the field they quit at
  in_market_categories  {category: age_bucket}[]
  channel_fit           enum      text|email|voice|unknown
  best_contact_window   timerange
```

### ⭐ 11.3 `PersonIdentity` — the waterfall, stored

The Clay/Apollo pattern applied to identity: **one row per field per source, with
confidence and provenance.** Never a flat `email` column that silently overwrites.

```
PersonIdentity
  person_id       → E3
  field           enum      email|phone|name|company|title|linkedin|address
  value           string
  source          string    provider name, pixel, form, call, import, tenant-entered
  confidence      0.00-1.00
  observed_at     timestamp
  verified_at     timestamp|null
  superseded_by   → PersonIdentity|null
```

**The current value of a field is the highest-confidence unsuperseded row.**
Consequences that fall out for free:

- A tenant-entered value outranks any provider, because tenant-entered ships at
  confidence 1.00.
- **You can always answer "where did this email come from and when?"** — which is
  what makes the waterfall auditable and the enrichment spend reviewable.
- Re-enrichment writes a new row; it never destroys what was there.
- The six-tier waterfall (`CC-32C`) is a `source` ordering, not new machinery.

---

## 11.4 E4 `Visit` — the pixel's spine

```
Visit
  id · business_id · person_id (nullable — anonymous visits are normal)
  started_at · ended_at · duration
  entry_asset_id → E10 · exit_asset_id → E10
  referrer · utm{source,medium,campaign,term,content}
  device · browser · os · viewport
  ip_org             company resolved from IP (30-65% expected, §7D)
  geo                city/region, coarse
  events             VisitEvent[]         ⭐ the 16 published types
  web_vitals         {lcp, inp, cls, ttfb}   ← field data, the §7D benchmark
  page_classes       string[]             home|pricing|service|blog|contact|checkout
  ⭐ call_token       string|null          the DNI number shown this visit (E-X137)
```

**`call_token` is the join.** It is the one field that turns a phone call back
into a page, a keyword and a campaign — the thing §7F said the plan was missing.

---

## 11.5 E5/E6 `Conversation` and `Message`

```
Conversation
  id · business_id · person_id
  channel        enum   sms|mms|whatsapp|email|webchat|voice|social_dm
  direction      enum   inbound|outbound|mixed
  state          enum   open|awaiting|human_takeover|closed
  assigned_to    → user|null
  originating_visit_id → E4|null     ⭐ closes web → conversation
  originating_call_token string|null
  summary · sentiment · intent · topics[]

Message
  id · conversation_id · person_id
  direction · sent_at · delivered_at · read_at
  body · media[] · encoding_class      (GSM|UCS-2, from the language packs)
  actor          enum   customer|agent_ai|human|system
  actor_user_id  → user|null           ⭐ human takeover is attributable
  transcript     text|null             voice only
  recording_url  string|null
  cost_units     int                   what it debited
```

**A voice call is a Conversation with `channel=voice`** whose Messages are turns
with transcripts. One inbox, one thread model, no second system for calls.

---

## 11.6 E7 `Job` — the revenue join

```
Job
  id · business_id · location_id · person_id
  state       enum  quoted|booked|confirmed|in_progress|completed|cancelled|no_show
  service · description
  scheduled_for · window · duration · assigned_to
  quoted_amount_minor · final_amount_minor · currency
  invoice_id · paid_at

  ⭐ attribution
    originating_visit_id      → E4
    originating_conversation_id → E5
    originating_call_token    string
    originating_asset_id      → E10     the page that produced it
    originating_campaign_id   → E9
```

**Those five fields are `X-138 AttributionGraph`.** Page → call → job → invoice →
revenue is not a pipeline to build; it is a query over `Job` once these are
populated. That is why they live on the canonical entity and not in a reporting
table.

**All money in minor units, integer, never a float.**

## 11.7 E10 `Asset` — one noun, five shapes

```
Asset
  id · business_id · location_id|null
  type        enum  page|template|image|video|document|post
  state       enum  draft|published|unpublished|archived
  version     int                    ⭐ increments on every publish
  url · slug · title · meta{}
  blocks      json                   builder block state (X-103/X-116)
  content     text
  schema_ld   json                   structured data
  rendered_from → registry|null      ⭐ "a document is a VIEW", §7B.3

  -- SEO state, one place
  indexed · canonical_of · click_depth · internal_links_in/out
  vitals{lcp,inp,cls}  ← from E4, real visitors not lab
  earns_calls   int    ⭐ how many Jobs trace to this Asset
```

⭐ **`earns_calls` is the SEO report that matters** — not rank, but which page
produced a booked job. It is a denormalised count off E7's attribution fields.

---

## 11.8 ⭐ E12 `Fact` — WHERE THE INVALIDATION RULE LIVES

The best thing in the T592 harvest was the observation that two correct modules
plus no written join is where every bug lives — *a page publishes a price, the AI
learns it, the tenant raises the price, and the AI is still quoting last month's
number on the phone.*

**`Fact` is the entity that makes that impossible.**

```
Fact
  id · business_id
  subject          what it is about       service|price|hour|policy|person|place
  predicate · value
  source_type      enum  asset|registry|conversation|tenant_entered|profile
  source_id        → the row it came from
  ⭐ source_version int   the version of that row when the fact was minted
  valid_from · valid_until|null
  confidence
  spoken_by        enum[]  agent|voice|chat|reply     where it may be used
```

### The three rules

1. **A Fact is minted with its source's version.** When the source's `version`
   increments, every Fact carrying the old version is invalidated **in the same
   transaction** — never a job, never a queue that can lag.
2. **Unpublish removes; it does not orphan.** A deleted Asset takes its Facts
   with it, because a fact with nothing left to correct it is worse than no fact.
3. ⭐ **Prices never travel as text.** A price Fact carries a *reference* to the
   canonical price row, not a copied number. The AI reads the row; the page
   renders the same row. **A page is never the source of a number the AI will
   say out loud.**

---

## 11.9 THE EXTENSION MECHANISM

⛔ **No module may create a private table for anything in §11.1.** Extension is a
typed attribute bag on the canonical entity:

```
Attribute
  entity_type · entity_id
  namespace       the owning module, e.g. "seo" | "pixel" | "billing"
  key · value · type    string|int|decimal|bool|date|json
  set_by · set_at
```

**Namespaced by module, so two modules cannot collide on `status`.** Promotion
path: an attribute used by three or more modules is a candidate for a real column
at the next spine revision — that is how the graph grows without a committee.

---

## 11.10 TENANCY

Every entity except `Business` carries `business_id`. Enforcement is unchanged
from what the audit found already working — the double wall:

1. **Row-level security** on every table, `FORCE`d, so the database refuses
   cross-tenant reads even if application code forgets.
2. **Application scope** via a global scope on every model, with `idOrFail`
   semantics: **a query that cannot resolve a tenant fails rather than returning
   everything.**

⛔ **Set together or not at all.** The audit's finding stands: the two walls
drift apart when they can be added independently, so a new table lands with both
or the build fails.

**RLS-exempt tables must carry a written argument** in the migration. There are
19 today, every one argued.

---

## 11.11 IDs, TIME AND MONEY

- **ULID** everywhere. Sortable by creation, safe to generate client-side, no
  sequence contention across 60 build agents or across shards.
- **All timestamps UTC**, with the tenant's zone on `Business` and `Location`.
  Recipient-local windows resolve at send time from `Location`, never from a
  cached offset.
- **Money in integer minor units** with an explicit currency. No floats anywhere
  in the graph.
- **Soft deletes on E3, E7, E8, E10** — the entities a tenant can undo. Hard
  delete only on request.

---

## 11.12 WHAT THIS BUYS THE OTHER 222 MODULES

| Because | You get, free |
| :--- | :--- |
| One `Person` with a state machine | No prospect/customer sync. The lane router is one field read. |
| `PersonIdentity` per field | The waterfall is auditable and re-runnable; spend is reviewable |
| `Visit.call_token` | Phone calls join back to pages and keywords |
| `Job`'s five attribution fields | **The closed loop is a query, not a pipeline** |
| `Asset.version` + `Fact.source_version` | The AI cannot quote a stale price |
| `Asset.earns_calls` | The SEO report nobody else can produce |
| One `Conversation` for voice and text | One inbox, no second system for calls |
| Namespaced attributes | 223 modules extend without colliding or forking |

---

## 11.13 ACCEPTANCE — S1 IS DONE WHEN

☐ Twelve entities, each with schema, owner module and tenancy
☐ `Person` state machine with one-directional transitions and the own-act rule
☐ `PersonIdentity` waterfall with confidence, provenance and supersession
☐ Attribution fields present on `Visit`, `Conversation`, `Job`, `Asset`
☐ `Fact` with `source_version` and the same-transaction invalidation rule
☐ Extension mechanism namespaced by module
☐ Double-wall tenancy, set-together
☐ ULID · UTC · minor units · soft deletes named

**All eight ✅ — S1 EXECUTED.**

**S2 consumes this directly:** every action in the registry takes and returns
these twelve nouns, and nothing else.

## 11.14 ⭐ X-146 `ComplianceRegisters` *(owner ruling T462 — logged as a feature)*

Third-party list providers as a **pluggable integration**, exactly like any other
provider in the platform.

```
TenantRegister
  business_id · register_type    (provider-defined, open set)
  enabled          bool     ⭐ DEFAULT FALSE
  provider         string   the tenant's chosen vendor
  credential_ref   → the existing encrypted credential store
  loaded_at · last_error · row_count
```

- **Off by default. Not enabled → never consulted → affects nothing.** A tenant
  who never turns one on is indistinguishable from a platform that never had the
  feature.
- **The tenant brings their own provider and their own credentials.** We
  integrate the API; we do not resell the data.
- **Or they build their own internal list workflow** — an internal list is just a
  register with `provider = internal`, fed by whatever workflow they build on the
  automation canvas (X-125).
- Rotate, replace and revoke from the tenant's own screen. **Turning a register
  off stops using the credential** — off means off, not kept warm.
- Enabling or disabling is written to the activity log with actor and timestamp.

**Phase:** M12b · **Depends on:** X-125, the credential store · **Benchmark:**
nobody in the SMB category offers bring-your-own-provider registers at all.

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §12 · X-122 — THE ACTION REGISTRY  ⭐ *(S2 · EXECUTED T463)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

> **⛔ FIRST-PASS SHAPE — PRECEDENCE (T667, §0.A):** first-pass action registry; current §157. *Nothing here is deleted (law 10); read §0.A before treating this section as current.*

**One artifact, six surfaces.** Every capability of the platform is declared once
as an action. That single declaration becomes the API, the MCP server, the
assistant's tool list, the automation canvas palette, the Zapier actions, and the
help library — and none of them can drift from the code, because none of them are
written separately.

> ⛔ **THE LAW: if the UI can do it, an action can do it.**
> A button with no action behind it is a bug, not a design choice. This is the
> single rule that makes the assistant complete instead of half-working.

---

## 12.1 THE MANIFEST

```yaml
action:
  id:            reviews.invite.send            # module.object.verb
  version:       2                              # breaking change ⇒ new version
  module:        C-Reviews
  label:         "Send a review invite"         # ⑤ EXPLAIN
  summary:       "Asks a customer for a review on Google or another destination."

  params:
    person_id:     {type: Person, required: true}
    destination:   {type: enum[google,facebook,yelp], default: google}
    delay_hours:   {type: int, default: 0, max: 336}
    template_id:   {type: Asset, required: false}

  returns:
    invite_id:     {type: ulid}
    scheduled_for: {type: datetime}

  reads:         [Person, Job, Asset]           # ③ CONNECT — E-numbers, §11
  writes:        [Message, LedgerEntry]
  emits:         [review.invite.sent]           # ③ into the event bus, §13
  calls:         [sms.message.send]             # actions it invokes

  permission:    reviews.write
  reversal:      reversible                     # see 12.4
  inverse:       reviews.invite.cancel
  idempotent:    true

  preview:       "Ask {person.first_name} for a {destination} review{delay_phrase}."
  explain_result:"Sent. {person.first_name} will get a text in {delay_phrase}."
  explain_refusal:"{reason_in_plain_words}"

  outcome_event: review.received                # ④ MEASURE — what success looks like
  outcome_window: 14d
  cost_units:    1

  surfaces:      [api, mcp, assistant, canvas, zapier, help]
  benchmark:     "Birdeye: 3× volume in 90 days (vendor claim)."   # §7D
```

**Every field is required.** A manifest missing `preview`, `outcome_event`,
`emits` or `benchmark` fails the build — because those four are the five
expansion axes (§7A.4) made mechanical, and an action without them is a feature
that hasn't been upgraded yet.

---

## 12.2 NAMING — `module.object.verb`

⭐ **A closed verb set.** Consistency is not tidiness here — it is what lets an
assistant generalise from ten actions it has seen to the one it hasn't.

| Verb | Meaning | Reversal class |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `get` · `list` · `search` | read | *n/a* |
| `create` · `update` · `delete` | CRUD on an entity | reversible |
| `send` | dispatch a message | **compensable** |
| `schedule` · `cancel` | time-shifted work | reversible |
| `start` · `pause` · `resume` · `stop` | long-running state | reversible |
| `enable` · `disable` · `configure` | settings | reversible |
| `run` · `check` · `audit` · `scan` | analysis, read-only | *n/a* |
| `fix` · `apply` · `publish` · `unpublish` | ⭐ the automate axis | reversible |
| `charge` · `refund` · `credit` | money | **terminal** |
| `assign` · `tag` · `link` · `merge` | relationships | reversible |

⛔ **A new verb requires the Contract Warden's approval** (W6, §9). Thirty verbs
across 1,600 actions is learnable; a hundred is not.

### 12.3 THE NAMESPACE MAP — ~1,640 actions

| Namespace | Modules | Actions | Shape |
| :--- | :--- | ---: | :--- |
| `person.*` `visit.*` | E3, E4, X-132 | ~70 | identity, state, merge, enrich, timeline |
| `conversation.*` `message.*` | C-Conversations, C-Messaging | ~90 | send, takeover, assign, summarise, search |
| `voice.*` | X-66, CC-29 | ~60 | call, transfer, book, record, transcribe |
| `sms.*` `email.*` `whatsapp.*` `chat.*` | C-Sms, C-Mail | ~110 | send, template, schedule, thread |

| `review.*` `reputation.*` | C-Reviews, X-57 | ~70 | invite, reply, route, syndicate, widget |
| `seo.*` `gbp.*` `aeo.*` | X-26…X-40, CC-35–82 | **~240** | the 111 capabilities × audit/fix/track |
| `pixel.*` `intent.*` | X-110, X-13, CC-30–34 | ~130 | tag, identify, alert, panel, vitals |

| `campaign.*` `sequence.*` `automation.*` | C-Campaigns, X-68, X-125 | ~120 | build, launch, branch, wait, measure |

| **TOTAL** | **224 modules** | **≈1,640** | |

**Average ~7.3 actions per module.** A module with two actions is under-specified;
one with thirty is probably two modules.

---

## 12.4 ⭐ REVERSAL — THREE CLASSES, NOT A BOOLEAN

A boolean `reversible` is a lie for most of what this platform does. Three
classes, and the class decides the confirmation behaviour:

| Class | Meaning | Confirmation | Undo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`reversible`** | An inverse action exists and fully restores prior state | none — just do it | ⭐ **one tap**, calls `inverse` |
| **`compensable`** | Cannot be undone; can be offset | preview shown, one tap to proceed | offer the compensating action *(a sent text can't be unsent — a correction can be sent)* |
| **`terminal`** | Irreversible, external, or moves money | ⛔ **explicit confirmation, always** | none — say so plainly |

⭐ **This is what "the assistant asks" means concretely (D5).** It is not a global
setting; it is a property of each action. Autopilot may be granted per-tenant over
`reversible` actions only — never `terminal`, and `compensable` only with the
tenant's explicit opt-in per action family.

---

## 12.5 RETRIEVAL — FINDING ONE ACTION IN 1,640

You cannot put 1,640 tool schemas in a context window. **Two stages:**

**① Narrow.** Semantic search over `label` + `summary` + `id`, filtered by:
- the actor's permissions — an action they cannot run is never a candidate
- the entity in context — ⭐ if the user is looking at a `Person`, actions taking
  `Person` rank first
- the module's enabled state on this tenant

**② Load.** Full schemas for the top 5–10 only. The assistant sees a handful of
precise tools, not a catalogue.

**Multi-step** requests resolve to a **plan** — an ordered list of invocations
with each step's preview rendered — shown once, approved once, executed as a job.
*"Find everyone who got a quote and never booked, text them a 10% offer, and put
anyone who replies on my calendar"* is three actions and one approval.

---

## 12.6 THE EXECUTOR

```
ActionInvocation
  id · business_id · action_id · action_version
  actor_type      user|assistant|automation|api|mcp|webmcp|system
  actor_id · on_behalf_of
  params_resolved   json
  preview_shown     string        ⭐ exactly what the human was told
  approved_at · approved_by
  idempotency_key   string
  state             pending|running|succeeded|refused|failed|reversed
  refusal_reason    string|null
  result            json
  ⭐ before · after  json         the changed fields, prior values kept
  reversed_by       → ActionInvocation|null
  duration_ms · cost_units
  outcome_observed  json|null     ⭐ filled in when outcome_event fires
```

**One record does five jobs:**

- **The audit card** — timestamp, what changed, previous values *(the HubSpot
  pattern, §7F)*
- **Undo** — `before` is the restore payload
- **The activity feed** the tenant reads
- **⭐ Attribution** — every action is joined to its `Person`, `Job` and `Asset`,
  so ROI is a query over invocations, not a separate pipeline
- **⭐ The measure axis** — `outcome_observed` closes the loop: *did the fix move
  the number?* Reported either way, which is what §7A.4 ④ demands

**Idempotency is mandatory** on every non-read action. Agents retry; a retry must
not send twice.

---

## 12.7 THE SIX SURFACES — ONE MANIFEST, GENERATED

| Surface | Generated how | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **REST API** | `id` → route, `params` → validation, `returns` → response | versioned by `version` |
| **MCP server** *(X-142)* | manifest → MCP tool schema, 1:1 | ⭐ **full read/write**; the leaders ship read-mostly (§7D) |
| **Assistant tools** *(X-124)* | retrieval per 12.5 | `preview` before, `explain_result` after |
| **Automation canvas** *(X-125)* | each action is a node; `params` are its inputs, `returns` its outputs | ⭐ **the canvas and the assistant run the same actions** — no second engine |
| **Zapier / Make** *(X-99)* | actions marked `surfaces: [zapier]` | one app, every action |
| **⭐ Help library** *(X-11)* | `label` + `summary` + `params` + `preview` → a help card | see 12.8 |

**WebMCP** *(X-143)* is a seventh for tenant sites: a subset marked
`surfaces: [webmcp]` becomes `navigator.modelContext` tool contracts, so a
visitor's own browser agent can book or enquire directly.

### 12.8 ⭐ THE HELP LIBRARY WRITES ITSELF

A help card is a rendered view of an action manifest. **1,640 actions, 1,640 help
cards, always current, structurally unable to drift** — because there is no
second document to fall behind.

The 132 hand-written help articles from the harvest are not discarded (§7A.3,
nothing is removed): they become the **narrative layer** — *why* and *when* —
sitting above the generated *what* and *how*. Authored where judgement is needed,
generated where accuracy is needed.

⭐ And the assistant can **show instead of tell**: asked *"how do I turn on review
invites?"*, it renders the actual action with params filled and a preview, one tap
from running. Support and product collapse into the same surface.

---

## 12.9 VERSIONING AND OWNERSHIP

- **Additive changes** — a new optional param, a new return field — keep the
  version.
- **Breaking changes** — removing a param, changing a type, changing semantics —
  **mint a new version.** Both run until the old one's deprecation date.
- ⛔ **Never repurpose an id.** `reviews.invite.send` means one thing forever.
- **W6 the Contract Warden** owns the registry schema, the verb set, and every
  signature. Squads propose; W6 lands.
