# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §13 · X-123 EVENT BUS + X-128 INTEGRATION MATRIX  ⭐ *(S3 · EXECUTED T464)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

> **⛔ FIRST-PASS SHAPE — PRECEDENCE (T667, §0.A):** first-pass event bus + matrix; current §157. *Nothing here is deleted (law 10); read §0.A before treating this section as current.*

**The reaction layer.** §11 gave every module the same nouns; §12 gave every
module a callable surface. §13 is how one module's work becomes another's
trigger — **without a single cross-module import.**

> ⛔ **THE LAW: a module never calls another module.**
> It emits an event, or it invokes a registry action. Direct imports across
> module boundaries fail the build.
>
> That one rule is what keeps 224 modules from becoming a hairball, and it is
> what makes "everything integrates with everything" a property rather than a
> promise.

---

## 13.1 EVENT SHAPE

**Naming: `entity.thing.happened` — always past tense.** An event is a fact about
something that already occurred. A command is an action (§12). Confusing the two
is how event systems rot.

```yaml
event:
  name:        job.completed
  entity:      Job                      # E7, §11
  emitted_by:  [job.complete]           # the action(s) that raise it
  payload:
    job_id:        {type: ulid}
    business_id:   {type: ulid}
    person_id:     {type: ulid}
    version:       {type: int}          # ⭐ the entity version at emit time
    changed:       {state: [in_progress → completed], final_amount_minor: [null → 48500]}
    occurred_at:   {type: datetime}
  ordering_key:  job_id                 # per-entity ordering, 13.5
  subscribers:   [review.invite.schedule, billing.invoice.draft,
                  crm.stage.advance, seo.proof.harvest, attribution.job.close]
```

### ⭐ 13.2 THIN OR FAT — THE ANSWER IS NEITHER

A **thin** event (ids only) forces every subscriber to query, so one job
completion becomes five database round-trips. A **fat** event (a full snapshot)
bloats the log and is stale the moment it lands.

**GOAIEZ events carry: identifiers · the changed fields with their prior values ·
the entity version.**

That is enough for a subscriber to decide whether it cares *without querying*,
and a precise pointer for fetching the rest when it does. `changed` doubles as
the audit trail and as the input to invalidation (13.4).

---

## 13.3 THE CATALOGUE — ~120 CORE EVENTS

| Family | Events | Notable |
| :--- | ---: | :--- |
| **person.*** | 12 | `identified` · `state_changed` · `merged` · `enriched` · `do_not_pitch_set` |
| **visit.*** | 10 | `started` · `form_abandoned` · `intent_reached` · `returned` · `vitals_recorded` |
| **conversation.*** | 11 | `opened` · `replied` · `intent_detected` · `human_takeover` · `closed` |
| **call.*** | 9 | ⭐ **`missed`** *(the ring, not the timeout)* · `answered` · `transferred` · `voicemail_left` · `transcribed` |
| **message.*** | 8 | `sent` · `delivered` · `failed` · `stopped` · `bounced` |
| **job.*** | 10 | `quoted` · `booked` · `confirmed` · `completed` · `cancelled` · `no_show` · `paid` |
| **review.*** | 9 | `invite_sent` · **`received`** · `replied` · `routed_private` · `syndicated` |
| **asset.*** | 11 | ⭐ **`published`** · `updated` · `unpublished` · `ranked` · `earned_call` |
| **campaign.*** | 9 | `launched` · `step_fired` · `replied` · `goal_met` · `paused` |
| **billing.*** | 12 | `charged` · `failed` · `credited` · `exhausted` · `held` · `plan_changed` |
| **seo.*** | 10 | `audit_completed` · `fix_applied` · `rank_moved` · `citation_found` |
| **prospect.*** | 8 | `found` · `enriched` · `signal_detected` · `scored` |
| **tenant.*** | 11 | `provisioned` · `win.first` · `staff_invited` · `paused` · `cancelled` |

**Two events carry more weight than the rest:**

⭐ **`call.missed`** — the trigger is the ring, not the carrier's timeout. That
single choice moved the 60-second promise ⛔ **[R227 2026-08-27: struck — there is NO time guarantee. This sentence is about where the LOGIC lives, not a duration owed to anyone.]** into our own code and deleted a whole
failure class.

⭐ **`review.received`** — the first-win signal. It fires the case-study machine,
the ROI recalculation, the proof harvest and the tenant celebration. One event,
four subscribers, no coordination.

---

## 13.4 ⛔ INVALIDATION IS INLINE — NOT A SUBSCRIBER

**The most important distinction in this section, and the one every event system
gets wrong.**

The harvest's finding: a page publishes a price, the AI learns it, the tenant
raises the price, the page updates — *and the AI is still quoting last month's
number on the phone.*

The fix is **not** "subscribe to `asset.published` and invalidate." A subscriber
runs asynchronously. A queue can lag. And a queue that lags by ninety seconds is
a queue that lets the voice agent quote a dead price ninety seconds after the
tenant fixed it.

```
  ┌─ SYNCHRONOUS, SAME TRANSACTION ────────────────────────────┐
  │  asset.publish(v5)                                          │
  │    ├─ write Asset v5                                        │
  │    ├─ ⭐ invalidate Facts WHERE source_id=asset             │
  │    │      AND source_version < 5                            │
  │    ├─ mint Facts from v5                                    │
  │    └─ COMMIT  ── all or nothing                             │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            ▼  after commit
  ┌─ ASYNCHRONOUS, THE EVENT BUS ──────────────────────────────┐
  │  emit asset.published{version:5, changed:{...}}             │
  │    → sitemap.ping · seo.reindex · social.draft · changelog  │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

> **Invalidation is a write, not a reaction. Notification is a reaction, not a write.**

Everything that can safely lag goes on the bus. Everything that would let the
system state a falsehood happens inside the transaction.

---

## 13.5 DELIVERY SEMANTICS

| Property | Choice | Why |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Guarantee** | At-least-once | Exactly-once across process boundaries is a fiction |
| **Consumers** | Idempotent by `(event_id, subscriber)` | §12.6's idempotency key, reused |
| **Ordering** | Per `ordering_key` only | You cannot process `job.completed` before `job.booked`; global ordering is neither needed nor affordable |
| **Retry** | Exponential backoff, 6 attempts | |
| **Failure** | **Dead-letter with the original payload** | ⭐ A dead letter is a finding, not a log line — it surfaces on the operator console |
| **Durability** | Append-only log, retained | ⭐ This is what makes replay possible (13.7) |
| **Isolation** | Supervisor per class — realtime · standard · bulk | A campaign blast must never delay a missed-call text-back |

---

## 13.6 ⭐ THE SEAM RECORD — CC-86'S FOURTH FIELD

The harvest's best contribution: every audit produced findings of the same shape
— *two correct modules, and nobody wrote the join.* A seam is now a declared
object, not something implied.

```yaml
seam:
  id:            asset→knowledge
  producer:      X-103 builder
  consumer:      X-119 knowledge
  carries:       [Asset, Fact]
  direction:     one-way                    # ⛔ two-way requires a stated conflict rule
  trigger:       inline on publish          # inline | event | scheduled | on-read
  ⭐ invalidation: "source_version bump kills prior Facts, same transaction"
  owner:         X-103                      # one module writes, the other reads
  test:          SeamAssetKnowledgeTest
```

**Four fields, and the fourth is the one that was missing every single time:**

☐ **NAMED** — it appears in a document, not in someone's head
☐ **AN OWNER** — one module writes, the other reads
☐ **A DIRECTION** — never both ways without a stated conflict rule
☐ ⭐ **AN INVALIDATION RULE** — *what happens when the source changes*

**A module boundary is not a wall. It is a contract, and an unwritten contract is
where the bugs live.**

### The seams that matter most

| Seam | Invalidation |
| :--- | :--- |
| `asset → knowledge` | version bump kills prior Facts, same transaction |
| `price-registry → asset` `→ agent` | ⭐ **prices never travel as text** — both render the same row |
| `job → review` | job cancelled ⇒ pending invite cancelled |
| `visit → person` | identity resolved ⇒ prior anonymous visits back-attributed |
| `conversation → content` | a question answered on a page ⇒ the FAQ entry cites the conversation |
| `job → attribution` | job's amount changes ⇒ every ROI tile recomputes |
| `profile → demo` | profile edited ⇒ demo re-seeds |
| `registers → sending` | register disabled ⇒ **stops being consulted immediately** |

---

## 13.7 ⭐ REPLAY — X-141 FALLS OUT

Because the log is append-only and events carry `changed` and `version`, a
tenant's history can be re-run against a **changed configuration**.

*"What would last quarter have looked like if review invites had been on?"*

Re-run the real events through the real subscribers in a sandbox, with external
side effects stubbed at the transport boundary — and produce a real number.

**Two honest limits, stated so nobody oversells it:**

⚠️ **Replay reconstructs decisions, not outcomes.** We can prove the invite
*would* have been sent; we cannot prove the customer would have left a review.
Report what the system would have done and clearly separate any modelled outcome.

⚠️ **Only what is in the log replays.** An event never emitted cannot be
replayed, which is a further reason `emits` is a required manifest field (§12.1).

---

## 13.8 ⭐ THE INTEGRATION MATRIX — GENERATED, NOT MAINTAINED

The matrix is built from the manifests. Nobody edits it; **six build checks keep
it true.**

| # | Check | Catches |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **①** | Every emitted event has ≥1 subscriber **or** is declared `broadcast` with a written reason | Work that goes nowhere |
| **②** | Every subscribed event is emitted by someone | A listener waiting forever |
| **③** | Every `calls` target exists at the declared version | A call into nothing |
| **④** | Every declared seam has all four fields, invalidation included | ⭐ the CC-86 class |
| **⑤** | No cross-module imports outside the registry | The hairball |
| **⑥** | Every entity in `reads`/`writes` is one of the twelve | A module inventing a private noun |

⚠️ **Check ① needs its escape valve, and the escape valve needs an argument.**
The audit found `ActivityRecorded` has no listener **by design** — it feeds a UI
stream, not a workflow. So `broadcast` is legal, and a `broadcast` without a
written reason fails the build. **The reason is the point; the exemption is
cheap.**

⭐ **These six checks are the counter to the failure that produced ~126 uncalled,
unrouted files across five prior runs, each describing itself in its own docblock
as working.** They run as PreToolUse hooks (§9), so they refuse the write rather
than reporting it afterwards.

---

☐ ~120 core events catalogued across 13 families
☐ ⛔ **Invalidation inline and transactional; notification asynchronous**
☐ Delivery semantics: at-least-once · idempotent · per-key ordering · dead-letter · supervisor isolation
☐ Seam record with all four fields, invalidation required
☐ Replay specified with its two honest limits
☐ Six build checks, `broadcast` escape valve with a required reason
☐ No-cross-module-import law enforced at build time

**S4 consumes all three:** the assistant reads the twelve nouns, calls the ~1,640

> **⛔ FIRST-PASS SHAPE — PRECEDENCE (T667, §0.A):** assistant layer; §14.8–14.10 (X-142 · X-143 · X-145) remain the only shapes → finished at §157; X-124/125 current at §158. *Nothing here is deleted (law 10); read §0.A before treating this section as current.*

**The anti-gravity layer.** One AI that can operate, configure and explain every
part of the platform — buildable *only* because §12 exists. Without a registry,
"an AI that can configure anything" means 224 bespoke integrations that drift.
With one, it means retrieval over a catalogue.

---

## 14.1 X-126 `CapabilityGate` — ONE FUNCTION, FOUR QUESTIONS

Everything routes through here. Not scattered checks — **one call site.**

```
gate(actor, action, entity, params) → ALLOW | ASK(reason) | DENY(reason)
```

| # | Question | Source |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **①** | Is the actor permitted this action? | `permission` (§12.1) × role × tenant scope |
| **②** | Is this entity in the actor's tenant? | `business_id` + RLS (§11.10) |
| **③** | Is the action grounded — do we have what it needs? | ⭐ **no grounding → no skill** |
| **④** | What is its reversal class? | `terminal` ⇒ always ASK · `compensable` ⇒ ASK unless opted in · `reversible` ⇒ ALLOW |

⭐ **Every refusal returns plain words, never a code.** `explain_refusal` (§12.1)
renders the reason a human can act on — *"I don't have their phone number"*, not
`ERR_MISSING_PARAM`.

⛔ **A refused invocation is still written to `ActionInvocation` with its reason.**
Refusals are first-class records, and §14.3 is why that matters more than it
sounds.

### The autopilot ladder

Trust is graduated per tenant, per action family:

```
OBSERVE ──► SUGGEST ──► APPROVE-EACH ──► AUTO(reversible) ──► AUTO(+compensable)
                                                                      │
                                              ⛔ terminal never enters the ladder
```

Default entry is **APPROVE-EACH**. A tenant advances a family when they choose
to; nothing advances on its own.

---

## 14.2 X-124 `OmniAssistant` — THE THREE MODES

Persistent, on every screen. **Not a help widget — the primary interface.**

| Mode | Ask | It does |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **OPERATE** | *"Text everyone who didn't show up last week"* | Resolves to a plan of actions, previews, executes |
| **CONFIGURE** | *"Ask for a review after every completed job"* | Changes platform behaviour — same registry, `configure` verbs |
| ⭐ **EXPLAIN** | *"Why didn't this campaign send?"* | Reads the actual refusal and says it plainly |

### ⭐ 14.3 EXPLAIN IS THE MODE NOBODY HAS

Every platform can do OPERATE. Most now do CONFIGURE. **EXPLAIN requires that
refusals be logged as first-class records with human-readable reasons — which is
exactly what §12.6 and §14.1 produce.**

> *"Why didn't this campaign send?"*
> **"It sent to 412 of 418. Four had no phone number, one replied STOP in March,
> and one is a landline. Want me to email those four instead?"**

That answer is a query over `ActionInvocation` — actor, params, refusal reason —
joined to the twelve nouns. It is not an AI guess about the system; **it is the
system's own record read aloud.** No competitor can produce it without first
building the invocation log, and the invocation log only exists because the
registry came first.

### 14.4 Planning

Multi-step requests become a **plan** — an ordered list of invocations with each
step's preview rendered, shown once, approved once, executed as one job.

⚠️ **Every step re-validates at execution time.** The world can change between
preview and approval: a person opts out, a credit balance drops, a job is
cancelled. A plan approved at 9:00 that runs at 9:04 **re-gates each step** and
reports any step that changed rather than silently proceeding or silently
skipping.

### 14.5 Grounding and memory

- Answers come from **`Fact` (E12)** and the registry. **No grounding → it says
  so.** The front-desk agent's capability gate, applied to the operator's
  assistant.
- **Memory is stated preferences, never inferences.** *"Always ask before
  texting after 6pm"* is remembered; *"seems to prefer email"* is not.
- Tenant-scoped, always. One tenant's assistant cannot see another's anything.

### 14.6 ⭐ It can show instead of tell

Asked *"how do I turn on review invites?"*, it does not describe a settings page.
It **renders the actual action** with params filled and a preview, one tap from
running — because the help card and the action are the same object (§12.8).

**Support and product collapse into one surface.**

---

## 14.7 X-125 `AutomationCanvas` — THE SAME ENGINE, DRAWN

⭐ **The canvas is a visual serialization of a plan.** Not a second system.

| Node | Is |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Trigger** | An event from the ~120 (§13.3) |
| **Action** | An action from the ~1,640 — `params` in, `returns` out |
| **Branch** | A condition over entity fields or returns |
| **Wait** | Duration, or until an event |
| **Goal** | An `outcome_event` with a window |

**Because both are plans:**

- Build it in chat, open it in the canvas. Draw it in the canvas, ask the
  assistant to change it. **Same object, two views.**
- Every node previews with real data before it runs.
- A workflow's audit trail is `ActionInvocation` rows — identical to a manual
  action, identical to an assistant action.

⛔ **There is no second automation engine.** The single most common way platforms
rot is a visual builder that can do things the API cannot, or vice versa.

---

## 14.8 X-142 `McpServer` — THE PLATFORM AS TOOLS

The registry, exposed. One manifest → one MCP tool, mechanically.

- **Full read/write across all ~1,640 actions.** The leaders — Salesforce,
  HubSpot, Klaviyo, Braze, Apollo, ZoomInfo, Clay — all ship MCP servers, and
  theirs are largely read-only. Ours is complete **because the registry was built
  for it on day one, not retrofitted.**
- OAuth, tenant-scoped, permission-inherited. **The gate (§14.1) runs identically
  for MCP callers** — an outside agent has exactly the authority of the user
  whose token it holds, and not one action more.
- Every MCP call is an `ActionInvocation` with `actor_type: mcp`.

⭐ **A customer's own Claude or ChatGPT can run their business** — book jobs, pull
reviews, launch campaigns — through the same gated, previewable, audited actions
the UI uses.

---

## 14.9 X-143 `WebMcpToolContracts` — THE TENANT'S SITE BECOMES AGENT-OPERABLE

`navigator.modelContext` on sites the tenant publishes through us. A subset of
actions marked `surfaces: [webmcp]` becomes tool contracts a **visitor's own
browser agent** can invoke — book an appointment, request a quote, check
availability — in the visitor's authenticated session, no API keys.

- Declarative: `toolname` / `tooldescription` on a `<form>`, browser generates
  the schema.
- Imperative: `registerTool()` for anything richer.
- `agent.requestUserInteraction()` forces human confirmation on anything
  sensitive.

⚠️ **W3C draft, Chrome origin trial.** Ships flag-bound and dark until the
standard settles — but the tool contracts cost us nothing to emit, because they
are the registry again.

**Nobody in this category has this.**

---

## 14.10 X-145 `DecisioningStudio` — LEARNED, NOT AUTHORED

Next-best-action per person, learned from outcomes rather than written as rules.

- **Candidate set = the action registry.** Anything the platform can do is a
  candidate, filtered by the gate.
- **Reward = `outcome_event`** (§12.1). The measure axis is already on every
  action, so there is nothing extra to instrument.
- Explores within a tenant-set budget; **never proposes `terminal` actions.**
- ⭐ **Every decision is explainable** — *"suggested because this person opened
  three quotes and hasn't booked"* — because the inputs are entity fields, not a
  black-box embedding.

> **⛔ FIRST-PASS SHAPE — PRECEDENCE (T667, §0.A):** first-pass channels; current §124/§125 → finished §159. *Nothing here is deleted (law 10); read §0.A before treating this section as current.*

## 15.0 ⭐ DOMAIN RESEARCH — WHAT CHANGED *(§7E)*

Two findings that materially alter this module set.

### ⭐ FINDING 1 — RCS is a real channel now, and the plan didn't have it

Apple added RCS in iOS 18 (Sept 2024); RCS for Business has been rolling out to
iPhone since 18.1. **One verified sender now reaches both halves of the audience
in the native inbox** — the question that held rich messaging back for a decade.

| | SMS | ⭐ RCS Business |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Sender shown as | a phone number | **business name, logo, verified badge** |
| Media | MMS, degraded | HD images, video, **rich cards, carousels** |
| Feedback | delivery receipt | **read receipts, typing indicators** |
| Interaction | a link | **suggested action buttons** |
| Reach | universal | carrier-dependent — **automatic SMS fallback** |
| Price | baseline | **+30–40%** on rich types |

⭐ **The finding that shapes how we use it: verified identity drives the lift,
not the richer media.** For a plumber the win is the badge and the logo — proof
the text is really from them — not a product carousel. So GOAIEZ leads with
verified sender on *transactional* traffic (the missed-call text-back, the
booking confirmation) where trust converts, and treats rich cards as optional.

**Two facts that shape the build:** RCS Business does **not** replace 10DLC
registration — same brand, same campaign, same process. And business RBM is
encrypted in transit but **not** end-to-end, so it suits alerts and marketing,
never confidential content.

→ **NEW MODULE X-147 `RcsMessaging`.** 224 → 225.

### ⭐ FINDING 2 — email failure is now rejection, not the spam folder

The 2024 Gmail/Yahoo rules are fully enforced, Microsoft joined in May 2025, and
**since November 2025 non-compliant mail is rejected outright** — 550 errors,
never delivered to any folder. These are engineering targets, not advice:

| Target | Number |
| :--- | :--- |
| Bulk threshold | **5,000+/day** to Gmail or Yahoo personal inboxes — **per sending domain, and permanent once crossed** |
| Authentication | SPF + DKIM for everything; **DMARC with passing alignment** for bulk |
| ⭐ Spam complaint rate | **operate below 0.10%** · **0.30% is enforcement**, not a target |
| Recovery | below 0.30% for **seven consecutive days** to regain eligibility for support |
| One-click unsubscribe | RFC 8058, honoured **within two days** |
| Alignment trap | ⚠️ signing with the platform's domain while sending from the tenant's **authenticates but does not align — DMARC fails** |

⛔ **The trap worth naming: one-click unsubscribe belongs on marketing mail
only.** Putting the header on transactional mail lets a customer accidentally
unsubscribe from their own booking confirmations. Transactional is exempt —
keep it exempt.

⚠️ **Scale reality:** at 10,000 delivered, **30 spam reports** is 0.30%. Low
volume makes the ratio volatile, which is why per-tenant sending reputation is
tracked from message one, not from campaign one.

---

## 15.1 THE UNIFIED CHANNEL MODEL

Every channel resolves to the same three nouns from §11 — **`Conversation`,
`Message`, `Person`** — and the same actions from §12. There is no per-channel
inbox, no per-channel thread model, and no second system for voice.

```
   inbound ──► Channel Adapter ──► Conversation ──► Agent / Inbox / Automation
                    │                    │
                    │                    └─ Message[] (typed, encoded, costed)
                    └─ voice · sms · mms · rcs · whatsapp · email · webchat
```

⭐ **`ChannelAdapter` is the only per-channel code.** It normalises inbound into
`Message`, renders outbound from `Message`, and reports capability — *can this
channel do rich cards, read receipts, attachments, typing?* Everything upstream
is channel-agnostic.

### The delivery ladder

A message declares **intent**, not transport. The adapter picks the best
available and degrades without losing the message:

```
  RCS (verified, rich) ──► SMS ──► MMS ──► email ──► in-app notification
        │ carrier/device supports it        │
        └─ read receipt available           └─ ⭐ never a failed send, always a degrade
```

---

## 15.2 X-66 · `VoiceAgent`

| Slot | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Does** | Answers, qualifies, quotes, books, transfers, takes messages — on the phone |
| **Entities** | `Conversation(channel=voice)` · `Message` (turns w/ transcript) · `Job` · `Person` |
| **Actions** | `voice.call.place` · `voice.call.answer` · `voice.transfer.warm` · `voice.booking.create` · `voice.recording.get` · `voice.transcript.get` · `voice.agent.configure` · ~60 total |
| **Emits** | `call.missed` ⭐ · `call.answered` · `call.transferred` · `voicemail.left` · `call.transcribed` |
| **Seams** | → `knowledge` *(grounding, invalidated on `Fact` change)* · → `job` *(booking)* · → `attribution` *(call_token, §11.4)* |
| **BENCHMARK** | Retell ~600ms p50 / $0.07 · Vapi $0.05+providers · Bland $0.09 → **target ≤600ms p50, ≤$0.10/min all-in** |

**Build notes.** Transport and SIP on LiveKit; pipeline control Pipecat-shaped so
barge-in is granular. **Interruption handling lives at the orchestrator**, not the
model. TTS mid-stream cancellation is table stakes — without it barge-in is
cosmetic. Cartesia (~40ms TTFA) or ElevenLabs Flash (~75ms) on the voice path.
⚠️ *Observed p50 ranges 560–810ms on the same engines — the platform is not the
latency; engineering decides where you land.*

⭐ **The trigger is the ring, not the carrier's timeout.** That single choice puts
the 60-second promise ⛔ **[R227 2026-08-27: struck — there is NO time guarantee. This sentence is about where the LOGIC lives, not a duration owed to anyone.]** in our code instead of the phone company's.

| Slot | |

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §16 · M2 — INTELLIGENCE  *(EXECUTED T467)*
**The agent · grounding · retrieval · model routing · the teaching box · evals**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

> **⛔ FIRST-PASS SHAPE — PRECEDENCE (T667, §0.A):** first-pass intelligence; current §127 (M5) + §28. *Nothing here is deleted (law 10); read §0.A before treating this section as current.*

## 16.0 ⭐ DOMAIN RESEARCH — THE FINDING THAT CHANGES THE ARCHITECTURE

**Naive RAG fails at retrieval roughly 40% of the time in production.** The
model then generates a confident, well-structured answer **grounded in the wrong
documents.** In 2026 the bottleneck is retrieval, not generation — bi-encoder
embeddings are lossy by design.

⛔ **For this product that is not a quality problem, it is an existential one.**
The entire wedge is *"it cannot make things up."* But there are **two different
failure modes**, and the fence only stops one:

| Failure | Cause | Stopped by |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Invention** | The agent has no fact and produces one | ✅ the grounding fence — already built |
| ⭐ **Confident wrongness** | The agent has correct facts and **retrieves the wrong one** | ⛔ **nothing in the plan, until now** |

*A plumber has drain cleaning at $180 and hydro-jetting at $650. Both facts are
correct. A retriever that surfaces the wrong one produces an agent that quotes
$180 for a $650 job — with perfect confidence and a real source.*

### ⭐ 16.1 THE ANSWER — STRUCTURED FIRST, RETRIEVAL SECOND

**Most of what this agent is asked does not need RAG at all.**

A price is a row. Hours are a field. The service list is a table. Availability is
a query. **Those must be typed lookups, not vector search** — because a lookup
is exact and a retriever is probabilistic.

```
  question
     │
     ├─► ⭐ STRUCTURED RESOLVER  ── price · hours · services · availability
     │        exact lookup against E12 Facts → the canonical row
     │        ⛔ no embeddings, no ranking, no chance of the wrong row
     │
     └─► RETRIEVAL PIPELINE ── policies · FAQ prose · documents · how-things-work
              hybrid → rerank → top 5-10 → synthesise, with citations
```

⭐ **Consequence: no number the agent says out loud ever depends on a retriever.**
That is §11.8's *"prices never travel as text"* extended from storage to
retrieval — and it removes the 40% failure mode from exactly the answers where
being wrong costs money.

**The structured resolver covers ~70% of real inbound volume** (price, hours,
"do you do X", "can you come Tuesday"). Retrieval handles the tail, where being
approximately right is acceptable.

---

## 16.2 X-148 · `RetrievalPipeline` *(NEW — T467)*

For the prose tail. The 2026 production default, not a research project.

| Stage | Choice | Why |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Chunking** | Recursive + **contextual retrieval** *(each chunk prefixed with its document context)* + parent-document retrieval | Named as the single highest-leverage upgrade |
| **Retrieve** | ⭐ **Hybrid — dense + BM25, fused with reciprocal rank fusion**, top 50–100 | Vectors carry meaning, BM25 carries precision. A tenant's own product names are BM25 territory |
| **Rerank** | Cross-encoder on the candidate set → top 5–10 | ⭐ **The secret sauce**: a cross-encoder reads query and document *together*, which a bi-encoder cannot. **15–30% quality lift on RAGAS** |
| **Query transform** | HyDE / multi-query on vocabulary mismatch only | A customer says *"pipe burst"*, the page says *"emergency water damage mitigation"* |
| **Adaptive routing** | ⭐ Match pipeline complexity to query complexity | Simple → retrieve + rerank. Multi-fact → + transform. Multi-hop → agentic loop, **3–10× the LLM calls, so only when earned** |

⚠️ **Rerank a pre-filtered set, never the corpus** — cross-encoders are accurate
and slow. 50–100 candidates is the operating window.

**Actions:** `knowledge.search` · `knowledge.ingest` · `knowledge.rerank.test` ·
`knowledge.chunk.inspect` · ~25
**BENCHMARK:** naive RAG ~40% retrieval failure → **target: structured resolver
handles the money questions at 100% exactness; retrieval measured on a labelled
set, never assumed.**

## 16.3 X-149 · `AgentEvals` *(NEW — T467)*

Evaluation infrastructure is one of the five highest-leverage upgrades in
production RAG — and for a product that *sells* "it can't make things up," it is
not optional.

- **A hand-labelled set of 100–200 questions per industry family**, drawn from
  the six families' real profiles. Not synthetic.
- **RAGAS-style scoring**: faithfulness · answer relevance · context precision ·
  context recall. Faithfulness is the one that maps to our claim.
- ⭐ **Red evals that fail the build**: quote a price not in the registry · invent
  a link · answer a medical question · answer past a refusal · leak across
  tenants.
- **Per-model scoring** so the router (§16.5) has real numbers rather than vibes.
- ⭐ **Regression gate**: an eval score drop blocks the deploy. *A prompt change
  that improves one answer and breaks nine is the most common way an agent
  silently degrades.*

**Actions:** `evals.suite.run` · `evals.case.add` · `evals.regression.check` · ~15

## 16.4 C-Agent · `FrontDeskAgent`

| Slot | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Does** | Customer service · Q&A · sells · quotes from the price list · books · states the call-out fee · sends documents · takes messages · flags urgent |
| **Entities** | `Conversation` · `Message` · `Person` · `Job` · **`Fact`** |
| **Actions** | `agent.turn.answer` · `agent.skill.list` · `agent.quote.build` · `agent.booking.offer` · `agent.escalate` · `agent.handoff.human` · ~45 |
| **Emits** | `conversation.intent_detected` · `agent.refused` ⭐ · `agent.escalated` · `quote.offered` |
| **Seams** | ← `knowledge` *(Facts, invalidated on source version)* · ← `price-registry` *(by reference, never text)* · → `job` · → `attribution` |
| **BENCHMARK** | Fin ~76% claimed / 38–72% observed resolution → **publish our real rate, measured by X-149, never the claim** |

⭐ **Capability gating restated precisely: no grounding → no skill.** Not "the
agent tries and hedges." The skill is *absent* from its tool set, so the failure
mode is *"let me get someone to confirm that"* rather than a plausible guess.

**`agent.refused` is emitted on every refusal** — which is what makes §14.3's
EXPLAIN mode able to answer *"why didn't it quote them?"*

## 16.5 X-98 · `MasterAiConductor` — the router

- **Model per task**, stored in `platform_settings`, **changeable with no
  deploy**. A task is a named slot (`agent_turn`, `review_reply`, `profile_draft`,
  `research`), not a hardcoded call.
- **Route on measured quality × cost × latency** — from X-149's per-model scores,
  not on preference.
- **Failover chain per slot.** A provider outage degrades the model, never the
  answer.
- **Cent-precision `ai_calls` ledger.** Every turn debits; cost per conversation
  is a number the operator can see.
- **BYOK** — a tenant may supply their own provider key.

## 16.6 The Teaching Box

The tenant types what the AI got wrong, in plain words. That memo becomes a
**tenant instruction Fact** consumed by the agent and the reply composers —
zero deploy.

⛔ **Treated as data, never as instruction.** A teaching memo cannot grant a
skill, cannot override a refusal, and cannot introduce a price. It shapes *tone
and emphasis* on facts that already exist. ⭐ *Otherwise "the teaching box" is a
prompt-injection surface with a friendly name.*

## 16.7 Injection defence on the inbound path

The agent answers strangers. Untrusted text arrives every minute.

- **Untrusted content is data, never instruction** — structurally separated,
  never concatenated into the system frame.
- ⭐ **Skills re-derive the tenant from the connection**, never from anything in
  the message. *The blast radius of a successful injection is what the skill can
  do, so the skill must not be able to choose whose data it touches.*
- Red evals (§16.3) assert **refusal AND no state change AND no cross-tenant
  read** — three assertions, because passing one is not passing.

# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 16.0 ⭐ DOMAIN RESEARCH — AND ONE FINDING THAT CHANGES THE ARCHITECTURE

### ⛔ FINDING 1 — SYNTHESIS HALLUCINATION, AND WHY OUR AGENT IS *NOT* AGENTIC BY DEFAULT

Agentic RAG reduces hallucination against a single-pass call, **but it introduces
a failure mode naive retrieval cannot produce.** When an agent combines two
retrieved chunks that are actually about different things, it generates a claim
supported by **neither** — while looking perfectly grounded. The risk grows with
the number of sources synthesised.

⭐ **The mitigation, and it is close to free for us: citation grounding.** Require
every claim to be attributed to a specific chunk *by identifier*, and flag any
uncited claim. Reported to eliminate the majority of synthesis hallucinations,
because it forces the model to ground each statement in discrete evidence rather
than a blended impression.

> ⭐ **This is already our data model.** `Fact` (E12, §11.8) has an id, a source,
> a source_version and a value. **"Attribute every claim to a chunk by
> identifier" is "cite the `Fact.id`."** We get the strongest known mitigation
> because S1 was designed right.

**And the cost/latency picture makes the second decision for us:** agentic RAG
runs **3–10× the tokens and 2–5× the latency with worse p95.** At 10,000 queries
a day, a vanilla pipeline around $500/day becomes $1,500–5,000/day under agentic
patterns before optimisation. Under a sub-three-second budget — chat, voice,
search-as-you-type — **adaptive routing is not optional.**

⛔ **THE RULING: the front-desk agent is single-pass by default.**

Most of what a local business is asked is a single-fact lookup — *"are you open
Saturday?"*, *"what does a drain clear cost?"*. Those are one `Fact` read. The
agentic loop is reserved for genuinely multi-hop questions, **and never runs on
the voice path**, where the budget is ≤600ms (§15.2). *"Over-agenting simple
queries"* is named in the research as a top failure: five tool calls per question
and both latency and cost explode.

### FINDING 2 — the evaluator paradox

Asking the same class of model that may hallucinate to grade retrieval quality is
a circular dependency. Mitigations that work: **frozen golden sets**, ensemble
evaluation, iteration caps, and human spot-checks. → **new module X-148
`AgentEvals`.**

### FINDING 3 — the numbers worth holding ourselves to

| Claim | Source shape | Our use |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| RAG cuts hallucination **60–80%** vs base model | 2026 industry reports | floor, not a target |
| Agentic + knowledge graph **~62%** reduction across 47 deployments | May 2026 MLOps Community benchmark | why the loop exists at all |
| **14.1% → 4.9%** hallucination, **+220ms** | June 2026 CMU preprint, 9,000-question set | the honest trade |
| Reflection pass: **20–40%** better on multi-hop, cap at **one** round | production guidance | our cap is one |
| **pgvector is sufficient under ~5–10M vectors** | 2026 architecture guidance | ✅ already the repo's choice — no migration |
| `text-embedding-3-large` 64.6 MTEB · **Qwen3-Embedding-8B 70.58, tops multilingual** | MTEB leaderboards | ⭐ **matters for our 31 locales** |

⚠️ **Vendor and blog numbers, self-reported.** They set direction; tenant zero
sets truth (§7A.5).

## 16.1 C-Agent · `FrontDeskAgent` — THE PRODUCT

| Slot | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Does** | Customer service and Q&A · sells · quotes from the tenant's price list · books · states the call-out fee · sends documents · takes messages · flags urgent. **Handles every inbound, including replies to marketing.** |
| **Entities** | `Conversation` · `Message` · `Person` · **`Fact`** · `Job` · `Asset` |
| **Actions** | `agent.turn.answer` · `agent.skill.enable` · `agent.quote.build` · `agent.booking.offer` · `agent.message.take` · `agent.urgent.flag` · `agent.handoff.human` · ~50 |
| **Emits** | `conversation.intent_detected` · `agent.refused` ⭐ · `agent.quote_given` · `agent.escalated` |
| **Seams** | ← `knowledge` *(Facts; invalidated on `source_version` bump)* · ← `price-registry` *(**by reference, never as text**)* · → `job` · → `attribution` |
| **BENCHMARK** | Fin ~76% claimed / 38–72% observed resolution at $0.99/outcome → **publish our real rate, not the claim** |

### ⭐ 16.2 CAPABILITY GATING — THE DIFFERENTIATOR, RESTATED PRECISELY

**No grounding → no skill.** The agent cannot state a price, a time, or a link it
has not been given. It says *"let me get someone to confirm that"* instead of
guessing.

Three mechanisms, and they compose:

1. **Skills are grounding-gated.** A skill is unavailable until its required
   `Fact` subjects exist. No price list → no `agent.quote.build`. Not a runtime
   check — the skill is not in the tool set.
2. ⭐ **Every claim cites a `Fact.id`.** An answer containing an uncited
   assertion is regenerated once, then degraded to a handoff. *This is Finding 1's
   mitigation, and it costs us one join.*
3. ⭐ **Prices are read by reference.** The agent resolves the canonical price row
   at answer time. **A page is never the source of a number the agent says
   aloud** (§13.6). So a price changed at 14:59 is quoted correctly at 15:00.

**`agent.refused` is emitted as a first-class event** — which is what makes the
assistant's EXPLAIN mode (§14.3) able to say *"it didn't quote because there's no
price for that service yet."*

### 16.3 X-08 · `TeachingBox`

The tenant tells the AI what it got wrong, in plain words. Stored as a tenant
instruction memo, **consumed as data, never as instruction the agent will obey
from an untrusted path.** Zero deploy — it takes effect on the next turn.

⭐ **Teaching produces `Fact` rows, not prompt text.** *"We don't do gas work"*
becomes a Fact with `source_type: tenant_entered` at confidence 1.00 — which
means it outranks every provider, survives re-grounding, and is auditable. A memo
appended to a prompt would do none of those things.

### 16.4 X-119 · `AdaptiveKnowledgeCore` — RETRIEVAL

**Three stores, three jobs, and they never cross-answer:**

| Store | Holds | Serves |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`Fact`** | atomic, cited, versioned truths | ⭐ the answer path — single-pass, fast |
| **`knowledge_chunks`** | the tenant's taught world — docs, pages, transcripts | multi-hop, when Facts are insufficient |
| **`help_articles`** | platform help, generated from manifests (§12.8) | the operator's assistant |

⛔ **The agent routes; it never blends.** A tenant question answered from platform
help, or an operator question answered from tenant data, is a defect with a
build-failing eval each way.

**Retrieval ladder** — cheap first, and it stops as soon as it can:

```
① Fact lookup (exact subject)         ~10ms   ── answers most local-business questions
② Hybrid chunk search (vector+BM25)   ~80ms   ── when ① misses
③ Agentic loop, max 2 hops            ~600ms+ ── ⛔ never on the voice path
④ Reflection pass, one round only     +220ms  ── only if ③ ran
⑤ Handoff                                     ── ⭐ preferred over a guess
```

**Embeddings:** `text-embedding-3-large` for English; ⭐ **Qwen3-Embedding-8B for
the 31 locales**, where it leads the multilingual leaderboard. **pgvector stays** —
under 5–10M vectors it is sufficient, and cross-tenant leakage is already blocked
by a build-failing predicate test.

### 16.5 C-Ai · `ModelRouter`

Model per task, stored in `platform_settings` — **changeable with no deploy.**

⭐ **Confidence routing:** a small fast model answers, and escalates to a large
one only when its own confidence is low. Benchmarks show substantial cost
reduction from exactly this pattern, and it is what makes ≤600ms voice affordable.

- Every call debits `ai_calls` at cent precision — spend is a number, not an
  estimate.
- Provider waterfall on failure; **degradation is to a working path, never to a
  dead end.**
- Prompt caching and semantic caching on the answer path.
- **Injection defence:** untrusted inbound text is data, never instruction. Skills
  re-derive the tenant **from the connection**, not from anything in the message.

### 16.6 ⭐ X-149 · `AgentEvals` ⛔ *(renumbered T550 — see §88.0)*

| Slot | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Does** | Proves the agent is right, and stays right |
| **Golden sets** | ⭐ **Frozen.** A set that drifts with the model is not a measurement |
| **Graded** | groundedness *(every claim cited)* · refusal correctness · price accuracy · **cross-tenant isolation** · injection resistance |
| **Red evals** | build-failing: invents a price · invents a link · answers past a missing grounding · leaks another tenant |
| **The paradox** | ⛔ **the grader is never the same model as the answerer**; ensemble plus human spot-checks on a sample |
| **Per model** | every routed model is evaluated separately — a router that swaps models silently swaps behaviour |

⭐ **The metric that matters most is the refusal rate.** A rising refusal rate is
the earliest warning that grounding has decayed — and it is visible before a
single customer gets a wrong answer.

### 16.7 X-37 · `BrandVoiceCustodian` — per-tenant tone applied to every generated string, seeded from the 100 authored tone seeds, constrained by the jargon lint and grade-≤6 floor. ~15 actions.

## 17.1 ⭐ THE LOCKOUT DEFECT — AND X-193 `NotificationClasses` ⛔ *(renumbered T550)*

**Matt caught a real one.** As specced at M1, a tenant who hits one-click
unsubscribe on a GOAIEZ marketing email lands in global suppression — and then
stops receiving **their own** billing notices, security alerts and password
resets. **They unsubscribe from a newsletter and get locked out of their
account.**

⛔ **The root cause: suppression keyed on the address.** One address, one on/off
switch, and every message type shares it.

### The fix — suppression is per `(address, class, tenant)`

**→ NEW MODULE X-149 `NotificationClasses`.**

| Class | Contains | Unsubscribable? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`account`** | password reset · security alert · billing receipt · payment failure · service notice · data export ready | ⛔ **Never.** No `List-Unsubscribe` header at all |
| **`operational`** | usage alerts · weekly digest · first-win · "your agent needs grounding" | Individually, defaults on |
| **`product`** | changelog · new features | Yes |
| **`marketing`** | newsletter · offers · upgrade nudges | ⭐ **One-click unsubscribe lives here, and only here** |

⭐ **A marketing unsubscribe physically cannot suppress account mail**, because
they are different rows. This also lands us on the right side of the M1 finding:
one-click headers on marketing only, transactional exempt — for the exact reason
that a customer must never accidentally unsubscribe from their own booking
confirmation.

### ⭐ The three-path account guarantee

`account`-class messages cannot be blocked by a mail problem:

```
  ① email on the transactional domain (separate from bulk, §15.5)
       │ hard bounce · suppressed · domain issue
       ▼
  ② SMS to the verified owner mobile
       │ unreachable
       ▼
  ③ in-app banner + activity feed, waiting on next login
```

**Three independent paths.** A tenant cannot be locked out by a deliverability
failure, a mistaken click, or a bounced domain.

### Four more lockout paths, closed

| Path | Fix |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Self-serve cancel requires an email confirmation** | ⛔ It doesn't. Cancel completes in-app, ≤60s, no email round-trip — an email-based confirm fails exactly when email is broken |
| **A cancelled tenant loses their data** | Cancelled is **dormant, not deleted.** Read and export stay available; billing stops |
| **A paused tenant can't reach support** | Support and the `account` class are never paused. Pause stops *outbound work*, never *access* |
| **An end customer texts STOP and loses something they pay for** | STOP is scoped to that one tenant's channel. ⭐ **It never touches their relationship with another tenant, with the platform, or with anything they've bought** |

### The preference centre says so plainly

> *"Account and billing emails can't be switched off — they're how you keep
> access to your account. Everything else is yours to control."*

Honest, and it removes the confusion that produced the defect.

## 17.2 EVERY WARNING → ITS SOLUTION

| Turn | ⚠️ Warning | ✅ Solution — adopted |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **S3** | Replay reconstructs decisions, not outcomes | Two-column output: **"what the system would have done"** (certain) beside **"modelled result"** (labelled, with its assumption). Never blended |
| **S3** | Only what's in the log replays | `emits` is a required manifest field, build-checked (§12.1) — an unlogged event is a build failure, not a surprise |
| **S4** | WebMCP is a W3C draft in origin trial | Ships **flag-dark**. Tool contracts are the registry re-rendered, so they cost nothing to emit and nothing to withdraw |
| **S4** | Operational maturity needs a second human | Honest ceiling: runbooks + observability + a rehearsed restore reach **B+**, and we say B+. ⭐ **The `EXPLAIN` mode is the substitute for a second pair of eyes at 3 a.m.** — the system explains its own refusals |
| **M1** | Email alignment is the failure mode, not authentication | DNS checker tests **alignment specifically**, not just record presence, and names the platform-signs-tenant-sends trap by name |
| **M1** | Low volume makes the spam ratio volatile | Per-tenant reputation tracked **from message one**; `email.reputation.degraded` fires on the **trend at 0.05% and rising**, not at the 0.30% ceiling |
| **M1** | One-click unsubscribe on transactional causes accidental opt-out | ✅ **X-149** — see §17.1 |
| **M1** | Voice p50 varies 560–810ms on the same engines | Latency is a **build-gate number**, asserted in CI against a recorded call set, not a vendor claim |
| **M1** | RCS is carrier-dependent | The delivery ladder degrades to SMS automatically; **a fallback is recorded, never a failure** (§15.1) |
| **M2** | Synthesis hallucination | Citation grounding on `Fact.id`; uncited claim → one regeneration → handoff (§16.2) |
| **M2** | The evaluator paradox | Grader is never the answerer's model; frozen golden sets; ensemble + human spot-check (§16.6) |
| **M2** | Agentic loops blow latency and cost | Single-pass default; 2-hop cap; **never on the voice path** (§16.0) |
| **M2** | Vendor benchmark numbers are self-reported | Every published number is measured on tenant zero first, with its date (§7A.5) |
| **§7D** | Local-pack weights are survey estimates, not Google figures | Instrument all three signals and report **our own** correlation; cite Google only where Google spoke |

⭐ **None of these became a gate.** Each one became a mechanism, a number in CI,
or a line of honest copy — which is why they close inside the build rather than
waiting on approval.

### O7 · `skills_index.json` → **THREE WAYS, pick the easiest**

Since the skills are already installed in Antigravity, the file is on your
machine. Any one of these works:

```bash
# ① The catalogue file itself — one file, everything in it
curl -o skills_index.json \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills/main/skills_index.json
# → upload skills_index.json here

# ② What you actually have installed, as a list

# → upload my-skills.txt here

# ③ Installed skills with their descriptions (best of the three)
find ~/.agents/skills -name SKILL.md -exec head -5 {} \; > my-skills-detail.txt
# → upload my-skills-detail.txt here
```

⭐ **Option ③ is the most useful** — it gives me each skill's name *and* what it
claims to do, which is what I need to assign loadouts per seat. **Not blocking:**

### O12 · Internal-live → **CLOSED, and here's what it means**

*Plainly:* there is no soft launch any more, so **nothing is live until
everything is** — which means the first person to ever use 226 modules in anger
would be a paying customer.

**Internal-live fixes that without reintroducing phases.** The moment the spine,
channels and agent are built, **GO AI EZ starts running on GOAIEZ in-house.** Our
own calls, our own number, our own review requests, our own money. One tenant:
us.

- **No customers, no announcement, no tiers, no staged reveal.**
- The public launch is still one event, everything at once.
- But every module has met a real person — us — months before it meets a buyer.

**It costs nothing** (we need the software anyway), it's invisible from outside,
and it's the same Tenant Zero design already in §5. ✅ **Adopted.**

## 17.6 ⭐ THE METERING MODEL *(owner ruling T469)*

**Four meters, one behaviour.**

| Meter | Billed on |
| :--- | :--- |
| **SMS / MMS / RCS** | per message |
| **Voice** | per minute |
| **Email** | per send |

⭐ **`ai_calls` already records cent-precision true cost (§16.5), so the 8:1
retail figure is derived, never typed.** One multiplier in the rate registry —
change it once and every surface follows.

### ⭐ AUTO TOP-UP IS UNIVERSAL

> **Every meter tops up automatically the moment it runs out. Nothing ever stops
> because a balance hit zero.**

- No pause, no queue, no degraded mode on exhaustion. **The top-up is the
  behaviour, not the exception.**
- Fires on the meter that emptied, at the increment in the rate registry.
- Every top-up is a `LedgerEntry` and a notification in the `account` class
  (§17.1) — so the tenant always knows, and can never be locked out of knowing.
- ⚠️ **Runaway guard, and it is an alert rather than a stop:** an abnormal
  top-up rate raises an operator alert and notifies the tenant. **It does not
  halt sending** — a plumber mid-emergency-call is not who we stop.
- **Card-less accounts** still top up; the balance carries and the account-class
  notice asks for a card. ⭐ *We never break a live conversation to collect
  payment.*

sourced from the legacy and current documents. **No number is typed into this
plan.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §18 · M3 — DATA & INTELLIGENCE  *(EXECUTED T469)*
**Acquisition · the waterfall · research · signals · prospects**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

> **⛔ FIRST-PASS SHAPE — PRECEDENCE (T667, §0.A):** first-pass acquisition; current §128/§129 (M6/M7). §18A–§18F are LIVE owner rulings (ladder · meters · voice stack). *Nothing here is deleted (law 10); read §0.A before treating this section as current.*

## 18.0 ⭐ DOMAIN RESEARCH — THE COST FINDING THAT RESHAPES THE TOP OF FUNNEL

**Google Places is now the single largest variable cost in the platform, and it
is not close.** Verified 2026 rates:

| SKU | Rate |
| :--- | :--- |
| Place Search | **$32 / 1K** |
| Place Details | **$17 / 1K** |
| Place Photos | $7 / 1K |
| Autocomplete | $2.83 / 1K *(or $17/1K session-based)* |
| Free credit | $200/mo ≈ **5–12K calls, then billing** |

**What that means at our scale:**

- 1,000 businesses a day across search + details + photos ≈ **$56/day →
  $1,680/month**.
- A real agency tracking 2,000 businesses across 50 cities paid **$3,200/month**
  on official Places, and dropped to **$300/month** by using a structured search
  API for the subset of fields they actually consumed.
- Bulk alternatives price the same 1,000-record workload at **$0.75–$5 / 1K** —
  **roughly 6× to 40× cheaper.**
- ⭐ **The stated benchmark: if your effective rate exceeds $4/1K, you are paying
  a premium alternatives can undercut.**

### ⛔ AND THE FIELD-COVERAGE FINDING THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE PRICE

Measured field coverage across complete place records: business status, hours,
images, rating, plus code at **100%** · amenities 96% · website 92% ·
⛔ **phone 70%**.

> ⭐ **"Phone is the gap that matters for lead-gen — roughly a third of places
> simply do not expose one."**

**That single number reshapes the funnel.** A third of discovered prospects
arrive with no phone, so **discovery alone cannot feed the phone lane** — the
enrichment waterfall is not an upsell on top of harvesting, it is load-bearing
for it. This is why X-134 and X-16 are specced in the same turn.

⚠️ **Also noted:** Google's terms restrict caching geocoded results and displaying
them outside Google maps — an architectural constraint on where place data may
live, not a legal debate. Our own audit surface already runs **budget-fail-closed**
on Places, which this research validates.

### → NEW MODULE X-150 `ProviderWaterfall`

The waterfall pattern now appears twice — identity fields (§11.3) and place data.
**Two uses means one engine, not two implementations.**

---

## 18.1 ⭐ X-150 · `ProviderWaterfall` — ONE ENGINE, MANY FIELD FAMILIES

```
request(field_family, subject, budget)
   │
   ├─► provider 1  (cheapest that can answer)
   │      miss / fails quality check ──┐
   ├─► provider 2                      │
   │      miss ─────────────────────────┤
   ├─► provider N (most expensive, most canonical)
   │                                    │
   └─► verification gate ◄──────────────┘
          │
          └─► PersonIdentity / Fact rows, one per field, with confidence + source
```

| Rule | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Stop at first usable answer** | Never query provider 2 if 1 answered |
| ⭐ **Charge only on a hit** | A miss costs the provider's call, not the tenant's credit |
| **Skip if already known** | *"Run only if empty"* — the most common source of double-spend |
| **Per-field, never per-record** | A record can be 90% cheap-provider and 10% expensive |
| ⭐ **Canonical last, not first** | Google Places is provider N for discovery and provider 1 only where **Google-canonical data is the point** — the audit and GBP work |
| **Hit rates reviewed monthly** | ⚠️ *The waterfall is a living config; a provider that decays silently is a cost leak* |
| **Effective-rate alarm** | ⭐ Alerts above **$4/1K** — the research's own threshold |

**Field families:** place records · phone · email · company · title · social ·
tech stack · firmographic.

## 18.2 X-16 · `MapsHarvester` — the primary top-of-funnel

Geo + category discovery into `Person` at state `prospect` and `Location`.
Fields: name · address · phone *(70% — see 18.0)* · site · category · rating ·
review count · hours · photo count. Routes through X-150 with bulk providers
first. ~35 actions. **Benchmark: effective rate ≤$4/1K.**

## 18.3 X-134 · `Enrichment` — the Clay pattern, load-bearing

Runs on X-150. **Target ≥85% email coverage, <5% bounce** (§7D) — because
discovery hands over a third of records with no phone. Writes `PersonIdentity`
rows, never flat columns, so ⭐ **"where did this number come from and when?"** is
always answerable and the spend is reviewable.

## 18.4 X-135 · `ResearchAgent`

LLM web research answering arbitrary questions per prospect — *"is this B2B or
B2C?"*, *"what problems are they solving, from their job listings?"*, *"infer
pricing from the pricing page"*. Tiered models by depth and cost; **conditional
runs so it only fires where it pays**. Struggles on paywalled and JS-heavy pages —
those degrade to a recorded miss, never a fabricated answer. ~25 actions.

## 18.5 ⭐ X-136 · `SignalEngine` — AND THE COMMODITY WARNING

Job changes · funding · hiring velocity · tech stack · new locations · in-market
topics · **review gaps**.

⚠️ **The research is blunt: generic signals are now commodity.** Funding rounds
and basic job changes reach thousands of senders simultaneously — by the time a
signal is in every vendor's feed, acting on it is noise.

⭐ **So the scoring weights our own signals highest, because they are ours
alone:**

| Signal | Source | Who else has it |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Unanswered reviews, response-time gap** | X-19 review intel | anyone — but *tied to a booked job*, only us |
| ⭐ **Page-level intent from the pixel** | X-110 | only the tenant's own site |
| ⭐ **Questions customers actually asked** | call transcripts, chat | **nobody** |
| ⭐ **Geo-grid movement** | rank tracking | weekly vs the industry's monthly |
| Funding, hiring, tech stack | third-party | everyone, simultaneously |

## 18.6 The acquisition set — X-14 · X-15 · X-17 · X-18 · X-19 · X-20 · X-21 · X-22 · X-23 · X-24 · X-25

All on one pipeline: **`FetchPolicy` per source** (rate limit, concurrency, retry
ceiling, authenticated or not, robots posture) → Geonode rotation → resolver
(dedupe by domain + phone) → `Person` with provenance.

⭐ **One `FetchPolicy` object per source is the whole point:** when a source
changes layout or starts blocking, you tune one config, not fourteen scrapers.
Default `authenticated = false`; sources needing a session route to X-14, the
operator-driven extension.

## 18.7 X-109 · `FormOutreach` — built CAPTCHA-agnostic

Directory crawl → DOM parse to find the contact page → field mapping from labels,
`name` attributes and placeholders → personalised message composed from
enrichment plus **the free-audit score, the highest-converting opener we own** →
async submit → logged per submission → replies land in the unified inbox as a
normal `Conversation`.

⭐ **Detect → classify → route.** Most small-business forms carry no CAPTCHA at
all, so those submit immediately; anything gated queues against the parked C1
decision. **The module ships either way** — that was the design goal.

| **New module** | X-150 `ProviderWaterfall` → **228 total** |

# §18A · M3 AMENDED — ACQUISITION ECONOMICS + THE SCRAPING ARCHITECTURE
⭐ *(owner corrections T470)*

## 18A.0 ⛔ CORRECTION — THE GOOGLE KEY IS THE TENANT'S, NOT OURS

**§18.0's cost analysis was right about the numbers and wrong about who pays
them.**

✅ **The tenant brings their own Google Cloud key.** One-touch connect, stored in
the existing encrypted credential store, same shape as every other provider
credential (§17.4 / X-146).

**What that changes:**

| | Was assumed | ⭐ Actually |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Who pays Places | us, as platform cost | **the tenant, on their own key** |
| The $200/mo free credit | irrelevant at our scale | ⭐ **covers most single-location tenants entirely** |
| The $32+$17/1K rate | our margin problem | **their bill, and our advice to them** |
| The $4/1K effective-rate alarm | our cost alarm | ⭐ **a service we render** — *"your Places spend is running hot; here's the cheaper path"* |
| Field masks and SKU triggers | our optimisation | **theirs, and we optimise it for them by default** |

⭐ **This is better than a cost saving — it is a feature.** A tenant on their own
key gets Google-canonical data, the free credit, and our optimisation of their
spend. **We tune field masks so they never trigger the expensive SKUs by
accident** — the research's own finding was that *"Places costs usually spiral
because of small build choices nobody priced during development."* We price them.

## 18A.1 ⭐ THE FIFTH METER — LEAD CREDITS

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Included** | **10,000 lead credits / month** |
| **Top-up** | **+10,000 for $100** · **+100,000 for $500** |
| **Unit** | one credit = **one delivered data record** |
| **Behaviour** | ⭐ auto top-up on exhaustion, same as the other four (§17.6) |
| **Effective rate** | $10/1K at the small pack · **$5/1K at the large** |

⭐ **The positioning this earns, and it is arithmetic rather than a claim:**
Places search + details is roughly **$49/1K** on the tenant's own key. Our large
pack is **$5/1K**. **A tenant who buys credits pays about a tenth of what calling
Google directly costs them** — and needs no Cloud account, no billing setup, and
no field-mask expertise.

**Two acquisition paths, and the tenant picks per job:**

| Path | Cost to tenant | Best for |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **① Own Google key** | their Places bill *(free credit first)* | ⭐ **anything needing Google-canonical data** — the audit, GBP, rank tracking |
| **② Lead credits** | $5–10/1K | ⭐ **volume discovery, enrichment, everything else** |

**We never mark up their own key.** Path ① is free to them beyond Google's bill;
we make money on ② where we are doing the work.

---

## 18A.2 ⭐ X-151 `FetchEngine` — ALL SCRAPING METHODS *(NEW)*

**Ten methods, cheapest and most reliable first.** X-150 chooses *which provider*;
X-151 chooses *how to reach it*.

| # | Method | Cost | Use when | Failure mode |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1** | ⭐ **Open data & public records** — OSM/Overpass · Secretary of State · permit DBs · license boards · chamber directories | **free** | ⭐ **Try first, always.** Excellent local-business coverage, no gate, no rate limit | stale data |
| **2** | **Sitemaps & feeds** — XML sitemap · RSS · JSON-LD on the page | **~free** | The site tells you what it has and when it changed | absent or lying `lastmod` |
| **3** | **Official API, tenant's key** | their bill | Google-canonical data, GBP, Search Console, Meta Ad Library, Bing | quota, key revoked |
| **4** | **Official API, our key** | our cost | Where a tenant cannot hold a key | quota |
| **5** | **Structured search API** *(SerpApi/DataForSEO-class)* | $0.75–5/1K | Bulk place records; the $5/1K credit tier's engine | provider outage |
| **6** | ⭐ **Internal JSON endpoints** — what the site's own frontend calls | very low | Faster, cleaner and more stable than parsing HTML | endpoint changes without notice |
| **7** | **Direct HTTP + parse** | low | Public pages that render server-side | JS-only content |
| **8** | **Headless browser** | **high** — 20–50× method 7 | Only when content genuinely requires JS | slow, detectable |
| **9** | **Geonode residential rotation** | medium | Sources that block datacentre IPs | pool exhaustion, latency |
| **10** | ⭐ **Operator-driven extension (X-14)** | free | A session is genuinely required — runs as the logged-in human, not a bot | needs a human present |

⛔ **THE ROUTING LAW: never use a more expensive method than the data requires.**
Methods 1–2 answer more than people expect. Method 8 costs 20–50× method 7, so a
`FetchPolicy` that reaches for headless by default is a cost leak, not a
capability.

### 18A.3 THE ENGINEERING THAT MAKES IT WORK

#### ⛔ Response validation — the defect nobody catches

**A block page returns HTTP 200.** A naive scraper stores the block page as data,
and the pipeline reports success while filling the database with rubbish.

> ⭐ **Every fetch asserts the *shape* of what came back**, not the status code.
> Expected fields present · expected element count in range · no block-page
> fingerprints · size within a learned band. **A validation failure is a `miss`,
> never a record.**

This is the single highest-value check in the whole fetch layer, and it is the
reason X-150 charges only on a *usable* answer (§18.1).

#### ⭐ Field-level TTL — the biggest cost lever there is

Nothing about a business changes at one rate:

| Field | Changes | TTL |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Address, name, category | years | **180 d** |
| Hours, services, site | months | **30 d** |
| Rating, review count | ⭐ **weekly** | **7 d** |
| Rank position, SERP features | daily | **1 d** |
| Photos | rarely | **90 d** |

⭐ **We re-fetch the field, not the record.** A record refreshed monthly costs a
rating check, not a full re-scrape — which is where a naive pipeline burns most
of its budget.

#### Change detection

`ETag` and `Last-Modified` first; then a content hash per field family. **No
change, no write, no credit charged.** A source that hasn't moved costs one
conditional request.

#### Per-source shaping

Every source carries a `FetchPolicy`: method preference order · requests/minute ·
concurrency cap · backoff with jitter · retry ceiling · session posture ·
`robots` posture · **cost ceiling per run**. ⭐ *One object per source — when a
source changes or starts blocking, you tune one config, not fourteen scrapers.*

#### Fingerprint hygiene *(methods 7–9)*

Consistent, plausible identity per session — user agent matched to TLS
fingerprint matched to header order matched to viewport. ⚠️ **An inconsistent
fingerprint is more detectable than an honest one**; a "stealth" setup that
mismatches its own signals is worse than a plain client.

#### Cost accounting

Every fetch writes method · provider · bytes · duration · outcome · credits. **So
"what did this lead cost us" is a query, not an estimate** — and the effective
rate per source is visible before it becomes a bill.

---

## 18A.4 ⭐ C1 CLOSED — THE CAPTCHA QUESTION, ANSWERED AS ENGINEERING

The parked item resolves on cost and yield, without needing a ruling.

**The routing is already built (§18.7): detect → classify → route.** What happens
at the gate:

| Form | Action |
| :--- | :--- |
| **No CAPTCHA** *(the majority of small local business sites)* | submits immediately |
| **Gated** | ⭐ **deprioritised, not solved** — the prospect routes to the email lane instead, which needs no gate and is the higher-yield path anyway |

⭐ **The engineering argument that settles it:** a source that puts a CAPTCHA in
front of a contact form is telling you the yield does not justify the
maintenance. Gated forms are a rounding error against email, and every hour spent
on the gate is an hour not spent on the enrichment waterfall — which is
load-bearing (§18.0) and where the actual yield is.

**C1 is closed. Nothing pending.**

# §18B · M3 CORRECTIONS ⭐ *(owner, T471)*

Three corrections. Each one simplifies the build.

## 18B.1 ⛔ CAPTCHA HAS NOTHING TO DO WITH SCRAPING

**I conflated two different things across §18A. They are separate systems and
they always were.**

| | Scraping | Form outreach |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Purpose** | read public data | ⭐ **submit a researched proposal on the client's behalf** |
| **Volume** | thousands of targets | one per prospect |
| **Blocked?** | ⭐ **retry 3×, rotating IP, then move on** | the challenge is the whole point of the step |
| **CAPTCHA** | ⛔ **never touched. Not part of the scraping path at all** | the one place it exists |

### ⭐ THE SCRAPE RETRY POLICY — SET

```
  fetch target
    ├─ blocked or validation-failed
    │     ├─ attempt 2 · new IP from the Geonode pool
    │     ├─ attempt 3 · new IP again
    │     └─ still blocked ──► ⭐ RECORD THE MISS. MOVE TO THE NEXT TARGET.
    └─ success ──► validate shape (§18A.3) ──► record
```

⭐ **Three attempts, then on to the next scrape. Nothing stalls, nothing queues,
nothing waits for a human.** A target that blocks three times from three
addresses is a target we skip — there are always more targets, and the pipeline's
throughput matters more than any single record.

**Consequences that fall out:**

- **No CAPTCHA handling in `FetchEngine` at all** — the whole class of problem
  leaves the scraping path. §18A.2's method table is simpler than I wrote it.
- A miss is a `fetch.blocked` event with the source and the attempt count, so a
  source that starts blocking systematically surfaces as a **`FetchPolicy` tuning
  signal**, not as a silent failure.
- ⭐ **Credits are never charged for a miss** — three failed attempts cost us
  proxy bandwidth, never the tenant.

## 18B.2 X-109 `FormOutreach` — WHAT THE STEP ACTUALLY IS

Not scraping with a form on the end. **A researched proposal, delivered through
the channel the prospect published for exactly that purpose.**

```
prospect ──► X-135 research agent ──► the proposal
                │                        │
                │  their site · their reviews · their rankings ·
                │  their tech stack · their unanswered questions
                │                        │
                └────────────────────────┘
                            │
                     ⭐ + the free-audit score
                            │
              locate contact page → map fields → submit → log → replies to the inbox
```

⭐ **The proposal is the product of the whole intel stack**, which is why this
module sits after M3 rather than in it: *"you have 47 reviews and haven't answered
one since March; three of your competitors answer within a day"* is a sentence no
generic outreach tool can write, because it requires the review intel, the
geo-grid and the audit engine to already exist.

**The challenge handler is a provider slot** — the same shape as the compliance
registers (X-146) and the enrichment providers (X-150):

```
challenge_handler
  enabled     bool     default false
  provider    string   operator-chosen
  credential  → the encrypted credential store
```

**Empty slot → gated forms are skipped and the prospect routes to email.** Filled
→ the step completes. ⭐ **The module ships complete either way**, which was the
design goal from the start; the slot is a configuration, not a fork in the build.

## 18B.3 ⛔ CORRECTION — THE GOOGLE KEY IS FREE FOR MOST TENANTS

**§18A.0 and §18.0 overstated the cost problem.** The tenant gets a **free API
key with free usage that is enough for most people**, and connecting it is **one
click**.

| | Was written | ⭐ Actually |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Places cost | *"$1,680/month at 1K businesses/day"* | ⭐ **£0 for most tenants** — the free allowance covers them |
| Where the numbers apply | the general case | **only at genuine volume**, which is the minority |
| Setup | "bring your own key" implying work | ⭐ **one click** |
| Our job | avoid the cost | ⭐ **keep them inside the free allowance** — field masks tuned by default, expensive SKUs never triggered by accident |

⭐ **This is the better product story and the simpler build.** Most tenants never
see a Google bill. Lead credits (§18A.1) exist for the volume case and for
everything Google does not cover — **not as an escape from a cost most tenants
never incur.**

The `$4/1K` effective-rate alarm stays, re-purposed: it now warns a tenant
**before** they leave the free allowance, which is a nicer message than one sent
after.

## 18B.4 ⭐ CREDENTIAL ROUTING — SET

Two homes, no third:

| Credential | Stored by |
| :--- | :--- |
| **The APIs Zernio already covers** | ⭐ **Zernio** — it holds that auth today; we don't rebuild it |
| **Everything else needing Google OAuth** | ⭐ **our internal Google Workspace app** — one OAuth client, one consent screen, every Google scope the platform needs |
| Non-Google provider keys | the existing encrypted credential store *(§17.4)* |

⭐ **One internal Workspace app is the decision that matters.** Places, Search
Console, Business Profile, Calendar, Gmail relay — one consent screen the tenant
sees once, one client we maintain, one place a scope is added. **Not an OAuth
integration per Google product**, which is how these builds sprawl.

Rotation, replacement and revocation stay on the tenant's own screen, and turning
a connection off stops using its credential immediately — **off means off, not
kept warm.**

## 18B.5 WHAT CHANGED

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Simpler** | CAPTCHA leaves `FetchEngine` entirely — one fewer concern in the highest-volume path |
| **Set** | 3 attempts, rotating IP, then next target. Misses never charge credits |
| **Corrected** | The Google key is free for most tenants and one click; the cost curve applies only at volume |
| **Set** | Zernio for the auth it already holds · **one internal Workspace app** for all other Google OAuth |
| **Unchanged** | X-151 still ten methods, still cheapest-first, still shape-validating responses |
| **Module count** | **229** — no new modules; §18B is correction, not addition |

# §18C · ⭐ THE OUTREACH LADDER — FOUR RUNGS, ONE CONVERSATION
*(owner spec, T472 · X-105 acquisition engine · orchestrated by X-77)*

**The acquisition engine reaches a prospect four ways, in order, and stops the
moment they answer anywhere.**

```
  ① FORM        the contact form they published for exactly this purpose
       │  no reply
       ▼
  ② EMAIL       the researched proposal, their own words back to them
       │  no reply
       ▼
  ③ VOICE AI    an actual call — the agent, configured outbound
       │  ⭐ not answered  ── AMD decides ──►  ④ VOICEMAIL DROP
       │                                          the same proposal, spoken
       │  answered ──► ⭐ the AI has the conversation, and can book on the spot
       ▼
     replied on any rung ──► ⛔ LADDER STOPS. The agent takes the thread.
```

## 18C.1 ⛔ THE RULE THAT MATTERS MOST — STOP ON ANY REPLY, ANY CHANNEL

A reply to the **email** stops the **call**. A form auto-response stops the
**voicemail**. A text back to the caller ID stops **everything**.

⭐ **This is trivially easy for us and structurally hard for everyone else,
because of §11 and §15.** All four rungs write to **one `Conversation`** on one
`Person`. A reply on any transport is a `Message` on the same thread, and the
ladder reads one field.

⚠️ **Every competitor runs this as four tools with four databases**, which is why
their prospects get called about the email they already answered. **The seam
between their channels is where the embarrassment lives.** We don't have the
seam.

## 18C.2 ONE PROPOSAL, FOUR RENDERINGS

The research (X-135) produces **one proposal object** — the findings, the
evidence, the offer. Each rung renders it for its channel:

| Rung | Rendering | Length |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Form** | the tightest version — form fields are unforgiving | 1 short paragraph + link |
| **Email** | the full case: findings, evidence, what we'd do | 150–250 words |
| **Voice** | ⭐ spoken, conversational, and **it can answer questions** | a 20-second open, then a real conversation |
| **Voicemail** | 20–30 seconds, one finding, one reason to call back | ≤30s |

⭐ **Never four separately-written messages.** One set of findings, four
renderings — so the story is consistent whichever rung lands, and a prospect who
gets the email *and* the voicemail hears the same thing twice rather than two
different pitches.

**And the findings are only ours to make:** *"47 reviews, none answered since
March, and three competitors in your postcode answer within a day"* requires the
review intel, the geo-grid, and the audit engine to already exist (§18B.2).
Generic outreach tools cannot write that sentence.

## 18C.3 RUNG ③ — THE VOICE CALL IS THE SAME AGENT

⭐ **Not a dialler with a script. The front-desk agent (§16.1), configured
outbound.**

Which means on an answered call it can do everything the inbound agent does —
answer questions about what we found, handle the objection, quote from the price
list, **and book the meeting on the spot** — grounded in `Fact`, citing sources,
refusing to invent (§16.2).

- **Latency and cost:** the M1 targets hold — ≤600ms p50, ≤$0.10/min (§15.2).
- **Warm transfer** to a human on request, with the full context.
- **Every turn is a `Message`** on the same `Conversation` — so the transcript is
  in the thread beside the email that preceded it.

## 18C.4 RUNG ④ — VOICEMAIL DROP, AND WHAT MAKES IT WORK

⭐ **AMD — answering-machine detection — is the whole module.** Everything else is
plumbing.

| Detected | Action |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Human answers** | ⭐ hand to rung ③. **Never drop a voicemail on a live person** — that is the failure everyone has heard and remembers |
| **Machine / beep** | drop the 30-second proposal, then stop |
| **Ring-out, no pickup** | retry once at a different hour, then drop |
| **AMD uncertain** | ⛔ **treat as human.** A wrong drop is worse than a missed drop |

- **The voice is the tenant's configured agent voice** — the same one the prospect
  hears if they call back, so the callback is continuous rather than confusing.
- Sender identity stated in the first sentence. Callback number is the tenant's
  tracked number, so ⭐ **a returned call joins the same `Conversation` and the
  agent already knows the whole story.**
- Drop is logged as a `Message` with its recording and transcript.

## 18C.5 ADVANCE TIMING — DATA, NOT CODE

| Rung → rung | Default wait | Why |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| form → email | **2 days** | a form reply, if it comes, comes fast |
| email → voice | **3 days** | one full business cycle to read it |
| voice → voicemail | **immediate** | it is the same call attempt |
| voicemail → close | **stop** | ⭐ four touches and done. **The ladder never loops** |

⭐ **Every interval lives in the rate registry, not in code** — so a tenant can
tune the cadence, and we can tune it per vertical, without a deploy.

⛔ **The ladder never loops.** Four rungs, then the prospect returns to the pool
with a recorded outcome. A sequence that restarts itself is how outbound programs
destroy their own sender reputation and their brand at the same time.

## 18C.6 LANE ROUTING — MECHANICAL, ALREADY BUILT

The three-lane router (T450) already handles this, and each rung declares its
lane:

| Rung | Lane | Requires |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ① Form | the prospect's own published channel | nothing |
| ② Email | **Lane 3 — cold email** | accurate headers, postal address, working unsubscribe |
| ③ Voice | **Lane 2 — phone** | the recorded basis on the `Person` |
| ④ Voicemail | **Lane 2 — phone** | same |

⭐ **Nothing new to build.** The lane is a property of the rung, the router reads
it, and a prospect whose record can't satisfy a rung's lane **skips that rung and
continues** rather than stalling the ladder.

## 18C.7 WHAT THIS CONTRIBUTES

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Modules touched** | X-105 *(engine)* · X-77 *(orchestrator)* · X-109 *(form)* · C-Mail *(email)* · X-66 *(voice)* · X-79 *(voicemail + AMD)* · X-135 *(the proposal)* |
| **New modules** | **none** — the ladder is orchestration over modules that exist. **229 holds** |
| **Actions** | ~35 — `outreach.ladder.start` · `outreach.rung.advance` · `outreach.stop` · `voicemail.drop` · `amd.classify` |
| **Events** | `outreach.rung_sent` · `outreach.replied` ⭐ *(the stop signal)* · `outreach.exhausted` · `amd.detected` |
| **Seams** | ladder ↔ `Conversation` *(one thread, invalidated on reply)* · ladder ↔ `Person.state` *(a reply promotes prospect → contact, §11.2)* |

⭐ **The compounding effect worth naming:** a prospect who replies on rung ② has
just performed **their own act** — which is the one transition that promotes them
`PROSPECT → CONTACT` (§11.2). From that instant they are reachable on every lane,
the front-desk agent owns the thread, and the acquisition machine has handed off
to the product. **The ladder and the platform are the same system, and the
handoff costs nothing because there is nothing to hand.**
