# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §38 · M10 — SOCIAL  *(EXECUTED T497)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

> **⛔ FIRST-PASS SHAPE — PRECEDENCE (T667, §0.A):** first-pass social; current §148 (M19). *Nothing here is deleted (law 10); read §0.A before treating this section as current.*

## 38.0 ⭐ RESEARCH — SOCIAL FAILS ON EFFORT, NOT STRATEGY

**The numbers say organic social barely works any more:**

| Finding | Number |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔ **Organic reach for business pages** | **2–5% of followers per post** — *"paid amplification is a required component"* |
| ⛔ **Facebook feed composition** | ⭐ **up to 50% now comes from accounts users don't follow** — business pages pushed further down |
| ⭐ **Short-form video growth** | **+71% YoY**; Reels reach **~36% more users** than static images |
| Instagram median engagement | ~5.5% *(Buffer 2026, 52M posts)* |
| ⭐ **Retargeting CPL** | **40–70% lower** than cold audiences — *"often the highest-ROI paid channel for service businesses"* |
| Facebook Lead Ads | **$15–45 per contact** with proper geo-targeting |

### ⭐ SO WHAT IS SOCIAL *FOR*? THREE THINGS, AND ONLY ONE IS POSTING

| Function | Detail |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Trust validation** | *"Prospects who have already found you through Google or referral often check your social profiles to validate legitimacy. **A dormant or poorly managed presence loses deals that were almost closed.**"* |
| ⭐ **Retargeting infrastructure** | the pixel builds the audience; **the highest-ROI paid channel** |
| **Organic discovery** | ⭐ **only for visually rich verticals** — construction, landscaping, remodelling, salons |

⭐⭐ **That first line reframes the whole module.** For most local businesses
social is not a lead source — **it is a credibility check that happens after the
lead, and a dead page loses jobs that were already won.** So the goal is not
virality. **It is never looking abandoned.**

### The rest of what the research says

⭐ **"One or two platforms run well beats six run badly."** Priority: **GBP
weekly · Facebook 2–3×/week · Instagram 2–3×/week (skip if you can't produce
visuals) · LinkedIn daily for B2B.**

⭐ **Before-and-after photos are the single most powerful content asset** for
trades. **Facebook Groups** are where *"does anyone know a good electrician?"*
actually gets asked. **Nextdoor is underused and high-intent.** The **70/20/10**
mix: 70% educational, 20% community, 10% promotional.

⛔ **And the two lines that decide whether this module is worth building:**

> ⭐ *"**Unanswered DMs and ignored comments directly cost you booked jobs** —
> response time is as critical as your posting schedule."*
>
> ⭐ *"**If you can't connect a social media activity to a booked job, you're
> measuring the wrong things.**"*

---

## 38.1 ⭐⭐ X-182 `SocialAutopilot` — THE JOB IS THE CONTENT *(NEW)*

**Everything the research says works, we already generate as a by-product.**

| What works | Where it already comes from |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Before/after photos** *(the single most powerful asset)* | **X-171 TechMobile** — every completed job, uploaded at full quality (§30.4) |
| **Short-form video** *(+71%, 36% more reach)* | ⭐ **X-158 VideoEngine** — before/after pairs assembled automatically (§27.1) |
| **Educational content (70%)** | ⭐ **the questions customers actually asked** — call transcripts, chat, FAQ (§23.2) |
| **Social proof (20%)** | ⭐ **reviews, tagged by service and town** (§32.3 E7) |
| **Promotional (10%)** | the pricebook, offers, memberships |
| **Local relevance** | ⭐ **the job's own town** — *"another boiler sorted in Ashfield"* |

```
  job completed
       │
       ├─ photos ──► before/after pair ──► ⭐ post + Reel + GBP post
       ├─ service + town ──► the caption, specific and local
       ├─ review arrives ──► ⭐ social proof card
       └─ ⭐ scheduled into the cadence, not dumped
```

⭐⭐ **A tenant who does nothing still has a live, local, current page** — which is
precisely the *"never looks abandoned"* that the research says protects deals
already won. **The single biggest cause of social failure for a local business is
effort, and we removed it.**

**Cadence enforced, not suggested:** GBP weekly · Facebook and Instagram 2–3×/week
· ⭐ **Instagram auto-skipped if the tenant produces no visuals** *(the research's
own advice)* · LinkedIn daily only for B2B verticals. **70/20/10 mix balanced
automatically** from the available pool.

## 38.2 ⭐ THE SOCIAL INBOX — RESPONSE TIME IS THE PRODUCT

⛔ *"Unanswered DMs and ignored comments directly cost you booked jobs."*

⭐ **DMs and comments are `Conversation` rows** on the channel adapter pattern
(§15.1) — **so the front-desk agent answers them, in the same thread, with the
same grounding.** A comment asking *"how much for a service?"* gets the real price
from the pricebook, at 9pm, in under a minute.

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Platforms** | Facebook · Instagram · Google Business messages · LinkedIn · ⭐ **Nextdoor where the API allows** |
| ⭐ **Response SLA** | tracked and reported like any other channel — *because the research says it matters as much as posting* |
| **Escalation** | complaints and negative comments → human, immediately |
| ⭐ **Comment → lead** | a commenter who asks about price or availability becomes a `Person`, in the CRM, on the ladder |

## 38.3 ⭐ THE MEASUREMENT — CONNECT IT TO A BOOKED JOB

⭐ *"If you can't connect a social media activity to a booked job, you're
measuring the wrong things."*

**We can, and it needs no new machinery:** every social link carries the
`call_token` and campaign tags (§11.4), so a post → click → call → job → invoice
resolves through **X-138**, exactly like a page does.

| ⛔ Everyone reports | ⭐ We report |
| :--- | :--- |
| reach · impressions · followers | ⭐ **"this before/after post produced 3 calls and 2 booked jobs, £1,840"** |
| engagement rate | ⭐ **cost per booked job**, organic and paid |
| "best time to post" | ⭐ **which post type earns calls in this trade** |

## 38.4 PAID — WHERE THE RESEARCH SAYS THE ROI IS

⛔ **Full ads spec is M11.** What M10 wires:

- ⭐ **Retargeting audiences from the pixel** — 30–60 day window, **40–70% lower
  CPL**, and we already have the visitors (§19).
- ⭐ **Lookalikes from the customer list** — the research says it works at **200+
  past clients**, so ⭐ **the module tells the tenant when they cross that line**
  rather than letting them waste money before it.
- **Lead Ads** with geo-targeting, **$15–45/contact** as the benchmark to beat —
  ⭐ **and the lead lands in the CRM and on the ladder automatically** (§18C).
- ⭐ **Offline conversions pushed back** via X-139, so the ad platform optimises on
  **booked jobs, not form fills.**

## 38.5 THE PLATFORM SET

**Zernio covers 16 platforms through one endpoint** (§0.5) — publishing, OAuth
and the per-platform quirks. ⭐ **So the module spends its effort on *what to
post* rather than on *how to post it*.**

**Priority per the research, not per platform popularity:** GBP → Facebook →
Instagram *(visual verticals)* → Nextdoor *(hyper-local, underused)* → LinkedIn
*(B2B only)* → TikTok/YouTube Shorts *(where the video engine already produces
the cut)*.

⚠️ **Honest note:** platform APIs change constantly and Nextdoor's is the most
restricted. ⭐ **The adapter pattern means a platform that closes its API degrades
to a draft-and-notify, not a broken feature** — the same degrade-never-fail rule
as everywhere else (law 24w).

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §39 · ⭐⭐ X-183 `ContentStudio` — THE AI WRITES AND ILLUSTRATES  *(owner, T498)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

**M10 said the job produces the content. This is the engine that turns it into a
post — with its own topic and its own image.**

## 39.1 ⭐⭐ THE PHOTO SUPPLY CHAIN — AND THE SOURCE NOBODY USES

**Four sources, best first. And source ② is the one you named, which nobody
collects.**

| # | Source | Quality | Where it comes from |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **①** | **CUSTOMER-SENT PHOTOS** | ⭐ **the best there is** | see 39.2 |
| **②** | Technician before/after | very good | X-171 mobile, every job (§30.4) |
| **③** | The tenant's existing library | good | uploads, site, GBP |
| **④** | ⭐ **AI-generated** | fills gaps | X-178, its own model + cost line (§26.5) |
| **⑤** | Stock | last resort | flagged as stock, never passed off |

⭐ **Why customer photos beat everything:** a technician photographs *a completed
job*. **A customer photographs the thing they're proud of** — the finished
bathroom with their own towels in it, the driveway with their car back on it.
**One is documentation. The other is a recommendation.**

## 39.2 ⭐⭐ HOW WE GET THEM — THE QA MESSAGE ALREADY GOES OUT

⛔ **No new touchpoint. No extra message. It rides §37's QA step.**

```
  job completed ──► QA message *(already sending, §37.2)*
       │
       │  ⭐ "How did we do? If you're happy with how it looks,
       │      send us a photo — we'd love to see it."
       │
       ├─ 📷 arrives by SMS/MMS ──► ⭐ ALREADY a `Message` with media
       │                             on the `Conversation` (§11.5)
       │                             joined to the Job, the tech, the town
       │
       └─ ⭐ "Mind if we share it?"  ──► `share_permission` on the Asset
```

⭐ **It costs nothing to ask and it lands in the graph automatically**, because a
photo arriving by MMS was always a `Message` with media. **No new plumbing — one
sentence in a message that was already being sent.**

⭐ **Permission is a field, not a gate.** A yes marks the asset publishable; no
answer means it's used internally *(the QA report, the job record, the tech's
history)* and never published. **It's someone's home — asking is simply right,
and it costs one sentence.**

⭐ **And a customer who sends a photo has self-identified as delighted** — which
makes them the best review request, the best case study and the best referral ask
in the tenant's entire list. **The photo is a signal as much as an asset.**

## 39.3 ⭐ THE TOPIC ENGINE — NEVER A BLANK PAGE

**Eight sources, ranked by how specific and local they are:**

| Rank | Topic source | Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **1** | **The job just done** | *"Another leaking shower sorted in Ashfield this morning"* |
| ⭐ **2** | **Questions customers actually asked this week** | ⭐ *"Three people asked us this week whether a boiler service is worth it. Here's the honest answer."* — from **call transcripts** (§23.2) |
| **3** | **A review that just arrived** | tagged by service and town (§32.3 E7) |
| ⭐ **4** | **Seasonal demand** | ⭐ **from X-130's fleet counters** — *"boiler enquiries climb in week 41 round here; last year you were three weeks late"* |
| **5** | **An under-booked service** | the pricebook knows what isn't selling |
| **6** | **A gap the audit found** | a question competitors answer and they don't |
| **7** | **Weather and local events** | frozen pipes, storm damage, back-to-school |
| **8** | **Evergreen from the industry profile** | the 200-profile FAQ bank |

⭐⭐ **Source 2 is the one no competitor can reach.** Everyone else generates
"5 tips for winter plumbing" from a model's general knowledge. **We generate it
from three real people who rang up and asked this week** — which is specific,
timely, locally true, and answers a question the tenant's own market is
actively asking.

## 39.4 THE GENERATOR

```
  ① pick a topic          ranked pool, avoiding recent repeats
  ② choose the image      the ladder (39.1) — ⭐ real before generated, always
  ③ generate if needed    X-178, prompt built from the trade + the town + the season
  ④ write the caption     brand voice · grade ≤6 · the town named · one clear CTA
  ⑤ format per platform   ⭐ same post, different cut and length per surface
  ⑥ ⭐ preview or autopilot per the tenant's ladder (§14.1)
  ⑦ schedule into 70/20/10 (§38.1)
  ⑧ ⭐ measure in booked jobs (§38.3)
```

### The rules that keep it honest

| Rule | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔ **A generated image is never presented as their work** | *"a picture of a clean boiler install"* illustrates a point; **it never captions as a job they did** |
| ⭐ **Real always wins** | a generated image is **replaced automatically** the moment a real photo of that service arrives |
| ⛔ **Never a price in an image** | prices render from the registry, never burned into a graphic that can't be invalidated (§13.6) |
| ⭐ **Faces and property need permission** | source ① carries it; ② is the tenant's own job; ④ generates no identifiable person |
| **Grade ≤6, jargon linted** | same standard as every other string |
| ⭐ **Topic diversity enforced** | the pool tracks recency, so it can't post about drains four times running |

## 39.5 WHAT THE TENANT SEES

⭐ **One screen: next week's posts, already made.**

- Seven cards, each with its image, caption and platform.
- **Swap the image · edit the caption · reject · reschedule** — one tap each.
- ⭐ **"Why this post?"** on every card — *"three customers asked about this on the
  phone this week"*. **The reason is the sell** *(and it's `EXPLAIN`, §14.3)*.
- **Approve all** → the week is done in thirty seconds.
- ⭐ **Or autopilot** — and it still shows what it posted, after.

⭐ **This is the feature a local business actually wants**, and it is only possible
because the job, the transcript, the review, the photo and the pricebook are all
in one graph.

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §40 · ⭐⭐ X-184 `ContentPlan` · X-185 `GrowthLoop`  *(owner, T499)*
**The AI builds the plan, runs it, tests it, and learns what works**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 40.1 ⭐ X-184 `ContentPlan` — THEIR PLAN, NOT A CALENDAR TEMPLATE

**A 90-day plan built from their business, refreshed weekly.**

| Input | What it decides |
| :--- | :--- |
| Their **services and pricebook** | what gets promoted, and when |
| ⭐ **Their demand curve** *(X-130 fleet seasonality)* | ⭐ *"boiler content starts week 38 here, because enquiries climb week 41"* |
| **Their gaps** *(the audit)* | questions competitors answer and they don't |
| ⭐ **Their inbox** | what customers are actually asking, this month |
| **Their capacity** | ⛔ **don't promote emergency work in a week they're already full** |
| **Their assets** | what photos and reviews exist, and what's missing |
| **Their vertical** | the platform mix and cadence the research prescribes (§38.0) |

⭐⭐ **The capacity input is the one nobody thinks of.** Marketing that fills an
already-full week produces angry customers and no revenue. **The plan reads the
dispatch board** (§29.2) and pushes the services with slack.

### If an asset doesn't exist, it makes one

```
  plan needs: a before/after for bathroom fits
       │
       ├─ real photo exists? ──── yes ──► use it
       │        no
       ├─ ⭐ ask: the QA message on the next bathroom job requests one (§39.2)
       │        still nothing
       └─ ⭐ GENERATE IT — X-178, illustrative, never captioned as their work
                │
                └─ ⭐ and it self-replaces the moment a real one arrives (§39.4)
```

⛔ **The plan never stalls for want of an asset.** It generates, flags the gap on
the tenant's screen, and upgrades itself later.

## 40.2 ⭐⭐ X-185 `GrowthLoop` — THE SELF-LEARNING PART

> ⭐ **It optimises toward BOOKED JOBS, not engagement.**
> *Every content optimiser on the market maximises clicks. Clicks are free to
> measure and worth nothing. **We already have the job.***

```
  ⭐ EXPLORE ──► try a variant        (format · topic · time · platform · CTA · image type)
       │
  ⭐ MEASURE ──► pixel → call_token → call → job → revenue   (X-138, already built)
       │
  ⭐ LEARN   ──► shift allocation toward what earns
       │
  ⭐ EXPLOIT ──► more of what works, while STILL exploring
       │
       └──────────► weekly, forever, per tenant AND across the fleet
```

### ⛔ 40.3 THE HARD PROBLEM — AND IT IS REAL

**A plumber posts three times a week and books twenty jobs a month. That is
nowhere near enough data to declare a winner on a single post.**

⛔ **Most "AI optimisation" features declare winners on noise.** Ours will not.
Four solutions, and the first is the one only we can do:

| # | Solution | |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **1** | **LEARN AT THE FLEET LEVEL, APPLY AT THE TENANT LEVEL** | ⭐ *"Before/after photos out-earn educational posts 3:1 for plumbers"* is learnable across **500 plumbers** even though **no single plumber has the volume.** X-130's counters already aggregate this. **A single-tenant tool can never do this at any price** |
| ⭐ **2** | **Test FORMATS, not posts** | don't A/B two captions at n=4. Test **whether before/after beats educational for this trade in this town** — a question with real sample behind it |
| ⭐ **3** | **Bandit, not 50/50** | a multi-armed bandit shifts allocation toward the winner *while still exploring* — ⛔ **a classic A/B wastes half your posts on the loser, which a business posting 3×/week cannot afford** |
| ⭐ **4** | **Leading indicators, validated against jobs** | clicks, calls and DM replies arrive fast; **booked jobs are the truth.** A leading indicator that stops predicting jobs is **discarded, not trusted** |

### ⭐⭐ 40.4 THE HONESTY RULE — THE PART THAT MAKES IT CREDIBLE

> ⛔ **It says "not enough data yet" and keeps both running.**

| Situation | ⭐ What it says |
| :--- | :--- |
| n too small | *"Before/after is ahead, but it's 6 jobs vs 4 — **not a real difference yet.** Both still running."* |
| Fleet-confident, tenant-unproven | ⭐ *"This works for plumbers generally. **We're still testing whether it works for you.**"* |
| A confound it can see | ⭐ *"Your calls doubled in week 3, but so did everyone's in your area — **that was the cold snap, not the post.**"* |
| Genuinely proven | *"Before/after posts produced 11 booked jobs in 90 days. Educational produced 2. **We've shifted the mix.**"* |

⭐⭐ **That third row is only possible because of the fleet.** A single-tenant tool
would have claimed credit for the cold snap. **We can see it was weather because
we can see every other plumber in the region.**

⚠️ **Stated limits, in the product, not just here:** attribution windows *(a post
today can produce a call in three weeks — the window is 30 days and it's shown)*
· seasonality and weather confound everything *(hence the fleet baseline)* · a
tenant who changes their prices mid-test invalidates it *(and we say so)*.

### 40.5 WHAT IT TESTS

| Dimension | Variants |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Format** | before/after · educational · review card · video · carousel · plain photo |
| **Topic class** | the eight sources (§39.3) |
| **Timing** | day and hour, per platform |
| **Platform mix** | ⭐ **including "stop posting here"** — a platform earning nothing gets dropped |
| **CTA** | call · book · message · quote |
| **Image type** | ⭐ **customer-sent vs technician vs generated** — *and we expect source ① to win, but we'll measure it* |
| **Caption length and voice** | within brand-voice constraints |

⭐ **It also tests beyond content**, because the loop is generic: **offers · which
services to promote · outreach ladder timing · review-request wording · the QA
threshold.** Anything with an `outcome_event` (§12.1) is testable, **which is
every action in the registry.**

## 40.6 ⭐ AUTOPILOT — THE SAME LADDER

Per §14.1, never a separate switch:

```
  OBSERVE ──► SUGGEST ──► APPROVE-EACH ──► ⭐ AUTO(content) ──► AUTO(content + budget)
```

**Default is APPROVE-EACH.** ⭐ **The weekly card shows what it changed and why**
— *"shifted 2 of your 3 weekly posts to before/after; that format has produced 4
of your last 5 attributed jobs."* **Any change is one tap to revert**, and
⭐ **every allocation shift is an `ActionInvocation`**, so `EXPLAIN` can answer
*"why am I posting more photos?"* from the record.

⛔ **Budget autopilot is opt-in separately** and capped by the tenant. *Content
allocation is reversible; spend is not.*

## 40.7 WHAT §40 ADDS

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **New modules** | ⭐⭐ **X-184 `ContentPlan`** · ⭐⭐ **X-185 `GrowthLoop`** → **260 total** |
| **Actions** | ~55 — `plan.build` · `plan.gap.fill` · `loop.variant.start` · `loop.result.get` · `loop.allocation.shift` |
| **Events** | `plan.built` · `plan.gap_detected` · ⭐ `loop.winner_found` · `loop.inconclusive` · `loop.confound_detected` |
| **Reuses** | X-183 generator · X-178 images · X-110 pixel · **X-138 attribution** · X-130 fleet counters · X-141 replay · X-145 decisioning · X-162 capacity |
| **New modules needed for the loop itself** | ⛔ **none beyond these two — the measurement was built at S1** |

⭐⭐ **The line that matters:** every content optimiser on the market maximises
engagement because engagement is what they can see. **We maximise booked revenue
because `Job.originating_asset_id` has existed since turn one** — and we learn
across the whole fleet, which is the one advantage a single-tenant tool can never
buy.

## 40.8 ACCEPTANCE — §40

☐ ⭐ 90-day plan from their services, demand curve, gaps, inbox, ⭐ **capacity** and assets
☐ ⛔ **Plan never stalls** — generates the missing asset, flags the gap, self-upgrades
☐ ⭐ Loop optimises to **booked jobs**, never engagement
☐ ⭐⭐ **Fleet-level learning applied at tenant level** — the low-volume solution
☐ Formats tested, not individual posts; ⭐ **bandit not 50/50**
☐ Leading indicators **validated against jobs** and discarded when they stop predicting
☐ ⭐⭐ **"Not enough data yet" said out loud**, with both variants still running
☐ ⭐ Confounds named — *"that was the cold snap, not the post"*
☐ Autopilot on the standard ladder; ⭐ **budget opt-in separately and capped**
☐ Every shift an `ActionInvocation`, explainable and revertible

**All ten ✅ — §40 COMPLETE.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §41 · ⭐⭐ X-186 `CampaignManager` — MANY CAMPAIGNS, ONE QUEUE  *(owner, T500)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 41.1 ⭐ WHY MORE THAN ONE CAMPAIGN IS REAL

**Not a power-user feature. These are ordinary local businesses:**

| Business | Why one campaign isn't enough |
| :--- | :--- |
| Plumber doing **domestic and commercial** | ⭐ different audience, tone, platform, offer — *a landlord and a homeowner are not the same person* |
| Salon: **hair · beauty · training courses** | three products, three audiences |
| ⭐ **Multi-location** | each town has its own jobs, its own reviews, its own audience |
| **Seasonal push** | *"summer AC"* runs **alongside** always-on brand content, not instead of it |
| **New service launch** | *"we do EV chargers now"* — a burst, then it folds into the main campaign |
| ⭐⭐ **Recruitment** | **trades are desperate for staff, and hiring content is a completely different campaign** — different audience, different platform, different everything |

⭐ **Recruitment is the one that surprises people and it may be the most valuable
one on the list.** A trades business that can't hire can't grow, and nobody sells
them a hiring campaign.

## 41.2 ⭐⭐ THE SIMPLICITY RULE — YOU NEVER MEET THE CONCEPT UNTIL YOU NEED IT

> ⭐ **Everyone starts with exactly one campaign, created automatically, never
> named, never mentioned.**

**The word "campaign" does not appear in the UI until the tenant adds a second
one.** Until then it is just *"your content."*

⛔ **This is the whole answer to "make it super easy."** The complexity exists,
it is fully built, and **it stays invisible to the 80% who will never need it.**

### Adding one is four questions

```
  ⭐ + New campaign
       ├─ ① Who's it for?      → Commercial · Homeowners · Recruitment ·
       │                          A location · A specific service · Custom
       ├─ ② What do you want?  → Enquiries · Bookings · Applications · Awareness
       ├─ ③ How often?         → the cadence control (41.3)
       └─ ④ Where?             → platforms, pre-picked from ① and the vertical
```

⭐ **Six starter templates**, so nobody starts blank: **Commercial ·
Recruitment · New service · Seasonal · Location · Blank.** Each arrives with a
cadence, a platform set and a content mix already sensible for that job.

## 41.3 ⭐ THE CADENCE CONTROL

**One slider, five presets, and custom underneath:**

| Preset | Volume | Suits |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Quiet** | 1×/week | *"just don't look abandoned"* — ⭐ **and per §38.0 that alone protects deals** |
| **Light** | 2×/week | most sole traders |
| ⭐ **Standard** *(default)* | **3–4×/week** | the research's own recommendation (§38.0) |
| **Active** | daily | visual trades with steady job flow |
| ⭐ **Aggressive** | **2×/day** | salons, restaurants, retail — high-volume visual businesses |
| **Custom** | ⭐ **X per week, or exact days and times** | anyone |

**Per-platform overrides**, because one number can't fit all: ⭐ **GBP weekly is
correct even when Instagram is daily.** Set the campaign cadence once; override
per platform only if you want to.

## 41.4 ⭐⭐ THE TRAP — AND THE FEATURE THAT COMES FROM SOLVING IT

⛔ **"Twice daily" is 14 posts a week. A sole trader completing 3 jobs a week does
not have 14 posts' worth of real material.** The system would start generating
filler — **and filler is worse than silence**, because it reads as a business with
nothing to say.

### ⭐⭐ THE SUPPLY METER — shown the moment they move the slider

```
  You've asked for 14 posts/week.

  ⭐ Your real material supports about 5:
      3 jobs  ·  1 review  ·  1 customer photo

  The other 9 would be generated educational content.
  ⭐ That's fine — but here's how to make more of it real:

     ├─ ⭐ Ask customers for photos  ── ON      (+2–3/week typical)
     ├─ Ask techs for before/afters ── OFF → turn on   (+3/week)
     └─ Or drop to Active (daily) and every post is real.
```

⭐⭐ **No competitor tells a customer their cadence is too high.** They sell the
higher plan and let the feed fill with slop. **Showing the supply is honest, it's
useful, and it sells the thing that actually helps** — turning on photo requests,
which is free and improves everything downstream.

**And it self-corrects:** ⭐ if real material dries up, the cadence **eases back
automatically** and says so, rather than padding. *(Law 25 — automatic, not an
alert.)*

## 41.5 ⛔ ONE QUEUE — CAMPAIGNS PROPOSE, THE SCHEDULER PLACES

**The failure mode of multi-campaign systems is three campaigns posting to
Instagram at 9am on the same Tuesday.**

```
  campaign A ─┐
  campaign B ─┼──► ⭐ ONE SCHEDULER ──► one queue PER PLATFORM ──► published
  campaign C ─┘
                    enforces:
                    ├─ ⭐ minimum gap between posts on a platform
                    ├─ ⭐ a total daily cap per platform, whatever the campaign count
                    ├─ no two posts about the same service in a row
                    ├─ priority when they collide (⭐ time-sensitive wins)
                    └─ ⛔ a campaign CANNOT publish directly
```

⭐ **Campaigns never touch a platform.** They propose content with a desired
window; the scheduler decides when it actually goes. **Collision is structurally
impossible, not policed.**

⭐ **And one calendar shows everything merged**, colour-coded by campaign — so a
tenant with four campaigns still sees **one week, one view.**

## 41.6 EACH CAMPAIGN LEARNS SEPARATELY

X-185's loop (§40.2) runs **per campaign**, because each has its own goal:

| Campaign | Optimises toward |
| :--- | :--- |
| Domestic | ⭐ **booked jobs** |
| Commercial | ⭐ **enquiries** *(the cycle is too long for job attribution)* |
| ⭐ **Recruitment** | ⭐ **applications** |
| Seasonal | bookings inside the window |

⭐ **Fleet learning is shared across all of them** — *"before/after out-earns
educational for plumbers"* holds whichever campaign it's in. **Tenant-level
learning stays per campaign**, because what works for landlords isn't what works
for homeowners.

⚠️ **And the honesty rule holds harder here:** splitting a low-volume business
across four campaigns means **four small samples**. The loop says so, leans on
fleet learning until tenant data accumulates, and ⭐ **warns if a campaign is too
small to ever learn** — *"this campaign has produced 2 jobs in 90 days; we'll
follow the fleet pattern rather than pretend we've learned something."*

## 41.7 WHAT §41 ADDS

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **New module** | ⭐⭐ **X-186 `CampaignManager`** → **261 total** |
| **Actions** | ~35 — `campaign.create` · `campaign.cadence.set` · `campaign.supply.check` · `schedule.queue.get` · `campaign.pause` |
| **Events** | `campaign.created` · ⭐ `supply.insufficient` · `cadence.auto_eased` · `schedule.collision_resolved` |
| **Content** | ⭐ 6 campaign templates → the content pack (§34) |
| **Seams** | 7 — `campaign→scheduler` *(propose only)* · `plan→campaign` · `campaign→loop` · `supply→cadence` |

⭐⭐ **The design in one line: complexity available, invisible by default, and the
system tells you the truth about whether your cadence is achievable.**

## 41.8 ACCEPTANCE — §41

☐ ⭐ One campaign by default, **created automatically, never named** — the word doesn't appear until they add a second
☐ Four questions to add one; ⭐ **six starter templates incl. Recruitment**
☐ Cadence: five presets **Quiet → Aggressive (2×/day)** plus custom, per-platform overrides
☐ ⭐⭐ **The supply meter** — shows real material vs requested, and how to make more of it real
☐ ⭐ Cadence **eases back automatically** when material dries up, and says so
☐ ⛔ **Campaigns propose; only the scheduler publishes.** Collision structurally impossible
☐ Per-platform gaps and daily caps regardless of campaign count
☐ ⭐ One merged calendar, colour-coded
☐ Loop runs per campaign with its own goal; fleet learning shared
☐ ⭐ **Warns when a campaign is too small to ever learn**, and follows the fleet instead

**All ten ✅ — §41 COMPLETE.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §42 · M11 — ADS  ⛔ *(DESCOPED T503 — SEE §44. Kept for the record.)*
⛔ **The LSA platform is migrating THIS MONTH. Read 42.0 first.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

> **⛔ DESCOPED — PRECEDENCE (T667, §0.A):** by §44 — ads management fenced; kept for the record. *Nothing here is deleted (law 10); read §0.A before treating this section as current.*

## 42.0 ⛔⛔ LOCAL SERVICES ADS ARE MOVING INTO GOOGLE ADS — AUGUST 2026

**Research caught a migration that started this month and directly re-scopes
X-174** (§30.6).

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **What** | LSAs become **Performance Max pay-per-lead campaigns inside Google Ads** |
| ⛔ **The standalone LSA dashboard** | ⭐ **goes away after migration** |
| **Started** | ⭐ **August 2026** — US home and storefront services: **plumbing · HVAC · electrical · appliance repair · house cleaning · lawn care · roofing · pest control · moving.** *That is our core customer list, first in the queue* |
| **Late 2026** | service-area businesses without storefronts · custom bidding and booking configs |
| **2027** | non-US accounts and all remaining categories |
| **What doesn't change** | keywordless · Search and Maps only · **pay per valid lead — calls, messages, bookings — not clicks** · driven by the GBP |
| ⛔ **What is lost** | ⭐⭐ **historical performance reports do NOT migrate.** Google says download them first |
| **Notice** | 14-day email, 7-day reminder, warning banners |
| ⚠️ **Downtime** | ⭐ campaigns **may pause 24–48h** while Google reviews |
| **Also** | **BBB callouts deprecated** — need **6+ other structured callouts** |

### ⭐⭐ X-174 RE-SCOPED — AND THE MIGRATION IS A FEATURE

**Every one of our first-wave verticals gets 14 days' notice and loses their
history. We can make that painless:**

| ⭐ What X-174 now does | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Export history BEFORE migration** | **automatically, on the 14-day notice** — *the one thing Google tells them to do and most won't* |
| **Detect the migration** | from the notice, the banner, or the account shape |
| ⭐ **Warn about the 24–48h pause** | so a pause isn't mistaken for a broken campaign |
| **Rebuild the 6+ callouts** | BBB is dead; ⭐ **we generate replacements from the GBP** — hours, specialties, payment methods |
| ⭐ **Keep our own reporting regardless** | ⭐⭐ **their Google history vanishes; ours doesn't** — we hold every lead, call and job in our own graph (§22.2) |
| **Manage post-migration** | inside Google Ads, PMax pay-per-lead, GBP sync via Data Manager |

⭐⭐ **That last row is the quiet win.** A business that loses years of LSA
reporting still has **every lead, every call and every booked job in our
database** — because we were never reading it from Google's dashboard.

---

## 42.1 ⭐ SEARCH FIRST — AND THIS IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT GOOGLE PUSHES

| Finding | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Search beats PMax on cost per qualified lead by 25–45%** for service businesses | *independent 2026 data* |
| **PMax generates higher volume, lower quality** | its reach includes people **not actively searching** |
| ⛔ **PMax needs 30–50 conversions** before it works | most of our tenants don't have that |
| ⭐ **"For local service businesses, the honest answer is: proceed with extreme caution"** | on PMax |

⛔ **So the default is Search, and the module says why** — because Google's own
interface pushes the opposite, and a tenant who follows the prompts pays 25–45%
more per lead.

**PMax is offered when, and only when, the tenant crosses 30–50 monthly
conversions** — ⭐ **and we know exactly when that happens, because we count
booked jobs, not form fills.**

## 42.2 ⭐⭐ X-187 `AdWasteGuard` — THE 25% *(NEW)*

> ⛔ **"The average small business wastes 25% of its ad spend on irrelevant
> clicks — $500–1,250 per month lighting on fire."**

**On a £500/month budget that's £125 gone before anything works. This module
exists to take it back.**

| Guard | What it does |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Presence, not interest** | ⛔ **Set location options to "people in or regularly in your targeted locations" — NOT the default**, which includes people merely *interested* in the area. ⭐ *One setting, and most accounts have it wrong* |
| ⭐ **Real radius, not the metro** | target their **actual service area**, not the wider metro Google suggests — and ⭐ **we have the service area from the `Location` record** |
| **Aggressive location exclusions** | the towns they don't serve, excluded explicitly |
| ⭐ **Negative keywords, continuously** | *jobs · salary · DIY · free · courses · "how to" · wholesale* — plus ⭐ **mined from the search terms that produced calls that went nowhere** |
| ⭐⭐ **Waste report in money** | *"£118 last month on searches that never produced a call. Here they are."* |
| **Placement exclusions** | for anything running on Display |
| ⭐ **Budget protection** | daily caps and pacing so one bad day can't eat a week |

⭐⭐ **The negative-keyword mining is ours alone.** Everyone builds negative lists
from guesswork. **We build them from search terms that produced a click, a visit
and no call** — because the pixel and the call tracking are the same system
(§19.4 tier 4).

## 42.3 LOW-VOLUME BIDDING — A DISTINCT DISCIPLINE

⭐ **Local service accounts are low-volume, and most bidding advice assumes they
aren't.**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Learning reality** | ⭐ **meaningful conversion data takes 4–8 weeks; PMax 6–8; budget 3 months before firm conclusions** |
| **Start** | manual or maximise-clicks with tight caps until conversions accumulate |
| **Then** | maximise-conversions, and only later target-CPA |
| ⛔ **Never** | switch strategy mid-learning — ⭐ **it restarts the clock, and the module refuses to let you** |
| ⭐ **The honesty rule** | **the same as §40.4** — *"3 conversions is not a trend"* |

## 42.4 ⭐⭐ WHAT WE FEED GOOGLE THAT NOBODY ELSE CAN

```
  ad click ──► visit ──► call (call_token) ──► job ──► invoice ──► PAID
                                                          │
                                                          └──► ⭐ X-139 pushes it
                                                               back as an offline
                                                               conversion
```

⭐⭐ **So Google's bidding optimises on booked revenue instead of form fills.**
Most small accounts feed the platform a "conversion" that is a phone-click or a
form submit — **half of which are wrong numbers, tyre-kickers and wrong-area
enquiries.** We feed it the ones that paid.

| ⛔ Everyone optimises on | ⭐ We optimise on |
| :--- | :--- |
| clicks | **booked jobs** |
| form fills | **invoiced revenue** |
| phone-click events | ⭐ **calls that lasted, converted and paid** |
| cost per lead | ⭐⭐ **cost per booked job** |

## 42.5 META AND THE REST

⭐ **"Google captures demand; Meta creates demand."** Both, with different jobs:

| Channel | Job | From the research |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Search** | capture | the backbone, **25–45% better CPL than PMax** |
| **LSA / PMax pay-per-lead** | capture, top of Search and Maps | pay per valid lead |
| ⭐ **Meta retargeting** | ⭐ **the highest-ROI paid channel** | **40–70% lower CPL** than cold (§38.4) |
| **Meta Lead Ads** | create | **$15–45 per contact** geo-targeted |
| **Lookalikes** | create | ⭐ needs **200+ past clients** — *and we flag when they cross it* |
| **PMax** | scale | ⛔ **only above 30–50 conversions** |

⭐ **All lead forms land in the CRM and on the outreach ladder automatically**
(§18C) — *a Meta lead that sits in Ads Manager for three days is a lost job, and
that is the commonest failure in small-business paid social.*

## 42.6 THE MODULE SET — X-41…X-55

Audience builder *(from the pixel and the customer list)* · budget manager ·
bid strategy · creative from **X-183** · geo and radius · dayparting *(⭐ **from
the dispatch board — don't advertise emergency work when nobody can go**)* ·
competitor monitoring · landing-page matching · call-only campaigns · seasonal
scheduling from **X-130** · spend pacing · **cross-channel budget allocation
learned by X-185** · the waste report · the offline conversion push · unified
reporting in **cost per booked job**.

## 42.7 WHAT M11 CONTRIBUTES

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Actions** | ~140 |
| **Events** | 18 — `ad.lead_received` · ⭐ `ad.waste_detected` · `ad.migration_notice` · `budget.paced` · `conversion.uploaded` |
| **New module** | ⭐⭐ **X-187 `AdWasteGuard`** → **262 total** |
| **Re-scoped** | ⭐ **X-174 — LSA migration handling, history export, callout rebuild** |
| **Register lines drained** | 51 *(cumulative 739)* |
| **Seams** | 13 — ⭐ `job→offline_conversion` · `search_term→negative_keyword` · `dispatch→dayparting` · `pixel→audience` |

⭐⭐ **The position:** every small business wastes a quarter of its ad budget and
optimises on the wrong signal. **We cut the waste with their own call data, feed
the platforms booked revenue instead of form fills, and report in cost per booked
job** — and when Google takes their LSA history away this month, **we still have
all of it.**

## 42.8 ACCEPTANCE — M11

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §43 · ⛔⛔ LAUNCH REQUIREMENTS — NOTHING SHIPS WITHOUT THESE  *(owner + dev, T502)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

⛔ **Every item here is launch-blocking. This section is a checklist, not a
discussion.**

## 43.1 ⭐⭐ X-188 `NumberPool` — THE 10DLC BRIDGE *(NEW)*

> ⭐ **The review engine, missed-call text-back and reactivation all run on the
> GO AI EZ internal number pool until the tenant's own 10DLC is approved.**

⛔ **10DLC approval takes days to weeks and is outside our control. Without this,
a new tenant can't send anything on day one — which kills the whole
time-to-value story.**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Pool** | GO AI EZ-owned numbers, allocated per tenant on signup |
| **Assignment** | ⭐ **sticky** — a tenant keeps the same pool number throughout, so their customers see one number |
| **Runs on it** | ⭐ **missed-call text-back · review requests · reactivation** |
| ⭐ **Migration** | when their own 10DLC lands, ⭐ **traffic moves automatically** and the pool number is retained for a grace period so replies to the old number still land |
| **Conversation continuity** | ⛔ **the `Conversation` never breaks** — the number changed, the thread didn't (§11.5) |
| **Pool health** | per-number volume caps, rotation, ⭐ **reputation monitored per number** — one tenant can't damage the pool for everyone |

### ⭐ VOICE ON POOL NUMBERS — RESOLVED

**The question was what happens when someone rings a pool number back. Three
tiers, cheapest and simplest first:**

```
  inbound call to a pool number
       │
  ⭐ ① FORWARD to the tenant's real business number     ← default, simplest
       │  no answer / not configured
  ⭐ ② INFOBIP VOICEMAIL  ── recorded ──► transcribed ──► ⭐ lands in the inbox
       │                                                   as a `Message` on the
       │                                                   same `Conversation`
  ⭐ ③ full AI voice agent — only once their own number and 10DLC are live
```

⭐ **Tier ① is a forward and takes minutes to build.** Tier ② is the safety net so
**a returned call is never lost**. ⛔ **A pool number that rings out to nothing is
the one unacceptable outcome.recorded — someone called back a text they received, and
that's a lead.

## 43.2 ⭐ X-189 `ImageOverlay` — REACTIVATION IMAGERY *(NEW)*

**Reactivation messages need an image with the customer's name on it.**

```
  need an image
       ├─ ⭐ client image exists? ──► use it
       └─ no ──► ⭐ AI generates one (X-178)
                        │
       ⭐ OVERLAY SCRIPT puts the NAME on it ──► personalised MMS
```

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Overlay** | name, safe-area positioned, contrast-checked against the underlying image |
| **Templates** | per industry, from the profile |
| ⭐ **Fallback chain** | client image → generated → **brand-colour card with the name**, so ⛔ **it never fails to produce something** |
| **Cost** | AI credits for generation; ⭐ **the overlay itself is free** |
| **Reused** | the same overlay serves review requests, seasonal campaigns and offers |

## 43.3 ⭐⭐ THE TRIAL AND THE METERS — CONFIRMED NUMBERS

| Meter | Included | Top-ups |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **SMS** | ⭐⭐ **500/month, SHARED** across missed-call · review · reactivation | **$50 → 1,000** · **$250 → 10,000** |
| ⭐ **AI credits** | ⭐ **$50/month** | **$100** · ⭐ **$300 → $400** *(33% bonus)* |
| **Voice** | 100 min *(§18E.2)* | $100 → $100 · $300 → $400 |
| **Lead credits** | 10k/month | +10k/$100 · +100k/$500 |
| ⭐ **AI markup** | ⭐⭐ **8:1 — costs us $1, deducts $8 in credit** | derived from cent-precision `ai_calls`, never typed |

⭐ **"Shared across three systems" is the important word.** One SMS balance, three
consumers — so a tenant running a big reactivation push sees their missed-call
budget move, **and the panel shows the split.**

⭐ **Auto top-up on all of them** (§17.6). ⛔ **A missed-call text-back must never
fail for want of balance.**

## 43.4 ⭐ THE MODEL ROSTER — CHEAPEST FIRST, SECOND-CHEAPEST FOR DEPTH

**Two tiers per provider** (§28.3), so the router always has a cheap default and a
better option:

| Provider | ⭐ Cheapest *(tier 1 default)* | Second-cheapest *(tier 2)* |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **OpenAI** | ⭐ **GPT-5 mini class** | the next model up |
| **OpenAI images** | ⭐ **cheapest image model** | next up |
| **Google** | ⭐ **cheapest Gemma** | next Gemma up |
| **xAI** | ⭐ **cheapest Grok** | next Grok up |

⭐ **Failover across providers, not just tiers:** ⛔ **if one doesn't respond, it
goes to the next AI** — sideways at the same tier first, then up (§28.3). **Timeout
is a hard budget; a slow model is a failed model.**

⭐ **Every model is a row in `platform_settings`** — added, removed or reordered
**with no deploy**, and the roster is expected to change monthly.

## 43.5 ⭐⭐ THE AI CORE MUST SUPPORT — CONFIRMED LIST

⛔ **Launch-blocking. The agent can do all of these or it isn't finished:**

| ✅ | Capability |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ | **Send a payment link** *(§25.3)* |
| ⭐ | **Send a booking link** and book directly *(§29.3)* |
| ⭐ | **Answer from the FAQ** |
| ⭐ | **Answer from the knowledge base** *(uploads, §28.2)* |
| ⭐ | **Quote from the price list** |
| ⭐⭐ | **Quote a price RANGE** where a fixed price isn't possible |
| ⭐⭐ | **State the minimum fee to come out and quote** — *the single most-asked question in the trades, and the one that wastes the most time when unanswered* |
| ⭐ | Hours, service area, what they do and don't do |
| ⭐ | Take a message, flag urgency, hand to a human |

⭐ **Price range and callout fee are the two that stop time-wasting calls.**
*"It's £85 to come out and that comes off the job if you go ahead"* answers the
question a caller is actually asking, and the pricebook (§30.2) already holds it.

## 43.6 ⭐ REACTIVATION — TRIAGE INTO THE CRM

**Reactivation replies are triaged, not dumped:**

```
  reactivation sent ──► reply
       ├─ interested ──► ⭐ CRM as a live opportunity, agent continues
       ├─ question ──► agent answers, from the same grounding
       ├─ not now ──► ⭐ dated, re-queued for the right season
       ├─ stop ──► suppressed for that tenant (§17.1)
       └─ complaint ──► ⛔ human, immediately
```

⭐ **Every outcome lands in the CRM on the existing `Person` and `Conversation`.**
No separate reactivation list to reconcile.

## 43.7 ⭐⭐ MISSED-CALL ALERTS + THE 5-CHARACTER CODE

**Important missed calls text the tenant. The tenant replies by SMS. Everything
merges.**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Importance** | scored — new caller · repeat caller · out of hours · high-value service · existing customer |
| **Alert** | SMS to the owner, with the caller, the reason and ⭐ **the code** |
| ⭐⭐ **The code** | **5 characters, alphanumeric, never reused inside the TTL window** *(§20.2)* — ⛔ **a recycled code routes one customer's reply into another's thread; invisible in testing, obvious in production** |
| **They reply** | *"C"* call · *"T"* text · *"S"* snooze · *"X"* ignore — ⭐ **or free text, which the agent sends as the reply** |
| ⭐ **Merged** | ⛔ **the alert, the reply, the resulting call and the customer's own texts are ONE `Conversation`** |

## 43.8 ⭐ ALERT HOURS AND ROUTING — PER TENANT, PER CLASS

⭐ **Confirmed and expanded from §20.2:**

| Setting | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Quiet hours** | when they do **not** want alerts, per class |
| **Active hours** | when they **do** |
| ⭐ **Out-of-hours routing** | ⭐ **to a different number and/or email** — *the on-call phone, the office inbox* |
| **Per day** | ⭐ **different rules Saturday to Sunday** |
| **Escalation** | unacknowledged in N minutes → next recipient |
| **Rate cap** | ⭐ alert fatigue kills the feature faster than a bug |

## 43.9 ⭐ REVIEW REQUEST SURFACES — ALL FOUR

| Surface | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **SMS** | the default *(§37)* |
| ⭐ **Email** | ⭐ **full email review-request system** — template, brand, tracked, same triage |
| ⭐⭐ **QR code** | ⭐ **printed on the invoice, the van, the door hanger, the receipt.** Per-tenant, per-location, ⭐ **and per-technician so you can see who earns reviews** |
| ⭐ **Private link** | a permanent link the tenant can send **any way they like** — WhatsApp, in person, a business card |

⛔ **All four run the same triage** (§37.1) and the same threshold. **One rule,
four doors.**

## 43.10 ⭐ THE CLIENT IS IN THEIR OWN SYSTEM

⭐ **The tenant, their staff and their technicians are `Person` records in their
own tenant** — so they receive, appear in and are measured by the same systems as
their customers. **No parallel admin universe.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §45 · M12a — MONEY I  *(EXECUTED T503)*
**The rate registry · plans · credits · ⭐ dunning**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

> **⛔ FIRST-PASS SHAPE — PRECEDENCE (T667, §0.A):** money I; §45.2 grace rules SUPERSEDED by §45A; current §149 (M20a). *Nothing here is deleted (law 10); read §0.A before treating this section as current.*

## 45.0 ⭐⭐ RESEARCH — INVOLUNTARY CHURN IS THE BIGGEST PREVENTABLE LEAK

| Finding | Number |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Failed payments as a share of ALL SaaS churn** | **20–40%** |
| ⭐ **Card payments that fail on first attempt** | **10–15%** *(Visa/Mastercard)* — ACH/direct debit only **3–5%** |
| ⛔ **Median recovery rate** | ⭐ **47.6%** — *"more than half of every failed payment converts into involuntary churn"* |
| ⭐ **Best-in-class recovery** | **70–85%** |
| **MRR lost annually without dunning** | **9–12%** |
| ⭐ **Retry schedule alone — Day 1, 3, 5, 7** | ⭐ **recovers 58% with NO customer communication** *(Recurly, 40M transactions)* |
| ⭐ **Pre-dunning** *(prompt before the card expires)* | **+15–22% of at-risk revenue** |
| ⭐ **Multi-channel vs email-only** | ⭐ **cuts involuntary churn by up to 34%** |
| **Proactive dunning → chargebacks** | **−35–45%** |

> ⭐⭐ *"Involuntary churn is a billing infrastructure problem. It has a known fix
> with known economics, and you can calculate the recovery value before you invest
> a dollar."*

⛔ **And the line that frames the whole module:** *"Every failed payment that is
not recovered is revenue you already earned walking out the door. Not because
your product failed. Not because a competitor won. **Because a credit card expired
and nobody followed up.**"*

## 45.1 ⭐ THE RATE REGISTRY — ONE SOURCE FOR EVERY NUMBER

⛔ **Zero hardcoded prices anywhere** (money-number law). Every figure in §43.3
lives here:

| Holds | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Plan definitions** | ⭐ **two packages** (§17.4 D6), never changing |
| **Included allowances** | 500 SMS · $50 AI · 100 voice min · 10k lead credits |
| **Top-up ladders** | SMS $50/1k · $250/10k · AI $100 · **$300→$400** · voice · lead |
| ⭐ **The AI markup** | **8:1**, one multiplier |
| **Per-unit costs** | carrier, provider, per-model — ⭐ **measured, not estimated** |
| **Intervals** | ladder timings, dunning schedule, grace periods |

⭐ **A price appears once and every surface reads it** — the site, the app, the
invoice, the agent, the help card. **It cannot be wrong in two places.**

## 45.2 ⭐⭐ DUNNING — BUILT TO THE 70–85% BAR, NOT THE 47.6% MEDIAN

### ⭐ Prevention first — where the research says the real win is

> ⭐ *"Most involuntary churn is preventable before a card ever declines."*

- ⭐ **Pre-dunning at 30 days before expiry** — *+15–22% of at-risk revenue*.
- ⭐ **Card account updater** — refresh replaced cards **before** they fail.
- ⛔ **A card expiring is an `account`-class notification** (§17.1) — **it cannot
  be unsubscribed from**, because it's how they keep their account.

### The retry ladder

```
  ⭐ soft decline  ──► Day 1 · Day 3 · Day 5 · Day 7    ← 58% with NO email at all
  ⛔ hard decline  ──► ⭐ NO RETRY. Retrying is wasted attempts —
                        it cannot succeed until the customer acts
```

⭐⭐ **Separating soft from hard by decline code is the single highest-leverage
thing in the module.** *"Retrying a hard decline on the same schedule as a
temporary insufficient-funds decline wastes retry attempts."*

⚠️ **Card networks cap retries in a rolling window and exceeding them carries
penalties** — so the ladder is bounded and **stops entirely on hard declines**.

### Communication — multi-channel, front-loaded, and human

| Rule | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **First 72 hours** | ⭐ **recovers the most; decays sharply after two weeks.** Front-load it |
| ⭐ **Multi-channel** | email **+ SMS + in-app** — **up to 34% better than email alone** |
| ⭐ **Tone** | ⭐ *"converts better when it reads as helpful rather than a collections notice"* — ⛔ **it's a friend telling you your card expired, not a debt letter** |
| **Framing** | loss-aversion — what they're about to lose — outperforms transactional copy |
| **One-click fix** | update card in one tap, no login |

### Grace and access

⛔ **SUPERSEDED BY §45A — the owner's timeline is 21 days with a human call at day 7.** *(The 7→14 industry default below is kept for reference only.)*

⭐ *Industry practice: 7 days, extending to 14 on confirmed awareness.* **Ours is more generous, deliberately.**

⛔ **And during grace, per §17.1: nothing stops.** ⭐ **A missed-call text-back
must not fail because a card expired.** Access degrades at the end of grace, never
in the middle of a customer conversation.

### ⭐ The measurement the research insists on

**Two numbers, tracked separately:** involuntary churn rate *(involuntary MRR ÷
starting MRR)* and ⭐ **involuntary share of churn** *(involuntary ÷ total
churned)* — ⭐ *"the number that tells you how much of your leak is a billing
problem versus a product problem."*

⚠️ **And the honest one:** *"an account that hasn't logged in for 60 days and is
failing on a card decline is closer to voluntary churn wearing a payment-failure
disguise — no amount of retry sophistication changes that."* ⭐ **So the report
separates engaged from dormant failures**, and we don't claim credit for
recovering someone who'd already left.

## 45.3 CREDITS, PLANS AND THE LEDGER

**Every debit is a `LedgerEntry`** (§11.1), integer minor units, never a float.
Five meters (§43.3), ⭐ **auto top-up universal**, the runaway guard alerts and
never halts.

⭐ **The credit statement reads like a phone bill, not an accounting export:**
*"You used 340 of 500 texts, £31 of £50 AI credit, and 62 of 100 voice minutes.
Your AI credit went mostly on the front-desk agent — 210 conversations."*

**Plan changes:** upgrade immediate and prorated · downgrade at period end ·
⭐ **pause keeps the number and the data** (§17.1) · cancel is dormant, not
deleted, with export available.

## 45.4 WHAT §44–45 CONTRIBUTE

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Fenced** | ⛔ 17 ads modules → **247 total · 45 turns** |
| **Actions** | ~120 |
| **Events** | `payment.failed` · ⭐ `payment.recovered` · `card.expiring` · `dunning.escalated` · `credit.topped_up` · `plan.changed` |
| **New modules** | ⭐ **none — dunning lives in C-Billing**, one implementation shared with the tenant's own invoicing (§25.3) |
| **Register lines drained** | 58 *(cumulative 797)* |

⭐⭐ **The compounding line: the dunning engine we build for our own billing is
the same engine that chases the tenant's unpaid invoices** — one implementation,
two customers, and their receivables problem is the same shape as ours.

## 45.5 ACCEPTANCE — M12a

☐ ⛔ Ads fenced by name; ⭐ **X-139 and cost-per-booked-job stay** — they aren't management
☐ ⭐ Rate registry holds every number from §43.3; **zero hardcoded prices**
☐ ⭐ Pre-dunning at 30 days; account updater; ⛔ **card-expiry is `account`-class, unsubscribable never**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Soft vs hard decline separated by code** — hard declines get **no retry**
☐ Retry ladder Day 1/3/5/7, bounded by network caps
☐ ⭐ Multi-channel, front-loaded in 72h, ⭐ **helpful tone not collections**
☐ ⭐ Grace 7 days → 14 on confirmed awareness; ⛔ **nothing stops mid-conversation**
☐ ⭐ Involuntary churn rate **and** involuntary share tracked separately
☐ ⭐ Engaged vs dormant failures separated — **no credit for recovering someone who'd left**
☐ ⭐ One dunning engine, ours and theirs

**All ten ✅ — M12a EXECUTED.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §45A · ⭐⭐ THE PLATFORM DUNNING TIMELINE — OWNER LAW  *(T506)*
**How GO AI EZ handles a tenant's failed card. Supersedes §45.2's grace rules.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 45A.1 ⭐ THE TIMELINE

```
  DAY 0   card declines
     │
     ├─ ⭐ SOFT decline ──► retry ladder runs (Day 1 · 3 · 5 · 7)
     │                       ⭐ 58% recover here with no human involved
     └─ ⛔ HARD decline ──► no retry. Straight to outreach.
     │
  DAY 0–7  ⭐ MULTI-CHANNEL OUTREACH, alongside the retries
     │      SMS · MMS · email · in-app — ⭐ front-loaded, helpful in tone,
     │      one-tap card update in every message (§45.2)
     │
  ⭐ DAY 7   ⛔⛔ A HUMAN REACHES OUT
     │      customer success, not an automation. A call or a personal message.
     │
  DAY 7–21  ⭐⭐ FOURTEEN DAYS TO SETTLE
     │      ⭐ everything keeps working. Retries continue on soft declines.
     │
  ⭐ DAY 21  ACCOUNT PAUSES
     │
  ⛔ NEVER   ⭐⭐ THE ACCOUNT IS NEVER DELETED. IT STAYS INTACT.
```

⭐⭐ **Twenty-one days and a human phone call before anything stops.** That is
considerably more generous than the industry's 7-day grace — ⭐ **and it should
be, because the failure is usually a card, not a decision** (§45.0).

## 45A.2 ⭐⭐ DAY 7 — THE HUMAN CALL IS THE WHOLE DIFFERENCE

⛔ **Every SaaS sends dunning emails. Almost none pick up the phone.**

| Why it works | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Most failures are mechanical** | *"your card expired"* is a 30-second fix that an email didn't get to and a call does |
| ⭐⭐ **It separates the two churns** | ⭐ **a call reveals whether it's a card problem or a "we're stopping" problem** — and only a human can hear the difference (§45.2) |
| **It saves the ones worth saving** | someone about to leave for a fixable reason says so on a call and never says so to an email |
| ⭐ **It's cheap** | at our volumes this is a handful of calls a week, and each one is recurring revenue |

⭐ **The CS person gets the context automatically:** what failed, the decline code,
what they've used this month, ⭐ **what they'd lose** — *"they've had 340 missed
calls answered this month; that's the number to lead with."*

## 45A.3 ⭐ WHAT "PAUSED" MEANS — PRECISELY

⭐⭐ **Pause stops the marketing. It does not stop the phone.**

| ⛔ Stops at day 21 | ⭐ Keeps working |
| :--- | :--- |
| Outbound campaigns and sequences | ⭐⭐ **Missed-call text-back** |
| Scheduled social posts | ⭐ **Inbound calls and the agent answering them** |
| Review request sending | ⭐ **Their number and forwarding** |
| Reactivation sends | ⭐ **Their inbox, their data, their history** |
| AI content generation | ⭐ **Export, in full, any time** |
| New outbound of any kind | ⭐ **Support and account notices** (§17.1) |

### ⭐⭐ Why the phone keeps answering

**Three reasons, and the first is the one that matters:**

1. ⭐⭐ **Cutting the text-back punishes their customer, not them.** Someone rings a
   plumber, gets no answer, gets no text — **and that person did nothing wrong.**
2. ⭐ **It's the strongest argument to pay.** *"While your account has been paused
   we've still answered 40 calls for you"* is a better collections message than
   any email.
3. **It costs us almost nothing** — a text-back is one SMS.

### ⭐⭐ THE WIND-DOWN CLOCK — OWNER RULING T507

⛔ **Corrected from my 60-day guess. The clock runs from day 0, the decline.**

```
  DAY 0   decline
  DAY 7   ⭐ human reaches out
  DAY 21  ⭐ account pauses — marketing stops, ⭐ THE PHONE STILL ANSWERS
  ⭐ DAY 30  ⛔ CALLS STOP.  the phone path ends
  ⭐ DAY 60  ⛔ NUMBER RELEASED back to the carrier
  ⛔ NEVER   ⭐⭐ THE ACCOUNT AND ALL ITS DATA REMAIN. INTACT. INDEFINITELY.
```

| Day | What happens | ⭐ What they're told |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **21** | marketing pauses, ⭐ **phone keeps answering** | *"paused — and your phone is still being answered"* |
| ⭐ **30** | ⛔ **calls stop** | ⭐ **warned on day 25** — *"your phone stops being answered in 5 days"* |
| ⭐ **60** | ⛔ **number released** | ⭐⭐ **warned on days 45, 53 and 58** — *"you lose this number in X days and we cannot get it back"* |
| ever | ⭐⭐ **data never deleted** | |

⛔ **The number release is the only irreversible step in the whole system**, so it
gets the loudest and earliest warnings — ⭐ **three of them, on every channel,
`account`-class** (§17.1). *A tradesperson's number is on their van, their
paperwork and in a thousand customers' phones. Losing it is the one thing we
cannot undo, and we say so in those words.*

⭐ **Between day 30 and 60 the number is held but silent** — ⭐ **so paying inside
that window restores everything instantly, same number.** After 60 days they come
back to all their data and a new number.

## 45A.4 ⭐⭐ NEVER DELETED — WHAT "INTACT" MEANS

> ⭐⭐ **The account is never deleted. Ever. Under any circumstance short of the
> tenant asking us to.**

| Kept, indefinitely | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Every conversation, call, transcript and message** | |
| ⭐ **Every job, quote, invoice and payment** | |
| **Their pricebook, knowledge base and uploads** | |
| **Their site, pages and content** | ⭐ **unpublished, not destroyed** |
| ⭐ **Their reviews, photos and QA history** | |
| **Their number** | ⭐ held to **day 60**, then released *(the only irreversible step)* |

⭐⭐ **Coming back is one payment.** Not a re-onboarding, not a rebuild, not a
migration. **They pay, and everything they had is there — including the
conversations that happened while they were away.**

⭐ **Inside 60 days, that includes their number.** After 60 days, everything
except the number — ⭐ **which is still a far better return than any competitor
offers, because the alternative everywhere else is starting from nothing.**

⭐ **And that is a genuine competitive position:** the churn most SaaS treats as
final, we treat as paused. **A tenant who leaves in March and returns in
September finds their business exactly where they left it** — which makes
returning easy and makes leaving less frightening.

## 45A.5 THE MESSAGE LADDER

| When | Channel | Tone |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Day 0 | in-app + email | ⭐ *"your card didn't go through — here's a one-tap fix"* |
| Day 1 | SMS | short, link, no drama |
| Day 3 | email + in-app | ⭐ **what they'd lose**, in their own numbers |
| Day 5 | SMS + MMS | ⭐ **MMS with the overlay card** (X-189) — their name, their usage |
| ⭐ **Day 7** | ⛔ **HUMAN — call or personal message** | |
| Day 10 | email | the pause date named plainly |
| Day 14 | SMS | ⭐ *"a week left, and nothing's stopped yet"* |
| Day 18 | ⭐ human again if reachable | |
| Day 20 | all channels | ⭐ **final, clear, still helpful** |
| Day 21 | in-app | ⭐ *"paused — and your phone is still being answered"* |

⛔ **Every one of these is `account`-class** (§17.1) — **unsubscribable never**,
because this is how they keep their account.

## 45A.6 WHAT §45A ADDS

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔ **Supersedes** | §45.2's *"7 days grace, 14 on confirmed awareness"* → ⭐ **21 days with a human call at day 7** |
| ⭐ **New** | the day-7 human touchpoint · ⭐ **pause keeps the phone answering** · ⭐⭐ **the wind-down clock: 21 pause · 30 calls stop · 60 number released** · ⭐ **data never deleted, ever** |
| **Events** | `dunning.human_escalation_due` · `account.paused` · ⭐ `account.restored` · `phone.stopping_warning` · `phone.stopped` · ⭐ `number.release_warning` · ⛔ `number.released` |
| **Modules** | ⭐ **247 — no change.** Timeline and policy, not new machinery |

## 45A.7 ACCEPTANCE — §45A

☐ ⭐ Retry ladder Day 1/3/5/7 on **soft declines only**; hard declines go straight to outreach
☐ ⭐ Multi-channel from day 0 — SMS · MMS · email · in-app, one-tap fix in each
☐ ⭐⭐ **Day 7: a human reaches out**, with usage context and what they'd lose
☐ ⭐⭐ **14 more days to settle. Nothing stops until day 21**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Pause stops marketing; the phone keeps being answered**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Day 30 calls stop** *(warned day 25)*; ⭐⭐ **day 60 number released** *(warned days 45, 53, 58)*

☐ ⭐ Their number held throughout, never released

# §46 · M12b — MONEY II  ⛔ *(CORRECTED T505 — SEE §46A. The receivables ladder applies to the invoice-terms MINORITY only.)*
**The tenant's invoicing · ⭐ getting them paid · X-120 the vault**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

> **⚠️ CORRECTED — PRECEDENCE (T667, §0.A):** by §46A (a card, not an invoice); current §138 (X-199) + §149. *Nothing here is deleted (law 10); read §0.A before treating this section as current.*

## 46.0 ⭐⭐ RESEARCH — GETTING PAID IS THE PROBLEM, NOT INVOICING

| Finding | Number |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Small businesses hit by late payment** | **~62%** |
| ⭐⭐ **Average owed at any time** | **$17,000+ (US) · £21,000+ (UK)** per small business |
| ⛔ **Hours lost chasing** | ⭐ **~5 hours a week** following up on payments |
| ⭐ **Businesses losing 5–30% of annual revenue to bad debt** | **32%** |
| ⛔ **Business bankruptcies attributable to unpaid invoices** | ⭐ **roughly one in four** |
| ⭐ **Construction/trades** | ⭐⭐ **the worst-paid sector of any** |
| **Late invoices that do eventually get paid** | **75% within 14 days of due date · 90% within a month** |
| ⭐⭐ **SMS + email reminders vs email alone** | ⭐ **+56% chance of being paid within a week of the due date** |
| ⭐ **Automated collections** | **~50% DSO reduction within 30 days** |
| ⛔ **SMBs who give up chasing entirely** | **52%** |

> ⭐⭐ **The two numbers that define this module: a trades business is owed
> £21,000 and spends five hours a week chasing it — and half of them give up.**

⭐ **And "late" mostly isn't "gone":** 75% of late invoices are paid within 14
days of the due date. ⭐⭐ **Which means the entire problem is follow-up, and
follow-up is exactly what software does for free.**

---

## 46.1 ⭐⭐ THE RECEIVABLES ENGINE — THE SAME ONE AS §45.2

⛔ **Not a second implementation.** The dunning engine built for our own billing
chases the tenant's invoices. **One engine, two customers** (§45.4).

### The ladder — from the research, not invented

```
  invoice sent ──► ⭐ tracked: opened? viewed? clicked?
       │
  due date
       ├─ ⭐ Day 1 overdue ──► soft automated nudge, SMS + email
       │                        ⭐ (+56% vs email alone)
       ├─ Day 7 ──► firm, formal, and ⭐ reads as personally written
       ├─ Day 14 ──► ⭐⭐ CALL — the agent can place it, or it lands on the
       │              owner's list with the context and a script
       └─ Day 30+ ──► final notice · ⭐ statutory interest where it applies ·
                       escalation options laid out
```

⭐ **Every step is a `Message` on the customer's own `Conversation`** — so the
chase sits in the same thread as the job, the quote and the review request.
**The customer isn't being chased by a system they've never seen.**

### ⭐ What makes ours different

| ⭐ | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **The agent can make the call** | *"Hi, it's about invoice 1042 from the boiler service on the 3rd — it's a fortnight overdue. Shall I text you the payment link?"* **Grounded, polite, and it happens on day 14 whether or not the owner had time** |
| ⭐ **Payment link in every message** | one tap, no login, no bank details typed |
| **Open and view tracking** | ⭐ *"they opened it twice and didn't pay"* is a different conversation from *"they never saw it"* |
| ⭐ **Escalation is automatic, tone is not** | the ladder fires on schedule; ⭐ **the owner can soften or hold any step for a customer they value** |
| ⭐⭐ **Nothing gets forgotten** | *52% of SMBs give up chasing.* **The engine doesn't get embarrassed, doesn't get busy, and doesn't decide it isn't worth it** |

### ⭐ Prevention — worth more than chasing

| Lever | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Deposits at booking** *(§25.3)* | **the single best protection** — a deposit taken means partial payment is already banked |
| **Terms stated up front** | on the quote, the confirmation and the invoice |
| ⭐ **Pay-on-completion** | the tech takes payment at the door on the mobile app *(X-171)* — ⭐ **the invoice that never becomes a receivable** |
| **Card on file** *(X-120)* | with consent, for repeat and membership customers |
| ⭐ **Progress payments** | staged on larger jobs so exposure never builds |

## 46.2 ⭐ THE MONEY DASHBOARD — FOR SOMEONE WHO ISN'T AN ACCOUNTANT

⛔ **Not an aged-debtor report.** Four numbers a tradesperson understands:

| Shows | Example |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **"You're owed"** | **£8,430 across 11 invoices** |
| ⭐⭐ **"Overdue"** | **£2,100 across 3** — *with a chase button on each* |
| ⭐ **"Coming in"** | expected this week, from what's due |
| ⭐⭐ **"Average days to get paid"** | ⭐ **DSO in plain words, trending** — *"18 days, down from 27"* |

⭐ **And the risk flag that matters:** *"this customer has paid late on their last
three jobs"* — ⭐ **surfaced at quote time, not at chase time**, because the
`Person` record holds their whole payment history (§11.2).

## 46.3 X-120 `CardVault`

**Per R91: PAN + expiry storable, ⛔ CVV never, PCI DSS Level 1 pursued.**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Storage** | envelope encryption, AES-256-GCM, network-segmented |
| ⛔ **No CVV column** | ⭐ **a build-failing migration grep enforces it** — not a policy, a test |
| **Default write path** | ⭐ **Accept.js `opaqueData`** — the card doesn't touch our servers unless the vault is explicitly in play |
| **Uses** | memberships · repeat customers · deposits on file · ⭐ **the pay-on-completion tap** |
| **Consent** | recorded per card, revocable from the customer portal *(X-172)* |
| ⭐ **Never in the graph** | ⛔ card data is **never** a `PersonIdentity` or a `Fact` (§23.3 rule 2) |

## 46.4 ACCOUNTING, TAX AND THE REST

**Sync via X-173** *(one direction per object, idempotent, conflicts surfaced —
built against the double-entry complaint, §30.5)*. Tax rates per jurisdiction from
the registry. Multi-currency in minor units. Refunds and partial refunds with
reason codes feeding the QA report (§37.3②). Statements, remittance matching,
and ⭐ **cash-vs-accrual views**, because a trades business thinks in cash.

## 46.5 WHAT M12b CONTRIBUTES

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Actions** | ~130 |
| **Events** | `invoice.sent/viewed/overdue/paid` · ⭐ `receivable.escalated` · `payment.taken_at_door` · `customer.payment_risk_flagged` |
| **New modules** | ⭐ **none** — the engine is shared with §45, the vault is X-120, the sync is X-173 |
| **Register lines drained** | 47 *(cumulative 844)* |
| **Seams** | 12 — ⭐ `job→invoice` · `invoice→conversation` · `payment→attribution` · `payment_history→quote_risk` |

⭐⭐ **The sentence M12b earns:** *a trades business is owed £21,000, spends five
hours a week chasing it, and half of them give up.* **We chase every invoice on a
schedule, by SMS and email together (+56%), with a payment link in every message —
and on day fourteen the AI picks up the phone.** ⭐ **Nobody else in this market
can make that call.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §46A · ⛔⛔ M12b CORRECTED — IT'S A CARD, NOT AN INVOICE  *(owner, T505)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 46A.0 ⛔ MY ERROR, NAMED

**I built §46 around a 30-day invoice cycle with DSO, aged debtors and a
four-week chase ladder. That is a B2B SaaS receivables model and it is wrong for
this business.**

⭐⭐ **A card payment is approved or declined. There is no cycle.** The tech is
standing at the door, the customer taps, and it either works or it doesn't —
**and the whole thing resolves in about fifteen seconds, not thirty days.**

⛔ **§46's ladder is not deleted — it is re-scoped to the minority it actually
fits** *(§46A.3)*.

---

## 46A.1 ⭐⭐ THREE PAYMENT REALITIES — AND THE DEFAULT IS THE FIRST

| # | Reality | Failure mode | Who |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **①** | **CARD AT THE POINT OF SERVICE** *(the default)* | ⭐ **a decline, resolved in the moment** | most jobs, most tenants |
| **②** | **RECURRING / MEMBERSHIP** | a decline with **nobody standing there** | members, care plans, retainers |
| **③** | **INVOICE WITH TERMS** | genuinely late payment | ⭐ **commercial only** — landlords, letting agents, property managers, councils |

⛔ **§46 assumed ③ was the default. It's ①.**

---

## 46A.2 ⭐⭐ ① THE DECLINE AT THE DOOR — THE REAL DESIGN

**Fifteen seconds, not fourteen days. The tech is standing there and the customer
wants to pay.**

```
  tap ──► DECLINED
       │
  ⭐ SOFT decline (insufficient funds · velocity · issuer timeout)
       ├──► ⭐ "Try again" — retry immediately. ⭐ Often just works
       │
  ⛔ HARD decline (expired · stolen · invalid · do-not-honour)
       ├──► ⭐ retrying is pointless. Move straight to alternatives:
       │
       ├─ ⭐ another card                    ── tap again
       ├─ ⭐⭐ payment link to their phone     ── they pay on their own banking app
       ├─ ⭐ bank transfer                    ── details on screen, reference pre-filled
       └─ ⭐ "settle up later"                ── job closes UNPAID, ladder starts (46A.4)
```

⭐⭐ **The decline-code split from §45.2 matters even more here**, because at the
door a wrong guess costs the tech a minute of standing in someone's hallway
looking at a machine. ⭐ **Soft: press it again. Hard: stop and switch method.**
The screen says which, in words.

| ⭐ At-the-door rules | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔ **Never blame the customer** | *"the bank didn't authorise it — happens all the time"*, never *"your card was declined"* |
| ⭐ **The alternative is one tap** | payment link goes to their phone **while the tech is still there** — ⭐ *and it usually gets paid before he's back in the van* |
| ⭐ **The job doesn't hang** | it closes as **completed-unpaid** with the amount, so ⛔ **the work is never lost just because the payment wasn't taken** |
| **Tech never handles the problem alone** | the owner sees the unpaid job the moment it's marked |
| ⭐ **Every attempt logged with its code** | ⭐ *"three declines this month, all do-not-honour, all same issuer"* is a pattern worth knowing |

## 46A.3 ⭐ ② RECURRING — THIS IS WHERE §45'S ENGINE BELONGS

⭐⭐ **A membership card declining is the one case that genuinely needs dunning,
because nobody is standing there.**

**Everything in §45.2 applies exactly:** pre-dunning 30 days before expiry ·
account updater · ⭐ **soft/hard split** · retry Day 1/3/5/7 for soft only ·
multi-channel · **7→14 day grace** · ⭐ **and the member keeps their benefits
during grace**, because a care-plan member who loses priority dispatch over an
expired card is a cancelled member.

## 46A.4 ⭐ ③ INVOICE TERMS — THE COMMERCIAL MINORITY

⭐ **§46's ladder survives here and only here**, and it's the right tool for it:
letting agents and property managers genuinely pay on 30-day terms, genuinely pay
late, and genuinely need the Day 1/7/14/30 chase with the agent's call at day 14.

⛔ **But the tenant is asked once, at setup: *"do you invoice anyone on terms?"***
⭐ **If no — and for most it's no — the entire receivables apparatus never
appears.** No DSO tile, no aged-debtor view, no chase ladder. **Complexity that
doesn't apply is complexity that isn't shown** (§41.2).

### The short ladder for an unpaid domestic job

⭐ **Days, not weeks** — because it isn't a payment term, it's an unpaid job:

```
  completed-unpaid ──► ⭐ same evening: "here's the link for today's work"
                  ──► ⭐ +2 days: reminder, SMS + email
                  ──► ⭐ +5 days: the owner's list, with a call script
                  ──► then it's a conversation, not an automation
```

## 46A.5 ⭐ WHAT THE DASHBOARD ACTUALLY SHOWS

⛔ **§46.2's four tiles were built for the wrong model. Corrected:**

| ⭐ Shows | Why |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **"Paid today"** | the number a tradesperson actually wants at 6pm |
| ⭐ **"Unpaid jobs"** | ⭐ **count and value, each with a send-link button** — *the whole receivables problem for a domestic business, in one tile* |
| **"Declines this week"** | ⭐ with the reason, and whether it was recovered |
| **"Coming in"** | scheduled memberships and deposits |
| ⭐ *(only if they invoice on terms)* | the aged view, DSO, the chase ladder |

## 46A.6 WHAT §46A CHANGES

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔ **Corrected** | §46's default from **invoice terms** → ⭐ **card at the point of service** |
| ⭐ **Kept, re-scoped** | the receivables ladder → ⭐ **commercial invoice-terms tenants only, and hidden for everyone else** |
| ⭐ **Kept in full** | §45's soft/hard decline logic — ⭐ **it matters MORE at the door, not less** |
| ⭐ **New** | at-the-door decline flow · the alternatives ladder · **completed-unpaid** job state · the short domestic ladder |
| **Modules** | ⭐ **247 — no change.** The engine was already there; the default was wrong |

⭐⭐ **The lesson worth recording:** the research I found was about B2B invoicing
because that's what generates articles. **The business we're serving takes a card
in a hallway.** ⛔ **Research tells you what's written about, not what your
customer does — and §7E is only as good as the question I ask it.**

## 46A.7 ACCEPTANCE — §46A

☐ ⛔ **Card at the point of service is the DEFAULT**; invoice terms are opt-in
☐ ⭐⭐ Soft decline → **retry immediately**; hard decline → **stop, switch method**
☐ ⭐ Alternatives one tap: another card · ⭐ **link to their phone** · transfer · settle later
☐ ⛔ **Never blame the customer** — *"the bank didn't authorise it"*
☐ ⭐ **completed-unpaid** job state; the work is never lost with the payment
☐ Every attempt logged with its decline code; patterns surfaced
☐ ⭐ §45's dunning engine applies to **recurring/membership**, ⭐ **benefits kept during grace**
☐ ⭐ Receivables ladder for **invoice-terms tenants only** — ⛔ **hidden entirely for the rest**
☐ ⭐ Short domestic ladder in **days**: same evening · +2 · +5 · then a human
☐ ⭐ Dashboard: **paid today · unpaid jobs · declines**, aged view only if it applies

**All ten ✅ — §46A COMPLETE.**

## 47.0 ⭐⭐ RESEARCH — THE AGENCY CHANNEL IS REAL, AND ONE LINE DEFINES IT

| Finding | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **The margin math** | GoHighLevel Agency Pro **$497/mo**, agencies resell at **~$297/client** → ⭐ **10 clients = $2,970 against $497 ≈ 83% gross margin** |
| ⭐ **Why agencies chase it** | *"Project work is capped by hours... **the tenth client costs almost nothing more to serve than the first.** Traditional agency revenue is linear — hours in, fees out."* |
| ⛔ **Agency net margin in 2025** | ⭐ **13%** *(Promethean Research, 119 agency leaders)* — **which is why they need this** |
| ⚠️ **The catch, stated plainly** | ⭐ *"Software resale is a support business."* |

### ⭐⭐ THE LINE THAT DEFINES WHAT WE BUILD

> ⭐⭐ *"Plenty of platforms describe themselves as white label when what they
> actually sell is **distribution with a custom domain attached.** If your clients
> still see the vendor's name in emails, notifications, or support, **you are a
> reseller rather than an owner.**"*

⛔ **So white-label means white-label: no GO AI EZ in emails, SMS sender names,
notifications, support replies, PDFs, or the login page.** ⭐ **Anything less is a
custom domain and a lie.**

### ⭐ AND WHAT AGENCIES CAN ACTUALLY SELL NOW

> ⭐⭐ *"Rebranding a scheduler, a form builder, or a social posting tool is close
> to worthless now, because clients can buy those directly for $20 a month. **The
> offers that command real retainers are AI agents that do revenue work:**
> answering inbound leads in seconds, reactivating dormant CRM records by SMS and
> phone, giving live demos, and catching churn before the cancellation email."*

⭐⭐ **That paragraph is a description of this platform.** The missed-call agent,
reactivation by SMS and phone, the demo assistant, churn prediction — **we
already built every item on that list.** *The agency channel isn't a feature we
need to add; it's a distribution route for what exists.*
