# §48 · ⭐ THE CHANNEL ECONOMICS — RECORDED, WITH TWO FLAGS  *(T509)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

> **⚠️ CORRECTED — PRECEDENCE (T667, §0.A):** §48A sets it; §48B corrects the unlimited rule — read all three, last wins. *Nothing here is deleted (law 10); read §0.A before treating this section as current.*

## 48.1 ⭐ THE MODEL AS SET

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Agency discount** | **60% off all pricing** |
| ⭐ **Agency usage discount** | **40% off top-ups** |
| ⛔ **Per-client billing** | ⭐ **not offered.** *We don't piecemeal — it's a full platform* |
| ⭐ **Affiliates** | **40% on service, for lifetime** |
| ⭐ **The differentiator** | *we already have the solutions, and there are credits for everything* |

⭐ **The "no piecemeal" position is right and worth holding.** GoHighLevel's
per-module tiering is exactly what lets ServiceTitan and Birdeye nickel-and-dime;
⭐ **one platform, one price is a cleaner story and a cleaner build** (§30A.1).

---

## 48.2 ⚠️ FLAG ONE — 60% PER SEAT LOSES TO GHL'S FLAT FEE AT SCALE

**The arithmetic, plainly:**

| Agency size | ⭐ Ours *(60% off, per seat)* | GHL *(flat $497, unlimited seats)* |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 5 clients | 2 seats' worth | $497 |
| 20 clients | 8 seats' worth | $497 |
| ⛔ **50 clients** | ⭐ **20 seats' worth** | ⭐ **still $497** |
| ⛔ **100 clients** | **40 seats' worth** | **still $497** |

⛔ **A 50-client agency does that sum and we lose it** — not on capability, on
the invoice. ⭐ **And the agencies with 50 clients are the ones who bring the next
50.**

### ⭐⭐ MY RECOMMENDATION — AND OUR OWN LAW SUPPORTS IT

> ⭐⭐ **A flat agency platform fee with unlimited tenants, and usage metered
> separately at the 40%-off rate.**

⭐ **This isn't a concession — it's consistent with §30A.1, our own
included-software law: the software costs us nothing marginal.** The variable cost
of this platform *is* SMS, voice, AI and lead credits — **and those are already
metered separately and bill separately.**

**So a flat fee with unlimited tenants is not a risk.** ⭐ **The tenants who cost
us money are the tenants who send, and sending is billed either way.**

| ⭐ Why it's stronger | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **We beat GHL on their own model** | flat fee *plus* usage 40% cheaper *plus* the AI actually works |
| **It's what agencies already understand** | no re-education, no comparison spreadsheet |
| ⭐ **It scales the right way** | ⭐ **an agency adding clients costs us nothing until those clients send** |
| **Consistent with our own reasoning** | ⛔ we already said software is free at the margin — this just says it out loud to agencies |

⭐ **If you want to capture more from large agencies, band the flat fee** — 1–10,
11–50, 51+ — ⭐ **but never per seat.** Per-seat is the thing they're leaving
ServiceTitan to escape.

---

## 48.3 ⚠️⚠️ FLAG TWO — 40% LIFETIME ON *USAGE* IS A LOSS

⛔ **This is the one I'd change before launch.**

**Voice is priced near cost on purpose** (§18E.4) — 7¢/min against ~3–5¢ of real
cost. ⭐ **40% of a 7¢ minute is 2.8¢, which is more than the margin.**

| Revenue type | ⭐ 40% lifetime affiliate on it? |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Subscription** | ✅ **yes — and it's a strong, generous offer** |
| **SMS top-ups** | ⚠️ margin depends on carrier rates; ⭐ **workable but thin** |
| **AI credits** *(8:1)* | ✅ **yes — the margin easily carries it** |
| ⛔ **Voice top-ups** | ⛔⛔ **NO. 40% exceeds the entire margin** |
| ⛔ **Lead credits** | ⚠️ **check per-provider** — at $5/1K retail on cheap-first fetching the margin is real, but not 40%-real on every tier |

### ⭐ MY RECOMMENDATION

> ⭐⭐ **40% lifetime on subscription. A stated, lower rate on usage — or none.**

⭐ **And say it plainly in the affiliate terms**, because an affiliate who
discovers the rate differs by line item later is an angry affiliate. ⭐ *"40% of
the subscription, for as long as they stay"* is still one of the most generous
offers in the category — **and it's the number affiliates actually care about,
because subscription is the predictable part.**

⭐ **Downgrade, pause and return — SETTLED (§48A.2):** ⭐⭐ **40% of whatever the
account actually pays, forever** — including **£0 while paused**, resuming on
return *(§45A.4)*. ⭐ **This aligns the affiliate with retention, not just
signup.**

---

## 48.4 ⭐⭐ THE UNLIMITED QUESTION — YES AND NO, AND THE SPLIT IS THE PRODUCT

⛔ **Unlimited on anything with real marginal cost is how SaaS companies die.**
The 1% who abuse it cost everything and fund nothing.

⭐⭐ **But unlimited where marginal cost is ~zero is free marketing, and we have a
lot of that:**

| ⭐ UNLIMITED — costs us nothing | ⛔ METERED — costs us real money |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Users, staff, technicians** | SMS / MMS / RCS |
| ⭐ **Contacts and customer records** | Voice minutes |
| ⭐ **Jobs, quotes, estimates, invoices** | AI credits |
| ⭐ **Pages, sites, landing pages** | Lead credits |
| ⭐ **Campaigns and workflows** | |
| ⭐ **Pipelines, forms, templates** | |
| ⭐ **Locations** | |
| ⭐ **Conversations and message history** | |
| ⭐ **Reviews, photos, documents** | |
| ⭐ **Automations and integrations** | |

### ⭐⭐ THE POSITIONING THIS BUYS

> ⭐⭐ **"Unlimited everything, except what actually costs money to send — and
> that's metered honestly at a published rate."**

⛔ **That is a better story than "unlimited" with a fair-use clause that bites.**
Every competitor selling "unlimited" either throttles quietly or has a paragraph
they enforce when you get expensive. ⭐ **Ours is: unlimited where it's genuinely
free, and an honest number where it isn't.**

⭐ **And it kills the objection that matters most:** ⭐⭐ **unlimited staff.**
A trades business adding two apprentices should not pay more for software — **and
per-seat pricing is the single most resented thing in the category** (§30.1, where
*100% of ServiceTitan users who mention pricing say it's pricey*).

⚠️ **The one guard needed:** unlimited *records* invites abuse as a data dump.
⭐ **Soft fair-use on storage volume with a conversation, not a hard cap** — and
per §22.1 it should detect and flag automatically, not wait for someone to notice
a bill.

---

⭐ **Two flags, one recommendation each, and the rest is sound.** *The "we already

⭐ **And paying on what the account actually pays aligns the affiliate with

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §48B · ⛔ THE UNLIMITED RULE — CORRECTED  *(owner challenge, T511)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 48B.0 ⛔ YOU'RE RIGHT — LOCATIONS AREN'T FREE

**I put "locations" in the unlimited column without checking. A location has real
marginal cost:**

| A location brings | ⭐ Cost |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Geo-grid rank tracking** | ⭐ **up to 225 grid points, weekly, per location** — real provider spend |
| ⭐ **AEO visibility queries** | six engines × the query set × **per location** *(§32.4)* |
| **Review monitoring** | API polling per destination, per location |
| **Citation monitoring** | per location |
| **GBP calls** | quota per location |

⛔ **A 20-location business doing weekly geo-grid scans is 20× the API spend of a
sole trader. That is not free and I shouldn't have implied it was.**

## 48B.1 ⭐⭐ THE CORRECTED RULE — AND IT'S BETTER

> ⭐⭐ **Unlimited to CREATE and HOLD. Metered to SEND, SCAN or THINK.**

⭐ **That's a sharper rule than "unlimited where marginal cost is zero", because
it tells you which side of the line anything falls on without having to
estimate.**

| ⭐ UNLIMITED — creating and holding | ⛔ METERED — sending, scanning, thinking |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Users, staff, technicians** | SMS / MMS / RCS **sent** |
| ⭐ Contacts and customer records | Voice minutes **used** |
| ⭐ Jobs, quotes, estimates, invoices | AI credits **consumed** |
| ⭐ Pages, sites, landing pages | Lead credits — records **delivered** |
| ⭐ Campaigns and workflows *(**built**)* | ⭐ **what those workflows send and generate** |
| ⭐ **Location records** — addresses, service areas, dispatch, staff, jobs | ⭐⭐ **geo-grid scans · AEO queries · review polling — per location** |
| ⭐ Pipelines, forms, templates | |
| ⭐ Conversations and message history | |
| ⭐ Reviews, photos, documents *(stored)* | |
| ⭐ Agency sub-accounts | ⭐ what each sub-account sends |

## 48B.2 ⭐⭐ SO MULTI-LOCATION PAYS MORE — AUTOMATICALLY AND HONESTLY

⭐ **A 20-location business burns 20× the lead credits and AI credits, because it
scans 20 grids and runs 20 AEO query sets.** It ends up paying substantially more
than a sole trader — ⭐ **proportional to what it actually uses, not to a number
we counted on their door.**

| ⛔ The alternative I rejected | ⭐ Why |
| :--- | :--- |
| *"Package 1 = 1 location, Package 2 = up to 5, then £X per location"* | ⭐⭐ **that is per-seat thinking wearing a different hat** — and per-seat is precisely what we just rejected for agencies and staff *(§48A.3)* |

⭐⭐ **The metering does the work, and it does it more fairly:** a five-location
business that only tracks two of them pays for two. ⛔ **A per-location fee would
charge them for five.**

## 48B.3 ⭐ WHAT THE TENANT ACTUALLY SEES

⛔ **Not a surprise bill.** Adding a location shows its cost before it's added:

```
  ⭐ + Add location
       │
       └─ ⭐ "Tracking this location will use about 400 lead credits
             and £6 of AI credit a month, on your current settings.
             │
             ├─ ⭐ Track it fully           (rank + AEO + reviews)
             ├─ ⭐ Reviews and GBP only     (much cheaper)
             └─ ⭐ Just add it              (dispatch and jobs only — free)"
```

⭐⭐ **That third option is the important one.** A business with a storage unit, a
second yard or a registered office address ⭐ **should be able to add it as a
location for dispatch purposes without paying to rank-track a warehouse.**

## 48B.4 ⭐ THE SAME CHECK, APPLIED TO EVERYTHING ELSE

**I re-ran the rule across the whole unlimited list:**

| Entry | ⭐ Verdict |
| :--- | :--- |
| Users / staff | ✅ **genuinely free** — a login costs nothing |
| Contacts, jobs, invoices, conversations | ✅ **free** — storage only, and the fair-use guard covers volume |
| Pages and sites | ✅ **free enough** — hosting and CDN are flat |
| ⭐ **Campaigns and workflows** | ⚠️ ⭐ **corrected: free to BUILD, metered to RUN** — a workflow that sends 400 texts bills 400 texts |
| Reviews, photos, documents | ✅ storage, fair-use guard |
| ⭐ **Agency sub-accounts** | ✅ **free** — per D7, and for the same reason: ⭐ **they cost nothing until they send** |
| ⛔ **Locations** | ⛔ ⭐ **corrected: the record is free, the tracking is metered** |

⭐ **Two corrections out of ten, both found by asking the question properly.**

## 48B.5 WHAT §48B CHANGES

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔ **Corrected** | ⭐ **locations** — unlimited records, metered tracking · ⭐ **workflows** — free to build, metered to run |
| ⭐ **The rule sharpened** | ⭐⭐ *"unlimited to create and hold; metered to send, scan or think"* |
| ⭐ **New** | ⭐ **per-location tracking choice at add time**, incl. **"just add it" for free** |
| **Modules** | **247 — no change** |
| ⭐ **The claim stays true** | ⭐⭐ *"Unlimited everything, except what actually costs money"* — **and now it's accurate rather than nearly accurate** |

⭐⭐ **The honest version of the pitch:** *unlimited locations on every plan — you
pay only for the ones you choose to track.* ⛔ **Which is a better offer than any
per-location competitor, and it's one we can actually afford to make.**

# §49 · ⭐⭐ M14 — ATTRIBUTION & THE CLOSED LOOP  *(EXECUTED T512)*
**X-137 DNI · X-138 the graph · X-139 offline conversions · X-141 replay**
⭐ **The flagship. The thing the research said nobody ships.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

> **⛔ FIRST-PASS SHAPE — PRECEDENCE (T667, §0.A):** first-pass attribution; current §132 (M11). *Nothing here is deleted (law 10); read §0.A before treating this section as current.*

## 49.0 ⭐⭐ RESEARCH — ATTRIBUTION IS HAVING A RECKONING, AND IT FAVOURS US

### ⛔ Multi-touch attribution is being retired

**2026 produced a named thesis and a body of evidence behind it:** ⭐ *"Multi-touch
attribution survived the cookieless transition by accident; what finally retires
it is a single quarter of measurement data that nobody disputes."*

⭐ **What breaks without third-party cookies, precisely:** *"cross-site identity
disappears, multi-device stitching weakens, and deduplication across channels
becomes unreliable."* ⭐⭐ **The fix named in the same breath: *"authenticated
first-party identifiers so journeys can be connected without relying on
third-party tracking."***

⭐⭐ **That is our pixel, exactly** — first-party collector on the tenant's own
subdomain (§19.1), and ⭐ **tier 4 of the identity waterfall is a real phone call**
(§19.4), which is about as authenticated as a first-party identifier gets.

### ⭐ And the "dark funnel" number that matters

⭐ **60% of buying journeys happen "in the dark"** — people research without ever
revealing themselves on an instrumented surface. ⛔ **For a local business it's
worse: they ring the number off the van.**

⭐⭐ **Which is why the phone is the answer, not the problem.** *A call is the
moment the dark funnel becomes a person* — and DNI is what makes that moment
attributable.

### ⭐ The mechanics the research specifies

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Pool sizing** | ⭐ **peak hourly visitors ÷ 4** *(CallRail's published formula)* |
| ⭐⭐ **Never two people, one number** | *"a dynamic pool ensures the same number will never be displayed to two different people"* |
| **Captured at swap time** | ⭐ **UTM · gclid · fbclid · referrer · the visitor's anonymous ID** — *"the session metadata captured at swap time is what makes attribution work"* |
| ⭐ **Session persistence** | ⭐ **number assignment holds across page views for the whole session**, not just the landing page |
| ⛔ **The back-half webhook** | ⭐⭐ *"Without that back-half webhook, the call data sits in your call-tracking tool and never influences bidding"* |
| **Cookieless DNI** | device, IP, location and other discrete signals — ⭐ *"cookies can be and often are deleted by the users they supposedly track"* |
| **Reported uplift** | ⭐ **29–33% more conversions** than native platform reporting |

---

## 49.1 ⭐ X-137 `CallTracking` — DNI DONE PROPERLY

```
  visitor lands
     │
  ⭐ script swaps the displayed number ──► one from the pool
     │                                       │
     │   ⭐ LOGGED AT SWAP TIME:              │
     │   UTM · gclid · fbclid · referrer ·   │
     │   landing page · page class ·         │
     │   visitor id · session · timestamp    │
     │                                       │
  ⭐ number HOLDS for the whole session ─────┘
     │
  they call ──► ⭐ the pool number resolves the entire session
     │
     └──► ⭐⭐ `Visit.call_token` (§11.4) — the join that makes everything else work
```

| Rule | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Pool sized to peak hourly ÷ 4**, auto-scaling | ⭐ **and it grows itself before a traffic spike collides** *(law 25)* |
| ⛔ **Never the same number to two live sessions** | ⭐ **a collision silently corrupts attribution and is invisible in testing** |
| ⭐ **Session-persistent** | across pages, and across a return within the window |
| **Cookieless fallback** | device, IP, coarse location — ⭐ *because cookies get deleted* |
| ⭐ **Forwards to their real number** | the customer's experience is unchanged |
| ⭐ **Recording + transcription** | feeding the `Fact` graph, the FAQ and the QA report |
| ⛔ **SEO-safe** | ⭐ **the NAP number in schema and the GBP listing never changes** — only the on-page display swaps |

⭐⭐ **That last one is the thing agencies get wrong and it costs their clients
rankings.** NAP consistency is a local ranking factor (§32.3 D16); ⭐ **DNI must
never touch the canonical number.**

## 49.2 ⭐⭐ X-138 `AttributionGraph` — THE FLAGSHIP

> ⭐⭐ **It is a query, not a pipeline** — because S1 put the fields on the
> canonical rows twenty-eight turns ago.

```
  Asset (page) ──► Visit ──► call_token ──► Conversation ──► Job ──► LedgerEntry
       │              │           │               │            │          │
       │              │           │               │            │       ⭐ PAID
       │              │           │               │            │
       └──────────────┴───────────┴───────────────┴────────────┴──► ⭐⭐ ONE ROW
```

| ⭐ What it answers | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ *"Which page earned this £1,840?"* | `Job.originating_asset_id` |
| *"Which keyword?"* | the gclid logged at swap time |
| ⭐ *"Which technician closed it?"* | the `Job` |
| ⭐⭐ *"What did this customer ask before they booked?"* | the transcript on the same `Conversation` |
| *"How long from first visit to paid?"* | the timestamps |
| ⭐ *"What did that lead cost us?"* | every meter debit on the chain |

### ⭐⭐ Multi-touch — and the honest position on it

⛔ **The research says multi-touch is being retired for good reasons.** So we do
something more defensible:

| ⭐ We report | ⛔ We don't pretend |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **The full path, every touch, in order, with dates** | a fractional credit split we invented |
| ⭐ **First touch and last touch, both named** | that either one is "the answer" |
| ⭐ **The assist list** — every asset on the path | that we know their relative weight |
| ⭐⭐ **The measured truth: this page, this call, this job, this money** | |

⭐⭐ **Showing the path and refusing to invent the weights is more honest than any
attribution model on the market** — and for a local business with one or two
channels, ⭐ **the path is usually short enough that the answer is obvious.**

### ⭐ Self-reported attribution — the cheap thing that works

The research says self-reported attribution is replacing multi-touch. ⭐ **And we
have the perfect place to ask it: the agent, on the call.**

> ⭐ *"Can I ask how you found us?"*

⭐⭐ **One question, asked naturally by the AI, recorded as a `Fact`** — and it
catches the entire dark funnel: the van, the neighbour, the Facebook group, the
sign. ⛔ **No pixel can see any of those.**

## 49.3 ⭐ X-139 `OfflineConversionSync` — THE BACK-HALF WEBHOOK

⛔ *"Without that back-half webhook, the call data sits in your call-tracking tool
and never influences bidding."*

```
  Job PAID ──► ⭐ push to Google Ads (gclid) and Meta (fbclid)
                 with the REAL VALUE
                      │
                      └──► ⭐⭐ the platforms bid for JOBS, not form fills
```

⭐ **Even with ads descoped (§44), this stays** — because the tenant runs their own
ads and this makes their money work. ⛔ **Nothing to log into, nothing to manage.**

## 49.4 ⭐ X-141 `ReplaySimulator`

Re-run real history against a changed config (§13.7). ⭐ **Now it has something
worth replaying:** *"what would last quarter have looked like if review invites
had been on?"* — answered against **real visits, real calls, real jobs.**

⚠️ **The two limits, stated in the product:** ⭐ **it reconstructs decisions, not
outcomes** *(we can prove the invite would have sent, not that they'd have
reviewed)*, and ⭐ **only what's in the log replays.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §50 · K1 — THE CONTENT REGISTER + SCHEMAS  *(EXECUTED T513)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

*No market research this turn — §7E binds module turns. This is data architecture,
and the inputs are §7B, the verified t592 inventory (§34.1) and X-180's parser.*

## 50.1 ⭐⭐ THE THREE-WAY SPLIT — THE FRAME THAT DECIDES EVERYTHING

**Before any schema: every content asset is one of three kinds, and the kind
decides whether it needs writing at all.**

| Kind | Meaning | ⭐ Needs authoring? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **AUTHORED** | words a human wrote | ✅ **yes — goes in `CONTENT-PACK.md`** |
| ⭐ **GENERATED** | produced by an engine from a registry | ⛔ **no — code, not content** |
| ⭐⭐ **RENDERED** | ⭐ **a VIEW of live registry data at display time** | ⛔ **no — and it can never go stale** |

⭐⭐ **The RENDERED category is the one that saves the most work and the most
mistakes.** A quote sheet, a price card, an invoice, a service menu — ⛔ **none of
these are documents. They are views of the pricebook** (§30.2). *Change a price
and every one of them is correct instantly, because none of them holds a copy.*

⭐ **This is §7B.3's "a document is a VIEW" made operational.**

---

**Columns: `kind` · `count` · `shape` · `renderer` · `seeder` · `path` · `status`**

| ⭐ **Vertical landers** | **200** | block JSON + copy | `LanderSeeder` | ⭐ **5 done** + ⭐ **`PIII-18` skeleton** · 195 to fill |
| **Site page decks** | 7 | markdown → blocks | `SiteSeeder` | ✅ **done, v2** |

## 50.3 ⭐ THE SCHEMAS

### `═══ PROFILE ═══` — the one that matters most

```
═══ PROFILE ═══
slug:        emergency-plumber          # unique, kebab, permanent
family:      home-trades                # 1 of 6 picker tabs
name:        Summit Plumbing             # the demo business name
locale:      en-GB                       # drives currency + spelling
tone:        direct, reassuring, no jargon
payment_pattern: invoice-links           # ⭐ picks §25.0's pattern
schedule_mode:   job                     # ⭐ picks §29.1's mode
retail:      false                       # ⭐ gates the cart
─── PRICES ───
# service | amount | currency | note | callout_included
Drain clear | 85 | GBP | 1hr | true
...8–15 rows
─── PRICE RANGES ───            ⭐ where a fixed price is impossible
Boiler replace | 1800 | 3200 | GBP | depends on system
─── CALLOUT ───                 ⭐⭐ the most-asked question (§43.5)
fee: 85 | GBP | deducted_if_proceeding: true
─── FAQ ───
Q: Do you charge for a callout?
A: ...
...10–15 rows
─── SERVICES ───                for GBP + the site
─── EQUIPMENT ───               ⭐ what this trade services (X-175)
─── TONE SEED ───               3–5 sentences in their voice
─── SAFETY ───                  ⭐ required-review lines, 999/911-first
═══ END ═══
```

⭐⭐ **`payment_pattern`, `schedule_mode` and `retail` are the three fields that
configure a whole tenant.** ⭐ *A plumber and a salon differ by three lines of
data, not two code paths* — which is why §25.0 and §29.1 could be automatic.

### The other block shapes — same convention

⭐ **One `═══ TYPE ═══` … `═══ END ═══` envelope, one `─── SECTION ───`
delimiter, everywhere.** So `LANDER` · `AD_SET` · `CAMPAIGN` · `LIFECYCLE` ·
`HELP` · `VIDEO` · `QA_TEMPLATE` all parse with the same reader.

```
═══ AD_SET ═══                  ⛔ the only genuinely blank asset
slug · vertical · platform · objective
─── ANGLE ───     the argument this set makes
─── HEADLINES ─── 5, ≤40 chars
─── PRIMARY ───   3, ≤125 chars
─── CTA ───       one of the platform's allowed set
─── AUDIENCE ───  the signal hint, not a saved audience
═══ END ═══
```

## 50.4 ⛔ VALIDATION — FAILS LOUDLY AT PARSE

| Check | ⭐ Why |
| :--- | :--- |
| Every profile has prices, FAQ, tone, safety | a partial profile grounds a bad agent |
| ⭐ Every price has a **currency** | ⛔ *a bare number is a bug waiting for a border* |
| ⭐⭐ Every price is an **integer in minor units** | §11.11, no floats, ever |
| ⭐ `payment_pattern`, `schedule_mode`, `retail` present and valid | ⭐ **they configure the tenant** |
| ⭐ **Callout fee present or explicitly `none`** | ⛔ *silence here is the costly kind* |
| ⭐ No GSM-hostile characters in SMS-class strings | ⭐ **one em-dash halves the budget** (§15.3) |
| ⭐ Reading grade ≤6 on customer-facing strings | |
| Jargon lint | |
| ⭐ Every `slug` unique across the pack | |
| ⭐⭐ **No `[fill-me]` in a price that would go live** | §25.2 |

⭐ **Parse is all-or-nothing per block.** A malformed profile is rejected with its
line number; ⭐ **the other 199 still seed.**

## 50.5 ⭐ SEEDING ORDER

```
  ① language packs        everything else references keys
  ② profiles             ⭐ 200 — the spine of the content system
  ③ design systems       mapped from the 192 rules
  ④ page templates       generated procedurally
  ⑤ landers              authored, needs profiles for prices
  ⑥ site decks + app strings
  ⑦ help                 ⭐ generated from manifests, then narrative on top
  ⑧ lifecycle + campaigns + QA templates
  ⑨ ad sets · video scripts
  ⑩ ⭐ doc packs          ⛔ nothing to seed — they RENDER
```

⭐ **Idempotent by slug.** Re-running the seeder updates in place and never
duplicates — ⭐ **so the content day can be iterative rather than one shot.**

## 50.6 ⭐ SAMPLE BADGING AND PROMOTION

⭐ **Everything seeded from a profile is visibly SAMPLE until the tenant confirms
it.**

| State | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **SAMPLE** | ⭐ badged in the UI, ⛔ **the agent will not quote it** |
| **CONFIRMED** | tenant said yes → ⭐ **`Fact` at confidence 1.00** (§11.3) |
| **EDITED** | theirs entirely |
| ⭐⭐ **The promotion screen** | ⭐ *"here are 12 prices we guessed for a plumber — fix or confirm each"* — **the fastest onboarding path in the platform** |

⛔ **A SAMPLE price is never spoken by the agent** (§16.2 capability gating). ⭐ *It
says "I'd need to confirm that price" — which is true and is better than a
plausible guess.*

## 50.7 WHAT K1 CONTRIBUTES

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Register** | ⭐ **~300 assets indexed** across authored · generated · rendered |
| ⭐ **Authoring actually needed** | ⭐⭐ **100 profiles · 195 landers · ad sets · 6 video scripts · ~18 templates** |
| ⭐ **Needs no words at all** | ⭐⭐ **~1,900 help cards · 200 templates · 200 SEO pages · 200 design systems · 30 doc packs** |
| **Actions** | ~30 |
| **New modules** | ⭐ **none — X-180 already holds this** (§34) |
| **Register lines drained** | 31 *(cumulative 970)* |

⭐⭐ **The headline: of ~300 content assets, only about a fifth need a human to
write anything.** ⛔ **The rest generate or render** — and the rendered ones can
never go stale, because they don't hold a copy of anything.

☐ ⭐ Register of ~300 assets with shape, renderer, seeder, path and status

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §51 · ⭐⭐ THE CONTENT MAP — THE PLACEHOLDER SYSTEM  *(T514)*
⭐ **Five recommendations and five questions at the end. Read 51.7 before deciding.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 51.0 ⛔ THE REAL PROBLEM, NAMED

**It isn't "write the content." It's four things that all fail quietly:**

| ⛔ Failure | Why it happens |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Content written that doesn't match the schema** | a human writing prose ≠ a parser reading blocks → hours of manual fixing |
| ⭐⭐ **Content that's stale before it lands** | ⛔ **help articles describing a system that changed while they were being written** — *exactly what you just flagged* |
| ⭐⭐ **Images** | ⭐ **200 industries × 6–8 slots ≈ 1,200–1,600 images.** *This is the part that kills content projects* |
| ⭐ **No way to see what's done** | 300 assets, multiple sessions, no status → things get written twice or not at all |

---

## 51.1 ⭐⭐ RECOMMENDATION 1 — A MANIFEST, NOT A DOCUMENT

⭐ **`CONTENT-MANIFEST.json` is the map. It is machine-readable, and it is the
only thing Antigravity needs to read.**

```json
{
  "profile.emergency-plumber": {
    "type": "PROFILE",  "status": "AUTHORED",
    "file": "content/profiles/home-trades.md",  "block": "emergency-plumber",
    "seeder": "ProfileSeeder",  "depends_on": ["lang.en-GB"],
    "images": ["hero","service-1","service-2"],  "image_status": "BRIEFED"
  },
  "lander.emergency-plumber": {
    "type": "LANDER",  "status": "GENERATED",
    "generated_from": ["profile.emergency-plumber","skeleton.PIII-18"],
    "seeder": "LanderSeeder"
  }
}
```

| ⭐ Status values | |
| :--- | :--- |
| `MISSING` | nothing exists |
| `BRIEFED` | ⭐ the slot is described, not filled |
| `DRAFTED` | written, unreviewed |
| `AUTHORED` | ⭐ written and reviewed |
| `GENERATED` | ⛔ **needs no writing — an engine makes it** |
| `RENDERED` | ⛔ **needs nothing — it's a view** (§50.1) |

⭐⭐ **Antigravity's whole instruction becomes: *"read the manifest, run each
seeder in dependency order, report anything not `AUTHORED` or better."*** ⭐ **And
progress is a query, not a memory.**

## 51.2 ⭐⭐ RECOMMENDATION 2 — IMAGE BRIEFS, NOT IMAGES

> ⭐⭐ **We do not need 1,600 images. We need 1,600 sentences.**

⛔ **Pre-generating a library is the trap:** it costs a fortune, takes weeks,
⭐ **and gives forty plumbers the same hero photo.**

```
  TEMPLATE SHIPS WITH:
    hero: "a tradesperson's van parked outside a suburban home,
           daylight, wide shot, no visible branding"
       │
  AT TENANT SIGNUP:
       ├─ ⭐ their real photo exists?  ──► use it            (best)
       ├─ ⭐ generate once, for them   ──► X-178             (good, unique to them)
       └─ ⭐ replaced automatically when a real photo arrives (§39.4)
```

| ⭐ Why this is better, not just cheaper | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Every tenant's images are unique** | ⛔ *not the same stock photo as forty competitors* |
| **Cost scales with signups**, not with the library | |
| ⭐ **Generated is a placeholder that upgrades itself** | their real van photo replaces it |
| ⭐ **The brief is reusable** | one sentence serves 200 tenants, differently each time |

⭐ **The exception — where we DO need real images now:** the 7 site decks, the
marketing site, the 6 video scripts, and ⭐ **~20 hero images for the industry
picker** *(so the picker looks alive)*. **That's ~40 real images, not 1,600.**

## 51.3 ⭐⭐ RECOMMENDATION 3 — HELP ARTICLES ARE WRITTEN **LAST**

⭐ **You're right that they need rewriting. The answer is not to rewrite them
now.**

| ⭐ Layer | Status |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **~1,900 generated help cards** | ⛔ **need no writing, ever** — they render from action manifests and ⭐ **cannot go stale by construction** (§12.8) |
| ⭐ **~40 narrative articles** | ⭐ *why* and *when*, sitting above the generated *what* and *how* |

⛔ **The 132 legacy articles describe a system that no longer exists** — 247
modules, a different scheduler, a different commerce model, a different money
model. ⭐ **Rewriting them now guarantees rewriting them twice.**

⭐⭐ **So: help is authored at K3, after V1–V6 verification, when the system has
stopped moving.** ⭐ **And it drops from 132 articles to ~40**, because the
generated cards cover everything mechanical.

## 51.4 ⭐⭐ RECOMMENDATION 4 — GENERATE THE 200 LANDERS, POLISH 20

⭐ **A lander needs: a headline, a problem, proof, services, prices, FAQ, a CTA
and a town.** ⭐⭐ **The profile already holds all of it.**

```
  profile + PIII-18 skeleton + the 192 design rules ──► ⭐ 200 landers, generated
                                                            │
                                        ⭐ hand-polish the top 20 verticals
```

⭐⭐ **That moves 195 assets from AUTHORED to GENERATED** — the single biggest
scope reduction available. ⭐ **And it's the same procedural approach already
proven for the 200 page templates** (§25.2).

⚠️ **The honest trade:** generated landers will be *good*, not *excellent*.
⭐ **So polish the 20 verticals that matter most** — the ones the outreach machine
targets first — and let the long tail be generated.

## 51.5 ⭐ RECOMMENDATION 5 — SEQUENCE BY WHAT THE SYSTEM CAN STILL CHANGE

| Batch | Content | ⭐ Depends on code? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **NOW** | **100 profiles** · **ad sets** · tone seeds | ⛔ **no — write today, safely** |
| **SOON** | campaign templates · lifecycle · QA templates | shape only, and it's settled |
| **AFTER U1–U4** | landers · site decks *(revisions)* | needs the final block schema |
| ⭐⭐ **LAST (K3)** | ⭐ **narrative help · video scripts** | ⛔ **needs the system to stop moving** |

⭐⭐ **Profiles and ad sets are safe to write today** — ⭐ **and they're the two
biggest authored blocks.** *Everything that can be written now, can be written
now.*

## 51.6 ⭐ THE FILE LAYOUT

```
  content/
    ⭐ CONTENT-MANIFEST.json      ← the map. Antigravity reads this.
    profiles/
      home-trades.md              ⭐ ~35 profiles, one file per family
      health-beauty.md
      auto.md  food.md  professional.md  home-services.md
    ads/        by-vertical.md
    landers/    ⛔ generated — no files
    campaigns/  templates.md
    lifecycle/  ladders.md
    qa/         templates.md
    help/       ⭐ narrative/ (~40, written at K3)
    site/       decks.md
    video/      scripts.md
    images/     ⭐ briefs.json  +  real/ (~40 actual files)
```

⭐ **Six profile files by family, not one giant file and not 200 small ones.**
⭐⭐ **A family is one sitting's work**, it merges cleanly, and a corrupted file
loses 35 profiles instead of 200.

⛔ **This supersedes §34.2's single-file design** — ⭐ **at 300 assets across
multiple sessions, one file is a merge risk and a progress blindspot.** *The
manifest gives us the single-handover property without the single-file fragility.*

---

## 51.7 ⭐⭐ FIVE QUESTIONS — I NEED THESE ANSWERED

| # | Question | ⭐ My recommendation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Q1** | **One file per family (6 files) or one giant file?** | ⭐⭐ **Six files.** One sitting each, clean merges, and a corruption loses 35 not 200 |
| ⭐⭐ **Q2** | **Images: briefs generated per tenant, or a pre-built library?** | ⭐⭐ **Briefs.** 1,600 sentences instead of 1,600 images — ⭐ **cheaper, faster, and every tenant's images are unique** |
| ⭐⭐ **Q3** | **The 100 new profiles — do I draft them for you to review, or do you supply the prices?** | ⭐ **I draft, you review.** ⛔ **But I need to know: are these UK, US, or both?** — *currency, spelling, callout conventions and 999 vs 911 all change* |
| ⭐ **Q4** | **Ad sets — which platforms, and how many per vertical?** | ⭐ **Meta + Google, 3 angles each per vertical.** *Ads are descoped as a product (§44), but sample ad copy is still content the tenant uses* |
| ⭐⭐ **Q5** | **200 landers: generate all, or hand-write?** | ⭐⭐ **Generate all 200, hand-polish 20.** Moves 195 assets from authored to generated — **the biggest scope cut available** |

⭐ **And one more I'd like a steer on:** ⭐⭐ **how many industries do you actually
want live at launch?** ⛔ *200 profiles at SAMPLE quality is worse than 60 that are
genuinely right* — and the picker can grow monthly. **My instinct is 60–80 excellent
beats 200 thin.** ⭐ **SETTLED (§52.4): all 200 exist so nobody hits a wall; 80 are premium-badged and the set is promoted by demand.**

## 51.8 WHAT §51 CHANGES

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **New artifact** | ⭐⭐ **`CONTENT-MANIFEST.json`** — the map, machine-readable, the only thing Antigravity reads |

| ⭐ **Scope cut** | ⭐⭐ **195 landers → generated · 1,600 images → briefs · 132 help articles → ~40, written last** |
| ⭐ **Actual authoring left** | ⭐⭐ **100 profiles · ad sets · ~18 templates · ~40 narrative articles · 6 video scripts · ~40 real images** |
| **Modules** | ⭐ **247 — no change.** X-180 gains the manifest reader |

⭐⭐ **The honest summary: the content job just got about a third the size it

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §52 · ⭐⭐ THE ANTIGRAVITY SETUP + THE CONTENT PATH  *(answers T515)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 52.1 ⛔⛔ Q1 ANSWERED — AND IT CONTRADICTS THE ASSUMPTION

**You said Antigravity works best with a master document. The research says the
opposite, and there's a hard number behind it.**

> ⛔⛔ **Rules files are capped at 12,000 characters.** *"That's generous compared
> to some tools, but it's a hard limit worth knowing **before you paste in an
> entire style guide and wonder why half of it gets ignored.**"*

⛔ **Our master plan is ~590,000 characters. That is 49× the cap.** ⭐ **A single
master document would be mostly ignored — silently.**

### ⭐⭐ WHAT ANTIGRAVITY ACTUALLY WANTS

| Mechanism | ⭐ Purpose | Where |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **`AGENTS.md`** | root-level constraints — **read since IDE 1.20.5** | workspace root |
| ⭐ **Rules** | ⭐ persistent context **at the prompt level** · ⛔ **12k char cap each** | `.agents/rules/` |
| ⭐⭐ **Skills** | ⭐⭐ **instructions + scripts + references + assets that LOAD ONLY WHEN RELEVANT — "preventing context bloat"** | `.agents/skills/` |
| ⭐ **Workflows** | ⭐ **a structured sequence of steps at the trajectory level** | `.agents/workflows/` |
| **Knowledge Items** | persistent memory across sessions | managed |

⛔⛔ **And the fact that decides everything:** *"Agent context resets between
sessions. Unlike Claude Code where your CLAUDE.md persists, **Antigravity agents
start fresh each session.**"*

⭐⭐ **So nothing can live in conversation. Everything must be in files the agent
re-reads.** *Which is exactly why our three-file discipline was right — but the
files need restructuring for Antigravity, not handing over whole.*

### ⭐⭐ THE RECOMMENDED LAYOUT

```
  workspace/
    ⭐ AGENTS.md                    ← under 12k. The map, the laws, the pointers.
    .agents/
      rules/
        ⭐ 01-precedence.md          §0 kill list — under 12k
        02-entities.md              the 12 nouns
        03-actions.md               the manifest format
        04-laws.md                  the 79 standing laws
      ⭐⭐ skills/
        goaiez-spine/     SKILL.md + references/§11–§14
        goaiez-channels/  SKILL.md + references/§15–§16
        goaiez-seo/       SKILL.md + references/§31–§32
        goaiez-money/     SKILL.md + references/§45–§46
        goaiez-fsm/       SKILL.md + references/§30
        ⭐ goaiez-content/  SKILL.md + scripts/seed.py + references/schemas
      workflows/
        ⭐ build-module.md · seed-content.md · verify-module.md
```

⭐⭐ **The master plan doesn't get pasted — it gets SPLIT into skill references,
and the agent loads only the section it needs.** ⭐ *That's the mechanism the tool
was built around, and it's why our §-numbering was worth maintaining.*

⭐ **One critical detail:** *"the description is the only thing the agent sees
before deciding whether a skill is worth reading in full"* — ⭐⭐ **so skill
descriptions must be third-person and keyword-dense.** *A vague description means
the skill never loads.*

### ⭐ SO FOR CONTENT (Q1)

⛔ **Not one giant file.** ⭐⭐ **The manifest + per-family files + a
`goaiez-content` skill that knows how to read them** — ⭐ **because a 200-profile
single file would blow past every context boundary the tool has.**

---

## 52.2 ⭐⭐ Q3 — US CORE. THIS IS THE BIGGEST SIMPLIFICATION YET

✅ **Adopted: everything is authored US-first.**

| ⭐ What this settles | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Currency | **USD** |
| Spelling | **US** |
| Emergency | **911** |
| Callout conventions | **US trade norms** |
| ⭐ Units | **imperial** |

⭐⭐ **And the localisation ruling: an AI script converts later.** ⛔ **Not 31
hand-written locale sets — one script, run per locale.**

### ⚠️ BUT — ONE THING THE SCRIPT MUST NEVER DO

> ⛔⛔ **Translate the words. NEVER convert the numbers.**

⭐ **A plumber's rate in Manchester is not a currency-converted US rate.** It's a
different market with different labour costs, different VAT and different
expectations.

| ⭐ Localised | ⛔ Never localised |
| :--- | :--- |
| FAQ answers, tone, copy | ⛔ **prices** |
| Service names | ⛔ **callout fees** |
| Spelling and idiom | ⛔ **price ranges** |
| Emergency number *(911 → 999 → 112)* | |
| Units *(imperial → metric)* | |

⭐⭐ **Non-US prices become `[MARKET-FILL]`** — ⛔ **and a `[MARKET-FILL]` price
cannot go live** (§50.4). ⭐ **The tenant's own prices override on day one
anyway**, so this costs nothing real — *it just stops us telling a British plumber
his callout fee is $85.*

---

## 52.3 ⭐ Q4 — SCRAPE THE PUBLIC AD LIBRARIES

✅ **3 angles per vertical, Meta + Google.** ⭐ **And there's a cleaner route than
scraping:**

| Source | ⭐ Access |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Meta Ad Library** | ⭐ **has a public API** — searchable, filterable by country and advertiser |
| ⭐ **Google Ads Transparency Center** | public, browsable by advertiser and region |

⭐ **So it's "use the public API", not "scrape"** — cleaner, more reliable, and it
doesn't break when a layout changes.

```
  pull live ads for a vertical ──► ⭐ AI extracts the ANGLE, not the words
                                        │
                                   ⭐⭐ rewrite original, in our voice,
                                        against our profile data
```

⛔ **We take the *pattern*, never the copy.** ⭐ *"Emergency trades lead with
response time; salons lead with the transformation"* is the useful output — and
it's an observation, not someone's sentence.

⭐⭐ **And this is the same engine as X-135's research agent and the Chrome
extension** — ⭐ *the ad-angle miner is a use of the scraper we already built,
pointed at a public API.*

---

## 52.4 ⭐⭐ Q6 — 200 EXIST, 80 ARE PREMIUM. AND THE LOOP IS THE CLEVER PART

✅ **Adopted, and it's the right shape:** ⭐ **nobody ever hits "your industry
isn't supported"**, but 80 are demonstrably excellent.

| Tier | Count | ⭐ State |
| :--- | ---: | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **PREMIUM** | **80** | ⭐ **hand-polished · real prices · full FAQ · polished lander · reviewed images** — **badged in the picker** |
| **STANDARD** | 120 | generated, functional, **SAMPLE-heavy, honestly labelled** |

⭐ **The picker defaults to premium**, with *"show all 200"* one tap away. ⛔ **A
standard profile never pretends to be premium** — its SAMPLE badges are visible
and the agent won't quote its prices (§50.6).

### ⭐⭐ THE PROMOTION LOOP

```
  an industry crosses N active tenants
       │
  ⭐ it earns promotion to PREMIUM ──► we author it properly
       │
  ⭐⭐ demand tells us which 120 are worth the work — we never guess
```

⭐⭐ **So the 80 aren't a fixed list, they're a leaderboard.** ⛔ *And no tenant
data crosses a boundary* — ⭐ **the signal is a count** (§20.0), and the authoring
is ours.

---

## 52.5 ⭐ Q5 — ALL 200 POLISHED, AS A SEPARATE PROJECT

✅ **Adopted.** ⭐ **A dedicated Claude Code project is the right call**, because:

- ⭐ **It's a different kind of work** — writing and image generation, not architecture
- ⭐ **It parallelises** — content generation runs while the build runs
- ⭐⭐ **It has a different output** — ⛔ **files, not a plan**
- **It can run long** — 200 landers is a batch job, not a conversation

⭐ **What it needs from us, and all of it now exists:** the profile schema
(§50.3), the `PIII-18` skeleton, the 192 design rules, the block JSON format,
the manifest, ⭐ **and the image-brief convention.**

## 52.6 ⭐ Q2 — IMAGES, DEFERRED AS YOU SAID

✅ **Parked until the build document is done.** ⭐ **The decision that matters is
already made (§51.2): briefs, not a library** — so ⭐ **the provider choice is a
config row, not an architecture.**

⭐ **A starting shortlist for when we get there:** Grok · the cheapest OpenAI
image model · Gemini/Imagen · and the open-weight options for self-hosting at
volume. ⭐ **It's the same per-component, measured-not-configured selection as the
voice stack** (§18F.4).

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §53 · ⭐⭐ THE ANTIGRAVITY PACKAGE — BUILT SO CONTEXT LOSS DOESN'T MATTER  *(T516)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 53.0 ⭐⭐ THE ACTUAL REQUIREMENT, IN YOUR WORDS

> ⭐ *"Antigravity loses context all the time."*

⛔ **That is not a problem to work around. It is the design constraint.** And the
research confirms it: *"Antigravity agents start fresh each session"* (§52.1).

> ⭐⭐ **So the plan is not documentation. The plan IS the agent's memory.**

⭐ **Everything below exists to make one sentence true:** ⭐⭐ *a fresh agent, with
zero context, opens the workspace and knows exactly what to do next and how to do
it correctly.*

---

## 53.1 ⭐ Q7 AND Q8 — ANSWERED

| # | ✅ Ruling |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Q7 · Localisation** | ⭐⭐ **RUNTIME, cached.** ⛔ 200 × 31 = **6,200 profiles pre-built is absurd** for locales with no tenants. Translate on demand, cache the result, ⭐ **and it's per-tenant anyway once they confirm their own words** |
| ⭐ **Q8 · Premium industries** | ⭐⭐ **Your 80 to start, then promoted by demand.** ⛔ *A count at zero tenants tells you nothing* — your judgement seeds it, the leaderboard runs it after launch |

---

## 53.2 ⭐⭐ THE PACKAGE

```
  workspace/
    ⭐ AGENTS.md                      ← <12k. The map. Read every session.
    │
    .agents/
      ⭐ rules/                        ← <12k each. Always in context.
        01-precedence.md              §0 — the kill list
        02-entities.md                the 12 nouns
        03-actions.md                 the manifest format
        04-laws.md                    the standing laws
        ⭐ 05-status.md                ⭐⭐ WHERE WE ARE
      │
      ⭐⭐ skills/                      ← loaded ONLY when relevant
        goaiez-spine/     goaiez-channels/   goaiez-intelligence/
        goaiez-data/      goaiez-pixel/      goaiez-surfaces/
        goaiez-builder/   goaiez-crm/        goaiez-fsm/
        goaiez-seo/       goaiez-reviews/    goaiez-social/
        goaiez-money/     goaiez-attribution/
        ⭐ goaiez-ui/      ⭐ goaiez-content/  goaiez-verify/
      │
      workflows/                      ← step sequences
        ⭐⭐ resume.md                  ⭐ THE FIRST THING EVERY SESSION RUNS
        build-module.md · verify-module.md · seed-content.md · merge.md
      │
      ⭐⭐ state/                       ⭐ THE TRACKING PACKAGE
        ⭐ BUILD-STATE.json            machine-readable, every module
        SESSION-LOG.md                append-only, what each session did
        CONTENT-MANIFEST.json         §51.1
```

## 53.3 ⭐⭐ `BUILD-STATE.json` — THE ANSWER TO "IT CAN'T GET LOST"

```json
{
  "X-163": {
    "name": "PriceBook",  "phase": "W1",
    "spec": "skills/goaiez-fsm/references/30-2-pricebook.md",
    "status": "BUILT",
    "manifest": true, "migrations": true, "routes": true,
    "wired": true, "tested": true, "runtime_proof": true,
    "verified_by": "QA-4",  "session": "2026-09-14-a",
    "blocks": ["X-164","X-166","X-175"]
  }
}
```

| ⭐ Status | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| `NOT_STARTED` · `MANIFEST` · `BUILDING` · `BUILT` · `WIRED` · `VERIFIED` | |
| ⛔ `BLOCKED` | with the reason, and what it's waiting on |

⭐⭐ **An agent reads the state, picks the next unblocked item, builds it, updates
the row. Context loss becomes irrelevant, because the state was never in its
head.**

⭐ **And it's greppable:** *"what's left?"* · *"what's blocked?"* · *"what did
last session do?"* are all one command — ⛔ **not a memory and not a guess.**

## 53.4 ⭐⭐ `workflows/resume.md` — THE ANTI-CONTEXT-LOSS PRIMITIVE

⭐ **The first thing every session runs, without being asked:**

```
  ① read .agents/state/BUILD-STATE.json
  ② read the last 3 entries of SESSION-LOG.md
  ③ report: "X of 247 built · Y verified · Z blocked"
  ④ ⭐ propose the next unblocked item and name its spec file
  ⑤ ⛔ STOP. Wait for confirmation.
```

⭐⭐ **Five steps, and step ⑤ is the important one** — ⛔ *an agent that resumes by
guessing is worse than one that asks.*

## 53.5 ⭐ `AGENTS.md` — THE ONE FILE THAT'S ALWAYS READ

⛔ **Under 12,000 characters. Ruthlessly.** It holds only:

| ⭐ Contents |
| :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **"Run `workflows/resume.md` first"** |
| The precedence law + a pointer to the kill list |
| ⭐ **The 12 entity names** *(not their schemas — the names)* |
| ⭐ **The 10 laws that prevent the worst mistakes** *(not all 80 — the ten)* |
| The skill index: ⭐ **which skill for which job** |
| ⛔ **"Never invent a module number. Check `BUILD-STATE.json`."** |
| ⛔ **"Never write to a file another agent owns. Check the warden map."** |

⭐ **Everything else is a pointer.** ⭐⭐ *If it isn't preventing a catastrophe, it
doesn't belong in the always-loaded file.*

## 53.6 ⭐⭐ EVERY REMAINING PHASE PRODUCES ITS SKILL DIRECTLY

⛔ **This is the change that stops B4 becoming a giant conversion job.**

| Phase | ⭐ Produces |
| :--- | :--- |
| **K1–K3** | ⭐ `goaiez-content/` — schemas, the manifest, `scripts/seed.py` |
| ⭐⭐ **U1–U4** | ⭐⭐ **`goaiez-ui/`** — see 53.7 |
| **V1–V6** | ⭐ `goaiez-verify/` + `workflows/verify-module.md` |
| **T1–T3** | tenant-zero config, as data |
| **W1–W3** | the 60 agent presets + the warden map |
| **B1–B4** | ⭐ `BUILD-STATE.json` seeded · dependency order · ⭐ **final assembly** |

⭐⭐ **So B4 assembles things already in the right shape** — ⛔ *rather than
converting 600KB of prose into an agent environment at the last minute, which is
exactly when it would go wrong.*

⭐ **NEW LAW 81:** *every phase from here produces its Antigravity artifact, not a
document about it.*

## 53.7 ⭐⭐ THE UI SKILL — AND WHY IT NEEDS REBUILDING

⛔ **`ui-ux-pro-max` was chosen when the plan had ~176 modules. It now has 247**,
and ⭐ **the new surfaces are the ones with no precedent in any design system:**

| ⭐ New surface | Nothing like it exists |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **The dispatch board** | *"what can be moved"* (§29.2) |
| ⭐⭐ **The supply meter** | ⭐ *"your cadence exceeds your material"* (§41.4) |
| ⭐ **The QA report** | themes, per-tech quality (§37.3②) |
| ⭐ **The content week** | 7 cards with *"why this post?"* (§39.5) |
| ⭐⭐ **The attribution row** | ⭐ *"this page earned £7,340"* (§49.5) |
| ⭐ **The COOLING list** | (§20.1) |
| ⭐ **The decline-at-the-door flow** | (§46A.2) |
| ⭐ **The multi-client console** | sorted by what's wrong (§47.1) |
| ⭐ **The wind-down warnings** | (§45A.3) |

⭐ **What `goaiez-ui/` must carry:**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **The two languages and which surface gets which** | D1 — God-Mode console, Honest Counter tenant app |
| **The 192 industry rules** | mapped to the 200 profiles |
| ⭐ **The full screen inventory** | U2's output — every screen of 247 modules |
| ⭐⭐ **The new patterns above**, as reference components | ⛔ *because no design system has them* |
| **Tokens, spacing, type scale** | from `ui-ux-pro-max`'s MASTER |
| ⭐ **The 16px floor and tabular numerals** | ⭐ *a plumber reading a number in a van* |
| ⭐ **Anti-patterns per vertical** | from the 192 rules |

⭐⭐ **U1–U4 don't write a design document. They write this skill.**

## 53.8 ⭐ THE UPLOAD PACKAGE — WHAT ACTUALLY GETS HANDED OVER

```
  goaiez-workspace.zip
    ⭐ AGENTS.md
    .agents/{rules,skills,workflows,state}/
    content/{CONTENT-MANIFEST.json, profiles/, ads/, ...}
    ⭐ README-FIRST.md      ← for the human: what this is, what to type
```

⭐⭐ **And `README-FIRST.md` is three lines:**

> ⭐ *"Open this workspace in Antigravity. Type: **run resume**. It will tell you
> where the build is and what's next."*

⛔ **Nothing else.** ⭐ *If a human needs more than three lines, the package has
failed.*

## 53.9 ⭐ WHY THIS IS WORTH TWO DAYS

⭐⭐ **You said you're spending two days on this plan because Antigravity loses
context. That's the correct trade, and here's the arithmetic:**

| ⛔ Without the package | ⭐ With it |
| :--- | :--- |
| Every session re-explains the architecture | ⭐ `resume` reports it in one command |
| Agents invent module numbers | ⛔ `BUILD-STATE.json` is the register |
| Two agents build the same thing | ⭐ status prevents it |
| ⭐ **A module ships unwired and nobody notices** | ⭐⭐ `wired: false` is visible and greppable |
| Context loss = rework | ⭐⭐ **context loss = one file read** |

⭐⭐ **Two days now against a rebuild later is not close.** ⛔ *Five prior runs
produced ~126 uncalled files that each described themselves as working — that is
what context loss without a state file costs.*

| ✅ **Q7** | ⭐ **runtime localisation, cached** |
| ✅ **Q8** | ⭐ **your 80, then promotion by demand** |

## 54.3 ⭐ THE AUTHORING BRIEF

**What the content project runs against. One profile at a time, schema at
§50.3.**

### ⭐⭐ The five things that make a profile good

| # | ⭐ Rule |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **1** | ⭐⭐ **Prices a real operator would recognise.** ⛔ *A wrong price is worse than a range — it teaches the tenant we don't know their trade* |
| ⭐ **2** | ⭐⭐ **The callout fee is mandatory** *(§43.5)* — the most-asked question in the trades |
| ⭐ **3** | ⭐ **FAQ from what customers actually ask**, not what a marketer would write |
| ⭐ **4** | ⭐ **Tone in their voice, not ours** — *a locksmith at 2am is not a spa* |
| ⭐ **5** | ⭐⭐ **The three config fields right** — `payment_pattern` · `schedule_mode` · `retail` *(§50.3)* — ⛔ **they configure the whole tenant** |

| **Standard (120)** | 5–8 | 5–8 | ranges where fixed pricing is impossible |

### ⛔ What every profile must NOT do

⛔ Give medical, legal or financial advice · ⛔ quote a price the trade prices by
inspection *(use a range)* · ⛔ promise a timeframe · ⛔ ⭐ **name a competitor** ·
⛔ use jargon above grade 6 · ⛔ ⭐ **omit the emergency line where the trade has
one** *(999/911-first, §50.3 SAFETY)*.

### ⭐ Image briefs — one line each

⭐ **Per §51.2: sentences, not images.** Six slots per profile:

```
hero:      "a [trade] van outside a suburban home, daylight, wide, unbranded"
service-1: "[the most common job] in progress, hands and tools, close"
service-2: "[the second job], mid-shot"
before:    "[the typical problem state]"
after:     "[the same, resolved]"
team:      "a [trade] professional at a doorstep, friendly, no logo"
```

⛔ **Never a face we'd need permission for. Never a brand mark. Never a price in
an image** *(§39.4)*.

# §55 · ⛔ LAW 82 + K2b — TEMPLATES, LANDERS, DESIGN MAPPINGS  *(T518)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 55.0 ⛔⛔ LAW 82 — NO CONTENT IS AUTHORED IN THIS CHAT

> ⛔ **This chat produces SPECIFICATIONS. It never produces the content itself.**

⭐ **The reason is arithmetic, not preference:** 200 profiles at ~600 words each
is **~120,000 words**. ⛔ **It would consume this context entirely and the
remaining turns would be lost** — ⭐ *which is the one outcome we're trying to
avoid, because migrating a chat this deep is genuinely hard.*

| ⭐ Here | ⛔ Elsewhere |
| :--- | :--- |
| Schemas · rosters · briefs · manifests · conventions | ⛔ **profiles · landers · ads · help · images** |
| ⭐ **Everything an agent needs to produce content correctly** | ⭐ **the content** |

⭐ **And a note on my own output:** ⭐⭐ **long sections are the risk to the
22-turn goal.** ⛔ *From here I keep them shorter — the specs stay complete, the
prose gets leaner.*

---

## 55.1 ⭐ K2b — WHAT THIS TURN SPECIFIES

### ⭐⭐ 200 LANDERS — GENERATED, NOT WRITTEN *(§51.4)*

```
  profile + PIII-18 skeleton + industry design rule ──► ⭐ lander
```

| Section | ⭐ Source — all of it already exists |
| :--- | :--- |
| Headline | ⭐ profile `name` + the primary service + the town token |
| Problem | ⭐ **the top FAQ, inverted** — *"Boiler out? Here's what it costs."* |
| Proof | review count + rating tokens *(live at render)* |
| Services | profile `SERVICES` |
| ⭐ **Prices** | ⭐⭐ **rendered from the pricebook, never copied** *(§50.1)* |
| FAQ | profile `FAQ`, top 5 |
| ⭐ **Callout line** | ⭐ profile `CALLOUT` — *the highest-converting single line* |
| CTA | `schedule_mode` decides: **book** vs **call** vs **quote** |

⭐ **Hand-polish only the 20 highest-value verticals.** ⛔ The other 180 generate
and stay good-not-excellent — ⭐ *and the growth loop will tell us which ones
deserve promotion* (§40.3).

### ⭐ 200 PAGE TEMPLATES — PROCEDURAL

⭐ **Unchanged from §25.2 and it was right:** generated in seconds by the block
engine, **not one LLM call per template**. Copy assembled from direct-response
frames, filled from the profile. ⛔ **No price is ever generated** — `[fill-me]`
that can't go live.

### ⭐ DESIGN MAPPINGS — 200 × THE 192 RULES

⭐ **A mapping table, not authored design:** each profile's `family` and
`schedule_mode` select one of the 192 industry rules → palette, type pairing,
layout pattern, **and its anti-patterns**.

⛔ **8 industries have no clean rule match.** ⭐ **They fall back to the family
default and are flagged in the manifest as `DESIGN_FALLBACK`** — ⭐ *visible, not
silently wrong.*

### ⭐ FUNNELS — THREE SHAPES, NOT 200

⛔ **A funnel per industry is waste.** ⭐ **Three shapes cover every vertical**,
selected by `schedule_mode` and `payment_pattern`:

| Shape | For | Path |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **EMERGENCY** | job mode, urgent trades | ⭐ *land → call now → booked* — **one step** |
| **QUOTE** | job mode, considered | land → detail → quote request → follow-up ladder |
| **BOOK** | appointment mode | land → service pick → slot → deposit |

⭐ **The profile picks the shape.** ⛔ *A locksmith and a wedding planner need
different funnels; a locksmith and a plumber do not.*

| Asset | Count | Status |

| ⭐ **Funnels** | ⭐⭐ **3** | `AUTHORED` — ⛔ **not 200** |
| Industry SEO pages | 200 | ⭐ `RENDERED` — views of the profile registry |

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §57 · U1 — THE DESIGN SYSTEM · WRITES `goaiez-ui/`  *(EXECUTED T520)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 57.1 ⭐ THE TWO LANGUAGES — D1 MADE CONCRETE

| | ⭐ **HONEST COUNTER** — tenant app | ⭐ **GOD-MODE** — operator + agency console + marketing site |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Read by** | ⭐⭐ **a plumber, on a phone, in a van, in daylight** | an agency buyer at a desk |
| **Background** | light | dark |
| **Depth** | ⭐ **borders, not shadows** | glass, glow, ambient motion |
| ⭐ **Type floor** | ⭐⭐ **16px minimum, no exceptions** | 14px acceptable |
| ⭐ **Numbers** | ⭐⭐ **tabular figures, always** | tabular |
| **Density** | generous | dense |
| **Motion** | ⛔ **functional only** | orchestrated |

⭐ **MASTER.md is Honest Counter; console pages override to God-Mode** — one
hierarchy, `ui-ux-pro-max`'s own mechanism (§0.5).

⛔ **The 16px floor is not a preference.** ⭐ *Sunlight, a cracked screen, and
reading glasses left in the other van. Every number a tenant acts on is 16px or
larger and set in tabular figures so columns align.*

## 57.2 ⭐⭐ THE NINE SURFACES WITH NO PRECEDENT

⭐ **These are why a stock design system isn't enough** (§53.7). Each gets a
reference component in the skill:

| ⭐ Surface | The design problem it poses |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **The dispatch board** | ⭐ *"what can be moved"* — **a third state between free and busy** |
| ⭐⭐ **The supply meter** | ⭐ **showing someone their ask exceeds their material, without it reading as a downsell** |
| ⭐ **The QA report** | themes ranked by frequency, with a per-person cut that ⛔ **must not read as a league table** |
| ⭐ **The content week** | 7 cards, each carrying ⭐ *"why this post?"* |
| ⭐⭐ **The attribution row** | ⭐ **one sentence that ends in money** |
| ⭐ **The COOLING list** | a list whose whole value is *"these went quiet"* |
| ⭐⭐ **Decline at the door** | ⭐ **one screen, glare, gloves, 15 seconds, and a customer watching** |
| ⭐ **The multi-client console** | 30 clients sorted by what's wrong, ⭐ **quiet ones collapsed** |
| ⭐⭐ **The wind-down warnings** | ⭐ **urgent without being cruel** — *they're losing their number* |

⭐⭐ **Decline-at-the-door is the hardest** and deserves the most care: ⛔ *the tech
is standing in someone's hallway, the customer is watching the screen, and the
wrong word blames them.* ⭐ **Biggest touch targets in the system, two choices
maximum, and the words come from §46A.2.**

## 57.3 ⭐ THE TOKENS

```
  ⭐ TYPE
    display   a characterful face, used ONLY on the marketing site
    body      a workhorse — legible at 16px on a bad screen in sun
    ⭐ data    ⭐⭐ tabular numerals, non-negotiable

  ⭐ SCALE     4px base · 16px type floor (tenant) · 44px min touch target
  COLOR       6 named values per language · ⭐ semantic, never literal
              (⭐ "urgent" not "red" — so a theme can move)
  ⭐ STATE     ⭐⭐ every component ships: default · loading · empty · error · SAMPLE
```

⛔ **`SAMPLE` is a first-class visual state** *(§50.6)* — ⭐ **the only design
system I know of that needs one**, because a seeded price must look unconfirmed.

⭐ **And per the design guidance: empty states are an invitation to act, errors
say what happened and how to fix it, and a button that says "Publish" produces a
toast that says "Published."**

## 57.4 ⭐ THE COPY RULES — DESIGN MATERIAL, NOT DECORATION

| ⭐ Rule | Example |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Name things by what people control** | ⭐ *"missed calls"* — ⛔ never *"webhook events"* |
| **Active voice, same word throughout a flow** | "Send" → "Sent" |
| ⭐ **Specific beats clever** | ⭐ *"9 leads it lost"* — ⛔ not *"recover lost revenue"* |
| ⛔ **Errors don't apologise and are never vague** | ⭐ *"the bank didn't authorise it"* *(§46A.2)* |
| ⭐ **Grade ≤6, jargon linted** | ⛔ *no "attribution", no "orchestration"* |

## 57.5 ⭐ WHAT `goaiez-ui/` CONTAINS

```
  goaiez-ui/
    ⭐ SKILL.md            third-person, keyword-dense (§52.1)
    references/
      ⭐ 01-languages.md    the two systems + which surface gets which
      02-tokens.md         type · scale · colour · state
      ⭐ 03-surfaces.md     ⭐⭐ the nine, as reference components
      04-copy.md           the rules above
      ⭐ 05-industries.md   ⭐ the 192 rules → 200 profiles + 8 fallbacks
      06-screens.md        ⭐ U2's inventory
    assets/                tokens.json · the two theme files
```

⭐ **SKILL.md's description decides whether it ever loads** *(§52.1)* — so it
names the surfaces and the languages explicitly, in third person.

## 57.6 ACCEPTANCE — U1

☐ ⭐ Two languages defined; ⭐⭐ **MASTER = Honest Counter, console overrides**
☐ ⭐⭐ **16px floor and tabular numerals, non-negotiable in the tenant app**
☐ ⭐ Nine precedent-free surfaces named with their design problems
☐ ⭐⭐ **Decline-at-the-door treated as the hardest** — glare, gloves, 15 seconds
☐ Tokens semantic not literal; ⭐ **`SAMPLE` as a first-class visual state**
☐ Every component ships 5 states
☐ ⭐ Copy rules: what people control · active voice · specific over clever
☐ ⭐⭐ **Delivered as `goaiez-ui/`, not a document** *(law 81)*

**All eight ✅ — U1 EXECUTED.**

## 59.1 ⭐ TODAY — *what needs you*

⭐ **Three sections, ranked by cost of ignoring:**

```
  ⭐ NEEDS YOU NOW      missed call 4m ago · unanswered lead · a job with no tech
  ⭐ WORTH A MINUTE     3 cooling · 2 unpaid · a review to reply to
  ⭐ HAPPENED           ⭐ 6 calls answered · 2 jobs booked · £840 paid
```

⛔ **No charts.** ⭐ **Every row is a tap-to-act.** ⭐⭐ **And "HAPPENED" is the
retention screen** — *the tenant sees what the platform did while they were under
a sink.*

## 59.2 ⭐ THE THREAD — *one person, every channel*

⭐ **Call, text, RCS, email, form, review, QA response, invoice — one timeline**
*(§15.1)*. ⭐ **Channel is an icon, not a tab.**

| ⭐ Header carries | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Name · ⭐ **how they found you** *(§49.2)* · lifetime value · ⭐ **payment risk** |
| ⭐ **Open job, if any** — one tap to the dispatch board |

⭐ **Reply box picks the channel automatically** *(last used, or the ladder's)* —
⛔ **and says which**, so nobody sends a text thinking it's an email.

## 59.3 ⭐⭐ DECLINE AT THE DOOR — *the hardest screen*

```
  ┌──────────────────────────────┐
  │  ⭐ The bank didn't authorise  │   ← ⛔ never "your card was declined"
  │     that one.                 │
  │                               │
  │  [ ⭐⭐  TRY AGAIN  ]           │   ← soft decline only
  │  [ ⭐   TEXT THEM A LINK  ]    │   ← ⭐ always present
  │                               │
  │  ⭐ Other ways ▾               │   ← another card · transfer · settle later
  └──────────────────────────────┘
```

| ⭐ Constraint | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Two choices visible. Everything else behind "other ways"** | ⛔ *a menu in a hallway is a failure* |
| ⭐ **Largest touch targets in the product** | gloves, cold hands |
| ⭐ **Highest contrast** | daylight on a doorstep |
| ⭐⭐ **The customer can see this screen** | ⛔ **so it never says anything that blames them** |
| ⭐ **Soft vs hard changes the buttons** | ⛔ *"try again" doesn't appear on a hard decline* |

## 59.4 ⭐ THE DISPATCH BOARD

⭐ **Three panes: board · map · ⭐⭐ what can be moved.**

⭐ **The movable pane is the one nobody builds** *(§29.2)* — it lists jobs that
could shift, ⭐ **with the cost of shifting each** *("moves Jenkins to 4pm, adds
12 min drive")*. ⛔ **An emergency at 3pm is a two-tap reshuffle, not a puzzle.**

⭐ **Conflicts show before they happen** — impossible travel, missing parts, skill
mismatch.

## 59.5 ⭐⭐ COOLING — *the list that earns the subscription*

⭐ **Each row is a sentence, not a record:**

> ⭐ *"**Acme Roofing** — 3 visits, pricing twice, quit the quote form at
> 'postcode'. **Quiet 9 days.**"*

| ⭐ Every row carries | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **A drafted opener** — *editable, one tap to send* |
| Call · text · dismiss |
| ⭐ **Why they're here** — the derivation, in words |

⛔ **Sorted by "was hottest, went quietest"** — ⭐ not by recency.

## 59.6 ⭐ THE CONTENT WEEK

⭐ **Seven cards. Image, caption, platform, and ⭐⭐ *"why this post?"***

⭐ **Approve all** finishes the week in one tap. ⭐ Per card: swap image · edit ·
reject · reschedule. ⛔ **A rejected card says what it'll do instead.**

## 59.7 ⭐⭐ PRICE CONFIRMATION — *the fastest onboarding there is*

```
  ⭐ "Here are 12 prices we guessed for a plumber. Fix or confirm each."

  Drain clear          $85    [✓ right]  [edit]      ← ⭐ SAMPLE styling
  Boiler service      $110    [✓ right]  [edit]
  ⭐ Callout fee        $85    [✓ right]  [edit]      ← ⭐⭐ can't skip this one
```

⭐ **One tap per row.** ⭐⭐ **The agent goes live the moment the callout fee and
one price are confirmed** — ⛔ *not when all twelve are.*

## 59.8 ⭐ THE ATTRIBUTION ROW

> ⭐⭐ *"Your **emergency drain** page earned **9 calls** last month. **6 became
> jobs. $7,340.**"*

⭐ **Tap it and the path unfolds** — the visit, the keyword, the call, the
transcript, the job, the invoice. ⛔ **No pie chart. No fractional credit** *(§49.2)*.

## 59.9 ⭐ INSTALL & VERIFY

⭐ **Seven live checks, each green or with the exact fix** *(§20.3)*. ⛔ **Never
"see documentation"** — ⭐ **the AI reads the failure and says the next step in
plain words.**

⭐ **The CNAME is the only manual step**, and it's copy-paste with a per-platform
recipe.

## 59.10 ⭐⭐ ALERT → REPLY BY CODE — *the whole product from a lock screen*

```
  ⭐ SMS: "Acme Roofing is on your pricing page. 3rd visit today.
          Reply C to call, T to text, S to snooze.  [7K3M9]"
```

⛔ **No app. No login.** ⭐ **Five-character code, never reused in the window**
*(§20.2)*. ⭐⭐ **Free text works too** — *the agent sends whatever they type as
the reply.*

## 59.11 ACCEPTANCE — U3

☐ ⭐ Today: three sections by cost of ignoring; ⭐⭐ **"HAPPENED" as the retention screen**
☐ ⭐ Thread: one timeline, ⭐ **channel auto-picked and named**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Decline: two choices, biggest targets, ⛔ never blames the customer**, soft/hard changes the buttons
☐ ⭐ Dispatch: ⭐⭐ **the movable pane with the cost of each move**
☐ ⭐⭐ **COOLING rows are sentences with a drafted opener**, sorted hottest-went-quietest
☐ ⭐ Content week: approve-all, ⭐ **"why this post?"** on every card
☐ ⭐⭐ **Price confirmation: agent goes live on the callout fee + one price**
☐ ⭐ Attribution: one sentence ending in money, ⛔ **no pie charts**
☐ ⭐ Install: seven checks, ⛔ **never "see documentation"**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Alert: five-char code, free text works, no app needed**

**All ten ✅ — U3 EXECUTED.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §61 · V1 — THE VERIFICATION METHOD · WRITES `goaiez-verify/`  *(EXECUTED T524)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 61.0 ⛔⛔ THE STANDING POSITION

> ⛔ **Assume nothing works.**

⭐ **Five prior runs produced ~126 files that were uncalled, unrouted, and each
described itself in its own docblock as working.** ⭐⭐ **That is the failure this
phase exists to catch — and a docblock is not evidence.**

## 61.1 ⭐⭐ THE VERIFY SLOT — THE 16TH FIELD

⭐ **Every module carries it. An empty slot is a visible gap** *(§7A.6)*.

```yaml
VERIFY:
  files:          [the actual paths, listed]
  ⭐ assertion:    "what must be TRUE, stated so it can be false"
  ⭐⭐ runtime_proof: "a real artifact — a row, a log line, a recording, a screenshot"
  verdict:        MATCHES | PARTIAL | ABSENT | WRONG
  ⭐ dated:        when · by which agent · against which commit
```

⛔ **Four verdicts, and `PARTIAL` is the important one** — ⭐ *"it exists and it
half-works" is the state that gets rounded up to "done" and then ships broken.*

## 61.2 ⭐⭐ THE EVIDENCE LADDER

| Rung | ⭐ Counts as proof? |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔ *"I wrote it"* | **no** |
| ⛔ *"the docblock says so"* | ⭐ **no — this is exactly what produced the 126** |
| ⛔ *"a unit test passes"* | ⭐ **no — a test double proves the double works** |
| ⚠️ *"an integration test passes"* | ⭐ **partial** |
| ⭐⭐ **"a real artifact exists"** | ⭐ **YES** — a database row, a delivered message, a recorded call, a rendered page, a pushed conversion |

⭐⭐ **Runtime proof or it isn't verified.** ⛔ *A module that has never produced a
real artifact has never run.*

## 61.3 ⭐ THE FOUR ASSURANCE ROLES *(§9)*

| | ⭐ Asks |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **QA-1 contract** | does it match its manifest? params, returns, permission, reversal class |
| ⭐⭐ **QA-2 wiring** | ⭐ **is it CALLED? is it ROUTED? does anything subscribe?** |
| **QA-3 behaviour** | does it do the right thing, including on failure? |
| ⭐⭐ **QA-4 runtime** | ⭐ **show me the artifact** |

⭐ **QA-2 is the one that would have caught all 126.** ⛔ *Everything else checks
whether code is correct; QA-2 checks whether it is reachable.*

## 61.4 ⭐ THE TWO-PASS RULE

⭐⭐ **Every sweep runs twice, and the second pass looks for what the first
missed** — ⛔ *not for the same things again.*

| Pass | ⭐ Asks |
| :--- | :--- |
| **1** | *"is each thing on the list correct?"* |
| ⭐⭐ **2** | ⭐ ***"what is NOT on the list that should be?"*** |

⛔ **Pass 2 is where absences are found**, and ⭐ **an absence never appears in
pass 1** *— because you can't check an item you never wrote down.*

## 61.5 ⭐ WHAT `goaiez-verify/` CONTAINS

```
  goaiez-verify/
    SKILL.md
    references/
      ⭐ 01-verify-slot.md      the 16th field, and how to fill it
      ⭐⭐ 02-evidence.md        the ladder — ⛔ what does NOT count
      03-roles.md              QA-1…QA-4
      ⭐ 04-sweeps.md           V2–V6, defined next
      05-verdicts.md           ⭐ MATCHES · PARTIAL · ABSENT · WRONG
  workflows/
    ⭐⭐ verify-module.md        ← the sequence a prover runs
```

⭐ **And it writes to `BUILD-STATE.json`** *(§53.3)* — ⛔ **`verified: true` is
never set by the agent that built the thing.**

## 61.6 ⭐⭐ THE FIVE SWEEPS — V2 TO V6

⭐ **Systemic, not per-module** — *because the 126 were each individually
plausible and collectively invisible.*

| Sweep | ⭐ Question |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **V2 · Entry points** | ⭐⭐ **every route, command, job, webhook and listener — does anything reach it?** |
| **V3 · Writers & readers** | every table: who writes, who reads, ⛔ **who does neither** |
| ⭐⭐ **V4 · Screens** | ⭐ **the ~179 — do they load, with real data, on a phone?** |
| ⭐ **V5 · Money paths** | ⛔ **every path that moves money or debits a meter** |
| ⭐⭐ **V6 · Cross-module promises** | ⭐ **every seam's invalidation rule — does it actually fire?** |

⭐ **V6 is the CC-86 class** *(§13.6)* — ⛔ *two correct modules and nobody wrote
the join.*

## 61.7 ACCEPTANCE — V1

☐ ⛔⛔ **"Assume nothing works" recorded as the standing position**
☐ ⭐ VERIFY slot defined; ⭐ **`PARTIAL` named as the dangerous verdict**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Evidence ladder — ⛔ docblocks and unit tests do NOT count**
☐ ⭐ Four QA roles; ⭐⭐ **QA-2 wiring identified as the one that catches the 126**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Two-pass rule — pass 2 hunts absences**
☐ ⛔ `verified: true` never set by the builder
☐ ⭐ Five sweeps defined for V2–V6
☐ ⭐ Delivered as `goaiez-verify/` *(law 81)*

**All eight ✅ — V1 EXECUTED.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §62 · V2 — THE ENTRY-POINT SWEEP  *(EXECUTED T525)*
⭐ **The sweep that would have caught the 126.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 62.0 ⭐⭐ THE QUESTION

> ⛔ **For every entry point: does anything actually reach it?**

⭐ **And its mirror, which is pass 2:** ⭐⭐ ***for everything that should be
reachable, is there an entry point at all?***

## 62.1 ⭐ THE NINE KINDS OF ENTRY POINT

| # | Kind | ⭐ Reached by |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1** | HTTP routes | a link, a form, a redirect |
| **2** | ⭐ **Registry actions** *(~2,900)* | ⭐ **API · MCP · assistant · canvas · Zapier · a screen** |
| **3** | ⭐⭐ **Event subscribers** *(~200 events)* | ⭐ **an emitter — and only an emitter** |
| **4** | Queue jobs | a dispatcher |
| **5** | Console commands | a schedule, a runbook, or a human |
| **6** | ⭐ **Scheduled tasks** | the scheduler — ⛔ *and is the scheduler running?* |
| **7** | Webhook receivers | ⭐ **a real provider callback** |
| **8** | Livewire components | ⭐ **a route or a parent** |
| **9** | ⭐ **Blade includes / partials** | a template that renders |

## 62.2 ⭐⭐ THE MECHANICAL CHECK

⭐ **This is a script, not a judgement:**

```
  for every entry point:
    ⭐ inbound = grep the codebase for anything that reaches it
    if inbound == 0:
       ├─ ⭐ declared `broadcast` with a written reason?  ──► OK (§13.8)
       ├─ ⭐ a public API surface by design?              ──► OK, must be documented
       └─ ⛔ otherwise ──► ⭐⭐ DEAD. Flag it.
```

⭐⭐ **Three outcomes for a dead entry point, and "leave it" isn't one:**

| ⭐ Verdict | Action |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **ORPHAN** | it should be called and isn't → ⭐⭐ **wire it** |
| **VESTIGIAL** | nothing needs it → ⛔ **delete it** |
| ⭐ **BROADCAST** | intentional, ⭐ **with the reason written down** |

⛔ **`ActivityRecorded` is the known legitimate broadcast** *(§13.8)* — ⭐ *it
feeds a UI stream, not a workflow. The exemption is cheap; the written reason is
the point.*

## 62.3 ⭐⭐ PASS 2 — THE ABSENCES

⭐ **Walk the plan, not the code.** For every promised capability, ⭐⭐ **name the
entry point that delivers it** — ⛔ *and if you can't, that's the finding.*

| ⭐ Source of promises | Count |
| :--- | ---: |
| Registry actions | ⭐ **~2,900 — each must be reachable from ≥1 of its declared surfaces** |
| Events | ⭐ ~200 — ⛔ **each must have an emitter AND a subscriber** |
| Seams | ⭐ **~150 — each must have a trigger that fires** |
| ⭐ **The ten screens** | ⭐⭐ **each must have a route and load with real data** |
| The 12 launch items *(§43.11)* | ⛔ **each must be demonstrable end to end** |

## 62.4 ⭐ THE HIGH-RISK LIST — WHERE ORPHANS HIDE

⭐ **Checked first, because these are where "built but unreachable" is most
likely and most expensive:**

| ⭐ Area | ⛔ Why it's risky |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Event subscribers** | ⭐ **the emitter is in a different module — nobody sees both** |
| ⭐ **Seam invalidations** | ⛔ *the CC-86 class: two correct modules, no join* |
| **Scheduled tasks** | ⭐ **registered but the scheduler never runs them** |
| ⭐ **Webhook receivers** | ⛔ *the provider was never pointed at it* |
| ⭐⭐ **Actions on `surfaces: [mcp]`** | ⭐ **never exercised by a human, so never noticed** |
| **Livewire components** | ⭐ **the 48 that had never been audited** |
| ⭐ **Degrade paths** | ⛔ *the fallback nobody has ever triggered* |

⭐⭐ **That last row deserves its own note:** ⭐ **every "degrade, never fail" path
(law 24w) is an entry point that only fires in failure** — ⛔ *so it must be
tested by forcing the failure, not by hoping.*

## 62.5 ⭐ THE OUTPUT

```
  ENTRY-POINT-SWEEP.json
    { "total": N, "reached": N, "orphan": [...],
      ⭐ "vestigial": [...], "broadcast": [...],
      ⭐⭐ "promised_but_absent": [...] }
```

⭐ **Written into `BUILD-STATE.json`** — ⛔ **a module with an orphaned entry
point cannot reach `VERIFIED`.**

## 62.6 ACCEPTANCE — V2

☐ ⭐ Nine kinds of entry point enumerated
☐ ⭐⭐ **Mechanical check — a script, not a judgement**
☐ ⭐ Three verdicts; ⛔ **"leave it" is not one of them**
☐ ⭐ `broadcast` allowed only ⭐ **with a written reason**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Pass 2 walks the PLAN and names the entry point for every promise**
☐ ⭐ High-risk list checked first
☐ ⭐⭐ **Degrade paths tested by forcing the failure**
☐ ⛔ An orphaned entry point blocks `VERIFIED`

**All eight ✅ — V2 EXECUTED.**
