# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §63 · V3 — THE WRITERS & READERS SWEEP  *(EXECUTED T526)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 63.0 ⭐ THE QUESTION

> ⛔ **For every table and every field: who writes it, who reads it — and who
> does neither?**

⭐ **V2 asked whether code is reachable. V3 asks whether DATA is.** ⭐⭐ *A field
nobody writes is a lie waiting to be believed; a field nobody reads is work
nobody needed.*

## 63.1 ⭐⭐ THE FOUR STATES

| State | ⭐ Meaning | Action |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **LIVE** | written and read | ✅ |
| ⛔ **WRITE-ONLY** | ⭐ **written, never read** | ⛔ *why are we storing it?* → justify or drop |
| ⭐⭐ **READ-ONLY** | ⭐⭐ **read, never written** | ⭐ **THE DANGEROUS ONE — see 63.2** |
| **ORPHAN** | neither | delete |

## 63.2 ⛔⛔ READ-ONLY IS THE ONE THAT SHIPS BROKEN

⭐ **A field that is read but never written returns its default, forever, and
nothing errors.**

| ⭐ What it looks like in production | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **`Asset.earns_calls`** reads 0 | ⛔ *"SEO isn't working"* — when nothing was ever incrementing it |
| ⭐ **`Person.channel_fit`** reads `unknown` | ⭐ the ladder silently defaults to email for everyone |
| ⭐⭐ **`Job.originating_asset_id`** null | ⛔ **attribution shows nothing and looks like a data problem** |
| **`share_permission`** false | photos never publish, and nobody knows why |

⛔⛔ **Every one of those is a silent product failure with a plausible innocent
explanation.** ⭐⭐ *That's what makes read-only worse than a crash.*

## 63.3 ⭐ THE HIGH-VALUE FIELDS — CHECKED FIRST

⭐ **The derived and denormalised ones, because they're the ones with a writer
that's easy to forget:**

| Field | ⭐ Must be written by |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ `Visit.call_token` | the DNI swap *(§49.1)* — ⛔ **without it, nothing downstream works** |
| ⭐ `Job.originating_*` *(five fields)* | the booking path *(§11.6)* |
| ⭐⭐ `Asset.earns_calls` | ⭐ **`job.completed`** — a denormalised count |
| `Asset.version` | every publish *(§25.1.1)* |
| ⭐ `Fact.source_version` | ⭐ **fact minting — or invalidation can't work** |
| `Person.state` / `state_reason` | ⭐ **only their own act** *(§11.2)* |
| ⭐ `PersonIdentity.confidence` | every waterfall write |
| `ActionInvocation.before/after` | ⭐ **the executor — or undo and EXPLAIN both fail** |
| ⭐ `outcome_observed` | ⭐⭐ **the outcome event — or "did it work?" is unanswerable** |

⭐⭐ **`ActionInvocation.before/after` deserves the loudest flag:** ⛔ *if the
executor doesn't populate it, undo silently does nothing and EXPLAIN silently
says less — and both look like they're working.*

## 63.4 ⭐ THE TENANCY CHECK — RUNS IN THE SAME PASS

⭐ **Every table gets both walls confirmed** *(§11.10)*:

☐ `business_id` present · ☐ **RLS `FORCE`d** · ☐ application global scope
☐ ⭐ **`idOrFail` semantics** — ⛔ *a query that can't resolve a tenant FAILS rather than returning everything*
☐ ⭐⭐ **RLS-exempt tables carry a written argument in the migration** *(19 today, every one argued)*

⛔ **A table with one wall and not the other is the finding** — ⭐ *because they
drift apart exactly when they're added independently.*

## 63.5 ⭐ PASS 2 — WHAT ISN'T STORED THAT SHOULD BE

⭐ **Walk the promises, not the schema:**

| ⭐ Promise | ⛔ Needs a field that exists |
| :--- | :--- |
| *"where did this phone number come from?"* | ⭐ `PersonIdentity.source` + `observed_at` |
| ⭐ *"why am I posting more photos?"* | ⭐⭐ the allocation shift, as an `ActionInvocation` |
| *"which ones went?"* *(review loss)* | ⭐ **review text + date, held locally** |
| ⭐ *"they opened it twice and didn't pay"* | invoice view events |
| *"three customers mentioned scheduling"* | ⭐ **QA free text, per response** |
| ⭐ *"that was the cold snap, not the post"* | ⭐⭐ **fleet counters by region and week** |

⛔ **Each of these is a sentence the product promises. ⭐ If the field isn't
there, the sentence is a lie.**

## 63.6 ⭐ OUTPUT

```
  DATA-SWEEP.json
    { ⭐ "read_only": [...],   ⭐ ← fix first
      "write_only": [...], "orphan": [...],
      ⭐⭐ "tenancy_gaps": [...], "promised_but_unstored": [...] }
```

⛔ **Any `read_only` on the §63.3 list blocks launch.**

## 63.7 ACCEPTANCE — V3

☐ ⭐ Four states defined for every table and field
☐ ⭐⭐ **READ-ONLY named as the dangerous one** — ⛔ *silent failure with an innocent explanation*
☐ ⭐ Nine high-value derived fields listed with their required writer
☐ ⭐⭐ **`ActionInvocation.before/after` flagged** — undo and EXPLAIN both depend on it
☐ ⭐ Tenancy double-wall checked in the same pass; ⭐ **`idOrFail` confirmed**
☐ ⛔ RLS exemptions carry a written argument
☐ ⭐⭐ **Pass 2 walks the promises** — *if the field isn't there, the sentence is a lie*
☐ ⛔ A read-only high-value field blocks launch

**All eight ✅ — V3 EXECUTED.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §64 · V4 — THE SCREEN SWEEP  *(EXECUTED T527)*
⭐ **~179 screens. 48 of them have never been audited once.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 64.0 ⭐ THE QUESTION

> ⛔ **Does it load, with real data, on a phone, in every state?**

⭐ **Not "does the component exist."** ⭐⭐ *A screen that renders on a developer's
laptop with seeded data has proved almost nothing.*

## 64.1 ⭐⭐ THE SIX CHECKS PER SCREEN

| # | Check | ⛔ Fails when |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **1** | **Loads** | reachable from a route or parent *(V2)* |
| ⭐⭐ **2** | ⭐ **Real data** | ⛔ *seeded demo data hides null-handling that production finds in an hour* |
| ⭐⭐ **3** | ⭐⭐ **On a phone** | ⛔ **the primary target** — *not a responsive afterthought* |
| ⭐ **4** | **Five states** | default · loading · ⭐ **empty** · error · ⭐ **`SAMPLE`** |
| ⭐ **5** | **Every row acts** | ⛔ *a row you can only look at is a report* |
| ⭐ **6** | ⭐ **Every number traceable** | tap → what it's made of |

⭐⭐ **Check 4's empty state is the one that gets skipped** — ⭐ *and it's the
first state every new tenant sees.*

## 64.2 ⭐⭐ THE THREE HARDEST STATES TO TEST

⭐ **They need to be forced, because they never occur naturally in development:**

| State | ⭐ How to force it |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Day one — everything empty** | ⭐ **a brand-new tenant, zero rows.** ⛔ *Every screen must say what to do, not show a spinner over nothing* |
| ⭐ **`SAMPLE` everywhere** | seeded profile, nothing confirmed — ⛔ **does the agent visibly refuse to quote?** *(§50.6)* |
| ⭐⭐ **Degraded** | ⭐ **provider down, meter empty, card failed, paused account** — *the screens nobody designs* |

⭐⭐ **The paused-account screens are a specific gap:** ⭐ *what does the marketing
tab look like at day 21 when it's paused but the phone still answers?* ⛔ **If
nobody designed it, it's a blank page at the worst possible moment.**

## 64.3 ⭐ THE 48 — SPECIAL HANDLING

⭐ **The Livewire components that have never been audited get the full treatment,
not a spot check:**

☐ ⭐ **Does anything route to it?** *(V2 orphan check)*
☐ ⭐⭐ **Does its data source still exist?** — ⛔ *the entity graph changed under it*
☐ **Does it obey the 12 nouns**, or does it read a table that no longer exists?
☐ ⭐ **Is it superseded** by something built later? → ⛔ **delete, don't fix**

⭐⭐ **Expect deletions.** ⛔ *A screen built against the old prospects/customers
split (§11.2) or the old commerce model (§25.0) should not be repaired — it
should be removed.*

## 64.4 ⭐ THE TEN GET MORE

⭐ **The ten that decide it** *(§58.3)* also get:

| ⭐ Extra check | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Timed** | ⛔ **decline-at-the-door must resolve in 15 seconds** *(§46A.0)* |
| ⭐ **In sunlight** | contrast tested at real brightness, not a simulator |
| ⭐ **One-handed** | ⭐⭐ *a tech is holding something in the other hand* |
| **Gloved** | touch targets at 44px minimum, actually tapped |
| ⭐ **Read aloud** | ⭐ *the copy tested by speaking it — if it sounds like software, rewrite it* |

## 64.5 ⭐ PASS 2 — THE SCREENS THAT SHOULD EXIST

⭐ **Walk the 12 launch items** *(§43.11)* **and the ten** — ⛔ **name the screen
for each.** ⭐⭐ *A launch item with no screen is a launch item nobody can use.*

⭐ **Known candidates for "promised, never designed":** the pool-number migration
notice · ⭐ **the wind-down warnings at days 25/45/53/58** · the supply meter's
downgrade path · ⭐ **the grounding-gap prompt** · the QA ticket resolution
screen.

## 64.6 ACCEPTANCE — V4

☐ ⭐ Six checks per screen; ⭐⭐ **real data, not seeded**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Phone is the pass condition, not a bonus**
☐ ⭐ Five states incl. ⭐ **empty — the first thing a new tenant sees**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Three forced states: day one · all-SAMPLE · degraded**
☐ ⭐ Paused-account screens designed, ⛔ **not left blank**
☐ ⭐⭐ **The 48 get the full treatment; ⛔ superseded ones are deleted, not fixed**
☐ ⭐ The ten timed, sunlit, one-handed, gloved, ⭐ **and read aloud**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Pass 2 names the screen for every launch item**

**All eight ✅ — V4 EXECUTED.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §65 · V5 — THE MONEY-PATH SWEEP  *(EXECUTED T528)*
⭐ **The only sweep where a bug costs cash on the day it ships.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 65.0 ⭐ THE QUESTION

> ⛔ **Every path that moves money or debits a meter — is it correct, is it
> logged, and can it be explained to the person it charged?**

⭐⭐ **Three failure modes, and the third is the one that kills trust:** ⭐ *charge
too much · charge too little · ⛔ **charge correctly and be unable to explain
it***.

## 65.1 ⭐ THE PATHS

| ⭐ Category | Paths |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Meters** | SMS · voice · email · ⭐ **AI at 8:1** · lead credits |
| **Top-ups** | 4 ladders + ⭐ **auto top-up on every one** |
| ⭐ **Tenant's money** | card at the door · payment links · invoices · deposits · progress payments · memberships · refunds |
| **Our money** | subscription · agency $497 · ⭐ **affiliate 40% of subscription only** |
| ⭐⭐ **Dunning** | ⭐ **soft vs hard · retry ladder · the 21-day timeline · pause · day 30 · day 60** |
| **Sync** | Stripe · Authorize.net · accounting *(one direction)* |

## 65.2 ⛔⛔ THE ARITHMETIC CHECKS

⭐ **Mechanical, and each one has a known way to go wrong:**

| ⭐ Check | ⛔ The failure it catches |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Integer minor units everywhere** | ⛔ **a single float anywhere** *(§11.11)* — grep for it |
| ⭐ **Currency on every amount** | a bare number crossing a border |
| ⭐⭐ **8:1 is DERIVED from `ai_calls`** | ⛔ **never typed** — *if it's typed, it drifts* |
| ⭐ **Voice 25% / usage 40% agency discounts** | ⛔ *applied once, not twice* |
| ⭐⭐ **Every debit has a `LedgerEntry`** | ⛔ **a charge with no row is unexplainable** |
| ⭐ **Rounding stated and consistent** | ⛔ *half-cent drift across a million debits* |
| ⭐⭐ **Refunds reverse the meter too** | ⭐ **not just the money** |
| ⭐ **Auto top-up fires before zero** | ⛔ *not at zero — a text-back must never fail* |

## 65.3 ⭐⭐ THE EXPLAINABILITY TEST

⭐ **For every charge, the tenant can ask "why?" and get a true answer** *(§14.3)*:

> ⭐⭐ *"That campaign cost $4.20 — **$3.10 of AI for 62 messages drafted, $1.10
> for the 22 that sent.** The other 40 were suppressed."*

⛔ **If EXPLAIN can't produce that sentence, the charge fails the sweep** — ⭐
*even if the arithmetic is perfect.*

## 65.4 ⭐ THE DOUBLE-CHARGE HUNT

⭐ **Every place a retry, a webhook or an idempotency gap could bill twice:**

☐ ⭐⭐ **Every non-read action idempotent** *(§12.6)* — ⛔ *agents retry*
☐ ⭐ **Webhook receivers idempotent by provider event id** — ⛔ *Stripe re-sends*
☐ **Queue jobs safe to re-run** after a partial failure
☐ ⭐⭐ **Failover doesn't double-bill** — ⛔ *provider A timed out but did the work*
☐ ⭐ **A resumed dunning ladder doesn't restart the charges**

⭐⭐ **That fourth one is the sneaky one:** ⭐ *a provider that times out at our end
may have succeeded at theirs — so the meter debit must key on the provider's id,
not on our attempt.*

## 65.5 ⭐ THE MONEY SCREENS — PROVEN WITH REAL NUMBERS

☐ ⭐ *Paid today* matches the ledger · ☐ *Unpaid* matches open jobs
☐ ⭐⭐ **Credit statement reconciles to the cent**
☐ ⭐ **The four meters' remaining balances are right after a mixed day**
☐ ⭐⭐ **A tenant's invoice to their customer and our invoice to them are visibly different things** — ⛔ *one implementation, two customers, and confusing them would be catastrophic*

## 65.6 ⭐ PASS 2 — MONEY THAT MOVES AND ISN'T TRACKED

| ⭐ Candidate | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **A blocked scrape** | ⛔ **must debit nothing** *(§18B.1)* — is that true in code? |
| ⭐⭐ **A failed send** | ⭐ **does it refund the meter?** |
| **A retried AI call** | ⛔ *one debit or two?* |
| ⭐ **A degraded voice tier** | ⭐ **is the cheaper cost actually recorded?** |
| ⭐⭐ **A paused account** | ⛔ **does the still-running phone path bill anyone?** |

⭐⭐ **That last one needs an explicit answer:** ⭐ **during pause we absorb the
text-back cost** *(§45A.3)* — ⛔ **so it must be recorded as our cost, not
silently untracked.**

## 65.7 ACCEPTANCE — V5

☐ ⭐ All six path categories swept
☐ ⭐⭐ **Integer minor units, currency everywhere, ⛔ no floats**
☐ ⭐⭐ **8:1 derived from `ai_calls`, never typed**
☐ ⭐ Every debit has a `LedgerEntry`; ⭐ **refunds reverse the meter too**
☐ ⭐⭐ **EXPLAIN produces a true "why" for every charge** — ⛔ *or it fails*
☐ ⭐ Double-charge hunt incl. ⭐⭐ **failover keyed on the provider's id**
☐ ⭐ Money screens reconcile to the cent
☐ ⭐⭐ **Pause-period costs recorded as ours, not untracked**

**All eight ✅ — V5 EXECUTED.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §66 · V6 — CROSS-MODULE PROMISES  *(EXECUTED T529 — PHASE 5 COMPLETE)*
⭐ **The CC-86 class: two correct modules and nobody wrote the join.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 66.0 ⭐⭐ THE QUESTION

> ⛔ **For every seam: does the invalidation rule actually fire?**

⭐ **Not "is it declared."** ⭐⭐ *A seam record with all four fields and no
mechanism behind it is documentation, not a join.*

## 66.1 ⭐ THE TEST — FORCE THE CHANGE, WATCH THE FAR SIDE

⭐ **Mechanical, per seam:**

```
  ① change the SOURCE
  ② ⭐ read the CONSUMER — ⛔ immediately, not after a queue
  ③ ⭐⭐ did it change too?   ── no ──► THE SEAM IS BROKEN
```

⛔ **And the harder half:** ⭐⭐ **change the source, then read the consumer at
+0ms, +100ms and +5s** — ⭐ *because a seam that eventually catches up is not the
same as one that was never wrong* **(§13.4: invalidation is inline, notification
is async).**

## 66.2 ⭐⭐ THE SEAMS THAT MUST NEVER LAG

| Seam | ⛔ The failure if it lags |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **price → agent** | ⭐ **the agent quotes last month's price on a live call** |
| ⭐ **asset publish → Fact** | the AI cites a page that changed |
| ⭐ **pricebook → estimate** | a signed estimate at the wrong price |
| ⭐⭐ **suppression → sending** | ⛔ **a message to someone who said stop** |
| ⭐ **register disabled → consulted** | ⭐ **off must mean off, immediately** *(§17.5)* |
| ⭐⭐ **availability → the agent's offer** | ⭐ **a window promised that can't be kept** *(§29.3)* |

⭐⭐ **These six are tested at +0ms.** ⛔ *Anything else is a defect, not a delay.*

## 66.3 ⭐ THE SEAMS THAT MAY LAG — BUT MUST ARRIVE

⭐ **Everything on the event bus. The test is different: ⭐⭐ does it arrive, and
does it arrive ONCE?**

☐ ⭐ **Arrives** — the subscriber ran
☐ ⭐⭐ **Once** — ⛔ *at-least-once delivery means the consumer must be idempotent, so re-deliver it deliberately and check*
☐ ⭐ **In order per entity** — ⛔ *`job.completed` cannot land before `job.booked`*
☐ **Dead-letters on failure** — ⭐ **and appears on the one pager surface**

## 66.4 ⭐⭐ THE FAN-OUTS — TESTED AS A WHOLE

⭐ **`job.completed` has eight subscribers** *(§30A.4)*. ⛔ **Testing them
individually proves nothing about the fan-out.**

```
  ⭐ complete one real job ──► ⭐⭐ ALL EIGHT must be observable:
     invoice · review invite · CRM advance · SEO proof ·
     attribution close · commission · inventory · timesheet
```

⭐⭐ **And the honest check: if one subscriber throws, do the other seven still
run?** ⛔ *A fan-out where one failure silently kills the rest is the worst
possible shape.*

## 66.5 ⭐ PASS 2 — PROMISES WITH NO SEAM AT ALL

⭐ **Walk the product's claims and find the join that delivers each:**

| ⭐ The product claims | ⛔ Needs a seam that exists |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ *"the agent can't quote a stale price"* | price → Fact, ⭐ **inline** |
| *"a reply stops the ladder"* | ⭐ any channel → ladder state |
| ⭐ *"your form broke, here are the 9 leads"* | ⭐⭐ handler-check → alert → inbox |
| *"reviews dropped from 47 to 41"* | daily count → comparison → alert |
| ⭐ *"we shifted your posts to before/after"* | ⭐⭐ loop → allocation → schedule → EXPLAIN |
| *"this page earned $7,340"* | ⭐ five attribution fields → the query |
| ⭐ *"paused, and your phone still answers"* | ⭐⭐ pause state → **which paths stop and which don't** |

⛔ **Every row is a sentence we say to a customer.** ⭐⭐ *If the seam isn't there,
we're lying — politely, and at scale.*

## 66.6 ⭐ PHASE 5 CLOSED

| Sweep | ⭐ Caught |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **V1** | the method — ⭐⭐ **runtime proof or nothing** |
| ⭐⭐ **V2** | ⭐ **unreachable code** — the 126 |
| ⭐ **V3** | ⭐⭐ **unreachable data** — read-only fields |
| **V4** | screens that don't survive real data, a phone, or day one |
| ⭐ **V5** | money that's wrong, double-billed, or ⭐ **unexplainable** |
| ⭐⭐ **V6** | ⭐ **joins that were never written** |

⭐⭐ **Six sweeps, two passes each, and pass 2 always hunts absences** — ⛔ *because
every one of these failures is invisible to the pass that only checks what's on
the list.*

## 66.7 ACCEPTANCE — V6

☐ ⭐ Every seam tested by ⭐⭐ **forcing the source change and reading the consumer**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Six seams tested at +0ms** — ⛔ *lag is a defect there, not a delay*
☐ ⭐ Bus seams tested for **arrival · once · order · dead-letter**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Re-delivered deliberately to prove idempotency**
☐ ⭐ Fan-outs tested whole; ⭐⭐ **one failure must not kill the other seven**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Pass 2 names the seam behind every customer-facing claim**
☐ ⛔ A missing seam behind a claim blocks launch

**All seven ✅ — V6 EXECUTED. PHASE 5 COMPLETE.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §67 · T1 — TENANT ZERO  *(EXECUTED T530)*
⭐ **GO AI EZ runs on GOAIEZ. Not a demo — the actual business.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 67.0 ⭐⭐ WHY IT EXISTS

⛔ **There is no soft launch** *(§5A)*, so **the first person to use 247 modules
in anger would be a paying customer.**

⭐⭐ **Internal-live fixes that without reintroducing phases** *(§17.3 O12)*: we
become tenant #0 the moment the spine, channels and agent are built. ⛔ **No
customers, no announcement, no tiers.** ⭐ **The public launch is still one
event.**

## 67.1 ⭐ WHAT WE ACTUALLY RUN

| ⭐ Module | ⭐⭐ Our real use |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **The agent** | ⭐ **answers our own inbound — sales questions, support, pricing** |
| ⭐ **Missed-call text-back** | our own number |
| ⭐ **The pixel** | ⭐⭐ **on goaiez.com, first-party** *(§60.4)* |
| ⭐ **DNI** | ⭐ **so we know which page earned a signup** |
| ⭐⭐ **The outreach ladder** | ⭐ **this is how we sell** — form → email → voice → voicemail |
| ⭐⭐ **The audit video** | ⭐ **our entire top of funnel** *(§27)* |
| ⭐ **The demo assistant** | ⭐⭐ **every prospect gets one, grounded in their own crawl** |
| ⭐ **Reviews + QA** | ⭐ **our own customers, our own triage** |
| **Content studio + campaigns** | our own marketing |
| ⭐ **CRM, jobs, invoicing** | ⭐ **our own money** |
| ⭐⭐ **The growth loop** | ⭐ **optimising our own acquisition** |

⭐⭐ **The acquisition machine and the product are the same code** *(§27.3)* — ⛔
*so every hour spent on our marketing is an hour spent on the product.*

## 67.2 ⭐⭐ WHAT THIS CATCHES THAT NO SWEEP CAN

⭐ **V1–V6 prove the system is correct. Tenant Zero proves it's usable.**

| ⭐ Only found by living in it | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **The onboarding that takes 40 minutes instead of 5** | ⛔ *no test measures tedium* |
| ⭐ **The alert that fires at the wrong moment** | correct, and still annoying |
| ⭐⭐ **The screen you open ten times a day** | ⛔ *and the one you never open* |
| ⭐ **The copy that reads fine and sounds wrong aloud** | |
| ⭐⭐ **The report nobody actually looks at** | ⭐ **cut it** |
| ⭐ **The thing you keep doing manually** | ⛔ **because the automation is almost right** |

⭐⭐ **That last row is the most valuable signal in the whole phase:** ⭐ *a
workaround you invent for your own product is a defect the product doesn't know
it has.*

## 67.3 ⭐ THE HONEST LIMITS

⚠️ **Tenant Zero is one business, in one vertical, with unusual users.**

| ⛔ We will NOT discover | ⭐ Because |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **What a plumber finds confusing** | ⛔ **we built it** |
| **Whether the trade prices are right** | we're not a trade |
| ⭐⭐ **Mobile-in-a-van reality** | ⛔ *we're at desks* |
| **Multi-location and crew problems** | we have neither |

⭐⭐ **So Tenant Zero is necessary and not sufficient.** ⭐ **T2 adds the friendly
tenants who ARE trades** — ⛔ *and their feedback outranks ours on everything
above.*

## 67.4 ⭐ THE RULES

☐ ⭐⭐ **We use it exactly as a customer would** — ⛔ **no admin shortcuts, no
direct database edits, no "I'll just fix it in Tinker"**
☐ ⭐ **Every workaround we invent is logged as a defect**
☐ ⭐⭐ **We pay our own meters** — ⭐ *at cost, but recorded, so the numbers are real*
☐ ⭐ **We are subject to our own dunning** *(§45A)* — ⛔ *including the day-7 call*
☐ ⭐⭐ **A feature not good enough for us doesn't ship** *(§60.4)*

⛔ **The first rule is the one that will be broken.** ⭐⭐ *The moment someone fixes
a tenant-zero problem with a database edit instead of a bug report, the phase has
stopped working.*

## 67.5 ACCEPTANCE — T1

☐ ⭐ Tenant Zero live on spine + channels + agent, ⛔ **no customers, no announcement**
☐ ⭐⭐ **We run the outreach ladder and the audit video as our real top of funnel**
☐ ⭐ Our own site carries our pixel, agent, DNI and published vitals
☐ ⭐⭐ **No admin shortcuts — we use it as a customer**
☐ ⭐ Every workaround logged as a defect
☐ ⭐⭐ **We pay our own meters and face our own dunning**
☐ ⚠️ ⭐ **The four things Tenant Zero cannot discover, stated** — ⭐⭐ **T2 covers them**

**All seven ✅ — T1 EXECUTED.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §68 · ⭐⭐ A1 — THE ACQUISITION MACHINE · DISCOVERY & INSPECTION  *(T531)*
⭐ **Three turns. This is turn one of three. 45 → 48 turns.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

> **⛔ FIRST-PASS SHAPE — PRECEDENCE (T667, §0.A):** A1 acquisition machine; current §128–§130 (M6–M8); owner content stays LIVE as detail. *Nothing here is deleted (law 10); read §0.A before treating this section as current.*

## 68.0 ⭐ WHY THREE TURNS

⛔ **The machine already exists — scattered across eight sections.** ⭐ *§18C the
ladder · §27 the video · §28.5 the demo assistant · §31–32 the audit · §39 the
content · §49 attribution.* ⭐⭐ **Nobody could build it from that. These three
turns make it one product.**

| Turn | ⭐ Covers |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **A1** | ⭐⭐ **discovery + inspection** — *finding them, and finding what's wrong* |
| **A2** | the artifacts — report · demo site · chatbot · video |
| **A3** | delivery · autopilot · conversion · measurement |

---

## 68.1 ⭐ DISCOVERY — THE SUPER-SCRAPER

⭐ **Ten methods, cheapest first** *(X-151, §18A.2)*. ⭐⭐ **For acquisition
specifically:**

| ⭐ Source | Gives |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Open data first** | ⭐⭐ **licence boards · permit databases · Secretary of State · chambers** — *free, no gate, and it's where trades legally must appear* |
| **Maps by geo + category** | the core sweep *(X-16)* |
| ⭐ **Directories** | Yelp · Angi · Thumbtack · BBB · trade bodies |
| ⭐⭐ **Social** | ⭐ **HVAC, plumbing and roofing firms almost all keep a Facebook page even with no website** |
| **Ad libraries** | ⭐ **who's already spending — they have budget** *(§52.3)* |
| ⭐ **Review platforms** | ⭐⭐ **who has reviews and isn't answering them** |
| **Job boards** | ⭐ **hiring = growing = budget** |

⭐⭐ **The signal that beats all of them: a business with reviews and no website.**
⛔ *They have demand and no way to capture it, and they know it.*

## 68.2 ⭐⭐ THE INSPECTION — EVERYTHING WRONG, FOUND

⭐ **Five layers. Every finding is measured, dated and reproducible** *(§27.2.1)*.

### ⭐ LAYER 1 · THE WEBSITE *(22 checks)*

⭐ **Speed** — LCP · INP · CLS · TTFB, from a real load on a real phone profile ·
⭐⭐ **mobile usability** — *does the booking form fit a phone?* · SSL and mixed
content · ⭐ **broken links and 404s** · ⭐⭐ **the contact form — we test it** *(see
68.4)* · ⭐ **phone number visible above the fold?** · ⭐⭐ **is it click-to-call?**
· NAP present and consistent · ⭐ **schema markup** · titles and metas · thin
pages · ⭐ **no FAQ** · ⭐⭐ **JS-dependent content** *(fetch with scripts off)* ·
⭐ **AI crawler access** *(X-176)* · ⭐ **stale copyright year** · ⭐⭐ **stock
photos only — no real work shown** · ⭐ **no prices anywhere** · no booking · ⭐
**no reviews displayed** · broken images · ⭐ **not indexed**.

### ⭐ LAYER 2 · GOOGLE BUSINESS PROFILE *(14 checks)*

⭐ **Claimed?** · category correct vs the town's top rankers · ⭐ **hours + special
hours** · ⭐⭐ **photo count and age** — *"your newest photo is 14 months old"* ·
⭐ **last post date** · ⭐⭐ **unanswered reviews and how long** · unanswered Q&A ·
services listed · booking link · ⭐ **rating vs the three nearest competitors** ·
⭐⭐ **review velocity — rising or falling** · ⭐ **suspension risk signals**
*(X-177)*.

### ⭐ LAYER 3 · VISIBILITY *(10 checks)*

⭐⭐ **Map-pack position for their core terms** · ⭐ **geo-grid gaps — where they
vanish** · who outranks them and why · ⭐⭐ **AI answer visibility across six
engines** *(X-144)* · organic positions · citations and NAP consistency · ⭐
**pages that used to rank**.

### ⭐ LAYER 4 · REPUTATION *(8 checks)*

Review count and rating vs competitors · ⭐⭐ **response rate and median response
time** · ⭐ **oldest unanswered negative** · platform spread · ⭐⭐ **review
recency — a top-5 local factor** *(§32.3)* · ⭐ **language customers use about
them** *(mined, and reusable as their copy)*.

### ⭐⭐ LAYER 5 · THE EXPERIENTIAL TESTS — *the ones that convert*

⭐ **Everything above is analysis. These are experience, and they're the findings
that land:**

| ⭐ Test | ⭐⭐ The finding |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Submit their contact form** | ⭐ ***"we filled in your form on Tuesday. Nobody replied."*** |
| ⭐⭐ **Call after hours** | ⭐ ***"we rang at 7:40pm. It rang out."*** |
| ⭐ **Text the number** | *"no reply — is texting on?"* |
| ⭐ **Time a business-hours response** | *"we asked a question at 10am. First reply: 2 days."* |

⭐⭐ **These are worth more than every metric combined**, because ⛔ *a load-time
number is an argument, and "nobody answered your phone" is an experience the owner
already suspects.*

### ⛔ THE RULES ON EXPERIENTIAL TESTS

☐ ⭐⭐ **One test each. Never repeated, never at volume**
☐ ⭐ **A real question a customer would ask** — ⛔ *never a fake emergency*
☐ ⭐⭐ **If a human answers, we say who we are immediately** and let them go
☐ ⭐ **Never a booking we don't intend to keep** — ⛔ *that wastes a slot*
☐ ⭐⭐ **Business hours for the response test; after-hours only for the ring test**
☐ ⭐ **The transcript is shown to them** — ⛔ *we quote nothing we can't produce*

⭐⭐ **The discipline is the point:** ⭐ *we're demonstrating what their customers
experience, not pranking them — and one polite test proves it as well as fifty.*

## 68.3 ⭐ THE SCORE

⭐ **Not a vanity number. Two figures a business owner acts on:**

| ⭐ Figure | ⭐⭐ Example |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **What it's costing** | ⭐ *"roughly 6–9 calls a month you're not getting"* — **from their traffic, their rank gaps and their answer rate** |
| ⭐ **The three fixes that matter** | ranked by ⭐⭐ **impact ÷ effort**, ⛔ *never a list of 40* |

⚠️ **Stated honestly:** ⭐ **the call estimate is modelled, and the model is
shown.** ⛔ *A made-up number in the first sentence poisons everything after it.*

## 68.4 ⭐⭐ THE FORM TEST IS THE KILLER

⭐ **We submit a real enquiry. Then:**

```
  ⭐ did their handler fire?     ── no ──► ⭐⭐ "your form is broken"
  ⭐ did anyone reply?           ── no ──► ⭐ "nobody replied in 6 days"
  ⭐⭐ how long did it take?      ──────► "4 days. Your competitor: 20 minutes."
```

⭐⭐ **And after they sign up, X-155 catches every submission independently**
*(§22.4.1)* — ⛔ *so the pitch and the product are the same mechanism.*

## 68.5 ACCEPTANCE — A1

☐ ⭐ Discovery across 7 source types, ⭐⭐ **open data first**
☐ ⭐ **"Reviews but no website" flagged as the strongest signal**
☐ ⭐⭐ **54 checks across 5 layers**, every finding measured and dated
☐ ⭐⭐ **Layer 5 experiential tests — form, call, text, response time**
☐ ⛔ **One test each · a real question · identify if answered · never a wasted booking**
☐ ⭐ Score is **cost in calls + three ranked fixes**, ⛔ **not a list of 40**
☐ ⚠️ ⭐ **The estimate is modelled and the model is shown**

**All seven ✅ — A1 EXECUTED.**

# §69 · ⭐⭐ A2 — THE ARTIFACTS  *(RESTORED T559 — lost in a failed write at T532)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 69.0 ⭐⭐ THE PACKAGE — FIVE THINGS, ONE LINK

```
  ⭐ demo.goaiez.com/summit-plumbing
       ├─ ⭐⭐ THEIR SITE, REBUILT   ← live, fast, SEO'd, claimable
       ├─ ⭐⭐ A LIVE CHAT AI        ← grounded in THEIR data (§28.5)
       ├─ ⭐⭐ A REAL PHONE NUMBER   ← they can text it. It answers as them
       ├─ ⭐ THE AUDIT              ← their numbers, dated (§68)
       └─ ⭐⭐ THE VIDEO             ← their real site, then the new one
```

⛔ *Nothing to imagine, nothing to install, nothing to sign.*

## 69.1 ⭐⭐ TWO BUILD PATHS, BOTH ABOUT A MINUTE

**PATH A — they have a site:** crawl *(X-129)* → score all 200 templates
*(X-179)* → populate with **their words, verbatim** → publish to a demo
subdomain. ⭐ **The template is better; the words are theirs.**

### ⭐⭐ PATH B — NO SITE: BUILD FROM GBP + FACEBOOK

⛔ **This is the unlock**, because ⭐ **the best prospects are the ones with
reviews and no website** *(§68.1)* — and *"we rebuilt your site"* means nothing
to them.

| ⭐ Source | Gives |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Google Business Profile** | name · category · services · hours · area · photos · reviews · Q&A |
| ⭐ **Facebook page** | about · services · photos · ⭐ **their own voice** |
| ⭐ **The industry profile** | ⭐⭐ **the FAQ and price scaffolding they've never written down** |
| **Reviews** | ⭐ **what customers say they're good at — as headline copy** |

⭐⭐ **A plumber with 47 reviews and no website gets a real site in a minute, built
from things he already wrote** — ⛔ *and he's never seen his business presented
properly before.*

⭐ **The full-stack site law applies to the demo** *(§26.2)*: pixel · chat AI ·
⭐ **a demo number** · SEO · schema · form capture · DNI · SSL.

## 69.2 ⭐⭐ THE DEMO NUMBER POOL

⛔ **A demo they can only look at is a screenshot.** ⭐⭐ **A demo they can TEXT is
a product.**

| ⭐ Mechanic | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ Each demo gets a pool number *(X-188)* | ⭐⭐ **it answers AS THEIR BUSINESS** |
| ⭐⭐ **Alphanumeric code per demo** | ⭐ **an inbound text resolves to the exact demo** across hundreds live |
| ⭐⭐ **They miss it → the text-back fires** | ⭐ *they experience their own missed-call recovery* |
| ⛔ **It never announces itself as a demo** | it's their business, answering |
| ⛔ **Bookings are demo-mode** | nothing real is scheduled, and the confirmation says so |
| ⭐ **Text-only until voice ships** *(§70.0)* | ⭐⭐ **call → forwards or voicemail** |
| ⭐⭐ **They texted it** | ⭐ **the hottest signal we will ever get** |

## 69.3 ⭐⭐ THE VIDEO — THEIR SITE, THEN THE NEW ONE

⭐ **Ninety seconds, two halves** *(X-159)*:

> ⭐ **HALF 1 — their real site, scrolling:** *"Here's your site on a phone. 6.2
> seconds. Your number isn't clickable. ⭐ **We filled in your form on Tuesday —
> nobody replied.** You've got 47 reviews and haven't answered one since March."*
>
> ⭐⭐ **HALF 2 — the new one:** *"Same words. 1.4 seconds. Number taps to call.
> And this answers your phone —" [plays the agent] "**Text it yourself:
> 555-0142.**"*

⛔ **Every claim measured and dated on screen** *(§27.2.1)* · captions burned in ·
⭐ **the number spoken aloud** · hosted on the demo page so ⭐ **watch depth
advances the ladder.**

## 69.4 ⭐ THE THREE ADOPTION PATHS

| ⭐ Path | Gets | ⭐ Preference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **1 · Our hosted platform** | everything | ⭐⭐ **best** |
| **2 · Their site + the plugin** *(X-104)* | agent, pixel, forms, reviews, SEO | good |
| ⭐ **3 · Widget only** | ⭐ **chat + pixel, one line of JS** | ⭐⭐ **the wedge** |

⭐⭐ **Path 3 is the wedge, not a consolation** — ⛔ *a tenant on the widget still
gets missed-call text-back and COOLING, and then path 1 sells itself.*

## 69.5 ⭐⭐ THE CLAIM

```
  ⭐ "This is mine" ──► signup ──► ⭐⭐ THE DEMO TENANT BECOMES THEIR TENANT
       Facts stay · site stays · SAMPLE badges come off as they confirm ·
       ⭐ the demo number swaps for theirs
```

⛔ **Nothing rebuilds. Nothing migrates.** ⭐ **And their conversations with the
demo agent come with them** — ⭐⭐ *the questions they asked while evaluating are
the first entries in their own inbox.*

## 69.6 ACCEPTANCE — A2

☐ ⭐ Path A crawl-and-rebuild, ⭐ **their words verbatim**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Path B from GBP + Facebook + industry profile** — ⛔ **for prospects with no site**
☐ ⭐ Full-stack site law applies to the demo

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §70 · ⭐⭐ A3 — DELIVERY, AUTOPILOT & CONVERSION  *(RESTORED T559)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

> **⛔ FIRST-PASS SHAPE — PRECEDENCE (T667, §0.A):** A3 restored T559, out of order; current §130. *Nothing here is deleted (law 10); read §0.A before treating this section as current.*

## 70.0 ⛔ TEXT FIRST, VOICE WHEN IT EXISTS

⭐ **The demo number is SMS-only until the voice agent is built.** ⭐⭐ **Not a
compromise — the text-back IS the headline feature.** ⛔ *A prospect who texts a
demo number and gets a correct instant reply about their own business has seen
the thing that matters.*

⭐ **The video says *"text it right now"*** — ⛔ **never "call it" until calling
works.**

## 70.1 ⭐⭐ THE LADDER AND THE CHANNEL SWITCH

```
  ⭐ COLD                                  ⭐⭐ ENGAGED
  ① their own contact form + audit link
  ② ⭐ email + the video
  ③ voice call        (when voice ships)
  ④ voicemail drop    (when voice ships)
       │
       └─ ⭐⭐ ANY response ──────────────► ⭐ SMS. FOR EVERYTHING AFTER.
```

⭐⭐ **Once contact is made, SMS is the channel** — ⛔ *not email, not a portal,
not a scheduled call.* ⭐ **It's where a tradesperson actually is** — between
jobs, one hand, no login — ⭐⭐ **and we sell texting by texting.**

⛔ **Stop on any reply, any channel** *(§18C.1)*. ⭐ **One `Conversation` holds the
form, the email, the video watch and every text** *(§11.5)*.

## 70.2 ⭐ AUTOPILOT

⭐⭐ **Fully automatic:** discovery · enrichment · ⭐ **the 54 checks** · the
experiential tests *(with §68.2's discipline enforced in code)* · scoring ·
⭐ **demo site build** · ⭐ **video generation** · rungs ①–②.

⭐ **Agent-led with human escalation:** the SMS conversation.
⛔ **Human:** closing anything above a self-serve claim.

⭐⭐ **So one person runs the whole funnel.** ⛔ **Cost gate: the demo build and
video fire on SCORED prospects only** — *a crawl, an audit, a render and a TTS
pass per prospect is real money.*

## 70.3 ⭐⭐ THE CONVERSION PATH

| ⭐ Signal | ⭐⭐ Means |
| :--- | :--- |
| Video watched <20% | continue normally |
| ⭐ **50%+** | advance immediately *(§27.2.3)* |
| ⭐⭐ **80%+ or shared** | ⭐ **human, now — they showed someone** |
| ⭐⭐ **Texted the demo number** | ⭐⭐ **the strongest buying signal in the system** — ⛔ *nobody texts a demo of a business they don't own* |
| ⭐ **Claimed** | the demo tenant becomes theirs *(§69.5)* |

## 70.4 ⭐ WHAT WE MEASURE

⛔ **Not "leads."** ⭐⭐ **Cost per PAYING TENANT, and where it leaks:** cost per
demo built *(actual, from the meters)* · demo → watched · ⭐ **watched → texted** ·
texted → claimed · claimed → paid · ⭐⭐ **and by vertical, because which verticals
convert is what promotes them to premium** *(§52.4)*.

⭐ **X-185 optimises the acquisition machine with the same bandit logic it gives
tenants** *(§40)* — ⛔ **the honest test of whether it works.**

## 70.5 ACCEPTANCE — A3

☐ ⛔ **Text-only until voice ships**; ⭐ the video says *"text it"*
☐ ⭐⭐ **Cold: form → email → voice → voicemail. ENGAGED: SMS for everything after**
☐ ⭐ Stop on any reply; one `Conversation` throughout
☐ ⭐⭐ **Autopilot through demo build and video**; human on escalation and closing
☐ ⛔ **Demo build fires on scored prospects only**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Texting the demo number is the strongest buying signal**
☐ ⭐ Watch depth advances the ladder — 50% · 80% · shared
☐ ⭐⭐ **Cost per PAYING TENANT, by vertical**

**All eight ✅ — §70 RESTORED.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §71 · W1 — THE GOAIEZ PLUGIN  *(EXECUTED T534)*
⭐ **The workspace the 60 agents actually build in.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 71.0 ⭐ WHAT W1 IS

⛔ **Not "configure the agents" — that's W2/W3.** ⭐⭐ **W1 is the workspace
itself: the rules, the skills, the workflows and the state that make 60 agents
build one platform instead of sixty** *(§53)*.

## 71.1 ⭐⭐ THE WORKSPACE — ASSEMBLED

```
  goaiez-workspace/
    ⭐ AGENTS.md                    <12k · ⭐⭐ "run resume first"
    .agents/
      ⭐ rules/                      <12k each · always loaded
        01-precedence   02-entities   03-actions   04-laws   ⭐ 05-status
      ⭐⭐ skills/                    ⭐ load on relevance only
        17 skills — spine · channels · intelligence · data · pixel · surfaces ·
        builder · crm · fsm · seo · reviews · social · money · attribution ·
        ⭐ acquisition · ui · content · verify
      workflows/
        ⭐⭐ resume   ⭐ build-module   verify-module   seed-content   merge
      ⭐⭐ state/
        ⭐ BUILD-STATE.json   SESSION-LOG.md   CONTENT-MANIFEST.json
      ⭐ wardens/
        ⭐⭐ OWNERSHIP.json           ← who may write what
```

## 71.2 ⭐⭐ THE FIVE WORKFLOWS

| ⭐ Workflow | ⭐⭐ Does |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **`resume`** | ⭐ **read state · report position · propose the next unblocked item · ⛔ STOP** *(§53.4)* |
| ⭐ **`build-module`** | ⭐ **manifest → migrations → handlers → wiring → screen → VERIFY slot** — ⛔ *in that order, and it refuses to skip* |
| ⭐ **`verify-module`** | the six checks + ⭐⭐ **runtime proof** *(§61)* |
| **`seed-content`** | manifest → parser → seeders → validation report |
| ⭐ **`merge`** | worktree → warden review → main |

### ⭐⭐ `build-module` — THE ORDER IS THE POINT

```
  ① ⭐ manifest first        ⛔ no code before the contract exists (§9 law 1)
  ② migrations              ⭐ entities from the twelve, never invented
  ③ handlers                the actions the manifest declared
  ④ ⭐⭐ WIRING              ⭐ routes · subscribers · seams — ⛔ THE STEP THAT GETS SKIPPED
  ⑤ screen                  if it has one (U2's inventory)
  ⑥ ⭐ VERIFY slot           ⛔ filled by a PROVER, never the builder
```

⛔ **Step ④ is where the 126 came from.** ⭐⭐ *The workflow refuses to advance to
⑤ until a caller exists* — ⭐ **checked, not asked.**

## 71.3 ⭐⭐ OWNERSHIP — ENFORCED BY WORKTREES, NOT DISCIPLINE

⭐ **`OWNERSHIP.json` maps every file pattern to exactly one owner** *(§9 law 2)*:

| ⭐ Owner | Owns |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **W2 Entity warden** | ⭐ **the twelve entities** — ⛔ *nobody else touches a canonical model* |
| **W3 Migration** | the migrations directory |
| **W4 Route** | the route files |
| **W5 Config** | `platform_settings`, the rate registry |
| ⭐ **W6 Contract** | ⭐⭐ **the action registry schema and the verb set** |
| **W7 Seed** | seeders and the content manifest |
| Squads | ⭐ their own module directories, and nothing else |

⭐⭐ **Each agent works in its own git worktree on its own branch** — ⛔ *so two
agents cannot edit the same file, because they cannot see the same working
directory.* ⭐ **The rule is enforced by the filesystem, not by a promise.**

## 71.4 ⭐ THE PreToolUse GATES

⭐ **They refuse the write rather than reporting it afterwards** *(§13.8)*:

| ⭐ Gate | ⛔ Blocks |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **No-mock lint** | ⭐ **a test double standing in for a real call** |
| ⭐⭐ **Caller check** | ⛔ **shipping something nothing calls** |
| ⭐ **Wiring check** | routes, subscribers and seams declared |
| **Namespace collision** | two modules claiming one action id |
| ⭐⭐ **Warden-file guard** | ⛔ **writing to a file you don't own** |
| ⭐ **Module-number check** *(build check ⑦)* | ⭐⭐ **one `X-nnn`, one name** *(§33.1)* |

⚠️ ⭐ **ASW's diagnostics hook is a no-op** *(§0.5)* — ⛔ **these six must be wired
separately, and W1 wires them.**

## 71.5 ⭐⭐ THE SESSION CONTRACT

⭐ **Every agent, every session, without exception:**

☐ ⭐⭐ **Run `resume` first** — ⛔ *never start from memory*
☐ ⭐ **Claim exactly one item** in `BUILD-STATE.json` — ⛔ *never two*
☐ ⭐ **Work only in your worktree**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Append to `SESSION-LOG.md` before finishing** — ⛔ *what you did, what you couldn't, what you noticed*
☐ ⭐ **Never set `verified: true`** on your own work

⭐⭐ **"What you noticed" is the underrated field:** ⭐ *an agent that spots a
problem in someone else's module has no other way to report it, and that
observation is often worth more than the work it was doing.*

## 71.6 ACCEPTANCE — W1

☐ ⭐ Workspace assembled — ⭐⭐ **AGENTS.md · 5 rules · 17 skills · 5 workflows · state · wardens**
☐ ⭐⭐ **`resume` runs first, every session, and STOPS for confirmation**
☐ ⭐⭐ **`build-module` refuses to pass wiring** — ⛔ *the step that produced the 126*
☐ ⭐ VERIFY filled by a prover, ⛔ **never the builder**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Ownership by worktree — enforced by the filesystem, not a promise**
☐ ⭐ Six PreToolUse gates wired; ⚠️ ⭐ **ASW's no-op replaced**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Session contract: resume · claim one · log what you noticed**

**All seven ✅ — W1 EXECUTED.**

# §73 · W2 — THE 60 AGENT PRESETS *(T535)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 73.1 ⭐ THE ORG

| ⭐ Role | Count | ⭐⭐ Preset carries |
| :--- | ---: | :--- |
| ⭐ **Conductor** | 1 | ⭐ **reads `BUILD-STATE`, assigns, never writes code** |
| ⭐⭐ **Wardens** | **7** | ⭐ **their owned paths from `OWNERSHIP.json`** — ⛔ *and nothing else* |
| ⭐ **Squads** | **12 × 4** | architect · builder · builder · ⭐ **prover** |
| ⭐⭐ **Assurance** | **4** | QA-1 contract · ⭐ **QA-2 wiring** · QA-3 behaviour · QA-4 runtime |
| | ⭐ **60** | |

## 73.2 ⭐⭐ WHAT EVERY PRESET CONTAINS

```yaml
  role:        squad-7-builder-a
  ⭐ skills:    [goaiez-spine, goaiez-fsm]      ← ⛔ ONLY what it needs
  ⭐⭐ owns:     app/Modules/PriceBook/**         ← from OWNERSHIP.json
  ⭐ worktree:  branch per agent                 ← §71.3
  workflow:    build-module
  ⭐⭐ gates:    all six PreToolUse
  ⛔ may_not:   [set verified, edit entities, add a verb, claim two items]
```

⭐⭐ **`skills` is the important line.** ⛔ *An agent loaded with all 17 skills has
no context left to work in* — ⭐ **two or three, chosen by its squad.**

## 73.3 ⭐ THE FOUR RULES THAT MAKE 60 SAFE

☐ ⭐⭐ **One owner per file** — ⛔ *filesystem-enforced, not agreed*

they author manifests for waves 1–3.**

# §74 · ⭐⭐ X-190 `LocalNetwork` — THE LINK ENGINE  *(owner, T536)*
⛔ **§72.5 corrected. I conflated two different things.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

> **⛔ FIRST-PASS SHAPE — PRECEDENCE (T667, §0.A):** X-190; current §130 — owner rulings LIVE. *Nothing here is deleted (law 10); read §0.A before treating this section as current.*

## 74.0 ⭐ WHAT I GOT WRONG

| ⛔ What I warned about | ⭐⭐ What you're describing |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **A footer link to GOAIEZ from every tenant site** | ⭐⭐ **relevant LOCAL links between TENANTS** |
| ⛔ **Thousands of identical links, one target, no relevance** | ⭐ **a plumber and a roofer in the same town** |
| *the pattern Google devalues* | ⭐⭐ **the pattern local SEO has always recommended** *(§32.3 F6)* |

⭐⭐ **And you're right on the hosting point.** ⛔ *Wix, GoDaddy and Squarespace host
millions of sites on shared infrastructure and it isn't a penalty.* ⭐ **Google
knows shared hosting from a content farm — and the tell is exactly what you named:
⭐⭐ every one of our sites has a real, verified GBP behind a real business.**

⛔ **The footer-blob warning stands. The local network is a different thing and
it's a good feature.**

## 74.1 ⭐⭐ MAKE THE RELATIONSHIP REAL, NOT JUST THE LINK

⭐ **The strongest version of this isn't a link exchange. It's a referral
network where the link is the by-product.**

```
  ⭐ two tenants matched ──► ⭐⭐ a real referral relationship
                                   │
       ⭐ the plumber sends overflow drainage work to the roofer
       ⭐ the roofer sends gutter jobs back
                                   │
       ⭐⭐ and each lists the other on a "who we work with" page
```

⭐⭐ **We can make it real because we have both sides.** ⭐ *We can pass an actual
referral between them, track whether it became a job, and show them the money it
produced.* ⛔ **A link backed by a real job is not a link scheme — it's a
directory of people you genuinely recommend.**

⭐⭐ **And that's the feature: the owner does nothing.** ⭐ *We find the match, we
make the introduction, they approve once, and the referrals start flowing both
ways.*

## 74.2 ⭐ THE MATCHING

| ⭐ Match on | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Same metro or region** | ⛔ **local, never national** |
| ⭐⭐ **Complementary, never competing** | ⛔ *a plumber is never matched to a plumber* |
| ⭐ **Both active tenants** | with a ⭐⭐ **verified GBP** |
| ⭐ **Actual overlap** | ⭐⭐ *roofers get drainage calls; plumbers get gutter calls* — **the profile knows** |
| **Both willing** | ⭐ **one approval each, once** |

⭐⭐ **The industry profiles already encode which trades refer to each other** —
⭐ *so the matchmaking is a lookup, not a guess.*

## 74.3 ⭐ THE RULES THAT KEEP IT CLEAN

☐ ⭐⭐ **A real page — "who we work with"** — ⛔ *never a footer blob*
☐ ⭐ **Capped at a handful per tenant** — ⛔ *"excessive" is the word in Google's own policy, so we stay nowhere near it*
☐ ⭐⭐ **Not reciprocal by requirement** — ⭐ **A can list B without B listing A**
☐ ⭐ **Owner approves each connection once** — ⭐⭐ **editorial intent, recorded**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Removable in one tap**, and removal is honoured immediately
☐ ⭐ **Only trades that genuinely refer** — from the profile map

⭐⭐ **The third rule is the one that matters most:** ⛔ *mandatory reciprocity is
what makes an exchange a scheme. "We list people we'd actually recommend" is what
every local business already does.*

## 74.4 ⭐⭐ THE PART THAT MAKES IT UNDENIABLE

⭐ **Referrals pass through the platform and are tracked** *(§49)*:

> ⭐⭐ *"You've sent Mike 4 jobs this quarter. He's sent you 6. Worth $3,100 to
> you."*

⭐⭐ **That number is the proof the relationship is real** — ⛔ *and it's a
retention feature on its own, because a tenant with three referral partners has
three reasons to stay.*

## 74.5 ACCEPTANCE — X-190

☐ ⭐ §72.5 corrected — ⛔ **footer blob still out**, ⭐⭐ **local network in**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Matched on region + complementary trade + verified GBP + real referral overlap**
☐ ⭐ Listed on a real page; ⛔ **capped, never excessive**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Not reciprocal by requirement**
☐ ⭐ One approval each; ⭐ **one-tap removal, honoured immediately**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §75 · ⭐⭐ X-191 `BacklinkBot` — GOD-LEVEL LINK ACQUISITION  *(owner, T537)*
⭐ **Nobody is doing this for local business. This is why it works.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

> **⛔ FIRST-PASS SHAPE — PRECEDENCE (T667, §0.A):** X-191; current §130. *Nothing here is deleted (law 10); read §0.A before treating this section as current.*

## 75.0 ⭐⭐ WHY IT'S OPEN GROUND

⭐ **Link building for local business is done by agencies, by hand, at
$100–300/link.** ⛔ *Which means a plumber gets zero, because nobody will do 50
outreach emails a month for a $200 client.*

⭐⭐ **We can, because the whole pipeline already exists:** ⭐ **X-151 fetches ·
X-135 researches · X-183 writes · X-109 submits forms · C-Mail sends · X-138
attributes.** ⛔ **The bot is orchestration over things already built.**

---

## 75.1 ⭐⭐ THE NINE TARGET TYPES — RANKED BY YIELD

| # | ⭐ Target | ⭐⭐ Why it converts |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **1** | **MANUFACTURER DEALER PAGES** | ⭐⭐ **the most underused link in the trades.** *Worcester, Trane, Carrier, Velux all run "find an installer" pages — high authority, perfectly relevant, and the tenant already fits their kit.* ⛔ **Almost nobody claims theirs** |
| ⭐⭐ **2** | **LINK-INTERSECT GAPS** | ⭐ **sites linking to 2+ competitors but not the tenant** — ⛔ *they already link to this trade in this town, so the answer is usually yes* |
| ⭐ **3** | **Non-competing local businesses** | ⭐⭐ **X-190's referral network** — *the relationship carries the link* |
| ⭐ **4** | **Supplier & wholesaler pages** | trade counters list their regulars |
| ⭐⭐ **5** | **Local resource pages** | *"best plumbers in [town]"* — ⭐ **they exist to list people** |
| **6** | **Trade associations & certifications** | ⭐ *membership usually includes a listing nobody claims* |
| ⭐ **7** | **Local sponsorship** | ⭐⭐ **a youth team, a fete, a charity** — *a real £150 sponsorship for a real local link* |
| **8** | **Chambers & BIDs** | membership listings |
| ⭐ **9** | **Local news & community sites** | ⭐ **hooked to something real** — a hire, an award, storm response |

⭐⭐ **Targets 1 and 2 are where the volume is**, and ⛔ *neither requires
persuasion — one is a form the tenant qualifies for, the other is a site that
already links to their competitors.*

## 75.2 ⭐ THE PIPELINE

```
  ① ⭐ DISCOVER      the nine types, per tenant, per town
  ② ⭐⭐ QUALIFY      ⛔ score before spending anything (75.3)
  ③ ⭐ FIND CONTACT  email · contact form · the right person by name
  ④ ⭐⭐ COMPOSE      ⭐ a real reason, from their own site
  ⑤ ⭐ SEND          email or their form (X-109)
  ⑥ FOLLOW UP        ⭐ once. ⛔ Never twice
  ⑦ ⭐⭐ MONITOR      ⭐ did the link go up — and does it stay up? (75.5)
```

## 75.3 ⛔⛔ THE QUALIFY GATE — WHAT WE REFUSE TO PURSUE

⭐ **Scored before a single credit is spent:**

| ⛔ Rejected | ⭐ Why |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔⛔ **Sites that sell links** | ⭐ **a paid link is a liability, not an asset** |
| ⛔ **PBNs and spun-content networks** | detectable by footprint |
| ⛔ **Irrelevant sites** | ⭐ *a plumber on a crypto blog helps nobody* |
| ⛔ **Low-quality directories** | ⭐ **the ones that list anyone** |
| ⛔ **Anything already flagged toxic** *(§32.3 F3)* | |
| ⛔ **Out of area** | ⭐⭐ **local is the entire point** |

⭐⭐ **The gate is the product.** ⛔ *An agency chasing volume takes the paid link.
A bot with a scoring gate never sees it.*

## 75.4 ⭐⭐ THE PITCH — WHY IT ISN'T SPAM

⛔ **Generic outreach is why link building has a bad name.** ⭐ **Ours is
specific because X-135 read their page first:**

| ⭐ Target | ⭐⭐ The actual pitch |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Manufacturer** | *"We're a Worcester-accredited installer in Ashfield — we fit about 40 a year. We're not on your installer finder."* |
| ⭐⭐ **Resource page** | ⭐ *"Your 'best plumbers in Ashfield' page lists 6 — two have closed. Here's a working one."* |
| ⭐ **Link intersect** | *"You've linked to two local plumbers. We cover the north side, which neither does."* |
| ⭐ **Sponsorship** | ⭐⭐ *"We'd like to sponsor the U12s. £150."* — ⛔ *and we actually pay it* |
| **Local news** | ⭐ *"We ran free emergency callouts through the storm. Happy to talk."* |

⭐⭐ **Every pitch names something true about their page.** ⛔ *If X-135 can't find
a real reason, the target is dropped — no reason, no send.*

## 75.5 ⭐⭐ MONITORING — THE HALF EVERYONE SKIPS

⭐ **Winning a link is half the job. ⭐⭐ Keeping it is the other half.**

| ⭐ Checked monthly | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Is the link still there?** | ⛔ *sites get redesigned and links vanish silently* |
| ⭐ **`nofollow` / `sponsored` / `ugc`?** | recorded, not judged |
| ⭐ **Anchor text** | ⛔ *over-optimised anchors are a footprint* |
| ⭐⭐ **Is the page still indexed?** | ⭐ *a link on a deindexed page is worth nothing* |
| ⭐ **Did the site turn toxic?** | ⭐⭐ **then we ask for removal** |

### ⭐⭐ RECIPROCAL ENFORCEMENT — HONOURING THE DEAL

⭐ **For X-190 partnerships where both sides agreed to list each other:**

```
  ⭐ partner's link disappears
       ├─ ⭐ day 0   detected
       ├─ ⭐⭐ day 1  ⭐ friendly note — "did your site get redesigned?"
       ├─ day 14     reminder
       └─ ⭐⭐ day 30 ⭐ OURS COMES DOWN, and both are told why
```

⭐⭐ **This is honest bookkeeping, not a threat.** ⛔ *They agreed to list each
other; if one side stops, the other shouldn't keep carrying it.* ⭐ **And the
grace period exists because a vanished link is usually a redesign, not a
decision.**

⚠️ ⭐⭐ **ONE THING TO WATCH, and it's a design point rather than a rule:** ⭐ **a
link profile that is 100% reciprocal looks engineered.** ⛔ *So the bot pursues
both — partnerships AND one-way editorial links (targets 1, 2, 5, 7, 9)* — and
⭐⭐ **the reciprocal share is a number on the dashboard.** *A healthy local
business has both, because that's what happens naturally.*

## 75.6 ⭐ VOLUME, COST AND CONTROL

| ⭐ Setting | Default |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Outreach attempts** | ⭐ **50 / month / tenant** — ⛔ **admin-adjustable** |
| **Pacing** | ⭐ **spread across the month**, never batched |
| **Follow-ups** | ⭐ 1 · ⛔ never 2 |
| ⭐ **Per-domain cap** | ⛔ *one pitch per domain per year* |
| **Metering** | ⭐⭐ **lead credits for discovery · AI credits for research and composition · email meter for sends** |

⭐⭐ **And X-185 optimises it** *(§40)*: ⭐ **which target types, which pitch
angles and which sequences actually win links — learned across the fleet**, ⛔
*so tenant #500 benefits from every pitch tenant #1 ever sent.*

## 75.7 ⭐⭐ THE REPORT

> ⭐⭐ *"47 sites approached. 9 replied. **6 links live.** 2 partnerships
> exchanging referrals. Your strongest: Worcester's installer finder — DA 71,
> and it sent 3 visits last month."*

⭐ **Reported in visits and calls where attribution can see them** *(§49)* — ⛔
**not in domain authority alone.**

## 75.8 ACCEPTANCE — X-191

☐ ⭐⭐ **Nine target types ranked** — ⭐ **manufacturer dealer pages and link-intersect first**
☐ ⛔⛔ **Qualify gate refuses paid links, PBNs, irrelevant and out-of-area**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Every pitch names something true about their page** — ⛔ **no reason, no send**
☐ ⭐ One follow-up; ⛔ **one pitch per domain per year**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Monthly monitoring: still there · rel · anchor · indexed · turned toxic**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Reciprocal enforcement with a 30-day grace** — ⭐ **friendly first, both told why**
☐ ⚠️ ⭐⭐ **Reciprocal share tracked** — ⭐ **the bot pursues one-way links too**
☐ ⭐ 50/month default, admin-adjustable, paced, metered
☐ ⭐⭐ **X-185 learns which pitches win, across the fleet**
☐ ⭐ Reported in **visits and calls**, ⛔ not DA alone

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §76 · ⭐⭐ X-192 `MembershipEngine` + THE PARTNER INTELLIGENCE LAYER  *(T538)*
⭐ **The final pass on link acquisition. This is the thinking half.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

> **⛔ FIRST-PASS SHAPE — PRECEDENCE (T667, §0.A):** X-192; current §130. *Nothing here is deleted (law 10); read §0.A before treating this section as current.*

## 76.1 ⭐⭐ THE PAID LINE — MEMBERSHIP YES, LINKS NEVER

> ⭐⭐ **Pay for MEMBERSHIP that comes with a listing. ⛔ Never pay for a LINK.**

⭐ **The distinction is real and it's defensible:** ⭐⭐ *a chamber membership has
value whether or not the link exists — networking, events, credibility, a badge
on the van.* ⛔ *A paid directory listing has no value except the link, which is
exactly why it's worthless.*

| ⭐ WORTH PAYING FOR | ⛔ NEVER |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Chamber of Commerce** *(1–2)* | ⛔ paid directories |
| ⭐ **Trade association / certification** *(Gas Safe · NICEIC · NFB · BBB)* | ⛔ "guest post" placements |
| ⭐⭐ **Manufacturer accreditation** | ⛔ link packages |
| **BID / town-centre partnership** | ⛔ PBN networks |
| ⭐ **Local sponsorship** *(a real team, a real fete)* | ⛔ anything sold as SEO |

## 76.2 ⭐⭐ THE CHAMBER PLAY — HIGHEST QUICK WIN

⭐ **Find the right 1–2, recommend the package, and ⭐⭐ BUILD THE PROFILE FOR
THEM.**

```
  ⭐ ① FIND        which chambers cover this postcode?
       │            ⛔ often 2–3 overlap: city · county · town
  ⭐⭐ ② RANK       ⭐ which actually ranks? — crawl their member directory,
       │            check it's indexed, check members' listings rank
  ⭐ ③ PRICE       tiers, what each includes, ⭐⭐ which tier gets a LINKED listing
  ⭐ ④ RECOMMEND   ⭐⭐ "join this one, this tier, £280/yr — here's why"
  ⭐⭐ ⑤ BUILD      ⭐ we write the profile: description · categories · services ·
       │            hours · photos — ⛔ ALL FROM DATA WE ALREADY HOLD
  ⭐ ⑥ VERIFY      it went live, it's linked, it's indexed
  ⑦ MONITOR        annually — renewal, and did the listing survive
```

⭐⭐ **Step ⑤ is the whole feature.** ⛔ *Most members never complete their profile
— they pay, they get a stub listing with a name and a phone number, and it ranks
for nothing.* ⭐ **We fill it properly in about a minute, because the profile,
services, hours and photos are already in the graph.**

⚠️ ⭐ **Not every chamber is worth it.** ⛔ *If their directory is noindexed, or
the listing tier that includes a link costs 4× the basic — we say so and
recommend against.* ⭐⭐ **A recommendation we'd decline ourselves is worth more
than one we always give.**

## 76.3 ⭐⭐ THE PARTNER INTELLIGENCE ENGINE — THE THINKING HALF

⛔ **This is what separates it from mail-merge.** ⭐ **Before any pitch, the bot
crawls and reasons about the target** *(X-151 + X-135)*:

### ⭐ SIX QUESTIONS, ANSWERED BEFORE A SINGLE SEND

| # | ⭐ Question | ⭐⭐ How it's answered |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **1** | **What do they actually do?** | crawl · services · service area · who they serve |
| ⭐⭐ **2** | ⭐ **Do they link out AT ALL?** | ⛔ *a site with zero outbound links will never be the first* |
| ⭐⭐ **3** | ⭐⭐ **Is there a PAGE that would host the link?** | ⭐ **find it before pitching** — resources · partners · "who we recommend" |
| ⭐ **4** | **Do they already link to competitors?** | ⭐⭐ **the strongest yes-signal there is** |
| ⭐ **5** | ⭐ **Is it worth having?** | authority · relevance · ⭐⭐ **is the page indexed** · does it get traffic |
| ⭐⭐ **6** | ⭐ **Who decides, and how do we reach them?** | named person · email · form · the right channel |

⭐⭐ **Question 3 is the one that changes the pitch entirely.** ⛔ *"Would you link
to us?"* is spam. ⭐⭐ *"Your resources page lists six plumbers and two have
closed"* is a favour — **and it requires actually reading the page.**

### ⭐⭐ THE REVERSE-REFERRAL SIGNAL

⭐ **The smartest single check:** ⭐⭐ **does this business already recommend
someone in our tenant's trade?**

```
  ⭐ a roofer's site says "we work with a great plumber" and links out
       │
       └─ ⭐⭐ THE RELATIONSHIP ALREADY EXISTS. They just don't know ours yet.
```

⭐⭐ **A business that already refers this trade is the highest-probability
partner in the entire dataset** — ⛔ *they've proved they do it, publicly.*

### ⭐ THE FIT SCORE

⭐ **Composite, and it decides spend:**

| ⭐ Factor | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Geographic overlap** | same town > same county > same region |
| ⭐⭐ **Complementary, not competing** | ⛔ **hard filter, from the profile map** |
| ⭐ **Audience overlap** | do they serve the same customers? |
| ⭐⭐ **Link-out behaviour** | do they, ever? |
| ⭐ **Competitor links** | already linking to this trade |
| **Page quality** | indexed · trafficked · not a link dump |
| ⭐ **Reachability** | is there a real contact? |

⛔ **Below threshold, nothing is spent** — ⭐ *no crawl beyond the first page, no
research, no composition.*

## 76.4 ⭐ WHAT THE TENANT SEES

> ⭐⭐ *"**Ashfield Chamber** — £280/yr, and their directory ranks. **We'll build
> your listing.** Worth it.
> **County Chamber** — £450 and their directory is noindexed. **Skip it.**
>
> ⭐ **14 partners found.** 6 already recommend plumbers. **We've written to all
> 14.**"*

⭐⭐ **Two decisions and a number.** ⛔ *Not a spreadsheet of 200 prospects.*

## 76.5 ACCEPTANCE — X-192

☐ ⭐⭐ **Membership yes, links never** — ⭐ *a membership has value without the link*
☐ ⭐⭐ **Chamber play: find · rank · price · recommend · ⭐ BUILD THE PROFILE · verify · monitor**
☐ ⚠️ ⭐ **Recommend AGAINST a chamber whose directory is noindexed**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Six questions answered before any send**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Question 3: find the page that would host the link, before pitching**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Reverse-referral signal — businesses already recommending this trade**
☐ ⭐ Fit score gates spend; ⛔ **below threshold, nothing is spent**
☐ ⭐ Tenant sees **two decisions and a number**, ⛔ not a spreadsheet

**All eight ✅ — X-192 SPECCED. Modules: 249 → 250.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §77 · ⭐⭐ X-190 EXTENDED — THE OPT-IN REFERRAL NETWORK  *(owner, T539)*
⭐ **The bot proposes it to both sides and runs the whole thing.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

> **⛔ FIRST-PASS SHAPE — PRECEDENCE (T667, §0.A):** X-190 extended; current §130. *Nothing here is deleted (law 10); read §0.A before treating this section as current.*

## 77.1 ⭐ THE OFFER — ASKED ONCE, AT ONBOARDING

> ⭐⭐ *"You're in Ashfield. There are **3 roofers and 2 electricians** on GO AI EZ
> near you who don't compete with you. **Want referral partnerships? We'll set it
> all up.**"*

⭐ **One toggle. That's the entire ask of the tenant.** ⛔ *Everything after it is
the bot.*

## 77.2 ⭐⭐ BOTH SIDES, PROPOSED AUTOMATICALLY

⭐ **When both are our tenants there is no cold outreach at all** — ⭐⭐ **it's an
in-app offer to two existing customers:**

```
  ⭐ A opts in
       ▼
  ⭐⭐ bot matches B  (region · complementary · verified GBP · real overlap)
       ▼
  ⭐ bot proposes to B:
     "Summit Plumbing in Ashfield wants to send you gutter work. Interested?"
       ▼
  ⭐⭐ B accepts ──► ⭐ THE BOT DOES EVERYTHING:
       ├─ the "who we work with" block on both sites
       ├─ ⭐⭐ the referral routing rule in both agents
       ├─ a shared view of what's passed each way
       └─ ⭐ the honouring check (§75.5)
```

⭐⭐ **Neither owner does anything but tap accept.**

## 77.3 ⭐⭐ THE AGENT MAKES THE REFERRAL — LIVE, ON THE CALL

⛔ **This is the part that turns a link into revenue.**

> ⭐ *Caller:* "Do you do roofs?"
> ⭐⭐ *Agent:* **"We don't — but we work with Ashfield Roofing and they're good.
> Want me to text you their number?"**

| ⭐ What just happened | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **A wasted call became a referral** | ⛔ *instead of "sorry, no"* |
| ⭐ **The customer got helped** | ⭐⭐ **which is why they'll call back for plumbing** |
| ⭐ **The partner got a job** | and owes one back |
| ⭐⭐ **It's tracked both ways** | *(§77.4)* |

⭐⭐ **Every trade takes calls it can't serve.** ⛔ *Today those are pure loss.*
⭐ **Here they're the currency of the network — and the agent that already
answers the phone does it for free.**

## 77.4 ⭐ TRACKED, VALUED, REPORTED

> ⭐⭐ *"You've sent Mike **4 jobs** this quarter. He's sent you **6**. **Worth
> $3,100 to you.**"*

⭐ **Both sides see the same numbers** — ⭐⭐ **which is what keeps it honest
without anyone policing it.** ⛔ *An imbalance is visible to both, so it corrects
itself or ends cleanly.*

## 77.5 ⭐⭐ NON-TENANT PARTNERS = AN ACQUISITION CHANNEL

⭐ **When the best match isn't a tenant yet, the bot recruits them:**

> ⭐⭐ *"**Summit Plumbing in Ashfield wants to refer you work.** Join free to
> accept referrals."*

| ⭐ Why this converts unusually well | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **It opens with an offer, not a pitch** | ⛔ *somebody wants to give them jobs* |
| ⭐ **A named local business vouches** | ⭐⭐ **not a cold ad** |
| ⭐ **The first value is immediate** | a referral, not a trial |
| ⭐⭐ **And they land in the full machine** | demo site, agent, audit *(§69)* |

⭐⭐ **So one tenant's network need becomes the next tenant's acquisition.** ⛔
*That loop costs nothing and compounds with density.*

## 77.6 ⭐⭐ THE DENSITY EFFECT — THE REAL MOAT

⭐ **The network gets more valuable to every member as more join the same town:**

| Tenants in a town | ⭐ Partnerships available |
| :--- | ---: |
| 5 | a handful |
| 20 | ⭐ meaningful |
| ⭐⭐ **50** | ⭐⭐ **a genuine local trade network** |

⛔ **And it's the hardest thing for a competitor to copy** — ⭐⭐ *they'd need our
density in that specific town, not just our software.*

⭐ **Which is also why acquisition should go town by town, not scattershot** —
⛔ *50 tenants in one town is worth more than 500 spread across fifty.*

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §78 · ⭐⭐ THE PARTNER SLOT ENGINE  *(owner, T540 — §77.1 corrected)*
⭐ **On by default. Never gives up. And it turns partners into customers.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

> **⛔ FIRST-PASS SHAPE — PRECEDENCE (T667, §0.A):** partner slot engine; §78.4 CORRECTED by §79; current §130. *Nothing here is deleted (law 10); read §0.A before treating this section as current.*

## 78.0 ⛔ CORRECTION — ON BY DEFAULT, NOT OPT-IN

| ⛔ §77.1 said | ⭐⭐ Correct |
| :--- | :--- |
| a toggle at onboarding | ⭐ **ON automatically** |
| tenant opts in | ⭐⭐ **tenant can toggle OFF** |

⭐ **Right default, and it's genuinely in their interest.** ⭐⭐ **One honest
requirement: it's visible.** ⛔ *A link published on their site is shown on their
dashboard from day one — on by default is fine, hidden is not.*

## 78.1 ⭐⭐ THE SLOT MODEL

⭐ **Every tenant has partner SLOTS, derived from the industry profile's referral
map** *(§76.3)*:

```
  ⭐ A PLUMBER'S SLOTS
     ├─ roofer          ⭐ FILLED — Ashfield Roofing
     ├─ electrician     ⭐ SEARCHING
     ├─ HVAC            ⭐⭐ HELD — 2 declined, 1 in the pool
     ├─ builder         EMPTY
     └─ drainage        ⭐ PROPOSED — awaiting reply
```

| ⭐ State | ⭐⭐ Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| `EMPTY` | no candidates found yet |
| ⭐ `SEARCHING` | ⭐⭐ **the bot is actively looking — this is the resting state, not a failure** |
| `PROPOSED` | pitched, awaiting a reply |
| ⛔ `DECLINED` | ⭐⭐ **→ goes straight back to SEARCHING. ⛔ The slot is never closed** |
| ⭐⭐ `HELD` | ⭐ **a good candidate said no — kept in the regional pool** *(78.3)* |
| `FILLED` | live, linked, referring |

⭐⭐ **A slot is finite and local, which is what makes it valuable.** ⛔ *There are
only so many good roofers in a town — so the bot never abandons a slot, it just
keeps working it.*

## 78.2 ⭐ IT NEVER STOPS LOOKING

⛔ **A decline is not an ending.**

```
  ⭐ candidate declines
       ├─ ⭐⭐ slot → SEARCHING immediately
       ├─ ⭐ candidate → the regional pool (78.3)
       ├─ ⭐ next candidate queued
       └─ ⛔ cooldown before re-approaching THAT candidate (one pitch/year, §75.6)
```

⭐⭐ **The tenant never sees a dead end** — ⭐ *they see "we're still looking for
your electrician partner", which is true and costs nothing.*

## 78.3 ⭐⭐ THE REGIONAL POOL — A DECLINE IS NEVER WASTED

⭐ **The insight: a roofer who said no to Summit Plumbing might say yes to
Ashfield Plumbing next month.** ⛔ *Same trade, different partner, different
chemistry, different day.*

```
  ⭐⭐ THE POOL — per region, per trade
     Ashfield Roofing     declined Summit (Mar)  ⭐ → available to match
     Crown Roofing        declined Summit (Apr)  ⭐ → available to match
     Vale Roofing         ⭐⭐ ACCEPTED Riverside (May) — now a tenant
```

| ⭐ Rule | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **A decline enters the pool, never a blacklist** | ⛔ *they declined a partner, not the idea* |
| ⭐ **Re-matched to a DIFFERENT tenant** | ⛔ never re-pitched for the same one |
| ⭐ **Cooldown honoured** | one approach per domain per year *(§75.6)* |
| ⭐⭐ **Everything learned is kept** | ⭐ *their contact, their page, the angle we used* — **the next pitch starts warm** |

⭐⭐ **So the research cost is paid once and reused forever.** ⛔ *Which is exactly
why 50 outreach attempts a month compounds instead of evaporating.*

---

## 78.4 ⛔ PARTNER → CUSTOMER *(TIMING SUPERSEDED BY §79 — the link is enough)*

> ⭐⭐ **We give them jobs first. Then we show them the product.**

⛔ **Cold outreach opens by asking. This opens by giving** — ⭐ **and by the time
we pitch, they've been paid.**

### ⭐ THE SEQUENCE — AND THE TIMING IS THE WHOLE THING

```
  ⭐ DAY 0    partnership accepted · link live · they're in the network
       │      ⛔ WE PITCH NOTHING
       │
  ⭐⭐ DAY 1–20  ⭐ REFERRALS FLOW. They get real jobs from our tenant.
       │        ⛔ STILL NOTHING.
       │
  ⭐ DAY ~21   ⭐⭐ the first referral converts to a paid job
       │       "That gutter job came through Summit Plumbing."
       │
  ⭐⭐ DAY ~25  ⭐ NOW: "Summit runs on GO AI EZ. Here's what yours would look like."
       │              ──► ⭐⭐ THE FULL PACKAGE (§69): their site, their agent,
       │                     their audit, their number, the video
       │
  ⭐ THEN     ⭐⭐ the standard ladder — but as a WARM lead
```

### ⭐⭐ WHY THIS CONVERTS FAR ABOVE COLD

| ⭐ By the time we pitch | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **They've received money from us** | ⛔ *not a promise — an actual paid job* |
| ⭐ **They've already said yes once** | to the partnership |
| ⭐⭐ **They've seen our work** | ⭐ **our tenant's site — which we built** |
| ⭐ **A local business vouched** | by name, not an ad |
| ⭐⭐ **They understand what we do** | ⛔ *the hardest part of any cold pitch, already done* |

⭐⭐ **This is the highest-intent lead the machine can produce.** ⭐ *A stranger who
has been paid by our network, seen our work, and said yes to us once already.*

### ⛔ THE DISCIPLINE THAT PROTECTS IT

☐ ⭐⭐ **Nothing is pitched until a referral has actually converted** — ⛔ *pitching
on day 1 spends the goodwill before it exists*
☐ ⭐ **The referral relationship survives a "no"** — ⛔ *we don't withdraw the
partnership if they decline the product*
☐ ⭐⭐ **One pitch, then the standard ladder** — ⛔ never pressure inside a working
partnership
☐ ⭐ **They can stay a partner forever without buying anything** — ⭐⭐ *and that's
fine, because the link and the referrals still serve our tenant*

⭐⭐ **That last one is what keeps it honest** — ⛔ *if the partnership were
contingent on buying, it would be a sales tactic. It isn't, so it's a network.*

## 78.5 ⭐ WHAT THIS DOES TO ACQUISITION MATH

| ⭐ Channel | Opens with | ⭐⭐ Intent |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Cold audit *(A1–A3)* | a problem we found | ⭐ warm |
| Inbound *(A4)* | they searched | ⭐ warm |
| ⭐⭐ **Partner-first** | ⭐⭐ **a paid job we sent them** | ⭐⭐⭐ **hot** |

⭐⭐ **And it scales with the network, not with spend** — ⭐ *every new tenant
creates 4–6 slots, every slot is an outreach, and every accepted partner is a
future customer who has already been paid.*

## 78.6 ACCEPTANCE — §78

☐ ⛔ **§77.1 corrected — ON by default, toggle-off, ⭐ and visible on the dashboard**
☐ ⭐ Slots from the profile's referral map; six states
☐ ⭐⭐ **`DECLINED` → `SEARCHING` immediately — ⛔ a slot is never closed**
☐ ⭐⭐ **The regional pool: a decline is re-matched to a DIFFERENT tenant**, research reused
☐ ⛔ Cooldown honoured — one approach per domain per year
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **Partner → customer: nothing pitched until a referral has CONVERTED**
☐ ⭐ Full package sent at ~day 25; then the standard ladder as a warm lead
☐ ⭐⭐ **The partnership survives a "no"** — ⛔ *never contingent on buying*
☐ ⭐⭐ **Partner-first recorded as the highest-intent channel**

**All nine ✅ — §78 COMPLETE. 250 modules holds.**

# §80 · ⭐⭐ SIX MORE FOR THE BOT  *(T542)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

> **⛔ FIRST-PASS SHAPE — PRECEDENCE (T667, §0.A):** six more for the bot; current §130. *Nothing here is deleted (law 10); read §0.A before treating this section as current.*

## 80.1 ⭐⭐⭐ MINE THEIR OWN CONTACTS FIRST — NOBODY DOES THIS

⛔ **Every link tool starts with strangers.** ⭐⭐ **The tenant already has
relationships with dozens of local businesses — and §23 already ingested them.**

| ⭐ Source, already in the graph | ⭐⭐ The link opportunity |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Invoices they've PAID** | ⭐ *suppliers, the trade counter, the van signwriter, their accountant* |
| ⭐⭐ **Invoices they've SENT** | ⭐⭐ **customers who own businesses** — *the café they fixed a boiler for* |
| ⭐ **Email + calendar** *(§23.1)* | who they actually deal with |
| ⭐ **Phone contacts** | the people they call |

> ⭐⭐ *"You've invoiced **Ashfield Builders 14 times.** Want us to ask them for a
> listing? We'll write it."*

⭐⭐ **That is the warmest link on earth** — ⛔ *a business they already work with,
who already knows them, approached on their behalf.* ⭐ **And the yield should be
several times cold outreach.**

⚠️ ⭐ **One rule:** ⭐⭐ **the tenant approves each ALLIANCE INTRO before we write ⭐ *(**`R235`-COMPLIANT** — not a permission gate on a lane: **approaching someone the tenant PERSONALLY knows, on their behalf, spends the tenant's own relationship capital**, and the AI cannot judge that. `P-096`/`D5` confirmation at the ACTION. ⛔ **Cold outreach stays fully unattended.**)*** ⛔ *Their
relationships are theirs — we don't email their accountant without asking.*

## 80.2 ⭐⭐ THE COMPETITOR'S DEAD LINKS — HIGHEST YIELD OF ALL

⭐ **When a local competitor closes, rebrands or lets their domain lapse,
⭐⭐ every page that linked to them now points at nothing.**

```
  ⭐ find competitors that died          (GBP closed · domain lapsed · 404)
       ▼
  ⭐⭐ find who linked to them            ← those pages still need a local trade
       ▼
  ⭐ "Your plumber link is dead — here's a working one"   ⛔ a genuine favour
```

⭐⭐ **Conversion should be the highest in the whole target set**, because ⛔ *the
page owner has a broken link they didn't know about and we're fixing it.*

## 80.3 ⭐ LOST LINK RECOVERY

⭐ **Links the tenant HAD and lost** — ⭐⭐ *far easier to recover than to win.*

☐ Site redesigned and the link dropped → ⭐ **"was this intentional?"**
☐ Page 404'd → suggest the replacement URL
☐ Went `nofollow` in a template change → ask
☐ ⭐⭐ **The partner removed theirs** → §75.5's ladder

## 80.4 ⭐ BROKEN-LINK BUILDING

⭐ **Crawl relevant local pages for ANY broken outbound link** — ⛔ not just to
competitors — ⭐⭐ **and offer the tenant's page where it genuinely fits.**

⛔ **Only where it fits.** ⭐ *Offering a plumber as a replacement for a broken
recipe link is the spam everyone hates.*

## 80.5 ⭐ UNLINKED MENTIONS + NETWORK-BY-DEGREE

⭐ **Two cheap sources already half-built:**

| ⭐ Source | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Unlinked mentions** *(§32.3 F5)* | ⭐ **someone already names them and didn't link** — *"thanks for the mention, mind linking it?"* is a 90% ask |
| ⭐⭐ **The partner's own partners** | ⭐ **once a partner joins, THEIR partners become candidates** — the network expands by degree, and each one is vouched twice |

## 80.6 ⛔⛔ THE ONE I'D HAVE FLAGGED ANYWAY — WHAT HAPPENS WHEN A TENANT LEAVES

⭐ **A paused or wound-down tenant's site is unpublished** *(§45A.4)*. ⛔⛔ **So
every partner who linked to them now points at a dead page — and we did that.**

| ⭐ What we do | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Tell the partner immediately** | ⛔ *never leave them with a silent 404* |
| ⭐⭐ **Offer a replacement from the same trade** | ⭐ **from the slot pool** *(§78.3)* — *their slot refills the same week* |
| ⭐ **Ask them to remove or repoint** | their choice, one tap |
| ⭐⭐ **And the leaving tenant's slots go back to the pool** | ⛔ *nothing is stranded* |

⭐⭐ **This matters for two reasons:** ⭐ **it's the honest thing** — we introduced
them — ⛔ **and a network that leaves dead links behind is a network nobody
trusts.** ⭐⭐ *Handling it well is also a second touchpoint with a business that
already knows us.*

## 80.7 ACCEPTANCE — §80

☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **Mine the tenant's own invoices, email, calendar and contacts first** — ⚠️ ⭐ **tenant approves each ALLIANCE INTRO** ⭐ *(`R235`-COMPLIANT — their own relationship capital; **cold outreach is unattended**)*
☐ ⭐⭐ **Competitor dead-link recovery — the highest-yield target in the set**
☐ ⭐ Lost-link recovery across four causes
☐ ⭐ Broken-link building, ⛔ **only where it genuinely fits**
☐ ⭐ Unlinked mentions wired in; ⭐⭐ **network expands by degree**
☐ ⛔⛔ **Departing tenants: partners told immediately, replacement offered from the pool, slots returned**

**All six ✅ — §80 COMPLETE. 250 modules holds.**

| ⭐ **Double-counts: many** | ⛔ **the 65-line overcount is real** |
| ⭐⭐ **Superseded-not-lost: several** | ⭐ *things replaced by better designs — those aren't gaps, and the matrix must say so* |
| **Fenced: 17 ads + 40 expansion** | ⭐ already accounted |

⛔ **A capability replaced by a better mechanism is NOT a loss** — ⭐⭐ *but it must
be recorded as replaced, with what replaced it, or the next reader will "restore"
it.*

## 82.5 ⭐ THE ALIAS MAP

⭐ **Closing O3 properly** *(§17.3)*:

| ⭐ Legacy id | Maps to |
| :--- | :--- |
| M-24 … M-110 *(this window)* | ⭐ **the section that resolved it** |
| M-190 … M-425 *(other account)* | ⭐ same |
| R66 … R92 | ⭐⭐ **the ruling that superseded or confirmed it** |
| CC-2 … CC-131 | the section that absorbed it |

⭐⭐ **So an agent reading any legacy document can resolve any id forward** — ⛔
*without which the corpus is a minefield of dead references.*

## 82.6 ⭐ THE OUTPUT

```
  RECONCILIATION.json
    { ⭐ "register": { "total": 905, "covered": N, "fenced": N,
                      ⭐⭐ "gaps": [...], "superseded": [...] },
      "cc_slices": {...}, "aliases": {...} }
```

⛔ **A gap becomes a module or a written decision not to build it.** ⭐⭐ **Neither
option is "leave it undecided."**
