# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §83 · B1–B2 — THE DEPENDENCY GRAPH & THE WAVES  *(EXECUTED T545)*
⭐ **Where the single launch date finally comes from.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

> **🗄️ HISTORICAL — PRECEDENCE (T667, §0.A):** B1–B2 waves of the 51-turn plan; the doctrine waves (tail §9) are the live ones. *Nothing here is deleted (law 10); read §0.A before treating this section as current.*

## 83.0 ⭐⭐ THE DATE IS DERIVED, NEVER PICKED

⭐ **The one-build law** *(§5A)* **means there is no phased calendar to hide
behind.** ⛔ *One launch, everything at once.* ⭐⭐ **So the date is an output of
the graph, not an input to it.**

⛔⛔ **And that's the honest position:** ⭐ *any date named before the graph exists
is a guess wearing a suit.*

## 83.1 ⭐ THE GRAPH

⭐ **Every module declares what it needs** *(from its manifest, §12.1)*:

| ⭐ Edge type | ⭐⭐ Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **`reads` / `writes`** | needs those entities to exist |
| ⭐ **`calls`** | ⛔ **needs that action to be built** |
| **`subscribes`** | needs the emitter |
| ⭐ **seams** | ⭐⭐ **needs both sides** |
| ⭐ **content** | needs its seeder and schema |

⭐⭐ **It's generated from the manifests, not drawn by hand** — ⛔ *which is the
only version that stays true as modules change.*

## 83.2 ⭐⭐ THE CRITICAL PATH

⭐ **Longest chain of hard dependencies:**

```
  ⭐⭐ SPINE (§11–§14)
       └─► ⭐ X-163 PriceBook          ⛔ 4 modules wait on it (§30A.6)
             └─► X-164 Estimates
                   └─► ⭐ X-165 Memberships
                         └─► ⭐⭐ X-166 JobCosting
                               └─► X-169/170 Payroll · Commissions
                                     └─► ⭐ X-173 AccountingSync
```

⭐⭐ **Two things sit alone at the front and everything else waits:** ⭐ **the
spine, then the pricebook.** ⛔ *Get either wrong and the graph reshapes under
you.*

⚠️ ⭐ **The non-code items on the critical path — and they're the ones that
slip:**

| ⭐ Item | ⛔ Not in our control |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **GBP API quota** | ⭐ **zero by default · 60-day verified GBP · weeks of approval** *(§32.1.1)* — ⛔ **start it NOW, and Zernio is the hedge** |
| ⭐ **10DLC brand + campaign** | days to weeks — ⭐ **X-188's pool is the hedge** |
| **PCI DSS L1** | ⭐ Accept.js means nothing waits *(§46.3)* |
| ⭐ **The content pack** | ⭐⭐ **parallel, separate project** *(§52.5)* |

⭐⭐ **Every one of those has a hedge already built.** ⛔ *That was deliberate, and
it's why none of them can stop the build.*

## 83.3 ⭐ THE WAVES — B2

| Wave | ⭐ Builds | ⭐⭐ Gate to exit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **0** | ⭐ **the spine, SQ-0 alone** | ⛔ **12 entities · registry format · bus · gate all runtime-proven** |
| **1** | channels · intelligence · data · pixel | each emits a real artifact |
| **2** | surfaces · builder · CRM · ⭐ **FSM (X-163 first)** | ⭐ pricebook read by 4 consumers |
| **3** | SEO · reviews · social · money · ⭐⭐ **acquisition** | end-to-end: ⭐ **a real job, invoiced, attributed** |
| ⭐⭐ **4** | ⛔ **NOTHING — V2–V6 only** | ⭐⭐ **all six sweeps clean** |
| ⭐ **5** | ⭐ **launch** | ⭐⭐ **the 12 items of §43.11 green** |

⭐⭐ **A wave doesn't end on a date. It ends on its gate** — ⛔ *which is why the
date is derived.*

## 83.4 ⭐⭐ THE PARALLELISM CEILING

⛔ **60 agents does not mean 60× speed.**

| ⭐ Constraint | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Wave 0 is one squad** | ⛔ *the other 56 write manifests — necessary, but not throughput* |
| ⭐ **The critical path is serial** | ⭐⭐ **pricebook → estimates → memberships → costing cannot compress** |
| ⭐ **Wardens are a merge bottleneck** | by design |
| ⭐⭐ **Wave 4 is build-frozen** | ⛔ *zero build throughput, deliberately* |

⭐⭐ **Honest expectation: the graph's critical path sets the floor, and no amount
of agents beats it.** ⭐ *What 60 agents buy is that everything OFF the critical
path is free.*

## 83.5 ⭐ WHAT B1–B2 OUTPUT

```
  ⭐ DEPENDENCY-GRAPH.json      every module, its edges, its wave
  ⭐⭐ BUILD-STATE.json seeded    250 rows, ⭐ NOT_STARTED, ⭐⭐ blocked-by populated
  WAVES.md                     the six, with their exit gates
```

⭐⭐ **`BUILD-STATE.json` seeded from the graph is the deliverable that makes
§53.3 real** — ⭐ *every `blocks` and `blocked_by` field filled from the manifests,
so `resume` can name the next unblocked item on day one.*

## 83.6 ACCEPTANCE — B1–B2

☐ ⭐⭐ **The date is DERIVED from the graph** — ⛔ *any date named before it is a guess*
☐ ⭐ Graph generated from manifests, ⛔ **never drawn by hand**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Critical path identified: spine → pricebook → the FSM chain**
☐ ⚠️ ⭐ **Non-code items named, ⭐⭐ each with its hedge already built**
☐ ⭐ Six waves, each ending on a **gate, not a date**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Wave 4 build-frozen**
☐ ⛔ **Parallelism ceiling stated honestly — 60 agents ≠ 60× speed**
☐ ⭐⭐ **`BUILD-STATE.json` seeded with 250 rows and their blockers**

**All eight ✅ — B1–B2 EXECUTED.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §85 · ⭐⭐ THE OUTSIDE READ — ANSWERED HONESTLY  *(T547)*
⭐ **An external review of the plan. Three of four criticisms were right.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 85.0 ⭐ THE STATUS PORTION WAS STALE

⭐ **It read 37 of 48 with A2 next.** ⭐⭐ **Actual: 49 of 49, 250 modules, all
eight phases closed.** ⛔ *A2, A3, A4, W1–W3, H1 and B1–B4 all landed after that
snapshot.*

⭐⭐ **But the criticisms don't depend on the count — and three of the four
were correct.**

## 85.1 ⭐⭐ CRITICISM 1 — FILE SIZE AND NOISE · ⭐ **RIGHT, AND WORSE THAN STATED**

⭐ **I ran the audit rather than defending** *(law 71)*, and it found more than the
review claimed:

| ⛔ Found | ⭐ Fixed |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **The tracker was 859KB — LARGER than the plan** | ⭐ **rebuilt to 177KB** |
| ⭐ **§16 genuinely duplicated** *(same root cause as §33's X-157)* | ⭐ deduped |
| ⛔ **"MODULE COUNT — 240"** | ⭐ **250** |
| ⛔ **"THE 46 TURNS"** | ⭐ **49** |
| ⛔ **Five conflicting turn counts**, incl. a garbled *"412 of 41"* | ⭐ one |
| ⛔ **22 rows with ☐ beside ✅ DONE** | ⭐ cleared |
| ⛔ **2 conflicting NEXT markers** | ⭐ zero |

⭐⭐ **Root cause, named:** ⛔ *my string-replace edits either matched in more than
one place or silently failed when the target had drifted, leaving stale copies
behind.* ⭐ **Same class as the X-157 collision, and the same lesson: a generated
register beats a remembered one.**

⚠️ ⭐ **The size point is half-answered by design:** ⭐⭐ **the plan never goes to
Antigravity whole** — it's split into skills that load on relevance *(§52.1, and
Rules are capped at 12k characters anyway)*. ⛔ **But the hygiene failure was real
and it's now fixed.**

## 85.2 ⭐⭐⭐ CRITICISM 2 — PLAN VS REALITY · ⭐⭐ **THE SHARPEST POINT ANYONE HAS MADE**

> ⭐⭐ *"The verification sweeps were run against the specification. The historical
> failure mode was green tests and confident documentation over non-running
> systems. That risk has not been retired; it has only been postponed."*

⛔⛔ **Fully conceded. This is exactly right and it deserves to be written into
the plan rather than argued with.**

| ⭐ What V1–V6 actually did | ⛔ What they did NOT do |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Defined the method** | ⛔ **verify anything** |
| ⭐ Named the evidence ladder | ⛔ produce a single artifact |
| ⭐ Identified QA-2 as the role that catches the 126 | ⛔ run QA-2 |

⭐⭐ **The plan says "assume nothing works" — and no sweep has run, because there
is no code.** ⛔ *A document that specifies rigour is not the same as a system
that has passed it, and the distinction is precisely the one that killed five
prior attempts.*

⭐ **What actually retires the risk:** ⭐⭐ **wave 0's exit gate — twelve entities,
the registry, the bus and the gate all runtime-proven with real artifacts before
wave 1 starts** *(§83.3)*. ⛔ **Until that gate is passed, the plan's confidence
is unearned and should be read that way.**

⭐ **→ Recorded as LAW 103.**

## 85.3 ⭐⭐ CRITICISM 3 — SURFACE AREA · ⭐ **RIGHT, WITH ONE MITIGATION IT MISSED**

> ⭐ *"250 modules remains extreme. Most all-in-ones die from this, not from weak
> architecture."*

⭐⭐ **True, and worth taking seriously rather than defending.**

⭐ **The mitigation it didn't see:** ⭐⭐ **launch is gated on §43.11's TWELVE
items, not on 250 modules.** ⛔ *Everything else is "also built" — so the surface
area threatens the schedule, not the launch decision.*

⚠️ ⭐ **But the honest half:** ⭐⭐ **nothing in the plan forces a smaller
first release**, and 250 modules is 250 modules to operate, support and keep
correct. ⛔ *The one-build law protects coherence and does nothing for load.*

⭐ **The real mitigations, stated plainly:** ⭐⭐ **the twelve-item launch gate ·
the wave gates · degrade-never-fail on every provider · one pager surface · and
EXPLAIN as the substitute for a second human at 3am.** ⛔ **If those don't hold,
the review's warning is what happens.**

## 85.4 ⭐⭐ CRITICISM 4 — ARTIFACTS OVER MODULES · ⭐ **RIGHT, AND IT CHANGES THE BUILD ORDER**

> ⭐ *"A working demo site, a measured report, and a video shown to a real prospect
> will surface more truth than another round of module authoring."*

⭐⭐ **Agreed — and it has a concrete consequence I'm adopting:**

| ⭐ Artifact | Needs | ⭐⭐ Earliest wave |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **The AUDIT REPORT** | ⭐ **crawl + inspection + scoring only** | ⭐⭐ **WAVE 1 — far earlier than planned** |
| The demo site | crawl · matcher · builder · agent · Fact | wave 2 |
| The video | the demo site + TTS | wave 2 |

⭐⭐ **The audit is testable long before the demo site is** — ⭐ *and it can be shown
to a real business owner in wave 1 to find out whether the findings actually land.*

⛔ **Moved from wave 3 to wave 1.** ⭐⭐ *External truth beats another module.*

⭐ **→ Recorded as LAW 104.**

## 85.5 ⭐ THE BOTTOM LINE, ACCEPTED

> ⭐⭐ *"It is still a blueprint."*

⭐ **Correct. And the right response is not to argue but to name what would change
that:** ⭐⭐ **wave 0's gate passed with real artifacts, and an audit report in
front of a real prospect.** ⛔ *Until then, everything here is a well-reasoned
document that has never met a running system.*

## 85.6 ACCEPTANCE — §85

☐ ⭐ Stale status corrected — **49 of 49**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Noise audit run, ⛔ worse than claimed, ⭐ all seven defects fixed**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Tracker rebuilt 859KB → 177KB**
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **Criticism 2 fully conceded — ⛔ the sweeps verified nothing, and the risk is postponed not retired** → **LAW 103**
☐ ⭐ Surface-area risk accepted; ⭐⭐ **the twelve-item launch gate named as the real mitigation**
☐ ⭐⭐ **The audit report moved WAVE 3 → WAVE 1** → **LAW 104**
☐ ⭐ *"It is still a blueprint"* — accepted, with what would change it

**All seven ✅ — §85 COMPLETE.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════

> **🗄️ HISTORICAL — PRECEDENCE (T667, §0.A):** F2 matrix at 255 — the METHOD is live (X-128); the instance is stale. *Nothing here is deleted (law 10); read §0.A before treating this section as current.*

## 89.0 ⭐⭐ WHAT "INTEGRATED" ACTUALLY MEANS

⛔ **Not "the modules exist."** ⭐ **Four things, each of which a script can check:**

| ⭐ | ⭐⭐ Checkable claim |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **1** | ⭐⭐ **Every module's entities are among the twelve** — ⛔ *no private nouns* |
| ⭐ **2** | ⭐⭐ **Every action is reachable from ≥1 declared surface** |
| ⭐ **3** | ⭐⭐ **Every event has an emitter AND a subscriber** — ⛔ *or a written `broadcast` reason* |
| ⭐ **4** | ⭐⭐⭐ **Every seam has all four fields, ⛔ invalidation included** |

## 89.1 ⭐⭐ THE SEAM MATRIX — THE SIX THAT CANNOT LAG

⭐ **Inline, same transaction, tested at +0ms** *(§66.2)*:

| Producer → Consumer | ⭐⭐ Invalidation rule |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **X-163 PriceBook → C-Agent** | ⭐ **version bump kills the Fact, same txn** — ⛔ *else the agent quotes a dead price on a live call* |
| ⭐ **X-103 publish → X-119 Fact** | `source_version` bump, same txn |
| ⭐ **X-163 → X-164 Estimate** | estimate freezes the version it was sold at |
| ⭐⭐ **suppression → all sending** | ⛔ **immediate** — *a message to someone who said stop* |
| ⭐ **X-146 register off → consulted** | ⭐ **off means off, now** |
| ⭐⭐ **X-108 availability → agent offer** | ⛔ **a window promised must be keepable** |

## 89.2 ⭐ THE ASYNC SEAMS — ARRIVE, ONCE, IN ORDER

| Producer → Consumer | ⭐ Carries |
| :--- | :--- |
| `job.completed` → ⭐⭐ **eight subscribers** | invoice · review invite · CRM · SEO proof · attribution · commission · inventory · timesheet |
| ⭐ `review.received` → four | case study · ROI · proof harvest · celebration |
| ⭐ **`call.missed` → text-back** | ⭐⭐ **fires on the RING, not the carrier timeout** |
| `payment.received` → attribution | ⭐ **closes the graph** |
| ⭐ `form.handler_failed` → alert | ⭐⭐ *"your form broke, here are the 9 leads"* |
| ⭐ `agent.refused` → EXPLAIN + grounding ladder | ⭐ **a refusal is a product signal** |
| `visit.identified` → back-attribution | prior anonymous visits |
| ⭐ `video.watched` → ladder advance | 50% · 80% · shared |
| ⭐⭐ **`partner.link_removed` → the 30-day ladder** | §75.5 |
| `qa.resolved` → fix-then-ask | *(off by default)* |

## 89.3 ⭐⭐ THE CROSS-CUTTING SPINES — WHERE INTEGRATION REALLY LIVES

⭐ **Five things every module touches. ⛔ Get one wrong and 90 modules are wrong
together:**

| ⭐ Spine | ⭐⭐ Every module must |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **`business_id` + RLS** | ⛔ **both walls, set together** *(§11.10)* |
| ⭐ **`ActionInvocation`** | ⭐⭐ **write before/after — or undo and EXPLAIN both fail silently** |
| ⭐ **The meters** | ⭐⭐ **AI credits ALWAYS, channel meter additionally** *(§18E.1)* |
| ⭐⭐ **`Fact` + `source_version`** | anything the agent may say aloud |
| ⭐ **`notification_class`** | ⭐⭐ **account-class can never be unsubscribed** *(§17.1)* |

⭐⭐ **These five are the integration.** ⛔ *The seams are pairwise and visible; the
spines are everywhere and invisible — which is why they're the ones that fail.*

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §90 · ⛔⛔ THE AUDIT DISPOSITION — WHAT THE REWRITE DROPPED  *(T552)*
⭐ **Grok was right. Three hard properties were lost. Here they are back.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 90.0 ⭐ I RAN THE GREP RATHER THAN DEFENDING

| ⭐ Property | Hits in the plan | ⛔ Verdict |
| :--- | ---: | :--- |
| ⛔ **`SendPermit`** | **0** | ⭐⭐ **LOST** |
| ⛔ **"insight-only" identity** | **0** | ⭐ **preserved under another name — see 90.2** |
| ⛔ **Closed refusal set** | **0** | ⭐⭐ **LOST** |
| ⚠️ **Quiet hours** | 1 | ⭐ **barely present** |
| ⛔ **Audit disposition** | **0** | ⭐⭐ **never written** |
| ⚠️ **Queue worker** | 1 | ⭐ **the entry point, not concrete** |

⭐⭐ **The kill list declared old rulings void without recording which findings
they had resolved** — ⛔ *so the resolutions went with them. That's the mechanism
that lost these, and it's worth naming.*

## 90.1 ⭐⭐ RESTORED — `SendPermit` *(→ X-126 `CapabilityGate`)*

⛔ **`ActionInvocation` records what happened. It does not gate whether it may
happen.** ⭐ **Those are different objects and I collapsed them.**

```
  ⭐⭐ SendPermit — immutable, minted BEFORE any outbound send
     person_id · channel · ⭐ basis         ← WHY we may contact them
     ⭐⭐ basis_evidence                      ← the Message/Job/Form that proves it
     minted_at · minted_by · expires_at
     ⛔ NO permit ⇒ NO send. Not a check — an ABSENCE of the ability.
```

| ⭐ Valid basis | ⛔ Never a basis |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **They contacted us** *(call · text · form · chat · review)* | ⛔ **a pixel match** |
| ⭐ **An existing job or invoice** | ⛔ **an enrichment record** |
| ⭐ **A confirmed partnership** *(X-190)* | ⛔ **a scraped list** |
| **Their own act** *(§11.2)* | ⛔ **inference of any kind** |

⭐⭐ **And it makes EXPLAIN exact:** ⭐ *"we texted her because she submitted your
quote form on the 4th"* — ⛔ *not "because the system decided to."*

## 90.2 ⭐⭐ NOT LOST — INSIGHT-ONLY IDENTITY IS §11.2 UNDER ANOTHER NAME

⭐ **R88 said the pixel pool can never mint a SendPermit.** ⭐⭐ **§11.2 says:**

> ⭐⭐ *"`PROSPECT → CONTACT` happens only by the person's own act — never by
> import, never by enrichment, never by a pixel match."*

⭐ **Same property, different vocabulary** — ⛔ *which is exactly why Grok couldn't
find it, and exactly why it needed naming.*

⭐⭐ **→ LAW 107: pixel and enrichment data are INSIGHT ONLY. They may inform a
score, a list or an alert. ⛔ They may never mint a SendPermit.**

## 90.3 ⭐⭐ RESTORED — THE CLOSED REFUSAL SET

⛔ **An open set of refusal reasons drifts, and EXPLAIN degrades into free text.**

⭐ **Twenty, closed. A new one requires the Contract Warden** *(§12.9)*:

| ⭐ Group | Reasons |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Permission** | no permit · basis expired · ⛔ **STOP received** · class unsubscribed · minor rejected |
| ⭐ **Grounding** | no fact · ⭐ **SAMPLE price** · price version stale · no availability |
| **Capability** | skill ungrounded · action not permitted · tenant paused |
| **Resource** | meter empty and top-up failed · provider down · rate limited |
| ⭐ **Data** | no phone · no email · invalid number · duplicate suppressed |
| **Timing** | outside alert hours · ⭐ **quiet hours** · pacing cap |

⭐⭐ **Every refusal is one of these twenty, logged with its code** *(§14.1)* —
⛔ *and a refusal with no code fails the build.*

## 90.4 ⭐⭐ THE FIVE ENTRY POINTS — MADE CONCRETE

⭐ **§62 gave the sweep METHOD. Grok's point stands: the five specific
starters were never re-specified. Here they are:**

| # | ⭐ Entry point | ⭐⭐ The concrete artifact |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **1** | **Voice webhook** | ⭐⭐ **`POST /webhooks/voice/{provider}` → emits `call.ringing` then `call.missed` ON THE RING** *(§13.3)*. ⛔ **Runtime proof: a real inbound call producing a row** |
| ⭐⭐ **2** | **Scheduler + worker** | ⭐ **deploy asserts a running queue worker AND a cron tick.** ⛔ **Wave-0 gate: a scheduled job observed executing — ⭐ not "configured"** |
| ⭐ **3** | **Agent dispatcher** | ⭐⭐ **`message.received` → dispatcher → `agent.turn.answer`.** ⛔ *Message stored with no agent turn = the defect* |
| ⭐ **4** | **Voicemail** | ⭐ producer *(carrier callback)* **and** consumer *(writes a `Message` with recording + transcript on the same `Conversation`)* |
| ⭐⭐ **5** | **Wizard honesty** | ⛔ **"Done" is FALSE until a real send has succeeded.** ⭐ *A wizard that says done while the tenant can't send is the original sin* |

⭐⭐ **All five are wave-0 exit criteria** *(§83.3)* — ⛔ *not wave 1, because
nothing downstream works without them.*

## 90.5 ⭐ THE OTHER SOFTENED PROPERTIES

| ⭐ Property | ⭐⭐ Restored as |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **STOP is absolute** | ⛔ **LAW 108 — STOP is honoured immediately, on every channel, for that tenant, permanently, and NO setting overrides it.** *A refusal code exists for it (§90.3)* |
| ⭐ **Quiet hours as a floor** | ⭐⭐ **LAW 109 — a jurisdictional floor the tenant may narrow, ⛔ never widen.** *§20.2's per-class hours sit INSIDE it* |
| ⭐ **Agent invents nothing** | ⭐ already law *(§16.2)* — ⭐⭐ **reaffirmed and cross-linked** |

## 90.6 ⭐⭐ THE REGISTER IS A MINE, NOT A COMMITMENT LIST

⭐ **Grok's framing is right and §87 didn't say it plainly enough:**

> ⭐⭐ **826 lines are MAPPED. That is not the same as 826 lines COMMITTED.**

⭐ **A mapped line means "a section covers this territory."** ⛔ *It does not mean
every capability on that line ships.* ⭐⭐ **Drain the good ones into modules; park
the rest without guilt** — ⛔ *many are speculative or expensive, and treating 905
as a build list is how scope explodes.*

## 90.7 ⭐ R91 — CARD STORAGE, SETTLED

⭐⭐ **R91 STANDS. This is the instruction, not a question.**

| ⭐ Rule | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **PAN + expiry ARE stored** | in **X-120 `CardVault`** |
| ⛔⛔ **CVV is NEVER stored** | ⭐ **enforced by a build-failing migration grep** — *not a policy, a test* |
| **Encryption** | envelope, AES-256-GCM, ⭐ **network-segmented** |
| **Default write path** | ⭐ **Accept.js `opaqueData`** — the vault engages only where card-on-file is the point |
| ⭐ **Compliance posture** | **PCI DSS Level 1** |
| ⛔ **Never in the graph** | ⭐⭐ **card data is never a `PersonIdentity` and never a `Fact`** *(§23.3 rule 2)* |
| **Consent** | recorded per card, revocable from the customer portal |

⭐ **Uses:** memberships · repeat customers · deposits on file · ⭐ **the
pay-on-completion tap at the door.**

⛔ **Build it as specified. There is no alternative path to weigh.**

## 90.8 ACCEPTANCE — §90

☐ ⭐ Grep run; ⛔ **three properties confirmed lost**
☐ ⭐⭐ **`SendPermit` restored — ⛔ no permit, no send, and it's an absence not a check**
☐ ⭐ Insight-only shown to be §11.2 — ⭐⭐ **named as LAW 107 so it can't hide again**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Closed refusal set restored — 20, warden-governed**
☐ ⭐⭐ **The five entry points made concrete, all wave-0 exit criteria**
☐ ⭐ **LAW 108 STOP absolute · LAW 109 quiet hours as a floor**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Register reframed: mapped ≠ committed**
☐ ⭐ **R91 settled — ⛔ PAN + expiry stored, CVV never, PCI L1. No open question**

**All eight ✅ — §90 COMPLETE.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §91 · ⭐⭐ AGENCY BILLING — THREE MODES, SET PER CLIENT  *(owner, T555)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 91.1 ⭐ CONFIRMED, UNCHANGED

| ⭐ | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Affiliate** | **40% of subscription, ⛔ nothing on usage** — ⭐ **paid as long as the client pays and doesn't leave** |
| ⭐⭐ **Agency platform** | **$497/month, unlimited tenants** |
| ⭐ **Agency usage discount** | **40% off** SMS · AI · lead credits |
| ⭐ **Agency voice discount** | **25% off** *(voice is near cost)* |

## 91.2 ⭐⭐ THREE BILLING MODES — CHOSEN PER CLIENT, NOT PER AGENCY

⛔ **An agency doesn't run every client the same way.** ⭐⭐ **So the mode is a
per-sub-account setting:**

| Mode | ⭐ Who pays usage | ⭐⭐ Who gets the discount |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **AGENCY_PAYS** | ⭐ **the agency's card** — all services, all clients | ⭐⭐ **the agency.** *They mark it up however they like, or absorb it* |
| ⭐ **CLIENT_PAYS** | ⭐ **the client's own card**, direct | ⭐⭐ **the agency — as a rebate on their next invoice** |
| ⭐ **SPLIT** | ⭐⭐ **agency covers the included allowance; client pays their own top-ups** | agency on the base, ⭐ **rebate on the top-ups** |

⭐⭐ **The discount belongs to the agency in every mode** — ⛔ *they brought the
client, so the margin follows them whether or not they front the cash.*

⭐ **CLIENT_PAYS is the mode for an agency that only wants to charge for their
service** — ⛔ *no float, no collection risk, and the rebate still arrives.*

## 91.3 ⭐⭐ NO PRE-FILLED CREDIT ON AGENCY SUB-ACCOUNTS

⛔ **A direct signup gets the included allowance** *(500 SMS · $50 AI · 100 voice
min · 10k leads)*. ⭐⭐ **An agency sub-account gets ZERO by default.**

| ⭐ Why | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **The agency decides what a client gets** | ⛔ *it's their product and their pricing* |
| ⭐ **We'd otherwise fund every sub-account they create** | ⛔ **unlimited tenants × a free allowance is an unlimited bill** |
| ⭐ **They can grant an allowance per client** | ⭐⭐ **from their own balance, in one field** |

⭐ **And it's shown at creation:** ⭐⭐ *"This client starts with no credit. Grant
an allowance, or set them to pay their own."*

## 91.4 ⭐⭐ WHOSE CARD DOES AUTO TOP-UP CHARGE?

⭐ **Auto top-up is universal** *(§17.6)* — ⭐⭐ **so the mode decides the card:**

```
  ⭐ meter empties
       ├─ AGENCY_PAYS ──► ⭐⭐ the AGENCY's card, at the agency rate
       ├─ CLIENT_PAYS ──► ⭐ the CLIENT's card, ⭐⭐ agency rebate accrues
       └─ SPLIT       ──► ⭐ client's card for top-ups, agency for the base
```

⛔ **Nothing stops for want of a balance, in any mode** *(§17.6)* — ⭐ **the
question is only whose card is charged.**

## 91.5 ⛔⛔ THE FAILURE CASE THAT MATTERS — THE AGENCY'S CARD FAILS

⭐ **An agency card failing must not take 30 businesses off the air.**

| ⭐ Rule | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **The agency runs the standard dunning timeline** *(§45A)* | 21 days, day-7 human call |
| ⭐⭐ **Clients keep working throughout** | ⛔ **their customers did nothing wrong** *(§45A.3's logic, applied one level up)* |
| ⭐ **At day 21** | ⭐⭐ **agency marketing pauses. ⛔ Client phones keep answering** |
| ⭐ **At day 30** | ⭐⭐ **clients are offered direct billing** — *"your agency's account lapsed; keep your number and your data by paying directly"* |
| ⛔ **Never** | ⭐⭐ **a client's data deleted because their agency stopped paying** |

⭐⭐ **That day-30 offer is both the honest thing and the commercially right
thing** — ⛔ *the alternative is 30 local businesses losing their phone system
over an invoice they never saw.*

## 91.6 ACCEPTANCE — §91

☐ ⭐ Affiliate confirmed: **40% of subscription, ⛔ nothing on usage, while they pay**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Three billing modes, set PER CLIENT** — agency pays · client pays · split
☐ ⭐⭐ **The discount belongs to the agency in every mode** *(rebate when the client pays)*
☐ ⭐⭐ **Agency sub-accounts start with ZERO credit** — ⛔ *unlimited tenants × a free allowance is an unlimited bill*
☐ ⭐ Allowance grantable per client from the agency's balance
☐ ⭐ Auto top-up charges the card the mode names; ⛔ **nothing ever stops**
☐ ⛔⛔ **An agency card failure never takes clients off the air** — ⭐⭐ **day-30 direct-billing offer, ⛔ never deletion**

**All seven ✅ — §91 COMPLETE.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §92 · ⭐⭐ CURRENCY & COUNTRY  *(owner, T556)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 92.1 ⭐⭐ USD IS THE BASE. ALWAYS. EVERYTHING ELSE IS DERIVED.

| ⭐ Rule | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Every rate in the registry is USD** | ⛔ **there is no second price list** |
| ⭐ **A local-currency charge is a CONVERSION** | ⭐⭐ **derived at billing time, ⛔ never stored as a price** |
| ⛔ **A converted figure never becomes the source of truth** | ⭐ *that's how two prices drift apart* |
| ⭐ **Minor units, integers, both sides** | *(§11.11)* |

## 92.2 ⭐⭐ THE BILL MUST SHOW THE CONVERSION — ALWAYS

```
  ⭐ Subscription        $149.00 USD
     ⭐⭐ Exchange rate    1 USD = 0.7840 GBP   ⭐ (locked 1 Mar 2026)
     ⭐ Charged           £116.82 GBP
```

⛔ **Four things on every invoice, every time:** ⭐ **the USD amount · the rate ·
the date the rate was locked · the converted total.**

⭐⭐ **A tenant who can't reconstruct their own bill doesn't trust it** — ⛔ *and a
converted charge with no rate shown looks like a price change.*

## 92.3 ⭐⭐ THE RATE IS LOCKED PER PERIOD, NOT SPOT

| ⭐ Rule | ⛔ Why |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Locked at the start of the billing period** | ⛔ *a spot rate makes the same invoice irreproducible an hour later* |
| ⭐ **Stored on the `LedgerEntry`** | ⭐⭐ **so a historic invoice re-renders identically, forever** |
| ⛔ **Historic invoices are NEVER re-converted** | ⭐ *the rate that was charged is the rate that shows* |
| ⭐ **Source and timestamp recorded** | which feed, which moment |

## 92.4 ⭐⭐ THE HONESTY PROBLEM — AND HOW WE SAY IT

⛔ **"Pricing never changes"** *(§17.4 D6)* **is a USD promise.** ⭐ **If FX moves,
their local bill moves — and that looks like we broke it.**

⭐⭐ **So the invoice says it plainly, before they ask:**

> ⭐⭐ *"Your price hasn't changed — it's **$149**, the same as the day you joined.
> Your bank was charged **£116.82** this month because the exchange rate moved
> from 0.7690 to 0.7840."*

⭐ **One sentence, and it converts a support ticket into a non-event.**

## 92.5 ⭐⭐ COUNTRY FIELDS — EVERYWHERE, INCLUDING THE PIXEL

| Entity | ⭐ Country field |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **`Business`** | country of registration · ⭐⭐ **billing currency** |
| ⭐ **`Location`** | country · region · ⭐ **postcode format** |
| ⭐ **`Person`** | derived from their identities |
| ⭐⭐ **`PersonIdentity`** | ⭐ **phone country code — ⛔ E.164, always** |
| ⭐⭐ **`Visit`** *(the pixel)* | ⭐⭐ **country + region from IP** — see 92.6 |
| ⭐⭐ **`Message`** | ⭐ **DESTINATION country — ⛔ this one is billing-critical** |
| ⭐ **`Job`** | service country *(may differ from billing)* |
| ⭐ **`LedgerEntry`** | ⭐⭐ **currency · USD amount · rate · rate date** |
| **Pricebook** | currency per zone *(§30.2)* |

## 92.6 ⭐⭐ WHY THE PIXEL NEEDS COUNTRY

⛔ **Not a nice-to-have. Five things depend on it:**

| ⭐ | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **1** | ⭐ **SMS cost varies hugely by destination country** — *a lead in one country costs a different amount to text than a lead in another* |
| ⭐ **2** | ⭐⭐ **The demand index is per-region** *(§20.5)* — ⛔ *without country the fleet counters are meaningless* |
| ⭐ **3** | **Locale selection** — language, spelling, units, emergency number |
| ⭐ **4** | ⭐⭐ **Phone validation and formatting** — ⛔ *E.164 needs the country to parse* |
| ⭐ **5** | ⭐ **AI-visibility queries run from the tenant's geography** *(§32.4)* |

## 92.7 ⭐⭐ THE METER CONSEQUENCE — COST VARIES BY DESTINATION

⛔ **A flat "1 SMS = 1 credit" is wrong once a tenant texts across borders.**

| ⭐ Rule | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **The meter debits by DESTINATION country rate** | ⭐ **from the registry, per country** |
| ⭐ **The panel shows it** | *"most of your messages went to one country; 12 went abroad and cost more"* |
| ⛔ **Never a surprise** | ⭐⭐ **an international send is priced before it goes, not after** |
| ⭐ **Voice the same** | per-destination minute rates |

⭐⭐ **This is the same principle as everything else in the money model: ⭐ the
meter matches the actual cost, which is why the bill can be explained** *(§65.3)*.

## 92.8 ACCEPTANCE — §92

☐ ⭐⭐ **USD is the base; ⛔ a converted figure is NEVER a stored price**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Every invoice shows USD · rate · rate date · converted total**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Rate locked per period and stored on the `LedgerEntry`** — ⛔ **historic invoices never re-convert**
☐ ⭐⭐ **The FX sentence on the invoice** — ⭐ *"your price hasn't changed"*
☐ ⭐ Country fields on `Business` · `Location` · `PersonIdentity` · ⭐⭐ **`Visit`** · `Message` · `Job` · `LedgerEntry`
☐ ⭐⭐ **Phone numbers are E.164 with a country code, always**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Meters debit by DESTINATION country rate** — ⛔ **international sends priced before they go**

**All seven ✅ — §92 COMPLETE.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §93 · ⭐⭐ PER-COUNTRY RATES — WHAT VARIES, WHAT DOESN'T  *(owner, T557)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 93.1 ⭐⭐ THE SPLIT — AND IT'S A CLEAN ONE

| ⭐ Meter | ⭐⭐ Varies by country? | ⛔ Why |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **SMS / MMS / RCS** | ⭐ **YES — admin-configured per country** | *carriers charge us differently everywhere* |
| ⭐⭐ **Voice minutes** | ⭐ **YES — admin-configured per country** | *termination rates vary enormously* |
| ⭐ **AI credits** | ⛔ **NO — same everywhere** | ⭐⭐ *a token costs the same from any country* |
| ⭐ **Email** | ⛔ **NO — same everywhere** | ⭐ *an ESP send has no destination premium* |
| ⭐ **Lead credits** | ⛔ **NO — same everywhere** | ⭐ *our fetch cost doesn't move with the lead's country* |
| ⭐ **Number rental** | ⛔ **NO — same everywhere** | ⭐⭐ *one price per number, whatever the country* |

⭐⭐ **The rule underneath it:** ⭐ **a meter varies by country only where OUR cost
varies by country.** ⛔ *Anything else would be charging for geography we don't
pay for.*

## 93.2 ⭐ THE ADMIN SURFACE

⭐ **A rate table in the registry, editable without a deploy** *(§45.1)*:

```
  ⭐ country_rates
     country · meter · ⭐⭐ our_cost · retail_rate · effective_from
     ⛔ USD base, minor units, integers (§92.1)
```

| ⭐ Rule | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Admin-set, per country, per meter** | SMS · MMS · RCS · voice |
| ⭐ **A default rate covers unlisted countries** | ⛔ *never a failed send for want of a row* |
| ⭐⭐ **`our_cost` recorded alongside retail** | ⭐ **so margin per country is visible, not inferred** |
| ⭐ **`effective_from` dated** | ⛔ **historic messages keep the rate they were charged at** *(§92.3)* |
| ⭐⭐ **A rate change never applies backwards** | |

## 93.3 ⭐⭐ WHAT THE TENANT SEES — BEFORE, NOT AFTER

⛔ **A per-country rate is only fair if it's visible before the send.**

| ⭐ Surface | ⭐⭐ Shows |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Composing a message** | ⭐⭐ *"this goes to 3 countries — 40 at the standard rate, 12 at a higher one"* |
| ⭐ **The meter panel** | usage split by destination country |
| ⭐⭐ **Before a campaign sends** | ⭐ **the estimated cost, by country, ⛔ before the send button** |
| ⭐ **The statement** | ⭐⭐ **a line per country, not one lump** |

⭐⭐ **And EXPLAIN can answer it** *(§65.3)*: ⭐ *"that campaign cost more because
14 of the 52 recipients were abroad."*

## 93.4 ⭐ WHAT THIS DOESN'T CHANGE

☐ ⭐⭐ **The subscription price never changes** *(§17.4 D6)* — ⛔ *per-country rates
are USAGE, not the plan*
☐ ⭐ **AI stays at 8:1 everywhere** *(§17.6)*
☐ ⭐⭐ **USD stays the base** — ⭐ *a per-country rate is a USD rate, converted like
everything else* *(§92.1)*
☐ ⭐ **Auto top-up still universal** — ⛔ **nothing stops for a costly destination**
☐ ⭐⭐ **The agency discounts still apply** — 40% usage, ⭐ **25% voice, on whatever
the country rate is**

## 93.5 ACCEPTANCE — §93

☐ ⭐⭐ **SMS and voice vary by country; ⛔ AI, email, leads and number rental do NOT**
☐ ⭐ **The rule: a meter varies only where OUR cost varies**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Admin rate table per country per meter, no deploy**
☐ ⭐ **A default rate covers unlisted countries** — ⛔ *never a failed send*
☐ ⭐⭐ **`our_cost` stored beside retail — margin per country visible**
☐ ⭐ **`effective_from` dated; ⛔ rate changes never apply backwards**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Cost shown BEFORE the send, split by country, on the statement**

**All seven ✅ — §93 COMPLETE.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §94 · ⭐⭐ PER-COUNTRY ALLOWANCES  *(owner, T558)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 94.0 ⭐ WHY IT FOLLOWS FROM §93

⛔ **If SMS costs 4× more in one country and the allowance is a fixed 500, the
included bundle costs us 4× more there.** ⭐⭐ **Same plan price, wildly different
cost of goods.**

⭐ **So the allowance varies by country — but ⭐⭐ the PLAN PRICE does not**
*(§17.4 D6)*.

## 94.1 ⭐⭐ VALUE INSIDE, COUNT OUTSIDE

> ⭐⭐ **The admin sets a VALUE. The tenant sees a COUNT.**

```
  ⭐⭐ ADMIN SETS:   included messaging value = $X
                    included voice value     = $Y
       │
  ⭐ SYSTEM DERIVES per country, from the §93 rate table
       │
  ⭐⭐ TENANT SEES:  "500 texts and 100 voice minutes included"
                    ⛔ never "$X of messaging value"
```

| ⭐ Why this shape | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Our cost of goods is constant everywhere** | ⛔ *that's the whole point* |
| ⭐ **"500 texts" is comprehensible** | ⛔ *"$12.50 of messaging value" is not* |
| ⭐⭐ **A rate change re-derives the count automatically** | ⭐ **no manual table of 200 countries** |
| ⭐ **One number to tune, not hundreds** | |

## 94.2 ⭐ WHAT STAYS FIXED EVERYWHERE

| ⭐ Fixed | ⭐⭐ Varies by country |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **The plan price** | ⭐ **SMS / MMS / RCS allowance** |
| ⭐ **AI credit allowance** *($50)* | ⭐ **voice minute allowance** |
| ⭐ **Lead credit allowance** *(10k)* | |
| ⭐ **Email allowance** | |
| ⭐ **Number rental** | |
| ⭐⭐ **The 8:1 AI markup** | |

⭐ **Same rule as §93: ⭐⭐ only the meters whose cost varies have an allowance that
varies.**

## 94.3 ⭐⭐ SHOWN AT SIGNUP — NEVER DISCOVERED

⛔ **Two tenants paying the same and getting different allowances must be able to
see why.**

> ⭐⭐ *"Your plan includes **220 texts** and **60 voice minutes** a month.
> ⭐ Messaging costs more to your country than to the US, so the included
> allowance reflects that — **the plan price is the same everywhere.**"*

| ⭐ Rule | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Stated at signup, on the pricing page, per country** | ⛔ *never found later on a meter panel* |
| ⭐ **The reason given in one sentence** | ⛔ *an unexplained smaller allowance reads as a penalty* |
| ⭐⭐ **Top-up rates shown alongside** | so the full picture is one screen |

## 94.4 ⭐ THE MECHANICS

☐ ⭐ **Allowance derived at signup and re-derived when the rate table changes**
☐ ⭐⭐ **An existing tenant's allowance never DROPS mid-term** — ⛔ *a rate rise
takes effect at renewal, with notice*
☐ ⭐ **A rise in allowance applies immediately** *(good news needs no notice)*
☐ ⭐⭐ **The derived count is stored on the subscription**, so a bill re-renders
identically *(§92.3)*
☐ ⭐ **Agency sub-accounts still start at zero** *(§91.3)* — ⭐⭐ **the derivation
governs what a granted allowance costs the agency**

## 94.5 ACCEPTANCE — §94

☐ ⭐⭐ **Allowance varies by country; ⛔ the PLAN PRICE never does**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Value set by admin, count derived per country, ⛔ count is what the tenant sees**
☐ ⭐ **Only SMS and voice allowances vary** — AI, email, leads, numbers fixed
☐ ⭐⭐ **Stated at signup with the reason**, ⛔ never discovered later
☐ ⭐⭐ **An allowance never drops mid-term** — ⭐ **rises apply immediately**
☐ ⭐ **Derived count stored on the subscription** for reproducible bills

**All six ✅ — §94 COMPLETE.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
> ↪ **§69 lived here** *(restored out of order at T559; re-seated in numeric order at H-5, T675)*

> ↪ **§70 lived here** *(restored out of order at T559; re-seated in numeric order at H-5, T675)*

# §95 · ⭐⭐⭐ THE MODULE CONTRACT  *(T560 — SCALE ARCHITECTURE, 1 of 4)*
⭐ **The code becomes the source of truth. Everything else is generated.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 95.0 ⛔ THE ROOT CAUSE OF EVERY SCALE PROBLEM

**There is no source of truth that is both authoritative and machine-readable.**

| ⭐ Artifact | Authoritative? | Machine-readable? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| The master plan | ⭐ **yes** | ⛔ **no — 800KB of prose** |
| `BUILD-STATE.json` | ⛔ **no — hand-maintained, wrong twice** | ⭐ yes |
| `EXISTING-MAP.md` | ⛔ **no — stale on write** | ⛔ no |
| ⭐⭐ **The code** | ⭐⭐ **YES — it's what runs** | ⛔ **no module identity** |

⭐⭐ **Fix: put module identity IN the code. Generate everything else from it.**
⛔ *A generated map cannot go stale. A hand-written one is stale on write.*

## 95.1 ⭐⭐ WHAT A MODULE IS

> ⭐⭐ **A module is a set of annotated files with a declared public surface — ⛔
> NOT a folder.**

⛔ **Nothing moves.** ⭐ *Moving 102,301 lines to satisfy a directory name is the
highest-risk operation available and it buys a folder.*

## 95.2 ⭐⭐⭐ THE ANNOTATION — `@visibility` IS THE LOAD-BEARING FIELD

```php
/**
 *
 * ⭐⭐ @visibility public          ← public | internal
 * @provides   pricebook.lookup, pricebook.confirm
 * @emits      pricebook.updated
 * @consumes   consent.decide, facts.invalidate
 * ⭐⭐ @owns_table price_book_items, price_book_versions
 * @decisions  2570, T176-P14
 */
```

| Field | ⭐ Purpose |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **`@module`** | binds the file to one of the 90 IDs — ⛔ **exactly one, never two** |
| ⭐⭐ **`@visibility`** | ⭐⭐ **public = the module's API · internal = nobody outside may import it** |
| **`@provides`** | registered actions this file handles |
| **`@emits`** | events it publishes |
| ⭐ **`@consumes`** | ⭐ **what it depends on — the seam, declared** |
| ⭐ **`@decisions`** | ⭐⭐ **legacy decision refs — the *why*, preserved** |

⭐⭐ **Without `@visibility`, `doctor` cannot distinguish a legal call from a
violation** *(Gemini's catch — and it's the reason build check ⑤ has never been
enforceable)*.

### ⛔⛔ 95.2.1 THE TWO BACKDOORS — CLOSED *(Gemini, T561)*

⭐ **`@visibility` locks the front door. Two others were left open:**

| ⛔ Backdoor | ⭐⭐ The fix |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **DATA COUPLING** — ⛔ *`@visibility` stops class imports and does nothing to stop `DB::table('their_table')->update()` or querying their Eloquent model.* **In a modular monolith a cross-module write is as fatal as a cross-module import** | ⭐⭐ **`@owns_table`** — every table belongs to exactly one module. ⛔ **`doctor` flags any query builder or Eloquent call touching a table owned elsewhere.** ⭐ *If A wants B's data, it asks B's public interface* |
| ⭐⭐ **EVENT PAYLOAD LEAKAGE** — ⛔ *an event carrying an internal Eloquent model couples every subscriber to that module's schema. Rename a column and four modules break* | ⭐⭐ **Public events carry primitives or DTOs only.** ⛔ **Never an internal model.** ⭐ `doctor` fails any event class with a model-typed property |

⭐⭐ **Table ownership is the more important of the two**, because ⛔ *a database
write leaves no import to grep for — it's invisible to every class-level check.*

## 95.3 ⭐⭐ THE LEGALITY RULE — FOUR LINES

```
  ⭐ Module A MAY import Module B's @visibility public classes
  ⭐ Module A MAY subscribe to Module B's events            (always legal)
  ⭐ Module A MAY call Module B's registered actions        (always legal)
  ⛔ EVERYTHING ELSE IS A VIOLATION
```

⭐⭐ **Specifically illegal: importing a class marked `@visibility internal` from
another module.** ⛔ *That is the single rule that keeps 400 modules from becoming
one system nobody can hold.*

### ⭐ THE `CORE` EXEMPTION — AND IT'S NECESSARY

⛔ **The twelve entities cannot belong to one module** — everything reads
`Person`, `Fact`, `Conversation`.

| ⭐ `@module CORE` | Universally importable |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **The twelve canonical entities** *(§11.1)* | |
| **Contracts and interfaces** | `SendDriver`, etc. |
| **Enums** | `SendRefusalReason`, `OutreachPurpose` |
| **Value objects** | `SendPermit`, `Identifier` |

⚠️ ⭐ **`CORE` is a privilege, not a dumping ground.** ⭐⭐ **`doctor` reports its
size every run** — ⛔ *if CORE grows, the boundaries are wrong and everything
becomes legal.*

## 95.4 ⭐⭐ HOW 90 IDs BIND TO 102,301 LINES

| ⭐ Rule | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **The annotation is authoritative** | ⛔ **not `EXISTING-MAP.md`, which is retired** |
| ⭐ **One file, one module** | ⛔ **never two** |
| ⭐⭐ **A file serving two modules** | ⛔ **either it's `CORE`, or the boundary is wrong.** ⭐ *Force the decision — don't allow both* |
| ⭐ **No `@module` = ORPHAN** | ⭐⭐ **`doctor` flags it** — *the 126-file check, automated* |
| ⛔ **Never move a file to satisfy a boundary** | ⭐ **annotate it where it lives** |

## 95.5 ⭐⭐⭐ THE THREE HEALTH METRICS — THEY REPLACE LINE COUNT

⛔ **Line count is not a health metric. These are:**

| # | ⭐ Metric | ⭐⭐ Why it's the real ceiling |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **1** | **Context tokens per module** | ⭐⭐ **THE hard limit.** *Under 20k and an agent can work forever; at 200k you've already lost — and that arrives long before a million lines* |
| ⭐ **2** | **Files changed per fix** | ⭐ *One module = healthy at any size. Six modules = trouble at 300k lines* |
| ⭐⭐ **3** | ⭐ **Public surface per module** | ⭐⭐ **the leading indicator.** *40 public classes isn't a module, it's a namespace — and it's the swamp arriving early* |

⭐⭐ **Track all three in `doctor`. ⛔ A module breaching metric 1 or 3 must
split** — *that's the rule that makes 400 modules possible.*

## 95.6 ⭐ WHAT THIS TURN DECIDES

☐ ⭐⭐ **Module identity lives in the code; everything else is generated**
☐ ⭐ A module is annotated files with a declared surface — ⛔ **not a folder, nothing moves**
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **`@visibility` public/internal — the field that makes build check ⑤ enforceable**
☐ ⭐ Four-line legality rule; ⛔ **internal imports across modules are violations**
☐ ⭐ `CORE` exemption for the twelve entities, contracts, enums, value objects — ⚠️ **size reported every run**
☐ ⭐ One file, one module; ⛔ **orphans flagged; ⛔ nothing moves to satisfy a boundary**
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **Three health metrics replace line count — context tokens is the real ceiling**
☐ ⭐ `@decisions` preserves the *why* from legacy docblocks

**All eight ✅ — §95 COMPLETE. ⭐ T2 next: the four commands.**

# §96 · ⭐⭐⭐ THE FOUR COMMANDS  *(T561 — SCALE ARCHITECTURE, 2 of 4)*
⭐ **Every check becomes a command. No check is ever a prompt again.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 96.1 ⭐ `php artisan goaiez:map`

⭐⭐ **Scans annotations → writes `app/Modules/{ID}/module.yaml`. ⛔ Generated
every run, never hand-edited.**

```yaml
id: X-163
name: PriceBook
files: [app/Services/Assistant/PriceBook.php, app/Models/PriceBookItem.php]
⭐ public:   [PriceBook]
⭐ internal: [PriceBookVersionResolver, PriceBookCache]
⭐⭐ owns_tables: [price_book_items, price_book_versions]
provides: [pricebook.lookup, pricebook.confirm]
emits: [pricebook.updated]
consumes: [consent.decide]
⭐ consumed_by: [C-Agent, X-164, X-166, X-183]     ← DERIVED, not declared
tests: [tests/Launch/LaunchSprintThreeTest.php]
⭐⭐ context_tokens: 14,200
status: VERIFIED
```

⭐⭐ **`consumed_by` is derived by inverting every `@consumes` in the codebase** —
⛔ *which is why it's true, and why a hand-written map never was.*

⛔ **`BUILD-STATE.json` and `EXISTING-MAP.md` are RETIRED. `map` replaces both.**

## 96.2 ⭐⭐⭐ `php artisan goaiez:doctor` — THE ONLY GATE THAT MATTERS

⭐ **Ten checks. ⛔ Exit code 1 fails CI.**

| # | ⭐ Check | ⛔ Fails when |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **1** | **Orphan files** | no `@module` — ⭐⭐ *the 126-file check, automated* |
| ⭐⭐ **2** | ⭐⭐ **Internal import across modules** | build check ⑤, finally enforceable |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **3** | ⭐⭐ **Cross-module table access** | `@owns_table` violated — ⛔ *the invisible one* |
| ⭐⭐ **4** | ⭐ **Event OR ACTION RETURN carries a model** | ⛔ payload leakage *(§96.2.1)* |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **4b** | ⭐⭐ **UNDECLARED CONSUMPTION** | ⛔ **a cross-module reference not in `@consumes`** — *the Ghost Consumer* |
| ⭐ **5** | **Action with no handler** | registry lies |
| ⭐ **6** | **Event with no subscriber** | ⛔ unless `@broadcast` with a written reason |
| ⭐⭐ **7** | ⭐ **Seam with no test** | ⛔ *the CC-86 class* |
| ⭐ **8** | **Module with no README** | *(§97)* |
| ⭐⭐ **9** | ⭐⭐ **Context tokens > 20k** | ⛔ **module must split** |
| ⭐⭐ **10** | ⭐ **Public surface > 8 classes** | ⛔ **namespace, not a module** |

⭐ **Plus reported every run: `CORE` size** — ⚠️ *if it grows, boundaries are
wrong and everything is legal.*

### ⛔⛔ 96.2.1 THE THREE LEAKS — CLOSED *(Gemini, T562)*

| ⛔ Leak | ⭐⭐ Fix |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **THE GHOST CONSUMER** — ⛔ *A imports B's PUBLIC class but forgets `@consumes B`. Check 2 passes because the class is public. **A never appears in B's blast radius, so B gets edited and A breaks silently*** | ⭐⭐ **Check 4b: any cross-module reference — class import, registry action call, or event subscription — not declared in `@consumes` FAILS the build.** ⛔ *`impact` is the tool that prevents silent failures; an undeclared edge makes it lie* |
| ⭐⭐ **REGISTRY-BLIND CONTEXT** — ⛔ *modules integrate through the registry and the bus, not direct imports. Class signatures alone don't describe that contract* | ⭐ **`context` outputs MANIFEST SIGNATURES** — params, return types and event payloads for every action called and event subscribed *(§96.3 step ②b)* |
| ⭐⭐ **ACTION PAYLOAD LEAKAGE** — ⛔ *check 4 stopped events carrying models and missed the registry. `pricebook.lookup` returning a `PriceBookItem` leaks the schema exactly as an event would* | ⭐ **Check 4 expanded: event payloads AND action return types must be primitives, DTOs, or the twelve canonical entities** |

```
  ⛔ FAIL  X-183  ContentStudio
     ✗ [3] app/Services/Content/Studio.php:214
           DB::table('price_book_items') → owned by X-163
           ⭐ use PriceBook::lookup() instead
     ✗ [9] context_tokens 31,400 > 20,000 — SPLIT REQUIRED
```

## 96.3 ⭐⭐⭐ `php artisan goaiez:context X-163` — THE SILVER BULLET

⭐⭐ **Outputs exactly what an agent loads. ⛔ Nothing else.**

```
  ① the module's own files                        (full source)
  ② ⭐ the PUBLIC interfaces of what it consumes   (⛔ signatures only, NOT bodies)
  ⭐⭐ ②b MANIFEST SIGNATURES — params, returns and event payloads for every
       action it calls and every event it subscribes to  ⭐ (the API contract)
  ③ ⭐⭐ the seams it participates in, with their invalidation rules
  ④ its tests
  ⑤ ⭐ its README's "non-obvious decisions" and "traps"
  ⑥ the twelve entities' schema                   (⛔ schema only)

  ⭐⭐ TOTAL: 14,200 tokens
```

⭐⭐ **Step ② is the whole trick: an agent working on X-183 sees `PriceBook`'s
method SIGNATURES, never its body** — ⛔ *so it cannot couple to internals it
can't see, and the context stays bounded no matter how large the codebase gets.*

⛔ **This is what makes a million lines survivable.** ⭐ *The repository size stops
mattering; only the per-task context does.*

## 96.4 ⭐⭐ `php artisan goaiez:impact X-163`

```
  ⭐ X-163 PriceBook — BLAST RADIUS
  ⭐⭐ CONSUMED BY 4:  C-Agent · X-164 · X-166 · X-183
  ⭐⭐ SEAMS 2:
     → C-Agent  ⛔ INLINE, same txn — a version bump kills the Fact
        ⚠️ CHANGING `version` BREAKS INVALIDATION ON A LIVE CALL
     → X-164    estimate freezes the version it was sold at
  TESTS 6 · ⭐ OWNS 2 TABLES
  ⭐⭐ ⚠️ HIGH RISK: 4 consumers, 1 inline seam
```

⭐⭐ **Run before editing legacy code.** ⛔ *The `$purpose` bug and the `RINGING`
bug both happened because nobody could see downstream.*

## 96.5 ⭐ WHERE THEY RUN

| ⭐ Command | When |
| :--- | :--- |
| `map` | ⭐ **pre-commit hook** — the map is never stale |
| ⭐⭐ **`doctor`** | ⭐⭐ **CI. ⛔ Exit 1 blocks the merge** |
| ⭐ **`context`** | ⭐⭐ **the FIRST thing every agent runs** — replaces "read the plan" |
| `impact` | before any edit to a `consumed_by` module |

⭐⭐ **Add to `.agents/workflows/build-module.md`: step ① is `goaiez:context`, not
"read the spec."**

## 96.6 ACCEPTANCE — §96

☐ ⭐ `map` generated from annotations; ⛔ **BUILD-STATE and EXISTING-MAP retired**
☐ ⭐⭐ **`consumed_by` DERIVED by inverting `@consumes`** — *which is why it's true*
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **`doctor` — 10 checks, ⛔ exit 1 fails CI**, incl. ⭐⭐ **cross-module table access**
☐ ⭐ CORE size reported every run
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **`context` outputs consumed modules as SIGNATURES ONLY** — ⛔ *bounded context at any repo size*
☐ ⭐⭐ **`impact` shows blast radius and flags inline seams**
☐ ⭐ `doctor` in CI · `map` pre-commit · ⭐⭐ **`context` is step ① of every build**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §97 · ⭐⭐ DOCUMENTATION & MEMORY  *(T562 — SCALE ARCHITECTURE, 3 of 4)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 97.0 ⛔ THE PROBLEM ISN'T MISSING DOCUMENTATION

⭐ **The evidence files hold real reasoning** — why the guard re-reads state, why
`$purpose` matters, why the exemption is 7 days. ⛔ **But they're chronological.**
*Nobody will ever open `launch-sprint-2-retry-evidence.md` to understand the
number pool.*

⭐⭐ **The reasoning exists. It's filed by date instead of by subject.**

## 97.1 ⭐⭐ THREE LAYERS, AND ONLY ONE CAN'T ROT

| Layer | ⭐ Holds | ⛔ Rots? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Generated** *(`module.yaml`)* | files, surface, seams, tables, metrics | ⭐⭐ **no — regenerated every commit** |
| ⭐ **Written** *(`README.md`)* | ⭐⭐ **the WHY** — decisions, traps | ⚠️ **yes** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **Enforced** *(the tests)* | ⭐⭐ **the WHAT** | ⛔ **NO — it passes or it fails** |

> ⭐⭐⭐ **The README explains the why. The test enforces the what. ⛔ Trust the
> test.**

⭐ *A README saying "fires on the ring" survives a change to timeout behaviour and
quietly becomes a lie.* ⛔ **`MissedCallTextBackTest` asserting an answered call
sends zero messages cannot.**

## 97.2 ⭐ THE README CONTRACT — SIX SECTIONS, ⛔ NO PROSE

```markdown
# X-163 PriceBook
## What it does          ⭐ three sentences, plain
## Contract              inputs · outputs · guarantees
## Non-obvious decisions ⭐⭐ THE SECTION THAT MATTERS
## Traps                 ⭐ what a future agent will get wrong
## Tests                 which file proves what
## Deferred              ⛔ known gaps, with reasons
```

⭐⭐ **"Non-obvious decisions" is the whole point:**

> ⭐ *"The reply comes from `$call->to`, the number the caller dialled — not the
> optimal number — **because the customer must recognise it.**"*
>
> ⭐ *"The job re-reads call state at execution. **Queue deletion is unreliable
> across drivers and doesn't survive a worker restart.**"*
>
> ⭐ *"`ReviewInviteSender` passes `Transactional` deliberately. **`Marketing`
> engages DNC and would refuse every invite on the platform.**"*

⛔ ***What* the code does is readable. *Why* it does it that way dies with the
session** — and every bug caught this week came from not knowing a why.

⭐ **`doctor` check 8: no README, not VERIFIED.**

## 97.3 ⭐⭐ `DECISIONS.md` — HARVEST WHAT'S ALREADY THERE

⭐ **The legacy docblocks reference decisions 1225, 2454, 2570, T176-P14.**
⭐⭐ **Somebody wrote those, and they encode reasoning that predates every one of
us.**

```
  ⭐ grep every `decision \d+` · `T\d+ P\d+` · `R\d+` in app/
       ▼
  ⭐⭐ DECISIONS.md — id · the rule · file:line · which modules cite it
       ▼
  ⭐ @decisions in the annotation links code → reasoning
```

⭐⭐ **This is institutional memory sitting in comments** — ⛔ *and it's the
guardrail that would have stopped the `$purpose` bug outright.*

## 97.4 ⭐⭐⭐ THE TEST IS THE DOCUMENTATION

⭐ **At a million lines you cannot verify by reading. ⭐⭐ You verify by running.**

| ⭐ Rule | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Tests assert the CONTRACT, not the implementation** | ⭐ *so an agent can rewrite X-163's internals entirely and know in 0.9s whether anything downstream broke* |
| ⭐⭐ **Every seam has a test** | ⛔ `doctor` check 7 — *the CC-86 class* |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **Every trap has a NEGATIVE test** | ⛔ *an answered call sends zero · a SAMPLE price is refused · a Marketing send at 11pm is refused* |
| ⭐ **Test names read as sentences** | ⭐⭐ **`php artisan test --list` becomes the behaviour spec** |

### ⛔⛔ 97.4.1 THE TWO EXECUTION TRAPS — CLOSED *(Gemini, T563)*

| ⛔ Trap | ⭐⭐ Fix |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **THE FALSE NEGATIVE** — ⛔ *the easiest way for an agent to make a negative test pass is a broken setup. If the factory is wrong, the 11pm marketing send fails anyway, `count() === 0` passes, and the bot believes quiet hours works.* ⚠️ **This is already in the codebase — Sprint 4's test asserted `count() === 0`** | ⭐⭐ **A negative test MUST assert the explicit REFUSAL CODE from the closed set** *(§90.3)* — `RefusalReason::QuietHours`, not absence. ⛔ **`doctor` fails any test in `tests/Launch/` or `tests/Spine/` that asserts only a zero count** |
| ⭐⭐ **THE LLM OVERWRITE** — ⛔ *an agent reads the README, decides the old decisions aren't relevant to today's task, and rewrites it tidily — dropping the historical why* | ⭐⭐ **"Non-obvious decisions" and "Traps" are APPEND-ONLY.** ⛔ A reversal is struck through and appended — `~~decision 1225~~ → reversed T561 because …` — **never deleted.** ⭐ `doctor` fails on deleted lines in those sections |

⭐⭐ **The False Negative is the more dangerous:** ⛔ *a test that passes for the
wrong reason is worse than no test, because it actively certifies a guardrail
that isn't there.*

⭐⭐⭐ **The negative tests are the real documentation.** ⛔ *Every one encodes a bug
that already happened once — and each is a sentence a future agent can't argue
with.*

## 97.5 ⭐ WRITTEN BY THE BOT, NOT BY YOU

⭐⭐ **Permanent directive, appended to every sprint from now on:**

> ⭐ **After the tests pass:** write or update `app/Modules/{ID}/README.md` to the
> six-section contract. ⭐⭐ **Pull "non-obvious decisions" from the fixes you just
> made and the traps you just avoided.** ⛔ **A module without a README is not
> VERIFIED — record it in the Gap Ledger.**

⛔ **Documentation is not a phase.** ⭐ *It's the last directive of every sprint,
and `doctor` fails the build without it.*

## 97.6 ACCEPTANCE — §97

☐ ⭐ Three layers: generated *(can't rot)* · written *(rots)* · ⭐⭐ **enforced *(can't rot)***
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **The README explains the why; the test enforces the what — ⛔ trust the test**
☐ ⭐ Six-section README contract; ⭐⭐ **"non-obvious decisions" is the point**
☐ ⭐⭐ **`DECISIONS.md` harvested from legacy docblocks**, linked via `@decisions`
☐ ⭐⭐ Tests assert the contract, ⛔ **never the implementation**
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **Every trap gets a NEGATIVE test** — *each encodes a bug that happened once*
☐ ⭐ Written by the bot as the last directive of every sprint; ⛔ **`doctor` check 8 enforces it**

**All seven ✅ — §97 COMPLETE. ⭐ T4 next: the backfill and the prompts.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §98 · ⭐⭐⭐ THE BACKFILL  *(T563 — SCALE ARCHITECTURE, 4 of 4)*
⭐ **102,301 lines into the cage — without pausing the build.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 98.0 ⛔ THE RULE THAT MAKES IT SAFE

> ⭐⭐⭐ **Annotate everything. Enforce incrementally.**

⛔ **Turning on all ten `doctor` checks against 102k un-annotated lines produces
hundreds of failures and a red build nobody can fix.** ⭐ *Then the checks get
disabled, and you're back where you started.*

⭐⭐ **So: annotate first — which changes no behaviour — then turn checks on one at
a time, each only after the existing violations are cleared.**

## 98.1 ⭐⭐ FIVE PASSES, AND THE BUILD NEVER STOPS

| Pass | ⭐ Does | ⛔ Risk |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **B1** | ⭐⭐ **Annotate every file** — `@module`, `@visibility`, `@owns_table` | ⭐ **zero — comments only** |
| **B2** | ⭐ `map` + `context` + `impact` built; ⭐⭐ **metrics measured, nothing enforced** | zero — read-only |
| ⭐⭐ **B3** | ⭐ **`doctor` in REPORT mode** — all ten checks, ⛔ **exit 0 always** | ⭐ **zero — it just counts** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **B4** | ⭐⭐ **Enforce one check at a time**, each after its violations are cleared | ⭐ **contained — one class of failure at a time** |
| ⭐ **B5** | READMEs + `DECISIONS.md` backfilled from evidence files | zero |

⭐⭐ **B1 through B3 are pure addition. ⛔ Nothing can break** — *which is why the
launch sprints continue in parallel throughout.*

## 98.2 ⭐⭐ B1 — THE ANNOTATION PASS

⭐ **~400 files. ⭐⭐ `@visibility` is the judgement call and it needs a default:**

| ⭐ Heuristic | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Default to `internal`** | ⛔ *a wrongly-internal class fails loudly; a wrongly-public one leaks silently* |
| ⭐ **`public` only if** | it's already imported by another module, ⭐ **or it's the module's obvious entry point** |
| ⭐⭐ **`@owns_table`** | from the migration that creates it — ⛔ **one table, one owner, no exceptions** |
| ⭐ **Unmappable file** | ⛔ **`@module UNASSIGNED`** — *never guessed. `doctor` lists them* |

⭐⭐ **`UNASSIGNED` is the honest escape hatch.** ⛔ *A wrong module ID is worse
than no module ID, because it makes `impact` lie.*

## 98.3 ⭐⭐⭐ B4 — ENFORCEMENT ORDER

⭐ **Cheapest and least contentious first:**

```
  ① check 1  orphans            ⭐ pure bookkeeping
  ② check 5  action no handler  ⭐ registry lies — small
  ③ check 6  event no subscriber
  ④ check 4  payload leakage    ⭐ mechanical
  ⑤ check 8  README             ⭐ writing, not refactoring
  ⑥ ⭐ check 4b UNDECLARED CONSUMPTION  ← ⭐⭐ expect MANY. Annotation only
  ⑦ check 7  seam has a test    ⭐⭐ real work
  ⑧ ⭐⭐ check 2  internal imports  ← ⛔ REAL REFACTORING. Expect the most pain
  ⑨ ⭐⭐⭐ check 3  cross-module tables ← ⛔⛔ THE HARDEST. Legacy code writes anywhere
  ⑩ checks 9+10 metrics         ⭐ splits, last
```

⭐⭐ **⑧ and ⑨ are where the legacy codebase will fight back** — ⛔ *102k lines
written before module boundaries existed will contain dozens of cross-module
writes.* ⭐ **Each becomes a public method on the owning module. That's real work
and it's the price of the cage.**

⚠️ ⭐ **If a violation is genuinely load-bearing and expensive to fix:
`@allow-violation check-3 reason: …` — ⛔ visible in `doctor` output, counted
every run, never silent.** *An exemption you can see is fine; one you can't is
how the rule dies.*

## 98.4 ⭐ B5 — BACKFILL THE WHY

⭐ **The evidence files are the source.** ⛔ *Read them, not the code — **the code
shows what, the evidence shows why.***

⭐⭐ **Seven verified modules already have their reasoning captured**: the
execution guard, `$call->to`, the `Transactional` purpose, the 7-day window, the
pool lock, the SAMPLE refusal, the latency budget.

## 98.5 ⭐⭐ THE FOUR PROMPTS

> **⭐ B1 — ANNOTATE.** ⛔ *Do not move, rename or refactor any file. Comments
> only.* Add `@module`, `@visibility`, `@owns_table`, `@provides`, `@emits`,
> `@consumes` to every file in `app/`. ⭐ **Default `@visibility internal`;
> `public` only where already imported cross-module.** `@owns_table` from the
> creating migration. ⛔ **Unmappable → `@module UNASSIGNED`, never guessed.**
> Report: files annotated · `UNASSIGNED` count · public count per module.

> **⭐ B2 — THE COMMANDS.** Build `goaiez:map`, `goaiez:context`,
> `goaiez:impact` per §96. ⛔ **Read-only. Enforce nothing.** Run `map` and paste
> the tally. ⭐⭐ **Run `context` on all 90 and paste the token count for each —
> that's metric 1's baseline.**

> **⭐⭐ B3 — DOCTOR IN REPORT MODE.** All ten checks incl. **4b undeclared
> consumption.** ⛔ **Exit 0 always.** Paste the full violation count per check.
> ⭐ *This is the honest picture of the codebase and it will be ugly.*

> **⭐⭐ B4 — ENFORCE CHECK 1.** Clear orphans, then flip check 1 to exit 1 in CI.
> ⛔ **One check only.** Then stop and report.

⭐ **Then repeat B4's shape for ② through ⑩, one per prompt.**

## 98.6 ⭐⭐ WHAT THIS COSTS AND BUYS

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **B1–B3** | ⭐ **3 prompts, zero risk, ⛔ zero behaviour change** |
| ⭐ **B4** | ⭐ **10 prompts spread over weeks**, ⛔ **build never red for long** |
| ⭐ **B5** | 2 prompts |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **Bought** | ⭐⭐ **bounded context per task · enforced boundaries · a map that can't lie · and 400 more modules that don't compound** |

⛔ **Nothing here pauses the launch sprints.** ⭐ *B1–B3 are additive; B4 runs one
check at a time between sprints.*

## 98.7 ACCEPTANCE — §98

☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **Annotate everything, enforce incrementally** — ⛔ *ten checks at once = a red build nobody fixes = disabled checks*
☐ ⭐ Five passes; ⭐⭐ **B1–B3 are pure addition and cannot break anything**
☐ ⭐ Default `@visibility internal`; ⛔ **`@module UNASSIGNED` never guessed**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Enforcement order cheapest first** — ⛔ **checks 2, 3 and 4b are where legacy fights back**
☐ ⚠️ ⭐ **`@allow-violation` with a reason — visible and counted, ⛔ never silent**
☐ ⭐ B5 backfills the *why* from evidence files, ⛔ **not from reading code**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §99 · ⭐⭐⭐ THE OPERATING PROTOCOL  *(T564)*
⭐ **How Claude and Gemini work from now on. Binding on both.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 99.0 ⛔ THE HONEST ERROR LOG — WHAT WE ACTUALLY MISSED

⭐ **Not to flagellate. To find the pattern.**

| ⛔ Miss | Caught by | ⭐ Class |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **"250 modules" claimed 20 turns, never counted** | ⭐ a grep | **unverified assertion** |
| **Read an audit as a fix** *(Sprint 2)* | ⭐ Gemini | **plausible completeness** |
| **Lost SendPermit + refusal set in the rewrite** | ⭐ Gemini | **absence is invisible** |
| **DB backdoor — `@visibility` doesn't stop `DB::table()`** | ⭐ Gemini | **absence is invisible** |
| **Ghost Consumer — undeclared `@consumes`** | ⭐ Gemini | **absence is invisible** |
| **False Negative — `count() === 0` proves nothing** | ⭐ Gemini | **absence is invisible** |
| **§69 + §70 silently missing from the plan** | ⭐ a grep | **unverified assertion** |
| ⛔ **10DLC and GBP: named 8 times, started 0 times** | ⭐⭐ **NOBODY** | ⛔ **no owner** |

⭐⭐ **The pattern is stark: Claude catches what's FALSE in an artifact — because
Claude can run commands. Gemini catches what's ABSENT from an argument. ⛔ And
neither of us was watching the calendar.**

## 99.1 ⭐⭐ EVERY PROPOSAL — RISK FIRST, THEN DESIGN

⛔ **§95–§98 opened with architecture. They should have opened with what kills
it.**

**From now on, every turn opens with:**

> ⛔ **WHAT KILLS THIS** — the failure mode that makes the whole proposal
> worthless, stated before any design.

⭐ **And closes with three lines, unprompted:**

| ⭐ | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **CHECKED** | what I ran mechanically and what it returned — ⛔ **"nothing" is a valid and important answer** |
| ⭐ **FAILS IF** | what breaks if this is wrong |
| ⭐⭐ **LEAST CONFIDENT** | ⭐ **the specific thing to hand the other model before acting** |

⛔ **No "that's complete, send it" without a CHECKED line.** ⭐ *Rubber-stamping
a prompt by reading it is what let §69–§70 nearly reach the workspace.*

## 99.2 ⭐⭐⭐ THE PRE-MORTEM — BEFORE FINALISING, NOT AFTER

> ⭐⭐ **"It's six months on. This decision caused a serious problem. What was
> it?"**

⛔ **We have been finding flaws reactively** — Gemini audits what Claude
finalises. ⭐ **A pre-mortem finds them before the artifact exists**, and it's
one paragraph.

⭐⭐ **Every design turn includes one. ⛔ If it produces nothing, say so — that's
also information.**

## 99.3 ⭐⭐ REVERSIBILITY DECIDES THE SCRUTINY

⛔ **We have applied identical rigour to a config value and a schema change.**
⭐ **That wastes effort on one and under-protects the other.**

| ⭐ Class | Examples | Scrutiny |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **REVERSIBLE** | config, copy, thresholds, rates | ⭐ **decide fast, move on** |
| ⚠️ **COSTLY** | schema, module boundaries, action IDs, public surface | ⭐ **pre-mortem + both models** |
| ⛔⛔ **IRREVERSIBLE** | ⭐ **deleted files · released numbers · sent messages · a customer's data** | ⛔⛔ **STOP. Explicit confirmation. Never inside a batch** |

⭐⭐ **Antigravity deleted ~250 migrations inside a routine prompt.** ⛔ *That was
irreversible work treated as reversible, and no rule prevented it.*

## 99.4 ⭐ WHEN CLAUDE AND GEMINI DISAGREE

⛔ **We have always agreed so far. That will not hold** — and adjudicating is
exactly the burden Matt shouldn't carry.

```
  ⭐ ① Both state the failure mode we're each protecting against
  ⭐ ② Is it CHECKABLE? ──► ⭐⭐ run the command. ⛔ Evidence ends it
  ⭐ ③ Not checkable? ──► ⭐ take the SAFER option and log the disagreement
  ⭐⭐ ④ Only escalate when it's a PRODUCT decision, not a technical one
```

⭐⭐ **Matt decides what the product is. ⛔ He does not decide which of us is
right about a queue driver.**

## 99.5 ⭐⭐ THE "DON'T ACT" SIGNAL

⛔ **Every message from both of us has ended in "send it."** ⭐ **Sometimes the
right answer is to do nothing:**

| ⭐ Signal | Means |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **SEND** | ready, verified |
| ⚠️ **WAIT** | ⭐ **something else should happen first** |
| ⭐ **SKIP** | ⛔ **this doesn't matter enough — don't spend the turn** |
| ⛔ **STOP** | ⭐ **irreversible or blocking; do not proceed** |

⭐⭐ **"SKIP" is the one we have never used and should have.** ⛔ *Both of us
generate improvements indefinitely. That's scope creep with better manners.*

## 99.6 ⛔⛔ SOMEBODY OWNS THE CALENDAR

> ⛔⛔ **10DLC and GBP have been named eight times and started zero times.**

⭐ **They are the only work where waiting a week costs a week.** ⭐⭐ **Every
sprint message from both models now carries one line at the top until they're
done:**

> ⛔ **CALENDAR: 10DLC — not started, day N. GBP — not started, day N.**

⭐⭐ **It stays there, visibly counting, until Matt says they're submitted.**
⛔ *A risk nobody owns is a risk nobody manages — and no amount of architecture
compresses a carrier review.*

## 99.7 ⭐⭐ THE QUESTION NOBODY HAS ASKED

⛔⛔ **830KB of plan, 99 sections, and nobody has described what a plumber sees
on day one, minute one.**

⭐ **Not the architecture. The experience:** *he signs up at 9pm · what happens?
· what does he have to do before the phone gets answered? · how long from signup
to first answered call? · ⭐⭐ what does he see the next morning?*

⭐⭐ **That is the product, and it has never been written down.** ⛔ *It should be
a turn of its own, and it should have come before the module count.*

## 99.8 ⭐ OUR OWN DECISIONS NEED A LOG

⭐ **`DECISIONS.md` was proposed for legacy docblocks. ⛔ But every ruling in this
chat — quiet hours, the conversational exemption, PAN, agency billing — lives
only in prose across 99 sections.**

⭐⭐ **`JOURNAL.md`, append-only, in the workspace:** date · ruling · reasoning ·
what it supersedes. ⛔ **Never edited, only appended.** *A reversal is a new
entry, not a rewrite.*

## 99.9 ACCEPTANCE — §99

☐ ⭐ Error log honest; ⭐⭐ **pattern named — Claude finds FALSE, Gemini finds ABSENT, ⛔ nobody watched the calendar**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Every turn opens with WHAT KILLS THIS**, closes with CHECKED · FAILS IF · ⭐ **LEAST CONFIDENT**
☐ ⛔ **No "send it" without a CHECKED line**
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **Pre-mortem before finalising, not after**
☐ ⭐ Reversibility classes; ⛔⛔ **irreversible work never inside a batch**
☐ ⭐ Disagreement protocol — ⭐⭐ **evidence ends it; escalate only product decisions**
☐ ⭐ Four signals; ⭐⭐ **SKIP is the one we've never used**
☐ ⛔⛔ **CALENDAR line on every sprint message until 10DLC and GBP are submitted**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Write what day one looks like** — it has never been written
☐ ⭐ `JOURNAL.md` append-only for our own rulings

**All ten ✅ — §99 COMPLETE. Binding on both models.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §100 · ⭐⭐ SHARED TABLES + B1 BATCHING  *(T565)*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 100.0 ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

⭐ **`@owns_table` is the check that catches the invisible backdoor. ⛔ If it has
an exception nobody can enforce, it's decoration** — and a rule with an
unenforceable exception dies faster than no rule at all.

## 100.1 ⭐⭐ GEMINI'S CATCH IS REAL — VERIFIED

⭐ **Grepped the plan: `pivot`, `polymorphic`, `morphTo`, `many-to-many` — ⛔ ZERO
occurrences across all 99 sections.** ⭐⭐ *The plan genuinely never addressed
tables that legitimately span modules.*

| ⛔ Case | Why "one table, one owner" breaks |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Pivot tables** *(`campaign_customer`)* | ⭐ *the relationship belongs to neither entity* |
| ⭐⭐ **Polymorphic tables** *(`activities`, `audits`, `notes`)* | ⛔ **written by every module by design** |
| **Junction with payload** | attributes on the relationship itself |

## 100.2 ⛔⛔ BUT `@shared_table` WITH AN ACL IS THE WRONG FIX

⭐ **Gemini proposed `@shared_table` with an allowed-writers list.** ⛔ **That
recreates the backdoor it was meant to close:**

| ⛔ Why it fails | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Anyone can add themselves to the list** | ⛔ *and `doctor` passes, because the list is the rule* |
| ⭐ **The list grows and never shrinks** | ⭐⭐ *within a year `activities` is writable by 40 modules — which is where you started* |
| ⛔ **No schema protection** | ⭐ *five writers means nobody can change a column* |

## 100.3 ⭐⭐⭐ THE FIX: ONE OWNER, PUBLIC WRITE METHOD

> ⭐⭐ **A shared table still has ONE owner. Others call its public method — ⛔
> never the table.**

```
  ⭐ activities  →  @module CORE  @owns_table activities
                    ⭐⭐ CORE provides: ActivityLog::record(Activity $dto)
       │
  ⛔ X-183 writing DB::table('activities')     ──► doctor FAILS
  ⭐ X-183 calling ActivityLog::record(...)    ──► legal, declared in @consumes
```

| ⭐ Case | ⭐⭐ Owner |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Pivot between two CORE entities** | ⭐⭐ **CORE** |
| **Pivot between a CORE entity and a module** | ⭐ **the module** |
| ⭐⭐ **Polymorphic** *(activities, audits, notes)* | ⭐⭐ **CORE, with a write-through service** |
| **Pivot between two modules** | ⛔ **the boundary is wrong — one must own the relationship** |

⭐⭐ **This preserves the rule instead of exempting from it.** ⛔ *A write-through
method can validate, version and audit. A shared table cannot.*

⚠️ ⭐ **And it keeps schema ownership real:** *one module can change a column on
`activities` because one module owns it — ⛔ forty writers means nobody can.*

## 100.4 ⭐⭐ GEMINI'S OTHER CATCH — RIGHT DIAGNOSIS, ⛔ IMPOSSIBLE FIX

⭐ **The diagnosis is correct:** annotating ~400 files in one pass degrades
context, and the last hundred get sloppier than the first.

⛔⛔ **But the proposed fix — build `goaiez:context` before B1 — cannot work.**

```
  ⭐ goaiez:context scopes BY MODULE
       ▼
  ⛔ modules are defined BY @module annotations
       ▼
  ⛔ which is what B1 creates
       ▼
  ⛔⛔ CIRCULAR. Context has nothing to scope by until B1 is done.
```

### ⭐⭐ THE ACTUAL FIX: BATCH B1 BY DIRECTORY — NO TOOLING NEEDED

```
  ⭐ B1a  app/Models/ + app/Enums/ + app/Contracts/   → mostly CORE
  ⭐ B1b  app/Services/Consent/ + Messaging/          → the compliance core
  ⭐ B1c  app/Services/Sms/ + Voice/
  ⭐ B1d  app/Services/Billing/
  ⭐ B1e  app/Services/Reviews/ + Feedback/
  ⭐ B1f  app/Services/{Assistant,Agents,Ai}/
  ⭐ B1g  everything remaining
```

| ⭐ Why this is better | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Each batch is 30–60 files** | ⛔ *context stays fresh throughout* |
| ⭐ **A bad batch is re-runnable alone** | ⛔ *not a 400-file redo* |
| ⭐⭐ **Related files are annotated together** | ⭐ **`@consumes` is far more accurate when you can see both ends** |
| ⭐ **B1b first** | ⭐⭐ **the compliance core is the most-consumed and the least forgiving** |
| ⛔ **No tooling prerequisite** | ⭐ *works today* |

⭐⭐ **Per-batch report: files annotated · `UNASSIGNED` · public count · ⭐ and the
grep proving zero unannotated files IN THAT DIRECTORY.**

## 100.5 ACCEPTANCE — §100

☐ ⭐ Gemini's shared-table gap **verified by grep — ⛔ zero occurrences in 99 sections**
☐ ⛔⛔ **`@shared_table` with an ACL rejected** — ⭐ *the list grows, never shrinks, and doctor passes*
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **One owner + public write method** — ⭐ **preserves the rule instead of exempting from it**
☐ ⭐ Ownership rules for pivot, polymorphic and junction cases
☐ ⭐⭐ **B1-before-context confirmed CIRCULAR** — ⛔ context scopes by module; modules come from B1
☐ ⭐⭐ **B1 batched by directory, 7 passes, B1b first** — ⛔ no tooling needed
☐ ⭐ Per-batch grep proof

**All seven ✅ — §100 COMPLETE.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 101.0 ⛔⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS — VERIFIED BY GREP

**Across 100 sections and 896KB:**

| Term | Occurrences |
| :--- | ---: |
| ⛔ **rollback** | **0** |
| ⛔ **backup** | **0** |
| ⛔ **disaster** | **0** |

| ⛔ **point-in-time** | **0** |
| ⛔ **migration on live data** | **0** |

⭐⭐ **We planned 90 modules, 121 laws and a swarm — and nothing about the day a
deploy breaks a live tenant's phone at 2pm on a Tuesday.**

---

## 101.1 ⭐ ASK 1 — THE API KEY VAULT

⭐ **Admin can add, retrieve, replace and copy keys. ⛔ With four rules that
aren't optional:**

| ⭐ Rule | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Encrypted at rest, decrypted only at call time** | ⛔ **never in a log, never in an exception, never in an evidence file** |
| ⭐ **Masked on display** — `sk-...4f2a` | ⭐ **reveal is a separate, logged action** |
| ⭐⭐ **Every access writes an `ActionInvocation`** | ⭐ *who read which key, when* |
| ⛔ **Rotation without a deploy** | ⭐⭐ **paste a new key → next call uses it** |

⛔ **A key in a log file is a key on the internet.** ⭐ *This is the one place a
mistake is instantly and permanently expensive.*

## 101.2 ⭐⭐ ASK 2 — MULTI-ACCOUNT FAILOVER *(a real change to §43.4)*

⛔ **Current ladder: same tier sideways to another provider, then up a tier.
⭐⭐ Missing rung: another ACCOUNT on the same provider and model.**

```
  ⭐⭐ ① SAME MODEL, NEXT ACCOUNT   ← NEW. Rate limit · billing hold · key revoked
  ② same tier, different provider
  ③ escalate a tier
  ④ degrade gracefully
```

| ⭐ Why rung ① comes first | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Identical output** | ⛔ *a different provider is a different model with different behaviour* |
| ⭐ **Identical cost** | no billing surprise |
| ⭐⭐ **Most outages are account-level** | ⭐ *rate limits, billing holds, a revoked key — not the model being down* |

⭐ **N accounts per provider-model, ordered, health-tracked.** ⛔ **A 429 marks
that account cold for a window; it does not condemn the model.**

## 101.3 ⭐⭐⭐ ASK 3 — UPGRADES ON A LIVE SYSTEM

⛔⛔ **This is the biggest hole in the plan.**

| ⭐ Rule | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Expand → migrate → contract** | ⛔ **never rename or drop a column in one deploy.** Add, backfill, dual-write, cut over, drop later |
| ⭐⭐ **Migrations must be reversible** | ⛔ **`down()` is mandatory and tested** |
| ⭐ **Deploys are additive first** | new code tolerates old data |
| ⭐⭐ **Rollback in one command**, tested monthly | ⛔ *an untested rollback is a hope* |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **A queued job must survive a deploy** | ⛔ *a delayed text-back mid-flight cannot vanish* |
| ⭐ **Feature flags per tenant** | ⭐⭐ **new behaviour on one tenant before fifty** |

⛔⛔ **And the rule that protects everything: NO AGENT TOUCHES PRODUCTION.**
⭐ *Antigravity deleted ~250 migrations in a routine prompt. On a live database
that is the business.* ⭐⭐ **Agents work on a branch. A human — or a CI pipeline
with `doctor` green — deploys.**

## 101.4 ⭐⭐ ASK 4 — HOW A NON-CODER RUNS THIS

⛔ **Today every fix needs you copy-pasting between three AIs. ⭐⭐ At 11pm with
fifty tenants live, that is not a plan.**

| Layer | ⭐ Does |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **1 · Self-healing** | ⭐ **retries, failover, degrade-never-fail — already built.** *Most incidents end here and nobody wakes* |
| ⭐⭐ **2 · The alert says what to DO** | ⛔ not *"queue depth 4,000"* — ⭐⭐ *"messages are backing up. Restart the worker: `php artisan queue:restart`"* |
| ⭐ **3 · The runbook** | ⭐ **one page per failure mode, in your words, with the exact command** |
| ⭐ **4 · Antigravity with a diagnostic prompt** | ⭐⭐ **`goaiez:doctor` + the evidence law — the loop we already run** |
| ⭐ **5 · A human on call** | ⛔ **you will need one before fifty tenants** |

⭐⭐ **Layer 2 is the whole answer.** ⛔ *An alert that states a fact requires an
engineer. An alert that states an action requires a person.*

---

## 101.5 ⛔⛔ WHAT ELSE IS MISSING — THE HONEST LIST

| # | ⛔ Gap | ⭐ Why it matters |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **1** | **BACKUP + POINT-IN-TIME RECOVERY** | ⛔ **Conversations, recordings, ledgers. Lose them and the business ends.** *Zero mentions in 100 sections* |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **2** | **AGENT PRODUCTION ACCESS** | ⛔ *nothing currently stops Antigravity running a destructive command against live data* |
| ⭐⭐ **3** | **STAGING WITH REAL-SHAPED DATA** | ⛔ *every test so far used fixtures. Fixtures never have the weird row* |
| ⭐⭐ **4** | **PLATFORM COST CEILING** | ⛔ *a runaway loop costs thousands overnight. Tenant guards exist; ⭐ **platform guards don't*** |
| ⭐⭐ **5** | **INCIDENT PROCESS** | ⭐ *when Infobip drops at 9am: who knows, what do tenants see, what do you say* |
| ⭐⭐ **6** | ⭐ **REACTIVATION ON THE SHARED POOL** | ⛔ **reactivation is `Marketing` purpose. Complaints on a shared number damage EVERY tenant.** *Needs an explicit ruling — see 101.6* |
| ⭐ **7** | **TENANT DATA EXPORT + DELETION** | ⭐ *§45A.4 says never deleted — but a tenant asking to be forgotten has rights* |

| ⭐ **9** | **ABUSE PROTECTION** | ⛔ *one tenant blasting the pool is everyone's problem* |
| ⭐ **10** | **WHERE IT RUNS** | ⛔ *infrastructure has never been specified* |

## 101.6 ⚠️ THE RULING I NEED FROM YOU

⭐ **You said the pool carries: reviews · reactivation · review requests · web
chat · SMS support · missed-call · the demo system.**

⛔ **Six of those are transactional. ⭐⭐ Reactivation is not** — it's `Marketing`
purpose, and §78's own test ⑥ refuses it at 11pm.

| ⚠️ The risk | |

⭐ **My recommendation: reactivation runs on the pool ONLY at reduced volume with
a per-number complaint ceiling — ⛔ and moves to their own 10DLC first, ahead of

## 101.7 ⭐ THE TURNS
