## 139.0 ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

⭐⭐ **A stale price on a live call.** ⛔ *The tenant raises the callout fee at
09:00. At 09:02 the agent quotes the old one to a customer who books on it. ⭐
That is not a cache bug — it is the business losing money on a promise we made
for them.*

## 139.1 ⭐⭐ M13 RULINGS — LOCKED

☐ ⭐⭐ **LATE FEES — the distinction is right.** ⛔ **Platform→tenant: KILLED.**
⭐ **Tenant→customer: APPROVED.** *A plumber invoicing a property manager
absolutely may charge for late payment; ⛔ we never charge a tenant for it.*
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **ONE INVOICE ENGINE — we eat our own dog food.** ⭐ *`X-199
TenantInvoicing` generates EVERY invoice — ours and theirs.* ⭐⭐ **`C-Billing`
becomes the subscription and metering LEDGER; ⛔ it hands data to X-199 rather
than rendering its own bills.**

---

## 139.2 ⭐⭐⭐ X-163 `PriceBook` — ⛔ THE BEDROCK

**① CAPABILITIES FOLDED — 14**
⭐⭐ **Services with prices** · ⭐⭐⭐ **Good / better / best tiers** ·
⭐⭐ **PRICE RANGES** *(min/max — "boiler replacement £1,800–£3,200")* ·
⭐⭐⭐ **THE CALLOUT FEE** *(⭐ with `deducted_if_proceeding`)* · ⭐ **SAMPLE
state** *(§50.6)* · **Versioning** · ⭐ **Location-Specific Pricing** *(regional
books per location)* · **Dynamic Pricing Engine** · **Price Testing** *(⛔ OFF —
§134.6)* · **Discount Thresholds** *(⛔ off for us, ⭐ tenant may enable)* ·
**Bundling Logic** · ⭐ **Margin Calculations** · **Auto-Line Items** ·
**Fractional Inventory** *(⭐ 2.5 metres of pipe)*.

**② WIZARD** ⭐⭐⭐ **THE HIGHEST-VALUE WIZARD IN THE PRODUCT.** ⭐ *The AI extracts
prices from their site, their PDFs, their old invoices and the industry profile —
⛔ all seeded as **SAMPLE**.* ⭐⭐ **They confirm TWO things and the agent goes
live: the callout fee, and one real price** *(§59.7)*.
**③ AUTOPILOT** ⭐ **a price change invalidates every dependent `Fact` INLINE**
**④ EMITS** `pricebook.updated` · `price.confirmed` · `version.bumped`
**④ CONSUMES** `document.ingested` · `job.completed` *(⭐ actual vs expected)*
**⑤ AI-CORE** ⭐⭐⭐ **the agent reads it and NEVER generates a price**

### ⭐⭐⭐ 139.2.1 THE FOUR CONSUMERS — ⛔ why it builds ALONE

```
  ⭐⭐ X-163 PriceBook
       ├─→ ⭐ C-Agent        quotes on a live call        ⛔ INLINE invalidation
       ├─→ ⭐ X-103 Site     renders at display time      ⛔ never stale
       ├─→ ⭐⭐ X-164 Estimates  FREEZES the version sold at
       └─→ ⭐ X-166 JobCosting  actual vs expected
```
⛔⛔ **If four modules each invent their own price storage, you get four sets of
numbers that drift** — ⭐ *the agent quotes one, the invoice says another, and the
customer is right to be angry.*

### ⭐⭐⭐ 139.2.2 THE THREE LAWS

☐ ⭐⭐ **VERSIONED.** *Every change bumps a version, and the version travels with
anything sold at it.* ⛔ **A price change never rewrites a quote someone already
accepted.**
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **INLINE INVALIDATION, SAME TRANSACTION.** ⛔ *Not a queue.* ⭐ *A lagging
queue is the stale-price-on-a-live-call defect.*
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **A SAMPLE PRICE IS NEVER SPOKEN.** ⭐ *"I'd need to confirm that price"* —
⛔ **never a plausible number.**

### ⭐⭐ 139.2.3 THE CALLOUT FEE IS THE PRODUCT'S SHARPEST FEATURE

⭐ ***"£85 to come out, and that comes off the job if you go ahead."***
⛔ **It is the most-asked question in the trades and the one that wastes the most
time when unanswered.** ⭐⭐ *Two fields — `callout_fee` and
`deducted_if_proceeding` — and the agent can answer the question that ends half
of all enquiries.*

---

## 139.3 ⭐⭐ X-164 `FieldEstimates`

**① CAPABILITIES FOLDED — 11**
⭐⭐ **Good/better/best presentation** · ⭐ **Auto-Line Items** *(the AI reads the
job notes and structures it)* · ⭐⭐ **Expiry Enforcement** *("valid 7 days" — ⛔
day 8 locks and offers a refresh)* · **Legally Binding Signatures** ·

being asked*

**④ CONSUMES** `pricebook.updated` · `job.created`
**⑤ AI-CORE** ⭐ *line-item structuring and the covering note*

⭐⭐⭐ **IT FREEZES THE VERSION IT WAS SOLD AT.** ⛔ *If the pricebook moves
tomorrow, an accepted estimate does not.* ⭐ **That is the versioning law earning

⚠️ ⭐ **Expiry is a KINDNESS, not a trick** — ⭐⭐ *"this quote expired, here's a
refreshed one" beats honouring a price that now loses money, ⛔ and beats silence.*

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §143 · ⭐⭐⭐ TENANT MULTI-CURRENCY  *(owner, T640)*
⛔ **And four things it drags in that nobody has raised.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 143.1 ⭐⭐ THE RULING

> ⭐⭐⭐ **A tenant charges THEIR customers in THEIR OWN currency.**
> ⭐ **GOAIEZ bills tenants and agencies in USD** *(§92 — the conversion is shown
> on every invoice)*. ⛔ **The two are independent.**

| ⭐ Relationship | Currency |
| :--- | :--- |
| GOAIEZ → tenant | ⭐ **USD base**, local conversion shown |
| GOAIEZ → agency | ⭐ **USD base** |
| agency → their client | ⭐⭐ **the agency's currency** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **tenant → their customer** | ⭐⭐ **THE TENANT'S CURRENCY** |

⭐ **Their merchant account settles natively** *(X-198)* — ⛔ *no conversion, no
FX spread, no surprise.*

## 143.2 ⭐ WHAT IT TOUCHES — ⛔ seven modules

`X-163 PriceBook` *(prices)* · `X-164 FieldEstimates` · `X-199 TenantInvoicing` ·
`X-117 Commerce` · `X-198 MerchantConnect` · `X-166 JobCosting` *(margin)* ·
`X-170 Commissions`.

⭐⭐ **STORE MINOR UNITS + AN ISO CODE. ⛔ NEVER A FLOAT.** *£1,234.56 = `123456`
+ `GBP`.* ⛔ *A float loses a penny per thousand transactions and nobody finds it
for a year.*

⭐ **And §140.1's location-binding already solves the branch case:** ⭐⭐ *an Irish
branch gets a EUR pricebook, the UK branch GBP — ⛔ same tenant, no conflict.*

---

## ⭐⭐⭐ 143.3 THE FOUR THINGS NOT YET RAISED

## ⛔⛔ 1 · ZERO-DECIMAL CURRENCIES — a real bug class

⭐ **JPY, KRW and eight others have NO minor unit.** ⛔ *¥1,000 is stored as
`1000`, ⛔ **not `100000`**.*
⛔⛔ **A hardcoded ×100 breaks Japan and Korea silently** — ⭐ *and it does not
error; it just charges a hundred times too much or too little.*
☐ ⭐⭐ **The currency table carries `minor_unit_digits` (0, 2 or 3)** — ⛔ **never
assume 2**
☐ ⚠️ ⭐ **Three-decimal currencies exist too** *(BHD, KWD, TND)*

## ⭐⭐⭐ 2 · TAX-INCLUSIVE DISPLAY — ⛔ bigger than currency

⭐ **In the UK, Ireland, Australia and most of the EU, a consumer price MUST be
shown INCLUDING VAT.** ⛔ *In the US, tax is added at checkout.*

⛔⛔ **Showing "£100" and charging "£120" is a complaint, a chargeback and in some
places a trading-standards issue** — ⭐ *and it has nothing to do with currency.*

☐ ⭐⭐ **`X-163` carries `tax_inclusive: bool` per pricebook**
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **THE AGENT MUST SPEAK THE INCLUSIVE PRICE** where the region requires it
— ⛔ *"eighty-five pounds" must be what they actually pay*
☐ ⭐ **The site, the estimate and the invoice all render the same basis** — ⛔ *a
quote that is ex-VAT and an invoice that is inc-VAT is the most common billing
complaint in the trades*

## ⭐⭐ 3 · THE AGENT SPEAKS AMOUNTS ALOUD — ⛔ currency affects SPEECH

⭐ *`X-66` reads prices to a caller.* ⛔ **"85" is not a price — it is a number.**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Currency drives the spoken form:** *"eighty-five pounds" · "eighty-five
euros" · ⭐ "eighty-five dollars"*
☐ ⚠️ ⭐ **Decimal separators differ in TEXT too** — *`1.234,56` in Germany,
`1,234.56` in the UK* — ⛔ *an SMS quote formatted the American way reads wrong in
Europe*
☐ ⭐ **`X-154 TenantLexicon` already holds locale** — ⭐⭐ *currency formatting
belongs beside it*

## ⭐⭐ 4 · FLEET AGGREGATION NEEDS A REPORTING CURRENCY

⛔ **`X-130 DemandIndex` aggregates across every tenant** *(§129.6)*.
⭐ *"Average boiler job value" across GBP, EUR and USD tenants is meaningless
unaggregated.*
☐ ⭐⭐ **A `reporting_currency` (USD) with the rate AND DATE stored on every
converted figure** — ⛔ *never a live re-conversion, which would make last month's
report change today*
☐ ⭐ **Tenant-facing numbers stay in THEIR currency** — ⛔ **only fleet-wide
aggregates convert**

---

## 143.4 ⭐ TWO SMALLER ONES

☐ ⭐⭐ **REFUNDS NEVER RE-CONVERT.** ⭐ *A refund three months later is the same
amount in the same currency* — ⛔ *the tenant's currency throughout, so no FX
question ever arises.*
☐ ⚠️ ⭐ **Rounding differs:** *CHF rounds cash to 0.05.* ⭐ **The currency table
carries a rounding rule** — ⛔ *not a global `round(2)`.*

## 143.5 ACCEPTANCE — §143

☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **The tenant charges in THEIR currency; ⭐ GOAIEZ bills in USD.** ⛔ Independent
☐ ⭐⭐ **Minor units + ISO code, ⛔ never a float**
☐ ⭐ Location-binding already handles multi-branch, multi-currency
☐ ⛔⛔ **ZERO-DECIMAL CURRENCIES — `minor_unit_digits` per currency.** ⭐ *A hardcoded ×100 breaks Japan silently*
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **TAX-INCLUSIVE DISPLAY per region** — ⛔ *"£100 shown, £120 charged" is the most common trades billing complaint*
☐ ⭐⭐ **The AGENT SPEAKS the inclusive price** where required
☐ ⭐⭐ **Currency drives SPOKEN form and decimal separators** — ⛔ *not just a symbol*
☐ ⭐⭐ **Fleet aggregates use a reporting currency with the rate AND DATE stored**
☐ ⭐ **Refunds never re-convert; ⚠️ rounding rules are per-currency**

**All nine ✅ — §143 COMPLETE.**


---

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §144 · ⭐⭐⭐ PER-CUSTOMER CURRENCY  *(owner, T641 — "include all")*
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 144.1 ⭐⭐ THE RULING

⭐ **All four §143 gaps are IN, ⭐⭐ and so is per-customer currency.**
> ⭐⭐⭐ **A tenant may charge different customers in different currencies.**

## 144.2 ⛔⛔ THE RULE THAT MAKES IT HONEST — ⭐ YOU CANNOT FX-CONVERT A PRICE

⭐⭐ **A price is a business decision, ⛔ not an arithmetic one.**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔ **WRONG** | *£1,800 boiler × 1.17 = €2,106* |
| ⭐⭐ **RIGHT** | *the tenant prices it **€1,999**, because that is how pricing works* |

⛔⛔ **Converting at quote time means the price MOVES WITH THE FX RATE** — ⭐ *a
customer quoted €2,106 on Monday and €2,131 on Wednesday will ask why, and the
tenant will have no answer.*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **A PRICEBOOK CARRIES A CURRENCY. A tenant serving two currencies has TWO
> PRICEBOOKS.**

## 144.3 ⭐⭐ THE BINDING — ⛔ location + currency

⭐ **§140.1 bound pricebooks to LOCATIONS. ⭐⭐ Now: `location × currency →
pricebook`.**

```
  ⭐ Summit Plumbing
     ├─ Leeds branch    ├─ GBP book  ⭐ (primary)
     │                  └─ EUR book  ⭐⭐ (for Irish commercial clients)
     └─ Dublin branch   └─ EUR book  ⭐ (primary)
```

⭐ **The `Person` carries `preferred_currency`.** ⛔ *Set explicitly, or inherited
from their service address — ⭐ never guessed from an IP.*

## 144.4 ⭐⭐⭐ THE FALLBACK — ⛔ when no book exists in their currency

```
  ⭐ customer prefers EUR · the tenant has only a GBP book
       ▼
  ⭐⭐ QUOTE IN GBP — the real, charged price
       ▼
  ⭐ SHOW an indicative conversion, ⛔ clearly labelled:
     "£1,800 (about €2,100 at today's rate — you will be charged £1,800)"
       ▼
  ⭐⭐⭐ THE CHARGE IS ALWAYS IN THE BOOK'S CURRENCY
```

⛔⛔ **The indication is never the charge.** ⭐ *That is §92's FX-honesty rule
applied to the tenant's own commerce — **"your price hasn't changed; your bank
charged you at today's rate."***

⚠️ ⭐ **The AGENT states it the same way** — ⛔ *never "about two thousand one
hundred euros" as if that were the price.*

## 144.5 ⭐ WHAT ELSE THIS TOUCHES

☐ ⭐⭐ **`X-166 JobCosting`** — ⛔ *margin is computed in the BOOK's currency;
⭐ tenant-level roll-up uses their primary*
☐ ⭐ **`X-170 Commissions`** — paid in the technician's currency, ⛔ *not the
customer's*
☐ ⭐⭐ **`X-199 TenantInvoicing`** — ⭐ *one invoice, one currency.* ⛔ **Never a
mixed-currency invoice**
☐ ⭐ **`X-198 MerchantConnect`** — ⭐⭐ *the merchant account must SUPPORT the
currency; ⛔ if it does not, that book cannot be sold from*
☐ ⭐ **`X-164 FieldEstimates`** — ⭐⭐ **freezes the currency alongside the
version**

## 144.6 ⭐⭐ AND THE SAMPLE RULE COMPOUNDS

⛔ *A tenant with a GBP book and an empty EUR book has an agent that refuses every
euro quote.* ⭐⭐ **The Price Approval Nudge** *(§140.1)* **fires per book** — ⭐
*"you could not answer 4 pricing questions in EUR today."*

## 144.7 ACCEPTANCE — §144

☐ ⭐ **All four §143 gaps INCLUDED**
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **A tenant may charge different customers in different currencies**
☐ ⛔⛔ **YOU CANNOT FX-CONVERT A PRICE** — ⭐ *a pricebook carries a currency; two currencies = two books*
☐ ⭐⭐ **Binding is `location × currency → pricebook`**
☐ ⭐ **`Person.preferred_currency` — explicit or from the service address, ⛔ never from an IP**
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **Fallback: quote in the book's currency, ⭐ show an indication, ⛔ the indication is NEVER the charge**
☐ ⭐ **One invoice, one currency** — ⛔ never mixed
☐ ⭐⭐ **An estimate freezes the CURRENCY alongside the version**
☐ ⭐ **The Nudge fires per book** — ⛔ *an empty EUR book means an agent that refuses every euro quote*

**All nine ✅ — §144 COMPLETE.**

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §145 · ⭐⭐⭐ THE COMMERCE ENGINE  *(owner, T642)*
⛔ **Everything up to "paid". ⭐ Shipping leaves through one webhook.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 145.0 ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

⭐⭐ **Integration debt.** ⛔ *Shipping is not one feature — it is UPS, FedEx,
USPS, DHL, Royal Mail and fifty regional carriers, each with rate APIs, label
formats, tracking webhooks, dimensional weight, zone tables, fuel surcharges,
customs forms and returns.* ⭐ **They change constantly, and integrating them is a
full-time job forever.**

⭐⭐⭐ **Cutting shipping is not a limitation. It is the decision that keeps this
buildable.**

---

## 145.1 ⭐⭐⭐ THE MODEL — ⛔ one `Sellable`, SIX fulfilment types

⭐ **Most local businesses are not selling goods.** ⛔ *They are selling TIME,
CAPACITY, or a COMMITMENT.* ⭐⭐ **Only one of six types ever needs shipping:**

| ⭐ Fulfilment type | Creates | ⭐⭐ Leaves the system? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **DIGITAL** | nothing | ⛔ no |
| ⭐⭐ **SERVICE** | ⭐ **a `Job`** → dispatch *(X-162)* | ⛔ no |
| ⭐⭐ **APPOINTMENT** | ⭐ **a booking** *(X-108)* | ⛔ no |
| ⭐⭐ **MEMBERSHIP** | ⭐ **recurring** *(X-165)* | ⛔ no |
| ⭐ **RENTAL** | ⭐⭐ **a time-bound hold + return** | ⛔ no |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **GOODS** | a pick list | ⭐⭐ **YES — ⭐ one webhook** |

⭐⭐⭐ **Five of six fulfil INSIDE the platform, using modules that already
exist.** ⛔ *That is why "covers all industries" is achievable — most industries
never touch the sixth.*

## 145.2 ⭐ WHAT EACH INDUSTRY ACTUALLY BUYS

| Industry | ⭐ Sellables |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Trades** | service · parts · ⭐⭐ **service plans** · deposits |
| **Salon · spa** | appointments · ⭐ **packages** · products · gift cards |
| **Restaurant** | ⭐ catering orders · gift cards *(⛔ delivery is theirs)* |
| **Professional** | ⭐⭐ **retainers** · packages · consultations |
| **Fitness** | ⭐ **memberships** · class packs · sessions |
| ⭐ **Equipment hire** | ⭐⭐ **rentals with deposits and damage holds** |
| **Retail** | ⭐ products *(⛔ the ONLY one needing the webhook)* |

## 145.3 ⭐⭐⭐ THE SHIPPING BOUNDARY — ⛔ ONE EVENT, NOT FIFTY INTEGRATIONS

```
  ⭐ we own EVERYTHING to here:
     catalogue → cart → tax → payment → ⭐⭐ order.paid
                                              │
  ⛔ ────────────── THE LINE ─────────────────┤
                                              ▼
  ⭐⭐⭐ ONE WEBHOOK: order.paid
     ⭐ a complete, STABLE payload — items · quantities · SKUs ·
       address · customer · order id · totals
                    │
     ┌──────────────┼──────────────┬───────────────┐
     ▼              ▼              ▼               ▼
  ShipStation   their 3PL      a warehouse     ⭐ CSV export
                                with a printer
```

☐ ⭐⭐ **`order.paid` is a CONTRACT** — ⛔ *versioned, never broken, documented once*
☐ ⭐ **`order.shipped` comes BACK IN** — *tracking number, carrier, timestamp* —
⭐⭐ *so the customer portal shows it and the agent can answer "where is it?"*
☐ ⭐ **CSV export for anyone without a system** — ⛔ *a lot of them print and pick*
☐ ⛔⛔ **WE NEVER: rate-shop · buy labels · validate addresses · compute
dimensional weight · handle customs**

⭐⭐⭐ **THE HONEST PITCH:** ⛔ *"we do not do shipping"* is a weakness only if you
hide it. ⭐ **"Your orders land in ShipStation in two seconds, and tracking comes
back automatically"** is a feature — ⭐⭐ *and it is TRUE on day one, which "we
integrate with 50 carriers" would not be.*

## 145.4 ⭐⭐ TAX — ⛔ the same cut

⛔ **Nexus calculation is shipping all over again** *(Avalara, TaxJar, 12,000 US
jurisdictions, changing quarterly).*

☐ ⭐⭐ **A tax RATE per pricebook** *(§143 — with `tax_inclusive`)*
☐ ⭐ **Multi-rate per line** *(⭐⭐ zero-rated food, standard-rate goods — one
field on the sellable)*
☐ ⭐ **`X-173` syncs it to their accountant's software** — ⛔ **which is where tax
belongs**
☐ ⛔ **We NEVER file, and we never calculate nexus**

⭐ **Same principle as payroll** *(§140.5)*: ⭐⭐ **we make the numbers correct and
hand them over.**

## 145.5 ⭐⭐ INVENTORY — ⭐ two directions, ⛔ both already scoped

| ⭐ Direction | Module | Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **SELLING** *(stock decrements)* | `X-167` | ⭐⭐ **specced §140.3** |
| ⭐ **BUYING** *(reorder → PO → supplier)* | `X-167` | ⭐ **specced — PDF PO, emailed** |
| ⭐⭐ **Fractional** *(2.5m of pipe)* | `X-167` | ⭐ specced |

⛔⛔ **Warehouse depth stays PARKED** *(§16.1)* — ⭐ *pick paths, FIFO, kitting,
3PL, cycle counts.* ⭐⭐ **A van and a storage unit, not a distribution centre.**

## 145.6 ⭐⭐⭐ "SUPER SIMPLE" IS THE WIZARD'S JOB, ⛔ NOT A SMALLER FEATURE SET

⭐ **§17 already ruled it: the client does nothing.**

```
  ⭐ the AI reads the industry profile + X-163 PriceBook + their site
       ▼
  ⭐⭐ THE CATALOGUE BUILDS ITSELF
     a salon gets packages and products · ⭐ a plumber gets parts and plans
     a gym gets memberships and class packs
       ▼
  ⭐⭐⭐ they confirm what to SELL — ⛔ they never build a catalogue
```

⭐⭐ **Same engine, different seeds.** ⛔ *That is how one commerce system covers
every industry without becoming a configuration project.*

⚠️ ⭐ **And the optimiser ban holds** *(§134.6)*: ⛔ **it may test a product image
or a button label. ⭐ It may NEVER test a price.**

## 145.7 ACCEPTANCE — §145

☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **One `Sellable`, SIX fulfilment types** — ⭐ *five fulfil inside the platform*
☐ ⭐⭐ **Only GOODS leaves** — ⛔ *which is why "all industries" is achievable*
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **ONE webhook `order.paid`, a versioned CONTRACT** — ⛔ *not fifty integrations*
☐ ⭐ **`order.shipped` returns tracking** — ⭐⭐ *so the agent can answer "where is it?"*
☐ ⭐ **CSV export for anyone without a system**
☐ ⛔⛔ **We NEVER rate-shop, buy labels, validate addresses or handle customs**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Tax is a RATE per pricebook** — ⛔ *no nexus calculation, no filing*
☐ ⭐ **Inventory both directions; ⛔ warehouse depth stays PARKED**
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **"Simple" is the wizard's job — ⭐ the catalogue builds itself from the pricebook and profile**
☐ ⚠️ **The optimiser may test an image — ⛔ never a price**

**All ten ✅ — §145 COMPLETE.**


---

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §146 · ⭐⭐⭐ THE APPOINTMENT ENGINE  *(owner, T643)*
⛔ **For businesses whose calendar IS their revenue.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 146.0 ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

⭐⭐ **A double-booking.** ⛔ *A trade with a clash reschedules and apologises. ⭐ A
med spa that books two clients into one laser room at 2pm has one client sitting
in reception watching the other be treated — and that is a review, a refund and a
lost regular.*

⭐⭐⭐ **For these businesses the calendar IS the business.** ⛔ *A bug here is not
an inconvenience; it is lost revenue that cannot be recovered, because an empty
2pm never comes back.*

---

## 146.1 ⭐⭐⭐ TWO MODES — ⭐ §29.3 named them; here is what they actually differ on

| | ⭐ DISPATCH *(trades)* | ⭐⭐ APPOINTMENT *(salon · spa · clinic · accountant)* |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Who travels** | ⭐ the technician | ⭐⭐ **the customer** |
| **Time** | an arrival WINDOW | ⛔ **an exact START** |
| **Duration** | estimated | ⭐ **known per service** |
| **Booked against** | a person + a territory | ⭐⭐⭐ **a person AND a space AND equipment** |
| **Overrun** | the next job slips | ⛔⛔ **the next CLIENT is in reception** |

⭐⭐ **The profile picks the mode** *(§29.3)* — ⛔ *and a contractor who also does
showroom consultations needs BOTH, on different services.*

---

## 146.2 ⭐⭐⭐ THE MODEL — ⛔ THREE RESOURCE TYPES, ONE RULE

> ⭐⭐ **A service DECLARES the resources it needs. ⭐⭐⭐ Availability is the
> INTERSECTION of all of them.**

| Resource type | ⭐ Examples |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **PERSON** | stylist · practitioner · accountant · hygienist |
| ⭐⭐ **SPACE** | chair · treatment room · meeting room · bay |
| ⭐⭐ **EQUIPMENT** | ⭐ laser · scanner · lift · specialist tool |

```
  ⭐ "Laser hair removal, 45 min"
     needs: PERSON(certified) + SPACE(treatment room) + EQUIPMENT(laser 2)
       ▼
  ⭐⭐⭐ BOOKABLE ONLY WHERE ALL THREE ARE FREE
```

⛔⛔ **This is the whole model, and it covers every industry without one line of
per-industry code.** ⭐ *A salon needs person + chair. An accountant needs person
only. A med spa needs all three. ⭐⭐ Same engine.*

---

## 146.3 ⭐⭐⭐ GAP TIME — ⛔ the thing most systems get wrong

⭐ **A colour appointment is 2 hours. ⛔ But the stylist is only NEEDED for
0–30min and 90–120min.** ⭐⭐ *In between, the client is processing and the
stylist is free.*

```
  ⭐⭐ 00:00 ─ 00:30  STYLIST BUSY  · chair busy   (apply)
  ⭐⭐⭐ 00:30 ─ 01:30  ⭐ STYLIST FREE · chair busy   (processing)
  ⭐⭐ 01:30 ─ 02:00  STYLIST BUSY  · chair busy   (finish)
```

☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **A service defines BUSY SEGMENTS per resource, ⛔ not one flat block**
☐ ⭐⭐ **The stylist can be booked into that gap** — ⛔ *and a salon that cannot do
this loses a third of its capacity*
☐ ⭐ **The chair stays held throughout**

⭐⭐ **This single feature is why salons abandon generic booking tools.**

---

## 146.4 ⭐⭐ WHAT EACH INDUSTRY ADDS

| Industry | ⭐ The thing it cannot live without |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Salon** | ⭐⭐⭐ **gap time** · provider preference *("I want Sarah")* · walk-ins · ⭐ **waitlist on cancellation** |
| ⭐⭐ **Med spa · clinic** | ⭐⭐⭐ **INTAKE BEFORE BOOKING IS CONFIRMED** · contraindications · ⭐ **series/packages** · recall intervals |
| ⭐ **Accountant · professional** | ⭐⭐ **document intake** · deadline-driven load *(⛔ tax season is not a normal week)* · remote vs in-person |
| **Dental · medical** | room + provider + equipment · ⭐ **recall at N months** |
| ⭐ **Fitness · workshops** | ⭐⭐ **CAPACITY** — *one slot, many bookees* |
| **Contractor** | ⭐ dispatch mode *(§136)* — ⛔ **already built** |

⭐⭐⭐ **NOT ONE OF THOSE NEEDS NEW SCHEDULING CODE.** ⛔ *They are all
configuration on the three resource types plus five shared mechanics below.*

---

## 146.5 ⭐⭐ THE FIVE SHARED MECHANICS

☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **INTAKE GATE** — ⭐ *a service may require a form before the booking is
CONFIRMED.* ⛔ **Booked-but-unconfirmed holds the slot for N hours, then
releases** — ⭐⭐ *so a med spa never has an unusable slot held by someone who
never filled in their medical history.*
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **DEPOSIT + NO-SHOW PROTECTION** — ⭐ *card on file, deposit, cancellation
window.* ⛔ **A no-show charge is a TENANT setting** *(→ X-198)* — ⭐⭐ *salon
no-shows are the single biggest revenue leak in that industry.*
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **WAITLIST** — ⭐ *a cancellation texts the next person automatically.*
⭐⭐ **First to reply gets it** *(⛔ the same claim mechanic as §102.2, with a
short expiry)*
☐ ⭐⭐ **SERIES & RECURRENCE** — *"every 6 weeks" · "quarterly" · ⭐ "consultation
→ treatment → 6-week follow-up"* — ⛔ **booked as a SET, ⭐ cancellable as a set
or individually**
☐ ⭐ **CAPACITY** — ⭐⭐ *a slot with N places instead of 1.* ⛔ *One flag, and
classes work.*

---

## 146.6 ⭐⭐⭐ THE AGENT BOOKS IT — ⛔ the hard requirement

⭐ **`X-66` answers the phone. ⭐⭐ The whole product is that it can say:**
> ⭐ *"Sarah has 2pm Tuesday or 4:30 Thursday — which suits?"*

⛔⛔ **That is a three-resource availability intersection, resolved inside a 600ms
voice budget** *(§126.2.1)*.

☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **Availability is PRE-COMPUTED into a slot index** — ⛔ *never solved live*
☐ ⭐⭐ **The index invalidates INLINE on any booking** *(§118.4's law)*
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **THE GROUNDING RULE APPLIES TO TIME** *(§136.4)* — ⛔ **the agent offers
ONLY a window the scheduler CONFIRMED.** ⭐ *A promised slot that does not exist
is worse than a missed call*
☐ ⭐ **Provider preference is honoured** — ⭐⭐ *"Sarah's next free is Thursday; ⛔
would you take Maria at 2pm today?"*

---

## 146.7 ⭐⭐ WHY THE SITE MATTERS MORE FOR THESE TENANTS

⛔ *For a plumber the site is a lead source. ⭐⭐ For a salon it is the front
desk.*

☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **`@renders booking_widget`** — *service list · provider photos · live
availability · deposit at checkout*
☐ ⭐⭐ **Book without an account** — ⛔ *magic link after, ⭐ never a registration
wall* *(§141.4)*
☐ ⭐ **The portal shows their series, their history and their next recall**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Reminders at 24h and 2h** — ⛔ *and a no-show charge that was WARNED about
is defensible; one that was not is a chargeback*

## 146.8 ACCEPTANCE — §146

☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **Two modes: DISPATCH vs APPOINTMENT** — ⛔ *the customer travels, and the next client is in reception*
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **THREE RESOURCE TYPES; availability is the INTERSECTION** — ⭐ *covers every industry with no per-industry code*
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **GAP TIME — busy segments per resource, ⛔ not one flat block.** *A salon without it loses a third of its capacity*
☐ ⭐⭐ **Intake gate: unconfirmed holds N hours, ⛔ then releases**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Deposits and no-show charges — ⭐ the biggest revenue leak in salons**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Waitlist with first-to-reply claim** · ⭐ **series booked as a SET** · **capacity is one flag**
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **Availability PRE-COMPUTED into a slot index** — ⛔ *never solved live inside 600ms*
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **The grounding rule applies to TIME** — ⛔ *only confirmed windows are offered*
☐ ⭐⭐ **For these tenants the SITE IS THE FRONT DESK** — ⛔ *book without an account*

**All nine ✅ — §146 COMPLETE.**


---

# ══════════════════════════════════════════
# §147 · ⭐⭐⭐ THE SEVEN GAPS IN §143–§146  *(T644)*
⛔ **Two are correctness bugs. Five are missing features.**
# ══════════════════════════════════════════

## 147.0 ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

⭐⭐ **Two things can be SOLD TWICE.** ⛔ *§145 built a cart and §146 built a
booking engine, and neither specified a lock. ⭐ At one tenant nobody notices; at
500 with concurrent traffic it happens weekly.*

---

## ⛔⛔ THE TWO CORRECTNESS BUGS

## 147.1 ⭐⭐⭐ DOUBLE-BOOKING — ⛔ no lock was specified

⭐ *Two customers open the same 2pm slot. Both see it free. Both confirm.*

☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **A booking takes a `lockForUpdate` on EVERY required resource** — ⛔
*person AND space AND equipment, in a deterministic order* *(⭐⭐ alphabetical by
resource id — ⛔ or two concurrent bookings deadlock each other)*
☐ ⭐⭐ **The slot index is a CACHE, ⛔ never the authority** — ⭐ *the write path
re-checks under lock*
☐ ⭐ **A losing booking gets a REASON**, ⛔ not a generic failure — ⭐⭐ *"that slot
just went; here are the next three"*
☐ ⚠️ ⭐ **The agent must handle it mid-call** — ⛔ *"sorry, that just went — 4:30
instead?"* ⭐ *silence is worse than a re-offer*

## 147.2 ⭐⭐⭐ OVERSELLING — ⛔ stock is decremented at PAID, not at CART

⭐ *Ten in stock. Fifteen people put one in a cart. ⛔ Five find out at payment.*

☐ ⭐⭐ **Stock RESERVES at checkout-start with a TTL** *(⭐ 15 minutes)* — ⛔ *not
at "add to cart", which would let one abandoned cart hold stock for a day*
☐ ⭐ **The reservation releases on timeout, ⭐⭐ converts on payment**
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **Overselling is prevented at the DATABASE, ⛔ never in application logic**
— *a conditional decrement that fails if it would go negative*
☐ ⚠️ ⭐ **Fractional stock too** *(§140.3 — 2.5m of pipe)*

⭐⭐ **Both bugs share a root cause:** ⛔ *an index or a cart is a VIEW; ⭐ the
write path must re-verify under a lock.*

---

## ⭐ THE FIVE MISSING FEATURES

## 147.3 ⭐⭐ ORDER CANCELLATION BEFORE FULFILMENT

⛔ *§145 sends `order.paid` and the order is gone.* ⭐ **But a customer who cancels
two minutes later is normal.**
☐ ⭐⭐ **`order.cancel_requested` fires immediately** — ⛔ *the receiving system may
already have picked it*
☐ ⭐ **A cancellation WINDOW per tenant** *(⭐⭐ default: until `order.shipped`
returns)*
☐ ⭐ **Refund via `X-198`; ⭐⭐ stock returns to available**

## 147.4 ⭐ ABANDONED CART

⭐⭐ **The single highest-ROI recovery in ecommerce, ⛔ and it was absent.**
☐ ⭐ **A cart with an identified `Person` is recoverable** *(⭐⭐ the pixel already
identifies them — §132.3)*
☐ ⭐⭐ **Recovery is `Marketing` class** — ⛔ **so quiet hours APPLY** *(§137)*
☐ ⭐ **One nudge, ⛔ not a sequence** — *§79's honesty: nobody wants four emails
about a forgotten basket*

## 147.5 ⭐⭐ APPOINTMENT OVERRUN

⛔ *§146.1 named it — "the next client is in reception" — ⭐ and then never
handled it.*
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **An overrun is DETECTED** *(⭐ the appointment has not been closed and the
next starts in 10 minutes)*
☐ ⭐⭐ **The NEXT CLIENT IS TEXTED AUTOMATICALLY** — ⭐ *"running about 15 minutes
late, sorry"* — ⛔ **before they arrive, ⭐ not while they wait**
☐ ⭐ **Transactional class** *(§137)* — ⛔ *so it sends at any hour*
☐ ⭐⭐ *This is the same insight as `EN ROUTE`* *(§136.5)* — ⭐ **the customer
being told is the product.**

## 147.6 ⭐ GROUP BOOKING, ONE PAYER

⭐ *A family of four at a salon. A team offsite. ⛔ Four appointments, one card.*
☐ ⭐⭐ **One `Order`, N `Appointments`** — ⭐ *each with its own resources and
provider*
☐ ⭐ **Cancel one without cancelling all** — ⭐⭐ *and the refund is partial*
☐ ⭐ **Reminders go to EACH attendee** — ⛔ *not only the payer*

## 147.7 ⭐⭐ PROVIDER COMMISSION ON SERVICE

⛔ *§140.6 built commissions for a TRADE — a job costed and cash collected.*
⭐⭐ **A salon pays its stylists per SERVICE, often at different rates, ⛔ and that
path did not exist.**
☐ ⭐ **Commission per SELLABLE, ⛔ not per job** — ⭐⭐ *"Sarah gets 40% on colour,
50% on extensions"*
☐ ⭐ **Tips are separate and pass through 100%** — ⛔ *never a commission base*
☐ ⭐⭐ **Still paid on CASH COLLECTED** *(§140.6's law holds)*
☐ ⭐ **Product sales commission differs from service commission** — *one field*

---

## 147.8 ⚠️ AND ONE THIN ITEM — ⭐ the customer's timezone

⭐ *§102's waterfall resolves a **recipient's** zone for quiet hours.* ⛔ **But a
booking confirmation must show the time in the CUSTOMER's zone while the slot
lives in the BUSINESS's zone.**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Slots are stored in the LOCATION's timezone** — ⛔ *always*
☐ ⭐ **Displayed in the customer's** — ⭐⭐ *"2pm your time, 3pm theirs"* where they
differ
☐ ⚠️ ⭐ **DST transitions** — ⛔ *a recurring 2pm appointment crossing a clock
change must stay 2pm LOCAL, ⭐ not drift by an hour*

## 147.9 ACCEPTANCE — §147

☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **DOUBLE-BOOKING: `lockForUpdate` on every resource in DETERMINISTIC ORDER** — ⛔ *or they deadlock*
☐ ⭐⭐ **The slot index is a CACHE; ⛔ the write path re-checks under lock**
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **OVERSELLING prevented at the DATABASE** — ⭐ *stock reserves at checkout with a 15-min TTL*
☐ ⭐⭐ **Order cancellation before fulfilment** — ⭐ *`order.cancel_requested` fires immediately*
☐ ⭐ **Abandoned cart: ONE nudge, ⛔ Marketing class, ⭐ quiet hours apply**
☐ ⭐⭐⭐ **APPOINTMENT OVERRUN texts the next client BEFORE they arrive**
☐ ⭐ **Group booking: one `Order`, N appointments, ⭐⭐ partial cancellation**
☐ ⭐⭐ **Commission per SELLABLE for services; ⛔ tips pass through 100%**
☐ ⚠️ **Slots stored in the LOCATION's zone; ⭐ DST must not drift a recurring booking**

**All nine ✅ — §147 COMPLETE.**

and not one script.*

## 153.2 ⭐⭐⭐ THE LEDGER CORE — 9

### ⭐⭐ `TenantCreditLedger` *(Ledger & Free Limits)*
**WHAT** ⭐ Grants the plan's allowance at each period boundary; ⛔ every spend
debits it.
**TRIGGER** `subscription.renewed` *(grant)* · ⭐ every metered action *(debit)*
**DATA** `credit_ledger_entries(business_id, product, delta_minor, balance_after,
source_type, source_id, granted_or_purchased, expires_at, created_at)` — ⭐⭐
**append-only, ⛔ never updated**
**FAILS** ⛔ *balance write fails* → ⭐ **the send still goes; a
`ledger.write_failed` alert fires.* ⛔⛔ **Never block a message on a ledger bug**
**TEST** ⭐ *debit → `balance_after` equals prior minus delta; ⛔ two concurrent
debits produce two rows and a correct final balance*

### ⭐⭐⭐ `Credit Expiry & Dormancy`
**WHAT** ⭐ **Granted credit expires at the period boundary. ⛔ PURCHASED credit
never expires.**
**TRIGGER** nightly sweep at the boundary
**DATA** `expires_at` null for purchased, ⭐ set for granted
**FAILS** ⛔ *sweep does not run* → ⭐ credit over-persists *(⭐⭐ favours the
tenant — acceptable)*
**TEST** ⭐⭐ *grant 500 + purchase 500 → boundary → **exactly 500 remain, and
they are the purchased ones***

### ⭐ `Credit Deduction Sync` · `Usage-Based Billing for AI Tokens`
**WHAT** ⭐⭐ Every AI call writes CENT-PRECISION provider cost to `ai_calls`;
⭐⭐⭐ **the retail debit is DERIVED at 8:1** *(§108.2)*
**TRIGGER** every completion, every TTS/STT second
**DATA** `ai_calls(business_id, model, provider, account_id, prompt_tokens,
completion_tokens, cost_cents_4dp, latency_ms, task, created_at)`
**FAILS** ⛔ *provider returns no usage* *(§?)* → ⭐ **cost 0, flagged
`usage_unavailable`** — ⛔ never estimated
**TEST** ⭐⭐⭐ *`SUM(cost_cents) × 8` equals the sum of AI debits for the period,
⛔ to the cent*

### ⭐⭐ `Credit Ledger Check`
**WHAT** ⭐ Estimates a spend BEFORE it happens — *"this will use about $0.40"*
**TRIGGER** any action with a predictable cost *(page build · research run)*
**DATA** read-only against the rate table
**FAILS** ⭐ *estimate unavailable* → ⛔ **proceed silently, never block**
**TEST** ⭐ *estimate within ±20% of the actual debit on 20 sampled runs*

### ⭐⭐⭐ `Trial Sandboxing` · `Frictionless Signup` · `100-Credit Demo Sandbox`
**WHAT** ⭐ **No card at signup.** ⭐⭐ A hard-capped ledger *(50 SMS · 100 AI
credits)*.
**TRIGGER** `tenant.created` without a payment method
**DATA** `trial_limits(business_id, product, cap, consumed)`
**FAILS** ⛔⛔ **CAP REACHED → R25 APPLIES: alert + ⭐ KEEP ANSWERING** — *degrade
to the PBX fallback, ⛔ never a hard stop*
**TEST** ⭐⭐ *consume 100/100 AI credits → the agent still answers a call, ⛔ and
does not consume credit 101*

### ⭐ `Mock Payment Gateway`
**WHAT** ⭐ Sandbox swaps the gateway for a mock — ⭐⭐ *deterministic decline
codes on demand*
**TRIGGER** `APP_ENV != production`
**DATA** same shape as live, ⛔ **`is_mock: true` on every row**
**FAILS** ⛔ *a mock row reaching production reporting* → ⭐ **`doctor` fails on
any `is_mock` row in a live database**
**TEST** ⭐⭐ *force decline `4000000000000002` → dunning advances exactly one step*

## 153.3 ⭐⭐ DUNNING — 5 *(⭐ one timeline, three techniques)*

### ⭐⭐⭐ `Dunning` *(§45A's 21 days — the ONE ladder)*
**WHAT** ⭐ Soft decline → retries d1,3,5,7. ⛔ Hard decline → straight to
outreach. ⭐⭐ Human at d7 · pause at d21 *(⛔ the phone still answers)* · calls
stop d30 · number released d60 · ⛔⛔ **data NEVER deleted**
**TRIGGER** `payment.failed`
**DATA** `dunning_states(business_id, stage, decline_type, attempts,
next_action_at, human_contacted_at)`
**FAILS** ⛔ *scheduler misses a day* → ⭐ **the timeline SHIFTS, it does not
skip** — *a tenant never loses a day they were owed*
**TEST** ⭐⭐ *hard decline → ⛔ ZERO retries, and outreach fires immediately*

### ⭐⭐ `Pre-Dunning Alerts` *(⭐ micro-dunning, repurposed)*
**WHAT** ⭐⭐⭐ **A card expiring next month is emailed 15 days BEFORE it declines**
**TRIGGER** nightly scan of `exp_month`/`exp_year`
**DATA** read `card_vault`, write `notification`
**FAILS** ⭐ *not sent* → the normal dunning path catches it
**TEST** ⭐ *a card expiring in 20 days → exactly ONE alert, ⛔ not a sequence*

⭐⭐ **THE CHEAPEST SAVE IN THE PLATFORM** — ⛔ *a decline, a dunning run and a
churn risk, all avoided by one email.*

### ⭐ `Voice Assistant Dunning`
**WHAT** ⭐ The agent CALLS a tenant whose card failed — ⭐⭐ *at the day-7 human
step, or just before it*
**TRIGGER** `dunning.stage == 7`
**FAILS** ⛔ *no answer* → ⭐ voicemail + SMS, ⛔ never repeated calling
**TEST** ⭐ *stage 7 → exactly one call attempt per day, max 2 days*

### ⭐⭐ `In-App Lockouts` *(⛔ AMENDED)*
**WHAT** ⛔ *The register says day 10 lockout.* ⭐⭐ **§45A says pause at 21 and
the phone still answers.** ⭐ **AMENDED: a day-10 BANNER, ⛔ never a lockout.**
**TEST** ⭐⭐ *day 10 → the banner shows; ⛔ every feature still works*

### ⭐ `Smart Retries` · `Billing Monitor`
**WHAT** ⭐ Retry timing from the gateway's own ML; ⭐⭐ detect repeated failures
across tenants *(⛔ a gateway outage, not 40 bad cards)*
**TRIGGER** `payment.failed`
**FAILS** ⭐ *gateway ML unavailable* → fixed d1,3,5,7
**TEST** ⭐⭐ *20 failures in 5 minutes → **`gateway.outage_suspected` fires and
dunning PAUSES globally***

---

## 153.4 ⭐⭐ COLLECTION & RECONCILIATION — 8

### ⭐⭐⭐ `Automated Reconciliation` *(⭐ two register rows merged)*
**WHAT** ⭐ Nightly: pull the payout report, match to invoices, ⛔ **flag every
discrepancy**
**TRIGGER** daily 23:59 tenant-local
**DATA** `reconciliation_runs(date, expected_minor, actual_minor,
discrepancy_count)`
**FAILS** ⛔ *report unavailable* → ⭐ retry hourly, ⭐⭐ alert after 3
**TEST** ⭐⭐⭐ *inject a 1-cent mismatch → ⛔ it is FLAGGED, never auto-corrected*

### ⭐⭐ `Billing Sweeps & Drops` *(`SettleBatchSweep`)*
**WHAT** ⭐ Settle in BATCHES, ⛔ not per-transaction polling
**FAILS** ⭐ *a batch fails* → ⛔ **the whole batch retries; ⭐ partial settlement
is never recorded**
**TEST** ⭐⭐ *100 transactions, 1 fails → 0 marked settled, ⛔ not 99*

### ⭐ `Stripe Metered Billing Sync`
**WHAT** ⭐ Batches usage every 15 minutes to the gateway's meter
**FAILS** ⛔ *sync fails* → ⭐⭐ **OUR ledger is the truth; the gateway
reconciles later**
**TEST** ⭐ *sync down 2 hours → ⛔ zero missed usage after recovery*

### ⭐⭐ `Automated Chargebacks & Dispute Handling`
**WHAT** ⭐ A chargeback pulls call logs and SMS history and ⭐⭐ **auto-generates
the dispute PDF**
**TRIGGER** `chargeback.received`
**FAILS** ⛔ *evidence missing* → ⭐ the PDF still generates, marked incomplete
**TEST** ⭐⭐ *a chargeback on a job with 3 calls → ⛔ all 3 appear in the PDF*

### ⭐ `Fraud Prevention – Radar` · `Ghost Account Detection`
**WHAT** ⭐ Gateway fraud rules; ⭐⭐ flag dormant profiles before spending on them
**TEST** ⭐ *a profile with no activity in 6 months → ⛔ excluded from outbound*

### ⭐⭐ `Cash-Collected Validation`
**WHAT** ⭐⭐⭐ **Commission pays only when cash CLEARS the bank** *(§140.6)*
**TRIGGER** `payout.reconciled`
**FAILS** ⛔ *reconciliation late* → ⭐ commission stays PENDING, ⛔ never paid
early
**TEST** ⭐⭐ *invoice paid but not settled → ⛔ commission does NOT pay*

### ⭐ `MRR Dashboard` · `MRR Prediction`
**WHAT** ⭐⭐ New · Expansion · Contraction · Churn, ⛔ separated
**FAILS** ⭐ *a component missing* → ⛔ **show the gap, never a total that hides
it**
**TEST** ⭐ *the four components sum EXACTLY to net MRR*

## 154.2 ⭐⭐⭐ THE BOUNDARY LAW *(process law — adopted; reverse `no-boundary-law`)*
| Class | Test | Consequence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **MODULE** | own primary table **and** own events **and** a dedicated UI/settings surface | X-number; 7 fields at module weight |
| **ENHANCEMENT** | a column, a payload, or a modified component | folds into the parent's capability table; ⑥⑦ inherit unless stated |
| **UNMAPPED** | passes MODULE, no parent exists | flagged with a *proposed* name; **minted only by owner/lead** |
| **KILLED** · **RE-HOME** | ruling collision · other domain's parent | cite the ruling · spec with the parent |
⛔ *Never deletes a feature (union rule §7A.3). Never changes a ruling (T352).* ⭐ **Nothing is specced at seven fields until it is classified.**

## HOW THE THREE FIT *(§119.4)*
```
tenant asks → X-124 decides the MODE
   OPERATE   → a registry action (preview → gate → execute → undo)
   CONFIGURE → a setting, or X-125 builds a flow
   EXPLAIN   → reads ActionInvocation
   RENDER    → X-194 materialises a view
   UNSUPPORTED → "I can't do that yet" + logged as the roadmap
   RECOMMEND runs underneath all of it, unprompted
```

### C-Telephony `TelephonyEngine` — the router, eight adapters, seven normalisers, the failover ladder *(§124; `@module M3a`)*

`@module C-Telephony` `@intent RECOVER`
**WHAT** makes eight carriers indistinguishable to everything above it. **Selection order: ① capability *(rcs · mms · sip · webrtc)* → ② STICKINESS *(a conversation keeps its carrier — a trust property, not an optimisation)* → ③ health → ④ latency for voice → ⑤ cost for bulk → ⑥ default Infobip.** One `CarrierAdapter` contract *(send · call · provisionNumber · verifyWebhook · capabilities · healthCheck)*, **eight implementations — Infobip ACTIVE, Telnyx · Bandwidth · Sinch · Plivo · Vonage · Bird · SignalWire DORMANT, all sandbox-contract-tested in CI; a dormant adapter that fails its test fails the build.** Seven normalisers hide the differences *(SignatureVerifier · ReceiptMapper → QUEUED/SENT/DELIVERED/FAILED/UNKNOWN · ErrorMapper · **SegmentCounter — the carrier's count is the billing truth, never our character math** · NumberFormatter · MediaHandler · RateLimitReader)*. Failover: same carrier next account → next carrier **with the capability** → escalate → degrade honestly + alert the operator, never the tenant. Voice fails over on elapsed milliseconds. Every hop writes an `ActionInvocation`.
**WIZARD** *(operator-side)* **inferred:** the roster from `platform_settings` *(supports · lacks · latency · cost · status)* · Infobip credentials from config · the health-check cadence. **confirmed once:** *(trigger: at deploy — operator only)* the operator on call for rung-④ alerts. **tenant-facing: none** — ⭐ *a tenant never chooses a carrier; they choose an outcome.recorded ⛔ **No LLM in the send path — the router is deterministic.**
**AUTOPILOT** routes every send and every call with no configuration ever asked of anyone · a 429 marks a carrier COLD for a window, never condemned · activation of a dormant adapter = credentials + one row · `goaiez:carrier:health` runs on schedule and feeds the roster
 `ships: L3 · ceiling: L3`** ⭐⭐⭐ *(**`R235` 2026-08-27 — EVERY AUTOPILOT SHIPS ON.** The owner overruled the `L1 PROPOSE` default: *"ALL AI ON, by my law. The client can turn it off if they want. All autopilots on, with AI watching them."* ⛔ **`ships:` now EQUALS `ceiling:` — this acts from minute one.** The ladder survives as a DESCRIPTION of what the action is, **never as a gate on when it may run.** ⭐ Safety is `X-126`'s capability gate — **no grounding Fact, no skill** — not a human approving.)* *(**ships-at is `@intent RECOVER` under `§227.2`** — ⛔ ~~escalates and PROPOSES; it does not act alone~~ **STRUCK by `R235`** — ⭐ **it ACTS on a bad situation from minute one; it escalates only when the AI ITSELF cannot proceed**; the ceiling is what this module may reach on measured clean runs, never set)***SWARM** owns `app/Services/Telephony/**` *(Contracts · Adapters · Roster · Routing · Normalisers · Health)* · **`@visibility public` = `CarrierAdapter` + `CapabilityRouter` ONLY; every adapter and normaliser is `internal`** *(what keeps the leak impossible)* · **must not touch** any channel module, `ConsentService`, `SendPermit` · runtime proof = one send routed to Infobip with the carrier's receipt and segment count; one forced 429 showing failover to the next account on the SAME carrier; one forged webhook rejected by `SignatureVerifier`
**SCREENS** none tenant-facing · operator: **the carrier roster + health board** *(status · latency p50 · cost · cold windows)* · the failover log *(every hop, with EXPLAIN's "why did this text come from a different number?")*
**DECLARATIONS** `@renders carrier_roster_health · failover_log` *(derived from SCREENS, 2026-08-27 — names only; the JSON schema each block carries is turn 69's)*
`@provides carrier.send · carrier.call · carrier.provision · carrier.health` · `@emits carrier.selected · carrier.failed_over · carrier.degraded · carrier.receipt` · `@consumes  number.needed · consent.decided` · `@owns_table carrier_roster · carrier_bindings · carrier_health · carrier_receipts`

@agent_reachable none · none · none ⛔ *(`P-209`'s BACKFILL GATE, 2026-08-27 — **every action here spends, sends, deletes or changes config. NONE is agent-reachable.** Silence would FAIL OPEN, so this declares the closed default explicitly.)*

## 162.0 ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS
**A stranger contacted wrongly, an audit that is wrong about their business, attribution that lies, and a site that looks generated.** *M8 is the module that touches people who never asked to hear from us; M9 is the deliverable itself, with their name on it; M11's numbers are what the tenant spends against; M12 is what their customers see. A mistake in any of the four is not a broken screen — it is a complaint, a lost prospect, a wasted ad budget, or spent trust.*

## 163.0 ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS
**A lead nobody sees, money that lands in the wrong account, a stale price on a live call, payroll that is wrong, and an app a technician will not open.** *This cluster is where demand lands, where money moves, where the price the agent quotes is decided, and where the day is actually run — from a driveway, in the rain, one-handed. Every block below is built so the default outcome is the honest one: assigned, routed to the right account, looked-up-or-refused, held until cash is collected, one tap.*

## 164.0 ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS
**A GBP suspension, content that embarrasses them, a wrong bill, and an onboarding that asks questions.** *A suspended Google profile is an extinction event for a local business; this is the only cluster that publishes in the tenant's name unsupervised; a tenant overcharged screenshots it and cancels while one undercharged costs us silently; and every field the wizard cannot infer is a defect. Everything below is built so the default is: guarded, gated, metered to the cent, and asked twice — the callout fee and one real price — never fourteen screens.*

# 165. C1 — THE BOUNDARY-LAW CLASSIFICATION OF G2 · G3 · G4 · G5 *(turn 30 of 109 · T677 · Step 2 active)*

> **LIVE.** The classification of 247 register lines under Q-025, in the format of `GOAIEZ-CAPABILITY-AUDIT-G1.md` §4. **No X-number is minted here; two are proposed (§165.5) and only the owner mints (Q-060).**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Classifying against the register's own "Modules of record" line instead of against the finished headers.** *The register was written at T604, before §157–§164 existed. It files `Universal Form Hijacker` under scraping, `Version Control` under infra and `Sentiment Matching` under the AI core — and in each case the module that actually owns the behaviour is somewhere else entirely. A parent taken from the register's guess produces a capability table hanging off a module that never agreed to own it, and turn 56's "every emit has a subscriber" sweep is where that surfaces, twenty turns too late.* **Every parent below was read out of a finished header (§157–§164) and checked against the pinned roster by script.**

## 165.0 THE METHOD, AND THE ONE CHANGE FROM G1

G1 classified 61 lines against three modules. This turn classified 247 against **58 distinct parents**, which is the finding in one number: *the register's domains are not the product's boundaries.* Three rules held throughout:

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **The header is the parent** | Q-041 — where a finished header already names the behaviour in its WHAT, the row says *"named in the header"* and the classification is a confirmation, not a judgement. **53 of the 247 are confirmations of that literal kind** — the phrase is already in the parent's WHAT line; the other 194 needed the header read and matched. |
| **The description outranks the title** | where a register title and its description point at different modules, the description wins and the collision is recorded as a finding *(three of them — §165.7)*. |
| **A ruling kills; I do not** | Q-060 — 7 rows are KILLED and every one cites a standing law. Where a row is only *uncomfortable*, it is classified, homed and flagged as an **owner question** — never quietly dropped (Q-021). |

## 165.5 ⭐⭐ THE TWO UNMAPPED — PROPOSED, NOT MINTED *(Q-025 · Q-060 — the owner mints, the audit never does)*

### ① `ApprovalDesk` *(proposed)* — 4 lines: G2-02 · G2-33 · G2-47 · G2-53 *(+ G5-11 escalates into it)*

**The MODULE test, all three parts:** own primary table `approvals` + `approval_steps` · own events `approval.requested · granted · rejected · escalated` · a dedicated queue surface *(the thing waiting on you, in one place)*.

**Why it is not already homed:** approval is scattered across six finished headers and each owns only its own case — X-183 approves content, X-192 approves a spend, X-111 nudges a price, X-164 freezes an estimate at approval, X-112 grants a role, R36 double-consents a case study. **Nothing owns "a decision is waiting, on whom, since when, and what happens if nobody answers."** That last clause — escalation on expiry (G2-33) — has no home at all.

⚠️ **The honest counter-argument, for the owner's decision:** X-126 `CapabilityGate` already returns a decision, X-125 `AutomationCanvas` can express a multi-step flow, and X-194 can render the queue. On that reading `ApprovalDesk` is three existing modules wearing one screen and should FOLD, not mint. **This is the G1 `DisputeDesk` shape exactly — and that one the owner minted (X-201).** ⭐ **Matt: mint it, or fold it into X-125 + X-194.**

### ② `ResiliencyDesk` *(proposed)* — 3 lines: G4-06 · G4-23 · G4-30 *(G4-37 · G4-42 · G4-51 lean on it)*

**The MODULE test:** own tables `backup_runs · restore_drills · recovery_points` · own events `backup.completed · restore.verified · rpo.breached` · a dedicated operator surface *(the last verified restore, and when)*.

⛔ **The structural point is not the module — it is that Step 11 has three turns (93 · 94 · 95) and no module to write them into.** *This is the identical defect G1 found for the FSM set: thirteen modules, no G-domain, five orphaned lines. A turn with nowhere to land writes into prose, and prose is not a spec.* **Whether or not the module is minted, C4 (turn 33) must give turns 93–95 an owner** — the fold alternative is that X-111 `OperatorConsole` grows a DR surface and the tables, which is defensible and cheaper.

# 166. C2 — THE BOUNDARY-LAW CLASSIFICATION OF G6 · G7 · G8 · G9 · G10 · G11 *(turn 31 of 109 · T677)*

> **LIVE.** 243 register lines classified under Q-025, in the format of §165. **Two X-numbers were minted this turn — by the owner, in §166.0 — and none by this audit. Three more gaps are proposed and wait on him.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Treating a compliance line as a compliance question.** *Forty-one G10 lines describe DNC scrubbing, quiet hours, consent ledgers, e-signature and privacy banners. Every one of them is a mechanism the plan already owns or should own — and not one of them is a question about what the law requires. Law 122 cuts exactly here: **we build the switch, the owner sets it.** A turn that reads G10 as "what must we comply with" writes policy into a build plan and stalls on a lawyer. A turn that reads it as "what switch does this need, and who owns the switch" finds what this one found — that the module which decides every send in the entire platform does not exist on the roster.*

## 166.5 ⭐⭐⭐ THE UNMAPPED — 12 LINES, TWO PROPOSALS *(Q-060 — the owner mints, the audit never does)*

### ⛔⛔ ① `ConsentService` — 5 lines · **and this is the finding of the turn**

**It is named in FOURTEEN finished headers — always as *"must not touch"* — and owned by none of the 106.**

*X-126 `CapabilityGate` "delegates customer-send permission to `ConsentService`." X-193 "must not touch the senders or `ConsentService` (it feeds them)." X-105, X-109, X-186, C-Mail, the whole growth group: "no module here contains a consent decision — `doctor` enforces." X-156's declarations end with "(attestations belong to consent)."* **Every one of those lines points at something outside itself. Nothing points back.**

**The MODULE test, all three parts, unarguably:** own tables `send_permits · suppressions · import_attestations · compliance_registers` · own events `consent.decided · stop.received · permit.granted · attestation.recorded` · a dedicated surface *(the do-not-text list — the jargon lint even renames it for tenants, so it is a screen someone has already designed)*.

⛔ **Why this is not a paperwork problem.** P-060 says the 20 refusal reasons are the entire set and `platformFloorRefusal()` fails closed. The thing that fails closed has no header, no seat, no wave and no owner. **Under Q-041 — the header is the spec, the code is the finding — consent is currently code with no spec**, which is the exact class the 15th template slot exists to catch. And it is wave-1 critical: C-Sms, C-Mail and X-186 cannot pass their own test anchors without it.

⭐ **Matt: this one is not "mint or fold" — there is nothing to fold it into.** The only real question is whether it is one module or two *(the permit engine, and the registers as provider slots per P-066)*. **Recommend one, minted before wave 1 opens.**

### ② `AffiliateProgram` — 7 lines

**The test:** own tables `affiliates · referral_clicks · affiliate_payouts · promo_codes` · own events `referral.attributed · commission.cleared · commission.clawed_back` · a dedicated **partner portal** *(a login that is not a tenant's and not an agency's)*.

**Why it is not already homed:** three near-neighbours each own something else. **X-170 `Commissions`** pays the tenant's own staff on cash collected. **X-82 `RatePolicy`** holds the rate *(affiliate 40% of plan)*. **X-190 `LocalNetwork`** is tenant-to-tenant referral. ⛔ **An affiliate is none of those: they are not staff, not a tenant, not a partner business — they are an outside person with a login, a balance and a W-9.** SQ-11's own seat line reads *"Billing · credits · X-120 · dunning · **affiliate**"* — the squad was given the work and never given the module.

⚠️ **The honest counter-argument:** X-112 `AgencyConsole` already runs a non-tenant login with margins and payouts, and an affiliate portal is a narrower version of it. On that reading this folds into X-112 + X-82 + C-Billing. **Weaker than the ConsentService case; stronger than a normal fold. Matt's call.**

### ③ ⚠️ `X-133 LegalDocumentSlots` — **not a mint. It already has a number and is missing from the roster** *(F-17)*

**P-167 is a live product law:** *"Legal documents are eight EMPTY admin slots (X-133), versioned on save."* The master plan's own tail says *"X-133 makes 211; it is a shell, counted separately."* **It was counted separately in a scheme that no longer exists, and the H-4 regeneration read §164.1 — so it fell out.** It owns a table, versions on save and has an admin screen: it passes the MODULE test. **X-146 `ComplianceRegisters`, the register's other named parent for G10, was KILLED at §150.7** — its behaviour is P-066's provider slots, which belong to `ConsentService` above.

⭐ **Matt: add X-133 to the roster (109), or state that the eight slots live inside X-111. Either is fine; silence leaves 41 compliance lines pointing at a module that is not on the list.**

⛔ **816 in scope − 778 classified = 38, and all 38 are G14, fenced at §44. The 717 pending are zero. Step 2's classification phase is finished.**

⭐⭐⭐ **Four X-numbers were minted across the whole phase — X-202 · X-203 · X-204 · X-205 — and every one came from the same place: an audit row whose behaviour had no owner.** *Not one came from a domain wanting its own module. That is the Boundary Law doing exactly what it was written to do.*

⭐ **Zero unmapped in the final 227 is the closing check on the roster.** *After four mints and one fold, 227 lines across nine unrelated domains — social, pixel, HR, video, voice, SMS, reviews, support and a cross-cutting bag — all landed on a module that already existed. **The 110 are now demonstrably complete against the corpus.***

# 167A. THE EXECUTION MODEL — INTAKE, CHECKED *(T677 · out-of-order insert, `A` suffix per §156.6 — ⛔ NOT a turn; Law 127 stays at 109 and turn 33 is still next)*

> **LIVE.** Gemini's execution-phase model, brought by the owner. **Four things adopted, six corrected against standing law, one number generated to replace a guess.** *The model is right in shape and wrong in five mechanisms — and two of the five would have reproduced documented failures.*

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**A second source of truth.** *The document routes the swarm through a `skills/` folder of hand-written per-module spec files. That folder existed for exactly one turn — the owner withdrew it at T665 and its content is §156–§158 of this file. A parallel folder of 110 hand-maintained specs is not a convenience; it is a fork. It drifts from the plan the first time a spec is amended in one place and not the other, and the swarm then builds from the stale copy while every audit reads the fresh one. **Q-086 is precise about the alternative: a brief is EXTRACTED per module from this document, never hand-written.** Step 9's turn 86 is titled "the Blueprint — the Antigravity workspace **GENERATED** from the master plan." Generated. Not maintained.*

## 167A.1 ✅ ADOPTED — four things the model gets right

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Dependency waves, not a linear session** | Correct and already law. A 2M-line build cannot run as one conversation; the doctrine's W0→W3 exists for exactly this. |
| ⭐ **The agent never reads the whole codebase** | Correct, and it is the payoff of Q-088's module contract: an agent loads its own module's annotated files and the public surfaces it calls. |
| ⭐ **The orchestrator derives build order from `@needs` / `@has`** | Correct, and it is why turn 33 writes them onto every manifest. **This is the first stated consumer of C4's output, and it raises C4's stakes: a missing `@needs` is a wave the orchestrator schedules wrong.** |
| ⭐ **Failure modes and test assertions written into the spec ahead of the code** | Correct — field ④ and field ⑤ of the seven. *Their purpose is corrected below.* |

## 167A.2 ⛔ CORRECTED — six, each against a cited law

| # | The document says | The plan says |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⛔⛔ **1** | *"It goes to the `skills/` folder and opens the ~1,500-word spec file for that X-module."* | **The `skills/` folder was WITHDRAWN by the owner at T665** *(§156.1)* and its content absorbed into §156–§158. **Q-086: the brief is extracted per module from this document — the module's section + its group's swarm block + the laws that bind it — never hand-written.** ⚠️ *And the owner's **skills file** (Q-092, Step 9) is a different object entirely: it maps agent SKILLS to the sixty seats. Two unrelated things are wearing one word.* |
| ⛔⛔ **2** | *"If the test fails, the agent doesn't ask for human help — it patches its own code and re-runs the test until it passes."* | **This is the five-starters failure, written as a feature.** Four features passed every test and did not run at all, **because a test supplies its own input** — a loop that terminates on "green" terminates on the wrong signal. **Law 4: done means a real artifact at runtime in an attached trace.** **Law 5: completion is proven, never claimed.** **Q-087: ON CONFLICT — STOP AND REPORT; an agent never reconciles a disagreement itself.** ⭐ **The correct rule: an agent may iterate freely against its RUNTIME PROOF; it may never iterate against its own test to green, and a spec disagreement always stops.** *QA-4 exists because self-certification is the failure mode.* |
| ⛔ **3** | *"If X-164 needs a price it cannot query X-163's database. It must broadcast an event (`estimate.requested`) and X-163 listens and replies."* | **Wrong substrate.** The spine has **three**, and request/response is the **ACTION REGISTRY** (X-122), not the event bus. Events are fan-out notification; a synchronous quote over an async round-trip is an anti-pattern that breaks the agent's latency budget and P-092 *(a price is looked up or refused)*. ⭐ **X-108 shows the real shape: the agent calls `availability.request` and offers only what came back.** And the entity-graph law is *"no module may create a private table for a canonical noun"* — **not** *"no module may read one."* **Prices never travel as text: the AI reads the canonical record, a page renders that same record** *(the invalidation rule)*. |
| ⛔ **4** | *"Every single one of the 108 pinned modules gets its own physical folder."* | **The roster is 110** *(X-204 · X-205 minted at §167.0)*, and **Q-088's default is the opposite for legacy: new modules get their own directory; existing code is annotated in place and nothing moves** *(reverse `move-everything`)*. §95.1: *"a module is a set of annotated files with a declared public surface, not a folder."* ⚠️ **Moving 102k working lines to satisfy a folder name is the riskiest move available** — and 8 of the 110 are C-modules sitting on that legacy. |
| ⛔ **5** | *"Wave 0: five worker agents build the event bus and X-204. Wave 1: X-163 PriceBook and X-111 OperatorConsole."* | **Wave 0 is SQ-0 alone — four seats** *(Architect · 2 Builders · Prover)* — **and the other 56 agents author manifests meanwhile** *(T456 Q3)*. **W0 is now nine modules including X-204** *(F-22)*. **X-163 is W2 — the first slice, built alone** *(F-10)*; **X-111 is W3**. W1 is channels + intelligence + reviews, 23 modules. |
| ⚠️ **6** | *"490 test contracts"* · *"150 to 180 isolated task dispatches"* | **Q-006 — every count is generated by a script or it is not stated.** Neither number has a denominator under it. *(The screen count, 179, is real but is explicitly re-counted at turn 65.)* **167A.3 generates what can be generated today; the dispatch count is turn 47's to produce, from the wave plan and the slice set.** |

⛔ *Two of these six — **1** and **2** — are not stylistic. A hand-maintained spec folder forks the source of truth, and an agent that patches until its own test is green is the precise mechanism that produced ~2,100 files and zero working features across five runs. Both were adopted in good faith by a document that is otherwise sound.*

**Re-weighting by changing the number of turns.** *Law 127 is not a target, it is a ceiling with a mechanism: **a turn is added ONLY by removing one.** The measured load made that tempting — one pass carried 115 rows and another carried 6, and the honest-looking fix is "give ops two turns and take the count to 110." **That is how 36 became 70 became 120.** The re-cut below moves modules between passes and merges two light ones to free the slot for the split. **Sixteen passes in, sixteen passes out.***

## 168.0 ⭐ OWNER ADJUDICATIONS — T677 · THIRD SET

| # | Ruling | Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ✅ **1** | **Session Replay (G13-32) is KILLED** — *"E3 first-party-only is an absolute law; replay tools are a privacy liability, bloat the tenant payload and violate our data-ownership doctrine."* **Closes F-23.** ⭐ *What survives: X-110's rage-click and scroll-depth aggregates, which answer the same question without recording anyone.* | **applied** |
| ⚠️ **2** | **"Review gating is KILLED; all review routing must be neutral."** **Applied — but its blast radius has to be drawn, because read at full width it deletes an owner law.** See below. | **applied, narrowly — one word needed** |

### ⛔⛔ 168.0.1 THE GATING RULING — WHAT IT KILLS, AND WHAT IT MUST NOT

**The ruling is right about the risk.** Google rewrote the Maps review policy in April 2026 and enforces the ban on review gating; **X-177 exists because a suspension is an extinction event.** Routing the public link by sentiment is the named mechanism.

⛔ **But "P-110 is killed" cannot be applied literally, because P-110 is §37 — the Client QA System — and §37 is the owner's own law, written at T496, which explicitly reversed kill-list item 22 to protect it.** §37.1 reads: *"§36.1's parallel-path-only design is void. Triage is the design and it does not change."* **A maximal reading of this ruling deletes the support ticket, the SLA, the resolution tracking and the QA report — none of which filters a review.**

⭐ **So the ruling is applied at its actual target — the ONE clause that routes the link:**

| | Before *(P-110)* | ⭐ After *(T677)* |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| The QA check after every job | runs | **runs — unchanged** |
| 1–3★ → a `SupportTicket` with `sla_due_at`, tracked to resolution | yes | **yes — unchanged** |
| 1–3★ never gets an auto-published public reply | yes | **yes — unchanged** *(this is about REPLIES, never about filtering)* |
| `fix_then_ask` ships OFF · the prompt lint · review-loss detection · NPS<7 → triage | yes | **yes — unchanged** |
| ⛔ **who receives the public review link** | **4–5★ only** | ⭐⭐ **EVERYONE. Sentiment may decide WHEN we ask and WHAT we do about it — never WHO gets the link.** |

**Consequences recorded this turn:** **P-110 amended** in §0.B · **§37.1 and §37.2 carry an `[AMENDED T677]` banner** *(nothing deleted — law 10)* · **the reverse word `keep-gate` RETIRES** — it existed to let the owner keep the T89/R45 gate, and the gate is now gone by his own ruling · **G20-11 and G20-12 re-classified** in §167 and the tracker: the routing half **KILLED**, the triage half **ENH → C-Reviews**.

⭐ **Matt — one word: "gating dies, triage lives."** *I have applied exactly that reading because it is both the compliant one and the one that preserves §37. If you meant the QA system to go too, say so and it goes — but it would be the largest deletion in the plan and I will not infer it.*

# 168A. THE REVIEW GATE — THE OWNER'S LAW *(T677 · out-of-order insert, `A` suffix · ⛔ NOT a turn; Law 127 stays at 109 and turn 34 is still next)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **OWNER RULING, DIRECT. This SUPERSEDES §168.0.1's "the link goes to everyone" — which came through a relay and was applied narrowly precisely so it could be corrected in one move. It is corrected here.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Writing the gate down as a filter.** *It is not one, and the difference is the entire ruling. A filter permanently diverts the unhappy customer — they never get the link, and that is the mechanism Google's policy names. **This is a SEQUENCE: fix it first, then ask again.** Nobody is denied a public review; the ask is deferred until the problem is solved and then re-offered on the new rating. Write it as "1–3★ don't get the link" and the spec is both wrong and indefensible. Write it as "1–3★ get a human, a fix, and a second ask" and it is what the owner actually said and what the product actually does.*

## 168A.1 ⭐⭐⭐ THE LAW

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **① The gate lives — as a TENANT PREFERENCE** | Not a platform rule. The tenant sets it. |
| **② The range is bounded** | ⭐ `public_threshold` **default 4** *(1·2·3 gated — **unchanged from §37**)*, **maximum 5** *(the tenant may extend the gate to 1·2·3·4)*. **4–5 ungated by default; 5 only if they gate to 4.** ⚠️ *Whether a tenant may turn the gate OFF entirely was not stated — see LEAST CONFIDENT. Not invented.* |
| **③ ⭐⭐ THE LOOP — this is the part that makes it a sequence** | gated rating → QA ticket with its SLA → **the issue is RESOLVED** → **the AI ASKS AGAIN** → if the new rating is at or above the ungated level, **the review system runs normally and the public link goes out.** *A customer who was unhappy and got looked after is exactly the customer whose public review is worth the most — and now they are asked for it.* |
| **④ Multi-destination** | The public review can go to **Google · Yelp · Facebook · BBB · Bing · Trustpilot · the app store** — not Google alone. |
| **⑤ The roster is a WIZARD + AUTOPILOT feature** | The tenant's destinations are **inferred where findable, confirmed once, then distributed unasked.** |

⭐ **The mechanism this needs already exists in the plan and was shipped switched off.** §37 carries `fix_then_ask_enabled` — *built, shipped, defaulted OFF* — with a 7-day timer. **This ruling turns it ON as the design and replaces the timer with the right trigger: `ticket.resolved`.** *A delay guesses when the problem is fixed. The ticket knows.*

⭐ **And the default does not move.** §37's `public_threshold` default of 4 already means 1–3 gated. **The owner's ruling changes the CEILING on tenant choice, not the default behaviour** — which is why nothing in the classification of C-Reviews' existing rows changes shape.

## 168A.2 THE ONE SHARP EDGE, AND THE SWITCH BUILT FOR IT

**Where this is not the banned mechanism:** classic gating diverts the unhappy customer permanently. **This never denies the link — it defers it and re-offers it after a fix.** The QA ticket, the SLA and resolution tracking are the deferral's teeth: without them the loop is a promise, with them it is a state machine.

⛔ **Where the exposure remains, stated once:** **the FIRST ask is still routed by sentiment**, and destinations do not all permit solicitation the same way. **Law 122 — we build the switch, the owner sets the rule.** So:

- ⭐ **`review_destinations` carries a per-destination `solicitation_policy` field, set by the owner, never inferred.** A destination the owner marks no-solicit gets **the ASK suppressed for that destination only — never for the customer**, who still reaches every other destination on the roster.
- ⭐ **X-177 `GbpGuardian`'s guard extends to it:** it already hard-stops posting to a suspended profile; it now also reads the destination's policy flag before a Google-bound ask leaves. *The module whose entire purpose is "we never learn of a suspension from a customer" is the right place for this check.*
- ⛔ **No legal text is written here and none is implied** (Q-061 · P-167). The field is a switch with a default of *permit*; what each destination's value should be is the owner's, with counsel, after the build.

## 168A.3 THE DESTINATION ROSTER — SIX NEW CAPABILITY ROWS ON `C-Reviews`

| # | Capability | ⑥ WIZARD | ⑦ AUTOPILOT |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **OWN-01** | the gate as a tenant preference — `public_threshold` 4 *(default)* or 5 | **confirmed once** — one sentence, in plain words: *"Customers who rate you 3 or below get a call from you first, then we ask again once it's sorted."* | the default runs from day one |
| **OWN-02** | ⭐⭐ the resolution loop — `ticket.resolved` → re-ask | none — it is the design | fires on resolution, not on a timer |
| **OWN-03** | the second ask routes on the NEW rating | none | at or above the ungated level → the public link, normally |
| **OWN-04** | the destination roster — Google · Yelp · Facebook · BBB · Bing · Trustpilot · app store | ⭐ **inferred** from the business name *(X-118's existing inference run already finds GBP, Facebook and the site — the same run finds the rest where they exist)*; **confirmed once** — the tenant ticks what they want and pastes anything not found | new destinations appear as the roster grows; a broken link raises an alert, never a silent drop |
| **OWN-05** | per-destination `solicitation_policy` | operator-side; **tenant-facing: none** | read before every ask; suppression is per destination, never per customer |
| **OWN-06** | destination rotation | none | ⭐ successive review requests rotate across permitted destinations rather than hammering one platform — *the reason to hold a roster at all* |

**`@owns_table`** gains `review_destinations`. **`@ingress rule.fired <clock> 
`@emits`** gains `review.re_requested · destination.suppressed`. **`@consumes`** gains `ticket.resolved`.

⚠️ **Boundary against X-192 `MembershipEngine`, drawn now so C4's discipline holds:** **X-192 owns directory LISTINGS** *(NAP presence, citations, and the noindex check — "can Google even see this directory")*. **C-Reviews owns review DESTINATIONS** *(where a customer can leave one)*. A site can be both; they join on the same business profile. **X-192's noindex test does not apply to a review destination** — a review on a directory Google cannot crawl is still a review the customer wrote.

## 168A.4 WHAT THIS CHANGES IN THE FILES

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **P-110** | re-amended — **the gate is a tenant preference with a bounded range and a mandatory resolution loop.** §168.0.1's "link to everyone" is superseded |
| **§37** | its banner rewritten to this ruling; **nothing in §37 is deleted** (law 10) — the QA check, the ticket, the SLA, the prompt lint, review-loss detection and the 1–3★ no-public-**reply** rule all stand exactly as written |
| **`fix_then_ask_enabled`** | ⭐ **default OFF → ON**, and its trigger changes from a 7-day timer to **`ticket.resolved`** |
| **`keep-gate`** | stays **RETIRED** — but for a new reason: it existed to reverse a default that no longer exists. **The gate is now the law's own default, so there is nothing to reverse** |
| **G20-11 · G20-12** | re-classified a second time: **ENH → C-Reviews.** The gate lives; what was killed at §168.0.1 was a reading, not a feature |
| **The bucket** | C-Reviews **14 → 20 rows**; the register total to spec **734 → 740** |
| **The re-weight** | ⭐ **pass 45 goes 45 → 51 rows — still inside the re-cut's 32–71 band, so NO pass moves and no turn changes.** *That headroom is what the balancing was for; this is the first time it has been spent.* |

**CHECKED:** §37's own settings table read in place before writing — `public_threshold` default **4** and `fix_then_ask_enabled` **built, shipped, defaulted OFF, with a 1–30 day delay** — which is why this ruling is expressible as **two field changes and a trigger swap** rather than a new mechanism, and why the DEFAULT behaviour is unchanged · the arithmetic checked against §168.8's re-cut: **C-Reviews +6 puts pass 45 at 51 against a measured band of 32–71, so the sixteen passes stand** · the X-192 boundary drawn against its own header text *(citations and the noindex check)* rather than from the domain name · **no legal text written and none implied — the destination policy is a field with a default, per Law 122.**
**FAILS IF:** the loop is built but the ticket is never actually resolved. *The whole defence of this design is the second ask, and the second ask fires on `ticket.resolved`. **A tenant who lets tickets sit has, in effect, the filter — without ever choosing it.*** ⭐ **The guard, and it belongs in the spec at turn 45: an unresolved QA ticket past its SLA raises an operator alert AND the customer is asked anyway.** *The gate defers a review; it must never be able to bury one.*
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **whether a tenant may turn the gate OFF entirely** — *"they can gate 1·2·3 up to 4"* states the range upward and says nothing about zero. **A tenant who wants every customer asked immediately is the safest configuration on the board, and I have not written it in because it was not stated.** One word adds it: **is `public_threshold = 0` (no gate) permitted?**
