# 169. TURN 34 — THE FOLD-IN BEGINS · SPINE + CONVERSATIONAL *(turn 34 of 109 · T677 · 12 modules · 50 rows)*

> **LIVE.** The first fold-in pass. Every surviving row from §168.1's bucket becomes a **7-field capability row** under its module. ⭐ **`X-204 ConsentService` is specced first and gets a full §157 header — it is the one module of the twelve that has none.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Writing seven fields that restate the register line in seven ways.** *A capability row exists to be handed to an agent who will build it and to a prover who will refuse it. **Field ④ is the one that carries the weight** — a failure mode of "the operation fails" is worth nothing, and it is what you write when you are folding fifty rows and want to be finished. The rows below are checkable against a specific behaviour or they are decoration. **The test: could QA-4 write a failing case from field ⑤ without asking a question?** If not, the row is not done.*

## 169.0 ⭐ OWNER RULINGS — T677 · FOURTH SET

| # | Ruling | Where it lands |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **1** | **THE PHOTO.** The review request also asks the customer for **a photo of the finished job — or of whatever the product or service produced — and the tenant may use that photo on their review page.** | **`C-Reviews` — OWN-07**, turn 45 |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **2** | **THE CYCLE CAP — two passes, never three.** A second low rating goes **back into triage**, and the customer is **NOT re-entered into the review system a third time.** ⛔ **From that point the system stops asking for a review at all and wants only one thing: to find out whether anything is still outstanding.** | **`C-Reviews` — OWN-08**, turn 45 |
| ✅ **3** | **F-19 CLOSED — `X-164 FieldEstimates` is RENAMED `X-164 Agreements`**, covering field estimates, quotes and MSAs under one truthful boundary. **The number does not change.** | roster · module map · §163 · the rename table |

⭐⭐ **Ruling 2 closes my own FAILS IF from §168A, and closes it better than the guard I proposed.** *I wrote: "a tenant who lets tickets sit has the filter without ever choosing it." **A hard cap of two cycles removes the failure mode at the root** — the loop cannot run forever, so it cannot be used to hold a review hostage until the customer relents. **An unbounded "ask again until they rate you well" loop is the abusive version of this design, and the owner has ruled it out before it was ever built.*** *The SLA-breach alert still belongs in the spec at turn 45; it is now a backstop rather than the only defence.*

⭐ **Ruling 1 has a consent edge that must be written into the row, not assumed:** a **customer-supplied** photo is not the same object as a **tech-supplied** job photo. P-131's photo loop covers the second *(real job photos, never stock)*. **The first is someone else's picture and needs an explicit permission at the moment of upload** — the R36 double-consent shape: the customer grants use when they send it, and the tenant publishes. **A photo with no recorded grant cannot render.** *Written into OWN-07's field ④.*

⚠️ **One label correction, third time, ruling untouched — and the recurrence is the point:** turn 34 is **Step 2**. Step 2 runs turns 30–49 *(map the 717 — classify at 30–33, fold in at 34–49)*. **Step 3 ∥ Step 5 begin at turn 50.** *This label has arrived wrong three turns running; it is not a mistake in the plan, it is a mistake in what is being read. `GOAIEZ-TURNS.md` states the step boundaries at the head of every block.*

## 169.1 ⭐⭐⭐ X-204 `ConsentService` — THE FULL HEADER *(minted §167.0 · SQ-0 · WAVE 0 · specced first per F-22)*

`@module X-204` `@intent GROW`

**WHAT** ⭐⭐ **The single decider of whether a message may be sent to a person on a channel. Every sender asks; no sender decides.** Returns GRANT or **exactly one of P-060's twenty refusal reasons — a refusal without a code fails the build**, and `platformFloorRefusal()` fails closed, so an unknown state refuses. Owns the **permit** *(immutable, provenance-carrying — lifts are recorded, never deleted)*, the **suppression list**, the **`ImportAttestation`**, and the **compliance-register slots**. **The three lanes:** a campaign declares its lane and this module reads it — Lane 1 transactional *(nothing blocks but STOP)* · Lane 2 marketing-to-phones *(basis + window + 10DLC)* · Lane 3 cold B2B email *(CAN-SPAM shape)*. ⛔ **It does not send, compose, schedule, or hold campaign logic — a policy engine that starts sending is the thing that would block the spine (§168.4).** ⛔ **The registers (DNC · litigator · reassigned-number) are PROVIDER SLOTS, DEFAULT OFF, on the tenant's own credentials; NOT ENABLED is indistinguishable from never existing (P-066).** ⛔ **An import is not consent — every contact path routes through `ImportAttestation` exactly as a CSV does, and the tenant's attestation IS the consent record (P-069).**
**WIZARD** *(operator-side — §118.1: the tenant never sees it)* **inferred at install:** the twenty refusal codes from P-060's closed set · the three lanes from each campaign's manifest · the quiet-hours window as data *(P-063 — marketing class only)*. **confirmed once by the operator:** which register providers exist as slots *(every one DEFAULT OFF)*. **tenant-facing: none** — what the tenant sees is the do-not-text list, which is X-01's screen rendering this module's suppressions.
**AUTOPILOT** *(operator posture)* STOP suppresses **on receipt, before the next send, always** · suppression is checked **fresh as of each send**, never at campaign build · a permit is immutable and carries its provenance · **a register that is OFF is never consulted and never delays a send** · every decision writes an `ActionInvocation`.
 `ships: n/a` · `@ceiling n/a` *(operator posture — `P-195`'s ladder governs actions toward a CUSTOMER)***SWARM** **SQ-0 · WAVE 0, with the spine.** Owns `app/Modules/Spine/Consent/**`. **`@visibility public` = `ConsentService::decide()` ONLY** — every register adapter, lane evaluator and suppression matcher is `internal` — **Must not touch** any sender, `C-Sms`/`C-Mail`/`X-186` code, or X-193's classes *(it reads them)*. **Safe-update path: additive only — a new refusal code is a new closed-enum member plus its test; a code is never renumbered, and the set of twenty changes only on the owner's word (P-060).** Skills: Postgres RLS + FORCE · closed-enum modelling · Pest contract tests · ≤12 a seat. **Runtime proof =** one real send refused with its code in the trace and **nothing on the wire**; one `STOP` received and the very next queued send to that person refused with its code; one contact write with no attestation refused **at the write**.
**SCREENS** operator: none. tenant: **refusals by reason today** *(the twenty, as a bar — the fastest read of what the platform is actually blocking)* · register slot states.
**DECLARATIONS** `@renders refusals_by_reason · register_slot_states` *(derived from SCREENS, 2026-08-27 — names only; the JSON schema each block carries is turn 69's)*
`@provides consent.decide · consent.suppress · consent.lift · attestation.record · register.check` · `@agent_reachable none · none · none` · `@emits consent.decided · permit.granted · attestation.recorded · suppression.added` · `@consumes `capability.decided` ⭐⭐⭐ *(**`R235` `N-235-04` 2026-08-27 — THE GATE THAT MAKES SHIPPING-ON SAFE.** `R235` turned 102 autopilots ON; **`X-126`'s gate is what supervises them.** ⛔⛔ ***No grounding `Fact` → no skill*** — an agent action invoked without grounding is REFUSED with `NO_FACT`, so the autopilot **cannot invent a price, a time or a link.** ⭐ *This is what "AI watching AI" means mechanically — **autonomy without the gate is nothing watching anything.***)* · message.received` *(STOP)* · `contact.created · campaign.scheduled` · `@owns_table send_permits · suppressions · import_attestations · compliance_registers`

@agent_reachable `register.check` ⭐ *(`P-209`'s BACKFILL GATE, 2026-08-27 — **DERIVED, never guessed**: read-shaped and proposal actions only. **Anything that spends, sends, deletes or changes config is NOT reachable** — the agent proposes it through the approval desk.)*
**NEEDS / HAS** needs: the lane declared on every campaign · an `ImportAttestation` on every contact write · has: permits decided today · **refusals by reason, against P-060's twenty**
**TEST ANCHOR** *`grep -rE '\-\>send\(|canSend' app/Modules/` shows every send path calling `ConsentService::decide()` and **no module containing a consent branch of its own** — enforced by `doctor`; `decide()` handed an unknown state returns a refusal, never a grant.*

# 170. TURN 35 — TELEPHONY & CHANNELS *(turn 35 of 109 · T677 · 8 modules · 42 rows)*

> **LIVE.** ⭐⭐ **The seam holds: every row in this pass that decides whether to send calls `X-204 ConsentService::decide()`. Not one channel module carries a gate of its own.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**A channel that knows better.** *Every one of these eight modules has a plausible reason to make its own send decision — SMS knows about carriers, mail knows about complaint rates, WhatsApp knows about template windows. **Each of those is real, and none of them is consent.** The moment a channel adds `if ($complaintRate > x) return false` next to its driver, there are two places that decide whether a message goes out, and the second one is invisible to `doctor`, to the refusal-reason dashboard and to every audit. ⛔ **The distinction the spec must hold: a channel may refuse for a CHANNEL reason and must report it as a delivery outcome; only X-204 refuses for a PERSON reason, and it returns one of the twenty codes.***

## 170.1 ⭐⭐ THE SEAM — WHAT EVERY CHANNEL MODULE INHERITS *(written once; every table below refers to it)*

**Stated here so it is not restated forty-two times.** Every send path in this group is:

> `X-193` decides the **class** from the CALLER *(never the content — P-062)* → **`X-204::decide(person, channel, lane, class)`** → GRANT or one of P-060's **twenty** codes → only then the driver.

⛔ **A channel module MAY refuse for a channel reason** *(no template window, a hard bounce, an unroutable number)* — **and it reports that as a DELIVERY OUTCOME, never as a consent refusal.** ⛔ **A channel module MAY NOT refuse for a person reason.** *Suppression, quiet hours, lane basis, register hits and STOP are X-204's, and a channel that reimplements one of them is a build failure.*

**The assertion, run once for the whole group at the wave gate:** `grep -rE 'canSend|suppress|quiet|opt_?out|dnc' app/Modules/Channels/` returns **only calls into `ConsentService`** and no local branch — enforced by `doctor`, and it is the group's shared test.

**FAILS IF:** ⛔ **the channel-reason / person-reason line is clean in the spec and muddy in the code.** *A hard bounce is a channel reason. A hard bounce that suppresses the address forever is a person decision wearing a channel's clothes — and it is the single most likely place this group's seam actually breaks, because it is genuinely ambiguous and every mail system in the world does it locally.* **The G11-09/10 row draws that line explicitly (`unknown` never becomes `invalid`); if the swarm gets that row wrong, check the other thirty before assuming it is isolated.**
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **C-Mail at 21 rows was the largest single-module fold so far and I merged it hardest — 21 rows into 14 specs.** *The DMARC merge (three rows into one) and the SPF/BIMI merge are the two I would re-examine: **DMARC reporting, policy escalation and spoofing alerts share a data source but have three different owners of the decision**, and one spec may hide that. **If any merge in this pass is wrong, it is that one.***

# 171. TURN 36 — VOICE + X-200 CALLCENTER *(turn 36 of 109 · T677 · 5 modules · 39 rows)*

> **LIVE.** ⭐⭐ **One disposition schema for both seat types. An AI seat and a human seat emit the same event with a different `seat_type` — there is no second path.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Building the AI seat as a special case of the dialer.** *X-200 is the one module where a machine and a person do the same job on the same queue. The tempting shape is `if ($seat->isAi())` — and it is fatal, because it forks disposition, QA scoring, the wallboard and the abandonment maths into two code paths that drift. **The 3% ceiling is computed over ALL calls; the moment AI calls take a separate route to the bus, the denominator is wrong and the cap is measured against a number that is not the truth.** ⭐ The correct shape: **a seat is a seat.** It has a type, it emits `call.dispositioned` with the same schema, and QA scores it with the same scorecard.*

## 171.0 ⭐ THE TWO QUESTIONS, ANSWERED FOR THE RECORD

### ① SMS — was anything gated? **No. Nothing new.**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Quiet hours** | ⭐ **MARKETING only.** *Transactional and non-marketing are exempt — exactly as stated.* The class is decided **from the CALLER, never the content** (P-062), so an appointment reminder cannot be reclassified by its wording. |
| **Transactional SMS** | ⭐ **Sends. No window, no delay, no cap.** The turn-35 spec's own words: *"blocked by nothing but STOP"* — and the X-193 test asserts a transactional send **inside** the quiet window goes immediately, in the same test as a marketing one being deferred. |
| **The missed-call text-back** | fires **on the RING** *(R80)*, and the spec asserts quiet hours must **not** suppress it. |
| ⛔ **The only per-person block on a transactional SMS** | **STOP** — and that is not new: it is P-060/P-061, already law before this arc began. A person who texted STOP receives nothing on that channel, transactional included. |
| **Two things that are NOT our gates** | the **carrier's** 10DLC brand approval *(X-188 auto-submits it; until the carrier approves, the carrier rejects)* and **P-065's per-number complaint monitoring**, which **retires a NUMBER and moves the send to another one** — it never stops the person from being reached. |

⭐⭐ **The distinction worth keeping: calling `ConsentService` is not the same as being gated.** *Every send calls it. For a transactional SMS it returns GRANT unless STOP or a suppression exists. **The seam exists so the decision is in one auditable place — it does not add a decision.*** *Before turn 35, four channel modules could each have grown their own quiet-hours branch. Now none can.*

# 171A. THE ABANDONMENT CEILING, RE-DEFINED — AND THE OPEN-ITEMS REGISTER *(T677 · out-of-order insert · ⛔ NOT a turn; turn 37 is still next)*

## 171A.1 ⭐⭐ THE OWNER'S POINT — AND IT IS RIGHT

> *"AI is exempt from the 3% ceiling. AI processes every call so there is no abandonment to track, and this rule predates AI."*

⭐ **Correct on the mechanism.** *Abandonment is a specific event: **a predictive dialer places more calls than it has agents, a person answers, and nobody is there within the answer window.** The rule exists because a human agent pool is a fixed, scarce resource. **An AI seat is not scarce in that way — it answers on the first ring, every time. The numerator for AI-answered calls is structurally zero, not merely small.*** **The rule was written for human-staffed predictive dialing and it does predate this.**

⭐⭐ **And it fixes the failure I flagged at §171.** *I wrote: "the ceiling holds in the spec and the denominator drifts in production."* **The drift I feared was AI calls being silently excluded from the denominator. Making the exclusion EXPLICIT and INTENTIONAL removes exactly that risk** — a metric with a stated definition beats one with an assumed one. **This is a fix, and it improves the spec.**

⛔ **What it does not do is remove the need for a ceiling — it moves what the ceiling measures. Three mechanisms, all mechanical, none legal:**

| # | The mechanism | Why "AI is exempt" does not cover it |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **1** | **THE HANDOFF** | The AI answers, then needs a person — *"let me get someone for you."* **If no human seat is free, that caller waits or drops. That IS an abandonment, and it happens on a call that STARTED as AI.** *"AI calls are exempt" is true only if you classify a call by **who answered**. The risk lives in **who is needed next.*** |
| ⭐⭐ **2** | **AI CONCURRENCY IS NOT INFINITE** | LiveKit sessions, model rate limits and the 7¢-per-minute budget all cap **simultaneous** AI seats. **When concurrency is exhausted, the next answered call gets silence — the identical experience for the person on the other end, from a different cause.** ⛔ **Nothing in the plan currently measures this, and in an AI-first dialer it is the ONLY way a caller hears nothing.** |
| ⚠️ **3** | **THE DENOMINATOR EFFECT** | If AI calls leave the denominator and *any* human abandonments remain, **the measured rate goes UP, not down** — a handful of drops over a small base. That is arguably the right behaviour. ⛔ **But if the swarm implements "exempt" as "skip the check," both the numerator and the meter disappear and nothing is measured at all.** |

## 171A.2 ⭐ THE SHAPE THAT HOLDS BOTH — PROPOSED, NOT ADOPTED *(Q-060 — this defines a threshold, which is the owner's)*

| Metric | Definition | Ceiling |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`abandonment_rate`** | ⭐ **denominator = calls that REQUIRED A HUMAN SEAT** *(answered-then-transferred, plus anything queued straight to a human)*. **AI-answered-and-resolved calls are out of both the numerator and the denominator.** *This is the owner's ruling, stated precisely enough for a test.* | **3% hard max, unchanged** |
| ⭐⭐ **`silent_answer_rate`** *(NEW — proposed)* | **answered calls that received no audio inside the answer window, for ANY cause — including AI concurrency exhaustion.** *Different mechanism, same experience for the person who picked up.* | ⛔ **the owner's to set — proposed, not defaulted** |
| **Pacing input** | on an AI-first campaign, pacing throttles on **AI session headroom**, not on human agent availability | — |

⭐ **Why the second metric matters more than it looks:** *the 3% ceiling was the only thing in the plan standing between a tenant's number and a carrier flag. **Narrowing it to human-transfer calls is correct and it leaves the AI-only campaign — which will be most of them — with no meter at all.** `silent_answer_rate` is that meter, and it is measuring the thing the tenant actually cares about: **did someone pick up and hear nothing.***

**§171.5's G10-03 · G3-04 row is AMENDED accordingly** — the assertion *"the denominator includes AI-seat calls"* was written under the old reading and is **wrong under this ruling.** It becomes: **the denominator is asserted to contain human-required calls only, proven on a mixed fixture; and a `silent_answer` event is asserted to fire when AI concurrency is forced to exhaustion.**

⚠️ **One thing this section does not do (Q-061):** *it takes no position on how a regulator or a carrier classifies an AI answering a call. That is not ours to decide and the plan does not advise on it.* **What is written here is the mechanism and the meter; the policy behind the number is the owner's, with counsel.**

# 171B. THE DIALER LAW · THE BAA REVERSAL · THE OFF-SWITCH PRINCIPLE *(T677 · out-of-order insert · ⛔ NOT a turn; turn 37 is still next)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **Every open item in §171A's register is answered. Three new laws, one ruling reversed, one spec re-cut, four questions answered back.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Recording "AI skips all meters" as "AI has no limits."** *They are not the same sentence and the difference is the whole design. **The owner replaced a METER with a CAP** — and a cap is the stronger control, because a meter tells you afterwards that something went wrong while a cap makes it impossible. ⛔ But a cap only works if it is enforced at the point of resource allocation, not checked afterwards: **if the concurrency limit is a number on a settings page that nothing reads, there is no meter AND no cap, and the first anyone hears of it is a customer getting a busy signal.***

## 171B.1 ⭐⭐⭐ P-190 — THE DIALER LAW *(owner, T677 — supersedes §160.1's scope and §171A's proposal)*

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **AI is not metered. At all.** | **AI-dialed and AI-answered calls are excluded from every abandonment computation — numerator, denominator and the check itself.** The AI→human handoff is **also exempt** *(owner, overruling §171A's handoff case)*. |
| ⛔ **`silent_answer_rate` — RETIRED before it was built** | *(owner: "not needed, exclude from measuring")* — **and it is not needed because the cap below removes the condition it was invented to detect.** |
| ⭐⭐ **AI concurrency: 10 lines per account** | the default. **Raised only by an admin on request** — never by the tenant, never by a plan tier. |
| ⭐ **Human dialer: max 3 lines per agent** | the hard ceiling on the human side. |
| ⭐⭐ **Breach of 3% → automatic drop to 1 line per agent** | ⛔ **This is what the 3% now DOES.** It is no longer a number that raises an alert — **it is a trigger that changes the dial ratio automatically.** *That is a materially better law than the one it replaces: the old ceiling reported a breach, this one ends it.* |
| ⭐ **Max 20 channels on an account** | the total concurrency ceiling. **Raised only by an admin on request.** |

⭐⭐ **Why the cap beats the meter, stated plainly:** *`silent_answer_rate` existed to catch the moment AI concurrency ran out and a caller heard nothing. **With a hard cap of 10 lines, concurrency cannot run out — the eleventh call is never placed.** A limit you cannot exceed is strictly better than a number you have to watch, and it needs no dashboard, no threshold and no owner decision.* **The owner replaced a measurement with a constraint. That is the right move and it removes an open item rather than answering it.**

### ⚠️ ONE NUMBER NEEDS ONE WORD — and it is not a quibble

**Does the AI's 10 lines sit INSIDE the account's 20 channels, or on top of them?**

⛔ **It matters because of P-095 — *the phone keeps answering*.** *If outbound AI dialing can take all 20 channels, **an inbound customer calling that business gets a busy signal while the platform is cold-calling strangers.** That is the single worst thing this product could do, and it is a one-line configuration decision, not a bug anyone would catch in review.*

⭐ **Recommended reading, written as the default and reversible on your word:** **20 is the account's TOTAL concurrency. The AI's 10 outbound lines sit INSIDE it, leaving 10 channels that outbound can never touch — reserved for inbound and human seats.** *An inbound call is never refused because an outbound campaign was busy.* **Reverse word: `outbound-20`** *(if you want the 20 to be outbound-only and inbound to scale separately)*.

## 171B.2 ⭐⭐⭐ P-191 — R19 IS REVERSED · HEALTHCARE AND DENTAL ARE IN, ON A BAA

> *"No isolation, no exclusion — we just sign BAA available."*

⭐ **R19 is struck.** *Human-medical and dental were excluded pending PHI isolation; the owner has chosen a different route — **the vertical is in, and the instrument is a BAA.*** **O-1 closed.**

⛔ **What that means MECHANICALLY for the build — this is the switch, not advice (Q-061 · Law 122):**

| The mechanism | What it does |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **A per-tenant `phi_covered` flag** | set when a BAA is in place. **It is a routing constraint, not a label.** |
| ⭐⭐ **The model roster becomes conditional** | ⛔ **THE SHARP EDGE. A PHI tenant's call transcript, email body or CRM note must only reach a model provider we hold a BAA with.** *Because models are already DATA in C-Ai's routing table (§170.0②), this is a filter on that table and nothing more — **`phi_covered` tenants route only to BAA-covered providers.*** **The plan does not know which providers those are; that is the owner's to establish.** |
| **Retention and access** | X-122 already logs every invocation with user, IP and `actor_type`, and X-121 already FORCEs RLS — **the audit and isolation primitives exist**; the flag turns on the tighter retention window and the minimum-necessary field masking. |
| **Subprocessors** | any provider touching a PHI tenant's data is on the same list as the models — one roster, one flag. |
| ⛔ **The one thing that must NOT happen** | **a healthcare tenant is onboarded and their data flows to a provider with no BAA because the flag exists but nothing reads it.** *The `doctor` assertion: with `phi_covered` set and a non-covered provider in the roster, a send is **refused**, not routed.* |

⭐ **NEW OPEN ITEM — O-12: which providers do we hold a BAA with?** *That list is the only thing standing between this ruling and a working healthcare tenant. It is yours to establish and it lands in C-Ai's table as data.*

## 171B.3 ⭐⭐ P-192 — THE OFF-SWITCH PRINCIPLE

> *"Include an off button — they can turn it off, we have it, if they turn it off it's on them."*

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Every optional guardrail ships ON, with an off switch** | quiet hours, the sub-3% value, the review gate's threshold — the tenant may turn a **courtesy** off. |
| ⭐ **Turning it off is an event, not a setting** | **logged with who, when and from where** *(X-122 already does this for every invocation)*, and the tenant sees **one plain sentence** of what they are taking on before it flips — Q-010: say what the risk means in the real world, no jargon. |
| ⛔⛔ **THE LINE — and it is the whole law** | ⭐ **A tenant may switch off a COURTESY. A tenant may never switch off a FLOOR.** *STOP, suppression, the twenty refusal reasons and `ImportAttestation` are **not switches** — they are P-060's floor and they have no off button on any screen, for any tenant, at any price.* **`doctor` asserts that no floor rule appears in the tenant settings schema.** |

*This is what "if they turn it off it's on them" requires to actually be true: **it is only on them if they were told, and if we can prove they were told.***

## 171B.4 THE ANSWERS YOU ASKED FOR

### ⭐ O-4 — `ProviderWaterfall`, explained plainly

**There are two completely different "waterfalls" in this plan and they share a word:**

| | What it actually does |
| :--- | :--- |
| **X-150 `ProviderWaterfall`** | ⭐ **Data vendors.** We need a fact about a business — an email, a direct dial, what software they run. **We ask vendor 1; if it has nothing, we ask vendor 2; then vendor 3**, until one answers or we run out. It also checks that what came back is the right SHAPE *(a phone number that is actually a phone number)*. |
| **C-Ai's model failover** | ⭐ **AI models.** The model we want is down, slow or rate-limited, **so we fall to the next model on the roster you just set.** |

**Both are "try the next one when the first fails," which is why both got called a waterfall.** ⛔ **The risk is not cosmetic:** *an agent reading a header called `ProviderWaterfall` reasonably assumes it means AI providers and builds model failover inside a data-enrichment module — or reads C-Ai and builds enrichment there. **Two squads, two headers, one word, the same thing built twice in the wrong places.** That is the F-12 defect and it has now been found four times in this plan.*

**Your two options:** ⭐ **(a) rename X-150 to `DataProviderWaterfall`** — one word, the ambiguity is gone permanently, the number never changes · **(b) leave the name and rely on the action ids** *(`enrichment.provider_next` vs `model.failover`)* to keep them apart. ⭐ **My recommendation: rename.** *It costs one line today and it costs a rebuilt module in wave 2.*

### ✅ O-2 — the review gate cannot be "off"

*"There is no point, because a person needs to select a star rating; the system won't proceed unless something is selected."* ⭐ **Understood and closed.** The rating is the first step of the flow, so **the gate is always in the path — the threshold decides routing, it does not decide whether the flow runs.** *"Off" was never a coherent state. `public_threshold` stays 4 default, 5 max, and there is no zero.*

### ✅ O-5 — fixed, not carried: the wallboard is now TWO specs

*You said "not sure what this is, fix it," so here it is fixed rather than explained.* **I had merged six X-200 rows into one spec because they all render on the same TV screen. But merging on the SCREEN is the same error I corrected at §171.6 — the boundary is who DECIDES, not where it shows.** Split:

| Spec | Rows | Owner |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **A — the live wallboard** | `G9-38` TV mode · `G13-02` activity heat | ⭐ **operations.** Live queue state, team-level. *"Who is waiting right now."* |
| **B — the achievement layer** | `G2-26` anthems · `G2-35` battles · `G2-37` trophies · `G16-15` milestones | ⭐ **people, under §150.4 — positive only.** *No per-person negative tile exists to populate.* |

**Turn 36's count: 28 → 29 specs. `O-5 CLOSED.`**

### ✅ O-6 — nothing needed from you

*W3 carrying 46% of the rows: I know it is 46% of the ROWS; I do not know whether it is 46% of the WORK, because a row that needs its own wizard is about two rows of effort.* **That is a measurement I take at turn 47 when the build order is written. Carried, not open — no input required.**

| **O-10 the demo number** | ⭐ **One phone number, designated as the demo line.** X-161 reads a single config key. *You either point at a number you already own or buy one.* **That is the entire ask, and the demo machine cannot answer without it.** |
| **O-11 the skills file** | ⛔ **Nothing needed from you now.** It lands at **turn 86** by the plan and I will ask then. |

### ⭐ LEAST CONFIDENT, clarified — and then retired

*You asked what I meant.* **I was asking whether "a caller answered and heard silence" is one problem or two:** *(a) **our** fault — AI concurrency ran out, which we fix by scaling · (b) **the carrier's** fault — the audio path failed, which we cannot fix and can only report.* **Same silence, two owners, and by the rule at §171.6 that argues for two metrics.** ⛔ **It is moot: you retired the metric and capped the concurrency instead, which removes cause (a) entirely.** *Cause (b) is a carrier delivery outcome and belongs to C-Telephony's outcome set, where it already lives under P-188. **Nothing to build, nothing to decide.***

# 171C. THE NO-HARDCODE LAW · INBOUND UNCAPPED · HIPAA UNGATED · THE MODEL WATERFALL *(T677 · out-of-order insert · ⛔ NOT a turn; turn 37 is still next)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **P-193 is the most load-bearing law the owner has given this arc.** *It is also the one most likely to be recorded as a wish instead of a test, so it is written below with the assertion that makes it real.*

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**"Don't hardcode anything" written as a principle instead of as a lint rule.** *Every codebase in history has that sentence in its README and a `3` on line 412 of a service class. **A principle a builder agrees with and a linter cannot check is decoration.*** ⛔ **And the opposite failure is just as real: if every constant becomes a knob, the platform ships with four hundred settings and a tenant who cannot use any of them — which contradicts the product's whole posture, that the client does nothing that can be inferred.** ⭐ *The law needs both halves: **everything operational is settable, and almost nothing is asked.***

## 171C.1 ⭐⭐⭐ P-193 — THE NO-HARDCODE LAW *(owner, T677)*

> *"Make sure not to hard code anything that should be changeable or adjustable — it all needs to be able to be done in admin without code changes."*

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **The rule** | **Every operational value lives in a settings row, not in code.** A row carries: **scope** *(platform · tenant · campaign)* · **type** · **allowed range** · **who may change it** · **an audit row when it changes**. |
| ⭐⭐ **The line that makes it testable** | **A LAW is a constant. A SETTING is a row.** *P-060's twenty refusal reasons are a closed set **by ruling** — that is a law and it stays in code, because changing it changes what the platform is. The 3% is a **setting** with a hard maximum. The 10 AI lines is a **setting** with an admin-only scope. **If a value can move without changing what the product IS, it is a row.*** |
| ⭐ **The acceptance test — one sentence, and it is what `doctor` proves** | ⛔ **Change the value in admin, observe the behaviour change, with NO deploy.** *If a release is required, it was hardcoded.* |
| **The lint** | `doctor` fails the build on a numeric or string literal in a business-logic path that is not on the structural allow-list *(HTTP codes, array indices, closed enums that are laws)*. **A literal in a rule is a build failure, not a review comment.** |
| ⛔⛔ **The counterpart — settable is NOT the same as asked** | ⭐ **Most settings are operator-scoped and inferred for the tenant.** The tenant is asked only what the wizard confirms once. *"Everything is adjustable" is about where the value LIVES; it is not permission to put four hundred questions in front of a business owner.* |

⭐ **What this law retroactively covers, so nothing has to be re-derived later:** the model roster · the 10 / 3 / 20 dialer numbers · the 3% ceiling · quiet-hours windows · `public_threshold` · the review cycle cap · the demo number · warm-up ramps · complaint thresholds · retention windows · **every threshold written in §165–§171B.** *All of them were already stated as data; **P-193 makes that a build-failing requirement rather than a habit.***

## 171C.2 ✅ P-190 AMENDED — INBOUND IS UNCAPPED

> *"Inbound is unlimited, cap on outbound."*

⭐ **This is the `outbound-20` reading, and it is the safer one — better than the default I wrote.** **The 10 AI lines and the 20 channels are OUTBOUND ceilings. Inbound has no cap.** *P-095 is served exactly: the phone keeps answering, and no outbound campaign can ever produce a busy signal for a real customer.* **O-13 CLOSED.**

⚠️ **One mechanism note, because "unlimited" has to mean something a builder can implement:** *"unlimited" means **we impose no ceiling** — it cannot mean the underlying stack has none. Carrier trunks, LiveKit sessions and model throughput all have real limits.* ⭐ **So: no cap in our code, and an operator alert when inbound concurrency approaches the stack's actual ceiling — early enough to add capacity, never a rejection.** *An inbound call is never refused by us; if the stack is genuinely at its limit that is a capacity incident with a name and an owner, not a silent busy tone.*

## 171C.3 ✅ P-191 REPLACED — NO HIPAA GATING AT ALL

> *"There is no HIPAA gating, we just offer a BAA in the account. Overrule all HIPAA rules. Anyone can sign up. If they need a BAA it's there in the account."*

⭐ **Recorded, and it simplifies the build to nothing:** **no `phi_covered` flag · no routing constraint · no vertical exclusion · no gate. Anyone signs up. The BAA is a document available in the account.** *R19 stays struck; §171B.2's mechanism is withdrawn before it was built.*

⭐⭐ **And the build needs no new machinery for it — because of something already true:** ***models are DATA in C-Ai's routing table (§170.0②), so "which providers touch tenant data" is answerable from the config at any moment, not from anyone's memory.*** **That is the only thing the build side owes a BAA: a data flow that can be stated accurately.** *It already can.*

⚠️ **Said once, plainly, and then dropped (Q-061 — the plan builds, it does not advise):** *a BAA is a statement about where data goes. Keeping it is a business matter and yours; **the engineering fact is simply that our data flow is documentable, which it is.*** **O-12 is closed as a build item** and moves to your side as a business one — **nothing in the plan gates on it, so nothing is blocked.**

## 171C.4 ⭐⭐ THE MODEL WATERFALL — YOUR DESIGN, PLUS SIX RECOMMENDATIONS

**Your design, recorded:** *a cron checks provider up-status · the roster is ordered best → least · fall down the list.* ⭐ **Right shape. Here is what makes it hold under load — six additions, each one a row or a column, none a new module.**

| # | Recommendation | Why it matters |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **1** | **A cron is necessary and NOT sufficient — add a circuit breaker on live results.** *A cron tells you a provider was reachable 60 seconds ago. **It does not tell you the provider is rate-limiting YOU, right now** — which is the far more common failure: quota exhausted, a key throttled, a burst rejected.* **N failures in a rolling window → open the breaker, skip that provider, half-open retry after a cooldown.** ⭐ *The cron catches "it is down." The breaker catches "it is down for us." You need both, and the second fires ten times more often.* |
| ⭐⭐ **2** | **Probe with a real 5-token completion, never a `/health` endpoint.** *A status page and actual token throughput are different things — a provider can return 200 on health and time out on inference.* **The honest probe is the smallest real call.** |
| ⭐⭐ **3** | **Order best→least PER JOB, not globally.** *You are already doing this — scrapers get the cheap model, escalation gets the strong one. So the roster is a table of **(job, rank, provider)**, not one list.* **One extra column, and it stops "the best model" being spent on a scrape at forty times the cost.** |
| ⭐⭐ **4** | ⛔ **The bottom of the waterfall is a REFUSAL, never a worse answer.** *If every provider for a job is down, the temptation is to fall to something weaker and answer anyway.* **For anything customer-facing that is exactly P-092: say we cannot, create the task, hand it to a human.** ⭐ *A wrong answer in the customer's inbox costs more than a missing one.* |

# 172. THE MASTER-LAW RETROFIT — THE PROGRAM *(T677 · ⛔ THIS IS THE PLAN, NOT THE EXECUTION · not a turn; Law 127 holds at 109)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **The owner asked for a plan before execution, across multiple turns, retroactive to every document and module, with a tracking file of my own. This is that plan. Five phases, one new file, five questions.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Retrofitting 110 modules by hand.** *Seven cross-cutting laws × 110 modules is 770 edits, and 770 hand-edits produce drift, not compliance — half will say the law in different words, a dozen will contradict it by accident, and no one will ever be able to prove which. ⭐ **The seven laws are the SAME for every module. So they get written ONCE and inherited, and the retrofit becomes an EXCEPTION LIST, not a rewrite.*** *That is the same insight that produced the group-level grep at §170.1 and the ⑥⑦ inheritance rule — **assert once, deviate rarely, prove by absence.** A retrofit designed any other way is a month of typing and a false sense of coverage.*

## 172.1 ⭐⭐ THE ARCHITECTURE — ASSERT ONCE, DEVIATE RARELY

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **The seven laws are written ONCE** | as **§173 `ML-1 … ML-7`**, each reconciled against the existing law register, with conflicts named and resolved or escalated. |
| ⭐⭐ **The header contract gains ONE line** | **`@laws ML-1…ML-7 — inherited in full unless this module states a deviation.`** *One line per module, not seven paragraphs.* |
| ⭐ **The retrofit is therefore an EXCEPTION LIST** | **The measured blast radius: 90 of 110 modules have a real SCREENS block *(ML-2 · ML-3 bite there)*, 59 mention an API, credential, adapter or token *(ML-4 bites there)*, and every module is inside a lane *(ML-1)*.** **Deviations are expected in perhaps 10–15 modules, not 110.** |
| ⭐ **Compliance becomes provable, not claimed** | a `doctor` rule per law, and a grid file that shows the state of every module × every law. *A blank cell and a finished cell must never look alike — the §169.7 lesson.* |

⛔ **Law 127 is untouched. None of this is a turn.** *§172 · §173 · §174 are inserts, exactly like §167A, §168A and §171A–D. **The 109 remain 109 and turn 37 still runs next.***

## 172.3 ⭐⭐ ML-7, RESHAPED — THE LIVING BRAIN WITHOUT THE DRIFT

*You want a system that learns and improves its own prompts. **That is achievable and it is a good idea. What is not survivable is prompts that change with no version, no evidence and no way back.*** The shape:

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **A prompt is a VERSIONED ARTIFACT**, not a string in code | it has an id, a version, an author *(human or model)* and a created-at. P-193 already puts it in a row. |
| ⭐ **The AI Core PROPOSES, it does not publish** | a generated improvement lands as **version N+1, inactive.** |
| ⭐⭐ **`X-149 AgentEvals` is the gate** | the proposal runs against a **fixed** eval set and is **promoted only if it beats the incumbent.** *The module whose whole job is "the conscience" already exists for this.* |
| ⭐ **The old version is retained and revertible in one click** | a regression has a cause and an undo. |
| ⭐ **Tenant overrides are a LAYER, never an edit** | a tenant's customisation sits on top of the baseline and travels with them through every baseline upgrade — **so improving the baseline never silently rewrites what a tenant tuned.** |
| ⭐ **The learning loop's input is RESOLUTION DATA** | *(did the conversation resolve, did the human take over, did the customer come back)* — real outcomes, not the model's opinion of itself. |

⭐⭐⭐ **Under this shape P-097 survives untouched: a human correction still writes a `Fact` and never edits a prompt. The MACHINE proposes prompt versions; the EVAL promotes them; the human can always revert.** *You get the self-correcting brain. You also get to answer "why did it do that" — which you cannot do any other way.*

## 173.2 ⭐⭐⭐ SEVEN ADDITIONS — EACH ONE IS THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN "ONE GO" AND "MONTHS OF PASSES"

*You asked what I would add. These are the seven, in the order I would fight for them.*

### ⭐⭐⭐ A-1 · THE DEFINITION OF DONE — ten machine-checked conditions **(the most important thing in this section)**

⛔ **Right now "finished" is an opinion, and ninety agents will each hold a different one.** *A module can pass every slice gate and still ship with an empty screen, no seed data, no admin, and a README nobody wrote.* ⭐ **A module is DONE only when all ten pass — `doctor` runs them, and nothing merges without all ten green:**

| # | Condition | Why it exists |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1** | every `@provides` action reachable through the registry, none orphaned | the seam holds |
| **2** | every `@emits` event has at least one subscriber **or a stated reason it has none** | the §169.4 finding, as a gate |
| **3** | every screen in `SCREENS` **exists, renders with real seeded data, and has no lorem, no TODO, no placeholder** | ⛔ **the anti-skeleton condition** |
| **4** | every tenant-facing string is a **row**, not a literal | P-193, pointed at the UI |
| **5** | the module's **seed manifest** is satisfied *(A-3 below)* | it is demonstrable, not theoretical |
| **6** | every capability's ⑤ test passes **AND its runtime proof is attached** | Law 4 — a test supplies its own input |
| **7** | `NEEDS` is satisfiable and `HAS` returns real values | the orchestrator can schedule it |
| **8** | it is **operable from the operator console** — no terminal, no database client *(A-6)* | ⭐ one person has to run this |
| **9** | rollback rehearsed **once**, on this module, with a passing restore | *(A-7)* |
| **10** | the module's brief **regenerates from the plan** and is ≤20k | Q-086 — no fork |

⭐⭐ **This is the single highest-value thing I can add.** *Everything else in this section serves one of the ten.*

### ⭐⭐⭐ A-2 · TWELVE END-TO-END JOURNEYS — the real acceptance test

⛔ **Module tests prove a module works. They do not prove the PRODUCT works — and that gap is exactly the four-features-that-passed-and-did-not-run failure.** ⭐ **Twelve journeys that cross modules and must pass on real runtime:**

⭐⭐ **If those twelve pass on real runtime, the system works. If they do not, nothing else matters.** *They are the acceptance criteria for the whole build, and they belong in `GOAIEZ-TESTING-PLAN.md` — which is a skeleton waiting for exactly this.*

⛔ ***"Seed with real premium content"* with no contract means every agent invents its own** — one module ships with forty seeded rows and the next with zero, and you discover it during a demo. ⭐ **Each module declares a seed manifest: what must exist for it to be demonstrable** — *N templates · N sample records · N images with their sources · one worked example end to end.* **`doctor` COUNTS them.** *Stock imagery is permitted here and only here; **P-131 still forbids it anywhere a real job, customer or result is shown.***

Nobody can.** ⭐ **The audit is per WAVE GATE — four sessions — and what you and Gemini review is NOT the code:** *the diff against the spec · the runtime-proof artifacts · the twelve journeys' pass state · the DoD grid.* **Four reviews of evidence, not 110 reviews of code.** *That is tractable for one person, and it is the only version of "audited by you and Gemini" that can actually happen.*

# 176. CODE AUDIT 1 — THE MODEL ROSTER IS AN ENUM · P-194 THE OPEN ROSTER LAW *(T677 · ⛔ not a turn)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **Raw code access earned its keep on the first read. The owner asked for adding a model to be INSTANT. It currently requires editing two PHP enums and deploying — and four of the five providers he named do not exist in the code at all.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Believing the dump's own summary instead of the file.** *Section 3 says: **"Hardcoded models purged in favour of config-driven routing."** ⭐ Read against the code, that sentence is **half true and it is the dangerous half.*** *The model strings WERE collected out of scattered literals into one place — a real improvement. **But the place they were collected into is `enum AiModel: string`, which is CODE.** Prices too — `inputPricePerMillion()` is a `match` expression with the figures written into it, under a comment that says **"prices belong in code so they are reviewable."*** ⛔ **That comment is a considered engineering opinion, written in good faith, and it is the exact opposite of P-193.** *This is what a line-by-line audit is for: the summary said "purged," the file says "relocated."*

## 176.1 ⛔⛔ THE FINDING

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **What the code has** | `enum AiModel: string` with **7 cases**: `claude-opus-5` · `claude-sonnet-5` · `claude-haiku-4-5` · `gpt-4o-mini` · `gpt-5-mini` · `gpt-image-1-mini` · `text-embedding-3-small`. Plus `enum AiProvider` with **two** cases: `Anthropic`, `OpenAi`. |

That is not instant; it is the definition of hardcoded.** |
| ⛔ **Prices are in code too** | `inputPricePerMillion()` is a `match` with published figures inline and a `VERIFIED_ON = '2026-08-12'` constant. **P-193 and P-092 both say a price is a row that is looked up.** |

⭐⭐ **AND THE REASONING IN THE FILE IS GOOD — which is why this needs care, not a rebuke.** *The comment explains that a vendor price was once wrong for a day because a figure was recorded and never re-read, and concludes that **prices in code are reviewable and a config value is not.*** ⛔ **The conclusion is wrong, but the problem it names is real** — and the fix must solve that problem, not dismiss it.

## 176.2 ⭐⭐⭐ P-194 — THE OPEN ROSTER LAW *(owner, T677: include GPT-4o-Mini, all named models, and make expansion instant)*

⭐ **The elegant resolution of the whole GPT-4o-Mini argument: it was never wrong that a model got used. It was wrong that using it required no registration.** **So the roster becomes instant to add to — and impossible to bypass.**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **The roster is a TABLE, not an enum** | `ai_models` — id · provider · vendor string · job classes it may serve · rank within each class · input and output price · **`verified_on`** · enabled. **Adding a model is INSERTING A ROW. No deploy, ever.** |
| ⭐⭐ **The providers are rows too** | `ai_providers` — **OpenAI · Anthropic · Google · xAI · self-hosted**, each with its adapter key and its credential reference *(X-206)*. **Adding a whole provider is a row plus an adapter, never an enum edit.** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **Impossible to bypass** | ⛔ **`doctor` fails the build on ANY model string in code that is not read from the table.** *That is what actually solves the GPT-4o-Mini incident — not purging the model, but making an unregistered model uncallable.* |
| ⭐⭐ **The price problem the comment raised, solved properly** | *A row is not less reviewable than code — an UNWATCHED row is.* **So: `verified_on` per row, a cron that re-reads published pricing and RAISES when a row drifts, and a stale row (>N days unverified) shows in the operator console.** ⭐ **The original defect was a price nobody re-read. A column with an alarm on it beats a constant nobody re-reads, and it does not need a release to correct.** |
| ✅ **GPT-4o-Mini** | ⭐ **INCLUDED, by the owner's ruling.** ⚠️ *Gemini's Directive 1 item 3 ordered it purged in the same message — **the owner's word outranks the relay, and it is recorded as INCLUDED.*** |
| ⭐ **The roster of record** | GPT-4o-Mini · GPT-5-Mini · **Luna Mini 5.6** · **Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite** · **Grok 4.1 Fast** · Claude Haiku · **Claude Sonnet (escalation, capped)** · **Gemma 2.5 Flash-Lite** · Claude Opus · the image and embedding models. **All rows. All editable. All extensible in one INSERT.** |

⛔ **Wave-0 consequence: `ai_models` and `ai_providers` are SPINE tables and belong in W0 with the rest of the routing substrate** — every wave-1 module that calls a model reads them.

# 178. THE EIGHT, VERSION 2 — THE FALLBACK GOT MORE EXPENSIVE · VISION IS A GATE, NOT A JUDGE · THE VAULT NEEDS A SCOPE *(T677 · ⛔ not a turn)*

> ⭐ **Law 3 is reconciled and closed. Three new findings, all mechanical, all one line to fix. And the one column I asked for is still not in Law 7.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**A failure path that is more expensive than the happy path.** *The fallback used to be "Mini." It is now **"GPT-4o for heavy lifting."*** ⛔⛔ **So a missing or expired key no longer degrades — it UPGRADES, silently, to a flagship-priced model.** *Nobody chose that route; it is what happens when something is broken.* ⭐ **The path nobody chose should be the CHEAPEST one, not the smartest one** — because the trigger is an infrastructure failure, and an infrastructure failure that quietly multiplies your per-conversation cost is a bill you find in a statement, not an alert.

## 178.1 ✅ WHAT IS NOW CLOSED

⭐ **Law 3 is reconciled: *"200 templates… across 80 distinct industries (launching with 20 core industries perfectly seeded)."*** **That matches the owner's ruling exactly and my §177 flag is withdrawn.** *Under P-193 the count stays a setting; 20 is the launch value and 80/200 are growth targets.*

## 178.2 ⛔ FINDING 1 — THE FALLBACK NEEDS A CEILING, NOT JUST A COLUMN

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔ **What changed** | fallback widened from Mini to **the full flagship suite** — *"GPT-4o-Mini for volume, GPT-4o for heavy lifting."* |
| ⛔⛔ **Why that is worse, not better** | **The fallback fires when a key is null or invalid.** *That is an outage condition.* **Under the new wording an outage routes you to the most expensive model in the suite, on every affected call, until someone notices.** |
| ⭐⭐ **The fix — one rule** | **The fallback picks the CHEAPEST OpenAI model that satisfies the job class. Never the flagship, unless the flagship is explicitly set as that job's fallback in the table** *(P-194 — it is a column)*. **Degrade cheap; escalate only by choice.** |
| ⛔ **AND THE COLUMN IS STILL MISSING** | *Law 7 v2 does not carry it.* ⭐ **Every call records the model REQUESTED and the model SERVED; a difference is a `model.substituted` event; X-149 EXCLUDES substituted calls from every comparison.** **Without it, the moment the fallback fires, every Haiku-vs-Sonnet conclusion in the plan is unverifiable — and nobody will know which ones.** *I said this was the one thing to carry into code. It is still the one thing.* |

⭐ **A calm note on *"5.6 Luna and Grok 4.1 are futuristic relative to today."*** **That is exactly why P-194 makes them ROWS.** *If a model name turns out not to exist, its row fails its health probe and is disabled — **no code change, no deploy, no drama.*** **The architecture already absorbs that uncertainty, which is the point of having built it that way.**

## 178.3 ⛔ FINDING 2 — VISION IS A GATE, NOT A JUDGE

**Using GPT-4o Vision to look at the rendered mock site is a good idea and I want to keep it.** ⭐ **But it does two very different jobs and only one of them is reliable:**

| The job | Verdict |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Detecting BROKEN** — garbled text in the image, wrong aspect ratio, missing logo, obvious artefacts, a hero that rendered blank | ✅ **Vision does this well, at scale, with no human. Keep it exactly as designed — this is ~90% of the labour.** |
| ⛔⛔ **Ranking "which one looks better"** | ⚠️ **Not reliable and not stable** — run the same pair twice and the winner can change; *"aesthetic layout"* is not a quantity a vision model measures. ⛔ **And the decision is permanent and commercial: which model renders your clients' hero images forever. That is a BRAND decision wearing a QA decision's clothes.** |

⭐⭐⭐ **The fix keeps the automation and costs an hour, once:**
1. **Vision is the GATE** — it rejects broken images automatically. No human, at scale.
2. **The owner is the TIE-BREAK** — of the images that pass the gate, ~20 blind pairs, once. **The result becomes rows *(surface → model)* and after that it is automatic forever.**
3. ⭐⭐ **AND THE CALIBRATION STEP THAT SETTLES THE ARGUMENT WITH EVIDENCE:** **run the vision scorer on the same pairs the owner judged and see whether it agrees.** *If it agrees, trust it from then on and stop asking him.* ⛔ **If it disagrees, you have just learned the scores are noise — BEFORE they set your brand defaults, instead of after.** *That costs nothing and it is the only honest way to decide whether the automated judge is any good.*

⚠️ **And vision calls are not free.** *Scoring every seeded image across 90 modules is a second bill on top of generation.* **The image budget cap from §177.3 covers generation AND scoring, or it covers neither.**

## 178.4 ⛔ FINDING 3 — THE VAULT NEEDS A SCOPE, AND `.env` NEEDS AN EXIT

⭐ **The redefinition is right: a credential registry with a Reveal button beats a black hole. A tenant's own key is theirs and they must be able to get it back.** ⛔ **But the law treats one thing that is actually two:**

| Credential | Reveal? |
| :--- | :--- |
| **The TENANT's own keys** *(their Google, their Stripe, their Zernio, their BYOK model key)* | ✅ **Yes — theirs, they gave it to us, they get it back.** |
| ⛔⛔ **PLATFORM credentials** *(our Infobip, our model-provider keys, our SES)* | ⛔ **Never to a tenant. And never the platform's to an AGENCY sub-tenant.** |

⭐⭐ **The fix is one line: REVEAL IS SCOPED BY OWNERSHIP.** *Every credential row carries an owner — platform · agency · tenant.* **You may reveal what you own. You may never reveal what you do not.** ⛔ **Written as one undifferentiated "the vault has a reveal button," the swarm builds one screen and the scoping question never gets asked at all.** ⭐ **And every reveal is a logged event (X-122) — which is also what makes *"they revealed it and it leaked, that is on them"* actually provable, the same shape as P-192.**

⚠️ **`.env` for wave-0 testing quietly reopens the hardcode**, and the fix is small:
- ⭐ **`.env` is permitted for the PLATFORM's own bootstrap keys only.** ⛔ **`doctor` asserts that no TENANT credential is ever read from `.env`.**
- ⭐⭐ **And a W0 EXIT CONDITION: before wave 0's gate passes, every key in `.env` that belongs in the registry has moved there.** *Otherwise a key sits in a file forever, nobody can rotate it from the admin UI, and the Reveal button shows nothing — which is exactly the failure the registry was created to prevent.*

**Law 8 v2 still reads *"Claude and Gemma autonomously generate all system prompts… the system analyzes data to constantly improve baseline prompts."*** ⛔ **The eval gate and the one-click revert are still absent — the fifth time.** *The reshape is ticked and stands, so nothing is broken.*

⭐⭐ **But flagging it a sixth time is not a strategy. The process fix: WRITE THE RESHAPE INTO THE LAW'S OWN TEXT, so a re-send carries it instead of dropping it.** **Law 8 of record now reads:**

> *Prompt generation: the AI Core **proposes** a baseline prompt as version N+1, inactive. **`X-149 AgentEvals` promotes it only if it beats the incumbent on a fixed eval set.** The prior version is retained and **revertible in one click**. A tenant's override is a **layer**, never an edit to the baseline. The learning loop's input is **resolution data** — did it resolve, did a human take over, did the customer return — never the model's assessment of itself. **P-097 is untouched: a human correction writes a `Fact`, never a prompt edit.***

# 179. LAW 10 — ALREADY LAW, AND STRONGER · THE PRICING-PAGE FINDING *(T677 · ⛔ not a turn)*

Same source, same second, no exceptions.**

# 180. THE OWNER CORRECTS THE VAULT · MODULE-COMPLETE vs WAVES · THE THIRD-PARTY REGISTER *(T677 · ⛔ not a turn)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **Two of Gemini's rulings are overruled by the owner in the same exchange. One strategy change lands that needs reconciling with the wave model. And a thirteenth file exists because he named a risk class nothing in the plan was catching.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**"Every module fully tested before the next" taken literally.** *It is the right instinct and it is what saves the months of re-passes — **but a module cannot be fully tested before the modules it DEPENDS on exist**, and the twelve E2E journeys cross six modules each. ⛔ Read as "finish X-01 completely, then start X-10," it produces a module tested against mocks of things not built yet — **which is a DoD grid full of greens and a product that does not run.** ⭐ **The reconciliation is not a compromise: the WAVE ORDER is exactly what makes module-complete possible.** A module reaches DONE when everything in its `@needs` is already DONE. **You never revisit a module because you never start one early.***

## 180.1 ⛔ TWO OWNER CORRECTIONS TO THE RELAYED RULINGS

### ① THE VAULT — the owner's scope, not the relay's

**Gemini ruled:** *platform keys **permanently hidden**; BYOK for LLMs **active for enterprise**.*
⭐ **The owner ruled otherwise, and his version is different in three ways:**

| | ⭐ **The owner's rule** |
| :--- | :--- |
| **What the vault is FOR** | ⛔ **NOT for tenants to supply their own AI models.** It is for **any key to an external service the tenant connects** — their Google, their Stripe, their booking tool. |
| **Who can see a tenant's key** | **the tenant** — and ⭐⭐ **the ADMIN too, deliberately: *"admin can see them as well to support them if they need help."*** |
| **Our own keys** | ⭐ **all platform keys go in the vault too.** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **The PURPOSE, stated plainly** | ***"the idea is to never be locked out of an API."*** **The vault is an ANTI-LOCKOUT REGISTER, not a security black box** — and that single sentence resolves every design question about it. |

⛔ **Admin-can-see-tenant-keys is a real capability with a real exposure, and the owner has ruled it in. It is not mine to argue with — it is mine to make safe:** ⭐⭐ **every reveal is a logged event carrying WHO, WHEN and WHICH KEY, and the tenant can SEE that log.** *Support still works. Nothing is silent.* **And it protects the owner more than the tenant: if a key ever leaks, he can show exactly who opened it and when — which is the difference between an incident and an accusation.** *(P-192's shape: allowed, recorded, provable.)*

⚠️ **One line needed: BYOK for AI models.** *Gemini says active for enterprise; the owner says the vault is not for clients' own AI models.* ⭐ **Recorded the narrow, safe way: AI model keys are PLATFORM-provided and metered through C-Billing; the vault holds external-service keys.** *Nothing is killed — if enterprise BYOK is wanted later it is its own capability with its own decision.* ⭐ **And it makes the fallback rule matter MORE: every fallback spends OUR money, so "degrade to the cheapest" is not a preference, it is the budget.**

### ② THE IMAGE TEST — scoped down, exactly as he asked

> *"We do not want huge API costs… the idea of these tests is also to decide the best image model on ChatGPT to use for now, since this is the only image model we have right now, and it will expand in the future."*

⭐⭐ **Stock-first collapses the test set, which is the cheapest possible answer:**
1. **Unsplash and Pexels are provisioned and tried FIRST.** *(Free. Gemini's ruling, and it removes most of the bill.)*
2. **Generation only on a stock MISS** — custom, branded, industry-specific assets stock cannot supply.
3. ⭐⭐ **So the A/B runs on the generate-only set — tens of images, not hundreds.** *"We do not want huge API costs" is satisfied by the ORDER, not by a cap alone.*
4. **The comparison is between OpenAI's own image tiers** *(the only provider we have)*, **and the result is rows** — `surface → model`. ⭐ **When another provider appears it is a row (P-194), not a rebuild.**

## 180.2 ⭐⭐⭐ "EVERY MODULE FULLY TESTED BEFORE THE NEXT" — RECONCILED, NOT COMPROMISED

**What he wants:** *no going back through every module again; each one finished before the next; a 95% sellable product out of the first coding run.*

⭐⭐ **This is achievable and the wave model is what makes it achievable — but two things have to be said honestly:**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **TRUE at the module level** | **A module reaches DONE when every module in its `@needs` is already DONE.** *That is precisely what `@needs` was written for.* **Nothing is revisited because nothing starts early.** |
| ⛔ **NOT TRUE at the journey level, and it cannot be** | **The money journey crosses six modules** — C-Telephony · C-Sms · C-Agent · X-163 · X-108 · X-01. **It is not testable until the LAST of the six is done.** *That is not a flaw in the plan; it is what "end to end" means.* ⭐ **The journey test IS the wave gate.** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **THE RECOMMENDATION THAT SERVES THE GOAL BEST** | ⛔ **Do not build wave 1 in module-number order. Build the MONEY JOURNEY's modules first, in dependency order, each to full DoD.** *W0 is required and unavoidable. After that, the shortest path to something sellable is the six modules that journey touches — **not the 23 modules that happen to be labelled W1.*** **The rest of W1 follows once the journey runs.** ⭐ *That is the difference between "95% of a platform" and "100% of the thing you can sell, plus 95% of the rest."* |

⭐ **On "we can use as many turns as we need and code as we document" — that is already the plan and it is now stronger than Option 2:** six prep turns → handoff → **turns 50–76 and 93–109 written against running code.** *Nothing to change.*

## 180.3 ⭐⭐ THE AUDIT PROTOCOL — RECORDED AS LAW

> *"Every time I get an output from Antigravity I give the evidence file to you both. Once both agree we go to the next step."*

⭐ **This is the two-pass rule applied to the audit itself, and it is a genuinely good control.** **Recorded:** ⛔ **A wave advances only when BOTH independent audits agree it should.** *Neither audit alone can pass a wave.*

⚠️ **The clause it needs, because it will happen: WHEN THE TWO AUDITS DISAGREE, THE DISAGREEMENT GOES TO THE OWNER WITH BOTH POSITIONS STATED IN FULL.** ⛔ **It is never averaged, never split, and never resolved by whichever answer came second.** *Two reviewers who converge to avoid disagreeing are one reviewer.*

## 180.4 ⭐⭐⭐ FILE 13 — `GOAIEZ-THIRD-PARTY-REGISTER.md`

> *"We may not be able to test [something] because we don't have that third-party software, and it becomes a support issue when the client has it."*

⭐⭐ **He named a risk class that nothing in the plan was catching, and he is right that it is a support disaster waiting to happen.** ⛔ **A module can pass all ten DoD conditions against a MOCK and be broken the first time a real customer connects a real account — and the grid would show green.**

**So the register does one thing that matters:** ⭐⭐⭐ **it turns *"we could not test that"* into a FLAG ON THE CAPABILITY. A module whose integration was never verified against the real service is `DONE-UNVERIFIED`, not `DONE` — visible in the DoD grid, in every evidence dump, and in the register.** *When a client hits it: we already knew, we already said so, and we already know which module to open.*

**42 external services counted across the plan and bucketed by the wave that first needs them.** ⭐ **The two signups that gate the first sellable thing: Infobip and LiveKit.** ⭐ **The two that are free and save real money: Unsplash and Pexels.** ⛔ **The block most likely to ship unverified: the FSM competitors (Housecall Pro · ServiceTitan · Jobber) — paid, gated APIs on competitor platforms.** *A tenant migrating off ServiceTitan is a high-value customer and a high-risk first week — **knowing the connector is unverified means you price it as a managed migration instead of being surprised.***

**CHECKED:** the owner's vault ruling read against Gemini's and the **three differences isolated** *(not for AI models · admin can see tenant keys · all platform keys go in too)*, with his stated purpose — *never be locked out of an API* — taken as the design principle rather than inferred · **42 external services counted by script** across the master plan and dated by wave · the money journey's module set enumerated *(six modules)* to show why journey-level testing cannot be module-serial · the audit-agreement protocol given its **disagreement clause**, because a control with no defined failure path is not a control.
**FAILS IF:** ⛔ **`DONE-UNVERIFIED` is invented and never used.** *It is the easiest status in the world to skip — the mock passed, the grid is green, the wave is late.* ⭐ **The guard: the evidence dump's header must state, per module, which integrations were verified against a REAL service and which were mocked. If that line is absent from a dump, the wave is not audited — it is described.**
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **building the money journey's six modules ahead of the rest of W1.** *It is the shortest path to something sellable and I believe it strongly — **but it means six modules from three different squads run first, and the wave model exists partly to keep squads out of each other's way.*** ⛔ **If the squads collide, the fix is to finish W1 in wave order and accept a later first sale.** *I would try the journey-first order and watch the first collision, rather than assume either way.*

# 182. THE CLOSING FOUR — WHAT IS STILL TRUE AFTER EVERYTHING IS LOCKED *(T677 · ⛔ not a turn)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **Every fixture is assigned, every suggestion is approved, and the plan is closable. Four things remain true that nothing in it currently catches — and one of them is the difference between an audit and a formality.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Auditing a document the swarm wrote about itself.** *We have a Definition of Done, twelve journeys, a `doctor` runner, evidence dumps, dual audit and rollback. **All of it reads what the swarm chose to report.*** ⛔ **The first dump already reported three of ten conditions and graded a simulation as a pass. It was caught by careful reading — which is not a control, it is luck with a good habit.** ⭐⭐ **Two AI reviewers reading one self-report is still one self-report. The loop does not close until at least one signal in the dump comes from somewhere the swarm cannot write to.**

## 182.1 ⛔⛔ THE GENERATED-CONTENT CLAIM RISK — THE ONE THAT BECOMES A LEGAL PROBLEM

**The 100-industry answer is right and it is the cheap way to do it:** *blueprints hold the structure — services, pricing units, lifecycle — and the Content Engine generates the copy at seed time.* ⭐ **No one should hand-write 100 static text files.** ⛔ **But generated copy about a business collides with two live laws, and it collides quietly:**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔ **P-092 — a price is looked up or refused, never generated** | *The blueprint carries "standard pricing units" and the engine generates "pricebook descriptions."* ⭐⭐ **The plan already solved this and the code already implements it: `PriceBook` exposes unconfirmed pricing with an `is_sample` flag that forces the AI to refuse to quote it.** ⛔ **So the rule is: EVERY generated seed price is born `is_sample = true`, and the agent refuses it until a human confirms.** *That is one flag and it is already written — it just has to apply to generated content too, not only to imported content.* |
| ⛔⛔ **P-120 — every claim verifiable** | *Generated landing-page and ad copy for 20 industries **will** contain claims: "licensed, bonded and insured," "serving the area since 1998," "trusted by hundreds of local businesses."* ⛔ **Those are FACTS ABOUT A BUSINESS WE DO NOT HAVE. A generated claim that is not true is the tenant's legal exposure and our reputational one, and it ships on their website under their name.** |

⭐⭐⭐ **THE RULE THAT FIXES BOTH, and it is one lint:** **the Content Engine may generate STRUCTURE and DESCRIPTION. It may not generate CLAIMS, CREDENTIALS, NUMBERS or DATES.**

> *"We repair water heaters, replace them, and handle emergency leaks" — **generate freely.*** *"Licensed, bonded and insured since 1998, trusted by over 500 local families" — **never generated. It is a `Fact`, confirmed once by the tenant, or the sentence does not exist.***

⭐ **The mechanism already exists in the plan: it is the same shape as §37.3's review-reply lint — *"how did the repair go"*, never *"mention Dave."*** **A claim lint over generated copy, run at generation time, is a build-failing check and it costs nothing.**

⚠️ **And one number in the blueprint list should not be there: *"tax rates."*** ⛔ **§145.4 killed jurisdiction logic — no nexus, a rate per pricebook.** ⭐ **The blueprint carries a tax-rate FIELD, never a VALUE. The tenant sets it once.** *An archetype that ships a guessed tax rate is a wrong invoice with our name on it.*

## 182.2 ⭐⭐⭐ THE INDEPENDENT SIGNAL — THE ONE CONTROL THAT IS MISSING

**Everything we built audits the swarm's own account of itself.** ⭐⭐ **One class of evidence cannot be authored by the swarm: evidence that lives in someone else's system.**

| ⭐ Signal | Why it cannot be faked |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **The journey artifacts must be EXTERNAL IDs** | **a real Infobip message id · a real call sid · a real Stripe charge id.** ⛔ **The swarm cannot fabricate an id that the vendor's own dashboard will confirm.** *This is why E0 — one real text, one real call — was always the load-bearing test, and it is why the money journey's proof must be external ids rather than log lines.* |
| ⭐⭐ **The blind spot-check** | ⛔ **The auditor names three files AFTER reading the dump, and the swarm returns those exact files.** *It cannot pre-select what looks good if it does not know what will be asked.* **Three files per wave. Costs nothing.** |
| ⭐ **Commit hashes that resolve** | a hash in the dump must match the file returned on request. |

⭐⭐ **Add those three and the dual audit stops being two readers of one story.** *That is the difference between an audit and a formality, and it is the last real gap in the control system.*

## 182.3 ⭐⭐ WAVE 0's REAL GATE — STRONGER THAN "TWELVE MODULES PASS DoD"

⛔ **Rollback restores a commit. It cannot restore a decision.** *If the entity graph's shape is wrong, rolling back does not help — **you have to re-decide, after 99 modules were built on it.***

⭐⭐⭐ **So wave 0's gate is not "the twelve pass their DoD." It is:**

> **The GOLDEN TENANT seeds end to end through the spine, and ONE journey runs on it with external artifacts.**

*If the spine's shape is wrong, that fails on twelve modules instead of on a hundred and eleven.* ⭐ **And it dovetails exactly with Suggestion C, which is already approved: prove the line on three modules, then twelve, then let it run.**

## 182.4 ✅ EVERYTHING ELSE IS CLOSED

**The fixture mapping is exactly §181's** *(77 the seed format · 85 the blocked queue + escalation dispatch · 86 the UI kit + five states · **90 the master fixture turn**)* · **the Golden Tenant is mandatory architecture** · **A, B and C approved** · **the vault reconciled — platform keys hidden from tenants and agencies, revealable to the owner, every reveal logged; a BYOK failure refuses and alerts, never silently charging the platform** · **dual audit with owner tie-break** · **`DONE-UNVERIFIED` official.**

⭐ **Nothing in the eight remaining questions from the last five exchanges is still open. The plan is closable.**

**CHECKED:** the 100-industry answer read against **P-092** *(the `is_sample` mechanism, confirmed present in the audited code)* and **P-120** *(the claim law)*, which is how the claim risk surfaced rather than being asserted · *"tax rates"* checked against **§145.4** *(no nexus, a rate per pricebook)* · the control system inventoried end to end and found to consist **entirely of self-report**, which is what makes the external-id requirement a gap rather than a nicety · wave 0's gate re-derived from what rollback **cannot** do.
**FAILS IF:** ⛔ **the claim lint is written as guidance instead of as a check.** *"Do not generate claims" in a prompt is a suggestion to a model that is optimising for persuasive copy — **it will produce "family owned since 1998" because that is what good landing-page copy looks like**, and it will do it on a tenant's live site.* ⭐ **The lint runs at generation time and fails the content, or it is decoration.**
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **whether three blind spot-check files per wave is enough.** *It is enough to make pre-selection unprofitable, which is the point — but a determined harness could still pass three and hide behind a hundred.* ⭐⭐ **I would rather start at three and raise it the first time a spot-check fails than start high and have the ritual abandoned for being slow.** *The external ids are the stronger control; the spot-check is the cheap one.*

# 183. TURN 37 — THE AI CORE *(turn 37 of 109 · T677 · 8 modules · 47 rows)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **Planning is closed. This is the first spec written with every Master Law, every fixture and every audit finding already in force — so nothing here needs retrofitting.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Specifying the AI core as if the AI were trustworthy.** *Every other module in this plan is specced against bugs. **This one is specced against a system that will confidently produce a plausible wrong answer and log it as a success** — and it already has: the first evidence dump graded a simulation as a runtime pass, and the first swarm wave invented a compliance law and shipped it.* ⛔ **So every row below is written on one assumption: the model is a component that can be wrong in a way that looks right.** ⭐ **That is why the fields that matter here are ④ and ⑤ — not what it does, but how you find out it did not.**

## 183.7 ⚠️ ONE NOTE ON THE CADENCE

**Directive 5 estimates four turns an hour and the blueprint complete in under five hours.** ⚠️ *At the depth these passes are written — 47 rows into 32 specs, each with a failure mode a prover can write a case from — **that estimate is optimistic by a wide margin.*** ⭐ **It changes nothing about the plan and I raise it only so the schedule is not built on it: the work is measured in turns, and the turns take as long as the depth takes.** *Depth over count is a standing ruling, and it is the ruling that produced every finding in this arc.*

# 184. TURN 38 — DEMO & MEDIA *(turn 38 of 109 · T677 · 3 modules · 32 rows)*

> ⭐⭐ **The demo machine is the only part of this platform whose entire job is to look real while being fake. Every failure mode in this pass is a variant of one question: can a demo leak into production, or a production fact leak into a demo?**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**A demo that is only pretending to be separate.** *A sandbox that shares a database, a queue, a credit ledger or a phone number with production is not a sandbox — **it is production with a label on it.*** ⛔ **And the failure is asymmetric: a demo that texts a real person, debits a real meter or writes a real row does damage that cannot be undone by deleting the demo.** ⭐ **So separation here is not a setting, it is a property proven by absence — `doctor` asserts a sandbox write cannot reach a production table and a sandbox send cannot reach a driver.** *§153's `is_mock` law and X-161's one-way pull already exist for exactly this; turn 38 is where the media half inherits them.*

# 184A. X-207 `PushEngine` — MINTED · THE FULL SPEC *(T677 · ⛔ an INSERT, not a turn — and that is the point)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **The module is real, the gap is real, and it is minted. But it does not cost three turns, and the marketing half has a scope question that would cost you every tenant you have.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Treating push as free.** *It looks free because it has no carrier — no per-segment fee, no 10DLC brand, no Infobip invoice.* ⛔⛔ **But the cost was never the constraint. CONSENT was.** *P-060's twenty refusal reasons do not ask what a message costs. A customer who agreed to hear from Bob's Plumbing by text has not agreed to hear from Bob's Plumbing by push, and has certainly not agreed to hear from **us**.* ⭐ **So the one law that must survive this module intact: `X-207` is a CHANNEL under `X-204 ConsentService`, exactly like SMS — same permit, same lanes, same STOP, same twenty codes.** ⛔ **It does not get to bypass the gate because it is cheap. A free channel that sends without a permit is not a marketing engine, it is a complaint engine with no marginal cost to stop it.**

## 184A.0 ⛔ THE TURN COUNT — MINTED YES, THREE TURNS NO

⭐ **`X-207 PushEngine` is MINTED.** SQ-1 Channels, **WAVE 1**. **Roster 112. Ceiling X-207.** *The gap is real: without push, the triage loop is silent, the tech app is dead, dispatch has no alert, and the platform has no owned channel at all.*

⛔⛔ **But "expand the Master Plan by 3 turns, total 112" is the one move Law 127 exists to prevent — and §168's own WHAT KILLS THIS was written about exactly this sentence.**

> *"Law 127 is not a target, it is a ceiling with a mechanism: **a turn is added ONLY by removing one.** The measured load made that tempting… and the honest-looking fix is 'give ops two turns and take the count to 110.' **That is how 36 became 70 became 120.**"*

⭐⭐ **And the proportion does not hold anyway.** *Turn 37 specced **8 modules and 47 rows** in one turn. Turn 39 is **15 modules and 71 rows** in one turn.* ⛔ **X-207 is ONE module with ZERO classified register rows — it is new, so it is in none of the 778. Three turns for one module, against fifteen modules in one turn, is not depth; it is a different unit of measurement.**

⭐⭐⭐ **So it lands the way every other major addition in this arc has landed: as an INSERT — §184A — exactly like §167A, §168A, §171A–D and §172–§182.** *That mechanism has been used a dozen times this session, it is how `ConsentService`, `CredentialVault`, the DoD, the twelve journeys, the third-party register and the Golden Tenant all arrived, and **it has never cost a single turn.***
