## 184A.1 ⛔⛔ THE SCOPE QUESTION THAT WOULD COST YOU EVERY TENANT

> *"Tenant Zero has root access to the entire push network to broadcast platform updates and promote GOAIEZ products directly to **all users**."*

⭐ **"All users" is ambiguous, and the ambiguity is the entire risk. There are two populations on this network and they are not the same people:**

| Population | Whose are they | ⭐ May Tenant Zero push to them? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **TENANT USERS** — the business owner, their staff, their techs. **They bought GOAIEZ.** | **ours** | ✅ **YES.** Platform updates, new features, GOAIEZ product marketing. *They are our customers; this is the revenue engine and it is legitimate.* |
| ⛔⛔ **A TENANT'S CUSTOMERS** — the homeowner who accepted push from **Bob's Plumbing** | ⛔ **the tenant's** | ⛔⛔ **NEVER.** *That person consented to hear from Bob's Plumbing. They have never heard of GOAIEZ.* |

⛔⛔ **Why the second one is not a policy preference but an existential risk:** *the day a tenant discovers that their software vendor is marketing to **their** customer list, you have not lost a feature — **you have lost every tenant who finds out, and the ones who hear about it second-hand.*** ⭐ **A tenant's customer list is the single most sensitive asset they hand us, and the entire product rests on their believing we will not touch it.** *P-068, P-069 and the whole consent architecture exist because of exactly this boundary.*

⭐⭐ **[AMENDED T677 · §184B — THE OWNER RULED OTHERWISE AND HIS VERSION IS RECORDED THERE.] The subsidy for a FREE module is that GO AI EZ has the network, including tenants' customers — reached through a DISCLOSED opt-in captured in the same prompt, with a per-sender flag, a frequency cap and tenant visibility.** ⛔ **`doctor` asserts a Tenant Zero broadcast to a customer-scoped audience requires `goaiez_optin = true` on that `Person`** — a query the send cannot bypass. **Tenant-to-tenant remains absolutely forbidden.**

## 184A.2 ⚠️ "ZERO-COST MARKETING BYPASSING SMS" — TRUE, AND SMALLER THAN IT SOUNDS

⭐ **Push genuinely has no carrier fee and that is a real advantage. Two things make it a supplement rather than a replacement:**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔ **Reach is gated by INSTALL, not by phone number** | *SMS reaches anyone with a number. Push reaches only someone who **installed an app or accepted a browser prompt**.* **For a local trade's residential customers, app-install rate is near zero and web-push accept rate is a single-digit-to-low-double-digit percentage.** ⭐ **So push replaces SMS for the small fraction who opted in, and the rest still need SMS.** *The business case is real; the size of it is an install-rate problem, not a channel problem.* |
| ⛔⛔ **Push consent is NOT SMS consent** | *A customer who agreed to texts has not agreed to push, and vice versa.* ⭐ **Per-channel permit, per-channel STOP** — which the consent architecture already handles, because `decide(person, CHANNEL, lane, class)` has always taken a channel. **X-207 changes nothing about that and must not.** |
| ⚠️ **And there is no customer app today** | ⭐ **X-171 `TechMobile` is the TECH's app.** *If there is no customer-facing app, customer push is **web push only** — which changes the marketing arithmetic considerably.* **Owner question below.** |

⭐ **None of this argues against the module. It argues for measuring the install rate before the marketing engine is sized on it** — and the telemetry to do that is `push_deliveries`, which the module owns.

## 184A.3 ⭐⭐⭐ X-207 `PushEngine` — THE FULL §157 HEADER

`@module X-207` `@intent GROW`

**WHAT** ⭐ **The platform's one OWNED channel — the only one with no carrier between us and the device.** Delivers to **Web Push** *(every desktop and mobile browser)*, **iOS via APNs** and **Android via FCM**, from one internal contract: a module emits an event, X-207 decides nothing about whether it may send and everything about how it arrives. ⛔⛔ **It is a CHANNEL under `X-204 ConsentService` — same permit, same three lanes, same STOP, same twenty refusal codes as SMS. Free does not mean ungated.** ⛔ **Payloads carry NO PII: a notification is a title, a deep link and a secure id; the client fetches the sensitive content after waking, authenticated.** ⛔ **It never polls — it subscribes to the bus.** Owns the **device register** *(tokens per user per device, rotated, invalidated on logout at the next request, not at expiry)*. **Class comes from `X-193`; the quiet-hours window applies to MARKETING class only, exactly as it does on every other channel.**

**WIZARD** **inferred:** the tenant's brand name, icon and colour for the notification chrome — from the brand kit, nothing asked · **confirmed once:** *(trigger: ⛔ **when a customer would FIRST receive a push — the EARNED prompt, never at signup**)* *"Let customers get updates on their phone instead of by text?"* — one sentence, one toggle · **tenant-facing:** the prompt copy their customer sees before the browser permission dialog *(the one screen where wording changes accept rate materially)*.

**AUTOPILOT** `ships: L3 · ceiling: L3`** ⭐⭐⭐ *(**`R235` 2026-08-27 — EVERY AUTOPILOT SHIPS ON.** The owner overruled the `L1 PROPOSE` default: *"ALL AI ON, by my law. The client can turn it off if they want. All autopilots on, with AI watching them."* ⛔ **`ships:` now EQUALS `ceiling:` — this acts from minute one.** The ladder survives as a DESCRIPTION of what the action is, **never as a gate on when it may run.** ⭐ Safety is `X-126`'s capability gate — **no grounding Fact, no skill** — not a human approving.)* *(**ships-at is `@intent GROW` under `§227.2`** — ⛔ ⛔ ~~**PROPOSES ONLY, ALWAYS, ON DAY ONE**~~ *(STRUCK by `R235` — it ACTS from minute one)* — earned up the ladder, never set; the ceiling is what this module may reach on measured clean runs, never set)* every module that already alerts by SMS or email gains push **automatically, with no per-module work** — the class already exists, the person already exists, the channel is new · a device that fails delivery **N** times is retired from the register and the send falls to the next channel · **an un-accepted permission prompt is never re-shown inside the cool-off window** *(a re-prompted user blocks permanently, and that is unrecoverable)*.

**SWARM** **SQ-1 Channels · WAVE 1.** Owns `app/Modules/Channels/Push/**`. `@visibility public` = `PushDriver::send()` and the register's read API. **Must not touch** `ConsentService`, `X-193`'s classes, or any other channel's driver. ⭐ **Lane 2's certificate handshake: APNs uses a token-based key (`.p8`) and FCM a service-account credential — ⛔ BOTH live in `X-206 CredentialVault` as PLATFORM-owned rows, never in `.env` past wave 0, never in code.** *A rotation is a row update and a re-handshake, no deploy* (P-193 · P-194's shape). **Runtime proof =** a real push delivered to a real device with the vendor's own delivery receipt id in the trace — ⛔ **an external id, per §182: the swarm cannot fabricate an APNs id that Apple will confirm.**

**SCREENS** tenant: the one confirm-once toggle · the prompt-copy editor · a delivery/open summary. operator: the device register, retirement reasons, and per-platform delivery health.

**DECLARATIONS** `@renders one_confirmonce_toggle · promptcopy_editor · retirement_reasons · perplatform_delivery_health` *(derived from SCREENS, 2026-08-27 — names only; the JSON schema each block carries is turn 69's)*

# 184B. THE PUSH SUBSIDY — THE OWNER'S RULING, AND THE ONE SENTENCE THAT MAKES IT WORK *(T677 · ⛔ not a turn)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **Recorded: the module is free, and the price of free is that GO AI EZ has the network. That is a legitimate model and it is his call. The three problems with it are not about competition — and one sentence in one prompt removes all three.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**A push that arrives from the wrong name.** *A browser push permission is granted to an **ORIGIN**, and a device token belongs to an **APP**. If Bob's customers accepted push at `bobsplumbing.goaiez.com`, every message on that subscription arrives **wearing Bob's name**.* ⛔ **So a GO AI EZ message on Bob's subscription is either presented as Bob's — which is misleading — or announces itself as ours, which the recipient never agreed to.** ⭐⭐ **And the recipient's remedy is one tap: block push for that origin. Which kills BOB's channel, not ours.** *The cost of our marketing is paid by the tenant, in lost reach, and the tenant never chose it — **that, not competition, is what a tenant would object to.***

## 184B.1 ✅ THE RULING, RECORDED

| | ⭐ **Owner, T677** |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Price** | **`X-207` is FREE to every tenant. No meter, no credit, no charge.** |
| **The subsidy** | ⭐ **GO AI EZ has access to the push network. That is what pays for it being free.** |
| ⛔ **Tenant-to-tenant** | **FORBIDDEN. No tenant may ever reach another tenant's audience.** *Already law — tenant isolation, RLS FORCEd; now stated explicitly for this module.* |
| **GO AI EZ's use** | **to let people know about GO AI EZ.** |
| **The reasoning** | *"clients will have no issue — GO AI EZ does not compete with them on any level."* |

⭐ **On the reasoning: he is right about competition, and it is the right thing to have checked.** *We sell software to local businesses; we are not another plumber. A homeowner hearing about GO AI EZ costs Bob nothing competitively.* **The objection was never competitive.** *It is the three mechanical facts below, and they are fixable.*

## 184B.2 ⛔ THREE MECHANICAL FACTS — stated once

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **① The message wears the tenant's name** | *(above)* — origin-scoped permission, app-scoped token. **There is no transport-level way to send "from GO AI EZ" on a subscription granted to Bob.** |
| ⛔⛔ **② One STOP kills both** | *A homeowner who wants Bob's job updates but not our product news **has no way to say so** — a single origin subscription has a single off switch.* **So a person mildly annoyed by us silently costs the tenant their entire push channel to that customer**, and nobody finds out because a blocked permission is invisible. |
| ⚠️ **③ The platforms have their own rules about it** | *Apple, Google and the browser vendors each restrict using a push subscription obtained for one purpose to deliver unrelated third-party promotion.* ⛔ **This is a dependency fact, not a legal opinion (Q-061): the risk is not a fine, it is the whole platform's push privileges being pulled — a single point of failure for every tenant at once.** |

⭐ **All three have the same root: the person was never told.** *And all three disappear the moment they are.*

## 184B.3 ⭐⭐⭐ THE ONE SENTENCE — THE SUBSIDY, INTACT, AND SAFE

**Nothing about the model changes. The network stays one network, GO AI EZ keeps its access, the module stays free.** ⭐ **The only change is WHEN the customer hears about us: at the moment they opt in, instead of the first time we appear.**

> ⭐⭐ **The prompt a customer sees before the browser dialog:**
> ***"Bob's Plumbing runs on GO AI EZ. Turn on notifications to get updates about your job — and occasionally something useful from GO AI EZ."***

| What that one sentence buys | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Not misleading** | they know we exist **before** they accept. A later GO AI EZ message is **expected**, not a surprise from a stranger. |
| ⭐⭐ **Per-sender unsubscribe becomes possible** | **two consents captured in one prompt, recorded as two flags.** *"Stop GO AI EZ, keep Bob" is a row update — **the tenant's channel survives our mistake**, which is the whole of problem ②.* |
| ⭐ **Disclosed at consent** | which is exactly what the platform rules are asking for. |
| ⛔ **Costs** | **one sentence. No revenue, no feature, no friction beyond a longer prompt.** |

⭐⭐⭐ **AND IT IS ALREADY IN THE PLAN.** *`X-190` carries **G12-01 "Powered By" Viral Loop** — every tenant surface quietly announcing what runs it.* **This is that mechanism applied to push, and it is stronger there than anywhere else: a notification is the highest-attention surface a person has, and every job update a local business sends becomes a GO AI EZ impression with the customer's knowledge.** *The disclosure is not a tax on the subsidy — **it IS the subsidy, working better.***

## 184B.4 ⭐ THREE GUARDS THAT KEEP THE NETWORK ALIVE

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **A frequency cap on Tenant Zero** | **a setting, low by default.** *Even disclosed, a platform pushing to every tenant's customer list becomes noise — and noise on a shared channel is not a per-message cost, **it is the permanent loss of the audience for everyone on it.*** **The cap protects the asset the subsidy depends on.** |
| ⭐ **The tenant can SEE it** | **every Tenant Zero broadcast that reached their customers is visible to them, with its copy and its date.** *Not a veto — it is the subsidy and they agreed to it — **but a tenant who can see it never feels it happened behind their back**, and that is the difference between a term of service and a grievance.* |
| ⭐ **Two audiences, two rules** | **TENANT USERS** *(owner, staff, techs — our users, on our domain)*: **push freely, no disclosure needed, no cap.** ⭐ *This is where most of the "let people know about GO AI EZ" value actually lives, and it has none of the three problems.* · **A TENANT'S CUSTOMERS**: **disclosed opt-in, per-sender flag, frequency cap, tenant-visible.** |

⛔ **`doctor` asserts a Tenant Zero broadcast to a customer-scoped audience requires the `goaiez_optin` flag true on that `Person`** — *the flag captured by the disclosed prompt.* **Not a review step; a query the send cannot bypass.**

---

**CHECKED:** the objection re-derived from the transport rather than from the business model — **origin-scoped browser permissions and app-scoped device tokens are how push works, and neither carries a per-sender identity**, which is what makes ① and ② mechanical rather than matters of taste · the competitive point **conceded, because it is correct** · the disclosed-opt-in design checked against the existing plan and found to be **`G12-01`'s "Powered By" viral loop**, already law, already owned by X-190 — *so this is not a new mechanism, it is an existing one pointed at a new surface* · the two audiences separated by `actor_type`, as §184A.1 already required.
**FAILS IF:** ⛔ **the disclosure sentence gets shortened in a redesign.** *It will read like friction to whoever is optimising the accept rate, and dropping it raises accept by a point or two while re-creating all three problems at once.* ⭐ **The guard: the `goaiez_optin` flag is written **from that prompt only**, and a broadcast without it is refused at the query — so removing the sentence does not quietly enable anything, it simply makes the audience empty.** *Make the shortcut fail loudly rather than silently.*
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **the frequency cap's number.** *I have said "low by default" and I do not know what low is — once a quarter reads as respectable, once a month reads as a newsletter, once a week reads as spam, and the real answer depends on how good the message is.* ⭐⭐ **Start at once a quarter, watch the block rate in `push_deliveries`, and raise it only if the block rate does not move.** *The block rate is the only honest measure of whether the audience minds — and unlike almost everything else in this plan, it is a number you cannot get back once it goes the wrong way.*

# 184C. THE EIGHT CHANNEL INJECTIONS — CHECKED, HOMED, WOVEN *(T677 · ⛔ not a turn · no turn count change, as directed)*

> ⭐⭐ **Two already exist. Four fold in cleanly. One is a genuine mint candidate. One collides with a standing law that killed eleven rows. And the word "hijack" appears twice — third strike.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Eight channels and one consent gate that has to hold for all of them.** *Every one of these adds a way to reach a person, and the platform's entire safety rests on a single sentence: **`decide(person, channel, lane, class)` before the transport.*** ⛔ **A postcard has no STOP keyword. A Nextdoor reply has no opt-in at all. A DM arrives on someone else's platform under someone else's rules.** ⭐ **So the test for each of the eight is not "is it valuable" — it is: **what does consent look like on THIS surface, and what happens when someone wants it to stop?** *Two of the eight have no honest answer to the second half, and that is the whole finding.*

## 184C.1 THE EIGHT

| # | Channel | Verdict | Home |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1** | **WhatsApp + Apple Business Chat** | ✅ **FOLD — C-Whatsapp gains a transport** | C-Whatsapp |
| **2** | **GBP Command Center** | ⭐ **ALREADY IN THE PLAN — nothing to add** | X-177 · C-Whatsapp |
| **3** | ⭐ **Programmatic Direct Mail** | ⛔⛔ **GENUINE MINT CANDIDATE — and the only channel here with a real per-unit cost and NO STOP** | *proposed* `X-208 DirectMail` |
| **4** | **Autonomous Viral Loop** | ⚠️ **FOLD, with the trigger changed** | X-190 · X-205 · C-Reviews |
| **5** | ⛔ **Hyper-Local Community "Hijack"** | ⛔⛔ **RESHAPE — signal, never send** | X-136 · X-196 |
| **6** | **Aggregator Intercept** | ✅ **FOLD** — ⚠️ *and it is a file-13 `DONE-UNVERIFIED`* | X-156 · X-10 |
| **7** | ⛔ **OTT / CTV Ads** | ⛔ **HALF IS FENCED BY A LIVE LAW** | X-158 *(the creative)* · §44 *(the bidding)* |
| **8** | **Social DM** | ✅ **FOLD — it is already how the plan works** | X-156 · C-Agent |

### ✅ 1 · WhatsApp + Apple Business Chat — folds, with the framing corrected

**Apple Business Chat is a TRANSPORT, exactly as APNs is a transport of X-207.** *Same shape: one contract, several carriers behind it.* **No mint.** ⚠️ *It needs Apple approval and a CSP — a file-13 row.*

⛔ **One correction: *"bypass 10DLC"* is the wrong frame, and it is the third appearance of that word class after `evasion` and `form hijacker`, both already struck.** ⭐ **WhatsApp is not subject to 10DLC because it is not SMS — that is true. But it is not a bypass of rules, it is a DIFFERENT and in places STRICTER set:** pre-approved message templates, a 24-hour customer-service window outside which only templates may send, and **per-conversation pricing — it is not free.** *Recorded so nobody specs it as "the cheap way around the carriers" and discovers the template approval queue in wave 2.*

### ⭐ 2 · GBP Command Center — already law, nothing to inject

**`X-177 GbpGuardian` already carries local post automation, Q&A seeding, claimed-status and the suspension guard. `G19-22` already routes GBP chat through Zernio onto ONE `Conversation`.** ⭐ **Auto-publish and DM-intercept are both specced.** *Good news: this one is done, and the instinct that it was missing is the same false alarm as Law 10 — which is a sign the plan is more complete than it feels.*

### ⛔⛔ 3 · PROGRAMMATIC DIRECT MAIL — the real find, and it needs a number

⭐ **Genuinely new. Nothing in the plan touches physical mail, and for a cold high-ticket estimate a postcard is a real channel.** ⛔ **It also breaks three assumptions every other channel in this platform shares:**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔⛔ **A postcard costs ~50¢–$1.** *An SMS costs a fraction of a cent and an email costs nothing.* **This is the first channel where a wrong audience query costs real money in the first second — and you cannot recall a postcard.** ⭐ **It needs a hard spend cap and a per-batch confirmation above a threshold, both settings** *(P-193)*. |
| ⛔⛔ **There is no STOP.** *Nobody replies STOP to a postcard.* ⭐ **So suppression is checked at GENERATION, a returned-mail event writes a suppression, and the physical address is a `Person` attribute under `X-204` like any other channel identity.** |
| ⚠️ **Delivery is asynchronous and physical** — days, not milliseconds, with its own outcome set *(in transit · delivered · returned · undeliverable)*. |

⭐ **It passes the Boundary Law cleanly:** own table `mail_pieces` · own events `mail.queued · printed · in_transit · delivered · returned` · a dedicated surface *(the piece designer and the spend view)*. **Proposed: `X-208 DirectMail`, SQ-1 Channels, W3. Only you mint.**

### ⚠️ 4 · Autonomous Viral Loop — fold, but change the TRIGGER

⭐ **The pieces exist: `X-190` owns referral links and the Powered-By loop, `X-205` owns affiliate payouts, `C-Reviews` owns the review.** ⛔ **The problem is not the mechanism, it is the TIMING.**

> ⛔ **An affiliate offer sent immediately after a five-star review reads as payment for the review — even when it is not.** *`G19-10` Incentive Blocking is already law: the compose-time block on "review for 10% off." **A referral link fired as a RESPONSE to a review is the same thing with a delay of zero.***

⭐⭐ **The fix costs nothing and keeps the whole value: DECOUPLE THE TRIGGER.** **The referral offer goes to happy customers on a CADENCE — not as a reply to a review.** *Same people, same offer, same zero-CAC growth, and no linkage anyone can point at.* **Recorded: `review.received` may raise a signal; it may never be the trigger for a referral send.**

### ⛔⛔ 5 · HYPER-LOCAL COMMUNITY — RESHAPED: signal, never send

⛔ **Three separate problems, and the third is the one that matters:**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⚠️ **"Hijack"** | third strike on that word class. *It is not a hijack; it is reading a public post.* |
| ⚠️ **Scraping Nextdoor / FB Groups** | needs an authenticated session — **`FetchPolicy.authenticated = false` by default (P-078)**, and the operator's own account safety outranks any scrape (P-145). *Already classified this way at `G3-24` and `G3-32`.* |
| ⛔⛔ **Drafting a quote AT a neighbour's post** | *That person posted in a **community**, to their neighbours. They did not contact a business.* **P-068: a signal never mints a send permit.** ⭐⭐ **And the commercial fact is worse than the legal one: a local trade that gets banned from their own neighbourhood group has lost the single best lead source they own — and it is our automation that did it to them.** |

⭐⭐⭐ **The version that is genuinely valuable and does not get them banned: it is a SIGNAL with a DRAFT.** **Surface the high-intent post to the tenant with a reply already written — and the HUMAN posts it, from their own account, as themselves.** *That is exactly `X-136 SignalEngine` plus a draft, it is a shape the plan already has, and it is better product anyway: a neighbour replying personally converts, a bot replying gets reported.*

### ✅ 6 · Aggregator Intercept — folds, with two honest caveats

⭐ **Valuable, and speed-to-lead is already law** *(`G2-72`, X-10's SLA)*. **An aggregator lead is an ingest source — `X-156` — routed by `X-10`. No mint.**
⚠️ **Caveat one: those APIs are gated partner programmes.** *Thumbtack, Angi and Yelp do not hand out lead APIs freely.* ⛔ **File-13 rows, `DONE-UNVERIFIED` until an account exists.**

## 185.2 ⭐⭐⭐ THE ONE FOUNDATIONAL SHIFT — **THE PRODUCT MUST PROVE ITSELF, IN MONEY, ON THE TENANT'S PHONE, UNPROMPTED**

### The gap, verified before claiming it

**Counted in the plan just now:** *"weekly report" appears **six** times and **every one is the AGENCY's report to its client** (G2-67 → X-112)* · **`Honest Counter` appears 14 times — as a DESIGN AESTHETIC** *(D1: MASTER for the tenant app)*, **not as an artifact** · and ***"calls you would have missed" · "jobs captured" · "revenue captured" — ZERO occurrences in 2.1 MB.***

⛔⛔ **So: this platform's entire promise is *"the AI answers every call you would have missed"* — and nothing in it ever TELLS the tenant that it did.**

### Why that is foundational and not cosmetic

*Think about who the customer actually is.* **A plumber is under a sink. He does not open a dashboard. He experiences this product as: his phone rang less, and jobs appeared.** ⛔ **179 screens and a generative console are magnificent — for a person who logs in.** ⭐⭐ **If the only proof the product works lives somewhere he never looks, he cancels in month four. Not because it failed. Because he could not tell it worked.**

⛔ **And local-SMB SaaS is not won on features. It is won on the ratio of lifetime value to acquisition cost, and that ratio is almost entirely CHURN.** *A tenant who can see the number every Monday does not cancel. A tenant who cannot, eventually does — and no feature on the roadmap changes that.*

### The artifact

> ⭐⭐ **Every Monday, unprompted, to the phone:**
> ***"Last week your AI answered 23 calls you'd have missed. 6 booked. That's about $4,200 in work. Here they are."*** *— with the six jobs listed, and one tap to open any of them.*

| Why every part of that sentence is chosen | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **"calls you'd have missed"** | *the counterfactual is the product.* **A count of conversations is a metric; a count of calls that would have gone to voicemail is the reason he pays.** |
| ⭐⭐ **"about $4,200"** | ⛔ **in MONEY, never in metrics** — and *"about"* because **`X-194`'s law already forbids blending a count with an estimate**, so the estimate is labelled and the counted part is exact. **P-120 holds: it is the tenant's own job values, never an invented average.** |
| ⭐ **"here they are"** | *proof, not a claim. He can tap one and see the job.* |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **It arrives on the PHONE** | **push — which is now free and exists as `X-207`** — or SMS. ⛔ **Never only a dashboard tile.** |

### ⭐⭐ It needs nothing new built

**`X-138`** already holds the attribution · **`X-194`** already renders and already has the counts-never-blend-with-estimates law · **`X-207`** now delivers, free · **`X-190`** already runs the Powered-By loop · **`X-08`** already predicts churn. ⭐⭐⭐ **This is a COMPOSITION of five modules that are already specced. It is not a feature — it is the one artifact that makes the other 112 modules visible.**

⭐ **And it pays three ways at once:** **retention** *(the number, weekly, forever)* · **referral** *(that message is screenshot-able and forwardable — it is the referral engine's actual CONTENT, which X-190 currently lacks)* · **and it is the proof `X-08` needs** — *a tenant who stops opening it is churning, and that signal arrives months before the cancellation does.*

⛔ **Where it lands: turn 46's social & content pass, and it is one row.** *`X-194` renders it, `X-207` sends it, and the honest-counter law it obeys is already written.*

# 185A. THE NO-URL FIX · THE LOCAL ALLIANCE — AND THE ONE STEP THAT MAKES IT LEGAL *(T677 · ⛔ not a turn)*

> ⭐⭐ **The No-URL problem is real and is already solved by three mechanisms in the plan. The Local Alliance is a genuinely strong idea with one serious defect — and the fix is ten seconds long and converts better.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Selling a customer's phone number for $50.** *That is not what it is meant to be, and it is exactly what it is if the plumber taps the button and the roofer starts calling.* ⛔ **From the homeowner's side: they hired a plumber, and now a company they never contacted is phoning them — and their plumber was paid for it.** ⭐⭐ **The plan's own laws already forbid it: `P-068` — a signal never mints a send permit — and `P-069` — an import is not consent. A referral hands the roofer DATA. It does not hand them a PERMIT.** *One extra step fixes it completely, and the fixed version converts better than the broken one.*

## 185A.1 ✅ THE NO-URL FIX — ALL THREE MECHANISMS ALREADY EXIST

⭐ **The problem is real:** *Instagram and TikTok suppress links, carriers filter link-bearing SMS, and a postcard has no link at all.* **Good news — the answer is three things the plan already has, pointed at one problem:**

| Medium | Tracking | Where it already lives |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Social, where links are banned** | ⭐ a human-readable **promo code** | **`X-205 AffiliateEngine` already owns `promo_codes`** *(G7-36 was one of the seven rows that became X-205)* |
| **Print · truck wraps · direct mail** | ⭐ a **dedicated tracking number** | **`X-188` provisions it; `X-137` already does "a static number per offline campaign"** *(G13-24)* — this points that mechanism at affiliate attribution |
| **Physical → digital** | **QR** | **`X-138` already owns `G17-24` QR Code Generation** |

⭐⭐ **So it is a FOLD, not a mint — and the rule worth recording is the general one: THE TRACKING METHOD IS CHOSEN BY THE MEDIUM, NEVER BY THE SENDER.** *A module asks "what can this surface carry" and gets a code, a number or a QR — it never emits a bare URL into a channel that will strip it.* ⛔ **`doctor` asserts no affiliate asset ships a raw URL to a link-suppressed medium.**

⚠️ **One cost finding: a dedicated phone number is not free — it is a recurring per-number charge.** ⛔ *Giving every tenant an affiliate number at signup is a permanent monthly cost on a free referral programme.* ⭐ **Provision on demand: a tenant gets an affiliate number the first time they actually need one — when they order print or a wrap — not at signup.** *One line, and it is the difference between a feature and a standing bill.*

## 185A.2 ⭐⭐⭐ THE LOCAL ALLIANCE — STRONG IDEA, ONE SERIOUS DEFECT

### It is not a new module — `X-190` is already named for it

**`X-190 LocalNetwork` — "THE LINK ENGINE" (owner, T536) — already owns tenant-to-tenant referrals and network graphing** *(G9-24)*. ⭐ **No mint. The module exists and was built for this.**

### ⛔⛔ The defect, and the ten-second fix

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔ **As proposed** | *plumber taps → the AI matches a roofer → the roofer gets the lead → the plumber gets a bounty.* **The homeowner is never asked.** |
| ⛔⛔ **Why it fails on the plan's own laws** | **`P-069`: the roofer receives a contact they have no relationship with — that is an IMPORT, and an import is not consent.** **`P-068`: the plumber's tap is a SIGNAL; it does not mint a send permit for a different company.** ⭐ **The roofer has data and no basis. Under this plan he cannot legally call.** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **THE FIX — the CUSTOMER makes the introduction** | **The plumber taps → ⭐ the AI asks the CUSTOMER: *"Want me to have a roofer call you? Bob recommends Dave's Roofing."* → the customer says yes → NOW the roofer has a permit, because the customer asked for the call.** |
| ⭐⭐ **And it needs nothing new** | **The AI is ALREADY in a conversation with that customer.** *The plumber taps a button, the AI texts, the customer replies. That is the product working exactly as designed — `C-Agent`, one `Conversation`, `X-204` writes the permit.* |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **It also converts better** | **A roofer calling someone who ASKED for a roofer converts at a multiple of a roofer cold-calling someone whose plumber passed on their number.** *The compliant version is the better funnel. That is not a coincidence — an asked-for call is a warm lead and a passed-on number is a cold one.* |

### ⭐ Three more, each one line

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Credits, not cash — and say so** | *Gemini specified **credits to the SaaS ledger**, and that is materially better than a cash kickback: it is a loyalty mechanic, not a payment for a name.* ⭐ **Disclose it anyway, in the intro: *"Bob gets a small credit if you book."*** *It costs one clause, removes the question entirely, and honestly makes Bob look organised rather than sneaky.* |
| ⛔ **"Non-competing" cannot be inferred** | *Plumber → roofer is obvious. **Plumber → HVAC is not — many plumbers DO HVAC.** Roofer → gutters overlaps.* ⛔ **A matcher guessing from an industry code WILL refer a customer to a direct competitor, and that tenant churns the same day, angrily.** ⭐ **The tenant declares who they will and will not refer to — a short list they control, confirmed once in the wizard. Never an algorithm's guess.** |
| ⚠️ **The density problem, stated honestly** | ⛔ **The alliance is worth nothing until two GOAIEZ tenants in complementary trades exist in the same city.** *Tenant #1 in a town gets an empty screen; tenant #50 gets a real network.* ⭐ **So it is a RETENTION feature that switches on with density — not a launch feature — and it must degrade honestly: *"I don't have a roofer in your area yet"*, never an empty list.** *The lock-in is real, but a network has to be worth having before it can hold anyone.* |

⭐⭐ **With those four changes the Local Alliance is exactly what it was pitched as — an inescapable local ecosystem — and it is one the tenants, the customers and a regulator would all be comfortable reading about.**

## 185A.3 ✅ THE ROI PUSH AND SUGGESTION C — LOCKED

⭐ **The pricebook loop is recorded exactly as ruled:** *"Your AI answered 14 missed calls and captured 6 jobs this week, but couldn't quote them because your pricebook is empty. Tap here to add your prices."* ⭐⭐ **That is the honest half doing more work than the money half would — it converts a limitation into the single strongest reason a tenant will ever have to finish onboarding, and it never estimates.**

⭐⭐⭐ **Suggestion C is absolute law: wave 0 opens with a THREE-MODULE micro-wave.** *Prove the factory line, the `doctor` runners and the QA-4 runtime proofs on three foundation modules — with real artifacts — before the remaining nine.* ⛔ **This is the single most important decision in the programme and it is now recorded as law rather than as a suggestion.**

**CHECKED:** all three No-URL mechanisms located in the existing plan before being called folds — **`promo_codes` on X-205 · X-137's static-number-per-offline-campaign · X-138's `G17-24` QR generation** · **`X-190 LocalNetwork` confirmed as "THE LINK ENGINE (owner, T536)" already owning tenant-to-tenant referrals**, so the alliance is a fold and not a mint · the referral defect derived from **P-068 and P-069 by name**, which is what makes it a law collision rather than an opinion · the recurring cost of a dedicated number identified before it became a default.
**FAILS IF:** ⛔ **the customer-consent step is implemented as a checkbox on the plumber's screen instead of a message to the customer.** *"Customer agreed" ticked by the plumber is the plumber's word, not the customer's — **it is `P-069`'s import attestation all over again, and it fails for the same reason.*** ⭐ **The permit must come from the CUSTOMER's own reply, in the thread, recorded by `X-204`. Anything else is a tick-box that proves nothing.**
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **whether tenants will accept declaring their own referral list.** *It is one more thing to configure, and the whole product promise is that nothing needs configuring.* ⛔ **But the alternative — a matcher guessing "non-competing" — refers a plumber's customer to another plumber eventually, and that is not a bug you recover from with an apology.** ⭐⭐ **The softening: infer the list from their industry profile and ask them to confirm it once, the same shape as every other wizard field. Inferred, confirmed, never asked cold.**

# 186. TURN 39 — SQ-4 WHOLE · ACQUISITION · ENRICHMENT · SIGNALS · PIXEL · IDENTITY · ATTRIBUTION *(turn 39 of 109 · T677 · 15 modules · 71 rows)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **The heaviest pass in the plan, and the one where a single law does most of the work: `P-068` — a signal never mints a send permit. Fifteen modules exist to LEARN things about people. Not one of them may send.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**A module that knows something and acts on it.** *SQ-4's whole job is to find out: who this business is, what they run, when they are hiring, which page they read twice, whether they came from an ad.* ⛔⛔ **Every one of those facts is one line of code away from becoming an email — and the line is always written by someone reasonable, at 2am, because the signal was so obviously actionable.** ⭐ **`P-068` is the wall: a signal RAISES, it never SENDS. `P-069` is the second wall: an enriched contact carries an attestation or it is not sendable at all.** ⭐⭐ **So the group-level test is one grep, exactly as it was for channels at §170.1: `grep -rE 'send|dispatch|notify' app/Modules/Data/` returns only EVENT emissions — no driver, no ConsentService call, no permit. Fifteen modules, one assertion.**

## 186.0 THE SEAM — WRITTEN ONCE FOR ALL FIFTEEN

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Signals raise, they never send** | every module here emits; **`X-105` and `X-186` decide whether to act, and `X-204` decides whether they may** *(P-068)*. |
| ⭐⭐ **Every enriched field carries `source` and `confidence`** | *(P-147)* — ⛔ **a field with neither is not enrichment, it is a guess with a database row.** |
| ⭐ **Every contact write carries an `attestation_id`** | *(P-069)* — **an import is not consent, and enrichment is an import.** |
| ⭐ **Fetch is polite or not at all** | *(P-145)* — a global concurrency and RPS ceiling; **the operator's own account safety outranks any scrape.** |
| ⭐ **Research fires only on distress** | *(P-146)* — **and every icebreaker names something TRUE.** |
| ⛔ **Staleness is `fetched_at`, never an eviction** | *(P-143)* — one database, nothing cached out of existence. |

# 187. TURN 40 — OUTREACH & GROWTH · AND THE EFFORT RE-WEIGHT *(turn 40 of 109 · T677 · 5 modules · 43 rows)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **The pass where the platform stops listening and starts reaching out — and the only pass where every single row is a message to a stranger. Plus the re-weight that turn 33 scheduled and turn 39's data finally made possible.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Forty-three rows that each look like one more send.** *Everything before this turn LEARNED. This group ACTS — and it acts on people who never asked to hear from us.* ⛔⛔ **The failure is not one bad send; it is that a prospect can be legitimately reached by the outreach ladder, the backlink pitcher, the referral loop AND the alliance in the same week, each one individually compliant, and the aggregate is harassment nobody authored.** ⭐⭐ **So the group-level law is not "check consent per module" — every module already does. It is: ONE PERSON, ONE CONVERSATION, ONE CADENCE. `X-204` decides the permit; `X-121`'s single `Conversation` is what makes the aggregate visible at all.** *A per-module conscience cannot see a per-person problem.*

If it does not, nothing else in the pass matters.* |

## 187.5 ✅ THE X-134 LINEAGE FIX — BETTER THAN MINE, AND I SHOULD SAY SO

⭐⭐⭐ **The ruling is right and my instinct was dangerous.** *I flagged "retract a disabled vendor's fields" as the seam I was least sure of. **The reason I was unsure is that retraction is destructive: disable a vendor and you may wipe the only phone number on a profile** — and the tenant loses data they never chose to lose.*

⭐⭐ **The fix, recorded, and §186.2's `G3-65` row is amended to it:**

> **Every field value logs its `vendor_id`. When a vendor is disabled, the data is NOT deleted — the affected fields are flagged `stale_vendor_disabled` and their confidence drops to ZERO.** *That prompts the AI or the tenant to re-verify, rather than executing a destructive cascade.*

⭐ **And it composes with two laws already written:** **confidence zero means `P-092` refuses to quote from it** *(the agent already refuses on ungrounded fields)*, and **`P-143` says staleness is a timestamp, never an eviction** — *this is that law applied to provenance instead of to time.* ⛔ **Nothing is deleted; something becomes unusable until re-verified. That is strictly better than what I proposed.**

⭐⭐ **The finding: 321 rows produced 201 specs. The remaining 418 rows are ≈260 specs, not 418.** ⛔ **But specs are not effort — a row that needs its own ⑥ and ⑦ is roughly two rows of work, and inheritance is running at 44%, not the 93% the enhancement ratio implied.**

⭐⭐⭐ **THE EFFORT UNIT, from measurement:** **effort ≈ specs × (1 + non-inherit rate).** *Measured: 201 specs × 1.56 = **314 effort-units for 321 rows — almost exactly 1:1.*** ⛔ **So the row count was accidentally right as a WORKLOAD proxy, for the wrong reason: the merge rate and the inheritance rate have moved in opposite directions and cancelled.**

⭐ **Which means the §168.8 re-cut stands, and turns 41–49 need no re-balancing.** *That is the honest answer and it is not the interesting one — **the interesting one is that two errors cancelled, and if either trend breaks, the balance breaks with it.*** **Re-check at 45, not at 49.**

# 188. TURN 41 — SURFACES & BUILDER *(turn 41 of 109 · T677 · 8 modules · 50 rows)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **The pass that builds what a stranger sees. Every other module fails privately — this one fails on a customer's screen, under the tenant's name, in public.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**A generated sentence that is a claim.** *Twenty industries, two hundred templates, funnels, landing pages, ad creative — **all of it written by a model that is optimising for persuasive copy.*** ⛔⛔ **A model asked to write a plumber's homepage will produce *"Licensed, bonded and insured — serving the valley since 1998"* because that is what good landing-page copy looks like. It is not a bug in the prompt; it is the model doing its job well.** ⭐ **And it ships on the tenant's live domain, under their name, about a business we know nothing about.**
⭐⭐⭐ **So the claim lint is not a review step in this pass — it is a BUILD-FAILING check at generation time: the engine may state STRUCTURE and DESCRIPTION. It may never state CLAIMS, CREDENTIALS, NUMBERS or DATES.** *"We repair water heaters, replace them, and handle emergency leaks" — generate freely. **"Licensed since 1998, trusted by 500 families" — a `Fact`, confirmed by the tenant, or the sentence does not exist.***

## 188.0 THE THREE LAWS THAT GOVERN EVERY ROW BELOW

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔⛔ **The claim lint** | *(§182)* structure and description only. **Build-failing at generation, not at review** — a lint a model can talk past is not a lint. |
| ⭐⭐ **P-193 · the Dynamic Admin law** | ⛔ **no text, no layout, no template hardcoded in the frontend.** *Every string, every block, every colour is a ROW.* **The acceptance test is unchanged: change it in admin, see it change, with NO deploy.** |
| ⭐ **P-126 · the template law** | **200 templates 1:1 with 200 industries as the CEILING; 20 seeded properly at launch, growing through admin forever.** ⛔ *The count is a setting, never a number in code.* |
| **D1** | **MASTER = the Honest Counter for the tenant app. God-Mode is console-only.** *A tenant's site is their brand, not ours.* |

# 189. THE AUTONOMY LADDER — HOW EVERY NEW FEATURE BECOMES AI-NATIVE *(T677 · ⛔ not a turn · the answer to "make it all AI, god tier")*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **Asked to make every new feature AI-powered at god tier, and to say how many turns it needs. The answer to the second is ZERO. The answer to the first is not more AI — it is one mechanism that changes what "AI-powered" means across all 113 modules.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Adding AI as a feature label.** *"AI writes your post." "AI picks your template." "AI optimises your campaign." **Every competitor already says all three, and none of it is a moat** — a button that calls a model is four hours of work for anyone.* ⛔⛔ **And it is the exact opposite of what has made every finding in this session valuable.**

> *Look at what actually earned its place: **P-092 — a price is looked up or REFUSED, never generated.** **P-097 — a correction writes a `Fact`, never a prompt edit.** **The claim lint — the model may NOT state a credential.** **P-068 — a signal never mints a permit.** **G10-19 — the honest empty-state, tested with a REAL model call because a stub proves nothing.***

⭐⭐⭐ **Every one of them is a CONSTRAINT on the AI, and together they are the product.** *"Our AI writes your website" is a commodity. **"Our AI refuses to invent your price"** is a category.* ⛔ **So the god-tier move is not to add AI to the new features. It is to make the AI the OPERATING LAYER instead of a button — and to give it a way to earn its way up.**

## 189.1 ⭐⭐⭐ THE REAL GAP — AND IT IS IN EVERY NEW FEATURE

**Read the new features back as they are currently written:**

> *The plumber **taps** the alliance button. The tenant **sets up** the referral. The tenant **picks** a template. The tenant **connects** the aggregator. The tenant **writes** the prompt copy.*

⛔⛔ **Every one of them is still a thing a TENANT INITIATES.** *That is AI-assisted. It is not AI-operated — and it is the one place this plan is still ordinary.*

⭐⭐ **The god-tier version, stated in one line: THE TENANT NEVER INITIATES. The system decides what to do, does it or asks, and reports what it did.** ⭐⭐⭐ **And the surface for that already exists — it is `X-202 ApprovalDesk`, minted this session for internal approvals. It is actually the interface for the entire autonomous layer.** *That is the synthesis: the module we minted to stop decisions getting lost is the module through which an autonomous platform asks permission.*

## 189.2 ⭐⭐⭐ THE AUTONOMY LADDER — FOUR LEVELS, ONE PROMOTION RULE

**Every AI action in all 113 modules sits at exactly one level, and it MOVES.**

| | Level | What it does | Where it surfaces |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **L0** | **OBSERVE** | watches, records, **acts on nothing** | a signal. *`P-068` lives here* |
| **L1** | **PROPOSE** | drafts it and **asks** | ⭐⭐ **`X-202 ApprovalDesk` — one queue, everything waiting, TTL and escalation** |
| **L2** | **ACT & REPORT** | does it, **tells them immediately** | the thread, the alert |
| **L3** | **AUTONOMOUS** | does it; **it appears in the weekly ROI push** | ⭐ *the §185 artifact is the L3 report* |

⭐⭐⭐ **THE PROMOTION RULE — and it is already law, just not general:** §149.1's content trust ladder says **N approved posts with no edits unlocks unattended publishing; an EDIT resets the counter; a DELETE turns it off.** ⛔ **That law is currently scoped to content. Generalise it to EVERY capability.**

> **A capability starts at its floor and climbs: approve it N times unchanged → it promotes one level. Edit it → the counter resets. Reject it → it drops a level. `X-149` measures, the tenant never configures it, and it is per-tenant.**

⭐⭐ **Why this is the god-tier answer and not a feature:**
- **It is per-TENANT.** *A cautious plumber's AI stays at L1 for months; a confident one is fully autonomous in three weeks. **Nobody sets a preference — they just behave, and the system reads it.***
- ⛔ **It makes autonomy EARNED, which is the only version that survives a mistake.** *An AI that was autonomous from day one and gets one thing wrong is switched off forever. An AI that earned L3 over six weeks gets a correction and keeps going.*
- ⭐ **It is a moat that compounds.** *A competitor can copy a feature in a week. **They cannot copy eight weeks of a specific tenant's approval history** — and a tenant at L3 who switches vendors drops back to L1 somewhere else.*
- ⭐ **And it costs nothing new: `X-202` is the surface, `X-149` is the measurement, §149.1 is the rule, the ROI push is the report. All four exist.**

## 189.3 THE FLOOR PER LEVEL — DEFAULTS, AND THE THREE THAT NEVER MOVE

| Floor | Applies to | Examples |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **L2** | ⭐ **anything a customer is already waiting on** | answering a call · the missed-call text-back · booking · a transactional reply. *Asking permission to answer the phone defeats the product* |
| **L1** | **anything that reaches a stranger, publishes, or spends** | the alliance intro · outreach openers · social posts · direct mail · a campaign · generated site copy |
| **L0** | **everything that only observes** | signals · enrichment · attribution · the community post |
| ⛔⛔ **NEVER PROMOTES** | ⭐ **three things, and they are hard-coded** | **① the CONSENT decision** *(X-204 — a permit is never earned by good behaviour)* · **② a PRICE** *(P-092 — looked up or refused, at every level, forever)* · **③ a CLAIM** *(the claim lint — no ladder position ever unlocks "licensed since 1998")* |

⭐ **Those three are the rails. Everything else is a dial the tenant moves by behaving.**

## 189.4 ⭐⭐ EVERY NEW FEATURE, RE-STATED AS AI-OPERATED

| Feature | ⛔ As written *(tenant-initiated)* | ⭐⭐ AI-operated |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **The Local Alliance** | the plumber taps a button | ⭐ **the AI HEARS the customer mention a roof in the transcript, and proposes the intro at L1.** *The plumber approves from `X-202` — or after N approvals it just asks the customer and reports it* |
| **X-207 Push** | the tenant writes prompt copy | **the AI writes it from the industry blueprint, tests two variants, and X-149 promotes the winner on ACCEPT RATE** — never on preference |
| **X-208 Direct Mail** | the tenant builds a postcard | ⭐ **the AI detects a cold high-ticket estimate that went quiet, drafts the piece, and proposes it — with the cost shown before approval.** *⭐ **CONFIRM AT THE ACTION for anything that spends the tenant's money** *(`R235`: the module ships ON; **the SPEND confirms**)** |
| **X-205 Affiliate** | the tenant sets up a referral | **the AI notices which customers already refer and proposes them as affiliates** |
| **The aggregators** | the tenant connects and configures | **it catches, quotes from the pricebook, and books — L2, because the lead is waiting** |

# 190. TURN 42 — CRM (a) · THE INBOX AND THE ROUTER *(turn 42 of 109 · T677 · 2 modules · 35 rows)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **Two modules, and everything else in the platform reads from them. `X-01` is the one place a customer's whole history exists; `X-10` decides which human meets them. If these two are wrong, 111 modules are wrong downstream and nothing else can compensate.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**A second inbox.** *Every module in this platform has a reason to want its own view of a person — the voice agent wants call state, the campaign wants send history, the dispatcher wants job status, reviews wants sentiment.* ⛔⛔ **The moment any of them keeps its own copy, there are two answers to "what did we say to this customer" and the AI is confidently reading the wrong one.** ⭐ **`P-163` — one `Person`, one `Conversation` — is not a data-modelling preference here. It is the reason the AI can answer at all**: a customer who texted on Monday, called on Wednesday and left a review on Friday is ONE thread, and an agent reading one third of it is worse than an agent reading none, because it sounds informed.
⭐⭐ **So the group test is a single assertion: `doctor` fails the build on ANY table holding a message, a thread or a contact outside X-121's twelve nouns.** *That one grep protects the whole platform.*

# 191. X-209 `Fixer` — THE PERSONAL AI, BUILT TO RUN NOT TO DRAFT *(T677 · ⛔ an insert, not a turn)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **The owner's instruction is the whole design: *"this needs to go beyond draft — it needs to run on autopilot."* Every competitor's assistant stops at a draft in a folder. The reason ours does not is `P-195` — and this module is the first thing built on it.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**An assistant that never graduates.** *"It drafts a reply and leaves it in Drafts" is where every AI assistant on the market lives — and it lives there because **drafting is safe and sending is scary**, so nobody builds the bridge.* ⛔⛔ **A draft the human still has to read, edit and send is not an assistant. It is a slower way to write an email**, and a technician under a sink will never open it twice.
⭐⭐⭐ **The bridge is already built: `P-195`. The Fixer starts at L1 PROPOSE and CLIMBS — per action type, per EMPLOYEE.** *Twenty clean approvals on "text the customer I'm running late" and it stops asking that person, forever, for that action.* **The autopilot is not a switch someone flips. It is a threshold the employee crosses without noticing.**

## 191.1 ⚠️ FIRST — A NUMBER COLLISION, CAUGHT BEFORE IT WAS MINTED

⛔ **`X-209 Migration & State Manager` was proposed for the Queue-and-Hold protocol — and `X-129 MigrationEngine` already exists in the roster** *("we always migrate", zero classified rows, CAPS ✅ at §188)*.

⭐⭐ **The Queue-and-Hold protocol itself is a genuinely good addition and it is recorded — it just belongs INSIDE X-129, not beside it:**

> **DRAIN & HOLD:** on an admin-triggered migration, **writes suspend · the UI shows scheduled maintenance · ⭐ the API ADAPTERS STAY ONLINE, return `200 OK` so Twilio, Stripe and Google do not retry-and-fail, and serialise the raw payload into a durable holding queue** · the database moves · on unlock, **X-129 replays the queue into the bus in arrival order.** ⛔ **Zero bounced webhooks, zero data loss.**

⭐ **This is a real gap the owner found: a bounced webhook is not a delayed message, it is a message that never existed.** *A missed call that Twilio could not deliver is gone — and "we were upgrading" is not something a customer ever hears about.*
⛔ **One addition it needs: the replay must be IDEMPOTENT.** *Some vendors retry anyway despite the 200; without a dedup key on replay, the same payment posts twice.* **Assert it by replaying the same queue twice and observing one `Payment`.**

⭐ **So `X-209` is free — and it goes to `Fixer`. Roster 114.**

## 191.2 ✅ THE TRI-INBOX — A GOOD CLARIFICATION, AND THE LINE THAT MAKES IT SAFE

⭐⭐ **The distinction is correct and I should say so plainly: my §190 assertion was about the DATA layer, and three UIs over one spine does not violate it at all.** **Three views. One table set.**

| View | What it filters | Reads from |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **The Global Unibox** | everything, every channel, live | X-121's `Conversation` |
| **The CRM Deal Inbox** | only what touches this deal | the same rows, filtered by deal |
| ⭐ **The Private Staff Inbox** | ⭐⭐ **this employee's own work — and it is where The Fixer lives** | the same rows, filtered by actor |

⛔⛔ **THE LINE, and it is one assertion: a VIEW may filter, sort, group and cache for RENDER. It may never OWN a row.** ⭐ **`doctor` asserts each inbox is a query, not a store — no `unibox_messages`, no `deal_inbox_items`, no `staff_inbox`.** *The moment one of them keeps its own copy, §190's whole finding returns wearing a UI's clothes.*
⭐ **And `G2-25`'s elevation is right: real-time is a WEBSOCKET FAN-OUT off the bus, never a poll.** *Three views subscribing to one stream is cheap; three views polling one table is how a database dies at 200 tenants.*

## 191.3 ⭐⭐⭐ X-209 `Fixer` — THE FULL §157 HEADER

`@module X-209` `@intent INFORM`

**WHAT** ⭐⭐ **The employee's own AI — the only agent in this platform that works for a PERSON rather than for the tenant.** *Everything else acts tenant → customer. **The Fixer acts employee → their own day**: their calendar, their inbox, their jobs, their reschedules.* ⛔⛔ **AND IT IS NOT A CHATBOT. It is a TOOL-CALLING AGENT: it mutates the system through `X-122 ActionRegistry` and only then communicates.** *A plumber texting "running 20 late, tell Smith and push my next" causes `fsm.job.update_eta` → `fsm.job.reschedule` → **then** the customer message. **The database changes first. The text is the consequence, never the substitute.*** ⭐ **It starts at L1 and climbs per action type, per employee** *(P-195)*. **Commanded by voice in `X-171`, by SMS from the employee's own phone, or from the private inbox — no dashboard required.**

**WIZARD** **inferred:** their role, their territory and their jobs — all already known · **confirmed once:** *(trigger: when the employee first opens their desk)* ⭐ **one button — connect my calendar** *(a unified provider, not four brittle native APIs)*, and **one paste — their static personal meeting-room link** · **tenant-facing:** nothing else. *A technician configures nothing.*

**AUTOPILOT** `ships: L3 · ceiling: L3`** ⭐⭐⭐ *(**`R235` 2026-08-27 — EVERY AUTOPILOT SHIPS ON.** The owner overruled the `L1 PROPOSE` default: *"ALL AI ON, by my law. The client can turn it off if they want. All autopilots on, with AI watching them."* ⛔ **`ships:` now EQUALS `ceiling:` — this acts from minute one.** The ladder survives as a DESCRIPTION of what the action is, **never as a gate on when it may run.** ⭐ Safety is `X-126`'s capability gate — **no grounding Fact, no skill** — not a human approving.)* *(**ships-at is `@intent INFORM` under `§227.2`** — factual, expected, safe)* ⭐⭐⭐ **This is the module where autopilot is the product.** **Every action type carries its own ladder position per employee:** *⛔ ~~draft a reply → 20 clean approvals → sends unasked. Reschedule a job → 20 clean approvals → reschedules~~ **STRUCK by `R235`** ⭐⭐⭐ *— **the employee's assistant SENDS and RESCHEDULES from minute one.** There are no "20 clean approvals" to earn; **that is the ladder-as-gate `R235` overruled.** The employee may switch any action off (`R236` `OFF_BY_CLIENT`), and `X-126`'s gate supervises every one.* and reportss.* **An EDIT resets that action's counter; a REJECT drops it a level** *(§149.1, generalised)*. ⛔ **A new hire starts at L1 on everything. A dispatcher of two years is at L3 on the things they have always approved and L1 on the things they have not.**

**SWARM** **SQ-2 · WAVE 2** *(it needs X-108's calendar and X-162's board)*. Owns `app/Modules/Staff/Fixer/**`. ⛔⛔ **`doctor` asserts this module contains NO direct model writes — every mutation is `ActionRegistry::call()`**, which means every Fixer action is **already logged by X-122 and already reversible where the action is `compensable`.** *Tool-call strictness is not new machinery; it is the seam that already exists.* **Runtime proof =** a real SMS from a real staff handset causing a real row change and a real outbound, with the message id in the trace.

**SCREENS** the private inbox *(a view, never a store)* · the one-tap approval card · **the ladder's own state, shown as *"I've handled 34 of these — want me to stop asking?"*** — ⭐ *the promotion is visible, never a setting.*

**DECLARATIONS** `@renders private_inbox · onetap_approval_card · ladders_own_state` *(derived from SCREENS, 2026-08-27 — names only; the JSON schema each block carries is turn 69's)*
`@provides fixer.command · fixer.approve · fixer.delegate` · `@emits fixer.command_received · fixer.action_taken · fixer.escalated · fixer.promoted` · ``@consumes `job.dispatched` · `job.completed`` ⭐ *(2026-08-27, owner-confirmed — the employee's assistant acts on THEIR day — `dispatched` starts it, `completed` ends it. ⛔ `job.created`/`job.started` are tenant-level lifecycle, not the employee's.)* · @owns_table fixer_commands · fixer_ladder · staff_calendar_links`

@agent_reachable none · none · none ⛔ *(`P-209`'s BACKFILL GATE, 2026-08-27 — **every action here spends, sends, deletes or changes config. NONE is agent-reachable.** Silence would FAIL OPEN, so this declares the closed default explicitly.)*

**NEEDS / HAS** needs **X-122** *(every mutation)* · **X-108** *(the calendar)* · **X-162** *(the board)* · **X-204** *(any outward send)* · **X-202** *(the approval queue)* · **X-149** *(the promotion measurement)* · **X-206** *(the calendar credential)* · has: ladder position per employee per action · commands handled · escalations raised.

**TEST ANCHOR** *an SMS from a staff handset saying "running 20 late, tell Smith" produces — **in this order** — a `job.eta_updated` row, a `ConsentService` decision, and an outbound message id. **If the message goes out and the row did not change, the build fails.***

## 191.4 ⭐⭐ THE FIVE MECHANICS — AND WHERE EACH ONE BREAKS

| # | Mechanic | ⭐ The design | ⛔ The failure it must survive |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **1** | **Tool-call strictness** | **every mutation is a registered action** — logged, reversible, replayable | ⛔⛔ **it texts the customer and the database never changed.** *"I told Smith you'd be late" while dispatch still shows 2pm is worse than silence — **now two systems disagree and the human trusts the wrong one.*** **Assert the ORDER: row first, message second.** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **2** | **Field SMS commands** | the employee's own handset, no app, no login | ⛔⛔ **CALLER ID IS NOT AUTHENTICATION. An SMS `From` is spoofable, and this path MUTATES a customer's appointment.** ⭐⭐ **The fix that keeps it frictionless: a command whose blast radius is the employee's own day executes on the SMS alone. Anything that touches a CUSTOMER gets a one-character confirm — *"Push Smith to 3pm and tell them? Reply Y."*** *One round trip, not one per command.* ⛔ **And a staff number that is also a customer number resolves to STAFF and logs the ambiguity** — never silently. |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **3** | **The Domino Gate** | a delay that collides with the next job **stops** | ⭐⭐ **Pushed further, because a question is work and a recommendation is a confirmation: the Fixer arrives with the ANSWER.** *"Delaying Smith overlaps Jones. **Mike is free and 8 minutes away.** [Reassign to Mike] [Push Jones to tomorrow] [I'll choose]"* — **the default is already right and it is one tap.** ⭐⭐⭐ **And it is on the ladder: pick "nearest free tech" twenty times and it stops asking.** *The domino gate is L1 today and L3 in six weeks — **that is the difference between a safeguard and a nag.*** |
| ⭐⭐ **4** | **The notification shield** | on a job → hold the non-critical | ⛔ **the AI decides what is "critical" from the CONTENT.** ⭐ **`P-062` again: the CLASS comes from the CALLER. A dispatch alert is critical by class; a marketing push is not. The shield reads `X-193`'s class and the calendar — it never reads the message and judges.** |
| ⭐ **5** | **Universal calendar sync** | ⭐ **one unified provider, not four brittle native APIs** — the owner is right and this is the single biggest support-ticket saver in the module | ⚠️ **it is a PER-SEAT recurring cost** *(these providers bill per connected account)*. **Same rule as the affiliate numbers: connect on demand, when the employee first needs scheduling — never for every seat at signup.** ⛔ **And a sync failure is VISIBLE: a calendar that silently stopped syncing double-books a technician in front of a customer.** |

⭐ **Meeting links: the static personal room, pasted once, injected into the invite. No Zoom API, no OAuth, no support tickets.** *That is the "5-year-old design" instruction applied correctly — **the frictionless version is also the one with fewer moving parts.***

## 191.5 ⛔⛔ THE ONE RAIL THAT DOES NOT MOVE

**The Fixer is an INTERNAL agent with an OUTWARD ARM, and the two halves have different rules:**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Inward** — reading the employee's calendar, moving their jobs, drafting in their inbox | **no `ConsentService`** — an employee is an actor, not a `Person` being marketed to |
| ⛔⛔ **Outward** — any message to a CUSTOMER | ⭐⭐ **`X-204` decides, exactly as it does for every other channel. No ladder position, no seniority and no "the tech said so" ever bypasses it.** *A promoted Fixer sends without ASKING THE EMPLOYEE. It never sends without asking `ConsentService`.* |

⭐⭐⭐ **That distinction is the whole safety of the module and it is one line in the code: `grep` shows every outward path in `Staff/Fixer/` passing `decide()`.** ⛔ *Get it wrong and you have built an autonomous agent, operated by a phone number, that can text a customer with no permit — **and it will feel like a feature right up until it is not.***

# 192. TURN 43 — CRM (b) · SCHEDULING · DISPATCH · NURTURE · CHURN *(turn 43 of 109 · T677 · 4 modules · 35 rows)*

> ⭐⭐ **The pass that owns a customer's TIME — and time is the one thing this platform promises that it cannot apologise its way out of. A wrong price is embarrassing. A missed appointment is a lost customer and a bad review in the same afternoon.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**A slot that was never really free.** *Scheduling looks like a calendar problem and is actually a **consistency** problem: the AI offers 2pm from one view of availability, the tech's own phone shows a personal appointment, the dispatch board shows travel time nobody subtracted, and the customer is told 2pm.* ⛔⛔ **Three systems, three answers, one customer waiting on a porch.**
⭐⭐ **So `P-092` is not only about prices — it is about TIMES: a slot is LOOKED UP from one authoritative availability view, or the AI refuses to offer one.** *"Let me check and text you right back" is a perfectly good answer. **"How's 2pm?" when 2pm is not free is the answer that costs the job.***

| ⭐ **P-077** | the claim expires at **30 minutes** *(X-153's shape)* — a held slot is released, never orphaned |
| ⭐ **P-195 floors** | **X-108 scheduling = L2** *(a customer is waiting)* · **X-162 dispatch = L3** *(internal)* · **X-07 nurture = L1** *(it reaches a person)* · ⭐ **X-08 churn = L0 — it observes and never acts** |
| ⛔⛔ **The Domino Gate** *(§191.4)* | **a cascade that collides drops to L1 and arrives with a recommendation** |

# 193. X-209 RENAMED · THE OLD SYSTEM, MINED AND FENCED · THE TWO-TIER VOICE FIX *(T677 · ⛔ not a turn · part A of three)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **The name goes. One idea from the dead system is genuinely better than what I wrote and is adopted. Two of its rules would break laws this plan spent eighty turns establishing, and they are fenced with the reason.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Mining a failed system for architecture instead of for symptoms.** *That document is a post-mortem of a platform that never launched, written as if its conclusions were sound.* ⛔⛔ **But a system that failed is authoritative about **what went wrong** and unreliable about **what to do instead** — and the two are mixed together in the same paragraph.** ⭐ *Its diagnosis is excellent: slow models tightly coupled to live streams, no idempotency, no compliance guard. **Its prescriptions include two rules that would break the laws that make this plan work** — and both are stated with the same confidence as the good parts.* **So every line of it is checked against the register before it is adopted, not after.**

## 193.1 ⭐ THE NAME — `StaffDesk`, and the real answer is that it does not matter yet

⛔ **`Fixer` is out. The owner is right — it is too close to a known platform and that is not a fight worth having over a module name.**

⭐⭐ **Proposed: `X-209 StaffDesk`.** *It fits the house convention exactly — the plan already runs `ApprovalDesk`, `ResiliencyDesk`, `RecoveryDesk` and `OperatorConsole`. **A boring compound of two ordinary words used descriptively is the lowest-collision choice available**, and it reads correctly the moment you see it.*

⭐⭐⭐ **And the thing that actually de-risks this: the MODULE name and the TENANT-FACING name do not have to be the same, and in this plan they never are.** *No tenant has ever seen the string `X-204 ConsentService`.* ⛔ **So the module is `StaffDesk` — an internal identifier in a codebase — and whatever an employee sees on their phone is a BRANDING decision, made later, with whatever check you want to run on it.** *That separation removes the whole risk from the engineering side and leaves it where it belongs.*
⚠️ **Stated plainly: I cannot check trademark availability, and I am not the right thing to rely on for that.** *Which is exactly why the tenant-facing name should be decided separately, once, deliberately.*

## 193.2 ⭐⭐ WHAT THE OLD SYSTEM GOT RIGHT — ONE OF THEM IS BETTER THAN WHAT I WROTE

### ⭐⭐⭐ THE TWO-TIER VOICE PIPELINE — ADOPTED, and it improves §171

> *Tier 1: an ultra-fast lightweight model, live on the call, conversation and AMD only, under 400 ms. **Tier 2: the heavy model runs AFTER the call ends** — CRM updates, summarisation, intent extraction.*

⭐⭐ **This is a genuinely better shape than what I specced at turn 36, and it fixes the exact number I flagged at §175.** *I found Sonnet at 410 ms inside a 600 ms budget — 68% of the budget on one call — and my answer was "the voice path defaults to the fast tier."* ⛔ **That was a routing preference. This is an architecture: the expensive model NEVER TOUCHES THE LIVE CALL AT ALL.**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Tier 1 — live** | conversation + AMD. **A hard budget, and the only models eligible are those the table says can meet it.** *Nothing else runs while a human is waiting to hear a voice.* |
| ⭐⭐ **Tier 2 — after hangup** | summarisation · CRM writes · intent · disposition · the QA scorecard. ⭐ **Three seconds does not matter here, so the strong model is finally the right choice** — and the cost is per CALL, not per TURN, which is a different order of magnitude. |
| ⛔ **The assertion** | **`grep` shows no Tier-2 model reachable from the live call path**, enforced by `doctor` — *the seam is structural, not a config value someone can raise under pressure.* |

⭐ **And it explains the historical failure precisely: the old platform coupled a slow model to a live stream, and every robotic pause was a customer hearing the architecture.** *Recorded, and §171's rows are amended to it.*

### ✅ Also right, and already law here
**Idempotency keys so a retry never double-charges or double-sends** — *already R9 for SMS debits, already added to X-129's replay at §191, and now stated as the general rule for every external call.* · **Defensive queuing and graceful rate-limit handling** — Step 8's pipeline. · **The 8:1 ratio** — ⭐ **confirmed already current: *"8:1 over true cost, DERIVED from cent-precision `ai_calls`, never typed."*** *Note the difference that matters: ours is **derived from measured cost**, the old one was a **typed constant.* **Derived survives a vendor price change; typed does not.**

## 193.3 ⛔⛔ WHAT MUST NOT BE ADOPTED — TWO RULES THAT BREAK LOAD-BEARING LAWS

### ⛔⛔ ① *"Content Linting Micro-AI — classify outbound content; if promotional vocabulary is detected, enforce marketing-class rules"*

**This breaks TWO of this plan's most load-bearing laws at once:**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔ **`P-062` — THE CLASS COMES FROM THE CALLER, NEVER THE CONTENT** | *Under the old rule, an appointment reminder that happens to say "we have a special on drain cleaning" becomes MARKETING and gets quiet-houred — **the customer misses their appointment.** And a marketing blast written carefully in transactional language sails straight through.* ⭐⭐ **Classifying by content means the wording decides the law, so the law can be written around. Classifying by CALLER cannot be.** |
| ⛔ **`P-071` — NO LLM IN THE SEND PATH** *(7 occurrences)* | *It puts a model between the permit and the driver: **latency on every message, a failure mode on every message, and a non-deterministic gate on a compliance decision.*** ⭐ **The current design already does the useful half at COMPOSE time and leaves the send path clean.** |

⭐ **The instinct behind it is not wrong — someone wanted a safety net.** ⛔ **But the net they built decides a legal question with a language model, at send time, on every message.** *That is the failure mode this plan's entire consent architecture exists to avoid.* **FENCED.**

### ⛔ ② *"Stage 1 Time Guard — EVERY outbound transaction outside 8am–9pm is delayed"*

⛔⛔ **Applied to every transaction, this kills the single most valuable feature in the product.** *The missed-call text-back at 9:15pm — **the one that fires on the RING and beats the competitor's voicemail** — does not go. R80 exists because that delay is the whole product.*
⭐ **The current law is the correct one and it is finer-grained: quiet hours are MARKETING CLASS ONLY** *(P-063)*; **transactional is exempt by its class, not by its wording**. ⛔ **The old rule is a blanket where a scalpel is needed. FENCED — the CLASS-based version stands.**

### ⚠️ ③ *"DELETE is banned; force DORMANT"* — right instinct, one reconciliation
⭐ **Consistent with this plan** *(48 references to dormant/soft-delete; nothing is destroyed)*. ⚠️ **The one thing it needs stated: "never delete" and "a customer asks to be forgotten" have to meet somewhere.** ⭐ **This plan's answer already exists: suppression is permanent, retention windows expire the CONTENT, and the audit trail keeps the FACT that a record existed.** *A row that proves we honoured a request is not the same as a row that keeps their data.* **Recorded so the two rules are not read as contradictory.**

⚠️ **And one framing not adopted: that document asks for a role, an acknowledgement phrase and a fresh session shape.** ⛔ **Forty-four turns of structure, 114 modules and 738 specced rows outrank a bootstrap prompt.** *The useful content is extracted above; the framing is superseded.*

# 194. THE LATENCY REFRAME · AND `StaffDesk`'s COMMAND GRAMMAR *(T677 · ⛔ not a turn · part B of three)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **The owner is right that the number is a target and not a law. But there is one distinction that changes the design — and one reframe that is worth more than any number: the defect is not the LATENCY, it is the SILENCE.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**A grammar that is a list of phrases.** *"The AI understands natural language" is where this gets built badly — someone writes thirty example sentences, the model matches them loosely, and **the same words mean different things on different days.*** ⛔⛔ **A technician's command MUTATES a customer's appointment. It cannot be pattern-matched.** ⭐ **Every command below resolves to exactly ONE registered action with exactly ONE guard, and an utterance that does not resolve cleanly is NOT guessed at — it asks.** *"I'm not sure — did you mean push Smith, or cancel Smith?" is a good answer. **Guessing between those two is how a customer's day gets cancelled by a typo.***

## 194.0 ⭐⭐ THE LATENCY REFRAME — THE NUMBER IS A TARGET, THE SILENCE IS THE DEFECT

⭐ **Accepted: 1000 ms is a working target, not a law, and no real call has happened. My §193 flag said exactly that — three numbers set independently and unreconciled — so this closes it the honest way.**

⚠️ **One distinction that must be recorded, because it changes what gets measured:**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔ **A model number is not a call number** | *The budget is **mouth to ear**: carrier in → speech endpointing → the model → TTS first byte → carrier out.* **The model is roughly HALF of it.** ⛔ **So "1000 ms" measured on the model lands near 1.8–2 s in the customer's ear — and that second number is the one that decides whether they talk over the agent.** ⭐ **Record the budget as TOTAL ROUND TRIP, and measure it there.** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **And the reframe that is worth more than the number** | **A 1200 ms gap with a filler is fine. A 900 ms SILENCE is not.** *That is what humans do — "let me check that for you" — and it is why a slow human receptionist never feels broken.* ⛔ **So the assertion changes shape: not *"the response arrives under X ms"* but *"NO SILENT GAP EXCEEDS X ms."*** **If the answer is going to be late, the agent says something first.** |
| ⭐ **What that buys** | **the latency ceiling stops being a hard architectural constraint and becomes a BEHAVIOUR** — *which is achievable, testable, and does not require the model to be fast.* ⭐ **It also means Tier 2 still matters for cost, not just for speed** *(§193 — the heavy model after hangup, per call rather than per turn)*. |

⛔ **The one thing that does NOT get more generous: the filler must be real speech, not a beep or a tone.** *A tone tells the caller they are talking to a machine that is thinking. **A filler tells them someone is looking something up.***

## 194.1 ⭐⭐⭐ THE COMMAND GRAMMAR — 30 COMMANDS · 5 GUARDS · 4 FLOORS

**How to read the GUARD column** — *this is the whole safety model of the module in five values:*

| Guard | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| **READ** | no mutation. **Runs on the SMS alone.** |
| ⭐ **OWN-DAY** | mutates only the employee's own schedule. **Runs on the SMS alone** — the blast radius is theirs |
| ⭐⭐ **CONFIRM** | ⛔ **touches a CUSTOMER. One-character reply required** *(§191 — caller ID is not authentication)* |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **DOMINO** | may collide with another job → **drops to L1 and arrives with a recommendation** |
| ⛔⛔ **MONEY** | **commits or spends. ⛔ ~~L1 FOREVER~~ **STRUCK by `R235`** — it never promotes** *(P-195's financial rail)* |

*Every row also passes `X-204` if it sends outward, and every mutation is an `ActionRegistry` call — those two are universal and are not repeated per row.*

## 194.2 ⛔ THE FOUR RULES THE GRAMMAR ITSELF OBEYS

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **① An unresolved utterance ASKS. It never guesses.** | ⛔ *"Cancel Smith" and "push Smith" are one word apart and one of them is unrecoverable.* **Below the confidence floor it asks a closed question — never a free-form clarification, and never a best guess.** |
| ⭐⭐ **② A number spoken aloud is READ BACK before it commits** | ⛔ *ASR hears "fifty" as "fifteen" reliably enough to matter, and rows 16 and 19 both commit money.* **Every MONEY row confirms the figure in the reply.** |
| ⭐⭐ **③ The action runs BEFORE the message** | *(§191)* — **the row changes first, the customer message is the consequence.** ⛔ *A text sent against a database that did not change is two systems disagreeing, and the human trusts the wrong one.* |
| ⛔⛔ **④ The grammar is a TABLE, not a prompt** | ⭐ **These thirty rows are DATA — action, guard, floor, per row** *(P-193 · P-194's shape)*. *Adding a command is a row.* ⛔ **`doctor` asserts no command string is hardcoded in `Staff/StaffDesk/`.** |

**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **row 27 — *"I'm off tomorrow."*** *I have put it at DOMINO/L1 because tomorrow's jobs must be re-homed before it commits — **but a technician saying they are sick at 6am does not want a negotiation, and a system that argues with them will be worked around within a week.*** ⭐⭐ **The version I would actually ship: it commits IMMEDIATELY, the jobs go to the dispatcher's queue with recommendations already attached, and the technician is done.** *The domino gate belongs on the DISPATCHER's screen, not on the sick person's phone.* **That is a genuine correction to my own table and part C should carry it.**
