# 195. `StaffDesk` PART C — THREE AXES, NOT ONE · THE THREE ADDITIONS ADJUDICATED *(T677 · ⛔ not a turn)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **One collision has to be fixed before anything else in this section is safe to read: the returned table merges THREE independent things into one column, and one of them silently inverts `P-195`'s scale.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Two "L2"s that mean different things.** *`P-195` is already law, already a column on the law sweep, and already the floor on every one of §194's thirty commands: **L0 observe → L1 propose → L2 act & report → L3 autonomous.*** ⛔⛔ **The returned table uses `L1 = human override, L2 = 2FA, L3 = high-confidence AI, L4 = automated` — offset by one, missing L0, and with a fifth level that does not exist.**
⭐ **This is the `F-12` defect class again — two vocabularies for one concept — and it is far worse here than it was for `ProviderWaterfall`, because *"L2"* and *"L2"* do not LOOK different.** *A swarm agent holding a 20k brief will read both and reconcile neither.* **It has to be fixed now, in the artifact the swarm builds from.**

## 195.1 ⭐⭐⭐ THE FIX — THEY ARE THREE INDEPENDENT AXES

**The table collapses three genuinely different questions into one column. They do not collapse — a command can be perfectly heard, still need money approval, and still touch a customer.**

| Axis | The question it answers | Values | Set by |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **① THE GUARD** | ***What is the blast radius?*** | `READ` · `OWN-DAY` · `CONFIRM` · `DOMINO` · `MONEY` | **fixed per command, forever** |
| ⭐⭐ **② THE AUTONOMY FLOOR** *(P-195)* | ***How much may it do without asking?*** | **`L0` observe · `L1` propose · `L2` act & report · `L3` autonomous** | ⭐ **starts at the floor, CLIMBS by earned trust** |
| ⭐⭐ **③ THE RECOGNITION THRESHOLD** *(new — and the returned table is right that it exists)* | ***How sure must we be that we heard it correctly?*** | a confidence value, **per command** | ⛔ **ENVIRONMENTAL — it moves with the noise** *(§195.3①)* |

⛔⛔ **Never write them as one number.** ⭐ **Worked example, and it shows why:** ***"Charge the card on file"*** **= GUARD `MONEY` · FLOOR `L1` forever · THRESHOLD very high.** *Three different values, three different reasons, and no single number can carry them.* ⭐ **A perfectly-heard command still needs approval; a badly-heard one asks again even at L3.**

⭐ **And the returned table's real contribution survives intact: the CLOSED-QUESTION fallback — *"Reply 1 to cancel, 2 to reschedule"* — is exactly right, and it is what axis ③ triggers.** *Better than my §194 wording, because a closed numeric question survives a noisy truck cab and a free-text clarification does not.*

## 195.2 ✅ THE GRAMMAR AMENDMENTS — three adopted, one held

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ✅ **"Call out sick" commits INSTANTLY** | ⭐ **My own §194 correction, adopted — good.** *The absence commits; the schedule chaos goes to the dispatcher's queue with recommendations attached.* **The domino gate belongs on the dispatcher's screen, not on the sick person's phone.** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **"Client approved $1,500" needs the CLIENT's confirmation — ADOPTED, and it is better than mine** | *I had "read the number back to the tech."* ⛔ **That confirms we heard the TECH correctly. It does not confirm the CUSTOMER agreed.** ⭐⭐ **The tech's word is not the customer's word — the same finding as the Local Alliance at §185A, and I missed it here.** **`quote.accept` stages the invoice and confirms with the CUSTOMER before it commits.** |
| ⭐⭐ **Call bridging MASKS the tech's cell — ADOPTED, and it is genuinely new** | *Zero occurrences in 2.26 MB.* ⭐ **A technician's personal mobile number must never reach a customer's handset** — it becomes their permanent private support line, it follows them when they leave the company, and **the tenant loses the customer relationship to an individual.** **Every tech↔customer call bridges through a platform number.** |
| ⛔ **"Cancel the 2pm" at L2 — HELD at L1, and it does not promote** | *The returned table has it at CONFIRM/L2 with a "reply Y".* ⛔⛔ **A cancel is not a reschedule. The customer cannot undo it, they are not told by the same action, and the slot is released to someone else within minutes.** ⭐ **The confirm is right and the promotion is not: this is the one command where twenty clean approvals must NOT buy autonomy.** |

## 195.3 ⭐⭐ THE THREE ADDITIONS — ONE EXCELLENT, ONE GOOD, ONE NEEDS ITS BLAST RADIUS CUT

### ⭐⭐⭐ ① ACOUSTIC ENVIRONMENT DETECTION — the best of the three, and half of it needs restating

⭐ **The core idea is excellent and I did not have it: THE RECOGNITION THRESHOLD IS ENVIRONMENTAL.** *A technician beside a 225-ton chiller and one in a quiet van are not the same speaker, and treating them the same is why field voice products fail.* **Measured noise raises the threshold; a raised threshold triggers the closed question. Adopted as axis ③'s driver.**

⚠️ **But the second half — *"dynamically raise TTS volume to punch through"* — does not work the way it reads.** *On a phone call the carrier normalises level, and the handset volume is the technician's own setting.* ⛔ **You cannot make a phone louder from the server.**
⭐⭐ **What actually works, and it is better: WHEN IT IS LOUD, STOP TALKING.** *Shorter sentences · DTMF instead of speech *("press 1")* · ⭐⭐⭐ **and above a noise ceiling, the whole exchange moves to SMS.** **A technician in a plant room cannot hear anything and reads a text perfectly.** *That is the honest answer, it is cheaper, and it is the one that survives contact with a real boiler room.*

### ⭐ ② PRE-FETCH RAG — adopted, with a trigger discipline

⭐ **Right technique: on `status.update_arrived`, warm the site's access codes, recent work orders and equipment history before anyone asks.** *The tech asks "where's the economizer damper" and it is already local.*
⚠️ **Two disciplines it needs:** ⛔ **prefetch on a STRONG trigger only** *(arrival at a site — not on every event, or you pay for context nobody asks for)*, and ⭐ **a prefetch that misses must fall through to a normal lookup, never to a stale answer** *(P-143 — `fetched_at`, and a warm cache is still a cache)*.
⚠️ *And the specific inference-server vocabulary is not this stack's — the plan runs its own; the TECHNIQUE is what is adopted, not the product name.*

### ⛔⛔ ③ THE LITIGATOR TRAP — the scrubbing is already ours; the "poison pill" needs its blast radius cut

⭐ **The owner is right: litigator scrubbing already exists in the plan** *(three references)* — **a third-party litigator/DNC list is a data source, and it is already in the suppression path.** *Nothing new is needed for the useful half.*

⛔⛔ **What must NOT be adopted as described: *"flags the ENTIRE TENANT ACCOUNT."***

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔ **One number should never flag a tenant** | *These lists are commercial, imperfect and third-party. **A person can be on one wrongly.*** ⭐ **`P-147` binds here exactly as it does to every other enriched field: SOURCE and CONFIDENCE.** **A hit SUPPRESSES the number — cheap, safe, correct. It does not accuse the tenant.** |
| ⭐ **A PATTERN is different from a hit** | ⛔ *Ten litigator hits in one import is a signal about the LIST the tenant bought, and that is worth raising.* ⭐ **So: one hit suppresses silently; a pattern raises an operator alert. Never an automatic account flag from a single third-party opinion.** |
| ⚠️ **"Permanently encrypts the number"** | *That is obfuscation, not a control.* ⭐ **Suppression is the mechanism** — the number is on the suppression list, `ConsentService` refuses it, and the refusal is logged with its reason. **Encrypting it makes it harder for US to prove we suppressed it.** |

⭐ **What survives, and it is the valuable part: the litigator list is checked at IMPORT, not at send.** *Finding it at send time means it is already in a campaign; finding it at import means it never enters one.*

## 195.4 ⭐ N PER ACTION — AND THE ESCALATION PATH

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **N is not one number** | *Promoting "send the on-my-way text" should be far cheaper than promoting "reschedule a customer".* **Proposed defaults: `OWN-DAY` N=5 · `CONFIRM` N=20 · `DOMINO` N=20 · `MONEY` and `cancel` — never.** ⛔ **All of them settings** *(P-193)*. |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **The reversal rate is the real signal** | *§189's flag: I do not know N and neither does anyone.* ⭐ **`X-149` watches whether a PROMOTED action gets reversed. A rising reversal rate means N was too low — and it demotes automatically, without anyone deciding.** *That is measurable in weeks; N is guessable now and wrong.* |
| ⭐⭐ **The escalation path — into the QUEUE, never a void** | ⛔ **When `StaffDesk` cannot resolve a command, it does NOT retry, guess or drop it.** ⭐ **It lands in turn 85's blocked-work queue with: what was said · what it could not decide · and the closed question it would ask.** *So a technician's unresolved command is visible to a dispatcher in seconds, and the swarm's own "stop and report" rule and the product's escalation path are the same mechanism.* |
| ⭐ **THE ONE TEST THAT PROVES THE MODULE** | **A real SMS from a real staff handset → `job.eta_updated` written → `ConsentService` consulted → an outbound message id returned — IN THAT ORDER.** ⛔ **If the message goes out and the row did not change, the build fails.** *One test, and it exercises the grammar, the guard, the action registry, the consent rail and the ordering rule at once.* |

---

**CHECKED:** the returned floor scale compared against `P-195` **as written in the register** and found **offset by one, missing L0, and carrying a fifth level** — which is what turned a table into a collision · the three axes separated by **asking what question each one answers**, and shown non-collapsible with a worked example · **litigator scrubbing confirmed already present** *(3 references)* before recommending anything new · **number masking confirmed ABSENT** *(0 occurrences in 2.26 MB)* — which is what makes it a genuine addition rather than a restatement · the TTS-volume claim checked against how a phone call actually works, and **the working half kept while the unworkable half was replaced with something better.**
**FAILS IF:** ⛔⛔ **the two floor scales both reach the swarm.** *Every other collision this session was between two different WORDS. **This one is between two identical strings that mean different things** — and it is written into the law sweep, into P-195, and onto thirty commands.* ⭐ **`P-195`'s `L0–L3` is the only scale. `L4` does not exist. If the returned table is used anywhere, it is re-mapped first or nothing built from it is trustworthy.**
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **the noise ceiling above which voice gives up and switches to SMS.** *I am confident the SWITCH is right — a tech in a plant room reads a text and cannot hear a word.* ⛔ **I have no idea what the dB threshold is, and a wrong one is bad in both directions: too low and it abandons voice in a normal truck cab, too high and it keeps talking into a boiler room.** ⭐⭐ **It is a setting, it starts conservative, and the number that tunes it is the CLOSED-QUESTION RATE — if the system is asking "press 1 or 2" constantly, the threshold is wrong, and that is visible in a week of real use.**

# 196. ⛔ "FSM" MEANS TWO THINGS · AND THE CONVERSATIONAL FRAME *(T677 · ⛔ not a turn)*

> ⛔⛔ **Third acronym collision in three sections — and this one would have silently deleted a whole turn's work. `FSM` in this plan means FIELD SERVICE MANAGEMENT. Turn 44 is twelve field-service modules and 35 rows. It is not finite state machines.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**A turn that runs on the wrong meaning of its own name.** *`GOAIEZ-TURNS.md`, turn 44, verbatim: **"FSM — pricebook · money trail · the field."** Twelve modules — `X-163 PriceBook`, `X-167 Inventory`, `X-171 TechMobile`, `X-164 Agreements` and the rest.* ⛔⛔ **Run turn 44 as "finite state machines" and those twelve modules are never folded in, 35 rows vanish from the count, and nothing ever notices — because turn 44 would be ticked.**
⭐⭐ **And the pattern is now the finding: THREE acronym collisions in three consecutive sections** — `ProviderWaterfall` *(data vs AI)*, the `L2` scale *(guard vs autonomy)*, and now `FSM` *(field service vs state machine)*. ⭐ **Two AIs with different vocabularies are writing into one plan, and the collisions are accelerating.** ⛔ **New standing rule: an acronym used in a directive is expanded on first use, or it is checked against the plan before it is acted on.**

## 196.1 ✅ WHAT IS RECORDED FROM THE RETURN

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **The Blocked-Work Queue = RECOMMENDATION PAYLOADS** | ***"The human is a reviewer, not a researcher."*** ⭐ **That is the best single sentence anyone has written about this queue.** *An item never enters as a raw error — it enters as a problem with a pre-calculated one-click answer:* **"Bob is out. 4 jobs need re-homing. Shift 8am to Alice (on route), push 10am to tomorrow, shift 2pm to Dave. [APPROVE PLAN] [MODIFY]."** ⛔ **A queue of problems is a second job. A queue of proposals is a morning's work in four taps.** **LOCKED.** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **Fillers are PRE-CACHED `.wav`, never generated** | ⭐⭐ **This is the correct fix and it closes a hole in my own §194 reframe: I said "the agent says something first" and never said WHERE the something comes from.** ⛔ **Generating a filler through the model adds latency to the latency — the cure would have caused the disease.** ⭐ **10–15 local files in the persona's voice, on the edge, injected by a hard timer when Tier-1 sees a heavy intent. Zero dead air, zero added latency.** **LOCKED.** |
| ✅ **The `AWAITING_CUSTOMER` state on a money commit** | *the tech says charge it → the CUSTOMER is texted to authorise → the ticket sits locked → after 10 minutes the dispatcher can call.* ⭐ **Right, and it is §195's finding implemented: the customer confirms money, not the tech.** |
| ✅ **All three of my corrections conceded** | acoustic → SMS not volume · litigator → suppress, **do not flag, do not encrypt** · **the customer confirms money · call bridging masks the cell.** |

## 196.2 ⭐⭐⭐ THE CONVERSATIONAL FRAME — AND WHY IT IS NOT A STATE MACHINE

⭐ **The question asked is a good one and the `WHAT KILLS THIS` behind it is exactly right: a customer mid-booking who asks *"how much is the diagnostic fee?"* and is told to pick a time first has just met a machine.** ⛔ **But "state suspension and resumption" is a fix for a problem that a state machine creates and a different structure does not have.**

### ⛔ Why a state machine is the wrong primitive here

*A state machine says: **you are in state `Awaiting_Time`.*** ⛔⛔ **But a real customer says: *"Yeah it's the water heater, I'm at 14 Oak, Thursday afternoon works, how much roughly?"*** — **four slots and a tangent in one breath.** *A state machine has to be in one state; that sentence is in four.* ⭐ **So you end up building suspension, resumption, a stack, re-entry guards — all to work around the fact that the primitive was wrong.**

### ⭐⭐⭐ The primitive: A FRAME OF SLOTS, and an INTENT STACK

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **A goal is a FRAME** | *booking = `{problem, address, window, contact}`.* **There is no "state" — there is only WHICH SLOTS ARE STILL EMPTY.** ⭐ **Slots fill in any order, several at once, from any channel.** |
| ⭐ **The next question is DERIVED, never scripted** | *"what is empty and most needed"* — **so there is no sequence to trap anyone in**, and no script to fall out of. |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **A tangent is a PUSH, not a transition** | *"How much is the diagnostic?"* → **push `answer_question`, answer it, pop, and the frame is untouched because nothing was suspended.** ⛔ **Nothing to resume, because nothing stopped.** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **A CORRECTION outranks everything, at any time** | ⛔⛔ ***"No, I said THURSDAY"* is the single most common real utterance in a booking, and it is the one a state machine handles worst.** ⭐ **A correction overwrites a filled slot from any position in the conversation, with no re-entry, no confirmation loop, and no "let's start again."** |
| ⭐⭐ **A REFUSAL is a first-class outcome, not a failure** | *If a slot needs a price and no grounded price exists* — ⛔ **that is not a dead end.** ⭐ ***"Let me find out and text you right back"* fills nothing, ends nothing, and keeps the frame alive** *(P-092)*. |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **THE ABANDONMENT RULE — and it is the anti-trap** | ⛔⛔ **After the SAME slot is asked for twice and not given, STOP ASKING.** *Nothing makes a person hang up faster than a third identical question.* ⭐ **Take what you have, book what you can, hand the gap to a human.** **A half-filled frame with a human attached beats a perfect frame nobody finished.** |

### ⭐⭐ THE PART NO COMPETITOR HAS — the frame lives on the `Conversation`

⛔ **Every phone bot on the market keeps its state IN THE CALL. The call drops, the state dies, and the customer starts again.**
⭐⭐⭐ **Here the frame is a column on `X-121`'s `Conversation` — so it survives the CHANNEL.** *A customer calls, gives three of four slots, loses signal, texts twenty minutes later — **and the agent says "hi again, just need a time for Thursday."*** ⛔ **That is only possible because of `P-163`, one `Person` one `Conversation`, and it is the single most visible payoff of a law that has cost effort in every pass since turn 34.**

### ⛔ THE DEAD-END GUARANTEE — one assertion

> ⭐⭐ **EVERY frame state — including the unrecognised one — has a path that reaches a human.** ⛔ **`doctor` asserts the frame graph has no terminal node without an escalation edge**, checked by walking it exhaustively, exactly as §184's widget state machine is walked.
*And the escalation lands in the same place StaffDesk's does: **the blocked-work queue, as a recommendation payload, never as a raw error.***

## 196.3 WHERE IT LANDS — AND WHAT ACTUALLY RUNS NEXT

⭐ **The conversational frame belongs to `C-Agent`, specced at turn 37 — so it is an AMENDMENT to §183, recorded here, costing zero turns.** *Twenty-sixth insert.*
⛔ **And turn 44 runs as written: FIELD SERVICE — twelve modules, 35 rows.** *`X-163 PriceBook` · `X-167 Inventory` · `X-171 TechMobile` · `X-164 Agreements` and the rest of the field group.*

**CHECKED:** `FSM` looked up in `GOAIEZ-TURNS.md` before acting on it — **turn 44 reads *"FSM — pricebook · money trail · the field"*, twelve modules and 35 rows**, which is what turned a design request into a collision catch · **three acronym collisions counted across three consecutive sections** and recorded as a pattern rather than three incidents · the frame primitive tested against **a real sentence containing four slots and a tangent**, which is what shows a state machine cannot hold it · **the pre-cached filler checked against my own §194 wording and found to close a hole I left** — I said the agent speaks first and never said where the words come from · the dead-end guarantee written as **an exhaustive graph walk**, matching the assertion style already used at §184.
**FAILS IF:** ⛔⛔ **the abandonment rule is dropped because it looks like giving up.** *It reads as the AI failing — asking a third time reads as persistence.* ⭐ **It is the opposite: a third identical question is the moment a real person decides the machine is broken and hangs up, and you lose the booking AND the goodwill.** **Two asks, then a human. It is the single most important behaviour in the frame and the easiest one to tune away.**
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **whether the frame should ever ask for a slot the customer skipped ONCE.** *I have set the abandonment rule at two asks — but there is a real difference between "they did not answer" and "they declined to answer," and I am treating them the same.* ⛔ *"I'd rather not say" and silence are different signals, and the second ask is fine after silence and slightly rude after a decline.* ⭐⭐ **Worth distinguishing at turn 90 with a real transcript set — it is the kind of thing that is obvious in ten real conversations and unguessable now.**

# 197. THE FOUR FSM INTERSECTIONS — INVENTORY · THE OLD QUOTE · RENEWALS · OFFLINE *(T677 · ⛔ not a turn · pre-work for turn 44)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **Four questions, four real answers — and three of them contain a trap that would have shipped. The quote one is the most dangerous and the answer is the simplest.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Repricing a quote the customer already accepted.** *Question 2 asks what happens when the pricebook moves and the customer finally says yes to the old number — and there is a reasonable-sounding answer that is catastrophic: **charge the new price, it is the current one.*** ⛔⛔ **A customer who agreed to $1,200 and is invoiced $1,400 does not file a support ticket. They file a chargeback, leave a one-star review naming the amount, and tell their neighbours** — and the platform's entire review engine then spends six weeks trying to repair damage the platform caused. ⭐ **The answer is one sentence and it is not negotiable: A QUOTE IS AN IMMUTABLE SNAPSHOT. It does not read the pricebook. It never did.**

*(⚠️ One vocabulary note in passing: "polymorphic ledger" is not this plan's term — the ledger is `X-82`'s and the conversation is `X-121`'s. **Fourth drift in four sections; flagging it small before it propagates.**)*

## 197.1 ⭐⭐ ① X-167 INVENTORY × THE DOMINO GUARD — and a data-model gap nobody has stated

### ⛔ The gap first: **this feature is impossible unless a job knows what parts it needs**

*"Check tomorrow's jobs for that compressor" requires a chain: **job → service type → pricebook item → its bill of materials.*** ⛔⛔ **The last link does not exist in the plan. `X-163`'s items carry PRICES; nothing says they carry PARTS.** ⭐ **So the first finding is a schema requirement: a pricebook item carries an optional bill of materials, and without it inventory foresight cannot exist at all.** *Recorded for turn 44's X-163 rows.*

### ⭐⭐ Then the mechanics — and "tomorrow" is the wrong horizon

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **The horizon is the PART's, not the calendar's** | ⛔ *Checking "tomorrow" is arbitrary.* ⭐ **A part with a three-day supplier lead time needs a THREE-DAY horizon; a part stocked at the warehouse needs a two-hour one.** **The horizon = that part's own replenishment lead time**, which is a column on the part. |
| ⭐⭐ **The trigger is `inventory.consume`** *(command 22, OWN-DAY, L3)* | stock hits zero on that truck → **the horizon query runs → any job inside it needing that part raises a DOMINO.** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **The payload is FOUR options, ranked — not "reorder"** | **① pull from another truck** *(who has one, how far, and does it break THEIR day)* · **② pull from the warehouse** · **③ reschedule the affected job** · **④ order it, with the lead time shown.** ⭐ **Ranked by ONE criterion: which keeps the most committed appointments.** *"The human is a reviewer, not a researcher" — the queue shows the ranked plan, one tap.* |
| ⛔⛔ **THE TRAP: the stock count is a lie** | *Technicians forget to log consumption. **The count drifts, and every recommendation above then fires on wrong data** — which is worse than no feature, because it moves real appointments.* ⭐⭐ **The fix: reconcile at COMPLETION. The job's expected bill of materials vs what was actually logged — a mismatch raises a low-priority correction, not a blocker.** ⛔ **Do not trust the count; verify it against what the job needed.** |

## 197.2 ⭐⭐⭐ ② X-163 PRICEBOOK × MONEY — THE OLD QUOTE

> ⭐⭐⭐ **A QUOTE IS AN IMMUTABLE SNAPSHOT, NOT A POINTER.**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **At send time, the line items and prices are COPIED onto the quote** | **The pricebook moving afterwards does not touch it.** ⛔ *A quote that re-reads a live pricebook is not a quote — it is a query, and the customer was shown a NUMBER.* |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **So the answer to "they said yes to the old price" is: WE HONOUR IT.** | **Inside its expiry, that is not an edge case — it is what a quote IS.** ⛔ **There is no discrepancy to handle, because there is no discrepancy: the quote never changed.** |
| ⭐ **Outside its expiry** | the acceptance is **REFUSED with the reason and a fresh quote offered in the same message** — never silently repriced, never silently honoured. ⭐ *"That quote expired on the 3rd — here's the current one, same work, $1,340. Reply YES and I'll book it."* |
| ⭐⭐ **And this SATISFIES `P-092`, it does not bend it** | *A price is looked up or refused.* ⭐ **A snapshot IS a lookup — one that already happened, at a recorded moment, with the source stored.** *The quote records what the pricebook said and when.* |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **The margin control is the EXPIRY, not the reprice** | ⛔ *"But costs rose 15% and we are honouring a loss."* ⭐ **That is what the expiry window is for: a short expiry on volatile items, a long one on stable ones — set per item, a setting.** **Fix the margin by shortening the window, never by changing a number a customer has already seen.** |
| ⛔ **The one thing that must fail the build** | **`grep` shows the quote renderer reading `quote_line_items`, never `pricebook_items`.** *If a quote can reach the live pricebook at render time, this whole guarantee is one join away from being untrue.* |

## 197.3 ⭐⭐ ③ X-164 AGREEMENTS × THE AUTOPILOT LAW — two different charges, and only one is ours

⛔⛔ **The question conflates two charges and they have opposite rules:**

| Charge | Rule |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **The TENANT's credit ledger, for the outbound SMS** | **metered usage at the 8:1 derived ratio — L3, fully autonomous, no human.** *This is ordinary and it is fine.* |
| ⛔⛔ **The CUSTOMER's card, for a renewed term** | ⭐⭐ **`P-195`'s financial rail: MONEY NEVER PROMOTES.** *An AI granting itself authority to charge a customer for another year is the subscription-trap complaint, and it arrives as a chargeback and a regulator's example.* |

### ⭐⭐⭐ THE RULE THAT RESOLVES IT: **THE AGREEMENT'S OWN TERMS DECIDE. THE AI READS THE TERM — IT NEVER INVENTS ONE.**

| The agreement says | What autopilot may do |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **auto-renews** | **the customer already authorised it, at signing.** **The AI executes: renew, invoice, notify — L3.** ⛔⛔ **BUT: THE NOTICE GOES BEFORE THE CHARGE, NEVER AFTER.** ⭐ *A renewal a customer sees coming is retention. The same renewal discovered on a statement is a chargeback — **and it is the identical amount, on the identical date. Only the order changed.*** |
| ⛔ **does NOT auto-renew** | **the AI drafts, prices from the pricebook, sends — and STOPS. `L1`.** *The customer's acceptance is the authorisation, exactly as with any quote.* |
| ⚠️ **is silent or ambiguous** | ⛔ **it does NOT guess.** *It raises to the blocked-work queue with the clause quoted.* **Q-087's shape: on conflict, stop and report.** |

⭐ **All of the ordinary work stays fully autonomous:** *spotting the expiry, drafting, pricing, scheduling the notice, sending it through the middleware, metering the SMS.* ⛔ **Exactly one thing is withheld: deciding, on a customer's behalf, that they have agreed to another year.**

## 197.4 ⭐⭐ ④ X-171 TECHMOBILE — OFFLINE IN A CONCRETE ROOM

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Every offline action carries a CLIENT-GENERATED ID** | so the replay is **idempotent** — *the same rule as `X-129`'s queue drain (§191): a retried action must not double-apply.* **Assert it by syncing the same queue twice and observing one row.** |
| ⛔⛔ **NEVER trust the device clock as the record** | *Phone clocks drift and can be set by hand.* ⭐⭐ **TWO fields, never one: the device clock is the ORDERING signal within that device's own queue; the SERVER's receive time is the RECORD.** |
| ⭐ **GPS still works offline** | *it needs satellites, not cell.* **Coordinates and a fix timestamp travel with the action.** ⚠️ **But an arrival stamp created offline can be back-dated** — ⭐ **so the record carries the CLAIMED time and the SYNC time, and a gap beyond N minutes is FLAGGED, never rejected.** *A technician in a basement genuinely has a two-hour gap and is not doing anything wrong.* |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **THE CONFLICT RULE — and this is the real question** | *A tech marks Jones complete offline; the dispatcher cancelled Jones an hour earlier.* ⛔⛔ **Never last-write-wins — that silently discards somebody's real work.** ⭐⭐ **THE FIELD WINS ON WHAT THEY OBSERVED** *(I was there, I did this, here is the photo, here are the coordinates)*. ⭐⭐ **THE OFFICE WINS ON ASSIGNMENT AND COMMITMENT** *(this job is cancelled, this is reassigned, this window was promised)*. **Two different kinds of truth, and neither overwrites the other.** |
| ⭐⭐ **An irreconcilable conflict goes to the QUEUE as a recommendation** | *"Bob marked Jones complete at 2:14pm; it was cancelled at 1:50. Photos and GPS attached.* **[Reinstate and bill] [Keep cancelled, log the visit] [Call Bob]"** ⭐ *Same mechanism as everything else — a reviewer, not a researcher.* |
| ⛔⛔ **NO LLM IN THE RECONCILIATION PATH** | ⭐ **The question is right to demand it.** *Reconciliation is deterministic rules on timestamps and ownership.* **The AI writes the recommendation TEXT; it never makes the reconciliation DECISION.** *A non-deterministic function deciding whether a job was completed is a function that decides differently on Tuesday.* |

---

**CHECKED:** the inventory chain traced link by link and **the bill-of-materials link found ABSENT from X-163** — *which makes the feature impossible as asked and is the finding, not a detail* · the horizon re-derived from **the part's replenishment lead time** rather than from "tomorrow" · the quote answer tested against **`P-092`** and shown to SATISFY it *(a snapshot is a recorded lookup)*, not to bend it · **the renewal question separated into TWO charges with opposite rules** — the tenant's meter and the customer's card — which is what dissolved it · the offline conflict resolved by **kind of truth** *(observed vs assigned)* rather than by timestamp, because last-write-wins discards real work · **idempotency carried across from X-129's drain**, so the same rule covers both replay paths.
**FAILS IF:** ⛔⛔ **the quote renderer is allowed to join to `pricebook_items` "just for the current price display."** *It will be proposed, it will sound helpful — **"show them what it costs today"** — and the moment that join exists, an accepted quote can render a different number than the one that was accepted.* ⭐ **One grep, asserted forever: a quote reads its own snapshot and nothing else.**
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **the auto-renew notice window.** *I have said the notice goes BEFORE the charge and I am certain of that. **I do not know how far before** — and it matters more than it sounds: too short and it is a formality nobody acts on, too long and you have handed them a diarised reminder to cancel.* ⭐⭐ **Thirty days is the common shape and I would start there as a SETTING, then watch the cancellation rate in the notice window** — *if cancellations spike right after the notice, the agreement was not delivering value and the notice only revealed it. **That is worth knowing, not worth hiding.***

# 198. TURN 44 — FIELD SERVICE · THE OPERATIONAL CORE *(turn 44 of 109 · T677 · 9 modules · 35 rows)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **The pass where the platform touches a technician's pay, a customer's signature and a business's cash. Everything before this could be corrected with an apology. From here, a wrong row is somebody's paycheque.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Payroll computed by an AI.** *This pass contains time tracking, overtime maths, commission splits, pro-rated final pay and payroll export.* ⛔⛔ **Every one of them is a number a human is legally owed, and a model that computes it "usually correctly" is a wage claim with a timestamp.** ⭐⭐ **So the rail is absolute and it is stricter than `P-092`'s: `P-092` says a PRICE is looked up or refused. Here — A PAYROLL FIGURE IS COMPUTED BY DETERMINISTIC ARITHMETIC OR IT IS NOT PRODUCED.** ⛔ **No model, at any autonomy level, ever. The AI may EXPLAIN a commission calculation; it may never BE one.** *`doctor` asserts no model call in `Modules/Field/Payroll/**` or `Commissions/**`.*

*(⚠️ And once more, small: the requested column heading says "Polymorphic Ledger." That is not this plan's term — the money ledger is **C-Billing's**, the rate table is **X-82**, and the thread is **X-121**'s `Conversation`. Second appearance; the columns below use the plan's own names.)*

# 199. TURN 45 — SEO & REVIEWS · THE PUBLIC-FACING PASS *(turn 45 of 109 · T677 · 6 modules · 53 rows)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **Every other pass fails in private. This one fails on Google, under the tenant's name, permanently indexed — and one of the three named traps is a collision with the owner's own law that has to be resolved before a line is written.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**A public reply that admits a fact.** *A 1★ says **"your tech flooded my basement."** An AI replying **"we're so sorry our tech flooded your basement"** has just published, under the tenant's name, on a permanent public page, a written admission that their technician flooded a basement.* ⛔⛔ **It will be screenshotted before it can be edited, and it is admissible.**
⭐⭐⭐ **The rule, and it is checkable: A REPLY MAY ACKNOWLEDGE THE FEELING. IT MAY NEVER RESTATE THE FACT.** *"I'm sorry you had this experience and I want to make it right — I'm calling you today"* says everything the tenant needs and concedes nothing. ⛔ **`doctor` asserts the reply text contains no noun phrase lifted from the review's allegation** — diffed mechanically, not judged. ⭐ **And a reply to any review below the threshold is `L1` FOREVER: it never promotes, at any trust level, for any tenant.**

## 199.1 ✅ THE REVIEW GATE IS LAW — SETTLED, T677

> ⛔⛔ **SETTLED BY THE OWNER. DO NOT RE-RAISE.** *This has been raised three times and ruled on three times. It is closed.*

⭐ **`P-110` stands exactly as the owner wrote it at §168A, and it is the design:**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **`public_threshold`** | **default 4** — 1–3 are gated · max 5 · the tenant may set it |
| **The loop** | gated → **QA ticket + SLA** → RESOLVED → **the AI asks again** → at or above the threshold → **the public link and the destination roster** |
| **The cap** | ⭐ **TWO PASSES MAXIMUM.** A second low rating triages again and does **not** re-enter the review system a third time |
| **`fix_then_ask_enabled`** | **ON.** Trigger = `ticket.resolved`, never a timer |
| **The photo** | the ask requests a photo of the finished work; **a photo with no recorded grant cannot render** *(OWN-07, checked at render)* |
| **Destinations** | Google · Yelp · Facebook · BBB · Bing · Trustpilot · app store — **inferred, confirmed once, distributed unasked**; per-destination `solicitation_policy` is **data** *(Law 122)* |

⭐ **This is how the product works. It is recorded, it is built, and no further commentary attaches to it.**

⚠️ **"Owner rows" here means rows recorded from the OWNER's rulings at §168A** — `OWN-01…08` — **not "rows that alert the business owner."** *Fifth vocabulary drift; noting it small.*
⭐ **But the question underneath is a good one and deserves its own answer: WHAT REACHES THE BUSINESS OWNER DIRECTLY, BYPASSING EVERYONE?**

> ⭐⭐⭐ **Three things, and only three: ① a 1★ · ② any review containing a LEGAL signal** *(lawyer, sue, attorney, small claims, licence board)* **· ③ any review NAMING AN EMPLOYEE.** ⛔ **These bypass the dispatcher, bypass quiet hours, bypass the digest, and arrive as a push within minutes** *(X-207, transactional class)*. **Everything else waits for the daily roll-up.**
⭐ *Rationale: those three are the only review types where the first hour changes the outcome. A 2★ about parking can wait until morning.*

# 200. TURN 46 — SOCIAL & CONTENT · THE PROVENANCE PASS *(turn 46 of 109 · T677 · 7 modules · 50 rows)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **One rule answers all four traps at once, and it is not a safety feature — it is what makes the content good.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**A post with no source.** *Every one of the four named traps is the same failure: **the AI wrote about a topic instead of about a THING THAT HAPPENED.*** ⛔ *A "$50 off tune-up" nobody approved · thirty days of "don't forget to change your filter" · the same "Happy First Day of Spring" on four hundred plumbing pages.* ⭐⭐⭐ **All three come from a generator asked to produce CONTENT rather than to REPORT A ROW.**

> ⭐⭐⭐ **THE LAW: A POST MUST CARRY A `source_row`. No source, no post.**
> *Not "write about HVAC maintenance" — **"job #4417: a 40-gallon heater replaced on Oak Street this morning, here is the tech's photo."***

⭐⭐ **And this is the part worth seeing: provenance is not a constraint on quality, it IS the quality.** *"We replaced a 40-gallon heater on Oak Street this morning" outperforms "don't forget to change your filter" by a wide margin — because it is true, specific, local and unrepeatable.* ⛔ **The generic filler was never good content that we are now restricting. It was always the worst content, and it was only ever produced because there was nothing forcing the generator to look at the business.**

⛔⛔ **AND THE COUNTERPART THAT MAKES IT REAL: when there is no source row this week, POST NOTHING.** *A quiet tenant had a quiet week.* ⭐ **The feed says nothing and the tenant is told why — "no jobs to show this week, so I didn't post." That is the honest counter applied to social, and it is the opposite of what every content tool on the market does.**

## 200.0 THE FOUR GUARDS FOR THIS PASS

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **① PROVENANCE** | **every post carries a `source_row`** *(a job, a review, a photo, a real fact)*. ⛔ `doctor` asserts the publisher refuses a post with a null source. |
| ⭐⭐ **② THE OFFER GUARD** | **any post containing a price, a discount or an offer carries a `promotion_id`** — a row in `X-163` with a start, an end and terms. ⛔ **No id → the claim lint rejects the copy.** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **③ THE ASSET LICENCE** | **every image carries a `license_source`.** *Three sources only: the tenant's own · licensed stock · generated.* ⛔ **A SCRAPED image has no licence row and therefore cannot enter the pipeline at all.** |
| ⭐⭐ **④ THE FLOOR** | **organic: `L1` → `L3` via §149.1's ladder, PER SURFACE.** ⛔ **A post containing an OFFER is `L1` FOREVER — it is a commitment.** ⚠️ **Paid/boost is ad MANAGEMENT and is FENCED by §44/P-128 — we generate the creative and hand it over; we never buy.** |

⭐ **On ④, the sharp part: the ladder is per SURFACE, not global.** *Earning autonomy on Facebook does not earn it on Google Business Profile — different audiences, different consequences.* ⛔ **A GBP suspension stops the tenant's phone ringing. Facebook going quiet does not. GBP starts stricter and stays stricter.**

# 201. TURN 47 — MONEY & MERCHANT · THE FINANCIAL RAILS *(turn 47 of 109 · T677 · 7 modules · 44 rows)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **Four traps named, and three of them have an answer that is a STRUCTURE rather than a rule — the card never arrives, the double charge is impossible rather than prevented, and the refund cannot be reached. Only one is a policy.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**A card number spoken aloud.** *A customer reads sixteen digits over a WebRTC trunk to pay an invoice. **The ASR transcribes them. The LLM reads them. The transcript is written to the `Conversation`.*** ⛔⛔ **And at that moment a plaintext PAN exists in the primary database, in a message row, indexed, backed up, and replicated — and it is in the ONE place this platform stores everything about a customer forever.** *It cannot be un-said, un-transcribed or un-backed-up.*
⭐⭐⭐ **A regex that redacts it afterwards is not the answer, because "afterwards" is already too late — the row was written.** ⭐ **THE ANSWER IS THAT THE AGENT NEVER HEARS IT: at the moment payment is requested, the call is HANDED to the gateway's own DTMF or hosted capture, the transcript is SUSPENDED, and the agent resumes when the token comes back.** ⛔ **We do not scrub the card out of our system. We arrange never to receive it.**

## 201.0 THE FOUR ANSWERS — THREE STRUCTURES AND A POLICY

| Trap | The answer | Kind |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **PCI contamination** | **suspend the transcript, hand to gateway capture, resume on the token.** *The PAN never enters our process.* | ⭐ **structure** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **The double charge** | **one `refId` derived from `(invoice, amount, attempt)`; the GATEWAY dedupes on it; a row-level lock on the invoice.** *Two clicks produce one charge because the second is the same request.* | ⭐ **structure** |
| ⭐⭐ **The autonomous refund** | **there is no refund action in the AI's registry.** *Not "the AI must not refund" — **the capability does not exist where the AI can reach it.*** | ⭐ **structure** |
| ⭐ **The chargeback** | **the evidence payload, compiled from what is already stored** | **policy + assembly** |

⭐⭐ **Three of the four dissolve into structure, and that is the finding: a money rule an engineer can break under deadline pressure is not a rule. A money capability that does not exist in the code cannot be reached at 2am.**

## 201.1 ⭐⭐⭐ ① THE REFUND GUARD — QUARANTINE BY ABSENCE

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔⛔ **The trap** | *a customer complains the tech was late; the AI "makes it right" and refunds $1,500 into a drained bank account.* |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **The structure** | **`payment.refund` is NOT in `X-122`'s registry for any agent seat.** ⛔ **`doctor` asserts no model-reachable action mutates a payment downward.** *The AI cannot issue a refund for the same reason it cannot issue a passport: **the verb is not there.*** |
| ⭐ **What the AI CAN do** | **propose one.** *It opens a refund REQUEST in `X-202` with the reason, the amount, the conversation link and the tenant's own refund policy quoted.* **One tap, by a human, executes it.** |
| ⭐⭐ **And the ceiling that survives the tap** | ⛔ **a refund above a threshold requires a SECOND human**, and the threshold is a setting. *The most common real-world failure is not an AI refunding — it is a junior staff member refunding, fast, to end a difficult call.* |
| ⭐ **Partial by default** | *a proposal defaults to the disputed LINE ITEM, never the invoice total* — **the AI cannot even propose the maximum by accident.** |

## 201.2 ⭐⭐⭐ ② PCI — THE PAN NEVER ARRIVES

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **Voice** | **at `payment.request`, the agent says one line and HANDS OFF: the leg is bridged to the gateway's DTMF capture or hosted IVR.** ⛔ **The ASR stream is SUSPENDED for the duration — no transcription, no model, no `Message` row.** **The agent resumes on the token.** *We receive a token; we never receive digits.* |
| ⭐⭐ **Web** | **the iframe boundary** *(P-160)* — **no card field exists in our markup**, asserted by grep. |
| ⭐⭐ **The field** | **`X-171` presents the gateway's own SDK sheet.** ⛔ *A technician never types a card into our app.* |
| ⛔⛔ **AND THE BACKSTOP, because a customer may say it anyway** | *unprompted, mid-sentence, before anyone can hand off.* ⭐ **A PAN-shaped token is detected in the ASR stream BEFORE the transcript is persisted — the segment is dropped, never written, and the agent says "I can't take card details this way — I'm sending you a secure link."** ⛔ **`doctor` asserts the persist path runs the detector, and a fixture transcript containing sixteen digits produces a `Message` row with none.** |
| ⭐ **Why the backstop is second, not first** | *a detector is a filter and filters have false negatives.* **The handoff means the detector should never fire. If it fires often, the handoff is broken — and the fire RATE is the metric.** |

## 201.3 ⭐⭐⭐ ③ IDEMPOTENCY — THE DOUBLE CHARGE IS IMPOSSIBLE, NOT PREVENTED

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **One key, derived not generated** | **`refId = hash(tenant, invoice_id, amount_in_cents, attempt_no)`.** ⛔ *Not a random UUID per click — **a random key makes two clicks two payments.*** ⭐ **A derived key makes the second click THE SAME REQUEST**, and the gateway returns the first result. |
| ⭐⭐ **The gateway dedupes, not us** | *Stripe and Authorize.Net both honour an idempotency key.* ⭐ **`G17-04` is exactly this row and it is why gateway-agnostic matters: the key is our contract, each adapter maps it.** |
| ⭐⭐ **A row-level lock on the INVOICE** | `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` — ⛔ *two concurrent workers cannot both start a charge on one invoice.* |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **The `attempt_no` is what makes a legitimate retry possible** | ⛔ *A pure `(invoice, amount)` key means a genuinely failed payment can never be retried — the gateway returns the old failure forever.* ⭐ **`attempt_no` increments only on a CONFIRMED terminal failure, never on a timeout** — *a timeout is unknown, and unknown must retry the SAME key.* |
| ⛔ **The assertion** | **fire the same payment twice concurrently and observe ONE `Payment` row and ONE gateway charge** — and **the same test with a 30-second network stall between them.** |

## 201.4 ⭐⭐ ④ THE CHARGEBACK EVIDENCE PAYLOAD

⭐ **The good news, and it is the whole reason this is cheap: every element already exists as a row.** *Nothing new is captured — it is ASSEMBLED.*

| The payload contains | Already stored by |
| :--- | :--- |
| the **consent record** with its timestamp, IP and method | `X-204` · `X-142` |
| the **`Conversation`** — every message both ways, in order | `X-121` |
| the **quote SNAPSHOT** they accepted, with its own line items | §197.2 |
| the **acceptance**: the SMS "YES" or the signature, with its own timestamp | `X-164` |
| the **job record** — arrival, GPS, completion, and **the tech's photos** | `X-171` |
| the **invoice and the payment**, with the gateway reference | C-Billing |
| ⭐ **a hash of the bundle and of each element** | `X-122`'s log |

⭐⭐ **Assembled into one PDF on `dispute.received`, and it lands in `X-202` as a recommendation payload — the tenant reviews and submits.** ⛔ **`L1`: the AI never submits a dispute response on the tenant's behalf.**
⚠️ ***"Cryptographically hashed"* is worth being precise about: a hash proves the bundle has not CHANGED since we made it. It does not prove the customer agreed.** ⭐ **What proves agreement is the CONTENT — a timestamped message from their number saying yes.** *The hash protects the evidence; the evidence is the message.*

# 201A. HOW A PAYMENT ACTUALLY HAPPENS — END TO END *(T677 · ⛔ not a turn · the flow §201 assumed and never wrote)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **Fair catch. §201 specced the GUARDS — PCI, idempotency, refunds, chargebacks — and never wrote the mechanism they guard. This is the mechanism, and the plan already commits to it: `X-198`'s header says it in one line — *"funds never route through us."***

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Confusing the two money flows.** *This plan has been using one vocabulary — "the ledger", "billing", "payment" — for **two completely different things that share no code, no gateway account and no legal position.*** ⛔⛔ **And the moment they touch, GOAIEZ stops being a software company and becomes a payment facilitator** — *with KYC on every tenant, liability for every chargeback, funds held on our balance sheet, and one fraudulent plumber becoming our regulatory problem.* ⭐ **For a one-person company that is not a feature, it is a different business.**

## 201A.1 ⭐⭐⭐ THE TWO FLOWS — AND THEY NEVER MEET

| | ⭐ **FLOW A — the customer pays the TENANT** | ⭐ **FLOW B — the tenant pays GOAIEZ** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Example** | a homeowner pays Bob's Plumbing **$1,200** for a water heater | Bob pays his **subscription** and buys **credits** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **Whose money is it** | **Bob's.** **[AMENDED T677 - P-197: true of the `EXTERNAL` relationship only. Under `ISO_SUBMERCHANT` and `GOAIEZ_PAYFAC` the route and the RISK both change - see section 203.]** | **ours — this is the revenue** |
| **Merchant of record** | ⭐ **BOB.** *His Stripe Connect account or his own Authorize.Net* | GOAIEZ |
| **Who eats a chargeback** | **Bob** *(we hand him the evidence payload — §201.4)* | us |
| **Where it settles** | **Bob's bank, on his gateway's schedule** | our bank |
| **The ledger involved** | the **INVOICE** ledger *(what his customer owes him)* | the **CREDIT** ledger *(the 8:1, metered usage)* |
| **Code path** | `X-117` → `X-198`'s adapter → **Bob's** gateway | C-Billing → **our** gateway |

⭐⭐ **`X-198`'s own header already rules this: *"Three consumers, one implementation — GOAIEZ → our account; AGENCY → their own; TENANT → their own."*** ⛔ **`doctor` asserts a Flow-A charge can never carry the platform's credential, and a Flow-B charge can never carry a tenant's.** *One assertion keeps us out of the payments business.*

## 201A.2 ⭐⭐ WHAT THE TENANT ACTUALLY DOES — ONCE

> **One button in the wizard: *"Connect how you get paid."*** *Stripe Connect onboarding, or their existing Authorize.Net credentials.* ⭐ **Their KYC is with the gateway, not with us. Their bank details never reach our database.**
⭐ **If they have no gateway, the flow creates a Stripe account in their name** — *they own it, they can take it with them, and it works on our platform and off it.* ⛔ **Not a wallet. Not "GOAIEZ payments."** *Their account, their money, their name on the customer's statement.*
**The credential lands in `X-206` as a TENANT-owned row — revealable to them, per §184B.**

## 201A.3 ⭐⭐⭐ THE SIX MOMENTS MONEY IS TAKEN

| # | Moment | Surface | Guard |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **1** | **A deposit at booking** | the booking flow's hosted checkout *(X-108 → X-117)* | **the deposit amount comes from the pricebook or there is no deposit** *(P-092)* |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **2** | **The invoice link** *(the common one)* | an SMS or email carrying a short link to a **hosted** payment page | ⭐ the link rides `shortLinkFor()` *(P-072)*, and the page renders the **invoice snapshot**, never a live pricebook *(§197.2)* |
| ⭐⭐ **3** | **In the field, on completion** | ⭐ **the gateway's own SDK sheet inside `X-171`** | ⛔ **a technician never types a card into our app** |
| ⭐ **4** | **Over the phone** | ⭐⭐ **the DTMF / hosted-IVR handoff** *(§201.2 — the transcript suspends)* | ⛔ **the agent never hears the digits** |
| **5** | **A card on file** | a stored **token** *(P-160)* | ⛔ **every charge needs a FRESH authorisation event — a stored token is not standing permission** |
| **6** | **Recurring, on an agreement** | the agreement's own terms *(X-164)* | ⛔ **notice BEFORE charge, always** *(§197.3)* |

⭐ **Every one of the six ends in the same place: a hosted surface the customer's card touches and we do not.** ⛔ **`P-160` and `Accept.js` are the mechanism — our markup contains no card field, asserted by grep.**

## 201A.4 ⭐⭐⭐ ONE PAYMENT, STEP BY STEP

> **The job is done. Bob's tech taps "complete." Here is every step, in order.**

| # | | |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1** | **The invoice is built** | from the **quote snapshot** plus any line items added in the field *(§197.2 — never from the live pricebook)* |
| **2** | **The AI sends it** | through `X-204` like every other message, on the **transactional** lane — ⛔ *quiet hours do not apply* |
| **3** | ⭐ **A payment intent is created** | on **Bob's** gateway, via `X-198`'s adapter, using **Bob's** credential from `X-206` · ⭐⭐ **`refId = hash(tenant, invoice, amount_in_cents, attempt_no)`** *(§201.3)* · **a row-level lock on the invoice** |
| **4** | **The customer pays** | on the **hosted page**. ⛔ *The PAN never enters our process at any point.* |
| **5** | ⭐⭐ **The gateway's WEBHOOK is the truth** | ⛔ **not the browser redirect.** *A customer who closes the tab still paid; a customer on a "success" page may not have.* **The `Payment` row is written on the SIGNED webhook**, and the signature is verified before the payload is parsed |
| **6** | **The invoice is marked paid** | ⭐ **in the same transaction as the `Payment` row** — *never two writes that can half-fail* |
| **7** | ⭐⭐ **Downstream fires from ONE event** | `payment.received` → **commission becomes payable** *(on COLLECTED — §198)* · the review ask enters its window · the ROI push's money figure moves · the job closes |
| **8** | ⭐ **The money settles to BOB'S BANK** | on **his** gateway's schedule. ⛔ **We are not in the path, we hold nothing, and we could not delay it if we wanted to.** |
| ⭐ **9** | **Separately, and unrelated** | *the AI minutes and SMS segments this job consumed were metered against **Bob's CREDIT ledger** at the derived 8:1 — **Flow B, a different ledger, a different gateway, a different day.*** |

## 201A.5 ⛔ WHEN IT GOES WRONG — THE THREE REAL CASES

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Declined** | **the invoice stays OPEN, the customer is told plainly, and a retry is a NEW `attempt_no`.** ⛔ *Never "payment failed" with no next step* — the message carries the link again. |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **Timeout — the dangerous one** | ⛔⛔ **We do not know whether it charged.** ⭐ **So we retry the SAME `refId`, and the gateway tells us: it returns the original result if it succeeded, or processes it if it did not.** *That is exactly why the key is derived and why `attempt_no` does NOT increment on a timeout.* **The customer is charged once, and we find out which.** |
| ⭐ **Partial** | *a deposit paid, a balance outstanding.* **The invoice tracks `amount_paid` against `amount_due`** — ⛔ **and commission pays only on what is COLLECTED, so a partial payment pays partial commission** *(§198)*. |
| ⛔ **Disputed** | **the evidence payload assembles itself and lands in `X-202`** *(§201.4)*. **Bob submits it. We never do.** |

---

**CHECKED:** the merchant-of-record question answered from **`X-198`'s own header, which already rules it** — *"three consumers, one implementation: GOAIEZ → our account; AGENCY → their own; TENANT → their own"* and *"funds never route through us"* — **so nothing new is decided here, it is written down** · the two flows separated by **whose money it is, who is merchant of record, who eats a chargeback and where it settles** — four tests, all pointing the same way · the webhook set as the source of truth **rather than the browser redirect**, which is the single most common real payment bug · the timeout case traced to **why `attempt_no` must not increment**, closing the loop with §201.3.
**FAILS IF:** ⛔⛔ **someone proposes "GOAIEZ Payments" as a revenue line.** *It is genuinely tempting — processing margin on every job across every tenant is a large number, and it will be pitched as leaving money on the table.* ⭐ **It converts a software company into a regulated payment facilitator: KYC on every tenant, chargeback liability, funds held, and one fraudulent plumber becoming your regulatory problem.** ⛔ **The `doctor` assertion — a Flow-A charge can never carry the platform credential — is what keeps that decision deliberate instead of accidental.**
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **whether creating a Stripe account IN THE TENANT'S NAME during onboarding is as frictionless as it reads.** *Stripe Connect onboarding asks for a tax id, a bank account and identity verification — **and that is a hard stop in the middle of a wizard whose whole promise is "nothing to configure."*** ⭐⭐ **So it must not block the rest of onboarding: the AI answers the phone, books jobs and sends invoices from day one, and *"connect how you get paid"* sits as a task until they do it.** ⛔ **A tenant who cannot take a card can still capture every job — and that is the right order, because the calls are the product and the payment is the plumbing.**

# 202. ⭐⭐⭐ P-196 — THE NATIVE CAPTURE & SCRUB LAW *(T677 · ⛔ SETTLED, DO NOT RE-RAISE)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **OVERRULE ACCEPTED, and the owner is right on the substance. My §201 position was correct for a company that never wants PCI scope. He is telling me that is not the company — GOAIEZ is going PCI DSS Level 1 and, in time, ISO / payment facilitator. That changes the correct answer, and it changes it in his direction.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**The exhaust, not the buffer.** *The Scrub Law is right about the database: no PAN in `messages`, no PAN in notes, no PAN in a table.* ⛔⛔ **But "the PAN never reaches persistent storage" is not the same as "the PAN never reaches disk," and the second one is what an auditor checks.**
*A PAN in process memory leaks through **an exception trace carrying the request payload · an APM or error-tracker breadcrumb · request-logging middleware · the load balancer's access log · a bound query parameter in a slow-query log · and a crash dump.*** ⭐⭐⭐ **Every one of those is written in good faith, usually by someone debugging at 11pm, and every one of them is the classic PCI incident.**
⭐ **The buffer is the easy part. The law has to cover the exhaust — and that is the one thing the returned design does not yet say.**

## 202.1 ✅ THE OVERRULE — WHAT IS ACCEPTED, AND WHY HE IS RIGHT

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **The friction point is real and I understated it** | *Sending a customer out of a live conversation to a hosted page is a conversion cliff, and in field service the moment is now — the tech is standing there.* **A purist answer that loses the payment is not a better answer.** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **And the direction settles it** | ⛔ **You cannot be an ISO / payment facilitator and not touch cards.** *The architecture has to support in-scope capture eventually.* ⭐ **Building it now, correctly and isolated, is forward-looking — not reckless.** |
| ✅ **Flow A / Flow B stands** | **funds settle to the tenant's own account. NOT a PayFac today.** *When that changes, it changes as a deliberate decision, not by accident.* |
| ✅ **CVV** | ⭐ **capture on the FIRST authorisation** *(it materially cuts fraud and declines)*, ⛔ **never stored, never required for a later charge on the token.** **X-120's build-failing CVV grep stays exactly as written.** |
| ✅ **Onboarding** | **pushed to a pending task. The AI books from day one.** |
| ✅ **GOAIEZ stores its own cards too** | ⭐ **and that is an argument FOR this design: one vault, one scope, one audit — instead of two environments to certify.** |

⭐⭐ **One thing worth knowing because it is free: on WEB and in the APP you can have native-feeling capture with the PAN never touching our server at all.** *Stripe Elements and Accept.js render an input inside our own page, styled as ours, no redirect, no context switch — and the card goes browser→gateway directly.* ⛔ **That is not the hosted page I described at §201 and it has none of its friction.** ⭐ **So the in-scope path below is what VOICE and verbal-in-the-field genuinely need — and those are the two channels where there is no browser to put an input in.** *Use the cheap path where it exists; use the in-scope path where it does not.*

## 202.2 ⭐⭐⭐ P-196 — THE LAW

> ⛔⛔ **SETTLED BY THE OWNER, T677. DO NOT RE-RAISE, DO NOT SOFTEN, DO NOT RE-DERIVE IN A LATER PASS.**

| # | The law |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **1** | **NATIVE CAPTURE IS PERMITTED.** *The platform may receive a PAN and expiry directly — by voice, by native app input, or in a secure conversational surface.* ⛔ **No hosted redirect is required, and the customer is never sent out of the flow.** |
| ⭐⭐ **2** | **THE TRANSIENT BUFFER.** *The PAN and expiry live in an encrypted, in-memory, transient buffer with a hard TTL measured in seconds.* ⛔ **Never a file, never a queue, never a cache, never a third-party log.** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **3** | **THE ABSOLUTE SCRUB.** ⛔ **The raw PAN is NEVER written, indexed or persisted to `messages`, notes, transcripts, or any table — and NEVER to a log, an exception trace, an APM breadcrumb, an access log, a query log or a crash dump.** *(§202.3 is how that is enforced.)* |
| ⭐⭐ **4** | **IMMEDIATE TOKENISATION.** *Server-side call to the tenant's gateway while the buffer is held; on the token's return **the buffer is flushed and overwritten**, not merely dereferenced.* |
| ⭐⭐ **5** | **WHAT IS STORED, AND ONLY THIS:** the gateway **token**, the **last four**, the **expiry**, the **brand**. ⛔ **CVV never, at any point, for any reason — X-120's build-failing grep stands.** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **6** | ⭐ **SCOPE ISOLATION — and this is what makes PCI L1 survivable for one person.** **`X-120 CardVault` is the ONLY component that may hold a PAN.** *It exposes `tokenize()` and nothing else.* ⛔ **`doctor` asserts no other module in the roster can receive card data — 113 of 114 modules stay OUT of scope, and the annual audit covers one small service instead of a platform.** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **7** | ⛔⛔ **VOICE: THE RECORDING PAUSES, NOT JUST THE TRANSCRIPT.** *Calls are recorded for QA and scoring. **A spoken PAN lands in the AUDIO FILE even when the transcript is clean** — and an audio file is storage.* **At `payment.capture` the recorder STOPS and the transcript suspends; both resume on the token.** ⛔ **Asserted by playing back a fixture call and finding silence where the digits were.** |
| ⭐ **8** | **FLOW A AND FLOW B STAY SEPARATE.** *§201A holds: funds settle to the tenant's own account.* ⛔ **`doctor` asserts a Flow-A charge never carries the platform credential.** *Becoming a PayFac is a decision, never a drift.* |

## 202.3 ⭐⭐ THE EXHAUST — HOW #3 IS ACTUALLY ENFORCED

⭐ **Six mechanical guards, because "do not log the card" is an instruction and instructions lose to a debugging session:**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **① The PAN is never a named field on a request object** | *It arrives, is consumed, and is gone before any framework binding happens.* ⛔ **If it is never in `$request->all()`, an exception handler cannot log it.** |
| ⭐⭐ **② A wrapper type, not a string** | **a `Pan` object whose `__toString`, `serialize`, `var_dump` and JSON encoding all return `****`.** ⭐ *So an accidental log line writes the mask, not the number — the language does the work.* |
| ⭐ **③ Exception handlers scrub before they report** | the APM/error-tracker integration is configured with the field on a **deny-list**, asserted in the config test |
| ⭐ **④ No request-body logging inside `X-120`'s scope** | asserted by config |
| ⭐ **⑤ Core dumps disabled on the vault service** | ⛔ *a crash dump is a memory image, and a memory image contains the buffer* |
| ⭐⭐ **⑥ The build-failing test** | **a fixture posts a real-format test PAN through the whole flow, then greps every log, trace and dump the run produced.** ⛔ **A hit fails the build.** *That is the only version of #3 that stays true after six months of debugging.* |

## 202.4 ✅ WHAT THIS CHANGES IN WHAT IS ALREADY WRITTEN

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **X-120 `CardVault`** | **its WHAT changes: "no raw PAN" becomes *"the ONLY component that may hold a raw PAN, transiently, in-memory, under P-196."*** ⛔ **Everything else about it stands** — token vault, brand/last4/expiry, CVV never, key rotation, the 15-day expiry warning. |
| ⭐ **§201.2's PCI section** | **amended: the DTMF handoff is now ONE option, not the only one.** *A tenant who wants the frictionless path gets native capture; the handoff remains available and is the cheaper path when it fits.* |
| ✅ **§201.3 idempotency · §201.1 the refund verb · §201.4 the evidence payload · §201A's two flows** | ⛔ **all unchanged.** *None of them depended on where the card was captured.* |
| ✅ **All 738 rows** | ⭐ **INTACT. Nothing is removed, nothing is re-scoped.** *626 specced at seven fields, 112 remaining across 11 modules, turns 48 and 49 unchanged.* |

---

**CHECKED:** the overrule tested on its merits rather than defended against — **the friction argument is correct, and the ISO/PayFac direction makes in-scope capture inevitable, which makes building it now the forward-looking choice** · **X-120 confirmed already present** as the token vault, so scope isolation costs **no new module** · the **exhaust** identified as the real gap in the returned design *(logs, traces, APM, access logs, query logs, crash dumps)* and given six mechanical guards rather than an instruction · ⭐ **the audio-recording gap found by asking where else a spoken number lands** — *the transcript was covered and the recording was not* · CVV confirmed consistent with X-120's existing build-failing grep · **all 738 rows confirmed intact.**
**FAILS IF:** ⛔⛔ **PCI scope leaks past `X-120`.** *It will happen the first time someone needs "just the last four plus the expiry" somewhere convenient and passes the whole object instead of the fields.* ⭐ **The wrapper type in §202.3② is what makes that harmless — a `Pan` that masks itself everywhere means a leak prints `****` instead of a card.** ⛔ **Scope isolation is not a folder convention; it is the difference between auditing one service and auditing a hundred and fourteen.**
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **the operational weight of PCI DSS Level 1 on a one-person company.** *Level 1 is the top tier — an annual on-site assessment by a QSA, quarterly ASV scans, segmentation testing, formal change control and evidence retention. **That is not a code problem; it is a recurring calendar and a recurring cost**, and it is the part that surprises people rather than the engineering.* ⭐⭐ **Scope isolation is the single biggest lever on that number** — *one bounded service in scope makes an assessment tractable; a platform in scope makes it a project.* **It is the reason §202.2's rule 6 is written the way it is, and it is worth protecting harder than anything else in this section.**

# 203. ⭐⭐⭐ P-197 — THE ISO / PAYFAC READINESS LAW *(T677 · ⛔ SETTLED, DO NOT RE-RAISE)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **Accepted, and it is a bigger correction than the last one. §201A said "funds never route through us" as though it were architecture. It was an ASSUMPTION about the business, and the business is different: the ISO contracts already exist. The processing margin is the revenue line, and the schema has to be built for it on day one — because retrofitting it later means migrating every tenant's saved cards.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**The tokens.** *Gemini's Phase 1 → Phase 2 flip — **"we can move a tenant to GOAI-EZ Payments with zero changes to the CRM, the AI or the front end"** — is true about CODE and false about DATA.* ⛔⛔ **A Stripe token is worthless on PayArc. An Authorize.Net token is worthless on NMI. The abstraction layer moves the CALL; it cannot move the CARD.**
*So the day you flip a tenant with 800 saved cards, either those 800 cards migrate processor-to-processor under a formal export, or **every one of those customers has to re-enter their card** — and a recurring-billing tenant discovers it as 800 failed payments in one morning.*
⭐⭐⭐ **This is the single hardest part of the whole plan and it costs nothing today: a `payment_method` row records WHICH PROCESSOR issued its token, and processor migration is designed now as a first-class operation with a re-collect fallback. Design it now, use it in two years.** ⛔ *Nobody discovers this early. They discover it during the migration.*

## 203.1 ⭐⭐⭐ THE CORRECTION — TWO AXES, NOT ONE

⛔ **The mistake that WILL be made if it is not written down now: treating "which gateway" and "whose merchant account" as one field.** *They are independent, and PayArc and NMI are the proof.*

| Axis | What it answers | Values |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **① THE GATEWAY** | ***how* the card is processed and tokenised** | Stripe · Authorize.Net · **NMI** · **PayArc** · *(more)* |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **② THE MERCHANT RELATIONSHIP** | ***whose account it settles into, and who owns the RISK*** | **`EXTERNAL`** *(the tenant's own)* · **`ISO_SUBMERCHANT`** *(underwritten through our ISO contract)* · **`GOAIEZ_PAYFAC`** *(our own, later)* |

⭐⭐ **NMI is a gateway that sits in front of many processors. PayArc is a processor and an ISO relationship. A tenant can be NMI-gateway + PayArc-processing + ISO-relationship all at once.** ⛔ **One field cannot express that. Three can.** *`gateway` · `processor` · `merchant_relationship` — and `doctor` asserts no code branches on the gateway to decide a settlement question.*

## 203.2 ⭐⭐ P-197 — THE LAW

> ⛔⛔ **SETTLED BY THE OWNER, T677. The ISO contracts exist. DO NOT RE-DERIVE THIS AS "software only" IN A LATER PASS.**

| # | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **1** | **THE ROUTER IS THE ONLY DOOR.** *No module — not `C-Billing`, not `X-117`, not `C-Agent` — ever calls a gateway SDK.* **`X-198` exposes `authorize · capture · refund · tokenize · payout` and nothing else.** ⛔ `doctor` asserts no gateway import outside `X-198/Adapters/`. ⭐ *This already existed as "built once, consumed by three" — it is now also **built once, flipped per tenant.*** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **2** | **THREE FIELDS, NOT ONE:** `gateway` · `processor` · **`merchant_relationship`.** ⛔ **A settlement decision may never be derived from the gateway name.** |
| ⭐⭐ **3** | **THE `merchant_status` STATE MACHINE** on the tenant: **`EXTERNAL_GATEWAY` → `PENDING_KYC` → `APPROVED_SUB_MERCHANT`**, plus ⭐ **`DECLINED` and `SUSPENDED`** *(underwriting says no sometimes, and a live merchant can be shut off mid-life)*. ⛔⛔ **NO STATE STRANDS A TENANT: a declined or suspended tenant falls back to `EXTERNAL_GATEWAY` and keeps taking money.** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **4** | ⭐ **THE APPLY DOOR IS SHUT UNTIL THE INTEGRATION EXISTS — STRUCTURALLY, NOT AS A FEATURE FLAG.** *No tenant can reach `PENDING_KYC` while the processor adapter is absent.* **The state machine IS the switch, so nobody has to remember to turn it off.** |
| ⭐⭐ **5** | **`transaction_fee_splits`** — every transaction records **gross · the processor's cost · the tenant's net · GOAIEZ's margin**, in integer hundredths of a cent *(§18)*, **derived from the rate table, never typed** *(P-194's shape)*. |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **6** | **TOKEN PORTABILITY** *(the WHAT KILLS THIS)*: **every `payment_method` records its issuing PROCESSOR.** **A processor migration is a first-class operation with a re-collect fallback**, and ⛔ **a tenant is never flipped without a migration plan for their stored cards.** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **7** | ⛔⛔ **THE RISK MOVES, AND THAT IS THE REAL CHANGE** — see §203.3. |
| ✅ **8** | **P-196 stands unchanged.** *Native capture, the transient buffer, the absolute scrub including the exhaust, the recording pause, and `X-120` as the only in-scope component.* ⭐ **Being a PayFac does not mean storing PANs — it means we tokenise at OUR processor instead of someone else's.** |

## 203.3 ⛔⛔ THE PART THE FOUR LAWS DO NOT COVER — WHO EATS THE CHARGEBACK

⭐ **This is the biggest consequence of the correction and it is not in the returned design at all.**

| Relationship | Who absorbs a chargeback the customer wins |
| :--- | :--- |
| **`EXTERNAL`** | ⭐ **the tenant.** *§201A's model — and it is why that model is comfortable.* |
| **`ISO_SUBMERCHANT`** | **the merchant, with the processor holding reserve** — *our exposure is indirect but real, because a merchant who cannot pay is a relationship we sponsored* |
| ⛔⛔ **`GOAIEZ_PAYFAC`** | ⭐⭐⭐ **WE DO.** *If a sub-merchant cannot cover it, it lands on the master account.* |

> ⛔⛔ **A plumber who takes £50,000 in deposits over a winter and goes out of business in March leaves the chargebacks with YOU.** *Not theoretically — that is the standard PayFac failure and it is why underwriting exists.*

⭐⭐ **So three mechanisms become part of the business, not features:**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **THE EXPOSURE LEDGER** | **per sub-merchant: money TAKEN against work DELIVERED.** ⛔ *A tenant sitting on a large balance of unfulfilled deposits is **our** risk, not theirs* — **and it is computable from data we already hold**, because the platform knows the job is not done. ⭐ *No other payfac has that. They see transactions; we see whether the water heater was fitted.* |
| ⭐ **VELOCITY LIMITS** | a new sub-merchant has a daily and monthly ceiling that rises with delivered history. **A setting** *(P-193)*. |
| ⭐ **RESERVE** | a rolling percentage held against exposure, released on delivery. **The mechanism must exist even if the rate starts at zero.** |

⭐⭐ **And the residual accounting, which is how an ISO actually gets paid:** ⛔ **a residual is EARNED at transaction time and RECEIVED weeks later, adjusted for chargebacks, refunds and interchange.** *Booking it at transaction and never reconciling makes the revenue number fiction.* ⭐ **So: accrue at transaction, reconcile monthly against the processor's residual report, and `G1-10`'s rule binds — an unreconciled cent RAISES.**

## 203.4 ✅ WHAT CHANGES IN WHAT IS ALREADY WRITTEN

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔ **§201A's *"funds never route through us"*** | **AMENDED — it was true of the EXTERNAL relationship and was never a law.** ⭐ **The two flows still stand** *(the customer pays the tenant; the tenant pays GOAIEZ)* — **but Flow A's route now depends on `merchant_relationship`, and under PayFac it passes through the master account.** |
| ⭐ **`X-198 MerchantConnect`** | **its WHAT gains: the router, the three fields, the state machine, and the adapter roster — Stripe · Authorize.Net · NMI · PayArc, adapters as rows** *(P-194's shape)*. ⭐ **It was already "built once, consumed by three"; it is now also flipped per tenant.** |
| ⭐ **File 13** | **PayArc and NMI added** — *contracts already in place, integration pending; the apply door stays shut until the adapter exists.* |
| ✅ **P-196 · §201.3 idempotency · the absent refund verb · the evidence payload · all 738 rows** | ⛔ **unchanged.** *626 specced, 112 remaining, turns 48 and 49 untouched.* |
| ⭐ **`X-120`'s scope isolation** | **more important, not less** — *a PayFac with 114 modules in PCI scope is not auditable; a PayFac with one is.* |

---

**CHECKED:** the correction taken at face value — **the ISO contracts exist, so this is a fact about the business and not a proposal** · **gateway and merchant relationship separated into two axes**, with NMI and PayArc as the worked proof that one field cannot carry both · **the chargeback question asked of all three relationships**, which is what surfaced the risk change the four laws omit · the exposure ledger shown to be **computable from data the platform already holds** *(the job status)* — ⭐ *a genuine structural advantage over a payfac that only sees transactions* · **residual accounting distinguished from split accounting** *(earned then, received later, adjusted)*, and tied to `G1-10`'s existing raise-on-unreconciled rule · **token portability identified as the real cost of the Phase 1 → Phase 2 flip.**
**FAILS IF:** ⛔⛔ **the apply door is a feature flag instead of the state machine.** *A flag is a boolean someone flips in a config to "test something," at which point a real tenant enters KYC against an adapter that does not exist and their onboarding dead-ends inside a compliance flow.* ⭐ **The state machine is the door: `PENDING_KYC` is unreachable while the processor adapter is absent, and that is a structural fact rather than a setting.**
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **whether `ISO_SUBMERCHANT` and `GOAIEZ_PAYFAC` are genuinely two states or eventually one.** *They differ in who underwrites and who holds the risk — and the commercial terms of your specific ISO agreements decide that, which I have not seen and should not guess at.* ⭐⭐ **I have modelled them separately because separating later is a migration and merging later is a delete** — *if they turn out to be the same thing under your contracts, collapsing two states into one costs an afternoon; discovering mid-flight that they were different costs a schema change on live money.*
