# 217. ⭐⭐⭐ THE 22 STRAYS — AND ONE OF THEM IS THE BIGGEST GROWTH FEATURE IN THE REGISTER *(T677 · reclamation pass 3)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **Twenty-two rows scattered across ten groups, read one at a time. They resolve into five clusters, one law, one held decision — and one capability that is the CRM equivalent of the card-portability moat and was sitting unmapped.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Three rows that are the same technology pointed in opposite directions.** *`Voice Cloning` · `Voice Biometrics` · `Deep Fake Audio Protection`.* ⛔⛔ **One of them is a protection, one is a marketing tool, and one is a biometric identifier collected — in the register's own word — *"PASSIVELY."***
⭐⭐⭐ **The difference between the defensible version and the indefensible one is entirely whether the person was TOLD.** *A voiceprint taken to confirm that the caller asking to move an appointment is really the customer is protective and welcome. **The same voiceprint taken silently, from every caller, is a biometric identifier collected without consent** — and in several jurisdictions that is the most heavily penalised category of personal data there is.*
⛔ **"Passively" is the word that has to go.**

## 217.1 ⭐⭐⭐ THE FIND — `Integration Marketplace` IS COMPETITOR MIGRATION

> *The register: **"Tenants can 1-click install the ServiceTitan, Jobber, or Housecall Pro apps, which instantly provisions the OAuth handshake and begins syncing the past 5 YEARS OF CUSTOMERS."***

⭐⭐⭐ **That is not an app store row. That is a MIGRATION-IN from the three direct competitors, and it is the single highest-leverage growth capability in the whole register — and it was unmapped.**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Why it is the one that matters** | *The hardest objection a local business gives is not price. It is **"everything is in ServiceTitan."*** ⭐⭐⭐ **A one-click import of five years of customers, jobs and history removes the only real switching cost — and it is the exact parallel of `P-199`'s card portability, applied to the CRM.** |
| ⭐ **It composes with what exists** | **`X-195`** hosts the connector · **`X-118`** already owns `Seamless Migration` · **`X-121`**'s twelve nouns are the destination · **`X-132`** de-dups on arrival. ⛔ **No new module.** |
| ⛔⛔ **And the rail it needs** | **An import is not a permit.** *Five years of a competitor's customer list arriving in one click is five years of people who never consented to hear from US.* ⭐⭐ **`X-204` treats every imported `Person` as UNPERMITTED until the tenant's own relationship is established — asserted.** *The data comes in; the ability to market to it does not.* |
| ⚠️ **The honest caveat** | *whether those APIs permit a bulk customer export to a competitor is their commercial decision, not a technical one.* ⭐ **The fallback is a CSV/file import, which nobody can block** — **and the module should be built so the transport is an adapter, exactly like the gateways.** |

## 217.2 ⛔⛔ THE VOICE CLUSTER — ONE LAW, THREE ROWS

> ⭐⭐⭐ **P-202: A VOICE IS A PERSON. NOTHING IS CLONED, FINGERPRINTED OR SYNTHESISED WITHOUT THE PERSON BEING TOLD.**

| Row | ⭐ Defensible | ⛔ Not |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Voice Cloning** *(the tenant's own voice, for ringless voicemail)* | **the tenant clones THEIR OWN voice, with an explicit recorded consent, for THEIR OWN messages** — ⛔ **and every message discloses it is AI-generated** | ⛔⛔ **cloning any other voice, at all** · **an undisclosed synthetic voicemail** *(this is the practice regulators and carriers are actively moving against)* |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **Voice Biometrics** *(caller recognition)* | **OPT-IN, disclosed at enrolment, used ONLY to authenticate a caller who is changing their own booking** | ⛔⛔ **the register's word is *"PASSIVELY fingerprints the caller."*** **STRUCK.** *A voiceprint is a biometric identifier; collecting one silently from every caller is the most heavily penalised class of personal data in several jurisdictions* |
| ⭐ **Deep Fake Audio Protection** | ⭐⭐ **the legitimate USE of the above: confirming the person asking to move an appointment is the customer on file** — *and this one is genuinely protective, which is why the enrolment is worth asking for* | — |

⛔ **The voiceprint is a `secure` field** *(`P-198`)* — **encrypted, never in a transcript, revealed by a named action, and deleted on erasure.** ⭐ *And the enrolment ask is worth its own sentence: **"want me to remember your voice so you don't have to confirm details next time?"** — a benefit, offered, refusable.*

## 217.3 ⭐⭐ THE RECRUITING CLUSTER — FOUR ROWS, ONE PRODUCT, HELD

**`Hiring Manager Extraction` · `Candidate Nurture Drips` · `Knockout Questions` · `One-Click Job Board Syndication`** *(scattered across `G3`, `G12`, `G17`, `G2`)*
⭐⭐ **Together they are an APPLICANT TRACKING SYSTEM — and they belong with the `G15` HRIS ruling, not scattered.** ⛔ **HELD pending your decision.**

⚠️ **But one of them needs flagging whatever you decide:**
> ⛔⛔ **`Knockout Questions`: *"if they select '2' years, the system automatically rejects them and sends a polite email instantly."*** ⭐ **An automated employment rejection on a single numeric answer, with no human, is exactly the class of automated decision that is increasingly regulated** — *and several jurisdictions now require notice, a human review path, or both.* ⛔ **If the ATS is ever built, a knockout question may FILTER and must not be the sole basis for a rejection.**

## 217.4 ⭐ THE INFRASTRUCTURE CLUSTER — NOT FEATURES, ARCHITECTURE

| Row | Verdict |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **ClickHouse Warehouse** | ⭐ **a real and good scaling decision — offload every pixel load, read receipt and API call OUT of Postgres to a columnar store.** ⛔ *It is not a capability row; it belongs in the DIGEST's stack section as an architectural note for when analytical volume outgrows Postgres.* **Recorded there.** |
| **ElasticSearch Indexing** | ⭐ *"type John Smith and see every click over three years"* — **the same shape: a search/analytics store, and the SAME decision.** ⚠️ *One store, not two — pick at wave 2 when the volume is real.* |
| **GraphQL Optimization** | an API-gateway option. ⛔ *Noted; not a wave-0 concern, and REST plus the action registry is sufficient until proven otherwise.* |
| ⭐ **Time Travel** · **Auto-Destruction** | ⭐⭐ **both are DEVELOPER SANDBOX capabilities and both are genuinely useful for THIS build**: *fast-forward the clock 30 days to test recurring billing* · *delete an untouched sandbox after 14 days to stop paying for it.* **They land in Step 8's pipeline work (turns 77–85), where the test environment is built.** |

## 217.5 ✅ THE REST — RE-HOMED

| Row | Owner | Note |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **Grandfathering** | **`X-210` + `C-Billing`** | ⭐⭐⭐ ***"raise prices in 2025 and the 2024 cohort keeps theirs."*** **This just became important: now that `P-001`'s list price can rise and discounts exist, a cohort's entitlement has to be a ROW on the subscription, not an assumption.** ⛔ **Asserted: an existing tenant's rate never changes without an explicit, notified action.** |
| ⚠️ **Multi-Entity Nesting** | **`X-176` SchemaEngine** | ⛔ **SIXTH TITLE-LIE: it is not agency hierarchies. It is nesting `Article` inside `WebPage` authored by `Person` for the knowledge graph.** *Pure SEO.* |
| **Embedded Apps · Private Apps** | **`X-195`** | iframe-embedded dashboards; a tenant-private connector hidden from the public store |

**CHECKED:** all 22 descriptions **read individually**, per §216's lesson — *which is what produced the sixth title-lie and the migration find* · **the voice trio recognised as one technology with three intents**, and the distinction located precisely at DISCLOSURE rather than at capability · the register's own word ***"passively"*** treated as the defect, not the feature · **the recruiting rows collected from four different groups** into one product decision instead of four scattered specs · **`ClickHouse` and `ElasticSearch` identified as the same decision made twice** — *one analytical store, chosen at wave 2* · `Grandfathering` re-read **in the light of §215's discounting change**, which is what made it newly load-bearing.
**FAILS IF:** ⛔⛔ **the competitor migration is built without the consent rail.** *It is the most exciting capability in the register and it arrives with five years of a stranger's customer list.* ⭐ **Every imported `Person` is UNPERMITTED until the tenant establishes their own relationship** — **the data comes in; the right to market to it does not.** ⛔ *Skip that and the first big win of the product is a mass unsolicited campaign to ten thousand people who never heard of the tenant's new platform.*
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **whether the competitor APIs actually permit a customer-history export.** *ServiceTitan, Jobber and Housecall Pro each have APIs, and none of them has a commercial interest in making departure easy — **the permission could be withdrawn the day the feature becomes visible.*** ⭐⭐ **So it must be built transport-agnostic from the start: an API adapter where one is allowed, a CSV/file import where it is not** *(and a file export is something no competitor can block, because the tenant owns their data)*. ⛔ **A migration feature that depends on a rival's goodwill is a feature with an off switch someone else holds.**

# 218. ⭐⭐⭐ THE INTEGRATION LAYER IN FULL — `X-212 MigrationIn` + `X-195` COMPLETED *(T677 · roster 117)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **Two things share one surface and have opposite risk profiles: bringing five years of a competitor's data IN, and running ongoing integrations. The first is the moat. The second is plumbing. Building them as one module would let the plumbing's convenience defeat the moat's safeguards.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Eleven thousand review requests on a Tuesday morning.** *The import lands 11,003 completed jobs. Each one writes a `Job` row. Each `Job` row emits `job.completed`. **`C-Reviews` subscribes to `job.completed`.*** ⛔⛔ **Every customer that tenant has served in five years receives a review request within the hour — from a company that just switched software, about a job from 2021.**
⭐⭐⭐ **This is the single most likely catastrophic bug in any migration, and it is invisible in testing because a 20-record test import looks perfect.** ⛔ **THE LAW: AN IMPORT WRITES ROWS AND EMITS NOTHING.** *Lifecycle events fire for things that HAPPEN. An import is a record of something that already happened somewhere else.* **`doctor` asserts the import path uses a `withoutEvents()` boundary, and the test imports 500 completed jobs and asserts ZERO outbound messages.**

## 218.1 ⭐⭐⭐ X-212 `MigrationIn` — THE FULL §157 HEADER

`@module X-212` `@intent INFORM`

**WHAT** ⭐⭐ **Bringing a tenant's whole business across from ServiceTitan, Jobber, Housecall Pro — or from a spreadsheet.** *Customers, properties, job history, invoices, payments, estimates, photos, notes, agreements, the pricebook, staff and reviews.* ⛔⛔ **AND IT IS A TRANSLATION, NOT A COPY.** *Their job-status enum is not ours; their pricebook shape is not ours; their custom fields have no home.* ⭐⭐⭐ **A migration that maps 80% and silently drops 20% is worse than no migration — because the tenant finds the hole three months later, on a job, in front of a customer.**

**WIZARD** ⭐ **inferred:** which system they are on *(detected from the connector they pick, or from the file's own shape)* · **confirmed once:** *(trigger: ⭐ at import — and ONLY for fields that could not be matched automatically)* ⭐⭐ **the field map — and ONLY the fields that could not be matched automatically.** *"We matched 41 of 44 fields. These three have no home: `Preferred Tech`, `Gate Code`, `Warranty Expiry` — where should they go?"* · **tenant-facing:** a progress bar and a report they can read.

**AUTOPILOT** `ships: L3 · ceiling: L3`** ⭐⭐⭐ *(**`R235` 2026-08-27 — `L1 FOREVER` OVERRULED.** The owner: *"ALL AI ON, by my law. The client can turn it off if they want."* ⛔⛔ **This module previously shipped at `L1` and could never rise; that exemption is STRUCK.** ⭐ **The autopilot runs from minute one.** *`P-096`/`D5` survive as a PER-ACTION confirmation at the moment of an IRREVERSIBLE step — **charge, sign, migrate, restore — never as a shipping posture for the whole module.** The client may switch this lane OFF; nothing requires them to switch it ON.)* ⛔ *(~~`L1 FOREVER` — the old exemption~~ **STRUCK by `R235`: this module ships at its CEILING and acts from minute one**)* *(was `@intent INFORM` under `§227.2`** — factual, expected, safe)* ⛔ **`L1` FOREVER on COMMIT — an import rewrites a business's entire history and is not reversible by a customer.** ⭐⭐ **What IS autonomous: the DRY RUN.** *It maps, imports into an isolated sandbox, reconciles, and produces the report — all unattended. **The tenant approves the COMMIT ⭐ *(**`R235`-COMPLIANT** — the dry-run, reconcile and report are **all unattended**; only the irreversible COMMIT confirms, per `P-096`/`D5`.)****

**SWARM** `SQ-13` · **W3**. Owns `app/Modules/Onboarding/MigrationIn/**`. ⭐ **Adapters per source, exactly like the gateways: `ServiceTitan` · `Jobber` · `HousecallPro` · `CSV` · `Generic`.**

**SCREENS** pick a source · the unmatched-field map · **the DRY-RUN preview** · the reconciliation report · the commit · the post-import audit.

**DECLARATIONS** `@renders pick_source · unmatchedfield_map · dryrun_preview · reconciliation_report · commit · postimport_audit` *(derived from SCREENS, 2026-08-27 — names only; the JSON schema each block carries is turn 69's)*
`@provides migration.dry_run · migration.commit · migration.rollback · migration.map_field` · `@emits migration.started · migration.dry_run_ready · migration.committed · migration.field_unmapped · migration.record_rejected` · ``@consumes `tenant.provisioned`` ⭐ *(2026-08-27, owner-confirmed — migration begins once a tenant EXISTS (`X-118`). ⛔ Not `tenant.created` — provisioning is the point at which there is somewhere to migrate INTO.)* · @owns_table migration_runs · migration_field_maps · migration_rejects`

@agent_reachable none · none · none ⛔ *(`P-209`'s BACKFILL GATE, 2026-08-27 — **every action here spends, sends, deletes or changes config. NONE is agent-reachable.** Silence would FAIL OPEN, so this declares the closed default explicitly.)*

**NEEDS / HAS** needs **`X-121`** *(the twelve nouns — the destination)* · **`X-132`** *(de-dup on arrival)* · **`X-204`** *(the permit state of every imported `Person`)* · **`X-206`** *(the source credential)* · **`X-163`** *(pricebook shape)* · **`P-198`** *(secure fields — see below)*. **Has:** what was imported, what was rejected and why, and **which fields had no home.**

**TEST ANCHOR** ⛔⛔ **import 500 completed jobs → assert ZERO outbound messages and zero `job.completed` subscribers fired.** ⛔ **A record with no strong identifier is REJECTED to the report, never merged.** ⛔ **A dry run writes NOTHING to the live schema — asserted by diffing row counts before and after.** ⭐ **And a committed migration is ROLLED BACK in the test, returning the tenant to their pre-import state.**

## 218.2 ⭐⭐ WHAT MOVES — AND THE FOUR THAT ARE DANGEROUS

| Moves cleanly | |
| :--- | :--- |
| customers → `Person` · properties → `Location` · jobs → `Job` · invoices and payments → `LedgerEntry` · estimates · photos → `Asset` · agreements → `Agreement` · pricebook → `X-163` · staff → `X-113` | ordinary field mapping |

| ⛔ **Dangerous** | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔⛔ **NOTES** | ⭐⭐⭐ **A competitor's free-text notes contain gate codes, alarm codes and key locations — the §204 burglary kit, arriving in bulk.** ⛔ **The import SCANS notes for access-code patterns and routes them to `secure` fields *(P-198)*, flagging what it moved.** *An import that dumps five years of alarm codes into a plain notes column has created the exact problem `P-198` exists to prevent, on day one, at scale.* |
| ⛔⛔ **CARDS ON FILE** | ⭐ *They are tokens on the competitor's processor and they are worthless to us.* **This is `P-197`'s token-portability problem arriving from the other direction** — ⛔ **either a processor-to-processor migration, or the customers re-enter.** **The report says which, in numbers, BEFORE the tenant commits.** |
| ⛔ **REVIEWS** | ⭐ **imported reviews are HISTORICAL and never re-published, never counted toward the tenant's public rating, and never re-solicited** *(P-110's two-pass cap has no history for them)* |
| ⚠️ **CUSTOM FIELDS** | ⭐⭐ **the honest one: some have no home.** ⛔ **They are NOT silently dropped — they land in a declared `imported_custom` store, listed in the report, and the tenant decides.** |

## 218.3 ⭐⭐⭐ THE FIVE RULES OF A SAFE MIGRATION

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **① AN IMPORT EMITS NOTHING** | *the WHAT KILLS THIS.* **Rows are written; the bus stays silent.** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **② DRY RUN FIRST, ALWAYS** | **into an isolated schema, with the full reconciliation report, and the tenant approves the COMMIT ⭐ *(**`R235`-COMPLIANT** — dry-run, reconcile and report are **all unattended**; only the irreversible COMMIT confirms.)*** ⛔ **Nobody migrates blind.** |
| ⭐⭐ **③ AN IMPORT IS NOT A PERMIT** | **every imported `Person` is UNPERMITTED.** *(`X-204`)* ⛔ **Five years of a competitor's list is five years of people who never consented to hear from US.** ⭐ *The permit is earned the ordinary way — they call, they reply, they book.* |
| ⭐⭐ **④ MERGE NEEDS TWO STRONG IDENTIFIERS** | *(§190)* — *the tenant may already have records from the trial.* ⛔ **A record with one weak match is REJECTED to the report, never merged.** *A merge is cheap to do and expensive to undo.* |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **⑤ THE RECONCILIATION REPORT IS THE PRODUCT** | ⭐ ***"4,812 customers · 11,003 jobs · 892 invoices imported. 47 customers had no phone or email — listed. 3 custom fields had no home — listed. 1,204 cards on file cannot transfer — your customers will re-enter them, here is the message to send."*** ⛔ **A number they can check beats a claim that it worked** — *the honest counter, applied to the most anxious moment in a tenant's life with this product.* |

## 218.4 ⭐⭐ AND THE EXIT — BECAUSE IT IS THE SAME PROMISE

> ⭐⭐⭐ **`P-203`: IF WE CAN IMPORT IT, WE CAN EXPORT IT.**
⛔ **A tenant may leave with everything — customers, jobs, invoices, photos, agreements, notes** *(secure fields exported to them, encrypted, never in plaintext)*. ⭐⭐ **Same mechanism, target reversed.**
⭐ *This is `P-199`'s card portability and `R34`'s 60-second cancel applied to the last asset that could hold someone.* ⛔ **A platform that makes arrival one click and departure a support ticket has not removed lock-in — it has moved it.** **And the sales line is stronger for being true: *"one click in, one click out."***

## 218.5 ⭐⭐ `X-195 Marketplace` — COMPLETED WITH THE FOUR RECLAIMED ROWS

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Install** | ⛔ **a MANIFEST plus config ROWS — never code.** *`doctor` asserts no eval path.* **The manifest declares its scopes, and a scope not declared cannot be granted.** |
| ⭐ **`Embedded Apps`** | **iframe dashboards** *(Looker, Sheets, a project board)* in the client portal — ⛔ **sandboxed iframe, no DOM access, and a tenant's data never crosses into it without an explicit scope** |
| ⭐ **`Private Apps`** | ⭐⭐ **a connector visible ONLY to the tenant that owns it** — *the enterprise case, and it costs nothing because it is a visibility flag on the manifest* |
| ⭐⭐ **`Automated Uninstalls`** | ⛔ **uninstall REVOKES the token, REMOVES the webhook subscriptions, and purges the app's local data** — *asserted by uninstalling and finding no orphaned subscription.* ⭐ **The most common integration leak is a webhook that keeps firing to an app nobody uses.** |
| ⭐ **Update propagation** | ⛔ **per-tenant REVERSIBLE** — *a global propagation that breaks one tenant's config must be undoable for that tenant alone* |
| ⚠️ **Third-party developers** | ⭐⭐ **MY RECOMMENDATION: first-party connectors only at launch.** *The manifest architecture supports third parties completely — **the store simply does not open.*** ⛔ **A third-party developer ecosystem for a one-person company is a support burden, a review queue and a security surface, all before it is a revenue line.** *Build the door; do not unlock it yet.* |

---

**CHECKED:** the event-storm failure derived from **the actual subscription graph** — *`Job` → `job.completed` → `C-Reviews`* — rather than imagined, and asserted with a **500-record test** because a 20-record test import cannot show it · **migration split from the app store** on risk profile, not on tidiness · the notes hazard traced to **§204's own finding** *(a competitor's notes column is a burglary kit arriving in bulk)* · **cards-on-file recognised as `P-197`'s token problem arriving from the other side**, and surfaced in the report BEFORE commit · **the exit written as `P-203`** so the promise matches `P-199` and `R34` rather than contradicting them · third-party developers **deliberately deferred with the architecture left ready.**
**FAILS IF:** ⛔⛔ **the dry run is made optional to "speed up onboarding."** *It will be proposed, because the dry run doubles the time to value and the sales pressure is real.* ⭐ **And a blind commit of five years of a business's history is the one action in this entire platform that a tenant cannot undo by themselves** — *a rollback exists, but by then they have been working in it.* ⛔ **The dry run is not a safety step bolted on. It is the feature: it is what lets a business SEE their old life in the new system before they leave the old one.**
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **the note-scanning for access codes.** *I am confident it must happen — a bulk import of five years of "gate code 1180" into a plain notes column creates the burglary kit on day one at scale.* ⛔ **But a pattern-matcher over free text will have false positives and false negatives, and the false NEGATIVE is the one that matters** *(a code phrased unusually stays in plaintext forever, and nobody ever looks again)*. ⭐⭐ **So the import should also FLAG the notes it scanned but was unsure about, and offer the tenant a one-screen review** — *"we moved 340 access codes to secure storage and there are 12 notes we were not sure about."* **Reviewing twelve is a five-minute job. Discovering one in a breach is not.**

# 220. ⛔⛔ NO PAYROLL, NO HR — THE PLATFORM MEASURES WORK, IT DOES NOT PAY PEOPLE *(T677 · owner ruling)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **This goes further than §219's fence and it removes the single largest liability in the plan. `X-169`'s own header already said *"we export, we do not file — becoming a payroll bureau is a different company with a different licence."* The owner is drawing that line tighter, and the prize is bigger than the rows it costs.**

## ⭐⭐⭐ WHAT THIS ACTUALLY BUYS

⛔ **At §198 I wrote the hardest rail in the plan: *"a payroll figure is a wage claim with a timestamp."*** *That rail existed because the platform was going to compute wages — overtime across a midnight shift, pro-rated final pay for a departing employee, garnishment pass-through.* ⭐⭐ **Every one of those is a number a person is legally owed, in a jurisdiction I cannot see, computed by software written by an AI swarm.**

> ⭐⭐⭐ **THE CLEANEST WAY TO NEVER PRODUCE A WRONG WAGE IS TO NEVER PRODUCE A WAGE.**

⭐ **`X-169` is fenced, the no-model zone shrinks to one module, and a whole class of failure leaves the plan.** *That is not a loss. It is the best trade in this session.*

## 220.1 ⭐⭐ THE LINE — AND IT IS ONE SENTENCE

> ⭐⭐⭐ **THE PLATFORM MEASURES WORK. IT DOES NOT PAY PEOPLE.**

| ✅ **IN — because it is the JOB's data** | ⛔ **OUT — because it is a WAGE or a PERSON** |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **JOB TIME** — *arrival, duration, completion.* **It is dispatch and job-costing data**, and the margin guard needs it | ⛔ **TIMESHEETS · ATTENDANCE · overtime maths · shift rules** |
| ⭐ **JOB EXPENSES** — *a part bought for a job, mileage driven to it.* **A job cost, feeding the pricebook's COST column and `X-210`'s margin guard** | ⛔ **EXPENSE REIMBURSEMENT as an HR process** — *the platform records the cost; it does not pay the person back* |
| ⭐⭐ **COMMISSION EARNED** — **a NUMBER derived from collected revenue and actual cost**, which only this platform can compute | ⛔ **COMMISSION PAID** — *that is a pay run* |
| ⭐ **THE EXPORT** — hours and commission handed to their real payroll provider | ⛔⛔ **PAYROLL ITSELF** — *wages, tax, withholding, filings, W-2, pay runs, garnishments, final pay* |
| ⭐ **The positive scorecard** *(`X-200`)* | ⛔ **ALL OF HR** *(§219's fence, unchanged)* |

## 220.2 ⛔ WHAT IS FENCED

| Module | Verdict |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔⛔ **`X-169` `Payroll`** | ⭐ **FENCED ENTIRELY. Roster drops to 116.** *Its seven capabilities — pro-rated final pay, overtime, garnishment pass-through, W-2 pre-flight, payroll reconciliation, provider sync, history — are all wage computation.* ⭐⭐ **Its one surviving function is an EXPORT, and an export is an adapter, not a module: it moves to `X-173 AccountingSync`.** |
| ⭐ **`X-168`** | ⭐⭐ **SURVIVES, RENAMED AND NARROWED: `JobTime`.** ⛔ *Not timesheets.* **Arrival, duration and completion on a `Job`** — *which the dispatcher already needs, the margin guard already needs, and §197.4's two-truths reconciliation already governs.* ⛔ **`G15-09` overtime maths is fenced with `X-169`.** |
| ⚠️ **`X-170` `Commissions`** | ⭐⭐⭐ **SURVIVES as a CALCULATION and a REPORT. It never pays.** *Commission earned is derived from `Job` + collected revenue + actual cost — **data no other system has**, and a service business's commission structure is a sales-motivation tool rather than an HR function.* ⛔ **The payment is an export.** ⚠️ **FLAGGED: if you read commission as payroll too, one word fences it — but then the platform loses the ability to tell a tech what they earned, which is one of the strongest reasons a tech logs a job properly.** |

## 220.3 ✅ THE SEVEN RESCUED ROWS — RE-CHECKED AGAINST THE NEW LINE

⭐ **§219 rescued seven rows into `X-168`/`X-169`. Three of them need re-homing now, and they survive because they are JOB COSTS rather than HR:**

| Row | ⭐ New home |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Job expenses · Mileage · Receipt OCR** | ⭐⭐ **`X-173 AccountingSync` + the pricebook's COST side.** *A part bought for a job and the miles driven to it are what make the margin guard honest — **they are the cost of the job, not the compensation of a person.*** |
| **Peer Recognition** | ✅ `X-200`'s positive scorecard — **unchanged** |
| **Reorder Point · Safety Stock** | ✅ `X-167` — **unchanged** |
| **Cancellation Funnel** | ✅ `X-210` + `C-Billing` — **unchanged** |

## 220.4 ⭐⭐ WHAT CHANGES IN WHAT IS ALREADY WRITTEN

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **§198's NO-MODEL ZONE SHRINKS** | *It covered `X-168` + `X-169` + `X-170`.* ⛔ **`X-169` is gone and `X-168` no longer computes anything owed.** ⭐ **It now binds ONE module: `X-170`'s commission arithmetic — integer, deterministic, no model call, byte-reproducible.** *The rail is unchanged where it still applies and it applies in one place.* |
| ⭐⭐ **`§198`'s FAILS IF becomes narrower and sharper** | *"an explain-my-commission feature built with a model that also has access to the calculation"* — ⛔ **still exactly right, and now the only version of that risk left.** |
| ⭐ **`X-173 AccountingSync` grows** | **it gains the payroll-provider export and the job-expense feed.** ⚠️ *Still `DONE-UNVERIFIED` until a QuickBooks/Xero account exists (file 13).* |
| ✅ **Commission-on-COLLECTED survives** | ⭐ *The single most common commission dispute in field service, and the platform still owns the answer.* |
| ⭐ **File 13 gains a line** | **a payroll provider** *(Gusto/ADP/QuickBooks Payroll)* **as an EXPORT TARGET, tenant-owned, never a platform account** — *the same shape as the tenant's gateway.* |

**CHECKED:** `X-169`'s own header read before ruling — *it already said "we export, we do not file," so this tightens an existing line rather than reversing one* · the cut made on **whose data it is** *(the JOB's vs the PERSON's)*, which is what let job time, job expenses and commission survive while timesheets, reimbursement and pay runs go · **the three §219 rescues re-checked against the new line** and re-homed to job costing rather than quietly left pointing at a fenced module · **§198's no-model zone re-scoped from three modules to one** and its `FAILS IF` confirmed still correct · ⚠️ **`X-170` flagged rather than assumed** — *last time I over-read a ruling (`R26`) and it cost a section to undo.*

NOTHING ELSE.** *If the provider needs gross pay, the provider computes it — that is what they are for and what they are licensed for.* ⛔ **`doctor` asserts no field named `gross`, `net`, `tax` or `withholding` exists in the export module.**
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **whether "commission earned" stays clear of the line in practice.** *I am confident it is analytics rather than payroll — it is derived from jobs and collected cash, and a tech seeing "you earned $2,400 this month" is the thing that makes them log jobs properly.* ⛔ **But a number a worker believes they are owed, produced by our software, sits closer to a wage claim than I would like** — *and the distance between "the platform says I earned $2,400" and "the platform owes me $2,400" is smaller in a dispute than it is in a spec.* ⭐⭐ **My recommendation: every commission figure the platform shows carries one line — *"calculated from collected revenue; your employer's payroll is the final word."*** *One sentence, on every screen, and the ambiguity never gets started.*

# 221. ⭐⭐⭐ THE RECONCILIATION — THE PACKAGE VERIFIED *(T677 · every law-established check, run)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **Eleven checks, run against the final state rather than claimed. Ten passed. One failed and was my own regex for the fourth consecutive time — which is now itself the finding worth keeping.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**A verification pass that reports a pass.** ⛔⛔ *Every check in this session that came back clean on its first run was WRONG — the section index, the header scan, the anchor scorer, and now the heading check.* ⭐ **Four times a first-pass check over-matched on MARKUP and produced failures that were not real.** ⛔ **And the danger is symmetrical: a check that cries wolf four times trains you to dismiss the fifth, and the fifth is the one that found three staff-surveillance rows live in the tracker.**
⭐⭐⭐ **THE RULE, now stated as law: A VERIFICATION CHECK REPORTS NOTHING UNTIL IT HAS BEEN RE-RUN AGAINST MEANING.** *Anchor on content, never on `#` or `|`.*

# 224. TURN 52 — ⛔⛔ MODULE ARBITRATION · THE INTENT LADDER *(turn 52 of 109 · T677)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **The turn that answers the one question no agent can answer from inside its own brief. Written first, before the rollups, because everything downstream inherits it — and because after turn 86 it exists in 116 briefs, in 116 shapes, and no two agree.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**A priority number per module.** *It is the obvious design: give `X-211` priority 9, `C-Reviews` priority 4, sort, done.* ⛔⛔ **And it is wrong, because priority is CONTEXTUAL. A payment reminder outranks a review request — until the customer has just complained about the job, at which point BOTH are wrong and a human should call.**
⭐⭐ **A number attached to a module cannot see the situation. And the moment one exists, every module's spec argues for a higher one — because from inside a brief, your module IS the important one.** ⛔ **Sixteen modules will each be written by an agent that believes it is the priority.**
⭐⭐⭐ **THE FIX: ARBITRATE ON WHAT THE ACTION IS TRYING TO DO, NOT ON WHICH MODULE WANTS IT.** *A module cannot lobby for its intent class, because the intent is a property of the action, not of the module.*

## 224.1 ⭐⭐⭐ THE INTENT LADDER — FOUR CLASSES, ONE ORDER

> **Every autopilot action declares exactly one `intent`. Four values. The order is fixed and it is DATA — four rows in a table, not a branch in code.**

| | Class | It means | Examples |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **1** | **`SERVE`** | ⭐ **someone is waiting RIGHT NOW** | answering the call · the missed-call text-back · booking · the arrival text · quoting from the pricebook |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **2** | **`RECOVER`** | ⭐ **something went wrong and we are fixing it** | a complaint · a failed payment · a no-show · a review below threshold · a domino collision · an escalation |
| ⭐ **3** | **`INFORM`** | **they need to know something factual** | the appointment reminder · the invoice · a status change · the renewal notice · the ROI push |
| ⛔ **4** | **`GROW`** | ⭐⭐ **WE want something** | the review ask · the referral · an offer · a nurture step · the alliance intro · a campaign |

⭐⭐ **`SERVE` > `RECOVER` > `INFORM` > `GROW`. Always. No module may override it and there is no per-module priority field to populate** — ⛔ **`doctor` asserts no table in the roster has a `priority` column on a module.**

## 224.2 ⛔⛔ THE RULE THAT UNIFIES FIVE EXISTING ONES

> ⭐⭐⭐ **AN OPEN `RECOVER` ON A `Person` SUPPRESSES EVERY `GROW` TOWARD THAT PERSON. Entirely. Until it closes.**

⭐⭐ **This is already written five times in five places and nobody noticed it was one rule:**
| Already written | Section |
| :--- | :--- |
| *an overdue invoice with an open complaint can never enter dunning* | §216 |
| *a survey is suppressed on a conversation with an open escalation* | §199 |
| *a no-show reactivation is MARKETING and defers* | §192 |
| *ghost risk feeds the cadence ceiling, it never raises frequency* | §190 |
| *the takeover latch — a human takes over and the AI produces nothing* | `R21` |

⛔ **Five modules each solved it locally. Turn 52 makes it ONE assertion at the arbiter**, ⭐ *and every one of those five specs becomes a consequence rather than a separate rule an agent might forget.*

## 224.3 ⭐⭐ WITHIN A CLASS — AND IT IS NOT PRIORITY EITHER

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **Oldest waiting wins** | **queue age, not module importance.** ⭐ *It is fair, it is data, and **it cannot be gamed by a module claiming to be important** — which is the exact failure a priority number invites.* |
| ⭐⭐ **The loser is DEFERRED, never dropped** | ⛔ **with a reason, and the deferral is VISIBLE.** ⭐ *If `X-210`'s offer keeps losing to `X-07`'s nurture, **that is a signal the tenant should see** — not a silence.* |
| ⭐⭐ **The cadence ceiling is the CAP, the ladder is the CHOICE** | *(§187)* — ⛔ **they are different mechanisms and both apply.** *The ceiling says "no more than N to this person this week." The ladder says "and this is which N."* |
| ⭐ **A deferred `GROW` expires** | ⛔ **it is not a queue that grows forever.** *An offer deferred past its own window dies with it, and that is correct — a stale offer is worse than none.* |

## 224.4 ⭐⭐⭐ THE SECOND KIND OF COLLISION — TWO MODULES MUTATING THE SAME THING

⛔ *`X-162` re-routes the day. `X-209` reschedules from a technician's text. `X-108` moves the same job for a customer. All three are correct and they arrive within a minute of each other.*

| Rule | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **① A HUMAN ACTION BEATS ANY AUTOPILOT, AND FOR A WINDOW AFTERWARDS** | ⛔ **an autopilot may not undo a human's change for N minutes** *(a setting)*. ⭐ **This is `R21`'s takeover latch generalised from conversations to every mutation** — *and it is the rule that stops a dispatcher's manual fix being silently reverted by an optimiser thirty seconds later.* |
| ⭐⭐ **② NARROWER SCOPE BEATS BROADER** | *a change to ONE job beats a bulk re-route of the day.* ⛔ **The specific was decided with more information.** |
| ⭐ **③ OBSERVED BEATS ASSIGNED** | *(§197.4, generalised)* — **the field wins on what it saw; the office wins on what it committed.** |
| ⛔ **④ Irreconcilable → the blocked-work queue** | **as a recommendation payload, never as an error** *(§196)* |

## 224.5 ⛔ THE THIRD KIND — TWO MODULES SPENDING ON ONE THING

⭐ *`X-210`'s promotion and `X-205`'s affiliate reward both land on one job.*
| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔⛔ **They do not arbitrate — they STACK against a ceiling** | ⭐ **because both are legitimate and both were promised.** *The promotion was promised to the customer; the affiliate reward was promised to the referrer.* |
| ⭐⭐ **The rule** | **a per-job MAXIMUM GIVE, expressed as a percentage of margin, and the second commitment that would breach it RAISES rather than silently reduces either.** ⛔ *Silently trimming a promised reward is how you lose an affiliate; silently trimming a promised discount is how you lose a customer.* |
| ⭐ **And the margin guard sees it** | *(§214)* — **the give is computed against the pricebook's COST column, so "we gave away the job" is visible before it happens** |

---

## 224.6 ⭐⭐ WHAT THIS ADDS TO EVERY BRIEF

> ⭐ **One line per autopilot action, and it is the smallest possible change to 116 briefs:**
> **`@intent SERVE|RECOVER|INFORM|GROW`**

⛔ **`doctor` asserts every autopilot action declares one, and that no module contains its own arbitration logic** — *the arbiter is a spine service, and a module that resolves a collision locally has re-created the problem this turn exists to remove.*

**CHECKED:** the failure located precisely — *a per-module priority number cannot see context, and every agent will argue for a higher one from inside its own brief* · the arbitration key moved from **WHO WANTS IT to WHAT IT IS FOR**, which is the property a module cannot lobby about · ⭐⭐ **the `RECOVER`-suppresses-`GROW` rule found to be ALREADY WRITTEN FIVE TIMES in five sections** *(§216, §199, §192, §190, R21)* — **five local solutions to one problem, now one assertion** · the within-class tie-break set at **queue age** because it is the only ordering that cannot be gamed · the mutation rules built on **`R21` and §197.4 generalised**, not invented · the spend case resolved as **stacking against a margin ceiling** rather than arbitration, because both commitments were genuinely promised.
**FAILS IF:** ⛔⛔ **a module implements its own arbitration "just for this case."** *It will happen in the module that feels most important — probably `X-204` or `X-01`, because they touch everything — and it will look like defensive programming.* ⭐ **The arbiter is one service, and a module that resolves a collision locally has re-created the exact problem: a decision made in one brief that the other 115 cannot see.** ⛔ **`doctor` asserts no arbitration outside the spine.**
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **whether `INFORM` really outranks `GROW` in every case.** *The ROI push is `INFORM` and a win-back offer is `GROW`, so the push wins — **and I think that is right, because the push is the thing that proves the platform's value and the offer is the thing that costs the tenant money.*** ⛔ **But a tenant with a quiet week might reasonably prefer the offer went out.** ⭐⭐ **The mechanism handles it: the ladder is DATA — four rows — so a tenant could in principle re-order two of them.** ⛔⛔ **I would NOT expose that at launch.** *A re-orderable ladder is a setting, a setting gets set once and wrongly, and the first tenant who puts `GROW` above `INFORM` will wonder why their customers stopped hearing about their appointments.*

# 225. ⭐⭐⭐ THE TWO CHECKS — AND THE REGISTER IS ABOUT A DIFFERENT BUSINESS *(T677)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **The wave check passes with one real violation and a better finding underneath it. The title-lie check found 34 candidates — and they are the OPPOSITE of §216's problem: the specs are right and the REGISTER TEXT beneath them describes a different company. That matters enormously for turn 86.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Turn 86 pulling the REGISTER DESCRIPTION into a brief.** *The Blueprint generator assembles a 20k brief from the module header, the specced rows, and the laws.* ⛔⛔ **If it also carries the register's original one-line description, an agent building `X-167` will read: *"a warehouse worker scans a SKU"* and *"if a customer buys the last pair of shoes in the Miami retail store, update global stock"* — and build ecommerce inventory for a plumber.**
⭐⭐⭐ **THE RULE: THE BRIEF CARRIES THE SPEC. NEVER THE REGISTER DESCRIPTION.** *The register was the MINE. The seven-field spec is the TRUTH, and it already corrected these — the correction just lives one layer above the text an automated generator would most easily reach.*

They live in the §-sections, in prose, which is harder to parse and is therefore exactly what a generator would skip.** ⛔ **`doctor` asserts the Blueprint generator never opens that file.**

**FAILS IF:** ⛔⛔ **the offline-payment reference requirement is softened to "optional" during a field trial.** *A technician standing in a driveway with a cheque and no signal will not photograph it, and the first support ticket will ask for the requirement to be relaxed.* ⭐ **And it is the single control on the oldest loss in field service** — *a "paid cash" entry with no reference and no reconciliation is an unauditable claim that money changed hands.* ⛔ **Make it queue offline and sync later; never make it optional.**
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **the ACH-forcing threshold.** *Disabling cards above a value saves the card fee on exactly the invoices where it costs most — on a $12,000 install that is roughly $350.* ⛔ **But a customer who wanted to put a large job on a card for the points, or for the float, is being told no by their plumber's software** — *and some of them will simply go elsewhere.* ⭐⭐ **My recommendation: the threshold defaults OFF, and the tenant turns it on knowing the trade** — *because the fee saving is the platform's idea and the lost job is the tenant's problem.*

# 227. TURNS 50 · 51 · 53 — ⭐⭐⭐ THE THREE ROLLUPS ARE ONE IDEA *(turns 50, 51 and 53 of 109 · T677)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **Written together because they collapse into one thing: `P-205`'s intent ladder already IS the wizard policy, the autopilot default AND the trust floor. Three turns, one table, and the arithmetic that makes "nothing to configure" survivable across 116 modules.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Ninety "confirmed once" fields.** *`X-118`'s TEST ANCHOR is absolute: **`doctor` reports the wizard's asked-field count = 2 and FAILS THE BUILD IF IT RISES.** Two fields — a business name and a phone number — and the AI is live.* ⛔⛔ **And the plan contains ninety `confirmed once` declarations across the module headers.**
⭐⭐ **If even thirty of them land in the signup flow, the count is thirty and the build fails — correctly.** ⛔ **And the tempting fix is to raise the number, which quietly kills the entire product promise.**
⭐⭐⭐ **THE REAL FIX: THE COUNT IS 2 AT SIGNUP. EVERY OTHER "CONFIRMED ONCE" IS ASKED JUST-IN-TIME — at the first moment its capability is actually used, once, and never again.** *A calendar connection is not a signup question. It is the question asked the first time someone tries to book.*

## 227.1 ⭐⭐ TURN 50 — THE MASTER WIZARD IS TWO TIERS AND A FACT REGISTRY

| Tier | | |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **① SIGNUP** | **exactly TWO fields: the business name, a phone number.** | ⛔ **`doctor` fails the build on a third.** *The AI answers the phone from there.* |
| ⭐⭐ **② JUST-IN-TIME** | **every other `confirmed once`, asked at the moment of first use** | ⛔ **and it must DECLARE ITS TRIGGER.** *A `confirmed once` field with no trigger is a signup question in disguise — `doctor` asserts every one names the event that summons it.* |

### ⭐⭐⭐ AND THE "ASKED TWICE" DEFECT — THE FACT REGISTRY

⛔ *Two modules want the business hours. `X-108` needs them to offer a slot; `C-Agent` needs them to answer "are you open?".* ⛔⛔ **If both ask, the tenant is asked twice and the product has already broken its promise.**
> ⭐⭐⭐ **EVERY QUESTION MAPS TO A `Fact`. EVERY `Fact` HAS EXACTLY ONE OWNING MODULE. A SECOND MODULE ASKING FOR AN OWNED `Fact` FAILS THE BUILD.**
⭐ **`doctor` walks all 116 wizard declarations, resolves each to a `Fact` key, and asserts the key set has no duplicate owner.** ⛔ *This is the only check that can see the defect — no agent can, from inside one brief.*
⭐⭐ **And the yield: the ninety declarations collapse to a much smaller set of distinct facts, because most of them are the same handful asked by different modules.**

## 227.2 ⭐⭐⭐ TURN 51 — THE MASTER AUTOPILOT · DAY ONE IS NARROW

⛔⛔ **116 modules each shipping their autopilot ON means a brand-new tenant has 116 autonomous systems acting on day one.** *It is overwhelming, it is unaccountable, and it destroys trust before any is earned.*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **`P-205`'S INTENT LADDER IS ALSO THE DEFAULT POLICY. One table does arbitration AND defaults.**

| Intent | Ships at | Meaning on day one |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **`SERVE`** | **`L2` — ON, acting, reporting** | **answer the phone · the missed-call text-back · book · quote from the pricebook · the arrival text.** ⭐ *This is the product. It works in the first hour.* |
| ⭐ **`RECOVER`** | **`L1`/`L2`** | *it escalates and proposes; it does not act alone on a bad situation* |
| **`INFORM`** | **`L2`** | reminders, invoices, status — *factual, expected, safe* |
| ⭐⭐ **`GROW`** | ⛔ ~~**`L1` — PROPOSES ONLY, ALWAYS, ON DAY ONE**~~ **STRUCK by `R235`** — ⭐⭐⭐ **`GROW` ships at its CEILING and markets from minute one.** *What stops it reaching the wrong person is `X-126`'s gate, consent and the cadence ceiling — **never a tenant clicking approve.*** | *review asks · referrals · offers · nurture · the alliance intro.* ⛔ ~~Every one of them is earned up the ladder, per tenant, per capability.~~ **STRUCK by `R235`** — ⭐⭐ **every one of them is ON from minute one, per tenant, per capability.** *`X-126`'s gate supervises; the client turns off what they don't want.* |

⭐⭐ **So a new tenant's day one is: the phone is answered, jobs are booked, and the AI asks before it does anything that reaches a stranger.** ⛔ **Nothing markets to anyone until the tenant has approved it enough times to mean it.**

### ⛔ THE "REVIEW FIRST" TOGGLE — AND THE TENSION IT CREATES

⚠️ *`P-195` says autonomy is **EARNED, never set**. A per-lane "review first" toggle is a setting. Both cannot be true.*
> ⭐⭐⭐ **THE RESOLUTION: YOU MAY ALWAYS GO BACKWARD. YOU MAY NEVER GO FORWARD.**
| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **DEMOTION is a right** | **a tenant may put any lane, or any single capability, back to "review first" at any time.** *It is a `P-192` courtesy switch: logged, disclosed, and it has an off button.* |
| ⛔⛔ **PROMOTION is earned** | **there is no control anywhere that raises an autonomy level.** *`doctor` asserts no settings row can increase a ladder position — only `X-149`'s measurement does.* |
⭐⭐ **That preserves both laws exactly, and it is the right asymmetry: a nervous tenant can always slow the system down, and an impatient one cannot skip the trust it has not built.**

## 227.3 ⭐⭐ TURN 53 — THE LADDER FLOOR PER MODULE · ASSERT ONCE, DEVIATE RARELY

⛔ **Not 116 paragraphs. Three defaults, a short exception list, and one column on the law sweep** — *the same method that put seven Master Laws across the roster without a turn.*

| Default | Applies to |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **`L2`** | anything a customer is already waiting on |
| ⭐ **`L1`** | anything that reaches a stranger, publishes, or spends |
| ⭐ **`L0`** | anything that only observes |

⛔⛔ **THE NEVER-PROMOTE SET, now complete and closed:** **the CONSENT decision · a PRICE · a CLAIM · a REFUND · a CANCEL · a SIGNATURE · PAYROLL/commission arithmetic · a first-party countersign on a non-template · a collections handoff · a price-match.**
⭐ **Ten items. `doctor` asserts each carries `ladder: fixed` and that no promotion path exists for them.**

⚠️ **And the deviations worth naming, because each has a reason:**
| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **`X-08 ChurnPredictor`** | ⛔ **`L0` and never higher — it observes and has no send path at all** |
| **`X-209 StaffDesk`** | ⭐ **per EMPLOYEE, not per tenant** — *a new hire starts at `L1` on everything* |
| **`X-202 ApprovalDesk`** | ⛔⛔ **the ROUTING is `L3`; the DECISION is always the item's own floor.** *The desk never decides.* |
| **`X-212 MigrationIn`** | ⛔ **the DRY RUN is autonomous; the COMMIT is `L1` forever** |

## 227.4 ⭐ WHAT THE THREE TURNS ACTUALLY PRODUCED

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **One table, three jobs** | **`P-205`'s four intents give the arbitration order, the day-one default AND the ladder floor.** ⛔ *Three turns were scoped as three artefacts; they are one.* |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **Two new build-failing checks** | **① the FACT REGISTRY — no `Fact` has two owning modules** · **② no settings row may raise a ladder position** |
| ⭐ **One promise made survivable** | **"nothing to configure" survives 116 modules only because the count is 2 AT SIGNUP and everything else is just-in-time** |

**CHECKED:** the conflict found by **counting the plan's own declarations** — *ninety `confirmed once` fields against `X-118`'s build-failing limit of two* — which is what forced the two-tier answer rather than a negotiated number · **the "asked twice" defect resolved as a `Fact` OWNERSHIP problem**, which makes it mechanically checkable instead of a review item · **the `P-195` / "review first" tension surfaced rather than smoothed**, and resolved by asymmetry *(backward always, forward never)* · the never-promote set **closed at ten and each traced to the section that put it there** · the ladder floors written **assert-once-deviate-rarely**, matching the method the Master Laws already use.
**FAILS IF:** ⛔⛔ **the signup asked-field count is raised from two.** *It will be proposed with a good reason — the calendar, the gateway, the logo, "just three more and onboarding is complete."* ⭐⭐ **And each one is individually reasonable, which is exactly why the limit is a BUILD FAILURE rather than a guideline.** ⛔ **Two fields is not a target; it is the product.** *A tenant who answers two questions and hears their phone answered has experienced the thing being sold. A tenant who answers eleven has experienced software setup, and every competitor already offers that.*
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **whether `INFORM` should really ship at `L2` on day one.** *An appointment reminder is factual, expected and safe — and it goes to a customer of a tenant who signed up ninety minutes ago, from a system that customer has never heard of.* ⛔ **The first message a tenant's customer ever receives from this platform will be sent autonomously, before the tenant has seen what it looks like.** ⭐⭐ **My recommendation: `INFORM` ships at `L1` for the FIRST FIVE SENDS ONLY, then promotes automatically** — *the tenant sees the first five, approves them in seconds, and never thinks about it again.* **Five taps buys the thing no policy can: the tenant knows what their customers are receiving.**

# 228. TURNS 56 & 64 — ⛔⛔ THE EVENT GRAPH IS BROKEN IN 51 PLACES *(turns 56 and 64 of 109 · T677)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **The emit matrix and the orphan hunt, run against all 103 declaration blocks. 330 events emitted, 142 consumed — and FIFTY-ONE events that a module waits for and NOTHING EMITS. Five modules are subscribed to `subscription.renewed`. Nothing sends it.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Five agents building five subscribers to an event that never fires.**
> ⛔⛔ **`subscription.renewed` is consumed by `C-Billing` · `X-120` · `X-198` · `X-199` · `X-82`. It is emitted by NOTHING.**
⭐⭐⭐ **That is the renewal machinery — the event `P-197`'s notice-before-charge hangs off, the event that tells the card vault to check an expiry, the event the rate table needs to roll a period.** ⛔ **Five modules would be built correctly, each waiting, and the renewal path would simply never run.**
⭐⭐ **And it would pass every test that does not involve waiting a month.** *Each module's own tests pass — a subscriber that is never called is not a failing subscriber.* ⛔⛔ **Nothing inside a single brief can see it. This is exactly the class of defect turns 56 and 64 exist for, and it took a matrix across 103 blocks to find.**

## 228.1 ⭐⭐ THE MATRIX

| | |
| :--- | ---: |
| Modules with a `DECLARATIONS` block | **103** |
| Distinct events **emitted** | **330** |
| Distinct events **consumed** | **142** |
| ⚠️ **Emitted, no declared consumer** | **239** |
| ⛔⛔ **Consumed, NOTHING EMITS** | ⛔ **51** |

⭐⭐⭐ **The two numbers mean different things and only one of them is unambiguously a defect.**
| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⚠️ **239 orphan EMITS — mostly not a defect** | *many are legitimately fire-and-forget: `ai.called` is telemetry, `action.refused` is audit, `agent.live` is a milestone.* ⭐ **They are consumed by generic sinks — the log, the ledger, analytics — that nobody declares.** ⛔ **The fix is a declaration, not a subscriber: `@emits … @sink telemetry` so the matrix stops flagging them and a REAL orphan becomes visible.** |
| ⛔⛔ **51 ghost CONSUMES — every one is a defect** | ⭐ **A module cannot consume what nothing emits.** *Either the emitter is missing, or the two modules named the same event differently — and both break the same way.* |

## 228.2 ⛔⛔ THE NINE WITH NO PLAUSIBLE EMITTER AT ALL

| Event | Waited for by | ⭐ What it means |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⛔⛔⛔ **`subscription.renewed`** | **`C-Billing` · `X-120` · `X-198` · `X-199` · `X-82`** | ⭐⭐⭐ **the renewal path. FIVE consumers, zero emitters. The single clearest buildable defect in the plan** |
| ⛔ **`signup.completed`** | `X-118` | *onboarding waits for its own completion signal and nobody raises it* |
| ⛔ **`help.human_requested`** | `X-111` | **the escalation to a human — the operator console waits for a call for help that is never sent** |
| ⛔ **`refresh.due`** | `X-134` · `X-151` · `X-16` | *three enrichment/scrape modules wait for a refresh tick nothing schedules* |
| **`operator.action`** | `X-196` | · **`rule.fired`** → `X-195` · **`note.voice`** → `X-175` · **`service.out_of_scope`** → `X-190` · **`zernio.webhook`** → `X-177` |

## 228.3 ⭐⭐ AND AT LEAST ONE IS A ONE-LETTER TYPO

> ⛔⛔ **`X-142` and `X-143` consume `action.invoke`. `X-122` emits `action.invoked`.**
⭐⭐⭐ **One letter. Two modules permanently deaf to the action registry's own event — and the action registry is the spine.** ⛔ *Neither module can see the other's spelling from inside its own brief, and a swarm agent will implement exactly what its brief says.*

⚠️ **My fuzzy matcher paired 42 of the 51 with a "near" event, and I checked them: some are real drift** *(`demo.built` vs `demo.provisioned`)*, **and some are my matcher being generous** *(`agent.teach` vs `agent.turn` are different things; `country.detected` vs `interest.detected` are not related)*. ⭐ **Reported as: at least one unambiguous typo, several probable drifts, and nine with nothing nearby — all 51 needing a decision.**

## 228.4 ⭐⭐⭐ THE THREE RULES THIS PRODUCES

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **① THE EVENT GRAPH IS BUILD-FAILING** | ⛔ **`doctor` builds the matrix from every `@emits` and `@consumes` and FAILS THE BUILD on any consumed event with no emitter.** *There is no acceptable count of these above zero — a subscriber to nothing is dead code that looks alive.* |
| ⭐⭐ **② EVENTS ARE A REGISTRY, NOT A CONVENTION** | ⛔ **an event name is a ROW** *(`P-194`'s shape)*. **A module may emit or consume only a registered name; a new name is an INSERT and a typo is a build failure at the point of use, not a silent disconnection at runtime.** ⭐ *That is what makes `action.invoke`/`action.invoked` impossible rather than unlucky.* |
| ⭐ **③ A FIRE-AND-FORGET EMIT DECLARES ITS SINK** | **`@sink telemetry` · `@sink audit` · `@sink ledger`.** ⛔ **An emit with neither a consumer nor a sink is a genuine orphan and fails.** ⭐ *This is what turns 239 noisy flags into a small list that means something.* |

## 228.5 ⭐ WHAT TURNS 56 AND 64 ACTUALLY DELIVERED

⭐⭐ **Turn 64's orphan hunt found the orphans it was scoped for — and turn 56's matrix found something worse: not events with no listener, but LISTENERS WITH NO EVENT.**
⛔ **The plan's own turn description says *"every emit has a subscriber."*** ⭐⭐⭐ **The dangerous direction is the reverse, and nobody had written it down: every CONSUME needs an EMITTER, and a missing emitter is invisible, silent, and passes every module-level test.**

**CHECKED:** the matrix built from **103 own-block `DECLARATIONS` sections**, parsed with bounded `@`-markers after the first attempt over-matched *(seventh over-match this session, caught before reporting)* · **`@consumes` confirmed present in the §157 contract** *(121 occurrences)* before concluding anything about missing declarations · the 17 "duplicate table owners" **checked and found to be the plan being CAREFUL** — *`X-01` writes "(people/conversations/messages are X-121's)", `C-Sms` writes "(messages themselves live on X-121's `messages`)"* — ⭐ **my regex grabbed module names out of the disclaimer** · the 51 ghosts **spot-checked individually rather than trusted from the fuzzy match**, which is why the drift count is reported as "several" and not 42.
**FAILS IF:** ⛔⛔ **the 239 orphan emits are "fixed" by adding subscribers.** *It is the obvious response to a big number, and it would add 239 pieces of machinery nobody asked for.* ⭐ **Most of them are correct as they are — telemetry, audit, milestones.** ⛔ **The fix is `@sink`, which costs a word per declaration and makes the FIFTY-ONE visible.** *A verification result you respond to by building things has been misread.*
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **whether the plan being careful in a parenthetical is good enough.** *`X-01` disclaims ownership of `people` in prose, inside brackets, after the declaration.* ⛔⛔ **A `doctor` check parsing `@owns_table` reads `messages` as owned by `C-Sms` — the machine-readable claim and the human-readable correction disagree, which is exactly `P-206`'s register problem in a different file.** ⭐⭐ **My recommendation: split the declaration — `@owns_table` for what a module owns, `@reads_table` for what it touches** — *one new marker, and the parenthetical stops being load-bearing.* **A correction that only a human can read is not a correction in a system built by agents.**

**A contract that exists only as a hundred and six separate sentences.** *`doctor` now has **106 assertions** — 57 written before turn 30, **49 added in this session alone** — and eleven new annotations that appeared across `§200`–`§228` as consequences of individual findings.* ⛔⛔ **Every one is correct. ## 229.3 ⭐⭐⭐ TURN 71 — THE AGENT'S ACTION SURFACE

> **The `ActionRegistry` seen from the AI's side: of ~310 registered actions across 116 modules, WHICH may an agent invoke, and under what gate?**

| Tier | | Examples |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **REACHABLE, ungated** | **reads.** *A read cannot break anything and refusing them makes the agent useless* | `pricebook.lookup` · `schedule.read` · `conversation.read` · `ledger.read` |
| ⭐⭐ **REACHABLE, gated by `@intent` + ladder** | **the working set** | `job.reschedule` · `message.send` · `quote.send` · `content.publish` |

⭐⭐⭐ **THE LAW: the agent's reachable set is a DECLARED ALLOW-LIST, not "everything registered minus a deny-list."** ⛔ **A deny-list fails open — a new action added in six months is reachable by default, and nobody notices until it is used.** ⭐ **`doctor` asserts every agent-reachable action carries `@agent_reachable` explicitly, and that the four `NOT IN` families cannot be resolved from an agent seat at all.**
⭐ **And three properties every reachable action must declare: `gated` *(what stops it)* · `previewable` *(the human sees it before it runs)* · `reversible` *(`compensable`, or explicitly not)*.** ⛔ **An action that is none of the three cannot be agent-reachable.**

Forty-nine were not.** ⭐⭐ **My recommendation: rank them and build the SEVEN BLUEPRINT GATES first** — *those seven are what stand between a correct plan and 116 briefs carrying a defect.* **The other ninety-nine can land across wave 0 and wave 1 without anything being built wrong** — *but if the seven are not in CI before turn 86, everything after it inherits whatever slipped through.*

# 230. TURN 90 — ⭐⭐⭐ THE TEST SYSTEM · AND WHO GRADES THE AGENT *(turn 90 of 109 · T677)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **Eight testing layers have accumulated across 109 turns and nobody has ever reconciled them. But the deeper problem is not overlap — it is that a swarm agent writes both the code and the test, and a test derived from the same brief as the code proves only that the agent understood its brief.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**A self-graded module.** *An agent receives a 20k brief, builds `X-108`, and writes `X-108`'s tests.* ⛔⛔ **Both artefacts come from the same reading of the same document by the same reader.** ⭐ **If it misread the brief, the code is wrong AND the test agrees with it — and the suite goes green.**
⭐⭐⭐ **Every quality gate in the plan is downstream of this. The DoD checks the tests pass. The evidence dump reports that they passed. The wave gate reviews the evidence.** ⛔ **All three inherit the same blind spot.**

> ⭐⭐⭐ **THE ANSWER, AND IT IS ALREADY WRITTEN: THE AGENT DOES NOT AUTHOR ITS TESTS.**
> *There are **539 `asserted` clauses** and **114 `TEST ANCHOR`s** already in this plan — **written before any agent existed, by a different process, against the failure modes rather than against the implementation.*** ⭐⭐ **The brief carries them as a REQUIREMENT. The agent IMPLEMENTS them. It does not decide what they are.**

## 230.1 ⭐⭐⭐ THE ID RULE — WHAT MAKES IT ENFORCEABLE

⛔ *"The agent must implement the specified tests" is an instruction, and an agent under pressure to make a suite green will quietly drop the one that will not pass.*

> ⭐⭐ **EVERY ⑤ ASSERTION CARRIES THE ID OF ITS CAPABILITY ROW. `doctor` asserts every id in the brief has a matching test in the module.**
⭐⭐⭐ **A module with 13 spec rows must produce 13 tests bearing those 13 ids.** ⛔ **An agent cannot delete an inconvenient test, because the id goes missing and the build fails** — *and it cannot weaken one either, because the assertion text came with the id.*
⭐ **This costs nothing: the ids already exist.** *`G2-06`, `G11-40`, `G20-11` — they have been the spine of the capability tracker since turn 30.*

## 230.2 ⭐⭐ THE EIGHT LAYERS, RECONCILED — WHAT EACH ONE ALONE CAN CATCH

| Layer | Count | ⭐ Catches | ⛔ Blind to |
| :--- | ---: | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **① Capability ⑤** *(assertion + refusal)* | **539** | **a behaviour, and its REFUSAL** | anything spanning two modules |
| ⭐⭐ **② The `TEST ANCHOR`** | **114** | **the one runtime proof — it actually happened** | the other capabilities |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **③ `doctor`** | **105** | ⭐ **STRUCTURE — boundaries, annotations, the event graph, the fact registry.** *The only layer that sees ACROSS modules* | behaviour |
| **④ The six sweeps** | 6 | grep-shaped structural rot | anything needing to run |
| ⭐⭐ **⑤ The twelve E2E journeys** | 12 | ⭐ **the seams — where modules meet** | a single module's edge cases |
| ⭐⭐ **⑥ The ten-condition DoD** | 10 | **mergeability** | *it checks that tests PASS, not that they were the right tests* |
| ⭐ **⑦ Red evals** *(X-149)* | — | **prompt regression** | deterministic code |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **⑧ The seven Blueprint gates** | 7 | **a defect in the PLAN, before any code exists** | *(they run once, at turn 86)* |

⭐⭐ **Reconciled, the picture is clean: ⑤ and ② prove BEHAVIOUR. ③ and ④ prove STRUCTURE. ⑤E2E proves the SEAMS. ⑥ decides mergeability. ⑦ guards the prompts. ⑧ guards the plan itself.** ⛔ **The only layer that can see across module boundaries is `doctor` — which is why 105 assertions is not excessive.**

## 230.3 ⭐⭐⭐ THE TWO-PASS RULE — RUN EVERYTHING TWICE

> ⭐⭐ **EVERY TEST RUNS TWICE IN CI. A SECOND RUN THAT DIFFERS FAILS THE BUILD.**

⭐⭐⭐ **One rule, and it catches four of this plan's most serious failure classes at once:**
| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔ **A model in a deterministic path** | *payroll, commission, reconciliation, a compliance class* — **a model gives a different answer on the second run.** ⭐ **`P-204`, `P-062` and §197.4's no-model rules become MEASURABLE rather than merely asserted** |
| ⛔ **A non-idempotent replay** | **`X-129`'s drain, `X-212`'s import, the payment `refId`** — *run twice, and a double-applied payment appears immediately* |
| ⛔ **Order dependence** | *a suite that passes only in one sequence is a suite hiding shared state* |
| ⛔ **An uninitialised fixture** | *a test that passes because the previous test left data behind* |

⭐ **And it costs one CI flag.** ⛔ *Nothing else in this plan has that ratio of cost to coverage.*

## 230.4 ⭐⭐ THE ORDER — TESTING AFTER CODING, `E0` FIRST

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **`E0` FIRST — before wave 1, not at its gate** | **one real call, end to end, on one number.** *It either validates the voice architecture or it does not, and it is a day's work.* ⛔ **Finding out early costs a day; finding out late costs a wave.** |
| ⭐ **Then: the module's own ⑤ set** | written from the brief, id-matched, **two-pass** |
| ⭐ **Then: the `TEST ANCHOR`** | ⛔ **the runtime proof — with an EXTERNAL ARTIFACT ID for any module whose purpose is a vendor** *(§210)* |
| ⭐⭐ **Then: `doctor`** | ⛔ **and it runs on every commit, not at the gate.** *A structural violation caught at a wave gate is a week of work built on a broken boundary* |
| **Then: the journeys** | at the wave gate, **money journey first** |

⛔⛔ **"Testing after coding" does NOT mean tests are written after code.** ⭐ **The tests are WRITTEN in the brief, before the agent starts. They are RUN after the code exists. Those are different sentences and the difference is the whole of §230.**

---

**CHECKED:** the eight layers **counted from the plan** — *539 `asserted` clauses, 114 `TEST ANCHOR`s, 105 `doctor` assertions* — rather than estimated · the self-grading problem identified by asking **who authors the test**, which is the question none of the eight layers asks · the answer found to be **already present** *(the ⑤ fields predate every agent)* — ⭐ **so the fix is an ID-MATCH RULE, not new tests** · the two-pass rule tested against **four named failure classes already in the plan**, all of which it catches · **`doctor` identified as the only cross-module layer**, which is what justifies 105 assertions rather than trimming them.
**FAILS IF:** ⛔⛔ **an agent is allowed to add tests but not required to keep the specified ones.** *It will add many — agents write tests enthusiastically — and the suite will look thorough.* ⭐⭐ **A hundred agent-authored tests that all confirm the agent's own reading are worth less than the thirteen that came from the brief**, *because the thirteen were written against the FAILURE MODE by someone who was not building it.* ⛔ **`doctor` matches ids: the thirteen must be present. Anything beyond them is welcome and proves nothing.**
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **whether two-pass is affordable on the full suite.** *Doubling CI time on 116 modules with 539 assertions is real money and real minutes, and the first slow build will produce a proposal to run it nightly instead.* ⭐⭐ **My recommendation: two-pass on every commit for the modules that carry a NO-MODEL or IDEMPOTENCY rule** — *payroll, commissions, reconciliation, the migration, the payment path, the drain* — **and nightly for everything else.** ⛔ **Those six are where a second-run difference means something is structurally wrong rather than merely flaky, and they are a small fraction of the suite.**


---

# 231. STEP 8 — ⭐⭐⭐ THE PIPELINE, AS A SPECIFICATION *(turns 77–85 · T677 · a DOCUMENT, not code)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **Antigravity implements this. It is written to be built from without judgement — six stages, three failure semantics, the 106 assertions ranked, and the four things a harness must be incapable of doing.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**A pipeline that runs the expensive checks first.** *A boundary violation is a two-second `grep`. A `TEST ANCHOR` needs a carrier, a gateway and a real call.* ⛔⛔ **Run them in the wrong order and an agent waits eleven minutes to be told it imported another module's class.**
⭐⭐ **And the second-order effect is worse: a slow pipeline gets bypassed.** *Someone adds `--skip-checks` for a hotfix, it becomes the habit, and six months later the boundary law is a comment.* ⭐⭐⭐ **THE ORDERING IS THE ENFORCEMENT: cheapest and most structural first, so the check that must never be skipped is the one that costs nothing to run.**

## 231.1 ⭐⭐⭐ THE SIX STAGES · AND THREE FAILURE SEMANTICS

| Stage | Runs | Cost | ⛔ Failing it blocks |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **0 · THE BOUNDARY** | **pure `grep`, no build** — *no cross-module import · no gateway SDK outside `X-198` · no model call in the no-model trees · no card field in our markup · no `priority` column · no arbitration outside the spine* | **~2s** | ⛔⛔ **THE COMMIT** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **1 · THE CONTRACT** | **the 16 annotations present on every module · THE EVENT GRAPH balances · THE FACT REGISTRY has no duplicate owner · no settings row raises a ladder · every `confirmed once` names a `@trigger`** | **~5s** | ⛔⛔ **THE COMMIT** |
| ⭐⭐ **2 · THE SCHEMA** | **RLS `FORCE` on every tenant table · no staging table for a canonical noun · money columns are integer · no `gross`/`net`/`tax`/`withholding` in the export module · every `secure` field encrypted** | **~20s** | ⛔⛔ **THE COMMIT** |
| ⭐⭐ **3 · CAPABILITY ⑤** | **id-matched to the brief · TWO-PASS on the six no-model/idempotency modules** | **minutes** | ⛔ **THE MERGE** |
| ⭐⭐ **4 · THE `TEST ANCHOR`** | **the runtime proof — with an EXTERNAL ARTIFACT ID for any module whose purpose is a vendor** | **minutes + services** | ⛔ **THE MERGE** |
| ⭐ **5 · THE TWELVE JOURNEYS** | **money journey first, external ids throughout** | **long** | ⛔ **THE WAVE** |

⭐⭐⭐ **Stages 0–2 fail the COMMIT. 3–4 fail the MERGE. 5 fails the WAVE.** ⛔ **The distinction is not cosmetic: you can merge a module with a failing behaviour test and fix it; you must never be able to COMMIT a broken boundary, because everything built on top of it inherits the break.**

## 231.2 ⭐⭐ THE 106 ASSERTIONS, RANKED FOR BUILD ORDER

| Tier | Count | Build when |
| :--- | ---: | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **A · THE SEVEN BLUEPRINT GATES** | **7** | ⛔⛔ **BEFORE turn 86.** *They stand between a correct plan and 116 briefs carrying a defect* |
| ⭐⭐ **B · Stage 0 + Stage 1** *(boundary + contract)* | **~30** | **wave 0, first** — *they are greps and they are what makes 116 parallel agents survivable* |
| ⭐ **C · Stage 2** *(schema)* | **~20** | **wave 0** — *schema is locked before UI anyway* |
| **D · behavioural** | **~49** | **across waves 0–1, as the modules that need them arrive** |

⛔ **The seven are non-negotiable and everything else can arrive incrementally without anything being built wrong.**

## 231.3 ⭐⭐ SEED MANIFESTS

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **Per module: `seeds.yml`** | **what rows must exist for its ⑤ set to run** — *and it DECLARES A COUNT* |
| ⭐⭐ **The evidence dump reports declared vs actual** | ⛔ *(already a DoD condition — this is where it is enforced)* |
| ⛔⛔ **THE SEED TRAP, and it is not in the plan yet** | ⭐⭐⭐ **A seeded tenant with a real-format phone number, and a test that sends.** *The test passes. Someone's actual phone rings.* ⛔ **`doctor` asserts every seeded sendable identifier is drawn from the RESERVED ranges** *(`555-01xx`, `example.com`, the carrier test numbers)* — **and that no seed row carries a routable address.** |
| ⭐ **Seeds are per-module and composable** | *wave 0's twelve seed together for the journeys; a module's own set runs alone* |

## 231.4 ⭐⭐⭐ THE EVIDENCE HARNESS — FOUR THINGS IT MUST BE INCAPABLE OF

> ⛔⛔ **The dump is what a human reviews at a wave gate. If the harness can be persuaded, the gate is theatre.**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **① It cannot accept a typed artifact id** | **an external id is captured from the VENDOR'S RESPONSE at the moment of the call and hashed with the request.** ⛔ *An agent may not write `msg_12345` into a report* |
| ⭐⭐ **② It cannot report a PASS it did not observe** | **the harness reads the runner's exit codes; it is never handed a summary** |
| ⭐⭐ **③ It cannot omit a FAIL** | ⛔ **the DoD grid is generated from the full result set, and every FAIL is NAMED.** *A dump with fewer rows than the DoD has conditions is itself a failure* |
| ⭐ **④ It records the BRIEF HASH per module** | ⛔ **proof the module was built from the CURRENT plan and not a stale copy** |

⭐⭐ **And the blind spot-check stands: the auditor names three files AFTER reading the dump.** *A dump written to look good does not survive three files chosen adversarially.*

## 231.5 ⭐ THE REPO SKELETON · AND THE SANDBOX

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Layout** | **`app/Modules/<Domain>/<Module>/**` — one folder, one owner.** ⭐ *The boundary law is a static import check over this tree, which is why the layout is a spec and not a preference* |
| ⭐ **The voice edge** | ⛔ **a SEPARATE service, separate repo or a top-level `edge/`** — *`doctor` asserts no business logic in it* |
| ⭐⭐ **`make:module`** | **scaffolds the folder, the 16 annotations, an empty `seeds.yml` and the ⑤ stubs from the brief's ids** — ⛔ *so a module cannot be created without its contract* |
| ⭐ **The sandbox** *(§217's reclaimed rows)* | ⭐⭐ **TIME TRAVEL — a per-sandbox clock offset, so recurring billing and renewals are testable in an afternoon rather than a month.** *This is what makes `subscription.renewed` provable* · **AUTO-DESTRUCTION — a sandbox untouched for 14 days is deleted** |

---

**CHECKED:** the stage order derived from **cost against enforcement** — *the check that must never be skipped is placed where it costs nothing, because a slow pipeline gets bypassed and a bypassed check is a comment* · **three failure semantics separated** *(commit / merge / wave)*, because a broken boundary and a failing behaviour test are not the same risk · the 106 assertions **ranked rather than listed**, with the seven gates isolated as the only non-negotiable set · ⭐⭐ **the SEED TRAP identified and it was not previously in the plan** — *a seeded tenant with a routable number and a test that sends is a passing test and a stranger's phone ringing* · the harness written as **four incapabilities rather than four requirements**, because a requirement can be met badly and an incapability cannot · **Time Travel connected to `subscription.renewed`** — §228's five-consumer orphan is only provable with a clock offset.
**FAILS IF:** ⛔⛔ **stages 0–2 are made to fail the MERGE instead of the COMMIT.** *It is the natural instinct — let people commit freely and gate at the merge — and it is wrong here.* ⭐⭐⭐ **With 116 agents committing in parallel, a boundary violation that survives to merge has already been built ON by whatever landed after it.** ⛔ **A cross-module import committed on Tuesday and caught on Friday is not one fix; it is however many modules imported the thing that should not have existed.** *Commit-time is the only time these are cheap.*
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **whether stage 4's external artifact ids can run on every merge.** *A real carrier send and a real gateway authorisation cost money and rate limits, and 116 modules merging repeatedly would make that a bill and a throttle.* ⭐⭐ **My recommendation: stage 4 runs the external path ONCE PER MODULE PER DAY and on every wave gate, with the vendor sandbox in between** — *and the evidence dump records WHICH ids came from a live call and which from a sandbox.* ⛔ **What must never happen is the distinction going unrecorded** — *because "we have artifact ids" and "we have artifact ids from a real vendor" are the same sentence in a report and different facts at a gate.*
