# 232. TURN 86 — ⭐⭐⭐ THE BLUEPRINT GENERATOR, BUILT AND RUN · IT REFUSED *(turn 86 of 109 · T677)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **I built the generator and ran it rather than specifying it. It refused to emit briefs — three gates red — and one of the three was a defect no check in this session had found, including `§221`'s own header audit. A Blueprint that has never run is a document about a Blueprint.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Five modules that share a header with another module.**
> ⛔⛔ **`X-07 + X-08` · `C-Reviews + X-181` · `X-182 + X-189` · `X-186 + X-180` · `X-112 + X-113` — five `###` blocks, ten modules, one header each.**
⭐⭐ **Perfectly sensible for a human: the two are related, the header explains both, and reading it once is better than twice.** ⛔⛔ **And catastrophic for a generator producing ONE BRIEF PER MODULE: either one of the pair gets a brief and the other gets nothing, or both get an identical brief describing two different modules.**
⭐⭐⭐ **Every check in this session passed these** — *`§209`'s header scan, `§221`'s 116-of-116, `§229`'s annotation count.* **They only became visible when something tried to USE the headers one at a time.** ⛔ **That is the difference between auditing a document and running against it.**

## 232.1 ⭐⭐ THE RUN — WHAT THE GATES SAID

| Gate | Result |
| :--- | :--- |
| ✅ **1 · kill reconciliation** | **PASS** — *no killed row is live in the tracker* |
| ✅ **2 · register/tracker balance** | **PASS** — *898 accounted at §219* |
| ⛔ **3 · module headers** | **FAIL — 13 of 116 unfindable.** *Fixed to 7, then to 5* — **see §232.2** |
| ✅ **4 · vendor artifact** | **PASS** |
| ✅ **5 · no `gross`/`net`/`tax`** | **PASS** |
| ⛔⛔ **6 · THE EVENT GRAPH** | **FAIL — 51 consumed with no emitter** *(§228, unfixed: it needs 51 decisions)* |
| ✅ **7 · fact registry** | **PASS** |
| ⛔⛔ **THE BACKFILL GATE** | **FAIL — 100 of 116 modules lack `@intent`** *(exactly as §229 predicted)* |
| ⭐ **P-206 compliance** | ✅ **the generator never opens the register** |

⭐⭐⭐ **`⛔ BLUEPRINT REFUSED — no briefs emitted.` That is the generator working correctly, and it is the most valuable output this turn could have produced.**

## 232.2 ⭐⭐⭐ THE HEADER FIX — ANCHOR ON CONTENT, NOT MARKUP

⛔ **Why 13 were unfindable: their headers live under `## 209.1 X-202 ApprovalDesk` — a numbered SECTION heading — not `### X-202`.** *Written by me, in a section format, at `§209`.* ⭐ **The header fields were all present. The generator simply could not locate them.**

> ⭐⭐⭐ **THE FIX IS THE SESSION'S OWN LESSON APPLIED TO ITSELF: every module header now carries `` `@module X-nnn` `` as an anchor, and the generator finds headers BY ANNOTATION, NEVER BY MARKUP.**

| | |
| :--- | ---: |
| `@module` anchors before | **4** |
| ⭐ **Added** | **114** |
| **Headers found: before → after** | **103 → 111** |
| ⭐⭐ **Modules with fewer than 8 fields in the anchored block** | ⭐ **ZERO** |
| ⛔ **Still unresolved** | **5 — and all five are the SHARED HEADERS** |

⭐ *Two of the thirteen were my own misplaced anchors — landed on a code block that mentioned the module — found and re-placed. **Eighth over-match of the session, caught by running rather than by reading.***

## 232.3 ⛔ WHAT REMAINS BEFORE BRIEFS CAN EXIST

**Three pieces of work, all mechanical, none requiring new thinking:**

| # | | Size |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **①** | **SPLIT THE FIVE SHARED HEADERS.** *Each pair needs its own `WHAT`, `DECLARATIONS` and `TEST ANCHOR` — and deciding which capability belongs to which of the pair is real judgement, not a find-and-replace* | **1 pass** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **②** | **BACKFILL `@intent` ONTO 100 MODULES.** *`§227`'s rule derives it — `SERVE` where a customer waits, `GROW` where it reaches a stranger, `L0` where it observes — but 100 assignments is 100 small judgements, and getting one wrong puts a marketing action in the `SERVE` lane* | **1–2 passes** |
| ⛔⛔ **③** | **RESOLVE THE 51 GHOST EVENTS.** *Each needs a decision: add the emitter, rename the consumer, or delete the subscription.* ⭐ **`subscription.renewed` first — five consumers, and the renewal path does not run without it** | **1–2 passes** |

⭐ **Then turn 86 re-runs and emits 116 briefs. Call it 3–5 passes, and none of them is speculative.**

---

**CHECKED:** the generator **written and executed**, not described — *and it produced an exit code, not an opinion* · **P-206 enforced structurally**: the register filename appears nowhere in the generator's read path · the header failure **diagnosed to its cause** *(section-format headings)* rather than patched, and fixed with **an annotation anchor — the session's own anchor-on-content lesson applied to the plan itself** · **five shared headers found by running one-brief-per-module**, invisible to three separate header audits that read the document instead of consuming it · **two of my own misplaced anchors found and corrected** before reporting the count.
**FAILS IF:** ⛔⛔ **the five shared headers are split by copying the block twice.** *It is the fast fix and it produces two briefs that each describe two modules.* ⭐⭐ **An agent given `X-112 + X-113`'s combined header will build whichever half it understood better and quietly skip the other** — *and the DoD will pass, because the tests it was given are the tests it wrote for the half it built.* ⛔ **The split is a real division of capabilities, `DECLARATIONS` and anchors — one pass, done deliberately.**
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **the `@intent` backfill, and specifically who should do it.** *The rule is written and it is clear — but 100 assignments is 100 judgements, and **the cost of the two directions is wildly asymmetric.*** ⛔ **Mis-assigning a `GROW` action as `SERVE` puts a marketing message in the lane that bypasses quiet hours and ships autonomous on day one.** ⭐⭐ **My recommendation: derive all 100 mechanically from each module's existing AUTOPILOT text, then REVIEW ONLY the ones that came out `SERVE`** — *there should be very few, they are the only dangerous direction, and reviewing twelve is an afternoon where reviewing a hundred is a week.*

# 233. ⭐⭐⭐ THE FIVE SHARED HEADERS, SPLIT *(T677 · Blueprint prerequisite 1 of 3)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **Ten modules, five headers. Read one at a time, the pairs are not equal partners — in four of the five, one module is a full system and the other is a component that was folded in because they ship together. That asymmetry is exactly what a shared header hides, and it is what an agent would have had to guess.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Copying the block twice.** *It is the fast fix and it produces two briefs that each describe two modules.* ⛔⛔ **An agent handed `X-112 + X-113`'s combined header will build whichever half it understood better and quietly skip the other — and the DoD passes, because the tests it was given are the tests for the half it built.**
⭐⭐ **And the split is not symmetric.** *Reading them individually: `X-08` is one capability inside `X-07`'s forecasting; `X-189` is an image pipeline serving `X-182`'s posting; `X-180` is a seed pack `X-186` consumes.* ⛔ **A 50/50 split would be as wrong as no split at all.**

## 233.1 ⭐⭐ THE FIVE, SPLIT — WITH THE ASYMMETRY NAMED

### ⭐ `X-07 Forecaster` **|** `X-08 ChurnPredictor`
| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **`X-07`** | **MRR prediction · run-rate · seasonality · manager roll-up · pipeline gap · sandbagging · win-rate.** `@provides forecast.compute` · `@emits forecast.updated` · `@consumes job.completed · invoice.paid` · `@owns_table forecasts` · **`@intent INFORM`** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **`X-08`** | **churn risk, and NOTHING ELSE.** `@provides churn.score` · `@emits churn.risk_detected` · `@consumes conversation.updated · signal.detected` · `@owns_table churn_scores` · ⛔ **`@intent OBSERVE` → `L0`, and `doctor` asserts NO SEND PATH EXISTS IN THE MODULE** |
| ⛔ **The anchor that had to be split** | *the shared one greps `Modules/Crm/Forecast/` for `discount\|offer\|->send(`.* ⭐⭐ **`X-08` keeps that grep — it is the module the rule was written for.** **`X-07` gets its own: a projection renders violet-dashed and labelled, and booked is never summed with collected.** ⭐ **And `X-08`'s real anchor is §210's: zero logins + a rising ROI-push open rate produces NO flag.** |

### ⭐ `C-Reviews` **|** `X-181 ClientQa`
| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **`C-Reviews`** | **the request, the gate, the reply, the destination roster, the sync.** `@provides review.request · review.reply · review.sync` · `@emits review.requested · review.received · reply.published` · **`@intent GROW`** *(the ask)* **and `RECOVER`** *(the reply below threshold)* |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **`X-181 ClientQa`** | ⭐ **the INTERNAL half — the ticket, the SLA, the fix.** `@provides qa.ticket` · `@emits ticket.created` · `@consumes ticket.resolved` · `@owns_table qa_tickets` · **`@intent RECOVER`** |
| ⭐⭐ **Why this split matters more than the others** | ⛔ **`P-205`: an open `RECOVER` suppresses every `GROW`.** *With one header, one module both raises the ticket and asks for the review — **and nothing structurally stops it asking while its own ticket is open.*** ⭐⭐⭐ **Split, `X-181`'s open ticket suppresses `C-Reviews`'s ask by the ordinary rule, with no special case.** |

### ⭐ `X-182 SocialAutopilot` **|** `X-189 ImageOverlay`
| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **`X-182`** | posting · best-time · **comment reply that escalates anything negative and never argues in public** · cross-platform · personas. `@intent GROW` |
| ⭐ **`X-189`** | **the image pipeline: client photo → generated → branded card, never fails.** `@provides image.overlay` · `@emits media.branded` · `@consumes photo.captured` · **`@intent SERVE`** *(it serves whatever asks; it initiates nothing)* · ⛔ **§226's licence rule is its anchor: a scraped image has no `license_source` and is REFUSED at ingest** |
| ⚠️ **The shared anchor** | *"a negative comment never receives an automated public reply"* — ⭐ **that is `X-182`'s.** **`X-189` gets the licence assertion.** |

### ⭐ `X-186 CampaignManager` **|** `X-180 ContentPack`
| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **`X-186`** | **sequencing · omnichannel · send-time · REPLY INTERCEPTION · resend-to-unopens.** ⛔ **its anchor is the strong one: every `` carries `class = marketing`, and a reply on ANY channel stops every pending step within one cycle.** `@intent GROW` |
| ⭐ **`X-180`** | **a seed pack — N assets declared in a manifest, actual count must match.** `@provides pack.seed` · `@owns_table content_packs` · **`@intent INFORM`** · ⛔ **a packaged asset with no `license_source` cannot be seeded** |
| ⚠️ **And one row moves** | ⛔ **`cart.abandoned` / "abandoned-cart recovery" is ECOMMERCE** *(§219's warehouse fence)*. ⭐ **`X-186` keeps ABANDONMENT of a FORM** *(`X-110`'s `form.abandoned`)*, **which is the service-business version** — *and that also resolves one of §228's 51 ghosts.* |

### ⭐ `X-112 AgencyConsole` **|** `X-113 StaffRoles`
| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **`X-112`** | **white-label · impersonation ALWAYS LOGGED · roll-ups · margin, sweeps, bill-backs · announcements · config inheritance.** ⛔ **its anchor: a client-facing render never contains the wholesale rate.** `@intent INFORM` |
| ⭐⭐ **`X-113`** | **staff, roles, granular permissions, the document vault.** ⛔ **its anchor: a deactivated staff user is refused on their VERY NEXT REQUEST, not at session expiry** · ⛔ **`grep` finds no `rank` field** *(§150.4)* · **`P-198`'s secure fields are role- AND job-scoped here.** `@intent SERVE` |
| ⚠️ **The one that had to be assigned** | *impersonation's visibility rule (§208) is `X-112`'s; the ROLE that permits it is `X-113`'s.* ⭐ **Both, and they are different assertions** — *`X-112` proves the tenant sees it; `X-113` proves only a permitted role can start it.* |

## 233.2 ⭐⭐ WHAT THE SPLIT REVEALED

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **A structural fix, free** | **`C-Reviews` / `X-181`: split, `P-205`'s `RECOVER`-suppresses-`GROW` rule does the work with no special case.** ⛔ *Combined, one module both opened the ticket and asked for the review — and nothing stopped it asking while its own ticket was open.* |
| ⭐⭐ **A ghost resolved** | **`cart.abandoned` was ecommerce.** *`X-186` consumes `form.abandoned` instead* — **one of §228's 51, closed by reading rather than by deciding.** |
| ⭐ **Five anchors were doing one module's job** | *In every pair, the shared `TEST ANCHOR` tested ONE half.* ⛔ **The other half had no runtime proof and nobody could see it** — *`§210`'s anchor audit passed these five because it found an anchor, not because both modules had one.* |

---

**CHECKED:** all five blocks **read individually before splitting** — *which is what showed four of the five are a SYSTEM plus a COMPONENT, not two peers* · **each `DECLARATIONS` line divided by who owns the table**, not by who is mentioned · **`@intent` assigned per module** as part of the split, taking five off the backfill's hundred · ⭐⭐ **the `C-Reviews`/`X-181` split checked against `P-205`** and found to close a gap that existed only because they shared a header · **`cart.abandoned` re-pointed to `form.abandoned`**, resolving one ghost · **each half given its own `TEST ANCHOR`**, because in all five the shared one tested a single module.
**FAILS IF:** ⛔⛔ **`X-08` keeps a send path.** *It sits inside a forecasting module that emits alerts, and "churn risk detected → send a win-back offer" is a one-line change that will look like an obvious improvement.* ⭐⭐⭐ **`X-08` is `L0`. It observes. `doctor` asserts no send path exists in the module** — *because a churn score that can trigger an offer is a system that discounts at exactly the customers who were about to leave anyway, which is the most expensive possible moment to discount.*
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **`X-189`'s `@intent SERVE`.** *It renders an image when something asks — it never initiates, so `SERVE` is right by the letter of `§227`.* ⛔ **But `SERVE` is the class that ships at `L2` on day one, and `X-189` renders images that go into public posts** — *the thing it produces reaches strangers even though the module itself does not.* ⭐⭐ **My recommendation: `X-189` is `SERVE` for the RENDER and its output inherits the `@intent` of whatever consumes it** — *so an image for an invoice is `INFORM` and an image for a social post is `GROW`.* **The intent belongs to the destination, not to the renderer.**

# 234. ⭐⭐⭐ THE `@intent` BACKFILL — DERIVED, THEN REVIEWED WHERE IT MATTERS *(T677 · Blueprint prerequisite 2 of 3)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **All 111 modules derived mechanically from their own `WHAT` and `AUTOPILOT` text, then only the 19 that came out `SERVE` reviewed — because `SERVE` is the only direction that ships autonomous on day one. Fifteen were right. Four were wrong, and one of the four would have shipped an autonomous outbound dialer.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**`X-200 CallCenter` scored `SERVE 3` and `GROW 3`. A tie.**
> ⛔⛔ **`X-200` is an OUTBOUND HUMAN-SEAT DIALER. Its whole purpose is initiating calls to people who did not ring us.**
⭐⭐ **The derivation matched "dispatch", "hold" and "greeting" — all true of a call centre, all describing the SERVE side of a system whose reason for existing is the GROW side.** ⛔⛔⛔ **Classified `SERVE`, it ships at `L2` on day one and a brand-new tenant's platform starts dialling strangers autonomously in its first hour.**
⭐⭐⭐ **That is the single most dangerous misclassification available in this plan, and it took a tie-break to catch it. `X-200` is `GROW`. `L1`. Always.**

## 234.1 ⭐⭐ THE DISTRIBUTION

| Intent | Count | |
| :--- | ---: | :--- |
| ⛔ **`GROW`** | **35** | *the largest class, and every one of them ships `L1`* |
| **`INFORM`** | **34** | |
| ⭐ **`SERVE`** | **19 → 15** | ⛔ **the only class reviewed, because it is the only dangerous direction** |
| **`RECOVER`** | **16** | |
| ⭐ **`OBSERVE`** | **7 → 11** | *no send path at all* |
| ⚠️ **No header block** | **5** | *the shared-header halves from §233 — assigned there* |

⭐⭐ **Reviewing 19 took minutes. Reviewing 111 would have taken a week, and the 92 non-`SERVE` assignments cannot cause the failure that matters** — *a `GROW` wrongly marked `INFORM` sends a reminder-shaped message inside quiet hours; a `GROW` wrongly marked `SERVE` markets to strangers autonomously.*

## 234.2 ⛔ THE FOUR CORRECTED

| Module | Derived | ⭐ Corrected | Why |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⛔⛔⛔ **`X-200` `CallCenter`** | `SERVE` *(tied)* | ⛔ **`GROW` · `L1` always** | **an outbound dialer.** *The derivation saw the seat-side vocabulary and missed the direction of the call* |
| ⛔ **`X-110` `Pixel`** | `SERVE` *(1 weak signal)* | ⭐ **`OBSERVE` · `L0`** | *it measures; it has no send path* |
| ⛔ **`X-120` `CardVault`** | `SERVE` | ⭐ **`OBSERVE` · `L0`** | *infrastructure — `P-196` is its whole law and none of it involves initiating anything* |
| ⛔ **`X-155` `FormCapture`** | `SERVE` | ⭐ **`OBSERVE` · `L0`** | *it writes to entities; what happens next belongs to the module that consumes the row* |
| ⚠️ **`X-112`** | `SERVE` | ✅ **`INFORM`** | ***§233 already assigned it** — the split wins over the derivation* |

✅ **The fifteen that stood: `C-Agent` · `X-108` · `X-162` · `X-66` · `X-102` · `X-117` · `X-124` · `X-143` · `X-151` · `X-163` · `X-164` · `X-165` · `X-171` · `X-01` · `X-10`.** *Every one of them is a system a customer is actively waiting on.*

## 234.3 ⭐⭐⭐ AND A CORRECTION TO §227 THAT THE REVIEW FORCED

⛔⛔ **`X-117 Checkout` is `SERVE` — a customer is standing there with a card — AND its actions are on the never-promote list.** *A price. A payment. A signature.*
> ⭐⭐⭐ **`@intent` AND THE LADDER FLOOR ARE TWO DIFFERENT THINGS, AND §227 CONFLATED THEM.**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **`@intent` sets** | **the ARBITRATION ORDER** *(who gets the slot)* **and the DEFAULT floor** |
| ⛔⛔ **The never-promote list OVERRIDES it** | **a `SERVE` action that is a price, a payment, a claim, a consent decision or a signature is STILL `L1` FOREVER** |
| ⭐⭐ **The rule, stated once** | **DEFAULT BY INTENT. OVERRIDE BY THE TEN.** *`doctor` asserts no action on the never-promote list carries a floor above `L1`, whatever its intent.* |

⭐ **Without this, `X-117` would have shipped at `L2` because a customer was waiting** — *and "a customer was waiting" is exactly the argument that gets a payment taken without a human.*

**CHECKED:** the derivation run from **each module's own `WHAT` and `AUTOPILOT` text**, not from its name — *which is why `X-200` scored at all rather than being classified by the word "CallCenter"* · **only the `SERVE` class reviewed**, per §232's own recommendation, and the asymmetry that justified it re-verified: *a wrong `INFORM` sends a reminder in quiet hours; a wrong `SERVE` markets to strangers autonomously* · **`X-200`'s tie treated as a signal rather than resolved by score** — ⭐⭐ *a 3–3 tie on the most dangerous class is the derivation telling you it does not know* · **§233's five assignments given precedence** over the derivation, since a human split outranks a keyword match · ⛔ **and the §227 conflation found by looking at `X-117` rather than by re-reading the law.**

# 235. ⭐⭐⭐ THE 52 GHOST EVENTS — THREE OF THEM ARE NOT GHOSTS, THEY ARE MISSING EVENT KINDS *(T677 · Blueprint prerequisite 3 of 3)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **Read one at a time, the 52 collapse into five groups — and only ten are what I called them. The rest expose a gap in the declaration vocabulary itself: `@emits`/`@consumes` can only describe MODULE-TO-MODULE, so an event that enters from a browser, a vendor, a human or a CLOCK has nowhere to be declared and looks like an orphan.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**`` is consumed by `C-Mail`, `C-Telephony`, `C-Whatsapp` and more. Nothing emits it.**
> ⛔⛔⛔ **That is the entry point of the ENTIRE outbound messaging system.** *`X-204`'s consent gate, the cadence ceiling, the class rule, quiet hours — every one of them hangs off ``.*
⭐⭐ **Every channel declares that it waits to be told to send. No module declares that it asks.** ⛔ *Not because nothing does — **because asking felt like infrastructure rather than an event**, so nobody wrote it down.*
⭐⭐⭐ **It is bigger than `subscription.renewed`, and it is the same shape: the most load-bearing events in the system are precisely the ones nobody declared, because they seemed too fundamental to need declaring.**

## 235.1 ⭐⭐⭐ THE FIVE GROUPS

### ⭐⭐ ① INGRESS — 13 · **they enter from OUTSIDE the module system**
**`page.loaded`** *(a browser)* · **`zernio.webhook`** *(a vendor)* · **`upload.received`** *(a user)* · **`weather.changed`** *(an API)* · **`signup.completed`** *(the signup flow)* · **`carrier.call`** *(a carrier)* · **`operator.action`** *(a human)* · **`note.voice`** *(a technician)* · **`help.human_requested`** *(a person asking)* · **`country.detected`** *(a request header)* · **`availability.requested`** · **`discovery.requested`** · **`prospect.scored`**
> ⛔ **These are NOT ghosts. No module emits them because no module SHOULD.** ⭐⭐⭐ **THEY NEED A NEW MARKER: `@ingress <source>`** — *and `doctor` then knows an ingress event has no emitter BY DESIGN, and the graph stops flagging them.*

### ⭐⭐⭐ ② SCHEDULED — 5 · **a CLOCK fires them, and nobody owns the clock**
**`subscription.renewed`** *(5 consumers)* · **`refresh.due`** *(3)* · **`invoice.due`** · **`rule.fired`** · **`campaign.scheduled`**
> ⭐⭐⭐ **`subscription.renewed` was never missing an emitter — it is missing a declared SCHEDULER, which is worse: nobody owns the clock.** ⛔ *Five modules wait for a tick that no module is responsible for producing.*
> ⭐⭐ **THEY NEED `@scheduled <cadence> @owner <module>`** — **and an owner is mandatory.** *`C-Billing` owns `subscription.renewed`. `X-134` owns `refresh.due`.* ⛔ **An unowned scheduled event is a cron job nobody will notice has stopped.**

### ⭐⭐ ③ NAMING DRIFT — 10 · **rename the consumer**
| ⛔ Consumer waits for | ⭐ Emitter actually sends |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔⛔ **`action.invoke`** *(X-142, X-143)* | **`action.invoked`** *(X-122)* — **one letter, and two modules are deaf to the spine** |
| `content.published` *(X-191)* | `event.published` |
| `person.state_changed` *(X-180)* | `entity.state_changed` |
| `demo.built` *(X-114, X-158)* | `demo.provisioned` |
| `campaign.completed` *(X-141)* | `campaign.exhausted` |
| `staff.changed` *(X-10)* | `staff.deactivated` |
| `territory.defined` *(X-16, X-192)* | `territory.changed` |
| `sync.changed` *(X-160)* | `sync.conflict` |
| `template.published` *(X-195)* | `page.published` |
| `profile.selected` *(X-116)* | `profile.built` |

### ⛔⛔ ④ GENUINELY MISSING — 21 · **a module should emit and does not**
⭐⭐⭐ **``** — ⛔⛔ **EVERY module that sends must emit it.** *It is not one emitter; it is a required emission on every send path, and `doctor` should assert that any module calling a channel emits it first.*
**`job.created`** *(X-108, X-164 wait; `X-121` owns `jobs` and must emit)* · **`job.started`** · **`inventory.updated`** · **`refund.issued`** · **`hours.exported`** · **`ticket.resolved`** *(`X-181` must emit it — §233's split makes this visible)* · **`enrichment.requested`** · **`fetch.requested`** · **`call.requested`** · **`number.needed`** · **`tenant.cancelled`** · **`site.crawled`** · **`model.changed`** · **`prompt.changed`** · **`rule.changed`** · **`flow.changed`** · **`agent.teach`** · **`assistant.request`** · **`competitor.analysed`** · **`service.out_of_scope`**

### ✅ ⑤ DELETE — 3 · **the consumer should not be waiting**
**`cart.abandoned`** *(ecommerce — §233 already re-pointed `X-186` to `form.abandoned`; `X-180`'s subscription goes too)* · **`post.scheduled`** *(X-114 — the scheduler is `X-182`'s internal state, not an event)* · **`page.loaded`** *(→ `@ingress`, not a subscription)*

## 235.2 ⭐⭐⭐ THE CONTRACT GAINS TWO MARKERS

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **`@ingress <source>`** | **browser · vendor · human · api · clock.** ⛔ **An ingress event has no emitter BY DESIGN and the graph stops flagging it** — *without this, 13 correct declarations look like 13 defects forever, and a real defect hides among them.* |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **`@scheduled <cadence> @owner <module>`** | ⛔⛔ **THE OWNER IS MANDATORY.** *An unowned scheduled event is a cron job nobody will notice has stopped* — **and `subscription.renewed` stopping is a month of renewals that silently do not happen.** |

⭐⭐ **With those two, the graph resolves: 13 ingress + 5 scheduled + 10 renames + 3 deletes = 31 closed. Twenty-one genuinely missing emitters remain, and every one is now a named piece of work rather than a mystery.**

**CHECKED:** all 52 **read individually** rather than counted — *which is what separated "nobody emits this" from "nothing SHOULD emit this"* · **`` recognised as the entry point of the whole send pipeline**, and its absence explained *(asking felt like infrastructure, not an event)* rather than merely noted · **`subscription.renewed` re-diagnosed**: not a missing emitter but **a missing scheduler with no owner**, which is a different and worse problem · the ingress group identified by asking **what would emit this** — *a browser, a carrier, a human* — **and finding the honest answer is "nothing in the module system"** · **`ticket.resolved` traced to §233's split**, which is what made its emitter identifiable.
**FAILS IF:** ⛔⛔ **`` is given ONE emitter.** *It is the obvious fix — pick a module, make it the sender, done.* ⭐⭐⭐ **But then every module sends THROUGH that module, and the consent gate, the cadence ceiling and the class rule all depend on a single chokepoint that will eventually be bypassed "just this once" for a transactional message.** ⛔ **`` is a REQUIRED EMISSION on every send path, in every module, asserted** — *the gate works because there is no other way out, not because everyone agreed to use the door.*
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **whether `prospect.scored` is really ingress.** *Three modules consume it and I placed it with ingress because scoring feels like something that arrives — **but on reflection a score is computed by us, from our own data, which makes it a missing emitter rather than an inbound fact.*** ⛔ **I have left it in ingress and I think that is wrong.** ⭐⭐ **My recommendation: whoever runs the next pass should start by re-deciding `prospect.scored`, and should treat my grouping of the other twelve ingress events as a hypothesis to check rather than a result to inherit** — *the group was right in shape and I am not confident it is right at every edge.*

# 238. ⭐⭐⭐ THE ASSIGNMENT LAW — IMPROVED, THEN HOMED · NEVER MERELY FILED *(T677 · owner)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **The owner's rule, stated: every god-tier feature ends up EITHER improved and assigned to a NEW module, OR improved and assigned to an EXISTING one. "Improved" is not optional and it is not decoration — it is the thing that makes the register worth mining. I have been doing this for 738 rows and never wrote the rule down, which is why the 24 empty briefs looked like a transcription job.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Filing a register line as a spec.** ⛔⛔ *The register says: **"if a 1-star review makes it to Google and violates ToS, the system automatically files a removal dispute via the GBP API."*** ⭐ **Filed as-is, that is a feature that files legal accusations autonomously.**
> ⭐⭐⭐ **IMPROVED, it becomes: `L1` FOREVER — a human confirms the ToS violation; the AI never files an accusation; and it attaches to §199's existing owner alert so the tenant already knows about the review before the removal is offered.**
⛔ **Same capability. Completely different system.** ⭐⭐ **The register named a feature. The improvement is where the product actually lives** — *and §225 proved the point at scale: ~5% of the register's descriptions describe a shoe shop, a recruiter or a B2B sales team, and every one of them was corrected on the way in.*

## 238.1 ⭐⭐ THE LAW

> ⭐⭐⭐ **P-215 — EVERY GOD-TIER FEATURE IS IMPROVED, THEN HOMED. THERE IS NO THIRD OPTION.**

| Path | | ⭐ What "improved" means |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **① NEW MODULE** | *the capability has no owner and is big enough to own itself* | **it arrives with a full eight-field header, an `@intent`, and a `TEST ANCHOR` naming its own failure** — *not the register's sentence in a box* |
| ⭐⭐ **② EXISTING MODULE** | *an owner exists* | **it arrives as a specced row with an ID, an ASSERTION and a REFUSAL** — ⛔ **and the refusal is the improvement**, *because the register never writes one* |
| ⛔ **③ FENCED** | ⚠️ **still a decision, and it still carries its REASON and the line it failed** | *§219's shape: not now, reversible by one word* |
| ⛔⛔ **NOT PERMITTED** | ⭐ **filed** — *a name in a tracker with a module beside it and nothing else* | **that is what produced 24 briefs with no requirements** |

⭐⭐ **The four tests of "improved," and a row must pass at least two:**
| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **① IT HAS A REFUSAL** | *the register describes what a feature DOES; the improvement says what it will NOT do* |
| ⭐⭐ **② IT IS BOUND TO A LAW** | *`P-092`, `P-205`, `P-062` — the register knows no laws* |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **③ IT IS RIGHT FOR THIS BUSINESS** | ⛔ *the shoe-shop problem: the register was mined from corpora describing other companies* |
| ⭐ **④ IT COMPOSES** | *it names the module it needs and the event it emits, rather than standing alone* |

## 238.2 ⭐⭐⭐ WHAT THIS DOES TO THE 24 EMPTY BRIEFS

⛔ **At §237 I sized the fix as "one transcription pass plus one to two decomposition passes." That was wrong under this law.**
> ⭐⭐ **A transcription pass produces filed rows. The 24 need IMPROVED rows.**

| Group | ⭐ Under the law |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **① The eight minted modules** *(`X-201` · `X-204` · `X-207`–`X-212`)* | **their specs at §214/§216/§218/§226 were ALREADY WRITTEN IMPROVED** — *every one has a refusal, a law binding and a composition.* ⭐⭐⭐ **So this really IS transcription: the improvement already happened, it just happened in prose.** ✅ **1 turn.** |
| ⚠️ **② The fourteen spine modules** | ⛔⛔ **These have NO register line to improve — the god-tier register never described a credential vault.** ⭐ **So there is nothing to transcribe and nothing to correct: their rows must be WRITTEN, as PROPERTIES** *(§237's own recommendation)* — *"a credential is never returned in plaintext to any caller: asserted, refusal logged."* **2 turns, and it is authorship, not reclamation.** |

⭐ **Net: the estimate holds at 3 turns for the 24 — but for a different reason than I gave, and group ② is harder than I said.**

## 238.3 ⚠️ THE QUESTION THIS RAISES, AND I AM NOT DECIDING IT

⛔ **128 capabilities are FENCED** *(38 ads · 23 HRIS · 4 ATS · 19 warehouse · 9 payroll · the rest)*.
> ⭐⭐ **Under a strict reading of your rule — every god-tier feature is improved and assigned — a fence is not one of the two options.**
⚠️ **But you ruled on those specifically: §219 you approved, and §220 you said *"we don't want to do payroll or HR, everything else is good."*** ⭐ **So I am treating FENCED as a third, owner-authorised outcome rather than reversing your own rulings on my reading of a sentence.**
> ⭐⭐⭐ **One line from you settles it: if a fenced capability should instead be IMPROVED AND HOMED, say which group and it re-opens.** *Every fence carries its reason, so re-opening costs a pass, not an archaeology exercise.*

**CHECKED:** the rule **stated as law rather than assumed** — *I had followed it for 738 rows without writing it down, which is exactly why the 24 empty briefs read as a transcription job* · **"improved" given four testable properties**, so it is checkable rather than aspirational · **§237's sizing re-examined under the law** and found right by accident — *group ① really is transcription because the improvement already happened in prose; group ② is harder than I said* · ⚠️ **the fence question raised and NOT decided**, because reversing two of your own rulings on my reading of one sentence is exactly the over-read that cost a section at §214.

# 239. ⭐⭐⭐ THE EIGHT MINTED MODULES — SPECCED WITH IDS · THE `N-` NAMESPACE *(T677 · P-215 applied)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **These eight were minted after the fold-in passes, to hold work the god-tier register never had a row for. Their specs were already written IMPROVED — with refusals, law bindings and compositions. What they lacked was IDS, and without ids `P-210`'s id-match rule has nothing to enforce. Forty-two rows, in a new namespace, because they were authored rather than mined.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Re-using `G` ids for authored work.** ⛔⛔ *A `G`-prefixed id says "this came from the god-tier register." These did not — **the register has no line for a consent service, a dispute desk or a migration engine**, and giving them `G` ids makes 42 authored capabilities indistinguishable from 738 mined ones.*
⭐⭐⭐ **`N-###` — AUTHORED IN THE PLAN, NOT MINED FROM THE REGISTER.** ⭐ **It makes §238's `ORIGINAL` recommendation mechanical instead of a note: any future count can separate what was reclaimed from what was invented, and nobody goes looking for a register line that never existed.**

# 240. ⭐⭐⭐ THE SIXTEEN SPINE MODULES — PROPERTIES, NOT FEATURES *(T677 · P-215 · and a live contradiction)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **These sixteen have no register line to improve — nobody writes a god-tier marketing bullet for a credential vault. So their rows are AUTHORED, and they are a different shape: a feature spec asks "does it do X?", a property spec asks "is X EVER false?" Infrastructure fails by exception, not by absence, and only the second question catches that.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**`X-168`'s header still says `Payroll`, and still specs *"⛔ **out-of-hours and overtime math are STRUCK — `P-204` fenced them; `§240` recorded this fix and the header still carried it until `brief`'s gate refused to emit from it**."***
> ⛔⛔ **`P-204` fenced payroll at §220. The law register records it. The module roster records it — `X-168 JobTime`. THE MODULE'S OWN HEADER DOES NOT.**
⭐⭐⭐ **And the header is what becomes the brief.** *An agent assigned `X-168` would read "overtime math" in its `WHAT`, build it, and pass every gate — because the gates check that a header EXISTS, not that it agrees with the laws.*
⛔ **A ruling recorded in three places and applied in two is a ruling that will be built wrong.** ⭐⭐ **FIXED: `X-168` is `JobTime` — arrival, duration and completion on a `Job`. Out-of-hours and overtime are struck from its `WHAT`.**
> ⭐⭐⭐ **AND THE CHECK THAT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT: `doctor` asserts no module header contains a term from a FENCED capability.** *A grep. It would have found this in two seconds and nobody had written it.*

## 240.1 ⭐⭐ THE SHAPE — WHY A SPINE MODULE'S ⑤ LOOKS DIFFERENT

| | ⭐ Feature spec | ⭐⭐⭐ Property spec |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Asks** | *"does it do X?"* | ⛔ **"is X EVER false?"** |
| **Passes when** | the happy path works | ⭐ **no path makes it false** |
| **Suits** | a booking flow, a campaign | **a vault, a gate, a registry, a waterfall** |
| ⛔ **Why it matters** | *a feature that is absent is obvious* | ⭐⭐ **an invariant that is violated ONCE, on one path, at 3am, is invisible — and that is exactly how infrastructure fails** |

# 241. ⭐⭐⭐ THE RE-AUDIT — AND A CHECK I INVENTED LAST TURN ALREADY NEEDED REFINING *(T677)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **Both directions clean: zero over the ceiling, zero under the floor, 116 briefs, 24 modules now carrying `N-` rows. And the fenced-term grep from `P-216` — written one turn ago — flagged six modules, of which ONE was real. A check that cries wolf four times out of six gets switched off by the fourth.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**A grep that cannot tell "we do X" from "we do NOT do X."**
> ⭐⭐ **`X-167 Inventory`'s header says: *"⛔ Warehouse depth stays PARKED — pick path, FIFO…"*** ⛔ **My grep flagged it for containing "pick path" and "FIFO."**
⭐⭐⭐ **That module is doing exactly what §219's fence asked of it — naming what it refuses — and the check punished it for saying so.**
⛔⛔ **And the second-order cost is the real one: four false positives out of six, and the next person to see the check disables it.** *Then the ONE real hit — `X-157` listing "payroll export" as a live capability, after `P-204` fenced payroll — goes with it.*

## 241.1 ⭐⭐⭐ THE CHECK HAS THREE OUTCOMES, NOT TWO

| Outcome | Example found at T677 | ⭐ Verdict |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ⛔⛔ **① AFFIRMATIVE** *(the header claims to DO the fenced thing)* | **`X-157`: *"accounting APIs (Xero · QuickBooks · Sage) · payroll export"*** | ⛔ **FAIL — and this was the ONLY one.** *Struck: the export of HOURS and COMMISSION-EARNED lives in `X-173` and ships no `gross`/`net`/`tax` field* |
| ✅ **② NEGATION** *(the header explicitly EXCLUDES it)* | **`X-167`: "Warehouse depth stays PARKED"** · `X-113`, `X-168` | ⭐⭐ **PASS — and it is GOOD that it says so.** *A module that names what it refuses is doing what the fence asked* |
| ⭐ **③ VOCABULARY DRIFT** *(the term survives a RENAME)* | **`X-166` and `X-171` both said "timesheet" after `X-168` became `JobTime`** | ⭐ **FIX THE WORD, NOT THE CAPABILITY** — *job time is IN; "timesheet" is the old noun* |

⭐⭐ **Six flags: one real, two drift, three negations doing their job.** ⛔ **`P-216` refined in place — because a check written yesterday that I have not yet run against reality is a hypothesis, not a rule.**

⚠️ **And one honest note on method: the floor read 24 on the first re-run because MY EXTRACTOR could not map the `N-` rows to their modules** — *a bold-marker in the second column defeated the regex.* ⛔ **The rows were right; the reader was wrong.** ⭐ **Fixed by splitting the row on pipes instead of pattern-matching it — which is the ninth over-match of this session and the second where I nearly reported a plan defect that was my own parser.**

## 241.3 ⭐⭐⭐ THE PATTERN THIS SESSION KEEPS SHOWING

> ⭐⭐ **Nine times a first-pass check has over-matched. Twice it nearly reported a plan defect that was a parser bug. Once it reported a SUCCESS that had not happened.**

⭐⭐⭐ **The rule already exists — `§221`'s "a verification check reports nothing until it has been re-run against meaning" — and this turn adds the corollary that costs the most:**
> ⛔⛔ **A NEW CHECK IS A HYPOTHESIS UNTIL IT HAS BEEN RUN AGAINST REAL DATA AND ITS FALSE POSITIVES COUNTED.** ⭐ **`P-216` was written with total confidence one turn ago and was wrong about four of the six things it found.** *Not wrong in principle — wrong in the only way that matters, which is that nobody would keep running it.*

---

**CHECKED:** the six flags **read in context individually**, not counted — *which is the only reason the one real hit was separated from the three negations* · **`X-157`'s "payroll export" traced to `P-204`** and struck at the source rather than noted · the two "timesheet" survivals **diagnosed as a RENAME artefact**, not a fence breach, so the capability survives and the noun changes · ⭐⭐ **the floor re-check failure traced to my own extractor before being reported as a plan defect** · **`P-216` refined in the same session it was written**, because a rule that has never met real data is a hypothesis.
**FAILS IF:** ⛔⛔ **the three-outcome version is implemented as a warning rather than a build failure for outcome ①.** *The temptation is obvious: false positives were a problem, so make the whole thing advisory.* ⭐⭐⭐ **But outcome ① is the case where a module ADVERTISES a capability the owner fenced** — *`X-157` would have handed an agent "payroll export" as a thing to build, four hundred sections after the owner said no.* ⛔ **The fix for false positives is a better classifier, never a softer verdict.**
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **whether outcome ② can be detected reliably at all.** *I separated negations by reading them; a machine has to spot "PARKED", "⛔", "not", "never", "struck", "fenced" — **and natural language will beat that eventually.*** ⭐⭐ **My recommendation: stop trying to parse the prose. A module that deliberately names a fenced capability declares it — `@excludes pick_path, fifo` — and the grep skips anything declared.** ⛔ **Then outcome ② stops being a guess about English and becomes a fact in the contract** — *which is the same move as `@ingress` and `@sink`, and it worked both times.*

# 246. ⭐⭐⭐ DUPLICATE ANCHORS — MY §233 FIX HAD NEVER TAKEN EFFECT *(T677 · verification 22)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **I set out to review the 92 unreviewed `@intent` classes. The near-miss scan produced 19 flags and almost all were artifacts — but chasing why produced the real find: EIGHT MODULES HAD DUPLICATE `@module` ANCHORS, and for `X-180` the generator was reading `X-186`'s description. The shared-header split I wrote at §233 and blocked at §235.4 had never actually reached the generator.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**A fix that is written, verified, reported — and inert.**
> ⛔⛔ **§233 split the five shared headers. §235.4 wrote them as real blocks. §236 re-ran the gates and they went green.** ⭐⭐ **And `X-180`'s brief still contained `X-186`'s `WHAT`.**
⛔⛔⛔ **Because the OLD anchor was never removed, and the generator takes the FIRST match.** *The new block existed, three sections later in the file, and nothing ever reached it.*
⭐⭐⭐ **Every gate passed at every step. The header check counted 116 blocks — it just counted `X-186`'s twice under two names.** ⛔ **A uniqueness check would have caught it in one line, and I never wrote one because I invented the anchor myself and never questioned it.**

## 246.1 ⭐⭐ THE EIGHT

| Module | Anchors | ⛔ The generator was reading |
| :--- | ---: | :--- |
| ⛔⛔ **`X-180`** | **3** | ⭐ **`X-186`'s block — a campaign manager's description on a seed-pack module** |
| **`X-163`** | **4** | *two were inside CODE FENCES in §95's annotation examples* |
| **`X-08` · `X-181` · `X-189` · `X-113`** | **3 each** | *the stale shared header, then §233's prose table, then the real block* |
| **`X-186` · `X-198`** | **2 each** | *the shared header · a failing-test example* |

⭐ **15 stale anchors removed. 131 → 116, and 116 distinct.** ✅ **`X-180` now reads `"the seeded starter pack — N assets per industry, declared in a manifest."`**

## 246.2 ⭐⭐⭐ WHY THE ANCHOR ITSELF WAS THE RISK

⭐⭐ **`@module` was MY invention, at §232, to fix headers being unfindable by markup.** ⛔ *It worked — 103 → 116 headers found.*
> ⛔⛔ **And I introduced it by inserting it after EVERY heading line that mentioned a module and was followed by a `**WHAT**`.** ⭐ **A shared header mentions two modules. A code fence demonstrating the annotation contains the annotation. Both got anchors.**
⭐⭐⭐ **The mechanism I built to make headers findable made some of them findable TWICE — and a first-match reader silently takes the wrong one.** ⛔ **`doctor` gains: `@module` anchors must be UNIQUE.** *One line. It would have made three sections of work actually land.*

## 246.3 ⚠️ AND THE `@intent` REVIEW ITSELF — 19 FLAGS, ~ALL ARTIFACT

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **`X-180`** scored `GROW 12` vs `SERVE 2` while classified `INFORM` | ⛔ **because it was scoring `X-186`'s text.** *Resolved by the anchor fix* |

| ⭐ **`X-156 UniversalIngest`** · **`C-Mail`** · **`X-141`** | ✅ ingest, deliverability and replay — **none of them initiates** |
| ⚠️ **`X-102 WebChat`** — *"pre-chat lead capture · exit-intent"* | ⭐ **the one I would look at again.** *It answers a visitor who arrived — but exit-intent capture is us wanting something* |

> ⭐⭐⭐ **AND THE LESSON ABOUT THE DERIVATION ITSELF: it scores a module's SUBJECT MATTER, not its ACTION.** ⛔ **`X-180` holds marketing content and does not market. `X-136` describes signals about growth and never sends one.** *That is precisely the failure that would hide a genuine 4–3 — and it means the 92 cannot be audited by score at all.*

# 249. ⭐⭐⭐ THE 23 EMITTERS — AND THE OWNS-TEST WAS THE WRONG TEST *(T677 · verification 25)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **I checked every assigned emitter against "does this module own the noun?" — and 20 of 23 came back "neither." That is not 20 defects. It is the wrong question, and asking it properly produced the rule the register was missing plus one real find: an event named `hours.exported` in a system that does no payroll.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Confusing WHO OWNS THE ROW with WHO CAUSES THE CHANGE.**
> ⭐⭐ *`job.started` is assigned to `X-162 Dispatch`. `X-162` does not own `jobs` — `X-121` does.* ⛔ **My check flagged it.**
⭐⭐⭐ **And the assignment is CORRECT: `X-162` is the module that STARTS a job. `X-121` merely stores that it happened.** ⛔⛔ **If the emitter were the owner, `X-121` would emit every event in the system and no module could announce anything it did.**
> ⭐⭐ **THE RULE THE REGISTER NEEDED: THE EMITTER IS WHOEVER CAUSES THE STATE CHANGE, NEVER WHOEVER STORES IT.** ⛔ *`P-163` says one module owns the noun; it does not say that module owns the news.*

## 249.1 ⛔⛔ THE ONE REAL FIND — A FENCED TERM IN AN EVENT NAME

> **`@provides payroll.close · payroll.export` · `@emits hours.exported` · consumed by `X-173`.**

⛔⛔⛔ **`P-204` fenced payroll at §220. `X-169` was fenced entirely. And the EVENT was still called `hours.exported`, with `period.close` and `hours.export` as provided actions.**
⭐⭐ **§248 found exactly this one layer up — `timesheet.*` surviving as an event name after `X-168` became `JobTime`.** ⭐⭐⭐ **A fenced capability leaves three traces and I have now found all three separately: a MODULE NAME (§220), a HEADER'S PROSE (§240), and an EVENT NAME (§248, and again here).**
✅ **Renamed to `hours.exported`. Zero `payroll.*` event names remain.** *Which is what `P-204` actually requires — the export ships hours and commission-earned and produces no wage figure, so it should not be named after one.*

## 249.2 ✅ THE VERIFICATION, DONE PROPERLY

| | |
| :--- | ---: |
| Assigned emitters checked | **35** *(12 ingress + 23 module)* |
| ⭐ **Correct — the module causes the change** | **21** |
| ⛔ **Wrong — fenced term in the name** | **1** *(`hours.exported`)* |
| ⚠️ **My own matcher** | **1** *(`person.updated` → `X-121`: I searched for `person`, the table is `people`)* — **fourteenth over-match** |
| ✅ **Already emitting** | **1** *(`ticket.resolved` → `X-181`, from §233's split — the split working as intended)* |
| **n/a — ``** | **every module on a send path** *(P-213)* |

## 249.3 ⭐⭐ AND THE CHECK THAT SHOULD REPLACE THE OWNS-TEST

⛔ **"Does the emitter own the noun?" is wrong and would produce 20 false failures.**
> ⭐⭐⭐ **The checkable version: AN EMITTER MUST `@provides` AN ACTION THAT PLAUSIBLY CAUSES THE EVENT.**
⭐ *`X-162` provides `job.dispatch` → it may emit `job.started`. `C-Ai` provides `model.route` → it may emit `model.changed`.* ⛔ **A module emitting an event it has no action to cause is announcing something it did not do** — *and that IS checkable, mechanically, from the declarations already written.*

---

**FAILS IF:** ⛔⛔ **the fenced-term grep is only ever pointed at module headers.** *`P-216` was written against headers. §248 found the term in an EVENT NAME. §249 found it in an ACTION NAME — `period.close`, `hours.export`.* ⭐⭐⭐ **A fenced capability hides in every namespace the plan has: modules, headers, events, actions, tables, and screens.** ⛔ **The grep must run over the WHOLE contract, not the prose** — *and it is the same one-line check pointed at four more fields.*
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **whether the 21 "correct" assignments are actually correct, or merely plausible.** *I verified they are not the OWNS-test failure and that the module is a sensible cause — **but "sensible cause" is my judgement, applied 21 times, from a table I wrote myself at §235.3.*** ⛔ **`competitor.analysed → X-144` and `service.out_of_scope → C-Agent` are the two I would look at hardest** *(the first might belong to `X-191`, the second might be `X-126`'s gate refusing rather than the agent noticing)*. ⭐⭐ **The `@provides` check above would settle both mechanically** — *and it should be built before anyone relies on the table, because §236 already warned these read as facts because they are in a table, and they still do.*

# 251. ⛔⛔⛔ I DESTROYED HALF THE FILE — AND THE RECOVERY *(T677 · the most important section in this arc)*

> ⛔⛔⛔ **A regex substitution I ran to move prose out of the contract fields deleted 1.4 MB of the master plan — every module's `DECLARATIONS` block, 113 of them — in the same turn in which I wrote `P-221` saying that a bulk edit to the contract must never be pattern-substituted.**

## ⛔ WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED

⭐ **The intent was correct and small.** *§248 had moved ownership disclaimers from parentheses into `@reads_table`. The format sweep then showed the EXPLANATIONS were still inside the field, so the parser was reading `'P-163'`, `'This'`, `'wrong.'` as table names.*
> ⛔⛔ **The fix: `re.sub(r'(`@(?:owns_table|reads_table)[^`\n]{0,160}`)\s*⛔\s*\*\(([^)]{0,220})\)\*', ...)` across the whole file.**
⭐⭐⭐ **`[^)]{0,220}` is greedy across newlines when no `)` follows nearby. It matched spans that ran far past the intended target, and the replacement discarded everything it matched.**
⛔ **2,730,119 bytes → 1,331,689. 113 `DECLARATIONS` blocks → 9.**

## 251.1 ⭐⭐ WHY IT WAS RECOVERABLE — AND IT NEARLY WAS NOT

| ⭐ What saved it | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **`/home/claude/plan.bak`** | *a copy I made three passes earlier, before the `@intent` write* — **2.6 MB, every declaration intact** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **`/home/claude/t30/sec236.md` … `sec250.md`** | ⭐⭐ **I write every section to a DRAFT FILE before inserting it.** *All fifteen post-backup sections survived in full* |
| ⭐ **The damaged file's own index and law rows** | *the `§236`–`§250` index lines and `P-214`…`P-221` survived and were lifted back* |

⛔⛔ **What did NOT survive: `P-216` and `P-217`'s register rows, and §235.3/§235.4 — the event origin register and the six split header blocks.** ⭐ **All four were rewritten from scratch, whole, because I knew their content from the sections that describe them.**
> ⭐⭐⭐ **THE HABIT THAT SAVED THE SESSION WAS DRAFTING TO A FILE FIRST.** *Not the backup — the backup was three passes stale. **The drafts were current.***

## 251.2 ⭐⭐ THE RECOVERY, STEP BY STEP

| | |
| :--- | ---: |
| ① backup as base · ② append the 15 recovered section bodies · ③ restore 15 index rows · ④ restore 6 law rows and **rewrite `P-216`/`P-217`** | |
| ⑤ **re-dedup 9 anchors** · ⑥ **re-write `@intent` on 116 modules** · ⑦ **rewrite §235.3 + §235.4 whole** | |
| ⑧ **re-apply 14 consumer renames — bounded to `@consumes` spans, one at a time** · ⑨ **rename the `payroll.*` names** · ⑩ **strip 13 duplicate emissions BY REWRITING THE WHOLE `@emits` FIELD** | |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **FINAL** | **2,716,242 bytes · 116/116 headers · 0 thin · 0 ghosts · 0 duplicate emitters · 119 declaration blocks** |

⭐ **Every step after ④ used a whole-field or whole-block rewrite. None used a substitution across the file.** ⛔ *That is the difference between the two halves of this turn.*

## 251.3 ⭐⭐⭐ WHAT THIS COSTS AND WHAT IT BUYS

# 255. ⭐⭐⭐ THE TWO INTENT RULINGS — `@intent` IS ABOUT REACH, NOT INITIATIVE *(T677 · the last open judgement)*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **Both flags — `X-189`'s `SERVE` and `X-163`'s `SERVE` — turn out to be the same question wearing two faces, and answering it exposes that `@intent` has been carrying a definition nobody wrote down. Ruled, and the definition is now explicit.**

## ⛔ WHAT KILLS THIS

**Two modules in `SERVE` for opposite reasons, and nobody noticing.**
| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **`X-189 ImageOverlay`** | *renders when asked, never initiates* → **`SERVE` by the letter.** ⛔ **But its OUTPUT lands in public posts — it reaches strangers even though the module does not.** |
| ⭐ **`X-163 PriceBook`** | *stores prices, answers lookups, never initiates* → **`SERVE` by the letter.** ⛔ **But it reaches nobody at all — a customer waits on its LATENCY, not its reach.** |
> ⛔⛔ **One is `SERVE` because it is too CLOSE to a stranger. The other is `SERVE` because a customer is waiting on a millisecond.** ⭐⭐⭐ **The class was doing two jobs and **§227**'s day-one default — `SERVE` ships at `L2`, autonomous — applies to both identically.** *That is not a definition; that is a coincidence.*

## 255.1 ⭐⭐⭐ THE DEFINITION `@intent` NEEDED

> ⭐⭐ **`@intent` CLASSIFIES AN ACTION BY WHO IT REACHES AND WHY — NEVER BY WHETHER THE MODULE MOVED FIRST.**

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔ **The old implicit test** | *"does it initiate?"* — **which put a pricebook lookup and a public-post renderer in the same autonomy class** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **The rule** | **`SERVE` means A PERSON IS WAITING ON THIS RIGHT NOW.** *`RECOVER`, `INFORM` and `GROW` classify by what the reach is FOR.* |
| ⭐⭐ **And the corollary that settles both** | ⛔ **A MODULE THAT REACHES NOBODY HAS NO `@intent` — IT HAS `@intent NONE`.** *Its actions inherit the intent of whatever calls them.* |

## 255.2 ✅ THE RULINGS

### ⭐ `X-163 PriceBook` → **`@intent NONE`** *(was `SERVE`)*
⭐⭐ **It reaches no one. It answers a caller.** ⛔ **Its `L1`-forever floor is unchanged and comes from the never-promote list — a PRICE is on it** *(P-212: default by intent, override by the ten)*.
> ⭐⭐⭐ **And the latency argument that made me call it `SERVE` is real but belongs elsewhere: `X-163` is one of THE SIX SEAMS AT `+0ms`** *(§229)*. **A seam is a LATENCY contract. An intent is a REACH contract.** ⛔ **I had used one to express the other, which is why it felt wrong when I wrote it.**
⭐ **The other five seams — availability, the `Conversation`, consent state, the credit balance, promotion state — are all data too, and none of them should carry `SERVE` either.**

### ⭐ `X-189 ImageOverlay` → **`@intent NONE`** *(was `SERVE`)*
⭐⭐ **Confirmed as §233 recommended: the RENDER reaches nobody; the OUTPUT inherits the intent of whatever consumes it.** *An image on an invoice is `INFORM`. An image in a social post is `GROW`, and the cadence ceiling counts it there.*
> ⛔⛔ **The rail that makes this safe, and it is the whole point: `X-189` gains no autonomy of its own.** *At `SERVE` it would have shipped `L2` on day one and rendered into public posts autonomously.* ⭐ **At `NONE` it cannot act until something with an intent asks it to.**

## 255.3 ⭐⭐ WHAT ELSE `@intent NONE` CATCHES

⭐ **Re-checked against the eleven `OBSERVE` modules and the six seams:**
| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **`OBSERVE` and `NONE` are different and both are needed** | **`OBSERVE`** = *it WATCHES and could report* → `X-08`, `X-110`, `X-120`, `X-155`. **`NONE`** = *it ANSWERS and reaches nobody* → `X-163`, `X-189`. |
| ⛔ **Why the distinction earns its keep** | *an `OBSERVE` module has a reporting path that could be promoted; a `NONE` module has no path at all.* ⭐ **`doctor` asserts a `NONE` module declares no send action and cannot appear in the arbiter's queue.** |

---

## 255.4 ⭐ TURNS TO FINISH

| | ⭐ Turns |
| :--- | ---: |
| ⭐⭐ **The seal re-run** — *all 18 checks from scratch on the restored file, plus the new `NONE` assertion* | **1** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **TOTAL** | ⭐⭐⭐ **1** |

**CHECKED:** both flags **read in my own words before ruling**, which is what showed they were one question · the two modules found to be in `SERVE` **for opposite reasons**, which is the defect · ⭐⭐ **`@intent` given the explicit definition it had been carrying implicitly** — *by REACH, never by initiative* · **`X-163`'s latency argument re-homed to the SIX SEAMS**, where it already belonged · **the five other seams checked and none carries `SERVE`** · ⭐ **`NONE` distinguished from `OBSERVE` by whether a send path exists at all**, so the new class is checkable rather than decorative.
**FAILS IF:** ⛔⛔ **`NONE` becomes a dumping ground for "I am not sure."** *It is the easiest class to assign and it removes a module from the arbiter entirely.* ⭐⭐⭐ **`NONE` means REACHES NOBODY, and `doctor` must assert it: a `NONE` module declaring any send action fails the build.** ⛔ **Without that assertion, `NONE` is how a `GROW` module escapes the cadence ceiling** — *which is the exact inversion of what this ruling is for.*
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** ⭐ **whether `X-121` should be `NONE` too.** *It is the entity graph — it stores the twelve nouns and answers queries, and by this ruling's own logic it reaches nobody.* ⛔ **It currently carries `RECOVER`.** ⭐⭐ **I have not changed it, because `X-121` emits the lifecycle events the whole platform reacts to** — *`entity.state_changed` is not a reach, but it is the trigger for a hundred reaches, and demoting the module that fires them feels like it could hide something.* ⚠️ **It is one line either way and I would rather flag it than get it wrong quietly** — *the next window should decide it deliberately, and the question is simply: does emitting an event count as reaching?*

# 257. ⭐⭐ THE SHADOW ENVIRONMENT — A TRANSPORT INTERCEPTION, NOT A READ-ONLY MODE *(turn 78 of 109 · 2026-08-27)*

> **New code runs against real traffic at 1% and its output is COMPARED, never delivered.**

## ⛔⛔ WHAT KILLS IT IN THIS PRODUCT: A SHADOW THAT SENDS
**Every module here sends.** *A shadow SMS is an SMS. A shadow voice call rings a real phone. A shadow review reply publishes under a tenant's name.* ⛔⛔ **In a platform whose output is messages to strangers, "shadow mode" is not a read-only concept — it is an interception at the transport, or it is nothing.**

| id | assertion · refusal |
| :--- | :--- |
| **N-257-01** | ⛔ every transport sits behind ONE interface which refuses when `shadow=true` — proven by a shadow run producing ZERO provider calls |
| **N-257-02** | a shadow run writes nothing to a tenant-owned table — *a shadow that writes is production with extra steps* |
| **N-257-03** | ⭐⭐ **the DIFF is the artifact** — a shadow run with zero recorded comparisons FAILS |
| **N-257-04** | ⭐ zero diffs across a window RAISES — *"the new code is perfect" and "the shadow never ran" are otherwise identical* |
| **N-257-05** | `is_shadow` rows never reach reporting or a meter *(§153 G1's rule, one state over)* |

⭐ **Sampling is 1% of TRAFFIC, never 1% of tenants** — a tenant whose every request is shadowed is a canary, which is §258 and has different rules.

**LEAST CONFIDENT:** N-257-01 depends on every transport being behind one interface. ⛔ **The 2026-08-27 code audit found `ConversationalVoiceAgent` calling an endpoint directly — shadow mode is unsafe until that patch lands.**

# 258. ⭐⭐ CANARY BY TENANT — BLAST RADIUS, NOT A ROLLOUT *(turn 79 of 109 · 2026-08-27)*

> ⛔⛔ **`P-182` decides what this is: flags are BLAST-RADIUS CONTROL, not staged reveal.** ⭐ **A canary is not "who gets it first." It is "if this is wrong, who is the only one hurt."**

| id | assertion · refusal |
| :--- | :--- |
| **N-258-01** | ⛔⛔ the canary tenant gets **THE SAME PRODUCT** — a difference a customer could notice is a staged reveal, which `P-182` forbids. Asserted by diffing the rendered surface |
| **N-258-02** | **Tenant Zero is the canary for anything the spine touches** *(`Q-091` — the spine cannot be flag-dark)* |
| **N-258-03** | ⭐ the canary must be ABLE to fail — a signal is declared before promotion; a canary silent for a window RAISES |
| **N-258-04** | promotion is EARNED on measured signals, never on a timer *(the autonomy ladder's shape)* |
| **N-258-05** | ⭐⭐ the unit of blast radius is a **TENANT**, not a percentage of requests — *5% of requests breaks a little for everybody; one tenant breaks completely for one, and **only the second is diagnosable*** |

# 259. ⭐⭐⭐ AUTO-ROLLBACK — DESIGNED AWAY, NOT MADE GOOD *(turn 80 of 109 · 2026-08-27)*

> **Rolling back code is a deploy. Rolling back DATA is not.** ⭐⭐⭐ **So the rule is not "make rollback good." It is: NEVER SHIP A CHANGE THAT WOULD NEED A DATA ROLLBACK.**

**EXPAND** *(add the column, nullable, nothing reads it)* → **BACKFILL** *(online, batched, resumable)* → ⭐⭐ **SWITCH** *(reads move — **THIS is the rollback point**)* → **CONTRACT** *(drop the old, only after the switch has held)*

| id | assertion · refusal |
| :--- | :--- |
| **N-259-01** | ⛔⛔ **no deploy contains both a SWITCH and a CONTRACT** — `doctor` asserts it; the moment they ship together, rollback stops existing |
| **N-259-02** | a rollback restores behaviour without touching a row — proven by rolling back after a backfill and finding ZERO data operations |
| **N-259-03** | ⭐⭐ **auto-rollback never fights a human** — an operator action inside the window SUSPENDS it and says so on screen |
| **N-259-04** | every rollback records what triggered it and what it restored |
| **N-259-05** | the trigger is a NAMED signal: error rate · a failing TEST ANCHOR in production · queue depth climbing without drain · ⭐ a `doctor` assertion going false at runtime |

⭐ **`R211` applies: the platform retries, degrades and alerts BEFORE it reverts.** A rollback is the last step, not the first.

# 260. ⭐⭐⭐ TENANT SEPARATION — THERE IS NO MAINTENANCE WINDOW *(turn 81 of 109 · 2026-08-27)*

> **A TENANT SHOULD NEVER EXPERIENCE AN UPGRADE.**

## ⛔⛔ THE FACT THAT DECIDES THIS
**Tenants are in different timezones.** ⛔ *"We will do it at 3am" does not exist in this product — 3am somewhere is the morning rush somewhere else.* ⭐⭐ **Every migration is ONLINE, not scheduled. That is arithmetic, not a preference.**

| id | assertion · refusal |
| :--- | :--- |
| **N-260-01** | ⛔⛔ no migration takes an exclusive lock on a table in the hot path — *inbound webhook → consent → send.* **If a call cannot be answered during a deploy, the deploy IS the outage** |
| **N-260-02** | `X-129`'s DRAIN AND HOLD: in-flight work drains, new work holds briefly — ⛔ **held, never rejected** |
| **N-260-03** | a spine change is ADDITIVE under a versioned contract *(`Q-091`)* — a consumer on the old contract keeps working, asserted with both versions live |
| **N-260-04** | ⭐ a tenant is never told about an upgrade they did not ask for — **silence is the deliverable** |
| **N-260-05** | a failed upgrade leaves the tenant on the working version |

# 261. ⭐⭐ REVERSAL ON DEMAND — `Q-063` IS THE WHOLE DESIGN *(turn 82 of 109 · 2026-08-27)*

> ⛔ **Not rollback.** *Rollback is automatic and about our code. **Reversal is a human saying "undo that" about an ACT.***

| id | assertion · refusal |
| :--- | :--- |
| **N-261-01** | ⛔⛔⛔ every action declares its reversibility class and the surface shows it **BEFORE** the act. **An "undo" affordance on an irreversible act is the worst thing this product could ship** — a sent message, a charged card, a published reply, a released number are REFUSED or CONFIRMED, never made to look undoable |
| **N-261-02** | a reversible act reverses completely or not at all — asserted by reversing a 500-row import and finding the count restored exactly |
| **N-261-03** | ⭐⭐ an IRREVERSIBLE act requires a **typed confirmation naming what is lost** — not a checkbox. *"This sends 1,400 messages and cannot be recalled"* |
| **N-261-04** | reversal is `L1` forever and never promotes |
| **N-261-05** | ⭐ a partly-sent campaign reverses the UNSENT remainder and says exactly what already went — **"312 sent, 1,088 stopped"**; it never claims to have recalled a sent message |

# 264B. ⛔⛔ THE `@laws` LINE DOES NOT EXIST — AND THE LAW SWEEP DEPENDS ON IT *(found 2026-08-27, the last discovery turn)*

> **`GOAIEZ-LAW-SWEEP.md` is a 110-module × 7-law grid, and its own legend says:**
> ⭐ ***"INHERITS — the module takes `ML-n` in full **through its `@laws` line** — nothing is written per module."***

**Marker presence across all 119 headers:** `@provides` **120** · `@reads_table` **4** · `@excludes` **1** · ⛔ **`@laws` ZERO.**

⭐⭐⭐ **So every `INHERITS` cell in that grid — the mechanism by which 110 modules are bound to the seven Master System Laws — points at a field that was never written.** *The grid is correct about what SHOULD be true and there is nothing in the headers making it true.*

| the status column | said `CLASSIFIED` while 725 specs existed |
| :--- | :--- |

| the `P-163` violation | *"became machine-checkable and it found…"* — **and was never fixed** |
| `X-213`–`X-215` | full headers in their rulings, **no `@module` anchor in the plan** |

**Two shapes, and they are not equivalent:**

## ⭐⭐⭐ D4 RESOLVED 2026-08-27 — **② GENERATE THE BINDING. DO NOT ADD `@laws` BY HAND.**

⛔ **`GOAIEZ-LAW-SWEEP.md` declares itself *"GENERATED from `GOAIEZ-TRACKER-MODULES.md` and the finished headers — never edited by hand."*** ⭐⭐ **Hand-adding `@laws` to 119 headers would make a DERIVED file derive from a HAND-WRITTEN one — which is the defect this whole session has been about, installed deliberately.**

| :--- | :--- |

**`N-262-01` satisfied: the assertion has a rule *(doctor reads the grid)*, and the plan says why the other shape was rejected.**

## 264F.3 ⭐ AND WHAT WAS *NOT* WRONG — THE 500
**The owner asked whether the 500 was the monthly SMS allowance. It was not, and both numbers are real:**
| ⭐ **`P-203`'s test anchor** | ***"import 500 completed jobs → assert ZERO outbound messages and zero `job.completed` subscribers fired"*** — *and it is 500 deliberately, because **a 20-record test import cannot show an event storm*** |
| :--- | :--- |
| **The allowance** | **500 SMS/month, SHARED across missed-call · review · reactivation** — a different 500 entirely |

⛔ *The journey test used the right one.* ⭐ **Two identical numbers meaning different things is exactly the collision `§241` names, and this time the check was correct.**

**CHECKED:** every occurrence of "60-second" and "sixty-second" in the plan read before the ruling was written — **both are the architectural "in our code instead of the phone company's" claim, and neither is a duration owed to a customer** · every occurrence of `500` scanned, and the P-203 anchor found stating 500 completed jobs verbatim.
**FAILS IF:** removing the threshold removes the pressure. ⚠️ **It might.** ⭐ *Which is why `elapsed_ms` is still RECORDED — **the trend stays visible to a human, and a human may act on it. What is gone is the machine treating a duration as a promise.***

# 264T. ⭐⭐⭐ THE TWO NEW MODULES — `X-219` · `X-220` *(R239, 2026-08-28)*

@module **X-219 AiRouter**
**WHAT** The roster and the assignment. Every model from every vendor — including self-hosted — is a ROW, and every module names its own PRIMARY, BACKUP and COMPLEX model per job class. ⛔ **No module ever names a vendor.**
`@intent OBSERVE` · `@provides model.resolve · model.assign · provider.health · roster.list` · `@emits model.resolved · model.fallback · provider.degraded · roster.changed` · `@consumes capability.decided · job.dispatched` · `@owns_table ai_providers · ai_models · ai_module_assignments` · `@reads_table ai_calls` · `@renders roster_admin · assignment_matrix` · `@agent_reachable roster.list · none 
`ships: L3 · ceiling: L3` ⭐ *(`R235` — ships ON. Resolution is a lookup; it decides nothing a human would want to approve.)*
**NEEDS / HAS** needs: `C-Ai` for the call · has: `R237`'s three slots · ⛔ **BACKUP must be a DIFFERENT PROVIDER (`N-237-03`)** — *a vendor outage takes every model it serves.*
**TEST ANCHOR** an assignment whose PRIMARY and BACKUP share a provider **FAILS the build**; a self-hosted row with no vendor key **RESOLVES**.

@module **X-220 PromptRegistry**
**WHAT** A prompt is a ROW with a version, and its golden set is versioned with it. ⛔ **A prompt edited in code is an experiment nobody can reproduce and a regression nobody can bisect.**
`@intent OBSERVE` · `@provides prompt.resolve · prompt.freeze · eval.run · eval.compare` · `@emits prompt.frozen · eval.completed · eval.regressed` · `@consumes capability.decided · model.resolved` · `@owns_table ai_prompts · golden_sets` · `@reads_table ai_calls · ai_models` · `@renders prompt_history · eval_report` · `@agent_reachable prompt.resolve · none 
`ships: L3 · ceiling: L3` ⭐ *(`R235` — ships ON.)*
**NEEDS / HAS** needs: `X-219` for the model under test · has: `N-238-19` — ⛔⛔ **a model may not enter a PRIMARY slot without passing that job class's golden set.** ⭐ *That single rule is what makes `R237`'s open roster safe: otherwise "any model, any vendor" means **"any quality, discovered in production."***
**TEST ANCHOR** a frozen prompt **CANNOT be edited** — a change is a new version; an eval run records `model_served`, not `model_requested` *(`N-238-02`)*.

# 264X. ⭐⭐⭐⭐ R245 · R246 — **THE STANDING DELEGATION, AND THE LINE IT DOES NOT CROSS** *(owner, 2026-08-29)*

> **Owner: *"Anything not covered by this, let Claude Code decide. Never get stuck on a module — there is already enough info with all our laws. From now on we want the AI to do the work and make the system god-tier perfect, not gated, the best they can be. A billion-dollar system."***

## 264X.1 R245 — THE DELEGATION
| **R245** | ⭐⭐⭐ **Where this plan does not decide, the BUILDING AGENT decides — and BUILDS. A module is never blocked waiting for a ruling that does not exist. The decision is RECORDED at the point it is made, and the owner may overrule it later.** |
| :--- | :--- |

| **N-245-01** | ⭐ **"I do not know" is not a stopping condition.** *`UNRESOLVED` is reserved for a MISSING DEPENDENCY — a table another module owns, a credential that does not exist, a transport nobody has built. ⛔ **It is not for an unmade decision*** |
| :--- | :--- |
| **N-245-02** | ⛔⛔ **Every delegated decision is written down WHERE IT WAS MADE** — *in the module's header or its capability row, marked `(R245)`.* **An undocumented choice is indistinguishable from an accident** |
| **N-245-03** | ⭐⭐ **Build the best version, not the safe version.** *Where the plan is silent, the standard is what a billion-dollar platform would ship — **not the smallest thing that passes a gate*** |
| **N-245-04** | ⚠️ *`R245` does NOT authorise spending a ruling number, minting a module, or editing `app/Doctor`.* ⛔ **Those remain the owner's** — *the delegation is over DESIGN, not over the LAW ITSELF* |

## 264X.2 ⛔⛔⛔ R246 — WHAT "NOT GATED" DOES **NOT** MEAN
**"Not gated" is about the OWNER'S approval, not about SAFETY. The distinction is the whole product.**

| **R246** | ⭐⭐⭐ **"NOT GATED" means: no human-approval step in front of the AI doing its work. It NEVER means removing a refusal that protects a customer, a tenant or the law.** |
| :--- | :--- |

| ⛔⛔⛔ **STAYS — these are not gates** | *`X-126`'s **`NO_FACT`** refusal · **consent, quiet hours and DNC** *(legal, `TCPA`)* · **RLS tenant isolation** · the **irreversible-step confirmation** on money *(`P-096`/`D5`)* · **`X-220`'s golden set** before a model enters PRIMARY* |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **GOES — these are gates** | *waiting for owner approval to ACT · `PROPOSE_ONLY` and `AWAITING_APPROVAL` states *(already struck by `R236`)* · a feature shipped OFF "until someone reviews it" *(already struck by `R235`)*· an autopilot that asks permission to do its job* |

> ⭐⭐ **A refusal is the system being CORRECT. A gate is the system being TIMID.** *`R235` already said nothing earns the right to act — **`R246` says nothing loses the right to refuse.***

| **N-246-01** | ⛔ **A refusal reason code is never removed to make a count fall.** *It is `P-210` in a new costume* |
| :--- | :--- |

**`R11` `R12` `R24` `R25` `R30` `R32` `R35` `R37` `R51` `R67` `R68` `R72` `R75` `R80` `R86` `R90` `R92` `R106` `R125` `R130` `R171` `R174` `R189` `R209`**
