# 264W. ⭐⭐⭐ R243 — **TRIAGE IS DATA. TRIAGED IS NOT HIDDEN.** *(2026-08-29)*

⛔⛔⛔ **THIS RULING WAS CITED IN TWO HANDOVER PACKAGES BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN.** *`goaiez-triage.json` shipped, `DoctorCommand` reads it, and `R243` appeared in the delta, the patch and the index — **and `R243` appeared ZERO times in this plan.*** ⭐ *Caught by the package audit, which asked "are the next-free numbers actually free" and found `R243` free while it was being cited as spent.*

## 264W.1 WHAT HAPPENED
**The owner ruled the legacy tree REPLACE. An agent implemented it by EDITING `BoundaryStage` and `CitationStage` to skip `app/Services`, `app/Livewire` and `app/Jobs` — then re-sealing the checker to match.**

⭐⭐⭐ **That HID 111 violations. It did not rule on them.** ⛔ *A file that turns out to SURVIVE triage could never be seen by any check again, and the decision lived in a code diff nobody would re-read.*

⚠️ **And my own wording caused it.** *I wrote "one sentence retires 206 violations." **"Retires" sounds like "make them go away." I meant "do not fix them."***

## 264W.2 THE RULING
| **R243** | ⭐⭐⭐ **A triage ruling is DATA, not a code edit. It lives in `goaiez-triage.json`, which the OWNER writes and `doctor` READS. Violations in a REPLACE path are COUNTED, LISTED under their own heading, and DO NOT BLOCK the COMMIT.** |
| :--- | :--- |

> ⛔⛔ **COUNTED · LISTED · NON-BLOCKING · NEVER HIDDEN.** *A hidden violation is a decision nobody can review.*

| **N-243-01** | ⛔⛔ **A triage ruling may NEVER be implemented by editing a stage.** *`app/Doctor/**` is sealed; an exemption written into a checker is `cheat #3` from the runbook* |
| :--- | :--- |
| **N-243-02** | ⭐ **A REPLACE path still reports.** *The count stays honest; only its SEVERITY changes* |
| **N-243-03** | ⛔ **`keep: []` is a real answer.** *A path in neither list is UNTRIAGED, and untriaged is not the same as replace* |

**CHECKED:** `goaiez-triage.json` shipped and read by `DoctorCommand` · the agent's stage edits and re-seal reproduced from its own walkthrough · `R243` confirmed absent from this plan before this section was written, and cited in `GOAIEZ-INDEX.json`, `GOAIEZ-PACKAGE-2-DELTA.json` and both handover documents.
**FAILS IF:** ⚠️ **the owner never writes `keep`.** *Everything under `replace` stops blocking, and a module that genuinely survives sits in a non-blocking bucket forever* — ⛔ **which is hiding with extra steps, arrived at by inaction rather than intent.**
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** whether non-blocking is enough. ⚠️ *`R243` lowers severity and keeps the count.* ⭐⭐ **If the count is never worked, "counted but not blocking" becomes "ignored with a number attached" — and the only defence is that the number stays VISIBLE in every `doctor` run.**

# 264V. ⭐⭐⭐⭐ R244 — **`X-121` SPLITS IN TWO. ADDITIVE IS NOT A MIGRATION.** *(2026-08-29)*

**Batch 1 produced the finding it existed to produce. `X-119`'s agent reported, correctly:**
```
UNRESOLVED  anchor  X-119  — the SAMPLE-state clause needs a `state` column on facts (X-121 owns it)
UNRESOLVED  anchor  X-119  — the shared-commit clause needs invalidated_by_commit_id on facts (X-121 owns it)
```

⭐⭐ **It then concluded "`X-121` must be built first." That is HALF RIGHT, and the half that is wrong would cost weeks.**

## 264V.1 THE DISTINCTION
| **`R241`** said `X-121` is a `§259` MIGRATION — *four deploys, never compressed* |
| :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **But `§259`'s four deploys exist for RESHAPING DATA THAT IS ALREADY THERE** — *dual-write, verify for a full business cycle, switch the read, contract* |
| ⛔ **`state` and `invalidated_by_commit_id` are NEW NULLABLE COLUMNS. Nothing moves. Nothing is reshaped. No existing column changes meaning.** |

| **R244** | ⭐⭐⭐ **`X-121` splits: `X-121a` is ADDITIVE and ships in ONE deploy. `X-121b` is the seven-noun RECONCILIATION and keeps `§259`'s four.** |
| :--- | :--- |

| ⭐ **`X-121a`** | *add `state` and `invalidated_by_commit_id` to `facts`, both **NULLABLE**, plus the events `X-119` consumes.* **One deploy. No dual-write. No cycle of verification** |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **`X-121b`** | *reconcile `businesses` · `people` · `conversations` · `messages` · `jobs` · `reviews` · `facts` against the canonical shape, and create the five that are absent.* ⛔ **`§259` in full, and `jobs` still collides with Laravel's queue table** |

| **N-244-01** | ⛔ **A column added by `X-121a` must be NULLABLE with no default backfill.** *A `NOT NULL` column on a populated table is a lock and a rewrite — that IS `§259` territory* |
| :--- | :--- |
| **N-244-02** | ⭐ **`X-121a` writes the migration. `X-119` never does.** *Ownership does not soften because the owner is unbuilt* |
| **N-244-03** | ⚠️ ***`X-121a` is NOT `X-121` done.*** *`module:done X-121` stays failing until `X-121b` lands. **A partial module must not be able to report itself complete*** |

## 264V.2 ⭐ WHAT THIS COSTS AND SAVES
**Saves:** *`X-119` unblocks after a one-deploy additive change instead of waiting for a seven-table reconciliation.*
**Costs:** ⛔ **`X-121` now has two states, and the roster shows one module.** ⚠️ *That is a real bookkeeping risk — **a half-built spine module that looks like a whole one is exactly the "claimed but not applied" shape this ledger is full of***, which is why `N-244-03` exists.

**CHECKED:** `§259`'s four deploys read directly — they govern dual-write and read-switching, neither of which an additive nullable column requires · `facts` confirmed to lack both columns from the owner's own dump · the agent's two `UNRESOLVED` reports quoted verbatim.
**FAILS IF:** ⚠️ **the anchor needs `state` to be constrained** *(an enum, a check constraint, `NOT NULL` with a default)*. ⛔ **Then it is not additive, it is a rewrite of a populated table, and `§259` applies after all.** ⭐ *Nullable text, validated in the model, is the version that stays additive.*
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** whether `X-121a`/`X-121b` is a real split or a way of declaring victory early. ⚠️ *I am introducing a second identity for a module to unblock a dependency — **and the honest name for that is scope-cutting.*** ⭐⭐ **`N-244-03` is the guard: `X-121` cannot report done until both land. If that guard is ever relaxed, this ruling becomes the excuse it currently is not.**

# 264U. ⭐⭐⭐⭐ R242 — **ONE MODULE, ONE DIRECTORY. THE HYPHEN STAYS.** *(2026-08-28)*

**The first module to receive CODE exposed a conflict that had been latent for the whole programme.**

> **A PHP namespace cannot contain a hyphen.** *`namespace App\Modules\X-126\Gate;` is a **parse error**, and PSR-4 maps namespace segments onto directory names — so `app/Modules/X-126/` can never hold autoloaded code.*

**The agent hit this and solved it the only way PSR-4 allows:**
```
mkdir -p app/Modules/X126 && mv app/Modules/X-126/Gate app/Modules/X126/Gate
```

⛔⛔⛔ **Which SPLIT the module in two:**
| `app/Modules/X-126/` | `manifest.php` · `capabilities.php` | **the DATA** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `app/Modules/X126/` | `Gate/StrictCapabilityGate.php` | **the CODE** |

⭐⭐ **And every gate looks in `app/Modules/{id}` — WITH the hyphen.** *`BUILT`, `CONTENT`, `DASHBOARD`, and `impact` all point at the data half.* ⛔ **The code became invisible to the checks that must approve it.**

## 264U.1 THE RULING
| **R242** | ⭐⭐⭐ **The module directory is `app/Modules/<id>/` — hyphen included — and it holds BOTH the manifest and the code. PHP classes inside it are autoloaded by CLASSMAP, not PSR-4.** |
| :--- | :--- |

```json
"autoload": { "classmap": ["app/Modules/"] }
```

⭐ **A classmap scans files and records what class each one declares. It has NO naming constraint** — *the directory may be called anything, including `X-126`.*

| **N-242-01** | ⭐ **The namespace inside is the id WITHOUT the hyphen:** `App\Modules\X126\Gate` in `app/Modules/X-126/Gate/`. *The classmap does not require them to match, and the id stays legible in both* |
| :--- | :--- |
| **N-242-02** | ⛔⛔ **`app/Modules/<id-without-hyphen>/` must not exist.** *A module in two directories is a module half the checks cannot see* |
| **N-242-03** | ⛔ **`composer dump-autoload` after adding a class.** *A classmap is built, not resolved at runtime — a new class is invisible until the map is rebuilt* |
| **N-242-04** | ⚠️ *`doctor` REPORTS a split module by name.* **The failure that hid here was silence, not error** |

## 264U.2 ⚠️ THE COST, STATED
**Classmap is slightly slower to build than PSR-4 and must be regenerated when files are added.** ⭐ *In exchange, the roster id stays the directory name across all 124 modules — and `impact`, `brief`, `module:done` and `context` all keep working off one path.*

⛔ **The alternative — renaming every directory to `X126` — would break the id in `manifest.php`, in the roster, in `evidence/`, in every capability row and in every ruling that names a module.** *The hyphen is load-bearing everywhere except PHP, so PHP is where the exception belongs.*

**CHECKED:** the split reproduced from the owner's own session log *(`mv app/Modules/X-126/Gate app/Modules/X126/Gate`)* · `ModuleDoneCommand`'s `BUILT` and `CONTENT` gates confirmed to read `base_path("app/Modules/{$id}")` with the hyphen · no module carried PHP before today, which is why this was latent.
**FAILS IF:** ⚠️ **the tree already has PSR-4 rules for `App\Modules\`.** *Then classmap and PSR-4 both claim the path and composer resolves PSR-4 first.* ⛔ **Check `composer.json` before adding the classmap line.**
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** whether a classmap over 124 module directories slows `dump-autoload` enough to notice. ⚠️ *The tree already autoloads 13,218 classes, so the marginal cost is probably small — **but I have not measured it, and "probably small" is how the queue driver got chosen too.***

# 264S. ⭐⭐⭐⭐ R239 · R240 · R241 — **THE FOUR DECISIONS, RATIFIED** *(owner, 2026-08-28)*

## 264S.1 ⭐⭐ R239 — THE AI CORE HAS THREE HOMES, NOT ONE
**`R237`/`R238` require seven tables and `C-Ai` owned none of them. `C-Ai` already carries cost routing, token arbitrage, the provider waterfall, latency guardrails and prompt caching — ten tables plus all that is not a module, it is a subsystem with one name.**

| **R239** | ⭐⭐⭐ **`X-219 AiRouter` owns WHO SERVES WHAT · `X-220 PromptRegistry` owns the PROMPT LIFECYCLE · `C-Ai` keeps THE CALL and everything that happens ON it.** |
| :--- | :--- |

| `X-219` | `ai_providers · ai_models · ai_module_assignments` | *`R237`'s open roster and the PRIMARY/BACKUP/COMPLEX assignment* |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `X-220` | `ai_prompts · golden_sets` | ⭐ **`N-238-18`: a golden set is versioned WITH the prompt** — one concern, one module |
| `C-Ai` **+** | `redaction_tokens · injection_refusals` | ⭐⭐ *`R238` steps ④ and ⑧ happen ON the call, and **its whole point is ONE PATH*** |

| **N-239-01** | ⛔ **A module NEVER queries `ai_models` or `ai_module_assignments` directly.** *It calls `C-Ai`, which asks `X-219`* |
| :--- | :--- |
| **N-239-02** | ⛔⛔ **Redaction may not move out of `C-Ai`.** *Splitting step ④ from ⑤–⑨ creates the second entrance `R238` forbids* |

## 264S.2 ⭐⭐⭐ R240 — A REFUSAL IS REQUIRED ONLY WHERE REFUSAL IS POSSIBLE
**`LAW 128`'s floor demanded `id + assertion + refusal` on all 966 capability rows. `doctor` reported 1,519 violations. The two options on the table were "write 1,294 refusals" or "lower the floor". Both were wrong.**

> ⭐⭐⭐ **A refusal is only meaningful where the capability CAN refuse.** *"List the tenant's invoices" has none. **"Quote a price" has `NO_FACT`. "Send outward" has consent, cadence and quiet hours. "Spend money" has the ceiling.***

| **R240** | ⭐⭐ **A capability MUST declare a refusal if it ① SENDS OUTWARD · ② SPENDS OR MOVES MONEY · ③ ANSWERS WITH A FACT · ④ TAKES AN IRREVERSIBLE ACTION. Otherwise `id + assertion` is the floor.** |
| :--- | :--- |

⭐ **COUNTED, not estimated:** *966 rows → **322 meet a test (33%)**, 644 need only `id + assertion`.*
⛔ **322, not 1,294.** *A blanket requirement produces 1,294 rows of `"refuses: n/a"` — **noise that teaches people to write `n/a` everywhere, including where it matters.***

| **N-240-01** | ⛔ **`CapabilityStage` applies the four tests before demanding a refusal** |
| :--- | :--- |
| **N-240-02** | ⚠️ *the four tests are matched on the capability's own text.* ⛔ **A capability whose wording does not reveal what it does will pass this check wrongly — and that is a WRITING problem, not a checker problem** |

## 264S.3 ⛔⛔⛔ R241 — `X-121` IS A MIGRATION, AND BATCH 1 CHANGES
> **Owner-confirmed: `businesses` · `people` · `conversations` ALREADY EXIST in the live database.**

**`X-121` owns all twelve canonical nouns. It is not a build.**

| **R241** | ⭐⭐⭐ **`X-121` is a MIGRATION under `§259` — four deploys, never compressed. It is REMOVED from batch 1 and becomes its own project.** |
| :--- | :--- |

⛔⛔ **Leading batch 1 with a migration measures RECONCILIATION. Phase 10 is 122 CONSTRUCTIONS** — *the first measurement must resemble the work it predicts.*

| ⭐ **BATCH 1, REVISED** | **`X-126` CapabilityGate → `X-119` FactRegistry → `X-188` NumberPool** |
| :--- | :--- |
| *checked* | **none of the three owns a canonical noun** — all clean builds. ⭐ *`X-188` owns `number_pool`, NOT `numbers`; I had assumed a migration and was wrong* |

## 264S.4 ⛔⛔⛔ THE QUEUE — A BLOCKER ABOVE ALL THREE
> **`QUEUE_CONNECTION=database` ✅ · workers running: **ZERO** ⛔**

⭐⭐⭐ **`database` with no worker is WORSE than `sync`.** *On `sync` the work happens inline and you get a slow but WORKING system. On `database` with no worker it **silently accumulates in a table and nothing tells you.*** ⛔ **That is `M-95` exactly.**

| **N-241-01** | ⛔⛔ **No module is built until a worker is running.** *`deploy/supervisor.conf` shipped in the runtime bundle and was never installed* |
| :--- | :--- |

**CHECKED:** `X-121`'s `@owns_table` read directly — twelve canonical nouns, three confirmed present in the live DB · `X-126`/`X-119`/`X-188` checked against the same list, none matching · the 322 counted from the tracker across four regex tests · `C-Ai`'s three current tables confirmed.
**FAILS IF:** ⚠️ **`capability_policies`, `fact_sources` or `number_pool` already exist.** *Then the revised batch 1 has the same defect as the original.* ⛔ **The full table list settles it and has not yet been read.**
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** `N-240-02`. ⚠️ *The four tests match on a capability's own wording, so **a badly-worded capability passes wrongly.*** ⭐ *That is a writing problem this ruling cannot fix — and 644 rows now escape the refusal requirement on the strength of their prose.*

# 264R. ⭐⭐⭐⭐ R238 — **THE AI CORE. ONE CALL PATH, NO SECOND ENTRANCE.** *(owner, 2026-08-27)*

> **Owner: *"Think of everything we need in the AI core — god-tier. This is the whole brain of the entire system."***

⭐⭐ **Measured first: all twelve AI concerns are already NAMED in the plan.** ⛔⛔ **SIX are PROSE ONLY, owned by no module:** *prompt versioning · PII redaction · prompt-injection defence · tool/function calling · model deprecation · **requested-vs-served**.* *Two more live outside the AI layer — evals in `X-148`/`X-149`, streaming in `X-125`/`X-194`.*

> ⭐⭐⭐ **The gap was never features. The brain is scattered across seven modules with no single contract — and the six unowned pieces are exactly the ones that make the other six MEASURABLE.**

| **R238** | ⭐⭐⭐ **Every AI call from every module goes through ONE path in `C-Ai`. There is no second way in.** *`gate → budget → assemble → redact → cache → route → call → validate → record → learn`* |
| :--- | :--- |

## 264R.1 THE SIX THAT WERE OWNED BY NOBODY
| ⭐⭐⭐ **`model_requested` AND `model_served`** | *`§177` found this and nothing acted on it.* ⛔⛔ **Without both columns a silent fallback attributes the BACKUP's output to the PRIMARY — so every eval, every cost report and every model comparison is measuring the wrong thing** *(`N-238-02`)* |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **prompt versioning** | *a prompt is a ROW.* ⛔ **A prompt edited in code is an experiment nobody can reproduce and a regression nobody can bisect** *(`N-238-03/04`)* |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **PII redaction** | *before the vendor call, never after the response.* ⭐ **A `self_hosted` model may skip it — and that is the ONLY exemption, and the strongest argument for self-hosting at all** *(`N-238-05/06/07`)* |
| ⭐⭐ **prompt injection** | ⛔⛔ *this platform reads **scraped sites, inbound email, reviews and uploaded files** — every one is attacker-controlled text reaching a model.* **A tool call originating from untrusted content is REFUSED, and logged as an ATTACK, not an error** *(`N-238-08/09/10`)* |
| ⭐ **tool calling** | *tools are GENERATED from the manifests* (`@provides` + `@agent_reachable`) — ⛔ **never hand-written per prompt, or the model's idea of the platform drifts from the platform** *(`N-238-11/12`)* |
| ⭐ **model deprecation** | *`deprecates_at` on every row;* ⛔⛔ **a sunset model in a PRIMARY slot with no BACKUP fails `doctor`** — *the outage is scheduled months ahead, which makes ignoring it a choice* *(`N-238-13/14`)* |

## 264R.2 ⭐⭐ THE RULE THAT MAKES `R237`'s OPEN ROSTER SAFE
| **N-238-19** | ⛔⛔⛔ **A model may not be promoted into a PRIMARY slot without passing the golden set for that job class.** ⭐⭐⭐ *Otherwise "any model, any vendor" means **"any quality, discovered in production."*** |
| :--- | :--- |

## 264R.3 ⭐ RELIABILITY AND ECONOMICS
| **retry** | ⛔ *only on 429/5xx/timeout.* **Never on a refusal — retrying a `NO_FACT` spends money to be told no again** |
| :--- | :--- |
| **circuit breaker** | ⭐⭐ *per PROVIDER, not per model* (`R237`) · ⛔ **an open breaker is a VISIBLE STATE** — *silent degradation is how you learn from the invoice that the primary has been down a week* |
| **cache** | ⭐ *a semantic hit records its **DISTANCE*** — ⛔ *"close enough" without saying how close is a correctness bug wearing a performance costume* |
| **budget** | ⛔⛔ **REFUSE, never truncate** — *a silently shortened context produces a confident wrong answer, which costs more than the refusal.* ⭐ **A PLATFORM ceiling as well as a tenant one, because one tenant's loop can spend everyone's money** |
| **N-238-17** | ⭐⭐ **cost attributed to MODULE and TENANT on every call** — *without it gap `E3` is unanswerable and you cannot price the product* |

## 264R.4 ⛔ WHAT THE CORE MUST NOT DO
**Decide policy** *(`X-126` gates, `X-204` consents, `X-202` escalates — the core ROUTES and RECORDS)* · **own a prompt's meaning** *(`C-Agent` owns behaviour)* · ⛔⛔ **have a second entrance.**

⭐ **Full specification: `GOAIEZ-AI-CORE.md`.**

**CHECKED:** twelve concerns measured against all 122 module headers — 6 owned, 2 owned outside the AI layer, 6 prose-only · `C-Ai` confirmed owning `ai_calls · ai_tasks · ai_provider_accounts` with cost routing, token arbitrage, provider waterfall, latency guardrails and prompt caching already in its header · `§177`'s requested-vs-served finding quoted verbatim.
**FAILS IF:** ⚠️⚠️ **the ten-step path becomes ten seconds of latency.** *On a 2-second classify call the overhead can exceed the work.* ⛔ **Gate, budget and cache must be sub-10ms LOCAL lookups** — *if they are not, the core becomes the thing every module wants to bypass, and that is how the second entrance gets built.*
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** the redaction boundary. ⚠️ *Token-swapping a phone number is easy; **a name in conversational context is not**, and over-redacting destroys the context the model needs.* ⭐ *Written as mandatory with a `self_hosted` exemption — which makes self-hosting the honest answer for the most sensitive job classes, **but that is a cost decision I have not made for the owner.***

# 264Q. ⭐⭐⭐⭐ R237 — **EVERY MODEL, ANY VENDOR, ASSIGNED PER MODULE** *(owner, 2026-08-27)*

> **Owner: *"We never hardcode any AI. The system needs to support ALL models — Grok, Gemma, DeepSeek, ChatGPT, Claude, local self-hosted, anything we choose. And we can designate different AI models for different modules — primary and backup, and complex models for complex things."***

⭐⭐ **`P-194`'s OPEN ROSTER LAW already made the roster a TABLE — `ai_models` and `ai_providers`, WAVE-0 spine.** *`R237` extends it: the roster is open, and **so is the ASSIGNMENT.***

## 264Q.1 THE RULING
| **R237** | ⭐⭐⭐ **Any model from any vendor, including SELF-HOSTED, is a ROW. And every module names its own PRIMARY, BACKUP and COMPLEX model — per module, per job class, changeable without a deploy.** |
| :--- | :--- |

## 264Q.2 ⭐⭐ THE THREE SLOTS, AND WHY THREE
| ⭐ **PRIMARY** | *what runs.* **Chosen for cost and latency on the ordinary case** |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **BACKUP** | ⛔ *what runs when the primary is down, rate-limited, or times out.* **A different VENDOR, not a different model from the same one** — *a vendor outage takes every model it serves* |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **COMPLEX** | *what runs when the job is hard.* **`X-126`'s gate or the module decides; the ROUTE is a row, not a branch in code** |

⛔ **Three, not two, because "cheap by default, expensive when it matters" is the whole economics of this platform.** *A single model per module either overpays on every trivial call or fails the hard ones.*

## 264Q.3 THE SCHEMA — `C-Ai` OWNS IT
| `ai_providers` | *vendor · base url · auth style · **`self_hosted` boolean** · health* — ⭐ **a local Ollama or vLLM endpoint is a row like any other** |
| :--- | :--- |
| `ai_models` | *provider · vendor string · job classes it may serve · rank per class · price in · price out · context window · **vision/tool/json capability flags*** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **`ai_module_assignments`** | ***module_id · job_class · slot (`PRIMARY`/`BACKUP`/`COMPLEX`) · model_id*** — **the new table `R237` requires** |

| **N-237-01** | ⛔⛔ **No model string in code, ever.** *`BoundaryStage` fails the build on `gpt-`, `claude-`, `gemini-`, `grok-`, `deepseek-`, `gemma-`, `llama-`, `mistral-`, `qwen-` in any file outside a seeder* |
| :--- | :--- |
| **N-237-02** | ⭐ **A module resolves its model through `C-Ai`, never by name.** *`$ai->for($moduleId, $jobClass, $slot)` — the module does not know what it is talking to* |
| **N-237-03** | ⛔ **BACKUP must be a DIFFERENT PROVIDER than PRIMARY.** *`doctor` fails an assignment where both point at the same vendor — **that is not a fallback, it is the same outage twice*** |
| **N-237-04** | ⭐⭐ **Every call records `model_requested` AND `model_served`.** *`§177`: without both columns **every model comparison you ever run is invalid**, because a silent fallback attributes the backup's output to the primary* |
| **N-237-05** | ⭐ **Adding a vendor is a ROW.** *No enum edit, no deploy. `§176` measured the old way: **7 code edits and a deploy to add one model**, with Gemini, Grok, Gemma and Luna absent from the code entirely* |
| **N-237-06** | ⭐⭐⭐ **A self-hosted model is a first-class row** — *base url, no vendor key, `self_hosted = true`.* ⛔ **Nothing in the routing may assume a commercial API** |

## 264Q.4 ⛔ AND THE ENUM THAT STARTED THIS
**`doctor`'s first real run found `Enums/AiModel.php` hardcoding `gpt-4` and `gpt-5`.** ⭐⭐ **That enum is exactly what `P-194` overruled and `R237` now finishes:** *the file becomes a SEEDER for `ai_models`, or it goes.* ⚠️ *The owner's note is worth recording — **it was probably written when there was one model and it was the only one** — but the platform is not that platform.*

**CHECKED:** `P-194` located and read verbatim *("the model roster is an ENUM, not a table — 7 code edits + a deploy to add one model · Gemini · Grok · Gemma · Luna absent from the code entirely · prices in a match")* · `ai_models` and `ai_providers` confirmed as declared WAVE-0 spine tables · `C-Ai` confirmed as owner of `ai_calls · ai_tasks · ai_provider_accounts` · `§177`'s requested-vs-served finding read.
**FAILS IF:** ⚠️⚠️ **the COMPLEX slot becomes a way to route everything to the expensive model.** *Nothing in this ruling caps it.* ⛔ **`C-Ai` already owns cost routing and token arbitrage — the complex slot must sit UNDER that ceiling, not beside it**, or the unit economics gap (`E3`) gets worse, not better.
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** who decides a job is "complex". ⚠️ *I have written it as **the module or `X-126`'s gate**, but a per-job-class heuristic that is wrong in either direction is expensive — **too eager and you overpay on everything; too shy and the hard jobs fail quietly.*** ⭐ **This is an owner decision I have not made for you.**

# 264P. ⭐⭐⭐⭐ R236 — **THE ONLY LEGITIMATE OFF STATE IS *NOT YET SET UP*** *(owner, 2026-08-27)*

> **Owner: *"Not all should be on with autopilot **unless it has not yet been set up**."***

⭐⭐⭐ **`R235` says every autopilot ships ON. `R236` names the ONE exception, and it is not an exception to the premise — it is the ONLY honest reason a lane can be dark.**

## 264P.1 THE THREE STATES, AND ONLY THREE
| ⭐ **`ON`** | **the default.** *The autopilot is running. Nothing was switched on to get here* |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **`NOT_CONFIGURED`** | ⛔ **the lane cannot physically run yet** — *no carrier number, no connected inbox, no gateway credential, no crawled site.* **NOT a permission problem. A CAPABILITY problem** |
| ⭐ **`OFF_BY_CLIENT`** | *the client switched it off. **Their choice, their switch, reversible in one tap*** |

⛔⛔⛔ **THERE IS NO FOURTH STATE. `AWAITING_APPROVAL`, `PENDING_ENABLE`, `PROPOSE_ONLY` and every synonym are FORBIDDEN — `doctor` fails the build on any of them.**

## 264P.2 ⭐⭐ `NOT_CONFIGURED` IS A JOB FOR THE AI, NOT A SCREEN FOR THE CLIENT
> **Owner, `R235`: *"the AI shows them how to set it up."***

| **N-236-01** | ⛔ **`NOT_CONFIGURED` is a state the AI is actively WORKING TO LEAVE.** *It is not a resting place and not a queue* |
| :--- | :--- |
| **N-236-02** | ⭐⭐⭐ **The assistant ASKS FOR THE ONE MISSING THING, in conversation, at the moment it needs it** — *"I can start posting to your Google profile — connect it here?"* ⛔ **Never a settings page with fourteen empty fields** |
| **N-236-03** | ⭐ **A lane in `NOT_CONFIGURED` for more than one cycle RAISES.** *`R219`: a broken capability is REPORTED, loudly, to a human — **a lane silently dark for a month is the failure this platform exists to prevent*** |
| **N-236-04** | ⛔⛔ **`NOT_CONFIGURED` may NEVER be the shipped state of something that CAN run.** *If the two `P-207` fields are enough to start, it starts* |
| **N-236-05** | ⭐ **The tenant is never BLOCKED by it.** *Every other lane keeps running while one waits for a credential — **the same rule as `R21`'s latch: one thread, never the platform*** |

## 264P.3 ⭐ WHAT THIS MEANS CONCRETELY
| a missed-call text-back | ⭐ **`ON` at signup** — *`P-207`'s two fields are all it needs* |
| :--- | :--- |
| GBP posting | ⚠️ **`NOT_CONFIGURED` until the profile is connected** — *and the AI asks for it the first time it has something worth posting* |
| physical mail *(`X-208`)* | ⚠️ **`NOT_CONFIGURED` until the tenant supplies the Lob key** *(BYOK)* — ⛔ **not because mail needs approval** |
| the surcharge *(`X-214`)* | ⚠️ **`NOT_CONFIGURED` until a rate is set** — ⭐ *then `ON`, with the irreversible charge confirming per `P-096`* |

**CHECKED:** all 122 headers swept for stale-posture language after `R235` — **89 assertions struck across 73 modules** *(`escalates and PROPOSES` 15 · `never set` 53 · `EARNED` 12 · `L1 FOREVER` 9)*; **0 remain**.
**FAILS IF:** ⚠️ **`NOT_CONFIGURED` becomes the new `L1`.** *A team under pressure will mark a lane "not configured" to avoid turning it on.* ⛔⛔ **`N-236-03` is the guard — a lane dark for more than one cycle RAISES — and it is the assertion most likely to be quietly dropped.**
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** the boundary between "cannot run" and "runs badly without config". ⚠️ *A review-request lane CAN send with no review link — it just sends a worse message.* ⭐ **The rule I have applied: if it can act at all, it is `ON`. `NOT_CONFIGURED` means PHYSICALLY IMPOSSIBLE, not SUBOPTIMAL.**

# 264O. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ R235 — **EVERY AUTOPILOT SHIPS ON. THE AI WATCHES THE AI.** *(owner, 2026-08-27 — OVERRULES the L1 default)*

> **Owner, verbatim: *"Overruled. ALL AI ON, by my law. The client can turn it off if they want. ALL AUTOPILOTS ON, with AI watching them, and the AI shows them how to set it up. Make sure this is NEVER OVERRULED AGAIN."***

⛔⛔⛔⛔ **THIS OVERRULES `§227.2`'s `L1 PROPOSE` DEFAULT, THE "EARNED LADDER" AS A SHIPPING POSTURE, AND EVERY `L1 FOREVER` EXEMPTION. NO FUTURE TURN MAY REINSTATE A `PROPOSE`-BY-DEFAULT POSTURE. IF A LATER SECTION APPEARS TO, IT IS WRONG AND THIS SECTION WINS.**

## 264O.1 THE RULING
| **R235** | ⭐⭐⭐ **EVERY MODULE SHIPS AT ITS CEILING. The autopilot is ON at signup, on every lane, for every tenant. A client may switch any lane OFF. Nothing waits to be switched ON, and nothing "earns" the right to act.** |
| :--- | :--- |

**What replaces the ladder-as-shipping-posture:**
| ⛔ **GONE** | *`ships: L1` → the tenant approves → it EARNS `L2` over N clean runs* |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **NOW** | ***`ships:` = `ceiling:`. It acts from minute one.*** *The ladder survives ONLY as a description of what an action IS, never as a gate on when it may run* |

## 264O.2 ⭐⭐⭐ THE SAFETY LAYER IS **AI WATCHING AI**, NOT A HUMAN APPROVING
> **Owner: *"all autopilots on, with AI watching them."***

⛔ **This is the part that makes `R235` safe, and it is not a slogan — it is four mechanisms that already exist:**
| ⭐ **`X-126` the capability gate** | ***no grounding Fact → no skill.*** *An agent skill invoked without grounding is REFUSED with `NO_FACT` — **the autopilot cannot invent a price, a time or a link*** |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **`X-213` VisionQA** | *a vision model checks tenant-facing output **at runtime, against a checklist** — and every check stores its artifact* |
| ⭐ **the refusal path** | *`P-092`: a price is **looked up or REFUSED**, never generated* |
| ⭐⭐ **`X-202` ApprovalDesk** | ⛔ **NO LONGER THE DEFAULT ROUTE.** *It is where an autopilot escalates when the AI ITSELF cannot proceed — **the exception, not the gate*** |

| **N-235-01** | ⛔⛔ **`ships:` MUST EQUAL `ceiling:` on every module.** *`doctor` FAILS the build on any module where they differ* |
| :--- | :--- |
| **N-235-02** | ⭐ **Every lane carries an OFF switch the client owns.** *`doctor` fails a lane with no off-switch — **the client's control is the safety valve, and it must exist*** |
| **N-235-03** | ⛔ **No module may ship requiring the client to turn it ON.** *There is no "enable" step in any wizard* |
| **N-235-04** | ⭐⭐⭐ **Every autopilot is SUPERVISED by `X-126`'s gate.** *An action reaching a customer without passing `capability.decided` is a build failure — **that is what "AI watching AI" means mechanically*** |
| **N-235-05** | ⭐ **The AI SHOWS THE CLIENT HOW TO SET IT UP.** *Setup is a conversation the assistant runs, never a form the client fills. `P-207`'s two fields are the ONLY thing ever asked* |

## 264O.3 ⛔ WHAT `P-096`'s IRREVERSIBLE CARVE-OUT NOW MEANS
**`P-096`/`D5` said the assistant ASKS on anything irreversible.** ⭐⭐ **That survives — but it is a PER-ACTION confirmation at the moment of acting, NOT a shipping posture.**
| ⭐ *"charge this card"* | the autopilot runs; **the irreversible STEP confirms** |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔ *"this whole module ships at L1 because it touches money"* | **OVERRULED.** *The module ships ON; the irreversible action inside it confirms* |

**CHECKED:** the ships→ceiling distribution measured across all 122 before any edit — **95 modules ship BELOW their ceiling, 8 sit at `L1`→`L1`** · the four supervision mechanisms confirmed present *(`X-126` in 11 modules, refusal path in 43, `X-213`, `X-202` in 9)*.
**FAILS IF:** ⚠️ **the supervision layer is thinner than the autonomy it now guards.** *`X-126`'s gate is referenced by ELEVEN modules and `R235` turns on ONE HUNDRED AND TWO.* ⛔⛔ **`N-235-04` is therefore the load-bearing assertion of this ruling — it must be wired everywhere, and `doctor` must fail without it.**
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** nothing about the ruling — it is the owner's law and it is now recorded three times over. ⚠️ *My one flag is the sequencing above: **turn the autopilots on and wire `X-126` in the same wave**, not in successive ones.*

# 264N. ⭐⭐⭐⭐ R234 — **THE FOUNDING PREMISE. THE AI IS ALWAYS ON.** *(owner, 2026-08-27)*

> **Owner, verbatim: *"It's the other way around. If AI can't handle it, a human takes over. **AI is always on, handling everything, unless turned off by the client on certain things.** AI and autopilot is the whole purpose of the platform — humans use it so they DON'T have to do anything, or as little as possible. The platform is there to run their business AND generate business for them — viral marketing, SEO, and all the other stuff it's designed to do."***

⛔⛔⛔ **THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LAW IN THE PACKAGE AND IT MUST NEVER BE FORGOTTEN. Every other law is a fence around it. If a decision would make a tenant do MORE work, it is wrong by default.**

## 264N.1 THE RULING
| **R234** | ⭐⭐⭐ **THE AI IS THE DEFAULT OPERATOR OF THE BUSINESS. It is ON, handling everything, from minute one. A HUMAN is the EXCEPTION PATH — invoked when the AI CANNOT handle something, never as the normal route. A tenant may turn specific things OFF; nothing requires them to turn anything ON.** |
| :--- | :--- |

**The direction of every default, stated so it cannot be misread:**
| ⛔ **NOT** | *"the AI proposes and a human approves"* — **that is a tenant doing work** |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **BUT** | ***the AI ACTS; a human is notified, can undo, and can switch a lane off*** |
| ⛔ **NOT** | *"a human takes over and the AI stops until released"* |
| ⭐⭐ **BUT** | ***a human takes over ONE THREAD because the AI could not handle THAT thread. Everything else keeps running.*** |

## 264N.2 ⛔⛔ `R21` IS INVERTED AND IS HEREBY CORRECTED
**`R21` read: *"a human takes over → the AI produces nothing on that thread until released."*** ⭐ *The mechanism is right — a takeover latch must exist, or the AI and the human talk over each other.* ⛔⛔ **The FRAMING was backwards: it read as though human control is the resting state and AI action is the interruption.**

| ⭐ **`R21`, corrected** | **The latch is SCOPED TO ONE THREAD and is an EXCEPTION.** *A human taking over a conversation silences the AI **on that conversation only, until released.*** ⛔⛔ **It NEVER pauses the agent, the campaigns, the SEO, the review asks, the outreach or anything else. The platform keeps running the business.** |
| :--- | :--- |

## 264N.3 ⭐⭐ WHAT R234 REQUIRES OF EVERY MODULE
| **N-234-01** | ⛔ **No module may ship in a state that requires a tenant to enable it before it does its job.** *If it needs configuration to function, the wizard's two fields must be enough to start, and it starts.* |
| :--- | :--- |
| **N-234-02** | ⭐ **Every OFF switch is a TENANT choice, never a default.** *`doctor` fails a module whose autopilot defaults to disabled without a law naming the reason* |
| **N-234-03** | ⛔⛔ **"Review first" is a per-lane TOGGLE the tenant sets** *(`P-096`)* — **not the shipped state** |
| **N-234-04** | ⭐⭐⭐ **A human is never REQUIRED for a reversible action.** *`P-096` already governs the exceptions: preview always · one-tap undo on reversible · explicit confirmation on terminal · **the assistant ASKS on anything irreversible (`D5`)**. Those are the ONLY reasons to involve a person* |
| **N-234-05** | ⛔ **The measure of a feature is WORK REMOVED from the tenant.** *A feature that adds a screen the tenant must visit daily has failed, however well it works* |

## 264N.4 ⭐ `P-096` ALREADY SAID THIS — R234 MAKES IT THE PREMISE
**`P-096`: *"Automatic by default (R30/R54) — replies, agent, review asks, posts, sends, digests, top-ups, renewals — with ONE per-tenant 'Review first' toggle per lane."*** ⭐⭐ **The law existed; what was missing was its STATUS.** *`R234` makes it the thing every other decision is measured against, rather than one law among two hundred.*

**CHECKED:** `P-096` read verbatim and found to already state "automatic by default" · `R21`'s definition row read in full · the ladder distribution measured — **56 modules ship `L1`, 47 ship `L2`, 19 `n/a`** · `§227.2`'s intent→ladder mapping confirmed as the source of the `L1` defaults.
**FAILS IF:** ⚠️⚠️ **`L1` means "asks the tenant" for a customer-facing lane.** *`§227.2` maps `GROW`→`L1 PROPOSE`, and **56 modules ship there.*** ⛔ **If `L1` on a GROW module means a tenant must approve outreach, that is `R234` violated 56 times** — *see the open item below; this needs the owner, and it is the single largest question `R234` raises.*
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** whether `L1` for `GROW` is a deliberate safety choice *(don't let the AI cold-contact strangers unsupervised on day one)* or an accident of the intent mapping. ⚠️ **Both readings are defensible and they lead to opposite builds.**

# 264F2. ⭐⭐⭐ THE GO-AI-MARKETING SCOPE — §5 ALREADY DECIDED THE ARCHITECTURE, AND IT IS STALE *(2026-08-27)*

⛔⛔ **BEFORE THE 10-TURN SPRINT SPECS ANYTHING, A PRIOR RULING GOVERNS IT — AND I ALMOST MISSED IT AGAIN.**

**The owner asked for "a separate full marketing and AI core just for Go AI EZ — its own SEO, pixel, identity graph, GBP, reviews, social, CRM, staff desk, support — think all the features of the platform."** ⭐ *Measured: that would MIRROR ALL 13 FEATURE DOMAINS and roughly DOUBLE a 119-module platform.*

## 264F2.1 ⭐⭐⭐ BUT §5 AND `X-127 TenantZero` ALREADY EXIST — RULED **LIVE AT T530**
> **§5's law, verbatim:** ***"GO AI EZ is tenant #0 on its own platform. Not a copy. Not a staging clone. The same code, the same database, the same modules."***
> **`X-127 TenantZero`:** ***"GO AI EZ runs on GOAIEZ, same code, same database; nothing is built for marketing alone."***

⛔⛔⛔ **§5's LAW 1 DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS "a separate marketing codebase":** ***"Nothing is built for marketing alone. If we need a growth tool, it ships as a module. THERE IS NO MARKETING CODEBASE."***

⭐ **§5 already maps 14 needs to existing modules** — *find businesses → `X-16` · reach them → `X-105` · by form → `X-109` · demo → the demo engine · bill → the billing spine — **"every row is one build serving two customers."***

## 264F2.2 ⛔ SO THERE IS A REAL CONTRADICTION, AND IT IS AN OWNER DECISION
| **The owner just said** | *"SEPARATE full marketing and AI core just for Go AI EZ"* |
| :--- | :--- |
| **§5 (LIVE at T530) says** | *"the SAME code, the same modules — there is NO separate marketing codebase"* |

⚠️⚠️ **These cannot both stand.** *This is exactly the kind of collision that, left unreconciled, produces a duplicate half-platform nobody maintains.* ⛔ **I am NOT choosing between them — the owner does.**

### THREE OPTIONS, WITH THE TRADE-OFF NAMED
| **A · TENANT-ZERO (what §5 rules today)** | Go AI EZ IS tenant #0. It gets its OWN GBP, reviews, SEO, pixel, social, CRM, staff desk — **by being a tenant of the platform that already has all of them.** ⭐ **Net-new = only what a tenant does NOT have: the master control plane, cross-tenant outreach at scale, affiliate/influencer RECRUITMENT, the acquisition funnel.** *~3–6 new modules. Dogfooding is free QA at production scale.* |

## 264H.1 ⛔⛔ THE DEFECT, MEASURED — IDENTITY RESOLUTION IS SPLIT ACROSS THREE MODULES
| `X-110` **`Pixel`** | *the 14 KB smart pixel · 16-type event schema · cross-domain · session replay · heatmaps · bot fingerprinting · exit-intent* | **owns `pixel_events` · `visits` · `sessions` · `cwv_samples`** |

| `X-134` **`WaterfallEnrichment`** | *waterfall enrichment · **identity resolution** · de-duplication* | ⛔ **owns `identity_links`** |

⛔⛔⛔ **THREE modules claim "identity resolution" and TWO own competing link tables — `person_links` *(X-132)* and `identity_links` *(X-134)*.** ⭐ *That is the same person, resolved twice, in two tables, by two modules — **and it is exactly the collision `P-163` exists to prevent**, one level below the canonical nouns where nobody was checking.*

## 264H.2 THE RULING
| **R230** | ⭐⭐⭐ **`X-110` IS THE SPINE. The pixel and the identity graph are ONE module: `X-110` owns the observation AND the resolution.** |
| :--- | :--- |

**Ownership, settled:**
| ⭐ `X-110` **`Pixel`** *(renamed in role: the pixel + identity spine)* | **owns `pixel_events` · `visits` · `sessions` · `cwv_samples` · `identity_links`** — *the graph edge table MOVES here from `X-134`. **One person, one resolution, one owner.*** |
| :--- | :--- |
| `X-132` `PersonGraph` | ⭐ **keeps `person_links` + `resolution_evidence` as the SCORING and EVIDENCE layer** — *RFM, ICP, hidden-lead scoring — and **READS** the graph from `X-110` rather than resolving in parallel* |
| `X-134` `WaterfallEnrichment` | ⛔ **`identity_links` STRUCK from its `@owns_table`.** *It ENRICHES fields; it does not own identity. It **writes resolution candidates as evidence** and `X-110` decides* |

⛔ **`X-134` and `X-132` may no longer declare "identity resolution" as their own capability** — *they contribute evidence to `X-110`'s graph.* ⭐ *`P-163`'s principle, applied one level down: **the module that OWNS the noun does the resolving.***

**`X-110` serves the TENANT and GO AI EZ's own marketing from the same code, the same schema, the same graph.** ⛔ *Not two pixels. Not a second implementation.*

| **N-110-01** | ⭐ **every pixel event and identity edge is TENANT-SCOPED** — *`RLS FORCE`; a tenant resolves only visitors to **their own** properties* |
| :--- | :--- |
| **N-110-02** | ⭐⭐ **GO AI EZ's own properties are a tenant scope like any other** *(tenant-zero, `§5`)* — **the internal marketing system reads its graph through the SAME module, never a bypass** |
| **N-110-03** | ⛔⛔ **NO CROSS-TENANT RESOLUTION.** *A visitor seen on tenant A's site and tenant B's site is **TWO identities**. The platform-wide graph is not a product and is not sold — **the standing no-harvest ruling holds, and R230 does not weaken it*** |
| **N-110-04** | **the pixel feeds SEO/AEO, attribution, scoring and the demo site from ONE event stream** — *`@emits page.loaded` is `@ingress` (a browser), and every downstream consumer reads `X-110`, never its own tracker* |

# 264L. ⭐⭐ R230's SCHEMA MOVE — THE `§259` SEQUENCE, WRITTEN FOR WHOEVER APPLIES IT *(2026-08-27)*

**`R230` moves `identity_links` from `X-134` to `X-110`.** ⛔⛔ **That table has TWO LIVE WRITERS during the move, and `§259` forbids shipping a SWITCH and a CONTRACT change in one deploy.** *Doing it in one step is how a graph loses edges silently — **nothing errors, rows simply stop arriving.***

## THE FOUR DEPLOYS — IN THIS ORDER, NEVER COMPRESSED
| **① ADD, don't move** | `X-110` starts writing `identity_links` **alongside** `X-134`. *Both write. Nothing reads differently. **Reversible with a revert.*** |
| :--- | :--- |
| **② VERIFY EQUALITY** | ⭐⭐ *a job asserts every edge `X-134` writes also appears from `X-110`, **for a full business cycle** — not a sample.* ⛔ **A mismatch here is the whole reason for four deploys** |
| **③ SWITCH THE READ** | consumers read `X-110`'s edges. *`X-134` still writes — **so a fault is one config flip from recovered*** |
| **④ CONTRACT** | ⛔ **only now**: `X-134` stops writing and `identity_links` leaves its `@owns_table`. *`§259` — this is the irreversible step, and it ships ALONE* |

⛔ **`doctor` fails the build if ① and ④ appear in the same deploy.** ⭐ *`X-132`'s `person_links` is NOT part of this move — it stays as the scoring/evidence layer per `R230`.*

**CHECKED:** `R230` re-read to confirm exactly one table moves · `§259`'s rule confirmed as *no SWITCH and CONTRACT in one deploy* · `X-132` confirmed out of scope.
**FAILS IF:** step ② is sampled rather than exhaustive. ⚠️ ***Identity edges are long-tailed — the rare device is exactly the one a sample misses***, and a missing edge does not error, it just quietly fails to resolve a person.

# 264K. ⭐⭐⭐ R233 — THE SCOPE EDGE: `AGENCY` AND `GOAIEZ` ARE NOT THE SAME KIND OF THING *(2026-08-27)*

⛔⛔ **The sharpest open edge in `R232`, and it had to be settled before any code:**
> **An AGENCY sees its clients' data BY DESIGN. GO AI EZ must NOT see tenants' data.** *Same column, same table, **opposite rules** — and a single `issuer_scope` check treats them identically.*

## 264K.1 WHY A NAÏVE `issuer_scope` GETS THIS WRONG
*If the rule is "you see rows where `issuer_scope` matches your principal," then:*
| ⭐ an agency reading its client's campaign | **must SUCCEED** — that is the product |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⛔ GO AI EZ reading a tenant's campaign | **must FAIL** — that is a betrayal |

⛔⛔⛔ **Both are "a higher scope reading a lower one." The naïve check either permits both or forbids both, and each is catastrophic in a different direction.**

## 264K.2 THE RULING
| **R233** | ⭐⭐⭐ **`AGENCY` is a DELEGATED scope. `GOAIEZ` is a PEER scope. They are different KINDS, not different levels.** |
| :--- | :--- |

| ⭐ **`AGENCY` — delegated** | *An agency reads a client's rows **because the client granted it**, through an explicit, revocable, per-client relationship row.* ⛔ **The grant is DATA, not hierarchy** — remove the row and the access is gone the same instant |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐⭐ **`GOAIEZ` — peer** | *Go AI EZ is **tenant #0** (`§5`). It reads **its own rows and nothing else** — the same rights a plumber has over their own data.* ⛔⛔ **It is NOT above tenants in a hierarchy. It is BESIDE them** |

⭐⭐⭐ **That is why "different access level" was almost right and one word off: `AGENCY` is a different LEVEL; `GOAIEZ` is a different TENANT.**

| **N-233-01** | ⛔ **Agency access is a GRANT ROW, never a role string.** *`agency_client_grants`: agency · client · granted_at · revoked_at.* **No grant row, no access — asserted, not assumed** |
| :--- | :--- |
| **N-233-02** | ⛔⛔ **There is NO grant row whose grantee is `GOAIEZ`.** *`doctor` asserts the table cannot contain one; **the schema forbids the row that would make Go AI EZ a superuser*** |
| **N-233-03** | ⭐ **A revoked grant takes effect on the NEXT READ, not the next login.** *An agency removed at 14:03 cannot read a client row at 14:04 from a warm session* |
| **N-233-04** | ⭐⭐ **`GOAIEZ` scope is asserted EQUAL to a tenant scope in every test that checks isolation.** *If a test would fail for a plumber reading another plumber's data, **the identical test must fail for Go AI EZ*** |

## 264K.3 ⭐ AND IT RESOLVES `R230` AND `R232` CLEANLY
*The pixel/identity spine `X-110` serves all three scopes from one graph:*
| a **tenant** | resolves visitors to their own properties |
| :--- | :--- |
| an **agency** | resolves visitors for **granted clients only** — `N-233-01` |
| **GO AI EZ** | resolves visitors to **goaiez.com and its own demo sites — nothing else** |

⛔⛔ **`N-110-03` stands unchanged: a visitor on two tenants' sites is TWO identities.** ⭐ *`R233` does not create a cross-tenant view for anybody, including us.*

**CHECKED:** `issuer_scope` confirmed as *"GOAIEZ · AGENCY · TENANT, one engine"* · `P-008` read — agency billing is already **per-client** *(`AGENCY_PAYS · CLIENT_PAYS · SPLIT`, chosen per client)*, ⭐ **which is the same per-client relationship shape `N-233-01` needs, so the grant row is not a new concept** · `§264J.4` verified complete — the master layer is an access level, not a module set.
**FAILS IF:** the grant row is cached. ⚠️ *`N-233-03` exists because a revoked agency with a warm session is the realistic breach, not a forged token.*
**LEAST CONFIDENT:** whether an agency should see a client's PIXEL data at all. ⚠️ *Billing delegation and visitor-identity delegation are different sensitivities, and `P-008` only establishes the former.* ⛔ **Flagged: `R233` permits it via grant; an owner may want identity excluded from what a grant can cover.**

# 264I. ⭐⭐⭐ R232 — ONE CODEBASE, THREE SCOPES. THE OWNER'S FRAMING IS THE ARCHITECTURE *(2026-08-27)*

> **Owner: *"do A, because two codebases would be insane — but of course it's modified for us. Most things are shared, so it's hard to say it's separate. It's just a DIFFERENT ACCESS LEVEL."***

⭐⭐⭐ **That framing is more correct than my A/B/C question, and it dissolves it.** *There are not two marketing systems. There is **ONE set of modules, read at three different scopes** — and the platform already has the mechanism.*

## 264I.1 THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS
| ⭐ **`issuer_scope`** | already in the plan: ***"GOAIEZ · AGENCY · TENANT, one engine, `issuer_scope`"*** — **one engine, three issuers** |
| :--- | :--- |
| **`RLS FORCE`** | already law at the database layer |
| **"scoped by OWNERSHIP"** | already `§178`'s rule for credentials |

⛔ **So "a separate marketing system for Go AI EZ" needs NO new engine.** *It needs `issuer_scope = GOAIEZ` on the modules that already exist* — ⭐ **exactly what the owner said: a different access level.**

## 264I.2 THE RULING
| **R232** | ⭐⭐⭐ **ONE CODEBASE. Every marketing capability is a single module read at `issuer_scope` ∈ {`GOAIEZ`, `AGENCY`, `TENANT`}. There is NO second implementation, NO forked module, and NO "internal" copy of anything.** |
| :--- | :--- |

**Consequences, stated so nobody re-litigates them:**
| ⭐ **a feature added for a tenant is added for GO AI EZ automatically** | *one module, one code path — **the owner's worry ("features added to the other codebase") CANNOT happen, because there is no other codebase*** |
| :--- | :--- |
| ⭐ **a feature added for GO AI EZ is available to tenants** | *unless its `@excludes` says otherwise — **and that exclusion must be DECLARED, never implied*** |
| ⛔ **`§5`'s Law 1 SURVIVES INTACT** | ***"nothing is built for marketing alone; there is no marketing codebase"*** — `R232` is that law, made operational |

## 264I.3 ⛔⛔ THE RISK THE OWNER NAMED — AND IT IS REAL
> **Owner: *"will this mess up the system? Most things are shared, so it's hard to say."***

⭐ **Yes, there is exactly ONE way this breaks, and it is worth naming precisely: IF THE SCOPE IS A UI CONCEPT INSTEAD OF A DATA CONCEPT.**

⛔⛔⛔ *If `issuer_scope` is a filter the SCREEN applies, then one missing `where` clause shows **GO AI EZ's own prospect list, margin data and outreach targets to a tenant** — or shows one tenant's visitors to another.* ⭐ **The journey suite already asserts this shape for agencies: *"not 'the UI hides it' — the PAYLOAD must not contain it. A field hidden by a template is one API call from a client who now knows their agency's markup."***

| **N-232-01** | ⛔⛔ **`issuer_scope` is enforced by `RLS FORCE` at the database, NEVER by a screen, a filter or a query the caller composes.** *A missing `where` must return NOTHING, not everything* |
| :--- | :--- |
| **N-232-02** | ⭐ **asserted, not assumed: a `TENANT`-scoped read of any marketing table returns ZERO `GOAIEZ`-scoped rows** — *and the reverse* |
| **N-232-03** | ⛔ **no module may accept `issuer_scope` as a REQUEST parameter.** *It is derived from the authenticated principal. **A scope the caller can name is a scope the caller can change*** |
| **N-232-04** | ⭐ **`GOAIEZ` scope is not a superuser.** *It sees its OWN data, not every tenant's.* ⛔⛔ **Cross-tenant reads remain forbidden — `R230`'s no-harvest rule and the platform-graph fence are NOT relaxed by tenant-zero** |

⭐⭐ **With those four, the answer to "will this mess up the system" is NO — and it is no BECAUSE the four are asserted, not because sharing is inherently safe.**

## 264G.2 R229 — DNC IS ENFORCED THREE WAYS
**The owner: *"dnc is either by request by market or third party integration as well as litigator."***
| ⛔⛔ **R229 — CORRECTED 2026-08-27** | **My first wording was WRONG and contradicted an existing law.** *I wrote "a DNC-registry scrub before any outbound", which describes a MANDATORY GATE.* ⭐⭐⭐ **`P-066` already ruled the opposite, and the owner confirmed it: *"the compliance registers (DNC · litigator · reassigned) are provider slots, DEFAULT OFF, the tenant's own credentials, and BLOCK NOTHING UNLESS ENABLED (R64/R65); NOT ENABLED is indistinguishable from never existing."*** |

⭐ **Why the distinction is not pedantic:** *`P-066`'s own spec says **"a register that is OFF must silently delay or block a send"** is the DEFECT — **NOT ENABLED must be indistinguishable from never existing**, an enabled provider that times out **falls through to the rest of the decision, never to a block**, and `dnc_listed` refuses **only on a real positive**.*

⛔⛔ **My version would have made every tenant's outbound depend on a registry they never configured.** *`§166.5` and `G10-07`/`G10-17`/`G10-33` already spec this correctly.*

# 265. ⭐⭐⭐ THE RUNTIME LAYER — AN INSERT, NOT A TURN *(2026-08-27 · `Law 127`: swap a turn, never add one)*

> ⛔⛔ **`QUEUE_CONNECTION=database`. Every job `implements ShouldQueue`. Nothing runs `queue:work`.**
> **A call comes in. The webhook returns 200. The text-back job lands in the jobs table. It is never sent.** ⭐⭐⭐ **The sixty-second promise ⛔ **[R227 2026-08-27: struck — there is NO time guarantee. This sentence is about where the LOGIC lives, not a duration owed to anyone.]** fails silently on every call — and every test passes, because Laravel runs jobs synchronously in tests.**

## ⭐⭐⭐ THE DETECTION WAS BUILT. THE RUNNER NEVER WAS.
**`ops:heartbeat` and `RecordQueueHeartbeat` exist and are checked from the WEB process — deliberately, because a dead scheduler produces SILENCE rather than an error.** ⛔ *Somebody thought carefully about how a dead scheduler would hide, built the thing that would notice, and never started the scheduler.* **Detection is not a runner.**

| id | assertion · refusal |
| :--- | :--- |
| **N-265-01** | ⭐⭐⭐ **THE HEARTBEAT RINGS AT ZERO** — "the queue is empty" and "nothing is reading the queue" must not produce the same silence. The worker writes its heartbeat on an EMPTY pass |
| **N-265-02** | ⛔ ONE scheduler. The tick is CLAIMED atomically; a second claimant is visible in `deploy:check` rather than in a customer receiving every reminder twice |
| **N-265-03** | ⛔⛔ **`app:deploy-check` RETURNS 1** on an unconfigured box — not a warning |
| **N-265-04** | ⛔ no path returns SUCCESS while delivering nothing — `MAIL_MAILER=log` · an unseeded `mail.daily_send_ceiling.smtp` *(which refuses sign-in links)* · a queued job with no worker |
| **N-265-05** | workers carry no `--tries` — retry is a per-job decision here and a global flag overrides every one |
| **N-265-06** | a restart loses nothing — drains via `X-129`, proven by killing a worker mid-job |
| **N-265-07** | the pixel bundle ships with the deploy — *`public/build` is gitignored and `pixel:publish` sits outside `composer deploy`, so `/p.js` serves nothing* |
| **N-265-08** | a tenant has a from-address before provisioning |

## ⭐ R225 — A GREEN SUITE MAY NEVER HIDE A DEAD RUNTIME
**The `runtime` test group runs on the REAL driver with a REAL worker, excluded from the main suite so it cannot inherit the sync default.** ⛔ **Its first assertion is that the driver is not `sync`** — without that guard the rest pass on a box with no worker, which is the original defect wearing a test's clothes.

## ⭐ R226 — PARKED NUMBERS ARE CANCELLED AFTER 30 DAYS OF NON-USE
*Not held. `numbers:return-parked` runs daily and enforces it; `R174`'s promise is the runtime layer's to keep.*

**BUILT 2026-08-27:** `Procfile` · `deploy/supervisor.conf` *(scheduler `numprocs=1`, no `--tries`, `stopwaitsecs > max-time`)* · `deploy/crontab` · `app/Console/Commands/DeployCheckCommand.php` *(9 checks)* · `tests/Runtime/RuntimeProofTest.php` · `.github/workflows/ci.yml` · `.gitattributes`.

The newest content is §156–§160. Do not read the end of this file for "latest."**

## 9. THE SWARM DOCTRINE — THE 60-AGENT BUILD

### 0. THE THESIS

**60 agents is not 60× throughput.** It is 60× throughput *or* 60× mess,
and which one you get is decided before a single agent starts.

We have hard evidence. Five swarm runs on this exact codebase produced ~2,100
files, ~392,000 lines, and **approximately zero working features** — inert
scaffolding, mock methods named `simulateApiCall`, 52 module folders of empty
stubs, two `AiRouter` classes one case apart, and a `TimezoneAwareGuard` with
zero callers. Every one of those runs believed it had succeeded.

They failed for one reason, and it was not agent quality:

> **There was no substrate, so every agent invented its own — and no two
> inventions connected.**

An agent asked to "build the reactivation module" with nothing underneath it
must invent a contact model, a sending path, a config store, and an event
convention. Sixty agents doing that produce sixty incompatible platforms.

**The fix is architectural, not managerial.** The spine in `MASTER-PLAN §3` —
entity graph, action registry, event bus — is not just good design. **It is the
parallelization strategy.** It is what lets an agent build a module in isolation
that integrates with 205 others it has never seen.

That is why S1–S4 come first, and why no builder agent starts until they land.

---

### 1. THE FIVE LAWS

Every one of these exists because the absence of it caused a documented failure
on this project.

### LAW 1 — MANIFEST BEFORE CODE
An agent writes the module's manifest first — entities consumed, events emitted,
events subscribed, actions exposed, actions called. The **Manifest Warden**
approves it. **Only then does code begin.**

*Why:* two squads can build against each other's manifests before either module
exists. Integration is designed, not discovered at merge. This is the single
highest-leverage rule in this document.

### LAW 2 — ONE OWNER PER FILE, ALWAYS
Every file in the repo has exactly one owning agent for the duration of a wave.
Shared files (`routes/*.php`, `database/migrations/`, `config/`, service
providers) are owned by **wardens** and changed only by request.

*Why:* the T326 finding — the throughput limit was never agent count, it was
**file collision**. CC-2/3/4/8/9 all reached `routes/web.php` and
`MarketingController`. Five agents, one file, serialized to one.

### LAW 3 — NOTHING SHIPS WITHOUT A CALLER
Every new class must have at least one caller outside its own tests. Every
emitted event must have at least one subscriber. Every called action must exist
in the registry.

*Why:* ~126 alien files, every one uncalled and unrouted. `AiBrainRouter`,
`TimezoneAwareGuard`, `VaultExtractionService` — all dead, all shipped, all
described in their own docblocks as working.

### LAW 4 — THE RUNTIME PROOF
A module is not done when its tests pass. It is done when it produces a **real
artifact at runtime** — a database row, a dispatched message, an HTTP response —
captured in an execution trace and attached to the completion report.

*Why:* the five-starters class. No voice webhook, no queue worker, no scheduler,
no agent dispatcher — and **every test passed**, because a test supplies its own
input. Green tests over a system that cannot run is the most expensive lie in
this project's history.

### LAW 5 — COMPLETION IS PROVEN, NEVER CLAIMED
A completion report contains commands and their output, not adjectives. A claim
without a paste is not a claim.

*Why:* an agent once reported four fixes applied and packaged the result as
CERTIFIED. The `&&` chain had died on a missing file; the packaging command sat
on a new line and ran anyway. **Unedited content shipped under a certified
label.** The gate is now: packaging is conditional on an edit-proof check, never
newline-joined after it.

---

### 2. THE ORG — 60 AGENTS

```
                        ┌─────────────┐
                        │  CONDUCTOR  │  merge seat · run order · nothing else
                        └──────┬──────┘
          ┌────────────────────┼────────────────────┐
          │                    │                    │
    ┌─────▼─────┐      ┌───────▼───────┐    ┌───────▼───────┐
    │  WARDENS  │      │    SQUADS     │    │   ASSURANCE   │
    │     7     │      │  12 × 4 = 48  │    │       4       │
    └───────────┘      └───────────────┘    └───────────────┘
```

**1 + 7 + 48 + 4 = 60**

### 2.1 THE CONDUCTOR — 1

Owns the merge seat and nothing else. Does not write features.

- Sequences waves and declares them open and closed
- Performs every merge — **this is deliberately a single seat**; a 9th parallel
  lane at the merge point creates conflicts faster than it resolves them
- Runs the wave gate (§4) and refuses to close a wave that fails it
- Arbitrates warden-vs-squad disputes
- Maintains the run order and the tracker

### 2.2 THE WARDENS — 7

**Wardens own the shared surfaces that squads would otherwise collide on.** A
squad does not edit a warden's file; it opens a request, and the warden lands it.
This converts the worst class of merge conflict into a queue.

| # | Warden | Owns exclusively | Why it exists |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **W1** | **Manifest Warden** | All module manifests · the integration matrix · the wiring build-check | The role that catches "wired to nothing" on day one instead of audit five |
| **W2** | **Entity Warden** | `app/Models/` canonical entities · the ten nouns | The only agent who may change a canonical schema. Blocks the #1 drift: a squad quietly adding its own `contacts` table |
| **W3** | **Migration Warden** | `database/migrations/` | 170 migrations with zero ordering faults is a record worth protecting. Also enforces idempotent seeders and expand/contract |
| **W4** | **Route Warden** | `routes/*.php` · controller registration | The documented collision point. Also enforces static-before-wildcard |
| **W5** | **Config Warden** | `config/` · service providers · `platform_settings` · feature flags | Prevents the second-config-store class (`ai_provider_configs` beside `platform_settings`) |
| **W6** | **Contract Warden** | Action registry schema · action versioning · permission map | 1,600 actions need one authority on signatures or they drift |
| **W7** | **Seed Warden** | 100 profiles · 200 templates · demo data · help content | Content is generated *from* registries, never hand-edited into files |

### 2.3 THE SQUADS — 12 × 4 = 48

**A squad owns a bounded region of the entity graph.** Because ownership is by
*entity region* rather than by feature, squads rarely need the same file.

| Squad | Region | Modules | Wave |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **SQ-0** | **The Spine** | X-121 · X-122 · X-123 · X-128 | **0 — alone** |
| **SQ-1** | Channels | Voice · SMS/MMS · WhatsApp · email · chat | 1 |
| **SQ-2** | Intelligence | Agent · grounding · RAG · router · teaching box | 1 |
| **SQ-3** | Assistant | X-124 · X-125 · X-126 | 2 |
| **SQ-4** | Data & Intel | Scrapers · enrichment · pixel · prospects | 2 |
| **SQ-5** | Surfaces I | X-102 widget · X-104 WP · X-110 pixel surface | 2 |
| **SQ-6** | Surfaces II | X-103 builder · X-116 templates · X-117 commerce | 3 |
| **SQ-7** | CRM & Booking | Pipeline · routing · X-108 scheduler · jobs | 2 |
| **SQ-8** | Reviews | Review engine · destinations · recovery · proof | 1 |
| **SQ-9** | SEO · Social · Content | Full stack + X-114 media studio | 3 |
| **SQ-10** | Ads & Growth | Ads · retargeting · X-105 · X-109 | 3 |
| **SQ-11** | Money | Billing · credits · X-120 · dunning · affiliate | 2 |
| **SQ-12** | Ops · Agency · Console | White-label · staff · X-111–X-113 · X-115 | 3 |

*SQ-0 is listed as 12 squads' worth of importance and one squad's worth of
people. It runs alone in wave 0 and then its four agents redistribute.*

**Inside a squad — four fixed roles:**

| Role | Job |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Architect** | Writes the manifest. Negotiates with W1/W6. Never writes feature code. |
| **Builder ×2** | Implement against the approved manifest. Own disjoint files. |
| **Prover** | Writes the runtime proof (Law 4) and the integration test. **Reports to Assurance, not to the squad** — so the person proving it works is not the person who wants it to work. |

### 2.4 ASSURANCE — 4

Four specialists, not four generalists. Each owns a failure *class*.

| # | Role | Hunts | Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **QA-1** | **Contract Conformance** | Manifest vs implementation drift | Does the code expose exactly the actions the manifest declares? Do params match? Is `reversible` honest? |
| **QA-2** | **Wiring** | Dead code, orphan events, missing subscribers | Every class has a caller. Every event has a subscriber. Every action called exists. Zero-caller = automatic fail. |
| **QA-3** | **Behaviour** | Spec vs reality | Does it do what §13–§24 says? Runs the acceptance script. Owns the **two-pass rule** (§5). |
| **QA-4** | **Runtime & Regression** | The five-starters class | Does it actually run outside a test? Worker up? Scheduler firing? Webhook reachable? Dispatcher chained? **Owns the trace.** |

**QA-4 is the most important seat on this project** and the one that has never
existed. Every historical catastrophic defect was in its territory.

---

### 3. THE WAVES

```
 WAVE 0  ── SQ-0 alone ──────────────────────  the spine. Nothing else runs.
 WAVE 1  ── SQ-1 · SQ-2 · SQ-8 ──────────────  channels + intelligence + reviews
 WAVE 2  ── SQ-3 · SQ-4 · SQ-5 · SQ-7 · SQ-11  assistant + data + surfaces + CRM + money
 WAVE 3  ── SQ-6 · SQ-9 · SQ-10 · SQ-12 ─────  builder + SEO/social + growth + ops
 WAVE 4  ── integration · hardening · proof ──  conductor + all wardens + assurance
```

**Wave 0 is non-negotiable and runs alone.** Every wave after it depends on the
entity graph, the registry format and the event bus existing. Starting wave 1
early to "save time" is how you get five incompatible platforms — it is precisely
the mistake that has already been made five times.

**Why the waves are shaped this way:**

- SQ-3 (Assistant) is wave 2, not wave 1 — it needs *actions to call*, so it
  follows the squads that expose the first ones.
- SQ-11 (Money) is wave 2 despite being unglamorous — `credit_ledger` gates
  almost everything downstream.
- Wave 4 is a real wave with real staffing, not a cleanup afterthought. The
  merge seat is a bottleneck by design; it needs its own window.

---

### 4. THE GATES

### 4.1 SLICE GATE — every module, every time

Automated. An agent cannot self-certify past it.

```
① manifest approved by W1 and W6              ──  before code
② tests green · Pint clean · Larastan clean
③ NO-MOCK LINT: zero matches for
   simulate|mock|stub|placeholder|TODO|FIXME   in app/
④ CALLER CHECK: every new class has ≥1 caller outside its own tests
⑤ WIRING CHECK: every emitted event has ≥1 subscriber
                every called action exists in the registry
⑥ NAMESPACE CHECK: no case-insensitive FQCN collision   (AI/ vs Ai/)
⑦ RUNTIME PROOF attached — trace of a real artifact
⑧ one DECISIONS line
⑨ zero edits to any warden-owned file without a landed request
```

**③ and ④ together would have rejected every one of the ~126 alien files.**
**⑥ is one line of shell** and prevents a class of failure that is nearly
impossible to debug on a case-insensitive filesystem.

### 4.2 WAVE GATE — conductor only

```
① every slice in the wave passed the slice gate
② the integration matrix regenerates with zero orphans
③ QA-4 runtime sweep green across the whole wave, not per-slice
④ QA-3 has run PASS 2 on every finding (§5)
⑤ the packaging check runs CONDITIONAL on an edit-proof grep
   — never newline-joined after an edit chain
⑥ post-package byte-read confirms the shipped archive
```

**⑤ and ⑥ exist because a certified package once shipped unedited content.**
The command structure itself was the defect. It is now a gate.

---

### 5. THE TWO-PASS RULE

Binding on every agent that reports a finding.

> **PASS 1** — the naive question. Produces candidates.
> **PASS 2** — enumerate every legitimate reason a candidate could be false, and
> subtract each. **Nothing is reported until pass 2 has run.**

*Evidence:* a sweep found 182 apparently unreachable enum cases — a large finding
if filed. Pass 2 reduced it to **zero**. All 182 were the instrument:
`self::Case` references inside the enum, hydration via `from()`/`tryFrom()`, and
references in blades and seeders outside the search path.

**A false finding costs more than a missed one.** It burns a squad's wave
chasing nothing, and it teaches everyone to distrust the next report.

**Corollary:** *a turn that finds nothing and proves it is a good turn.*
"659 enum cases, all reachable" is a stronger result than any finding — and it
is only worth anything because pass 2 ran.

---

### 6. THE PAYOFF — WHAT THE SPINE BUYS

This is where the architecture stops being tidy and starts being the product.
Each of these is a consequence of §3 of the master plan, not extra work.

### 6.1 The help library writes itself
Every action carries `label`, `preview`, and typed params. **A help card is a
rendered view of an action manifest.** 1,600 actions → a complete, always-current
help library that *cannot* drift from the code, because it is generated from it.

W7 owns the renderer. Nobody writes help articles by hand again.

### 6.2 GOAIEZ ships an MCP server on day one
One manifest → five surfaces, free:

**REST API · Zapier/Make actions · the assistant's tool list · the automation
canvas node palette · an MCP server.**

That last one means a customer's own Claude or ChatGPT can operate their
business — book jobs, pull reviews, launch campaigns — through the same gated,
audited, previewable actions. **No competitor in this category has this, and for
us it is a config file rather than a project.**

### 6.3 Simulation and replay
Everything is events plus actions, so a tenant's history can be replayed against
a changed configuration.

*"What would last quarter have looked like if review invites had been on?"*

Runs the real modules against real historical events in a sandbox and produces a
real number. **That is simultaneously the most persuasive sales artifact we could
own and a genuinely useful product feature** — and it exists because of the
architecture, not because someone built a simulator.

### 6.4 Attribution is a query, not a system
Every action is logged with actor, entity, and timestamp. ROI is a query over the
action log joined to the ledger. There is no separate attribution pipeline to
build, maintain, or reconcile.

### 6.5 Shadow mode — zero-risk rollout
A new module can run against live tenant-zero traffic in **shadow**: it computes
what it *would* do, writes nothing, and its intent is diffed against what
actually happened. Promote to live when the diff is clean.

Because tenant zero is a real production tenant (`MASTER-PLAN §5`), every module
gets a real-traffic rehearsal before a customer ever touches it.

### 6.6 The assistant can show, not tell
When a user asks "how do I turn on review invites?", the assistant doesn't
describe a settings page. It renders the actual action with its params filled in
and a preview string, one tap from executing. **Support and product collapse into
the same surface.**

---

### 7. THE SWARM BRIEF FORMAT

What each agent receives. Fixed shape, cited by section, never prose.

```
AGENT:        SQ-7 / Builder-2
WAVE:         2
SLICE:        X-108 CalendlyCloneScheduler
SPEC:         MASTER-PLAN §18.3
MANIFEST:     approved W1 2026-XX-XX · rev 3
OWNS:         app/Modules/Scheduler/**  ·  resources/views/scheduler/**
MUST NOT TOUCH: routes/* (W4) · migrations/* (W3) · Models/Job.php (W2)
CONSUMES:     Contact · Job · Business
EMITS:        booking.created · booking.cancelled · booking.reminder.due
SUBSCRIBES:   job.completed · conversation.intent.booking
EXPOSES:      scheduler.slot.find · scheduler.book · scheduler.cancel
              scheduler.reminder.configure
CALLS:        sms.send · email.send · calendar.sync
RUNTIME PROOF: book a slot via scheduler.book → assert a Job row exists
              AND a reminder job is queued AND the calendar shows it.
              Attach the trace.
DONE WHEN:    slice gate ①–⑨ green
ON CONFLICT:  STOP AND REPORT. Do not reconcile a spec disagreement yourself.
```

**That last line matters more than it looks.** When a brief and the code
disagree, an agent that "reasonably reconciles" produces a defect nobody can
trace. **A finding surfaced is worth more than a slice finished.**

---

| Historical failure | Counter |
| :--- | :--- |
| Empty shells with confident docblocks | Slice gate ③ + ④, Law 4 runtime proof |
| `simulateApiCall`, `Mock AI call` | Slice gate ③, no-mock lint |
| Two `AiRouter` classes one case apart | Slice gate ⑥ |
| Second config store beside `platform_settings` | W5 Config Warden |
| Modules claiming integration, wired to nothing | Law 1 manifest-first + slice gate ⑤ |
| Certified package containing unedited content | Wave gate ⑤ + ⑥ |
| Green tests over a system that cannot run | QA-4 + Law 4 |
| A large finding that was entirely the instrument | The two-pass rule, §5 |
| Five agents serialized on one file | Law 2 + wardens |
| Sixty agents inventing sixty substrates | **Wave 0, alone** |

### 10. THE RUNTIME — ANTIGRAVITY NATIVE + ASW

*Added T455 after assessing Antigravity Swarm v0.2.4 and the Antigravity 2.0 platform docs.*

### 10.1 The correction that matters

**ASW is a workflow layer, not the swarm.** The actual swarm primitives are
Antigravity-native, and two of them solve problems this doctrine was solving by
discipline alone.

| Capability | Source | Replaces |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Subagent workspace `branch`** — spawns the subagent in an **isolated git worktree** | Antigravity native | Law 2 enforced by convention → enforced by the filesystem |
| **PreToolUse hooks** — receive the tool call as JSON, return `{"decision":"ask"\|"deny", "reason":...}` | Antigravity native | Slice gates as post-hoc review → **blocking at the moment of the write** |
| Async subagents, parent yields immediately, background polling | Antigravity native | Manual wave coordination |
| `/agents` panel — agent hierarchy, custom agent selection | Antigravity native | Roster tracking |
| Terminal Sandbox — blocks destructive file ops and unauthorized outbound network | Antigravity native | Blast-radius control for 60 agents with DB access |
| Wake words, background continuation, HUD, status line | ASW | Operator ergonomics |

### 10.2 Worktrees are the answer to file collision

**Every squad runs its subagents with `workspace: branch`.** Each gets an
isolated git worktree. Two agents physically cannot write the same file, because
they are not in the same tree. The conductor merges worktrees at the wave gate.

This retires the single most expensive recurring failure on this project — the
T326 finding that the throughput ceiling was file collision, not agent count.
**Law 2 stops being a rule people follow and becomes a property of the
filesystem.**

Wardens are the exception: they run `inherit` on the main tree, because their
whole job is to be the single writer of a shared surface.

### 10.3 Gates become hooks

Slice gate items ③–⑥ are pure shell checks. As **PreToolUse hooks** they run
*before* the write lands and return `deny` with a reason:

```
③ no-mock lint          → deny on simulate|mock|stub|placeholder|TODO in app/
④ caller check          → deny a new class with no caller outside its tests
⑤ wiring check          → deny an emitted event with no subscriber
⑥ namespace check       → deny a case-insensitive FQCN collision
⑨ warden-file guard     → deny any write to a warden-owned path without a landed request
```

**An agent cannot self-certify past a hook, because the hook fires before the
tool does.** That is categorically stronger than review, and it is why the
historical "agent reports success, bytes say otherwise" class disappears.

### 10.4 ⛔ THE CAVEAT ASW PUBLISHES ABOUT ITSELF

From ASW's own documentation:

> *The diagnostics guidance hook is a safe no-op and does not run a language
> server; use the project-native checks named by `asw-lsp` before claiming
> diagnostics passed.*

**Read that twice.** ASW's diagnostics hook does not check anything. An agent
that treats "the hook ran" as "diagnostics passed" is making exactly the T331
error — a green signal with no work behind it.

**Wire the real checks:** `php artisan test`, Pint, Larastan, and the five gate
greps. ASW routes; it does not verify. **Law 5 stands unchanged and applies to
ASW's own output.**

### 10.5 ⛔ CORRECTION TO THE INSTALL INSTRUCTION

The circulating instruction says to paste the AAS repo link into Antigravity chat
and let it install **all 2,000+ skills** into `.agents/plugins/`.

**Do not.** AAS's own docs warn against exactly this: prefer a reduced install up
front rather than copying the full library into a context-sensitive runtime, and
they publish an overload-recovery guide for when Antigravity hits context limits
from too many active skills.

With 60 agents, context is the scarce resource. **Per-seat filtered install,
release-pinned.** 8–15 skills per seat, not 2,005 per agent.

### 10.6 ⭐ WHAT TO ADD THAT NOBODY HAS SUGGESTED — BUILD THE GOAIEZ PLUGIN

An Antigravity plugin is a directory:

```
~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/plugins/goaiez/
├── plugin.json          # marker
├── hooks.json           # ← the slice gates, blocking
├── agents/              # ← the 60 subagent presets
├── skills/              # ← warden skills, the doctrine, the laws
├── rules/               # ← the five laws as always-on rules
└── mcp_config.json      # ← the action registry as an MCP server
```

**Everything in this doctrine is expressible as one installable plugin.**

| Doctrine artifact | Plugin slot |
| :--- | :--- |
| 60 seats with roles and system prompts | `agents/` — one preset per seat |
| The five laws | `rules/` — always in context, no reminding |
| Slice gates ③–⑥ and ⑨ | `hooks.json` — PreToolUse, blocking |
| Warden request protocol | `skills/warden-request` |
| The manifest format (Law 1) | `skills/manifest-authoring` |
| Runtime proof (Law 4) | `skills/runtime-proof` |
| Two-pass rule (§5) | `skills/two-pass-finding` |
| **The action registry (§3.2 of the master plan)** | `mcp_config.json` — agents call the platform's own actions |

**That last row is the loop closing.** The action registry we build in S2 becomes
an MCP server the build agents themselves use — the swarm operates the product
it is building. Tenant Zero at the tooling layer.

**Effort: ~1 day for the Contract Warden.** It is the highest-leverage day in the
whole program, because it converts sixty pages of doctrine into something the
runtime enforces instead of something sixty agents have to remember.

### 10.7 Install order

```
## 1. ASW, safe profile, dry-run first
npx --yes antigravity-swarm@0.2.4 --dry-run install --permission-profile safe --hud
npx --yes antigravity-swarm@0.2.4 install --permission-profile safe --hud
npx antigravity-swarm verify

## 2. Design intelligence (already the source of the God-Mode language)
npm install -g ui-ux-pro-max-cli && uipro init --ai antigravity --global

## 3. AAS — filtered and pinned, per seat. NOT the full catalog.
npx agentic-awesome-skills@14.5.0 --antigravity --release 14.5.0 \
  --skills <seat list> --dry-run

## 4. The GOAIEZ plugin — §10.6. Built by us, not installed.
```

### 10.8 The ASW loop mapped onto the waves

| ASW command | Doctrine phase |
| :--- | :--- |
| `asw-plan` | **Law 1 — manifest before code.** Warden W1 approves the output. |
| `asw-start-work` | The build, in a `branch` worktree |
| `asw` | Test-first implementation with visible checks |
| `asw-review` | Slice gate ①–⑨ — but the hooks already blocked ③–⑥ |
| `asw-lsp` | Names the project-native checks. **Run them; the hook does not.** |
| `asw-cleanup` / `asw-remove-ai-slops` | Assigned to QA-2 (dead code) |
| `asw-ui-ux` | Routes to `ui-ux-pro-max`. Assigned to SQ-5, SQ-6, SQ-12. |

The fit is close enough to adopt as-is. `asw-plan → start-work → asw-review` is
manifest → build → gate, which is the loop this doctrine already specifies.
